- Requirements for Go port: Go types mirroring the enums and `_uiheroinfo`, plus the exported function set above. Cross-boundary callbacks (`UiSelHero*Dialog`, `UiProgressDialog`, `UiSelectGame`/`UiSelectProvider`) become Go function values, not interfaces. `_uiheroinfo` is marshalled across the save-file boundary via `gfnHeroInfo` callbacks — in Go it becomes a plain struct passed by pointer into `pfile` enumeration.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Enum ordinals are **load-bearing** because they are stored as `m_value` ints in list items and read back with casts (mainmenu.cpp:36, selhero.cpp): `MAINMENU_*` 0..7 (diabloui.h:37-46), `SELHERO_*` 0..3 (:48-53), `FOCUS_*` 0..2 (:31-35).
  - `_uiheroinfo.name` is a fixed **16-byte** buffer (`char name[16]`, :65) — the selhero edit control allows max length **15** (selhero.cpp:310) so a NUL fits; but `PlayerNameLength` is 32 (player.h:42) and `UiValidPlayerName` validates ≤32.
  - `_uidefaultstats` fields are `uint16_t` (:56-59); `_uiheroinfo.level`/`herorank` are `uint8_t`, stats `uint16_t`, `saveNumber` `uint32_t` (:63-74) — matters for save-file byte width.
  - `LoadBackgroundArt(..., int frames = 1)` default (:112) and `UiAddLogo(..., int y = GetUIRectangle().position.y)` default (:114) must be preserved (or made explicit at call sites).
  - `UiInitList` argument order + defaults (`wraps=false`, `fnFullscreen=nullptr`, `fnYesNo=nullptr`, `selectedItem=0`) (:121).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: default-argument `UiAddLogo` evaluates `GetUIRectangle()` **at each call** in C++ (it's a default arg, evaluated per call) — not a static. `gfnHeroInfo` is declared here but *defined* in selhero.cpp:48, a cross-TU global that must be set before `UiInitList` runs.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/types.go` (enums, `_uiheroinfo` → `HeroInfo`, `_uidefaultstats` → `DefaultStats`) plus `internal/ui/api.go` for the exported surface. Strategy — keep numeric enum values identical and add `String()` only for debug; do not export the C-style pointer-out-params: return `(result, saveNumber)` tuples.
- Risks/open questions: `HeroClass` underlying width is not visible here — check `tables/playerdat.hpp`/`player.h` for the enum's underlying type before fixing `HeroInfo.HeroClass` width; `_difficulty`/`GameData` need their own Go homes (selgame.h:7, multi.h) before this header can be ported.

### Source/DiabloUI/dialogs.cpp
- Purpose: In-UI modal "OK" popup (with optional caption and error-vs-normal art), used for fatal/non-fatal messages while the game is running; falls back to an OS message box when the UI is inactive, headless, or already inside a dialog.
- Public API: `UiErrorOkDialog(std::string_view text, const vector<unique_ptr<UiItemBase>>& renderBehind)`, `UiErrorOkDialog(caption, text, renderBehind)` (dialogs.h:10-11) plus `UiErrorOkDialog(caption, text, bool error = true)` (utils/ui_fwd.h:34, defined dialogs.cpp:217). Internals: `LoadDialogSprite`, `Init`, `Deinit`, `DialogLoop`, `UiOkDialog`, `DialogActionOK`.
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/button.h` (`LoadDialogButtonGraphics`, `FreeDialogButtonGraphics`, `DialogButtonWidth/Height`); `diabloui.h` (`UiLoadBlackBackground`, `UiClearScreen`, `UiRenderItems`, `UiRenderListItems`, `UiFadeIn`, `DrawMouse`, `UiItemMouseEvents`, `UiHandleEvents`, `DiabloUiSurface`, `ArtCursor`); `ui_item.h` (`UiImageClx`, `UiText`, `UiButton`); `engine/load_pcx.hpp`/`load_clx.hpp`, `engine/clx_sprite.hpp`, `engine/render/text_render.hpp` (`WordWrapString`, `FontSizeDialog`), `engine/point.hpp`, `engine/surface.hpp`; `utils/sdl_geometry.h` (`MakeSdlRect`, `ScaleOutputRect` implied), `utils/ui_fwd.h` (`GetUIRectangle`, `UiErrorOkDialog` decl), `utils/language.h` (`_`), `utils/log.hpp` (`LogError`), `utils/is_of.hpp` (`IsNoneOf`), `utils/sdl_compat.h` (`PollEvent`, `SDLC_ShowCursor`, `SDLC_ShowSimpleMessageBox`, `SDL_SetSurfaceClipRect` compat); `controls/input.h`, `controls/menu_controls.h`; `headless_mode.hpp` (`HeadlessMode`), `hwcursor.hpp` (`IsHardwareCursor`), `init.hpp` (`gbActive`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Sprite selection matrix (caption × error) → four assets, PCX transparency at index 255, CLX preferred for the captioned error: no-caption → `ui_art\srpopup` (error) or `ui_art\spopup` (info); caption+error → `ui_art\dvl_lrpopup.clx`, else `ui_art\lrpopup`; caption+info → `ui_art\lpopup`.
  - Build the dialog item list once in `Init`: background (black + default palette via `UiLoadBlackBackground`, showing the OS cursor on failure), ensure `ArtCursor` is loaded if neither hardware cursor nor `ArtCursor` exists, load dialog-button graphics, word-wrap the body to `spriteWidth - 40` at dialog font size, then push image + text + OK button with the exact offsets below.
  - Modal loop `DialogLoop`: drain events; mouse down/up → `UiItemMouseEvents(items)`; otherwise a `MenuAction` of BACK or SELECT ends the dialog; every event also goes through `UiHandleEvents`; then `UiClearScreen → UiRenderItems(renderBehind) → UiRenderListItems() → UiRenderItems(items) → DrawMouse → UiFadeIn` until `dialogEnd`.
  - `UiOkDialog`: always log via `LogError` (caption+text or text only); if `!gbActive || inDialog` → show OS cursor + `SDL_ShowSimpleMessageBox(ERROR, caption, text)` and return (unless `HeadlessMode`); if hardware cursor is active → `SDLC_ShowCursor()`; if `Init` fails → log again + message box; then set `inDialog`, clear the UI surface clip rect, run the loop, `Deinit`, clear `inDialog`.
  - `Deinit` releases the dialog sprite, the item vector, and the button graphics.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `constexpr uint8_t TransparentColor = 255` (dialogs.cpp:61) for all four PCX popups.
  - Text width `dialogWidth - 40` (:95-96) and wrap at `FontSizeDialog` (:98).
  - No-caption layout: sprite at `uiPosition + (180, 168)` with w/h = sprite size; text rect `+ (200, 211)`, size `(textWidth, 80)`, flags `AlignCenter | ColorDialogWhite`; OK button at `+ (265, 265)` size `DialogButtonWidth × DialogButtonHeight` (110×28) (:102-108).
  - Captioned layout: sprite at `+ (127, 100)`; caption rect `+ (147, 110)` size `(textWidth, 20)` flags `AlignCenter | ColorYellow`; body rect `+ (147, 141)` size `(textWidth, 190)` flags `AlignCenter | ColorDialogWhite`; OK button at `+ (264, 335)` size 110×28 (:110-120).
  - OK button action is the global function pointer `&DialogActionOK`, which sets the file-static `dialogEnd = true` (:51-53) — callbacks must be plain funcs, no closures over the dialog instance.
  - `SDL_SetSurfaceClipRect(DiabloUiSurface(), nullptr)` before the loop (dialogs.cpp:204) — must reset clipping/viewport before drawing the dialog.
  - `static bool inDialog = false;` re-entrancy guard (:166).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: five file-static mutable globals: `ownedDialogSprite` (:46), `wrappedText` (:47), `dialogEnd` (:49), `vecNULL` (:56), `vecOkDialog` (:57) plus the function-local `static inDialog` (:166) — a single-dialog-per-process design; `vecOkDialog` is *appended* by `Init` and cleared by `Deinit`, so a nested dialog would duplicate items. `dialogEnd` is reset at the top of `DialogLoop` (:135) after the OK callback could have fired. The loop is wall-clock independent (no ticks) but depends on `UiFadeIn` being pumped per frame.
- Test coverage: none found (`UiErrorOkDialog` is called from appfat.cpp:65, msg.cpp:2749/2755, language.cpp:364, selhero.cpp:347 — all untested paths).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/dialog.go`; strategy — represent the modal as a `dialog` struct pushed onto a small UI-stack (replacing `inDialog`), with `Run(ctx)` as an Ebiten `Update`-driven state machine; `renderBehind` becomes a `func(*ebiten.Image)` closure so the caller's game/panel frame can be drawn first; OS message-box fallback maps to a Go dialog library or a log-only stub.
- Risks/open questions: `ui_fwd.h:34` declares `UiErrorOkDialog(caption, text, bool error = true)` and this file defines it (dialogs.cpp:217) — three overloads across two headers; the Go port needs one variadic/option-based signature. Also: does the Ebiten port want blocking modals (C++ `DialogLoop` blocks the game loop) or non-blocking state? Blocking matches 1:1 but conflicts with Ebiten's fixed-rate main loop.

### Source/DiabloUI/hero/selhero.cpp
- Purpose: The hero select/create/delete screen for both single-player and multiplayer: lists existing saves, class chooser, name entry, load-vs-new-game prompt, delete confirmation, and (single-player) the difficulty-selection hack that hands rendering over to selgame.
- Public API: `selhero_Init()`, `selhero_List_Init()` (selhero.h:8-9); `UiSelHeroSingDialog(fninfo, fncreate, fnremove, fnstats, _selhero_selections *dlgresult, uint32_t *saveNumber, _difficulty *difficulty)` and `UiSelHeroMultDialog(fninfo, fncreate, fnremove, fnstats, dlgresult, saveNumber)` (diabloui.h:88-89, defined :632/:646); globals `selhero_isMultiPlayer`, `selhero_endMenu` (selhero.h:6-7, defined :45-46) and `gfnHeroInfo` (declared diabloudi.h:84, defined :48) plus file-scope `gfnHeroCreate` (:49), `gfnHeroStats` (:50). Everything else is anonymous-namespace (~25 static functions listed at :69-79 forward decls).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (whole UI engine: `UiInitList`, `UiRenderItems`, `UiPollAndRender`, `UiClearScreen`, `UiFocusNavigationSelect/Esc/YesNo`, `UiGetHeroDialogSprite`, `LoadBackgroundArt`, `UiAddLogo`, `ArtBackground`, `DifficultyIndicator`, `SelectedItem`, `UiValidPlayerName`, `UiLoadBlackBackground`-style globals); `DiabloUI/ui_item.h` (UiArtText/UiImageClx/UiList/UiScrollbar/UiArtTextButton/UiEdit); `DiabloUI/scrollbar.h` (`LoadScrollBar`/`UnloadScrollBar`, `ArtScrollBarBackground/Thumb/Arrow`); `DiabloUI/dialogs.h` + `DiabloUI/selok.h` (`UiSelOkDialog`) + `DiabloUI/selyesno.h` (`UiSelHeroYesNoDialog`) + `DiabloUI/multi/selgame.h` (`selgame_GameSelection_Select`, `nDifficulty`); `pfile.h` (`pfile_ui_get_first_unused_save_num`, `MAX_CHARACTERS = 99` pfile.h:24); `tables/playerdat.hpp` (`GetPlayerDataForClass`, `GetNumPlayerClasses`, `PlayerData::className`); `player.h` (`HeroClass` incl. Warrior/Rogue/Sorcerer/Monk/Bard/Barbarian); `game_mode.hpp` (`gbIsHellfire`, `HaveBardAssets`, `HaveBarbarianAssets`) and `init.hpp`/`options.h` (`GetOptions().Gameplay.testBard/testBarbarian`); `levels/gendung.h`/`gendung_defs.hpp` (`DIFF_LAST = DIFF_HELL`, gendung_defs.hpp:44); `controls/control_mode.hpp` (`ControlMode`, `ControlTypes`); `utils/language.h` (`_`, `FormatRuntime`), `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat`), `utils/utf8.hpp` (`CopyUtf8`), `utils/format.hpp`, `utils/sdl_geometry.h` (`MakeSdlRect`), `utils/enum_traits.h`, `engine/assets.hpp`, `engine/point.hpp`, `diablo.h` (`nDifficulty` via selgame.h:7).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - **State cache**: enumerate saves by invoking `gfnHeroInfo(SelHeroGetHeroInfo)` where the callback copies each `_uiheroinfo` into `selhero_heros[selhero_SaveCount++]` and returns true; then `std::reverse` the array so newest-first (:490-492).
  - `selhero_Init`: load `ui_art\selhero` background and insert its `UiImageClx` at the front of `vecSelHeroDialog`, add animated logo, load scrollbar art, reset count, enumerate + reverse heroes, build the title (`UiArtText` with a **pointer to the mutable `title` string**, so changing `title` re-renders), the hero portrait image (which the global raw pointer `SELHERO_DIALOG_HERO_IMG` keeps live), and the Level/Strength/Magic/Dexterity/Vitality label+value pairs (`_DEBUG` builds add "Savegame:").
  - `selhero_List_Init`: build "Select Hero" heading, one `UiListItem` per save (name + index i) plus a trailing "New Hero" item whose value == `selhero_SaveCount`, `selectedItem` = the index whose `saveNumber` equals the current `selhero_heroInfo.saveNumber`; list of max 6 viewport rows, scrollbar, and OK / Delete (disabled) / Cancel text buttons; `UiInitList(SelheroListFocus, SelheroListSelect, SelheroListEsc, items, wraps=false, fullscreen=nullptr, fnYesNo=SelheroListDeleteYesNo, selectedItem)`; then set `title` per MP/SP.
  - `SelheroListFocus(value)`: if value indexes a real save → `memcpy` it into `selhero_heroInfo`, refresh stats, enable/gold the Delete button, `selhero_isSavegame = true`; else show the "empty" portrait (`UiGetHeroDialogSprite(GetNumPlayerClasses())`), set all six stat strings to `"--"`, grey+disable Delete, `isSavegame = false`.
  - `SelheroSetStats`: set portrait sprite from `heroclass` and write level/str/mag/dex/vit/saveNumber as UTF-8 into the fixed 4-byte `textStats[6]` cells via `CopyUtf8(StrCat(...))`.
  - `RenderDifficultyIndicators` (called from the main render loop): only when `selhero_isSavegame`, tile `(*DifficultyIndicator)[0]` at `heroImg.x+1`, `heroImg.y + h - indicatorH - 1`, one per rank, `for i in 0..DIFF_LAST` but break when `i >= herorank`, advancing `rect.x += width`.
  - Class chooser screen (`SelheroListSelect(selhero_SaveCount)`): "Choose Class" heading, list of classes filtered by engine/asset availability (Monk needs Hellfire; Bard needs `HaveBardAssets()||testBard`; Barbarian needs `HaveBarbarianAssets()||testBarbarian`), `itemH = 33` or `26` when >4 classes, viewport = min(count, 6), vertical centring formula, scrollbar, OK/Cancel; `memset` name, `saveNumber = pfile_ui_get_first_unused_save_num()`, `isSavegame = false`, title = "New … Hero".
  - `SelheroClassSelectorFocus`: pull default stats from `gfnHeroStats(heroClass, &defaults)` and write level=1/class/4 stats, refresh portrait+stats.
  - `SelheroClassSelectorSelect`: spawn-locked classes (Rogue/Sorcerer, and Bard without assets) → remove background, show `UiSelOkDialog` purchase message, restore background, re-open class chooser; otherwise set title, clear name, optionally prefill a generated name, and open the "Enter Name" screen with a `UiEdit` bound directly to `selhero_heroInfo.name` (max length 15, `allowEmpty=false`).
  - Name screen: `UiInitList(nullptr, SelheroNameSelect, SelheroNameEsc, items)` (no focus callback → list focus disabled).
  - `SelheroNameSelect`: in multiplayer only, validate with `UiValidPlayerName` and on failure show OK dialog and re-ask; else `gfnHeroCreate(&selhero_heroInfo)` → success goes to "Load Game/New Game" via `SelheroLoadSelect(1)`, failure shows "Unable to create character." over `vecSelHeroDialog` and returns to class selection with the name cleared.
  - Load/New prompt (`SelheroListSelect` when `hassaved`): "Save File Exists", two items (Load Game=0, New Game=1), OK/Cancel, `UiInitList(SelheroLoadFocus /*no-op*/, SelheroLoadSelect, selhero_List_Init, …)`; title set to "Single Player Characters".
  - `SelheroLoadSelect(value)`: `UiInitList_clear()` + `selhero_endMenu = true`; item 0 → `SELHERO_CONTINUE`; item 1 → (SP only) the selgame hand-off: clear `endMenu`, clear `isSavegame`, `SelheroFree()`, `LoadBackgroundArt("ui_art\\selgame")`, `selgame_GameSelection_Select(0)`, then `selhero_result = SELHERO_NEW_DUNGEON`.
  - Delete flow: `SelheroListDeleteYesNo` returns/stores `selhero_navigateYesNo = selhero_isSavegame`; the delete button routes through `SelheroUiFocusNavigationYesNo` → `UiFocusNavigationYesNo`; when `selhero_navigateYesNo` breaks the render loop, `UiSelHeroDialog` builds "Delete {Single,Multi} Player Hero" + `Are you sure you want to delete the character "{:s}"?`, calls `UiSelHeroYesNoDialog`, and on yes invokes `fnremove(&selhero_heroInfo)`, then re-runs the whole init loop.
  - Driver `UiSelHeroDialog`: assign the three callbacks + `selhero_result = *dlgresult`; loop { init; if saves exist, pre-select the entry matching `*saveNumber` and show the list, else show class chooser; run render loop while `!selhero_endMenu && !selhero_navigateYesNo`; free; handle delete confirm } until the user stops saying yes; write back `*dlgresult` and `*saveNumber`.
  - `UiSelHeroSingDialog` sets `selhero_isMultiPlayer = false` then, after the dialog returns, writes `*difficulty = nDifficulty` (global difficulty chosen by selgame). `UiSelHeroMultDialog` sets it true.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Layout offsets (all relative to `GetUIRectangle().position` unless noted): title rect `+ (24, 161)` size `590×35` flags `AlignCenter|FontSize30|ColorUiSilver` spacing 3 (:498); portrait `+ (30, 211)` size `180×76` (:502); labels `labelX = x+39`, `valueX = x+159`, `labelWidth 110`, `valueWidth 40`, `statHeight 21`, first row `y+323`, then each subsequent row `statY += 21` starting `y+358` (:508-529); "Choose Class"/"Save File Exists"/"Enter Name"/"Select Hero" heading rect `+ (242, 211)` size `365×33`, `FontSize30|ColorUiSilver|AlignCenter`, spacing 3 (:168, :222, :307, :538); class list at `+ (264, itemY)` size `320×itemH` (`33`/`26`), `AlignCenter|FontSize24|ColorUiGold`, viewport `min(count,6)` (:197); `itemY = 246 + ((176 - min(count,6)*itemH)/2)` (:196); class scrollbar `+ (585, 244)` size `25×178` (:199-200); hero list at `+ (265, 285)` size `320×33` (:227) and in `selhero_List_Init` at `+ (265, 256)` size `320×26` viewport 6 (:546); load-screen OK `+ (279, 427)` `140×35`, Cancel `+ (429, 427)` `144×35` with `VerticalCenter` (:229-233); class/name-screen OK `+ (279, 429)` `140×35`, Cancel `+ (429, 429)` `144×35` (:202-206, :312-316); list-screen OK `+ (239, 429)` `120×35`, Delete `+ (364, 429)` `120×35`, Cancel `+ (489, 429)` `144×35` (:552-561); `UiEdit` rect `+ (265, 317)` size `320×33`, maxLength **15**, allowEmpty **false**, flags `FontSize24|ColorUiGold` (:310); difficulty indicator origin `heroImg.x + 1`, `heroImg.y + heroImg.h - height - 1` (:113-118).
  - `selhero_heros[MAX_CHARACTERS]` with `MAX_CHARACTERS = 99` (:55, pfile.h:24) — buffer size is a hard cap on the enumeration callback.
  - `textStats[6][4]` (:57) → each stat renders in ≤3 characters (`CopyUtf8` truncation is the real behaviour for values >999).
  - `--` is the empty-slot string (:150-151).
  - Portrait fallback slot: `UiGetHeroDialogSprite(GetNumPlayerClasses())` (:148) ↔ diabloudi.cpp:639-641 (`3`, or `5` when ≥6 portraits).
  - Random name: static `Names[6][10]` table in class order Warrior, Rogue, Sorcerer, Monk, Bard(=Rogue names), Barbarian (:396-475, e.g. "Aidan"…,"Rothat"; "Moreina"…,"Elexa"; "Jazreth"…,"Horazon"; "Akyev"…,"Zhota"; "Alaric"…,"Ulf" incl. `Qual-Kehk`), and `const int iRand = rand() % 10;` returned as `Names[heroClass % 6][iRand]` (:477-479) — **C `rand()`, unseeded**, not the game RNG.
  - Class filter rules (:180-192): Monk requires Hellfire; Bard requires assets or `testBard`; Barbarian requires assets or `testBarbarian`; spawn blocks Rogue/Sorcerer/Bard-without-assets at selection time (:292).
  - Prefill name when `ControlMode != KeyboardAndMouse`, or always under `PREFILL_PLAYER_NAME` (:267-274).
  - `saveNumber` for a new hero = `pfile_ui_get_first_unused_save_num()` (:210).
  - Delete-dialog buffers: `char dialogTitle[128]`, `char dialogText[256]`, `CopyUtf8` for the title, `strcpy` for the formatted body (:614-621).
  - `selhero_heroInfo = {}` then linear search for `saveNumber == *saveNumber` and `memcpy` of the whole struct (:591-598).
  - The 4-way `_selhero_selections` results: `SELHERO_PREVIOUS` on list Esc (:245), `SELHERO_CONTINUE` on Load (:384), `SELHERO_NEW_DUNGEON` on New (:394); `SELHERO_CONNECT` is never set here (multiplayer path uses it via the caller).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: heavy mutable global state — `selhero_SaveCount`, `selhero_heros[99]`, `selhero_heroInfo`, `textStats`, `title` (a `const char*` **aliased by a UI item's `const char**` text pointer**, so mutation is read at render time — the Go port must reproduce live-text binding), `selhero_result`, `selhero_navigateYesNo`, `selhero_isSavegame`, three item vectors, and two raw item pointers `SELHERO_DIALOG_HERO_IMG`/`SELLIST_DIALOG_DELETE_BUTTON` pointing into those vectors (dangling if the vectors are cleared without re-init). The "dangerous hack" (:378-393) makes selhero's own render loop draw selgame's items via the global `gUiItems`/`gUiList` in diabloudi.cpp — order-of-init and clear coupling between the two screens must be preserved exactly. `rand()` use is unseeded → the *same* suggested name sequence every run within a process; must not be switched to the deterministic game RNG if 1:1 matters.
- Test coverage: none found (`test/writehero_test.cpp` covers save writing, not this UI).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/selhero.go` (or `internal/menu/selhero`) with a `selheroState` struct owning the item lists and stat strings; strategy — replace the global raw item pointers with typed fields (`heroImage *uiImageClx`, `deleteButton *uiArtTextButton`) kept on the state object; replace the callback triad with a `HeroStore` interface (`Enumerate(func(*HeroInfo) bool)`, `Create(*HeroInfo) error`, `Remove(*HeroInfo)`, `DefaultStats(HeroClass) Stats`) so pfile/MP callers implement it; keep the selgame hand-off as an explicit state transition rather than the shared-global hack, and make `rand()` a named `suggestNameRand` source so the difference is visible.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `char name[16]` vs `PlayerNameLength=32` — decide the Go `HeroInfo.Name` width and where truncation happens (selhero.cpp uses the buffer size via `memset`/`strcpy` + `UiEdit` maxLength 15). (2) `selhero_heros` overflow if `gfnHeroInfo` yields >99 entries (C++ has no bound check at :132). (3) Does the Go port keep the difficulty-selection hack, or refactor selgame into its own state machine (this changes `UiSelHeroSingDialog`'s `*difficulty` output path)? (4) `nDifficulty` is a selgame global read after the dialog — needs a Go home.

### Source/DiabloUI/hero/selhero.h

### Source/DiabloUI/mainmenu.cpp
- Purpose: The main menu screen: builds the item list, background, logo and version string, maps selection to `_mainmenu_selections`, handles Esc→"Exit" item, and implements the attract-mode (intro) timeout.
- Public API: `bool UiMainMenuDialog(const char *name, _mainmenu_selections *pdwResult, int attractTimeOut)` (diabloui.h:85, mainmenu.cpp:108) and `void mainmenu_restart_repintro()` (diabloui.h:127, :103). Everything else is anonymous-namespace (`UiMainMenuSelect`, `MainmenuEsc`, `MainmenuLoad`, `MainmenuFree`).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (`UiClearScreen`, `UiPollAndRender`, `UiInitList`, `UiAddBackground`, `UiAddLogo`, `SelectedItem`, `ArtBackgroundWidescreen`, `ArtBackground`, `LoadBackgroundArt`, `LoadOptionalClx` via engine/load_clx.hpp, `UiFocusNavigationSelect` indirectly through list callbacks); `DiabloUI/ui_item.h` (`UiListItem`, `UiList`, `UiArtText`); `ui_flags.hpp` (`FontSize30/42`, `ColorUiSilver`, `ColorUiGold`, `ColorUiSilverDark`, `AlignCenter`); `engine/assets.hpp` (link-time asset availability), `engine/point.hpp`; `game_mode.hpp` (`gbIsSpawn`, `gbIsHellfire`, `HaveIntro()`); `utils/language.h` (`_`), `utils/ui_fwd.h` (`GetUIRectangle`, `gnScreenHeight`); `DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp` + SDL timers (`SDL_GetTicks`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Six (five with `NOEXIT`, plus a hidden attract entry) list items in fixed order: Single Player, Multi Player, Settings, Support, Show Credits, then Exit Hellfire/Exit Diablo (value `MAINMENU_EXIT_DIABLO`), each carrying its `_mainmenu_selections` enum as `m_value`; the list's select callback copies `vecMenuItems[value].m_value` into the result global.
  - Background choice: if `!gbIsSpawn || gbIsSpawn&&gbIsHellfire` → optional widescreen `ui_art\mainmenuw.clx` + `ui_art\mainmenu`; else spawn-only → `ui_art\swmmenu` (no widescreen). Then `UiAddBackground` + `UiAddLogo` push the image items.
  - Spawn+Hellfire only: an extra centered "Shareware" `UiArtText` line.
  - The version/name string is drawn bottom-left from the `name` argument, and the menu list plus callbacks are registered via `UiInitList(nullptr, UiMainMenuSelect, MainmenuEsc|nullptr, items, wraps=true)`.
  - Attract loop: `mainmenu_restart_repintro()` sets `dwAttractTicks = SDL_GetTicks() + timeout*1000`; it is called from `UiMainMenuDialog` before the inner loop *and* from diabloudi.cpp's `UiFocusNavigation` on any activity event, so user input continuously defers the intro. The inner loop renders and, once `SDL_GetTicks() >= dwAttractTicks` and (`HaveIntro() || gbIsHellfire`), forces `MAINMENU_ATTRACT_MODE`.
  - Outer loop reloads the whole screen until a result ≠ `MAINMENU_NONE`, freeing art and item vectors between iterations; `UiMainMenuDialog` always returns true.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Item creation order and values: `MAINMENU_SINGLE_PLAYER, MAINMENU_MULTIPLAYER, MAINMENU_SETTINGS, MAINMENU_SHOW_SUPPORT, MAINMENU_SHOW_CREDITS, MAINMENU_EXIT_DIABLO` (mainmenu.cpp:53-60) — note the enum ordinals in diabloudi.h:37-46 list SETTINGS after SHOW_SUPPORT, while the *menu order* puts Settings before Support; only `m_value` matters for behaviour, but the visible order must match.
  - List geometry: `UiList(vecMenuItems, viewport = vecMenuItems.size(), x = uiPosition.x + 64, y = uiPosition.y + 192, w = 510, h = 43, flags = FontSize42|ColorUiGold|AlignCenter, spacing = 5)` (:79).
  - Shareware label rect `{uiPosition.x, uiPosition.y + 145, 640, 30}` with `FontSize30|ColorUiSilver|AlignCenter`, spacing 8 (:75-76).
  - Version string rect `{17, gnScreenHeight - 36, 605, 21}` (absolute x, screen-relative y) with `FontSize12|ColorUiSilverDark`, spacing 1 default (:81-82).
  - Esc behaviour: `last = vecMenuItems.size() - 1`; if `SelectedItem == last` select it (quit), else move focus to last (:40-49).
  - Attract timeout arithmetic: `dwAttractTicks = SDL_GetTicks() + mainmenu_attract_time_out * 1000` (seconds→ms) (:105) and the trigger predicate `SDL_GetTicks() >= dwAttractTicks && (HaveIntro() || gbIsHellfire)` (:120).
  - Assets: `ui_art\mainmenuw.clx`, `ui_art\mainmenu`, `ui_art\swmmenu` (:62-67).
  - `NOEXIT` build flag removes the Exit item and the esc callback (:39, :58, :84-88).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: three anonymous globals — `mainmenu_attract_time_out` (seconds, uninitialized until `UiMainMenuDialog` sets it, but `mainmenu_restart_repintro()` may be called by diabloudi.cpp *before* that on other screens → reads 0 statically-initialised), `dwAttractTicks`, `MainMenuResult`, plus the two item vectors and `vecMenuItems` values. Wall-clock based (`SDL_GetTicks`), and `mainmenu_restart_repintro` is invoked from the shared UI event path, so the timer is global across all DiabloUI screens. `MainMenuResult` is written by the list callback during `UiPollAndRender`, read in the loops — a single-threaded handoff.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/mainmenu.go` — a `MainMenu` type with `Result()`, `RestartAttractTimer()` (called from the shared event pump), and an `Update()` that Ebiten calls; strategy — the attract timeout maps directly onto `time.Since(start)`, and the "reload the screen until a result" outer loop becomes a state that rebuilds the item list on re-entry.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `name` is a `const char *` version string owned by the caller while `UiArtText` stores the pointer — Go must keep a live text binding (same problem as selhero `title`). (2) Does the Go port keep attract-mode/intro movies at all (movie.cpp is out of this batch)?

### Source/DiabloUI/multi/selconn.cpp
- Purpose: "Select Connection" modal dialog: list the available network providers (ZeroTier / TCP / offline), show a per-provider description and max-player count, and on OK initialise the chosen provider. Entry point `UiSelectProvider`.
- Public API: `int provider;` (file-global, line 26 — the selected `conn_type`, read by selgame.cpp via `extern int provider`); `const char *ConnectionNames[] {"ZeroTier", N_("Client-Server (TCP)"), N_("Offline")}` (lines 27-31, indexable by `SELCONN_*`); `bool UiSelectProvider(GameData *gameData)` (lines 157-170, blocks until menu ends, returns true always unless cancelled path is added — see Risks). Namespace-internal (anonymous namespace, so not linkable): `SelconnLoad` (52-104), `SelconnFree` (106-113), `SelconnEsc` (115-119), `SelconnFocus(size_t)` (121-141), `SelconnSelect(size_t)` (143-151); file-scope statics `selconn_MaxPlayers[64]`, `selconn_Description[256]`, `selconn_Gateway[129]`, `selconn_ReturnValue`, `selconn_EndMenu`, `GameData *selconn_GameData`, `vecConnItems`, `vecSelConnDlg` (36-43); `#define DESCRIPTION_WIDTH 205` (46).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (`LoadBackgroundArt`, `UiAddBackground`, `UiAddLogo`, `UiInitList`, `UiClearScreen`, `UiPollAndRender`, `UiFocusNavigationSelect`, `UiFocusNavigationEsc`, `ArtBackground`, `GetUIRectangle`, `DiabloUiSurface`); `DiabloUI/ui_item.h` (`UiListItem`, `UiArtText`, `UiArtTextButton`, `UiList`, `UiItemBase`); `DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp`; `storm/storm_net.hpp` (`SNetInitializeProvider(uint32_t provider, GameData*)`, `conn_type` enum SELCONN_ZT=0/SELCONN_TCP=1/SELCONN_LOOPBACK=2, storm_net.hpp:15-19); `multi.h` (`MAX_PLRS 4`, multi.h:26, `GameData` via game_mode.hpp); `engine/render/text_render.hpp` (`WordWrapString`, `FormatRuntime` usage); `utils/utf8.hpp` (`CopyUtf8`); `utils/language.h` (`_()`, `N_()`); `utils/ui_fwd.h`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Provider-selection screen with a list of exactly the items built at lines 56-61 under the same build flags: ZeroTier entry first (unless `DISABLE_ZERO_TIER`), then TCP (unless `DISABLE_TCP`), then Offline always (60). Item label = translated `ConnectionNames[i]`, item value = the `conn_type` numeric.
  - Layout must reproduce the 10 text/button widgets and the list, all offsets relative to `GetUIRectangle().position` (see 1:1 list).
  - On focus of item i: set `players` = MAX_PLRS for TCP/ZeroTier, 1 for Offline (123-136); write description string per provider (126/129/132); then write `"Players Supported: {N}"` (translated, `FormatRuntime`) into `selconn_MaxPlayers` (139); then word-wrap `selconn_Description` to width 205 in place (140).
  - `selconn_Gateway` buffer exists and is rendered (rect6, line 86-87) but is never written in this file — port as an always-empty field unless gateway support is added.
  - "Change Gateway" `UiArtTextButton` created with `nullptr` action and `UiFlags::ElementHidden` (92-93): present but invisible/inert.
  - On OK (`SelconnSelect`): store chosen value in global `provider` (145), free the dialog art, call `SNetInitializeProvider(provider, selconn_GameData)` (149) and set `selconn_EndMenu` to its result, then rebuild the dialog (150). Note ordering: free → init provider → reload; the provider init itself opens the hero dialog (`storm_net.cpp:141` → `mainmenu_select_hero_dialog`), i.e. a nested UI loop runs inside the OK handler.
  - Escape (ESC / cancel button) sets `ReturnValue=false`, `EndMenu=true` (115-119).
  - `UiSelectProvider`: assign gameData pointer, load, then loop `UiClearScreen(); UiPollAndRender();` until `EndMenu` (163-167), free, return `selconn_ReturnValue`.
  - Background asset `ui_art\selconn` loaded on open and released (`ArtBackground = std::nullopt`) on free (54, 108).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `DESCRIPTION_WIDTH = 205` (46).
  - Buffer sizes: MaxPlayers 64, Description 256, Gateway 129 (36-38).
  - Rects (x+off, y+off, w, h) relative to uiPosition: rect1 (24,161,590,35) title "Multi Player Game", AlignCenter|FontSize30|ColorUiSilver, spacing 3 (71-72); rect2 (35,218,205,21) MaxPlayers, FontSize12|ColorUiSilverDark (74-75); rect3 (35,256,205,21) "Requirements:" (77-78); rect4 (35,275,205,66) description, FontSize12|ColorUiSilverDark, spacing 1, lineHeight 16 (80-81); rect5 (30,356,220,31) "no gateway needed", AlignCenter|FontSize24|ColorUiSilver, spacing 0 (83-84); rect6 (35,393,205,21) gateway, AlignCenter|FontSize12|ColorUiSilverDark (86-87); rect7 (300,211,295,33) "Select Connection", AlignCenter|FontSize30|ColorUiSilver, spacing 3 (89-90); rect8 (16,427,250,35) "Change Gateway" AlignCenter|VerticalCenter|FontSize30|ColorUiGold|ElementHidden (92-93); UiList at x=305,y=256,w=285,h=26, viewport size = vecConnItems.size(), flags AlignCenter|FontSize12|VerticalCenter|ColorUiGoldDark, spacing default 1 (95); rect9 (299,427,140,35) "OK" → UiFocusNavigationSelect (97-98); rect10 (454,427,144,35) "Cancel" → UiFocusNavigationEsc (100-101).
  - Push order into `vecSelConnDlg` is exactly: background, logo, rect1..rect10 with UiList between rect8 and rect9 (64-101) — z-order/iteration order matters for render and mouse hit-testing.
  - `UiInitList(focus, select, esc, items, wraps=true)` (103).
  - Description strings verbatim (126,129,132) and "Players Supported: {:d}" (139); wrap order = format maxplayers, then wrap description (139-140).
  - `ConnectionNames[SELCONN_ZT]` label is NOT translated (raw `N_` string, line 57); TCP and Offline labels ARE translated (60, 57-61).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable globals `provider`, `selconn_*` flags, and the two item vectors persist across opens; `vecConnItems`/`vecSelConnDlg` are only cleared in `SelconnFree` — double-load would duplicate list items. `selconn_ReturnValue` is set true right after load (162), so a Cancel returns false; loop condition reads `selconn_EndMenu` mutated only by handlers on the UI thread. No RNG, no serialization. All work is single-threaded on the UI loop.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln selconn test/` → no match).
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/multi` (or `internal/menu/selconn`) — one screen type implementing the shared UI-screen interface, with provider list as data (`[]Provider{Name, Desc, MaxPlayers}`) and `SNetInitializeProvider` mapped to `net.InitializeProvider(ctx, providerID, *GameData)`. Keep the global `provider` as a package-level var or a field on the app/session state, since selgame reads it.
- Risks/open questions: The nested `SNetInitializeProvider` → hero-dialog re-entrancy is easy to lose in a port (Go must allow a blocking sub-dialog from within an OK callback). `selconn_Gateway`/`selconn_Description` are `char` buffers filled by `CopyUtf8`; in Go use fixed-size byte arrays only if byte-exactness matters (it doesn't — purely display), so `string` is fine. ZeroTier build flags must be mirrored or the item list order changes.

  - Byte order: GameData is serialised big-endian for the wire — `SwapGameDataLE` swaps `size`, `programid`, `gameSeed[0..3]` only (multi.cpp:86-94); `gameTemplateSize` must equal `sizeof(GameData)` (storm_net.cpp:152-153 ABORTs otherwise).
  - Refresh timers (`static uint32_t lastRequest`, `lastUpdate`, 700-701, both 0-initialised): skip entirely when `selgame_enteringGame` (703-705); send request when `lastRequest==0 || currentTime-lastRequest > 30000` AND `DvlNet_SendInfoRequest()` returns true, then `lastRequest = currentTime`, `lastUpdate = currentTime - 3000`, and set `firstPublicGameInfoRequestSend` once (708-713); rebuild list when `lastUpdate==0 || currentTime-lastUpdate > 5000` (715): capture highlighted game name as `gameSearch` from `vecSelGameDlgItems[HighlightedItem]->m_value - 3`, replace `Gamelist` with `DvlNet_GetGamelist()` element-by-element, re-run `UiInitGameSelectionList(gameSearch)` (716-722).
  - `SDL_GetTicks()` uint32 wrap arithmetic is relied on for all three timers — port must keep unsigned 32-bit modular subtraction.
  - `UiSelectGame` ordering (728-751): reset `firstPublicGameInfoRequestSend=0` → set `gdwPlayerId`/`m_game_data` → `selgame_Init()` (loads `ui_art\selgame` + scrollbar) → `HighlightedItem=0` → `selgame_GameSelection_Init()` → `selgame_endMenu=false` → `DvlNet_ClearPassword()` → `DvlNet_ClearGamelist()` → loop {UiClearScreen; UiPollAndRender; if ZT RefreshGameList} → `selgame_Free()` → return `selgame_enteringGame`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: very large amount of cross-screen mutable file-scope state (`selgame_selectedGame`, `enteringGame`, `endMenu`, `HighlightedItem`, `Gamelist`, `title`, `nDifficulty`, `nTickRate`, `heroLevel`, `m_game_data`, `gdwPlayerId`) that the screens read each other's values of — the source even flags this ("dangerous hack", "Dialogs should not refer to each other's variables", FIXME at 437-439). `RefreshGameList`'s two static locals persist between `UiSelectGame` calls and are only neutralised by the `firstPublicGameInfoRequestSend` reset at 730; `lastRequest`/`lastUpdate` are NOT reset. `vecSelGameDlgItems`/`vecSelGameDialog` are shared across all screens and cleared via `selgame_FreeVectors()` — every screen transition must clear first or items duplicate. `UpdateHeroLevel` mutates `heroLevel` from a callback driven by `gfnHeroInfo`. No RNG. Network calls (`SNetJoinGame`/`SNetCreateGame`) are blocking and mutate `*gdwPlayerId`. Reading `Gamelist[...]` with a stale `HighlightedItem` after a list shrink is guarded only by the clamp at 199-202.
- Test coverage: none found (`test/` has no selgame/selconn/DiabloUI tests; only `test/animationinfo_test.cpp` mentions "progress" in an unrelated comment).
- Go mapping: `internal/menu/selgame` (Go-side package for the game-selection state machine) plus a `pkg/net`/`internal/net` façade exposing `InitializeProvider`, `CreateGame`, `JoinGame`, `SendInfoRequest`, `GetGamelist`, `ClearGamelist`, `ClearPassword`. Strategy: model the 5 screens as explicit states with an injected `ScreenDeps` interface (dialogs, hero info, options, clock `Now() uint32`, net) so timers and the public-game list are testable; serialize GameData through a single `func (GameData) MarshalLE() []byte` that mirrors `SwapGameDataLE` and asserts `size == unsafe.Sizeof(GameData{})`-equivalent constant.
- Risks/open questions: (1) Go must replicate the `PACKET_ENCRYPTION` / `NONET` / `DISABLE_ZERO_TIER` conditional item set — otherwise item values shift and the `m_value-3` convention breaks. (2) The single-player difficulty-selection hijack of the selhero loop (441-480) has no clean Go analogue; needs a real "return difficulty to caller" design or the port will regress hero-select behaviour. (3) `SDL_GetError()`/`SDL_ClearError()` has no Go equivalent — replace with an explicit last-network-error string and confirm "Unknown network error" fallback stays. (4) `_difficulty`/`nTickRate` are stored as `uint8_t` in GameData but as `int`/enum in UI — check conversions at 668-669. (5) Whether to keep the 129-byte `strcpy` of IP into options (buffer size match required: options fields are `char[129]`, options.h:678/680).

### Source/DiabloUI/multi/selgame.h
- Purpose: Header declaring the cross-file entry points of selgame.cpp so selhero (single-player difficulty selection) can drive the same screens, and so `nDifficulty` can be read outside selgame.cpp.
- Public API: `extern _difficulty nDifficulty;` and 13 free-function declarations: `selgame_GameSelection_Init()`, `selgame_GameSelection_Focus(size_t)`, `selgame_GameSelection_Select(size_t)`, `selgame_GameSelection_Esc()`, `selgame_Diff_Focus(size_t)`, `selgame_Diff_Select(size_t)`, `selgame_Diff_Esc()`, `selgame_GameSpeedSelection()`, `selgame_Speed_Focus(size_t)`, `selgame_Speed_Select(size_t)`, `selgame_Speed_Esc()`, `selgame_Password_Init(size_t)`, `selgame_Password_Select(size_t)`, `selgame_Password_Esc()` (lines 8-23). Note `UiSelectGame`, `UpdateHeroLevel`, `RefreshGameList`, `IsDifficultyAllowed` are defined in the .cpp but NOT declared here.
- Depends on: `levels/gendung.h` (line 3) only for `_difficulty`; the enum actually lives in `Source/levels/gendung_defs.hpp:39-45` (DIFF_NORMAL=0, DIFF_NIGHTMARE=1, DIFF_HELL=2, DIFF_LAST=DIFF_HELL).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Export the same set of screen-transition operations from the Go selgame package so the hero-select code can call `DiffSelect`/`GameSpeedSelection`-equivalents (the single-player difficulty hack).
  - Expose the chosen difficulty as package-level/shared state (or better: return it), mirroring `extern _difficulty nDifficulty`.
  - Keep the `size_t value` callback convention (item index) so the UI-list plumbing lines up.
- 1:1 constraints: `nDifficulty` type is `enum _difficulty : uint8_t` (gendung_defs.hpp:39) — must be uint8 on the wire; the function signatures with `size_t`/no-arg forms are what the `UiInitList` callbacks expect (`void(*)(size_t)` / `void(*)()`, see diabloui.h:116).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: declares mutable shared globals; header itself has no state. `#pragma once`.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: fold into `internal/menu/selgame` as an exported API surface (methods on a `SelGame` struct rather than globals); drop the `#include "levels/gendung.h"` — in Go import only the difficulty enum package (`internal/levels` or `pkg/dungeon` type defs).
- Risks/open questions: The 1:1 shape (package-level funcs + shared globals) fights Go idiom; porting to a struct changes call sites in selhero — decide the target shape once for the whole DiabloUI rewrite.

### Source/DiabloUI/progress.cpp
- Purpose: Progress-bar dialog used during level-load/init: renders a popup frame + background bar, drives a caller-supplied progress callback per frame, and offers a Cancel button; returns whether the work completed.
- Public API: `bool UiProgressDialog(int (*fnfunc)())` (line 106). Everything else is in an anonymous namespace: `ArtPopupSm`, `ArtProgBG`, `ProgFil` (32-34), `vecProgress` (35), `endMenu` (36), `DialogActionCancel` (38), `ProgressLoadBackground` (43), `ProgressLoadForeground` (50), `ProgressFreeBackground` (60), `ProgressFreeForeground` (67), `GetPosition` (74), `ProgressRenderBackground` (79), `ProgressRenderForeground(int)` (89).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/button.h` (`LoadDialogButtonGraphics`, `FreeDialogButtonGraphics`, `ButtonSprite(bool pressed)`, `DialogButtonWidth=110`, `DialogButtonHeight=28`, button.h:8-13); `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (`UiLoadBlackBackground`, `UiRenderItems`, `UiItemMouseEvents`, `UiFadeIn`, `UiClearScreen`, `GetCenterOffset`, `ArtBackground`, `DiabloUiSurface`); `DiabloUI/ui_item.h` (`UiButton`); `engine/load_pcx.hpp` (`LoadPcx`); `engine/render/clx_render.hpp` (`RenderClxSprite`); `engine/surface.hpp` (`Surface`, `subregion`); `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` (`OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList`); `utils/display.h` (`gnScreenHeight`, `RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface`, `PalSurface`); `utils/sdl_compat.h` (`PollEvent`, `SDLC_EventKey`); `controls/input.h` + `controls/menu_controls.h` (`GetMenuActions`, `MenuAction_BACK/SELECT`); `utils/ui_fwd.h` (`GetUIRectangle`); `utils/language.h`; `utils/is_of.hpp` (`IsNoneOf`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two-phase asset loading: background phase loads black background + `ui_art\spopup` + `ui_art\prog_bg`, renders the static backdrop once, fades it in, then unconditionally frees those three (108-124) — the backdrop is then only present in the backbuffer.
  - Multi-backbuffer handling: if `RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface && PalSurface != nullptr`, capture `PalSurface->pixels` before `UiFadeIn()` and loop `{render backdrop; UiFadeIn();}` while `PalSurface->pixels != initialPixels` (113-120) — i.e. repaint the backdrop into every swap-chain buffer.
  - Foreground phase loads dialog-button graphics + `ui_art\prog_fil` and creates the single Cancel button (50-58) whose action sets `endMenu = true` (38-41).
  - Per-frame loop until `endMenu || progress >= 100` (131): `progress = fnfunc()`; render foreground (fill bar scaled by progress, then only the top 2 pixel rows of the button sprite, 89-103); `UiRenderItems(vecProgress)`; `DrawMouse()`; `UiFadeIn()`; then drain all pending events (138-168).
  - Event handling: mouse down/up → `UiItemMouseEvents(&event, vecProgress)`; key down → Escape/Return/KP_Enter/Space set `endMenu` (144-153, KP_Enter skipped under SDL1); any other event type → iterate `GetMenuActions(event)` and set `endMenu` for `MenuAction_BACK` or `MenuAction_SELECT` (158-165); every event additionally goes to `UiHandleEvents(&event)` (167).
  - Return value is `progress == 100` (171) — the caller distinguishes cancel from completion; free foreground before returning (169).
  - Progress callback contract: returns an int 0..100 and is called once per frame from the UI thread (132).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Dialog box size 280x140; position `{ GetCenterOffset(280), GetCenterOffset(144, gnScreenHeight) }` (76) — note x centred on 280 but the popup subregion height used is 140 (85).
  - Background bar width 227 at `GetCenterOffset(227)`, y = `position.y + 52` (86); `subregion(GetCenterOffset(227), 0, 227, out.h())` — the subregion starts at y=0 and the sprite is drawn at y+52 inside it.
  - Fill width formula: `w = 227 * progress / 100` (integer division), drawn only when `progress != 0` (93-96); same x/y convention as the background bar.
  - Button strip: `subregion(GetCenterOffset(110), position.y + 99, DialogButtonWidth, 2)` drawing `ButtonSprite(false)` at (0,0) (99-102) — 2 rows only, deliberate (comment 98).
  - Cancel button rect `(uiPosition.x + 265, uiPosition.y + 267, 110, 28)` (56) using `DialogButtonWidth/Height`.
  - PCX asset paths, verbatim: `"ui_art\\spopup"`, `"ui_art\\prog_bg"`, `"ui_art\\prog_fil"` (46-47, 53).
  - Loop order inside the frame: render → items → mouse → fade → poll (133-138); `endMenu` checked before `progress < 100` (131).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: globals `ArtPopupSm/ArtProgBG/ProgFil/vecProgress/endMenu` are file-scope anonymous-namespace statics reused across calls; `endMenu` is reset to false at 112 each call. `fnfunc` is called on the UI thread once per frame — if it is a game-init worker in Go, it must not race with the render loop. Depends on `PalSurface->pixels` pointer identity for the multi-buffer loop (SDL-specific, non-portable to Ebiten). No RNG, no tick coupling.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/progress` (or `internal/menu/progress`) with `UiProgressDialog(step func() int) bool`; assets via the MPQ/PCX→CLX loader in `pkg/mpq` + `internal/render`; the backbuffer repaint loop becomes "draw backdrop into every Ebiten game-graphics buffer once" or simply a persistent backdrop image — Ebiten has no `PalSurface->pixels` pointer, so replace with an explicit "paint backdrop once to the off-screen layer" step (behaviour-equivalent for single-buffer, needs a note for triple-buffering).
- Risks/open questions: Ebiten manages its own vsync/present; the "render into all backbuffers" loop (113-120) and `RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface` branch have no direct analogue — decide whether the backdrop is kept as a live image drawn each frame (simpler, visually identical) instead of a one-shot blit. `DrawMouse` is done by Ebiten's input layer.

Consumers: `selgame.cpp:138` (`LoadScrollBar`/`UnloadScrollBar` at 79-88 and the `UiScrollbar` construction) and the `UiScrollbar` renderer in `DiabloUI/diabloui.cpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:

  - Expose per-frame arrow sprites indexed by the `ScrollBarArrowFrame` enum (UP_ACTIVE=0, UP=1, DOWN_ACTIVE=2, DOWN=3, scrollbar.h:16-21).
  - Release all three (assign empty) in `UnloadScrollBar`, order arrow→thumb→bg (23-25).
  - Frames must be indexable as `[0]` by callers (selgame.cpp:138 uses `(*ArtScrollBarBackground)[0]`, `(*ArtScrollBarThumb)[0]`, `*ArtScrollBarArrow`).
- 1:1 constraints: exact asset names at lines 16-18 (backslash-escaped MPQ paths `"ui_art\\sb_bg"`, `"ui_art\\sb_thumb"`, `"ui_art\\sb_arrow"`); arrow frame count literal `4` (18); width constant `ScrollBarBgWidth = 25` and `ScrollBarArrowWidth = 25` live in the header (scrollbar.h:14/23).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: three mutable package-level globals; load/unload must be balanced or the `UiScrollbar` item will hold dangling sprite references (C++ stores raw `ClxSprite` views into the owned list — selgame.cpp:138 does exactly this, so the list must outlive the widget). No threads.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/render` (or `internal/uiauto/assets`) — `type ScrollBarArt struct { BG, Thumb []ClxSprite; Arrow []ClxSprite }` loaded by a `LoadScrollBar(mpq) (*ScrollBarArt, error)`; GC makes explicit unload unnecessary (set to nil for parity). Keep the shared-instance semantics if selhero/selgame screens reference it.
- Risks/open questions: In Go, `UiScrollbar` holding a slice reference plus a global that can be nil-ed is fine (GC), but if the port keeps C++-style manual "free", the widget must be rebuilt after unload.

### Source/DiabloUI/scrollbar.h
- Purpose: Declares scrollbar art globals, the arrow-frame enum, the fixed scrollbar widths, and the pure-geometry helpers that compute the track/thumb/arrow rectangles for a `UiScrollbar` item.
- Public API: `extern OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList ArtScrollBarBackground/ArtScrollBarArrow/ArtScrollBarThumb` (11-13); `constexpr Uint16 ScrollBarBgWidth = 25` (14); `enum ScrollBarArrowFrame : uint8_t { UP_ACTIVE, UP, DOWN_ACTIVE, DOWN }` (16-21); `constexpr Uint16 ScrollBarArrowWidth = 25` (23); inline functions `SDL_Rect UpArrowRect(const UiScrollbar&)` (25-32), `DownArrowRect(const UiScrollbar&)` (34-41), `Uint16 BarHeight(const UiScrollbar&)` (43-46), `SDL_Rect BarRect(const UiScrollbar&)` (48-54), `SDL_Rect ThumbRect(const UiScrollbar&, size_t selectedIndex, size_t numItems)` (57-68); `void LoadScrollBar(); void UnloadScrollBar();` (70-71).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/ui_item.h` for `UiScrollbar` (fields `m_rect`, `m_bg`, `m_thumb`, `m_arrow`, ui_item.h:210-224); `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` (`ClxSprite::height()`, `ClxSpriteList`); `utils/sdl_geometry.h` (`MakeSdlRect`); `<cstdint>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Provide identical rect math for scrollbar drawing and hit-testing: up arrow at the top of `m_rect` with width 25 and height = arrow sprite height; down arrow at `y + h - arrowH`; track from `y + arrowH` with height `h - 2*arrowH`, width 25.
  - Thumb placement: `thumbMaxY = BarHeight - thumbHeight`; `thumbY = selectedIndex * thumbMaxY / (numItems - 1)` (integer division); thumb rect x = `m_rect.x + 3`, w = `m_rect.w - 3`, h = thumb height, y = `m_rect.y + arrowH + thumbY`.
  - Arrow frames selected by the 4-value enum (active/normal up/down) — the renderer consumes `m_arrow[frame]`.
- 1:1 constraints: widths 25/25 (14, 23); `ThumbOffsetX = 3` (59); thumb formula `selectedIndex * thumbMaxY / (numItems - 1)` (61) — exact integer truncation, division by zero when `numItems == 1` (C++ UB: callers must guarantee >1); thumb width is `m_rect.w - 3` (66) not `ScrollBarArrowWidth`; `BarHeight` returns `Uint16` (43) so a negative intermediate would wrap.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: header-only geometry, no state except the extern art globals. Pure functions of (rect, sprite heights, index, count) — trivially deterministic; `numItems-1` underflow with `numItems==0` (size_t → huge divisor → thumbY 0) is a latent edge case to preserve or fix deliberately.
- Test coverage: none found (`test/rectangle_test.cpp` covers `Rectangle` helpers only, not scrollbar geometry).
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/widget` (or `internal/render/scrollbar`) — free functions taking a `Scrollbar` struct `{Rect image.Rectangle; BG, Thumb ClxSprite; Arrow [4]ClxSprite}` and returning `image.Rectangle`s; arithmetic in `int` avoids the Uint16 wrap.
- Risks/open questions: Decide whether to guard `numItems <= 1` (Go panics on div-by-zero — must add an explicit branch rather than UB). `ScrollBarBgWidth` is declared but unused in these 12 files — check the renderer in `diabloui.cpp` before dropping it.

### Source/DiabloUI/settingsmenu.cpp
- Purpose: The Settings UI: a 5-level nested menu (Categories → Settings → ListOption / KeyInput / PadInput) built entirely from the options table, with a wrapped description pane, scrollbar, two-line option rows, key rebinding and a gamepad button-combo capture with a 10 s timeout. Entry point `UiSettingsMenu()`.
- Public API: `void UiSettingsMenu()` (362–583) — the only link-visible symbol. Anonymous namespace (47–360): `constexpr size_t IndexKeyOrPadInput = 1` (49), `IndexPadTimerText = 2` (50); globals `endMenu`, `backToMain` (52–53), `vecDialogItems`/`vecDialog`/`vecOptions` (55–57), `selectedCategory` (58), `selectedOption` (59), `ShownMenuType shownMenu` (61–69), `char optionDescription[512]` (71), `rectList`/`rectDescription` (73–74), `padEntryCombo`/`padEntryStartTime`/`padEntryTimerText` (84–86); `enum class SpecialMenuEntry : int8_t {None=-1, PreviousMenu=-2, UnbindKey=-3, BindPadButton=-4, UnbindPadButton=-5}` (76–82); helpers `IsValidEntry` (88), `CreateDrawStringFormatArgForEntry` (96), `NeedsTwoLinesToDisplayOption` (105), `CleanUpSettingsUI` (110), `GoBackOneMenuLevel` (123), `StartPadEntryTimer` (139), `StopPadEntryTimer` (150), `UpdatePadEntryTimerText` (161), `UpdateDescription` ×2 (174, 180), `ItemFocused` (186), `ChangeOptionValue` (210), `ItemSelected` (246), `EscPressed` (335), `FullscreenChanged` (340).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (`UiInitList`, `UiInitList_clear`, `UiClearScreen`, `UiPollAndRender`, `UiLoadBlackBackground`, `UiAddBackground`, `UiAddLogo`, `UnloadUiGFX`, `SelectedItem`, `ArtBackground`, `ArtBackgroundWidescreen`); `DiabloUI/scrollbar.h` (`LoadScrollBar`, `UnloadScrollBar`, `ArtScrollBarBackground/Thumb/Arrow`); `ui_item.h`/`ui_flags.hpp` (`UiListItem`, `UiList`, `UiArtText`, `UiScrollbar`); `options.h` (`GetOptions()`, `OptionEntryBase`, `OptionCategoryBase`, `OptionEntryBoolean`, `OptionEntryListBase`, `OptionEntryType`, `OptionEntryFlags::{Invisible,OnlyDiablo,OnlyHellfire,NeedDiabloMpq,RecreateUI}`, `SaveOptions()`, `GetOptions().Graphics.fullscreen`); `game_mode.hpp` (`gbIsHellfire`); `engine/assets.hpp` (`HaveIntro`); `engine/render/text_render.hpp` (`GetLineWidth`, `WordWrapString`, `DrawStringFormatArg`, `GameFontTables::GameFont24`, `GameFont12`); `controls/{controller,controller_buttons,controller_motion,plrctrls,remap_keyboard}.h` (`ControllerButton_NONE/IGNORE`, `ControllerButtonEvent`, `ToControllerButtonEvents`, `IsControllerMotion`, `DetectInputMethod`, `IsControllerButtonPressed`, `remap_keyboard_key`); `controls/keymapper.hpp` (`KeymapperOptions::Action`, `KeymapperMouseButtonMask` at 469, `MouseScroll{Up,Down,Left,Right}Button`), `controls/padmapper.hpp` (`PadmapperOptions::Action`); `items.h` (`FreeItemGFX`); `hwcursor.hpp` (`SetHardwareCursor`, `CursorInfo::UnknownCursor`); `utils/ui_fwd.h` (`gnScreenWidth/Height`); `utils/language.h` (`_`, `IsSmallFontTall`); `utils/utf8.hpp` (`CopyUtf8`), `str_cat.hpp`, `sdl_compat.h` (`SDLC_EventKey`, `SDLC_EventWheelIntX/Y`), `sdl_geometry.h` (`MakeSdlRect`), `static_vector.hpp`, `enum_traits.h`/`is_of.hpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Outer loop shape (369, 372, 571–578): `do { endMenu=false; UiLoadBlackBackground(); LoadScrollBar(); UiAddBackground(); UiAddLogo(); build title; build items by level; append the two trailer rows; compute rects + scrollbar + description + UiList; UiInitList(...); while(!endMenu){ UiClearScreen(); UpdatePadEntryTimerText(); UiPollAndRender(eventHandler); } CleanUpSettingsUI(); } while(!backToMain);` and `SaveOptions()` exactly once after the loop (580).
  - Entry filtering (88–94): skip if (`NeedDiabloMpq` && !HaveIntro()) or `Invisible`, or `OnlyDiablo` when Hellfire is on / `OnlyHellfire` when it is off — the flag chosen from `gbIsHellfire` at call time.
  - Categories level (407–420): one row per category that has ≥1 valid entry (the inner loop `break`s on the first valid one, 416), value = category index, colour `ColorUiGold`; remembers `itemToSelect` when `selectedCategory == pCategory` (413–415).
  - Settings level (421–437): per valid entry, `optionId = vecOptions.size()`; if the label needs two lines push row A = template `"{}:"` with `ColorUiGold|NeedsNextElement` (430) and row B = owned value string with `ColorUiSilver|ElementDisabled` (431), both with the same `optionId`; else one row with template `"{}: {}"` (433); then `vecOptions.push_back(pEntry)` (435).
  - ListOption level (438–445): one row per `GetListDescription(i)` with value `i`; `itemToSelect = GetActiveListIndex()`; update the description from the option.
  - KeyInput level (446–499): rows = [`_("Bound key:")` disabled ColorWhitegold (447), value row (index `IndexKeyOrPadInput`, `ColorUiGold`, 448), index assert (449), `_("Press any key to change.")` disabled (496), blank disabled (497), `_("Unbind key")` with value `UnbindKey` (498)]; `itemToSelect = 1` (450); installs an event handler (451–498) that, only when `SelectedItem == IndexKeyOrPadInput` (452), maps KEY_DOWN through `remap_keyboard_key` and uppercases `SDLK_A..SDLK_Z` (458–462), MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN for MIDDLE/X1/X2 → `button | KeymapperMouseButtonMask` (464–473), MOUSE_WHEEL → up/down from the `wheelY` sign then left/right from the `wheelX` sign (474–486); returns false for `SDLK_UNKNOWN` (487–489); `KeymapperOptions::Action::SetValue(key)` returning false leaves the screen open (490–492); on success row 1 text is refreshed from `GetValueDescription()` (493).
  - PadInput level (501–548): rows = [`_("Bound button combo:")` disabled (502), value row with value `BindPadButton` (503), timer-text row at `IndexPadTimerText` (507–508), blank (510), `_("Unbind button combo")` with value `UnbindPadButton` (511)]; sets `padEntryStartTime = 0` on entry (513); handler (514–548) returns false when the timer is off, converts the event to ≤4 `ControllerButtonEvent`s via `ToControllerButtonEvents` (518), calls `IsControllerMotion(event)` + `DetectInputMethod(event, ctrlEvent)` per event (520–521), aborts capture on KEY_UP+ESCAPE (522–525), skips motion events and NONE/IGNORE buttons (526–528), and on button-up stops the capture once the button is set and neither modifier nor button is still pressed (529–536); on press it promotes `button`→`modifier` when a button is held without a modifier, sets `padEntryCombo.button = ctrlEvent.button`, and pushes to `PadmapperOptions::Action::SetValue`, refreshing row 1 on success (541–546).
  - Pad timer (139–172): start = combo cleared, `padEntryStartTime = SDL_GetTicks()` with 0→1 bump (141–143) and `ElementHidden` OR'd onto every dialog item from `IndexPadTimerText+1` onward (144–146); stop = combo/time/text cleared, row 2 text reset, `ElementHidden` removed from the same range (150–159); per-frame update returns early unless the level is PadInput, stops if time==0 or `elapsed > 10000`, else sets text to `_("Press gamepad buttons to change.")` + " " + `10 - elapsed/1000`.
  - Navigation (246–333): negative `m_value` → `SpecialMenuEntry` (PreviousMenu → back one level; UnbindKey → `SDLK_UNKNOWN` + row refresh, 259–261; BindPadButton → start timer; UnbindPadButton → `ControllerButton_NONE` + row refresh, 268–270) and return (249–273). Categories → set `selectedCategory`, `endMenu`, level=Settings (277–280). Settings → List with `GetListSize() > 2` opens the submenu, else cycles `(active+1) % size` instantly (287–297); Key → KeyInput; PadButton → PadInput; other → `ChangeOptionValue(pOption, 0)`. ListOption → `ChangeOptionValue(selectedOption, vecItemValue)` then `GoBackOneMenuLevel()` (325–328).
  - Value mutation (210–244): Boolean → `SetValue(!current)`; List → `SetActiveListIndex(listIndex)`; Key/PadButton → nothing. `RecreateUI` flag → set `endMenu`, `CleanUpSettingsUI()`, `UnloadUiGFX()`, `FreeItemGFX()`, `selectedOption = pOption`, and after the switch call `UiInitialize()`, `InitItemGFX()`, `SetHardwareCursor(CursorInfo::UnknownCursor())` and return false (no in-place refresh).
  - Post-change refresh (300–321): recompute args; two-line-ness detected by `vecDialogItems[value]->m_value == vecDialogItems[value+1]->m_value` guarded by `value+1 < size`; if that classification changed → `selectedOption = pOption; endMenu = true` (full rebuild on the next outer iteration); else rewrite the row's `args` in place and, for two-line rows, row `value+1`'s `m_text`.
  - Back semantics (123–137, 335–338): Categories → `endMenu = true; backToMain = true`; Settings → Categories; anything deeper → Settings. Esc uses the same function.
  - `FullscreenChanged` (340–358): registered as the `UiInitList` fullscreen callback; scans rows, skips negative values and values `>= vecOptions.size()`, finds the row whose option is `&GetOptions().Graphics.fullscreen`, rewrites its args, and stops.
  - Description pane (174–184, 186–208): word-wrap the option/category description at `rectDescription.size.width` with `GameFont12`, spacing 1, and `CopyUtf8` into the fixed 512-byte buffer; `ItemFocused` zeroes the buffer first (191, 199) and skips rows with `m_value < 0`; the buffer is also zeroed at every menu build (387).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `IndexKeyOrPadInput = 1`, `IndexPadTimerText = 2` (49–50) asserted against push order (449, 504, 508); `SpecialMenuEntry` values −1..−5 (76–82).
  - Layout: `uiWidth = clamp(gnScreenWidth, 640, 720)`; `uiRectangle = { {(gnScreenWidth-uiWidth)/2, 0}, {uiWidth, gnScreenHeight} }` (373–376); title rect `(x, y+161, width, 35)` `FontSize30|ColorUiSilver|AlignCenter` spacing 8 (401); `ListItemHeight = 26` (557); `rectList = {uiRectangle.position + {50,204}, {width-100, min(items*26, height-272)}}` (558–559); `rectDescription = {rectList.position + {-26, rectList.height + marginTop}, {width-50, 80 - marginTop}}` (560–561); scrollbar rect `x + width + 5, y, 25, height` (562–563); description `UiArtText` `FontSize12|ColorUiSilverDark|AlignCenter`, spacing 1, lineHeight/marginTop = `IsSmallFontTall() ? 20:18 / 10:16` (384–385, 564–565); `UiList` viewport `rectList.height / 26`, flags `FontSize24|AlignCenter` (566–567).
  - Trailer rows always appended: blank (`None`, `ElementDisabled`) then `_("Previous Menu")` = `PreviousMenu` (554–555).
  - Two-line threshold `GetLineWidth("{}: {}", args, spacing 0, GameFont24, 1) >= rectList.width - 90` (105–107); countdown text `10 - (elapsed / 1000)` with integer division, stop at `elapsed > 10000` (165–170); `SDL_GetTicks()` 0 → 1 (142–143).
  - `padEntryStartTime = 0` doubles as "capture off" (161–166, 513); `StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent, 4>` caps the batch at 4 events (518).
  - `UiInitList(ItemFocused, ItemSelected, EscPressed, vecDialog, /*wrapAround=*/true, FullscreenChanged, nullptr, itemToSelect)` (569).
  - Verbatim translated strings: "Settings" (392), "Bound key:" (447), "Press any key to change." (496), "Unbind key" (498), "Bound button combo:" (502), "Unbind button combo" (511), "Previous Menu" (555), "Press gamepad buttons to change." (169). Title text source per level: `_("Settings")` / `selectedCategory->GetName()` / `selectedOption->GetName()` (390–399).
  - Letter normalisation `key -= 'a' - 'A'` only for `SDLK_A..SDLK_Z` (460–462), i.e. bindings are stored uppercase.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: everything is file-scope mutable state — the menu is neither reentrant nor safe to open twice. `CleanUpSettingsUI` (110–121) is the only thing that empties the three vectors and releases `ArtBackground`/`ArtBackgroundWidescreen`/scrollbar art (via `UiInitList_clear()` + `UnloadScrollBar()`); it runs on the `RecreateUI` path (215) and at the end of every loop iteration (577), so a rebuild always starts from empty vectors. The countdown couples to the render loop (one `UpdatePadEntryTimerText()` per frame, 573) and to a monotonic ms clock. `optionDescription` is a fixed buffer referenced by a `UiArtText` that reads it live — the Go port needs a live-bound label, not a snapshot. No RNG, no serialization.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln "settingsmenu\|UiSettingsMenu" test/` → no match).
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/settings` over the shared widget toolkit (`internal/uiauto/widget`) and an options package (`pkg/config`) exposing `Categories() []Category` with per-entry `Type/Flags/Name/ValueDescription/Description` and typed setters (`Bool.Toggle`, `List.SetActive(i)`, `Key.Set(code) bool`, `Pad.Set(combo) bool`) plus `Save()`. Model the 5 levels with one enum + a `rebuild()` returning rows; either keep a per-row `SpanTwoLines bool` or mirror 1:1 with two rows to preserve the `IndexKeyOrPadInput`/`m_value`-pairing logic. Inject `Now func() uint32` and an event sink for capture; `RecreateUI` must surface as a "reinit UI" signal to the app loop rather than tearing down mid-callback.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `ChangeOptionValue` frees and re-initialises the whole UI subsystem from inside a click callback (212–240) — in Go this must be a deferred action, or handlers will run against torn-down state. (2) The in-place refresh at 300–321 depends on adjacent rows sharing `m_value`; any representation that drops the duplicate second row breaks that detection. (3) Pad-capture semantics (514–548: modifier promotion, motion filtering, ESC cancel, release-all commit, 4-event cap) have zero upstream tests — drive them with synthetic event tables. (4) The countdown label renders `0` for elapsed 9001–10000 before stopping — keep that off-by-one only if pixel-parity matters.
