### Source/DiabloUI/text_input.cpp
- Purpose: SDL-event → editing-operation bridge for single-line text and number inputs, plus the out-of-line `NumberInputState` methods (digit filtering, clamping, value read).
- Public API: `bool HandleTextInputEvent(const SDL_Event &, TextInputState &)` (142–152); `bool HandleNumberInputEvent(const SDL_Event &, NumberInputState &)` (209–219); member definitions `int NumberInputState::value(int defaultValue) const` (154–157), `std::string NumberInputState::filterStr(std::string_view, bool allowMinus)` (159–172), `void NumberInputState::type(std::string_view)` (174–182), `void NumberInputState::assign(std::string_view)` (184–193), `void NumberInputState::enforceRange()` (195–207). Anonymous-namespace `bool HandleInputEvent(const SDL_Event &, TextInputState &, tl::function_ref<bool(std::string_view)> typeFn, tl::function_ref<bool(std::string_view)> assignFn)` (32–138).
- Depends on: `text_input.hpp` (1); SDL via `utils/sdl_compat.h` (`SDLC_EventKey`, `SDLC_SetClipboardText`, `SDLC_HasClipboardText`) and `utils/sdl_ptrs.h` (`SDLFreeDeleter`): `SDL_GetModState`, `SDL_KMOD_CTRL/ALT/SHIFT`, `SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN`, `SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT`, `SDL_EVENT_TEXT_EDITING`/`_CANDIDATES` (SDL2 `SDL_TEXTEDITING`), `SDLK_*`, `SDL_GetClipboardText`, `SDL_GetError`, `SDL_ClearError`; `utils/parse_int.hpp` (`ParseInt<int>`, `ParseIntResult<int>`); `utils/utf8.hpp` (`AppendUtf8`, SDL1 path); `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat(max_/min_)`); `utils/log.hpp` (`LogError`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Dispatch (36–137): read Ctrl/Alt/Shift modifiers once per event (36–39); on KEY_DOWN — `Ctrl+A` → `setCursorToStart()` then `setSelectCursorToEnd()` (select all) (44–48); `Ctrl+C` → copy `selectedText()` to the clipboard, logging + `SDL_ClearError()` on failure (50–57); `Ctrl+X` → same copy, and only on success `eraseSelection()` (59–68); `Ctrl+V` → if `SDLC_HasClipboardText()`, fetch, log on null, and feed non-empty text to `typeFn` (70–81); each case returns true (handled) whether or not Ctrl was held (49, 58, 69, 82). `BACKSPACE` → `backspace(word = isCtrl||isAlt)` (84–86); `DELETE` → `del(word = isCtrl||isAlt)` (87–89); `LEFT`/`RIGHT` → select-move when Shift, plain-move otherwise, word mode from Ctrl/Alt (90–95); `HOME`/`END` → the same Shift split (96–101).
  - Insertable-character handling: non-SDL1 returns `!isCtrl && !isAlt && SDLK_SPACE <= key <= SDLK_Z` purely to mark the event handled, deferring insertion to the following TEXT_INPUT event (113–115); SDL1 instead converts `event.key.keysym.unicode` with `AppendUtf8` and calls `typeFn` when Ctrl is not held and `unicode >= ' '` (106–111).
  - `SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT` → `typeFn(event.text.text)` normally, `assignFn(...)` (whole-value replace) on `__vita__` (119–125); `TEXT_EDITING`/`TEXT_EDITING_CANDIDATES` swallowed as handled with no edit (126–132); every other event type → false (134–137).
  - Wrappers: text wiring = typeFn→`state.type`, assignFn→`state.assign` (142–152); number wiring = typeFn→`state.type`, assignFn→`state.assign` on the `NumberInputState` (209–219) so digits pass through filtering.
  - Number filtering: `filterStr` accepts a `-` only as the first byte when `allowMinus`, then keeps only `'0'..'9'` (159–172). `type` uses `allowMinus = min_ < 0 && cursorPosition() == 0`, ignores an empty result, inserts, then clamps (174–182). `assign` uses `allowMinus = min_ < 0` and *clears* the field when nothing survives the filter (184–193).
  - `enforceRange`: returns when empty; parses; `> max_` → `assign(StrCat(max_))`, `< min_` → `assign(StrCat(min_))`; unparseable text is left as-is (195–207). `value(default)` = parsed or fallback (154–157).
- 1:1 constraints: the clipboard-failure test is `if (SDLC_SetClipboardText(...))` — nonzero means failure (53, 62); the insertable-key range is exactly `SDLK_SPACE..SDLK_Z` (115); digit test `c >= '0' && c <= '9'` and minus only at index 0 (162–170); `assign` with an empty filter result clears the buffer instead of leaving it (187–190); clamp writes the boundary value through `StrCat` (202–204); the trailing `return false` after the switch (137) is unreachable for KEY_DOWN-with-unicode paths but is the SDL1 fallthrough value.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless; mutates caller-owned state only. Clipboard reads/writes are external side effects and must stay on the UI/main goroutine (Ebiten `input.Clipboard` is main-thread-only). No clock, no RNG, no serialization.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln "HandleTextInputEvent\|TextInputState\|NumberInputState" test/` → no match); `test/parse_int_test.cpp` covers the `ParseInt` dependency.
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/textinput` — separate portable editing from platform: `type Key int`, `type Mod uint8`, `func HandleKey(ev Event, st *State, clip Clipboard) bool` with a `Clipboard` interface (`Has() bool`, `Read() (string, error)`, `Write(string) error`) so Ctrl+C/X/V is unit-testable; `type Number struct { Text *State; Min, Max int }` with `FilterStr`, `Type`, `Assign`, `EnforceRange`, `Value(def int) int`, reusing the Go port of `ParseInt` and keeping the "parse failure ⇒ don't touch text" rule.
- Risks/open questions: (1) IME/composition events are deliberately no-ops upstream — Ebiten exposes no composition stream, so paste (`assign`) becomes the only bulk entry path; confirm that is acceptable. (2) The `__vita__` assign-vs-type divergence (120–124) has no Go analog — drop it or hide it behind a build tag. (3) `type` vs `assign` differ in minus-acceptance rules (cursor-position-dependent) — do not unify them.

### Source/DiabloUI/text_input.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only single-line input model: byte-range cursor/selection state plus an editing engine over an unowned fixed-size UTF-8 buffer, and a numeric wrapper with digit filtering and range clamping; declares the two event handlers implemented in text_input.cpp.
- Public API: `struct TextRange { size_t begin=0, end=0; size_t size(); bool empty(); void clear(); }` (20–40); `struct TextInputCursorState { size_t position; TextRange selection; }` (43–46); `class TextInputState` (53–376) with private `struct Buffer` (57–126), public `struct Options { char *value; TextInputCursorState *cursor; size_t maxLength; }` (129–133), `TextInputState(const Options&)` (134–139), getters `value()`/`selectedText()`/`empty()`/`cursorPosition()` (141–158), mutators `assign` (164), `clear` (170), `truncate(size_t length)` (179), `eraseSelection` (190), `type` (200), `backspace(bool word)` (209), `del(bool word)` (220), `setCursorToStart` (231), `setSelectCursorToStart` (237), `setCursorToEnd` (247), `setSelectCursorToEnd` (253), `moveCursorLeft` (263), `moveSelectCursorLeft` (272), `moveCursorRight` (288), `moveSelectCursorRight` (297); `class NumberInputState` (380–431) with `Options { TextInputState::Options textOptions; int min; int max; }` (382–386), `empty()` (394), `int value(int defaultValue = 0)` (399), `max()` (401–404), `type` (411), `assign` (418), `textInput()` (420–423), private `enforceRange`/`filterStr` (426–427) and members `textInput_`, `min_`, `max_` (429–431); free functions `HandleTextInputEvent`, `HandleNumberInputEvent` (434–435).
- Depends on: `utils/utf8.hpp` (`TruncateUtf8` 63/80/120, `CopyUtf8` 81, `Utf8CodePoints` 326–327/346–347), `<algorithm>` (`std::min` 184), `<cstring>` (`memmove`/`memcpy` 89–97), SDL event type only for the two handler declarations (11–15); consumed by `ui_item.h:276` (`UiEdit::m_cursor`), `text_input.cpp`, and every screen with an edit box.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `Buffer`: constructed over a caller-owned `char*` + `maxLength`; the constructor reads it as a C string, UTF-8-truncates to `maxLength` and re-NUL-terminates, caching the length (58–66). `operator=` truncates then `CopyUtf8` and updates len (78–84). `insert(pos, value)` first truncates the *inserted* text to the remaining room `maxLength_ - len_` (118–121) and then memmove/memcpy + NUL (86–93). `erase(pos, len)` memmoves the tail left, decrements len, re-NULs (95–100). `clear()` sets len 0 and NULs byte 0 (102–106). Conversion to `string_view` uses the cached length, not `strlen` (108–111).
  - Cursor invariants: the constructor parks the cursor at the end of the existing value (138); `assign` moves it to the end (164–168); `clear` to 0 (170–173); `truncate(length)` is a no-op when `length >= size` and otherwise clamps the cursor with `std::min` (179–186).
  - Selection model: `eraseSelection` deletes `[begin,end)`, parks the cursor at `begin`, clears the range (190–197); `type` replaces a non-empty selection first, inserts at the cursor, and advances by the actual byte delta `value_.size() - prevSize` (200–207) — so a truncated insert still lands correctly.
  - `backspace(word)`/`del(word)` (209–230): with an empty selection, build the range from `prevPosition`→cursor or cursor→`nextPosition`, bailing at the string edges, then always `eraseSelection()`.
  - Word-boundary logic (314–361): `isWordSeparator(c)` is true iff `c <= U+7E` and NOT in `[0-9A-Za-z_]` (316–318) — every non-ASCII code point is a word character. `prevPosition` (321–340): char mode returns the start byte of the preceding code point (`std::prev(it.base()).data() - str.data()`, 329); word mode skips trailing separators, then skips word chars, returning `it.base().data() - str.data()` or 0 when it reaches the start (331–339). `nextPosition` (342–361): char mode returns `position + it.size()` (349); word mode consumes one code point first (351), then skips separators (352–354), then word chars (355–357), returning `position + (it.data() - str.data())` (360) or `position + str.size()` at the end (358).
  - Selection-drag rules (237–246, 253–262, 272–287, 297–312): when the moving end coincides with the cursor (`selection.end == position` growing left, `selection.begin == position` growing right) that end is relocated instead of extended, so a drag reverses cleanly; `setSelectCursorToStart` finally sets `begin = position = 0` (245–246) and `setSelectCursorToEnd` sets `end = position = size` (260); plain cursor moves clear the selection first (264, 289).
  - `NumberInputState` (380–431): owns a `TextInputState` over the same external buffer plus `min_`/`max_`; `max()` is exposed because renderers use it; `value()`/`type()`/`assign()`/`enforceRange()` are implemented in the .cpp.
- 1:1 constraints: every offset is a **byte** index, never a rune index (21–22, 146–149 `value().substr(selection.begin, selection.size())`); `maxLength` is bytes and `TruncateUtf8` is the only thing guaranteeing code-point safety (63, 80, 120); the ASCII-only word rule with its exact character ranges and the `c <= U'\x7E'` guard (316–318); `prevPosition` word mode = separators-then-word-chars (331–336) while `nextPosition` consumes exactly one code point *before* that pair of loops (351–357); `type` advances by the size delta (203–206); `UiEdit`/`Options` pass raw unowned pointers so buffer lifetime is the caller's (129–133, 373–374); `Buffer::insert` memmoves `len_ - pos` bytes and `erase` moves `len_ - (pos + len)` (89, 97).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: no statics, globals, clock, or RNG. State is aliased by pointer with the owning screen's fixed char array, so two `TextInputState`s over the same buffer would silently alias. All edits are O(n) memmoves on a bounded buffer — deterministic. Must stay on the UI goroutine because the widget (`UiEdit`) and the renderer read the same memory.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln "TextInputState\|NumberInputState" test/` → no match); `test/utf8_test.cpp` covers the `TruncateUtf8`/`Utf8CodePoints` behaviour it relies on.
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/textinput` (same package as the .cpp port). Strategy: `type Range struct{ Begin, End int }`, `type Cursor struct{ Position int; Selection Range }`, `type State struct{ buf []byte; maxLen int; cur *Cursor }` where `buf` is a caller-owned `[]byte` (keep the trailing NUL only if the value is handed to C). Expose `Value() string`, `SelectedText() string`, `CursorPosition() int`, `Assign`, `Clear`, `Truncate`, `EraseSelection`, `Type`, `Backspace/Del/MoveCursorLeft/MoveSelectCursorLeft/…` with `word bool`, `SetCursorToStart/End`, `SetSelectCursorToStart/End`; implement `prevPosition/nextPosition` with `utf8.DecodeLastRuneInString`/`DecodeRuneInString` and a `isWordSeparator(r rune) bool` copied verbatim. `Number{Text *State; Min, Max int}` wraps it.
- Risks/open questions: (1) Decide whether Go widgets read `Value()` snapshots or hold a live pointer (settingsmenu mutates the buffer and expects the label to change, settingsmenu.cpp:493/546). (2) `truncate(length)` at an arbitrary byte count can split a code point; upstream callers pass safe lengths — keep the behaviour and document it. (3) Word-motion edge cases (empty string, all separators, trailing separators, cursor at end) have no upstream tests; write table-driven tests before porting the handler.

### Source/DiabloUI/title.cpp
- Purpose: The ~7-second non-interactive title/copyright splash shown before the main menu, with two asset paths (Hellfire widescreen CLX animation vs. Diablo PCX logo animation). Entry point `UiTitleDialog`.
- Public API: `void UiTitleDialog()` (58–103). Anonymous namespace (30–56): `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList DiabloTitleLogo` (32), `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<UiItemBase>> vecTitleScreen` (34), `void TitleLoad()` (36–45), `void TitleFree()` (47–54).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (`ArtBackground`, `ArtBackgroundWidescreen`, `LoadBackgroundArt`, `UiAddBackground`, `UiRenderItems`, `UiFadeIn`, `UiHandleEvents`, `GetUIRectangle`); `ui_item.h` (`UiImageClx`, `UiImageAnimatedClx`, `UiArtText`); `ui_flags.hpp` (`AlignCenter`, `FontSize24`, `ColorUiSilver`); `engine/load_clx.hpp` (`LoadOptionalClx`), `engine/load_pcx.hpp` (`LoadPcxSpriteList`), `engine/clx_sprite.hpp`; `controls/input.h` (`PollEvent`), `controls/menu_controls.h` (`GetMenuActions`, `MenuAction_NONE`); `discord/discord.h` (`discord_manager::UpdateMenu()`); `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (`c_any_of`); `utils/language.h`; `utils/sdl_compat.h`, `utils/sdl_geometry.h`, `utils/ui_fwd.h`; SDL (`SDL_GetTicks`, `SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN`, `SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON_UP`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Asset path chosen at load (38–44): optionally load `ui_art\hf_titlew.clx`; if present → `LoadBackgroundArt("ui_art\hf_logo1", 16)` (16-frame Hellfire logo animation); if absent → `LoadBackgroundArt("ui_art\title")` and `DiabloTitleLogo = LoadPcxSpriteList("ui_art\logo", numFrames=15, transparentColor=250)`.
  - Widget stack (62–75): Hellfire branch pushes `UiImageClx((*ArtBackgroundWidescreen)[0], MakeSdlRect(0, uiY, 0, 0), AlignCenter)` then `UiImageAnimatedClx(*ArtBackground, same rect, AlignCenter)`; Diablo branch pushes `UiAddBackground(&vecTitleScreen)`, then `UiImageAnimatedClx(*DiabloTitleLogo, MakeSdlRect(0, uiY+182, 0, 0), AlignCenter)`, then `UiArtText` copyright at `MakeSdlRect(uiX, uiY+410, 640, 26)` with `AlignCenter|FontSize24|ColorUiSilver`.
  - Timed loop (77–100): per iteration render all items, `UiFadeIn()`, call `discord_manager::UpdateMenu()`, then drain every pending event; break out if any `GetMenuActions(event)` yields a non-`NONE` action (controller/menu mapping), or if the raw event type is `KEY_DOWN` or `MOUSE_BUTTON_UP`; each event is additionally passed to `UiHandleEvents(&event)`. The deadline is computed once (`SDL_GetTicks() + 7000`) and the loop condition is `!endMenu && SDL_GetTicks() < timeOut`.
  - Teardown (47–54, 102): release `ArtBackground`, `ArtBackgroundWidescreen`, `DiabloTitleLogo`, and clear the widget vector.
- 1:1 constraints: asset paths and parameters verbatim — `"ui_art\\hf_titlew.clx"`, `"ui_art\\hf_logo1"` with frame count 16, `"ui_art\\title"`, `"ui_art\\logo"` with `numFrames=15` and `transparentColor=250` (38–43); string `_("Copyright © 1996-2001 Blizzard Entertainment")` (74); offsets `+182` (logo) and `+410` with width 640, height 26 (71, 73); timeout `7000` ms (78); `MakeSdlRect(0, y, 0, 0)` with zero w/h is significant — the widget centres on image size, not rect size (63, 71); the extra `if (ArtBackgroundWidescreen)` guard inside the `has_value()` branch (64) is redundant but harmless.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `vecTitleScreen` is file-scope and only emptied by `TitleFree`, so calling `UiTitleDialog` twice without teardown duplicates widgets. Wall-clock (`SDL_GetTicks`) dependent and framerate dependent: `UiRenderItems`/`UiFadeIn` run once per unpaced iteration, so the fade animation advances with CPU/loop speed rather than a fixed tick. No RNG, no serialization, no mutable globals beyond the two vectors/optionals.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln "UiTitleDialog" test/` → no match).
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/title` — `func Show(ctx *Context)`; assets through the MPQ→CLX/PCX loader (`pkg/mpq` + `internal/render`) with "missing file ⇒ nil, no error" semantics for `LoadOptionalClx`; the busy loop becomes a game state whose `Update(dt)` compares against a deadline from an injected clock, checks `input.IsKeyPressed`/`input.IsMouseButtonJustReleased` plus the menu-action mapper, and calls the presence/Discord hook once per frame.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `UiFadeIn` is shared fade state used by all UI screens — the port must decide whether title owns a fade or uses the global one. (2) Under Ebiten's paced `Update` (60 Hz) the 7 s deadline still holds but the fade *rate* differs from the unthrottled C++ loop unless fade time is normalised by `dt`. (3) Hellfire-vs-Diablo branch is decided by runtime asset availability, not a build flag — keep that (a missing `hf_titlew.clx` must not error).

### Source/DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp
- Purpose: The single bit-flag enum that selects font size, text colour, alignment, kerning, element interactivity and list-row pairing for every DiabloUI widget.
- Public API: `enum class UiFlags : uint32_t` (9–53) plus `use_enum_as_flags(UiFlags)` (54), which generates `operator|`, `operator&`, `operator~`, `HasAnyOf`/`HasNoneOf` from `utils/enum_traits.h`.
- Depends on: `<cstdint>` (3), `utils/enum_traits.h` (5). Included by all of `Source/DiabloUI/*` and by anything that calls `DrawString`/`UiRenderItems`.
- Requirements for Go port: a `uint32` bitmask type with exactly these bit positions and `Has/With/Without` helpers, plus the renderer-side mapping from the Font*/Color* bits to the font table and palette index.
- 1:1 constraints: bit positions are stored in widget state and OR'd by call sites, so they are load-bearing — `None = 0` (11); FontSize12=1<<0, 24=1<<1, 30=1<<2, 42=1<<3, 46=1<<4, Dialog=1<<5 (13–18); ColorUiGold=1<<6, ColorUiSilver=1<<7, ColorUiGoldDark=1<<8, ColorUiSilverDark=1<<9, ColorDialogWhite=1<<10, ColorDialogYellow=1<<11, ColorDialogRed=1<<12, ColorYellow=1<<13, ColorGold=1<<14, ColorBlack=1<<15, ColorWhite=1<<16, ColorWhitegold=1<<17, ColorRed=1<<18, ColorBlue=1<<19, ColorOrange=1<<20, ColorButtonface=1<<21, ColorButtonpushed=1<<22 (20–36); AlignCenter=1<<23, AlignRight=1<<24, VerticalCenter=1<<25 (38–40); KerningFitSpacing=1<<26 (42); ElementDisabled=1<<27, ElementHidden=1<<28 (44–45); PentaCursor=1<<29, Outlined=1<<30 (47–48); `NeedsNextElement = 1U << 31U` (51) — the unsigned shift keeps it in bit 31 of a `uint32`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure type, no state, no init order. Enum declaration order is documentation only; the numeric values are the contract.
- Test coverage: none found for the header itself; exercised indirectly by `test/ui_test.hpp`-based UI tests and `test/text_render_integration_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/widget` (shared with the text renderer) as `type Flags uint32` with named constants at identical bits; `func FontFor(f Flags) Font` / `func ColorFor(f Flags) uint8` live in the render layer the way `DrawString`/`UiRenderItems` interpret them today.
- Risks/open questions: none, except that `ElementHidden`/`ElementDisabled`/`NeedsNextElement` must exist even if unused on day one — settingsmenu.cpp sets/clears `ElementHidden` directly on list items (147, 158).

### Source/DiabloUI/ui_item.h
- Purpose: The DiabloUI widget hierarchy: an abstract base carrying rect + flags and nine concrete item types (plain/art text, art-text button, static sprite, animated sprite, Diablo sprite button, list, list item, scrollbar, edit box). Rendering and polling live in `diabloui.cpp`; this file is data and accessors only.
- Public API: `enum class UiType : uint8_t { Text, ArtText, ArtTextButton, ImageClx, ImageAnimatedClx, Button, List, Scrollbar, Edit }` (18–29); `class UiItemBase` (31–91) — `GetType()`, `IsType(UiType)`, `GetFlags()`, `IsHidden()`, `IsNotInteractive()`, `Hide()`, `Show()`, protected ctor `(UiType, SDL_Rect, UiFlags)` (70–75), protected `SetFlags(UiFlags)` (77–80), public field `SDL_Rect m_rect` (86); `UiImageClx` (93–119) ctor `(ClxSprite, SDL_Rect, UiFlags=None)` + `isCentered()`, `sprite()`, `setSprite()`; `UiImageAnimatedClx` (121–143) ctor `(ClxSpriteList, ...)` + `isCentered()`, `sprite(uint16_t frame)`, `numFrames()`; `UiArtText` (150–207) with two ctors `(const char *text, rect, flags=None, int spacing=1, int lineHeight=-1)` (160) and `(const char **ptext, ...)` (176) + `GetText()` (184), `GetSpacing()` (191), `GetLineHeight()` (~196); `UiScrollbar` (210–226) ctor `(ClxSprite bg, ClxSprite thumb, ClxSpriteList arrow, rect, flags)` and public `m_bg`/`m_thumb`/`m_arrow`; `UiArtTextButton` (228–259) `using Callback = void (*)()`, ctor `(std::string_view text, Callback, rect, flags=None)`, `SetFlags`, `GetText()`, `Activate() const`; `UiEdit` (261–282) ctor `(std::string_view hint, char *value, std::size_t maxLength, bool allowEmpty, rect, flags=None)` with public `m_hint`, `m_value`, `m_max_length`, `TextInputCursorState m_cursor`, `m_allowEmpty` (273–277); `UiText` (284–303) ctor `(std::string_view, rect, flags = ColorDialogWhite)` + `GetText()`; `UiButton` (305–350) `using Callback = void (*)()`, ctor `(text, action, rect, flags=None)`, `GetText()`, `Activate() const`, `IsPressed()`, `Press()`, `Release()`; `UiListItem` (352–374) ctors `(StringOrView &&text = {}, int value = 0, UiFlags = None)` (354) and `(StringOrView &&text, std::vector<DrawStringFormatArg> &args, int value = 0, UiFlags = None)` (361) with public `m_text`, `args`, `m_value`, `uiFlags`; `UiList : UiItemBase` (376–458) `using vUiListItem = std::vector<std::unique_ptr<UiListItem>>`, public ctor `(const vUiListItem&, size_t viewportMaxSize, Sint16 x, Sint16 y, Uint16 item_width, Uint16 item_height, UiFlags=None, int spacing=1)` (378–383), `itemRect(int i)` (385), `indexAt(Sint16 y)` (396), `GetItem(size_t i)` (~406), `GetSpacing()` (409), `IsPressed(size_t)` (415), `Press(size_t)` (420), `Release()` (425), public `viewportSize`, `m_x/m_y`, `m_width/m_height`, `std::vector<UiListItem *> m_vecItems` (430–434), private tag ctor (439–452), `spacing_` (454), `pressed_item_index_` (457).
- Depends on: `text_input.hpp` (8, for `UiEdit::m_cursor` 276), `ui_flags.hpp` (9), `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` (10, `ClxSprite`/`ClxSpriteList`), `engine/render/text_render.hpp` (11, `DrawStringFormatArg`), `utils/enum_traits.h` (12), `utils/string_or_view.hpp` (13, `StringOrView`), `utils/stubs.h` (14, `ASSERT`), SDL `SDL_Rect`; included by every `DiabloUI/*.cpp` and by `diabloui.cpp`'s render/poll loops.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A widget abstraction carrying type tag, rect and flags, with `IsHidden()` == `ElementHidden` bit (49–52) and `IsNotInteractive()` == `ElementHidden|ElementDisabled` (54–57), and `Hide()`/`Show()` that only touch the hidden bit (59–67) — the settings pad-capture lockout depends on exactly that.
  - `UiArtText` must support both a snapshot string and a **pointer to a mutable C string** (`text_` vs `textPointer_`, 202–203; `GetText()` returns `text_` when non-null else `*textPointer_`, 184–189) so labels bound to buffers that change between frames (e.g. `optionDescription`) re-read live. Defaults: `spacing = 1`, `lineHeight = -1` (sentinel "use the font's own height").
  - `UiList` construction: viewport = `min(viewportMaxSize, len(items))` (381); base rect = `{x, y, item_width, Uint16(item_height * viewportSize)}` (440); `m_vecItems` stores **raw pointers** into the caller's `vector<unique_ptr<UiListItem>>` (448–449), so the caller must outlive the widget and may mutate items afterwards (settingsmenu writes `m_text`, `args`, `uiFlags` of those same objects while the list points at them).
  - Geometry: `itemRect(i)` = `{m_x, m_y + m_height*i, m_width, m_height}` (385–393); `indexAt(y)` = `(y - m_rect.y) / m_height` with `ASSERT(y >= m_rect.y)` and `ASSERT(index < m_vecItems.size())` (396–404); `GetSpacing()` returns the per-character spacing forwarded to text drawing (409).
  - Pressed-state: `IsPressed(index)` compares against `pressed_item_index_`, `Press(index)` stores the index, `Release()` stores the `-1` sentinel in a `size_t` (415–426, 451) — a "no pressed item" value of max `size_t`.
  - Buttons: `UiArtTextButton`/`UiButton` hold a free function pointer and `Activate()` only calls it (249–252, 322–325); `UiButton` tracks `pressed_` for sprite-frame selection (327–348).
  - `UiEdit` carries hint text, an unowned value pointer, a byte `m_max_length`, an `m_allowEmpty` validation flag, and owns its `TextInputCursorState` by value (261–282).
  - `UiListItem` is deliberately *not* a `UiItemBase` (352) and carries an `args` vector for `{}`-format drawing plus its own `uiFlags`; `StringOrView` must be modelled (borrowed label vs. owned/generated label).
- 1:1 constraints: `UiType` declaration order is the `uint8_t` discriminant that `diabloui.cpp` switches on (18–29); default flags are `UiFlags::None` for every widget except `UiText`, whose default is `UiFlags::ColorDialogWhite` (286); `UiArtText` spacing 1 / lineHeight −1 (160, 176) and `UiList` spacing 1 (379); `UiList` base-rect height computed in `Uint16` (440) — integer truncation semantics preserved; `indexAt` divides by `m_height` and references `m_rect.y` (398–400) while `itemRect` uses `m_y` (388); `pressed_item_index_ = -1` sentinel (426, 451); `UiEdit` field order `m_hint, m_value, m_max_length, m_cursor, m_allowEmpty` (273–277); `UiImageAnimatedClx::sprite(frame)` takes `uint16_t` and `numFrames()` returns `uint16_t` (134–141).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: header only, no statics. The real hazard is lifetime aliasing: `UiList::m_vecItems` are non-owning, so clearing the caller's item vector without recreating the `UiList` dangles (settingsmenu clears both together, settingsmenu.cpp:110–121). Widgets are mutated after construction, so a Go port must use `*ListItem` pointers rather than values. No clock/RNG/serialization.
- Test coverage: none found for the header directly (`grep -rln "ui_item" test/` → no match); exercised indirectly through `test/ui_test.hpp` plus `inventory_ui_test.cpp`, `spell_ui_test.cpp`, `stash_test.cpp`; `test/rectangle_test.cpp` covers the `Rectangle` maths used around it.
- Go mapping: `internal/uiauto/widget` — a `Base` struct `{ typ Type; rect Rect; flags Flags }` embedded in `ImageClx`, `ImageAnimatedClx`, `ArtText`, `Scrollbar`, `ArtTextButton`, `Edit`, `Text`, `Button`, `List`, plus an `Item` interface (`Type()`, `Rect()`, `Flags()`, `SetFlags`, `Hide/Show`, `IsHidden`, `IsNotInteractive`). Screens become `[]Item` where slice order is both paint and hit-test order. `UiListItem` → `*ListItem`; `StringOrView` → a small `TextOrView{ view string; owned string }`; `DrawStringFormatArg` → `[]FormatArg`; `ClxSprite`/`ClxSpriteList` → the `internal/render` sprite types.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `Callback = void(*)()` free function pointers are used everywhere by the sel* screens, including `nullptr` actions for hidden buttons (e.g. selconn.cpp:92) — the Go port must guard nil-func calls. (2) `indexAt` asserts on out-of-range y; the Go port should clamp/error instead, but must keep `(y-rect.y)/height` so mouse focus matches. (3) The `Uint16(item_height * viewportSize)` product can truncate — decide whether to mirror the truncation (pixel-parity) or widen to `int`.

### Source/appfat.cpp
- Purpose: Fatal-error handling: one shared "clean up networking, show an OK dialog, exit(1)" path plus the concrete error dialogs (generic error, assertion failure, log-file pointer, missing data archive, read-only directory).
- Public API: `void DisplayFatalErrorAndExit(std::string_view title, std::string_view body)` (62–67); `void app_fatal(std::string_view str)` (69–72); `void assert_fail(int nLineNo, const char *pszFile, const char *pszFail)` (75–79, `_DEBUG` only); `void ErrDlg(const char *title, std::string_view error, std::string_view logFilePath, int logLineNr)` (81–87); `void InsertCDDlg(std::string_view archiveName)` (89–96); `void DirErrorDlg(std::string_view error)` (98–104). Anonymous namespace (33–60): `bool Terminating = false` (36), `SDL_ThreadID CleanupThreadId` (39), `void FreeDlg()` (44–58).
- Depends on: `config.h` (7); SDL (`SDL_Delay`, `SDL_ThreadID`, `SDL_GetError` via the `ErrSdl` macro in the header) with `utils/sdl_thread.h` (`this_sdl_thread::get_id()`) and `utils/sdl_compat.h`/`sdl2_to_1_2_backports.h` for SDL1 (8–20); `diablo.h` (23, `diablo_quit`); `dvlnet/leaveinfo.hpp` (24, `leaveinfo_t::LEAVE_EXIT`); `multi.h` (25, `gbIsMultiplayer`); `storm/storm_net.hpp` (26, `SNetLeaveGame`, `SNetDestroy`); `utils/format.hpp` (27, `FormatRuntime`); `utils/language.h` (28, `_`); `utils/str_cat.hpp` (29, `StrCat`); `utils/ui_fwd.h` (30, `UiErrorOkDialog`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `FreeDlg()` order (44–58): if `Terminating` and the current thread id differs from `CleanupThreadId`, `SDL_Delay(20000)` (i.e. 20 000 ms = 20 s, deliberately parking the second thread so the first dialog stays visible); then set `Terminating = true` and `CleanupThreadId = this thread id` (49–50); if `gbIsMultiplayer` and `SNetLeaveGame(LEAVE_EXIT)` returns true, `SDL_Delay(2000)` (53–54); always `SNetDestroy()` (57).
  - `DisplayFatalErrorAndExit` = `FreeDlg()` → `UiErrorOkDialog(title, body)` → `diablo_quit(1)` (64–66): exit code is always 1 and the dialog is modal/blocking before exit.
  - `app_fatal(str)` → title `_("Error")`, body `str` (71).
  - `assert_fail` → `app_fatal(StrCat("assertion failed (", pszFile, ":", nLineNo, ")\n", pszFail))` (77) — file, then line, then the stringified expression after a newline.
  - `ErrDlg` body = `FormatRuntime` of `"{:s}\n\nThe error occurred at: {:s} line {:d}"` with `(error, logFilePath, logLineNr)` (85–86).
  - `InsertCDDlg` title `_("Data File Error")`, body `"Unable to open main data archive ({:s}).\n" "\n" "Make sure that it is in the game folder."` — a three-part concatenated literal (92–94).
  - `DirErrorDlg` title `_("Read-Only Directory Error")`, body `"Unable to write to location:\n{:s}"` (102).
- 1:1 constraints: `SDL_Delay(20000)` (47) and `SDL_Delay(2000)` (54); exit status `1` (66); the `\n\n` separator and `line {:d}` wording of the ErrDlg template (85); the two-step `\n` + `\n` + text concatenation of the CD message which yields exactly one blank line (92–94); `ErrSdl()` supplies the title `"SDL Error"`, `SDL_GetError()`, `__FILE__`, `__LINE__` (appfat.h:14); assert text format `assertion failed (file:line)\nexpr` (77); `SNetLeaveGame` is only awaited (2 s) when it returns true (53–54).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: the two file statics `Terminating` (36) and `CleanupThreadId` (39) are the only synchronisation and there is no lock: the first caller records its thread and proceeds to the dialog; a second caller from another thread sleeps 20 s and then also runs `SNetLeaveGame`/`SNetDestroy` (a double-destroy race upstream). Everything else is single-threaded UI + `exit(1)`. No RNG, no serialization.
- Test coverage: `test/appfat_test.cpp` — `EXPECT_EXIT` cases: `app_fatal("test")` exits 1 printing "test"; `ErrDlg("Title","Unknown error","appfat.cpp",7)` prints `"Unknown error\n\nThe error occurred at: appfat.cpp line 7"`; `InsertCDDlg("diabdat.mpq")` prints the archive name; `DirErrorDlg("/")` prints `"Unable to write to location:\n/"`. They rely on the test-only dialog stub `test/app_fatal_for_testing.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `pkg/fatal` (or `internal/appfatal`) — `func Fatal(title, body string)`, `func AppFatal(msg string)`, `func ErrDlg(title, err, file string, line int)`, `func InsertCDDlg(archive string)`, `func DirErrorDlg(path string)`; network cleanup maps to `net.LeaveGame(LeaveExit)` + `net.Destroy()`. The modal dialog needs a synchronous primitive (`dialog.ShowOKBlocking`) since the Ebiten game loop is the goroutine that must draw it; assertions become explicit `if !cond { fatal.AssertFail(file, line, "expr") }` at call sites, or a build-tagged helper, since Go has no `assert` macro.
- Risks/open questions: (1) The message strings are asserted verbatim by tests and pinned by translators' POT files — keep them byte-exact when converting `{:s}/{:d}` to Go formatting. (2) `UiErrorOkDialog` before exit requires a live renderer; if the fatal came from asset/SDL init the Go port needs a stderr fallback (upstream gets this from `app_fatal_for_testing.cpp` in tests only). (3) The 20 s cross-thread park is a UX device; in Go, blocking a non-main goroutine does not keep the dialog up — prefer "show dialog, then block forever until the dialog's OK handler calls exit".

### Source/appfat.h
- Purpose: Public interface for the fatal-error dialogs plus the project-wide `assert` and `ErrSdl` macros.
- Public API: macro `ErrSdl()` → `ErrDlg("SDL Error", SDL_GetError(), __FILE__, __LINE__)` (14); `#undef assert` (16) with `assert(exp)` → `((void)0)` when `!_DEBUG` (19) and `(void)((exp) || (::devilution::assert_fail(__LINE__, __FILE__, #exp), 0))` in debug builds (21); `[[noreturn]]` declarations `DisplayFatalErrorAndExit` (29), `app_fatal` (35), `assert_fail` (44, `_DEBUG` only), `ErrDlg` (49), `InsertCDDlg` (54), `DirErrorDlg` (59).
- Depends on: `<string_view>` (7), `utils/attributes.h` (9); it deliberately does *not* include SDL, so every `ErrSdl()` call site must have `SDL_GetError()` in scope.
- Requirements for Go port: the six noreturn functions with identical titles/templates, and an assertion story where release builds do not evaluate the condition and debug builds report `file:line` + the expression text.
- 1:1 constraints: `assert_fail`'s parameter order is `(line, file, expr)` at the macro (21) while the declaration reads `(int nLineNo, const char *pszFile, const char *pszFail)` (44) — the .cpp then composes `file` before `line` in the message, so both orders must be preserved; release `assert` expands to `((void)0)` so the expression is not evaluated (19); `#exp` stringification means the message contains the *source text* of the condition; `ErrSdl` hard-codes the title `"SDL Error"` (14).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `__FILE__` is the compiler-relative path and `__LINE__` the literal line, so edits change assertion text; upstream tests pass file/line explicitly instead of relying on real call sites. No state.
- Test coverage: `test/appfat_test.cpp` covers the functions; nothing tests the macro expansions.
- Go mapping: same package as appfat.cpp (`pkg/fatal`). Drop both macros: `fatal.ErrSDL(err error)` taking the error explicitly (Go has no global SDL error state — ebitengine/Ebiten errors are returned values), and real `panic`s or explicit `Assert(...)` calls at every site. Keep the noreturn contract by ending each path with `os.Exit(1)` after the dialog returns.
- Risks/open questions: the implicit "SDL must be included before this header" dependency means `ErrSdl()` cannot be mechanically translated; converting its dozens of call sites to pass an error value is a separate sweep and should be its own bean, not folded into this file's port.

### Source/automap.cpp
- Purpose: The automap/minimap overlay: loads per-tileset `.amp` tile-shape tables, maps dungeon tile ids to automap shapes, draws the iso diamond/line/pixel primitives for walls, doors, grates, arches, dirt, stairs, rivers, lava/acid and the pentagram, draws player arrows and item markers, renders the automap info text, and owns the automap state (active flag, scales, scroll offset, exploration array, minimap rect).
- Public API (link-visible, 1548–1963): globals `bool AutomapActive` (1548), `AutomapType CurrentAutomapType` (1549), `uint8_t AutomapView[DMAXX][DMAXY]` (1550), `int AutoMapScale` (1551), `int MinimapScale` (1552), `Displacement AutomapOffset` (1553), `Rectangle MinimapRect` (1554); functions `InitAutomapOnce()` (1556–1577), `InitAutomap()` (1579–1700), `StartAutomap()` (1702), `AutomapUp()` (1708), `AutomapDown()` (1714), `AutomapLeft()` (1720), `AutomapRight()` (1726), `AutomapZoomIn()` (1732), `AutomapZoomOut()` (1742), `DrawAutomap(const Surface &out)` (1752–1875), `UpdateAutomapExplorer(Point map, MapExplorationType)` (1877), `SetAutomapView(Point position, MapExplorationType)` (1883–1957), `AutomapZoomReset()` (1959). (`SetAutomapType`/`GetAutomapType` and `AmOffset`/`AmLine` are inline in `automap.h`.)
- Depends on: `automap.h` (`AutomapType`, `MapExplorationType` MAP_EXP_NONE/OLD/SHRINE/OTHERS/SELF, `AmWidthOffset`/`AmHeightOffset`/`AmLineLength`); `engine/render/automap_render.hpp` (`DrawMapLine{NS,WE,NE,SE,NW,SW}`, `DrawMapLineSteep{NE,SE,NW,SW}`, `DrawMapFreeLine`, `SetMapPixel`); `engine/render/primitive_render.hpp` (`DrawHorizontalLine`, `DrawVerticalLine`, `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo`); `engine/palette.h` (PAL8/`PAL16_*` base indices); `levels/gendung.h` (`dungeon[][]`, `dFlags[][]`, `DungeonFlag::Explored`), `gendung_defs.hpp` (`DMAXX/DMAXY/MAXDUNX/MAXDUNY`, `DTYPE_*`), `dun_tile.hpp` (`TILE_WIDTH 64`, `TILE_HEIGHT 32`); `levels/setmaps.h` (`setlevel`, `setlvlnum`); `quests.h`/`quests.cpp` (`Quests[]`, `Q_PWATER`, `_qslvl`, `_qactive`, `QUEST_DONE`); `player.h` (`MyPlayer`, `Players`, `Player::position/_pmode/_pdir/_pLvlChanging/plractive/friendlyMode/getId/isWalking/AnimInfo`, `GetOffsetForWalking`, `PM_WALK_SIDEWAYS`); `options.h` (`AutoMapShowItems`, `GetOptions().Graphics.showFPS`); `control/control.hpp` (`GetMainPanel()`); `diablo.h` (`currlevel`, `leveltype`, `gbIsMultiplayer`, `ViewPosition`, `GameName`, `GamePassword`, `PublicGame`, `IsLoopback`, difficulty enum); `engine/load_file.hpp` (`LoadFileInMem<AutomapTile>`); `engine/point.hpp` (`megaToWorld()`, `Point::operator+(Direction)`), `engine/rectangle.hpp`, `utils/ui_fwd.h`; `utils/{format,str_cat,language,utf8,is_of,enum_traits,attributes}.h*`, `function_ref.hpp`; `_DEBUG`: `debug.h` (`DebugGodMode`, `DebugInvisible`, `DebugVision`, `DebugPath`, `DebugGrid`, `DebugScrollViewEnabled`, `DisableLighting`, `ShouldHighlightDebugAutomapTile`, `IsDebugAutomapHighlightNeeded`), `lighting.h` (`IsTileLit`).

  - Raster walk (1842–1858): `map = {Automap.x - cells, Automap.y - 1}`; outer `i = 0..cells+1`; inner A `j = 0..cells-1` drawing `{map.x + j, map.y - j}` stepping `tile1.x += DoubleTileRight`; `map.y++`; inner B at `screen + FullTileLeft + FullTileDown`, `j = 0..cells`, same mapping, `tile2.x += DoubleTileRight`; `map.x++`; `screen.y += DoubleTileDown`. Start offsets: odd `cells` → `-DoubleTileRight*((cells-1)/2)`, `-DoubleTileDown*((cells+1)/2)`; even → `-DoubleTileRight*(cells/2) - FullTileLeft`, `-DoubleTileDown*(cells/2) - FullTileDown`; then odd `ViewPosition.x` → `-HalfTileRight`, `-HalfTileDown` and odd `ViewPosition.y` → `+HalfTileRight`, `-HalfTileDown`; then `screen.x/y += scale*myPlayerOffset/100/2` (1813–1831).
  - Item/player mapping: `px = i - 2*AutomapOffset.deltaX - ViewPosition.x`, `py = j - 2*AutomapOffset.deltaY - ViewPosition.y`; item `screen = {offX*scale/100/2 + (px-py)*AmLine(DoubleTile), offY*scale/100/2 + (px+py)*AmLine(FullTile)}` then `+GetAutomapScreen()`, panel shift `∓gnScreenWidth/4` (minimap exempt), `screen.y -= AmLine(FullTile)` (1294–1318); player base same but `(playerOffset + myPlayerOffset)` and `+ AmOffset(None, HalfTileUp).deltaY` in y (1356–1359).
  - Door tables (186–215, 234–263): CATHEDRAL/CRYPT line `QuarterTileLeft/QuarterTileUp` (V) or `None/HalfTileUp` (H), diamond `HalfTileLeft/HalfTileDown` or `HalfTileRight/HalfTileDown`, length `HalfTile`; CATACOMBS line `ThreeQuartersTileLeft/QuarterTileDown` or `QuarterTileRight/QuarterTileUp`, diamond `None/None`, length `FullTile`; CAVES line `QuarterTileLeft/ThreeQuartersTileDown` or `QuarterTileLeft/QuarterTileDown`, diamond `HalfTileRight/HalfTileDown` or `HalfTileLeft/HalfTileDown`, length `FullTile`; default `app_fatal("Invalid leveltype")`. Line drawn only when `!neighbour.hasFlag(*Passage) || leveltype != DTYPE_CATHEDRAL` (218, 267). Duplicate unreachable `break` after the CAVES case (262–263) — cosmetic.
  - Grate dots: positions `HalfTileLeft ± EighthTile{Right,Up/Left,Down}` (vertical) and `HalfTileRight ± EighthTile{Left,Up/Right,Down}` (horizontal), each drawn as colour 0 at `+{0,1}` first, then `colorDim` at the position (636–648, 653–665) — order matters.
  - `DrawStairs`: `NumStairSteps = 4` (574), step `AmOffset(QuarterTileLeft, QuarterTileDown)` (575), start `QuarterTileLeft/QuarterTileUp` or `QuarterTileLeft/ThreeQuartersTileUp` for CATACOMBS|HELL (577–582), line `AmLine(DoubleTile)` (586).
  - `DrawMapEllipse`: `a = radius`, `b = radius/2`, `from.x -= radius` (842–845), initial pixels at `(from.x, from.y±b)` (848–849), `p1 = b*b - a*a*b + (a*a)/4` (852), region-1 guard `(b*b*x) < (a*a*y)` (855) with the two `p1` update formulas (857–862), `p2 = b*b*(x+1)^2 + a*a*(y-1)^2 - a*a*b*b` (871), region-2 `while (y > 0)` with its two update branches (873–881), and 4-way mirrored `SetMapPixel` in both regions.
  - `DrawMapStar`: `scaleFactor = 128` (892), `from.x -= radius` (896), anchors `(∓121, +19)`, `(0, +64)`, `(∓75, −51)` each as `coef * radius / 128` with integer division (898–902), and line order 3→1, 1→0, 0→4, 4→2, 2→3 (905–909). Pentagram radius is `AmLine(OctupleTile)` and the shadow pass is offset `+{0,1}` in y only, drawn before the coloured pass (1238–1249).
  - `DrawHorizontal` default line start `None/HalfTileUp` with length `FullAndHalfTile`, switched to `QuarterTileRight/QuarterTileUp` + `FullTile` when a diamond is drawn (670–686); `DrawVertical` default `ThreeQuartersTileLeft/QuarterTileDown` + `FullAndHalfTile` with the caves/nest cross case moving to `HalfTileLeft/None` + `FullTile` (710–741); `DrawCaveHorizontal` line `HalfTileLeft/None/FullTile` for cross types else `ThreeQuartersTileLeft/QuarterTileUp/FullAndHalfTile` (778–788); `DrawCaveVertical` length `FullTile` for cross types else `FullAndHalfTile`, line start always `None/HalfTileDown` (812–821). Cave dirt pixel sets: 4 pixels at `ThreeQuartersTileLeft/QuarterTileDown`, `HalfTileLeft/HalfTileDown`, `QuarterTileLeft/ThreeQuartersTileDown`, `None/FullTileDown` (761–764) and `None/FullTileDown`, `QuarterTileRight/ThreeQuartersTileDown`, `HalfTileRight/HalfTileDown`, `ThreeQuartersTileRight/QuarterTileDown` (797–800), gated by `neighbour.hasFlag(Dirt) || (leveltype != DTYPE_TOWN && IsNoneOf(tile.type, wood types))`.
  - `DrawVertical` calls `FixVerticalDoor` twice (for `nwTile` and `neTile`) whereas `DrawHorizontal` calls both Fix functions (694–696, 722–724) — asymmetric and easy to "clean up" wrongly.
  - `.amp` paths verbatim, lowercase-with-backslash: `levels\towndata\automap.amp`, `levels\l1data\l1.amp`, `levels\l2data\l2.amp`, `levels\l3data\l3.amp`, `levels\l4data\l4.amp`, `nlevels\l6data\l6.amp`, `nlevels\l5data\l5.amp` (1526–1541).
  - Text overlay: origin `(8, 8)` (1429), advance `15 * numLines` (1432), strings `_("Game: ")` (1446), `_("Offline Game")` (1453), `_("Public Game")` (1455), `_("Password: ")` (1457), `_("Town")`, `_("Level: {:d}")`, `_("Level: Nest {:d}")` with `currlevel - 16` (1469), `_("Level: Crypt {:d}")` with `currlevel - 20` (1472), `_("Difficulty: {:s}")` (1496); `"0.0.0.0"`/`IsLoopback` skip rule (1445).
  - `SetAutomapView` world→map `{(x-16)/2, (y-16)/2}` with C++ truncating division toward zero (1885); `UpdateAutomapExplorer` monotonic-max write (1879–1880); `HasAutomapFlag`/`GetAutomapTileType` compare *y* against `DMAXX`, not `DMAXY` (917, 929).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: large mutable global set — `AutomapTypeTiles` (rebuilt per level load), `AutomapView[40][40]` (zeroed per level; written only with strictly increasing explorer values), `AutoMapScale`, `MinimapScale`, `AutomapOffset`, `MinimapRect`, `AutomapActive`, `CurrentAutomapType`, and the file-static `Point Automap` (36) recomputed at the top of every `DrawAutomap`. Because `AmOffset`/`AmLine` read `CurrentAutomapType` and the scale globals at call time, they are not pure functions of their arguments — the minimap/automap mode must be set before any draw, and `InitAutomapOnce` must run first (tests depend on scale 50 giving `AmLine(DoubleTile) == 16`, `test/automap_test.cpp:9-18`). Draw order is paint order (dirt → stairs → connections → per-type shape → players → items → text) and the `Fix*Door` functions exist only because later lines overwrite earlier bright pixels, so reordering changes output. No RNG and no serialization; `Types`/`Flags` are, however, read directly from `.amp` file bytes as `uint8_t`, making the enum's numeric order a file-format dependency. Everything runs on the render thread.
- Test coverage: `test/automap_test.cpp` — `InitAutomap` (asserts `AutomapActive == false`, `AutoMapScale == 50`, and the `AmLine` ladder `DoubleTile == FullTile raw`, `FullAndHalfTile == 6`, `HalfTile == Half raw`, `QuarterTile == 1`), `StartAutomap` (offset 0/0, active true), `AutomapUp/Down/Left/Right` (exact delta expectations), `AutomapZoomIn` (50→75 and the recomputed line lengths), `AutomapZoomIn_Max` (175→200, `AmLine(DoubleTile) == 32`), `AutomapZoomOut` (200→175, 28/14/7/3), `AutomapZoomOut_Min` (50→25, `AmLine(HalfTile) == 1`, `AmLine(QuarterTile) == 0`), `AutomapZoomReset`. Nothing covers `DrawAutomap`, `DrawAutomapTile`, `SetAutomapView`, or `InitAutomap`'s tile-override table; `test/drlg_l*_test.cpp` exercise the `dungeon`/`dFlags` inputs those consume.
- Go mapping: split into three packages. `internal/automap/state` — replace the globals with an explicit `Automap{ Active bool; Mode Type; Scale, MinimapScale int; Offset Displacement; MinimapRect Rect; View [40][40]uint8; Tiles [256]Tile }`, and turn the implicit scale lookup into a value: `type Scaler struct{ Mode Type; Scale, MinimapScale int }` with `Offset(w, h) image.Point` and `Line(len) int`, so minimap-vs-automap selection is passed in rather than read from a global. `internal/automap/tiles` — the `Tile`/`Flag` types, the `.amp` loader via `pkg/mpq`, and the per-leveltype override tables as data (`map[uint8]Tile` per tileset). `internal/automap/render` — the primitive wrappers (`SetMapPixel`, `DrawMapLine*`) from `internal/render`, the `DrawAutomapTile` dispatcher as a `switch`, and `DrawAutomap`'s raster loop; `DrawLava`/`DrawLavaRiver` (C++ `if constexpr` pixel masks) become generated tables of `{pixel, guard}` pairs so they can be golden-tested. Draw into an off-screen paletted/`ebiten.Image` layer with the same integer maths — do not use Ebiten vector primitives.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `Types` is loaded from disk as `uint8_t`, so its enumeration order is a byte-format contract; a "tidier" Go grouping silently breaks `.amp` loading. (2) `AutomapTypeTiles[i + 1] = tileTypes[i]` means amp byte 0 maps to tile id 1 and id 0 is never set — the classic port off-by-one. (3) `HasAutomapFlag`/`GetAutomapTileType` bound-check y against `DMAXX` (917, 929) while `GetAutomapTypeView` uses `DMAXY` — harmless at 40×40 but a latent bug the port must either mirror or fix deliberately. (4) `DrawMapVerticalDoor`/`DrawMapHorizontalDoor` `app_fatal` for TOWN/HELL/NEST/CRYPT (216, 265) — confirm the Go port can reach (or must reproduce) that fatal without crashing CI, and whether `DTYPE_CRYPT` folded into the cathedral branch is intentional. (5) No rendering tests exist upstream: recommend golden-image/hashing tests per tileset × scale × exploration type before starting the port. (6) The scale-from-global coupling (see notes) is the single biggest structural change a Go port must make; leaving it global keeps parity but makes the minimap/automap shared primitives order-dependent.

### Source/automap.h
- Purpose: Public interface of the in-game map overlay (automap + minimap). Declares the exploration-state array, zoom/scroll state, the tile-offset/line-length enums that encode automap geometry as fractions of a tile, and the automap draw/scroll/zoom API. Implementations live in `Source/automap.cpp` (1964 lines, covered in batch 003); this header also contains the only inline geometry helpers.
- Public API: `enum MapExplorationType : uint8_t {MAP_EXP_NONE, MAP_EXP_OLD, MAP_EXP_SHRINE, MAP_EXP_OTHERS, MAP_EXP_SELF}` (18–29). Globals: `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST bool AutomapActive` (32), `extern uint8_t AutomapView[DMAXX][DMAXY]` (34), `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST int AutoMapScale` (36), `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST int MinimapScale` (37), `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST Displacement AutomapOffset` (38), `extern Rectangle MinimapRect` (39). Enums `enum class AmWidthOffset : int8_t` (42–56), `enum class AmHeightOffset : int8_t` (58–72), `enum class AmLineLength : uint8_t` (74–81), `enum class AutomapType : uint8_t {Opaque, FIRST=Opaque, Transparent, Minimap, LAST=Minimap}` (83–89); `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST AutomapType CurrentAutomapType` (91). Inline functions: `SetAutomapType(AutomapType)` (95–98), `GetAutomapType()` (103–106), `AmOffset(AmWidthOffset, AmHeightOffset) -> Displacement` (110–114), `AmLine(AmLineLength) -> int` (116–120). Declared (defined in automap.cpp): `void SetAutomapType(AutomapType)` / `AutomapType GetAutomapType()` again (122–126), `InitAutomapOnce()` (131), `InitAutomap()` (136), `StartAutomap()` (141), `StartMinimap()` (146), `AutomapUp/Down/Left/Right()` (151–171), `AutomapZoomIn()` (176), `AutomapZoomOut()` (181), `DrawAutomap(const Surface&)` (186), `UpdateAutomapExplorer(Point, MapExplorationType)` (191), `SetAutomapView(Point, MapExplorationType)` (196), `AutomapZoomReset()` (201).
- Depends on: `engine/displacement.hpp` (`Displacement`), `engine/point.hpp` (`Point`), `engine/surface.hpp` (`Surface` by reference in `DrawAutomap`), `levels/gendung.h` → pulls `levels/gendung_defs.hpp` (`DMAXX`=40, `DMAXY`=40) and `levels/dun_tile.hpp` (`TILE_WIDTH`=64 line 7, `TILE_HEIGHT`=32 line 8) — both used only to size `AutomapView` and the offset enums. `utils/attributes.h` (`DVL_API_FOR_TEST`, which expands to nothing on non-MSVC — attributes.h:63). Consumed by `Source/automap.cpp` (globals defined at automap.cpp:1548–1554), `Source/control/*` (`CycleAutomapType`, `DoAutoMap`), `Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp`, `Source/player.cpp`/`Source/objects.cpp` (via `SetAutomapView`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Exploration state: a 40×40 byte array indexed `[x][y]` with the 5-level ordering NONE<OLD<SHRINE<OTHERS<SELF, and a monotonic "only upgrade" write (`UpdateAutomapExplorer` at automap.cpp:1877–1881 does `if (AutomapView[x][y] < explorer) AutomapView[x][y] = explorer;`). This ordering is semantically load-bearing (multiplayer who-explored-what rendering).
  - Global mutable automap state must be reachable from other packages: `AutomapActive` (on/off), `AutoMapScale`, `MinimapScale`, `AutomapOffset` (scroll in tile-ish units), `MinimapRect` (screen rect), `CurrentAutomapType`.
  - Automap type cycling: an enum with exactly 3 values and FIRST/LAST sentinels so callers can do `type = AutomapType(int(type + 1) > int(LAST) ? FIRST : type + 1)` (`CycleAutomapType`); `SetAutomapType` must NOT touch `AutomapActive` (documented at 93–94, 121–122, 128–129 and implemented as a pure assignment).
  - Geometry helpers used by every draw call in automap.cpp: `AmOffset(x, y)` and `AmLine(l)` — must pick the scale from `CurrentAutomapType` at call time (minimap scale vs automap scale) and apply integer `scale*value/100`.
  - API surface that the port must provide as callable functions: init-once (sets scale 50 + minimap rect/scale from screen size), tile-type table load (`InitAutomap`), open/close, 4 scroll directions, zoom in/out/reset, and `DrawAutomap(out)`.
  - `StartMinimap()` is declared here (146) but has no definition anywhere in `Source/` (grep of `StartMinimap` across `Source/`+`test/` returns only automap.h:148) — it is dead declaration; do not port.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `AmWidthOffset` values are bit-shift derived from TILE_WIDTH=64 (44–49): EighthTileRight=64>>4=4, QuarterTileRight=64>>3=8, HalfTileRight=64>>2=16, ThreeQuartersTileRight=(64>>1)-(64>>3)=32-8=24, FullTileRight=64>>1=32, DoubleTileRight=64; the Left variants are the negations (50–55) with `QuarterTileLeft` at 51 and None=0. Stored in `int8_t` — DoubleTileRight=64 fits.
  - `AmHeightOffset` from TILE_HEIGHT=32 (60–65): EighthTileDown=2, QuarterTileDown=4, HalfTileDown=8, ThreeQuartersTileDown=16-4=12, FullTileDown=16, DoubleTileDown=32; Up variants negated (66–71).
  - `AmLineLength` literal values (75–80): QuarterTile=2, HalfTile=4, FullTile=8, FullAndHalfTile=12, DoubleTile=16, OctupleTile=64. Note these are *hundredths-of-tile* factors, not pixels — see `AmLine`.
  - `AmOffset` formula (113): `{ scale * int(x) / 100, scale * int(y) / 100 }` — C++ integer division truncating toward zero, applied per-axis, and `scale` chosen by `(GetAutomapType() == AutomapType::Minimap) ? MinimapScale : AutoMapScale` (111). `AmLine` formula (120): `scale * int(l) / 100` with the same scale selection (118).
  - `MapExplorationType` is `uint8_t` and the enumerators are implicitly 0..4 in the written order (18–29); the comparison `<` in `UpdateAutomapExplorer` depends on exactly that ordering.
  - `AutomapType` is `uint8_t` with Opaque=0, Transparent=1, Minimap=2 (84–88).
  - `AutomapView` dimensions are `DMAXX][DMAXY]` = [40][40] (34), C-style row-major `[x][y]` (indexed as `AutomapView[map.x][map.y]`).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: All state here is process-global and mutated by the render/input path (`AutomapOffset` is clamped in-place inside `DrawAutomap`, automap.cpp:1752–1766 — i.e. drawing has side effects on scroll state). `AmOffset`/`AmLine` read `CurrentAutomapType`, `AutoMapScale`, `MinimapScale` implicitly, so their result depends on globals set during `InitAutomapOnce` (automap.cpp:1556–1577) and on zoom ops; calling them before init uses scale 0. No threads. `DVL_API_FOR_TEST` implies these are meant to be observable from unit tests → expose as exported Go vars/functions.
- Test coverage: `test/automap_test.cpp` (11 `TEST(...)` cases) covers this header directly: `Automap.InitAutomap` asserts `AutomapActive==false`, `AutoMapScale==50`, and the `AmLine` ladder (`AmLine(DoubleTile)==FullTile` as int, `AmLine(FullAndHalfTile)==6`, `AmLine(FullTile)==HalfTile`, `AmLine(HalfTile)==QuarterTile`, `AmLine(QuarterTile)==1`); `Automap.StartAutomap`, `AutomapUp/Down/Left/Right` assert the exact `AutomapOffset` deltas. Port these as Go tests.
- Go mapping: `internal/automap` (types + state + `AmOffset`/`AmLine` + the API decls), with the drawing implementation in the same package or `internal/automap/render`. Strategy: one Go package owning `View [40][40]uint8`, `Active bool`, `AutoMapScale/MinimapScale int`, `Offset Displacement`, `MinimapRect Rectangle`, `Type AutomapType`; keep `AmOffset`/`AmLine` as package funcs reading package state (1:1 with the implicit-global design) rather than threading a context, and port `test/automap_test.cpp` alongside.
- Risks/open questions:
  - The header declares `SetAutomapType`/`GetAutomapType` twice — once `inline` (95–106) and once non-inline (122–126); the inline definitions win and automap.cpp defines neither. A Go port must not re-create two versions.
  - `AmWidthOffset`/`AmHeightOffset` are `int8_t` enum classes whose negation is expressed as `-EighthTileRight` etc.; Go typed-const arithmetic will need explicit constants (no C++ implicit enum-from-negative-constant equivalent without care).
  - `StartMinimap()` has no implementation — confirm the minimap-open path uses `SetAutomapType(AutomapType::Minimap)` instead (batch 003 automap.cpp notes) before deciding the Go API shape.
  - `DrawAutomap` mutating `AutomapOffset` makes the function non-idempotent; a Go renderer that draws twice per frame (e.g. for a HUD pass) will drift scroll position.

### Source/capture.cpp
- Purpose: Screenshot implementation: pick a timestamped filename in the pref path, force one red-flashed frame, dump the global backbuffer to PCX or PNG, and hold the red flash for a fixed minimum time.
- Public API: `void CaptureScreen()` (85–122) — the only external symbol. Namespace-local (anonymous namespace, 38–81): `SDL_IOStream *CaptureFile(std::string *dstPath)` (45–66), `void RedPalette()` (72–81). Compile-time config macros: `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT_PCX 0` (23), `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT_PNG 1` (24), `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT` selects behavior (26–30, 47–52, 104–109).
- Depends on: `engine/palette.h` (`system_palette` — `std::array<SDL_Color,256>`, palette.h:74; `SystemPaletteUpdated()` palette.h:128); `engine/backbuffer_state.hpp` (`DrawAndBlit()`, `RedrawEverything()`); `engine/dx.h` (`GlobalBackBuffer()` — dx.h:24, `BltFast(nullptr,nullptr)`, `RenderPresent()`); `engine/render/scrollrt.h` (include at 34 — for `DrawAndBlit`/`RedrawEverything` path); `utils/surface_to_pcx.hpp` / `utils/surface_to_png.hpp` (`WriteSurfaceToFilePcx` / `WriteSurfaceToFilePng`, both taking `(const Surface&, SDL_IOStream*)` and returning `std::expected<void, std::string>`); `utils/file_util.h` (`FileExists(const char*)` line 20, `RemoveFile`); `utils/paths.h` (`paths::PrefPath()` line 10); `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat`, `LeftPad(value,length,padChar)` line 48); `utils/log.hpp` (`Log`, `LogError`); SDL `SDL_IOFromFile`, `SDL_GetTicks`, `SDL_Delay`, `SDL_GetError`, `SDL_ClearError`; `<ctime>` (`std::time`, `std::localtime`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Unique filename generation: base string `"Screenshot from YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS"` from *local* time (53–59); if `localtime` fails, fallback literal `"Screenshot"` (54, 60). Path = `PrefPath() + filename + ext` (61). Collision loop: `i=0; while (FileExists(path)) { i++; path = PrefPath()+filename+"-"+i+ext }` (62–66) → produces `...-1.pcx`, `...-2.pcx`, … Note the first retry uses `-1` and the non-colliding name has no suffix.
  - Extension is compile-time dependent: `.pcx` for PCX format, `.png` for PNG (46–52). The Go port needs one chosen format (or both behind a flag) and must keep the "filename extension matches encoder" invariant.
  - Open the output stream in write+truncate mode (`"wb"`, 66) *before* rendering; on failure log the SDL error, clear the SDL error, and return without touching the display (91–95).
  - Frame pipeline, in this exact order: `DrawAndBlit()` to get a fresh backbuffer (96) → snapshot `system_palette` into a local 256-entry copy (98) → `RedPalette()` (99) → restore palette (101) + `SystemPaletteUpdated()` (102) → encode `GlobalBackBuffer()` to the stream (104–109).
  - `RedPalette()` semantics (72–81): for all 256 palette entries set `g=0` and `b=0` leaving `r` untouched, then `SystemPaletteUpdated(); BltFast(nullptr,nullptr); RenderPresent();` — i.e. it forces a full-screen re-present with the red-only palette. This is the visible "flash".
  - Encode failure handling (111–116): if the encoder returns an error, `LogError` and `RemoveFile(fileName)` (delete the partial file); on success `Log("Screenshot saved at {}", fileName)`.
  - Minimum-flash pacing (117–120): measure `SDL_GetTicks()-startTime`; if elapsed `< 300` then `SDL_Delay(300 - elapsed)`. Then `RedrawEverything()` (121) to recover normal rendering.
  - The output stream is never closed in this file (SDL_IOStream leak on both success and failure paths) — decide whether the Go port fixes this (recommended: close) or preserves it.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Format selectors: `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT_PCX 0`, `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT_PNG 1` (23–24).
  - Filename layout (57–58): `LeftPad(tm_year+1900, 4, '0') + "-" + LeftPad(tm_mon+1, 2, '0') + "-" + LeftPad(tm_mday, 2, '0') + "-" + LeftPad(tm_hour, 2, '0') + "-" + LeftPad(tm_min, 2, '0') + "-" + LeftPad(tm_sec, 2, '0')`, prefix literal `"Screenshot from "` (56). Month is `tm_mon+1` (0-based → 1-based).
  - Palette loop bound is exactly `256` and only `g`/`b` are zeroed (74–77); `r` is preserved.
  - Palette snapshot is `std::array<SDL_Color, 256>` copy-by-value (98) — a full 256-entry restore, not just the modified entries.
  - Timing constant `300` ms appears twice (118, 119): `if (timePassed < 300) SDL_Delay(300 - timePassed)`. `startTime`/`timePassed` are `uint32_t` SDL tick wraps (88, 117) — subtraction must stay uint32 modular.
  - Collision suffix format: `"-" + i` where `i` starts at 1 on the first collision and increments (62–65); no zero padding (unlike vanilla's `screen??.pcx` mentioned in capture.h's stale comment).
  - Failure of `size`-related checks: none — this file has no size validation.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Reads and writes the global `system_palette` and the global backbuffer — must run on the render thread and be fully synchronous (it calls `BltFast`/`RenderPresent` and a blocking `SDL_Delay` up to 300 ms, which stalls the game loop deliberately so the red flash is visible). Non-reentrant: two simultaneous captures would share the collision counter only via the filesystem. Order of `DrawAndBlit()` vs `CaptureFile()` matters (file handle opened before the frame is produced, so a failed open skips all rendering work).
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln CaptureScreen test/` → no match; there is no `test/capture_test.cpp`).
- Go mapping: `internal/capture` (or `pkg/screenshot`) with an injected `PrefPath string`, `Palette` accessor, `Backbuffer` surface, and `Encoder func(io.Writer, *Surface) error` so tests can drive it without SDL. Strategy: keep the red-flash + 300 ms floor as an explicitly injectable clock/delay so it is testable; use `png.Encode` from stdlib if PNG is chosen, else port the PCX writer from `utils/surface_to_pcx.hpp`.
- Risks/open questions:
  - Which format is the project default? `DEVILUTIONX_SCREENSHOT_FORMAT` is defined by the build (`CMake`), not in this file — must confirm the active value before fixing the Go extension/encoder.
  - The SDL_IOStream is leaked; also `SDL_ClearError()` on the open-failure path (94) is a global side effect with no Go analogue.
  - `capture.h`'s comment ("screen??.pcx (00-99)", "red for 200ms") contradicts this implementation (timestamped names, 300 ms floor) — treat the code, not the comment, as the spec.
  - `LeftPad` is a lazy formatter type resolved inside `StrCat`; the Go port must reproduce zero-padding of a *year* to 4 digits (pre-1000 or post-9999 edge behavior unverified).

### Source/codec.cpp
- Purpose: Diablo's "codec" save-game encryption — a chained-SHA1 keystream XOR cipher over 64-byte blocks with an 8-byte trailer (checksum/error/last-chunk-size), used for hero/save files.
- Public API: `std::size_t codec_decode(std::byte *pbSrcDst, std::size_t size, const char *pszPassword)` (92), `std::size_t codec_get_encoded_len(std::size_t dwSrcBytes)` (130), `void codec_encode(std::byte *pbSrcDst, std::size_t size, std::size_t size64, const char *pszPassword)` (137). Anonymous-namespace internals: `struct CodecSignature {uint32_t checksum; uint8_t error; uint8_t lastChunkSize;}` (15–19), `constexpr size_t BlockSizeBytes = BlockSize*sizeof(uint32_t)` (21), `constexpr size_t SignatureSize = 8` (22), `SHA1Context CodecInitKey(const char*)` (24–52), `GetCodecSignature(std::byte*)` (56–63), `SetCodecSignature(std::byte*, CodecSignature)` (65–76), `ByteSwapBlock(uint32_t*)` (78–82), `XorBlock(const uint32_t*, uint32_t*)` (84–88).
- Depends on: `appfat.h` (`app_fatal`), `sha.h` (`SHA1Context`, `SHA1Calculate`, `SHA1Result`, `BlockSize`=16, `SHA1HashSize`=5 — sha.h:13–14; the "X-SHA-1" is *flawed* SHA1: sha.cpp uses sign-extending/arithmetic right shift in `SHA1CircularShift` and the message schedule is `w[i]=w[i-16]^w[i-14]^w[i-8]^w[i-3]` with no rotation, and there is no padding/length append — `SHA1Calculate` takes a raw 16-word block). `utils/endian_read.hpp` (`LoadLE32` — 4 bytes little-endian, endian_read.hpp:24–29), `utils/endian_swap.hpp` (`Swap32LE` → `SDL_Swap32LE`, endian_swap.hpp:31–37). `utils/log.hpp` (`LogError` at 121). Callers: `Source/pfile.cpp` (173–178 encode `hero` with `pfile_get_password()`; 628 decode), `Source/loadsave.cpp` (200, 251–253).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `CodecInitKey(password)`: build a 16-word buffer by re-reading the password bytes repeatedly until 64 bytes are consumed — reset the read index `j=0` whenever `pszPassword[j]=='\0'`, then `pw[i]=LoadLE32(&pszPassword[j]); j+=4` (26–33). Then `{SHA1Calculate(context,pw); SHA1Result(context,digest)}` on a fresh context (35–40). Then seed a 16-word key table with the fixed constants below and XOR each word with `digest[(i+3)%5]` (42–50). Then `SHA1Calculate(context,key)` on a fresh context and return that context (51–53) — i.e. the returned context's chaining state is the starting keystream.
  - Block loop for decode (103–111), per 64-byte block: copy block into `uint32 buf[16]`; byteswap the block (LE→host); `SHA1Result(context,dst)` (grab *current* state); `XorBlock(dst,buf)`; `SHA1Calculate(context,buf)` (feed the *plaintext* block back as the next message block); byteswap back; write to output. In-place over the same buffer.
  - Block loop for encode (148–161) has the SHA1/XOR order reversed: byteswap; `SHA1Result(context,dst)`; `SHA1Calculate(context,buf)`; `XorBlock(dst,buf)`; byteswap; write full 64 bytes (the tail of the last block is zero-padded by the `memset(buf,0,sizeof(buf))` at 150 before the partial `memcpy(...,chunk)`).
  - Trailer handling: decode validates `size > SignatureSize` and `size % BlockSize == 0` after subtracting 8, returning 0 on either failure (98–102); then reads the 8-byte signature from the position after the last processed block (114) and returns 0 if `sig.error > 0` (115–117); then compares `sig.checksum` against `dst[0]` from a final `SHA1Result` and returns 0 on mismatch after logging (119–124); final returned decoded length = `size + sig.lastChunkSize - BlockSizeBytes` (126).
  - `codec_get_encoded_len(n)` = round `n` up to a multiple of 64, then `+8` (130–135).
  - `codec_encode` validates `size64 == codec_get_encoded_len(size)` and calls `app_fatal("Invalid encode parameters")` otherwise (143–144); writes trailer via `SetCodecSignature` at the position after the last block, with `checksum = tmp[0]` (the first word of the final SHA1 state), `error = 0`, `lastChunkSize = uint8(last chunk byte count)` (162–167).
  - Secret zeroing: `memset(buf, 0, sizeof(buf))` after the loops (113, 162) and `memset(dst, 0, sizeof(dst))` on checksum mismatch (122) — Go port should still zero its scratch buffers to keep the same hygiene.
  - Callers expect `codec_decode` to return 0 for "wrong password/corrupt", and a positive byte length otherwise, plus a `*pdwLen` out-param pattern (`pfile.cpp:628–633`).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `BlockSizeBytes = 16 * sizeof(uint32_t) = 64`; `SignatureSize = 8` (21–22 with sha.h:13–14).
  - The hard-coded 16-word key table (43–46), exact decimal values as read from file: `2908958655, 4146550480, 658981742, 1113311088, 3927878744, 679301322, 1760465731, 3305370375, 2269115995, 3928541685, 580724401, 2607446661, 2233092279, 2416822349, 4106933702, 3046442503` (= 0xAD632FBF, 0xF72756D0, 0x2747436E, 0x425BC770, 0xEA1EAC58, 0x287D50CA, 0x68EE9343, 0xC503F307, 0x873FF65B, 0xEA28C9F5, 0x229D26B1, 0x9B6A7A85, 0x851A48B7, 0x900DC84D, 0xF4CAD5C6, 0xB5950607).
  - Key mixing index is `(i + 3) % SHA1HashSize` with `SHA1HashSize = 5` (47–49) — must be `(i+3)%5`, not `%16`.
  - `XorBlock` uses `shaResult[i % SHA1HashSize]` → the 16 words XOR against a 5-word state cycling 0,1,2,3,4,0,1,… (84–88).
  - `SetCodecSignature` byte order (65–76): checksum written LSB-first by explicit shifts `>>0, >>8, >>16, >>24`, then `error`, then `lastChunkSize`, then two zero bytes. So the trailer is 8 bytes little-endian checksum + 2 flag bytes + 2 hard zeros.
  - `GetCodecSignature` reads `checksum = LoadLE32(src)` then `error = byte[4]`, `lastChunkSize = byte[5]` (56–63); bytes 6–7 are ignored.
  - `CodecInitKey` password refill rule: `if (pszPassword[j]=='\0') j = 0;` is tested *at the start of each 4-byte read*, so a password shorter than 4 bytes can restart mid-word and mix in bytes of the next cycle (28–32).
  - Decode guard order is exact: `size <= 8 → 0`; `size -= 8`; `size % 64 != 0 → 0` (98–102). Encode guard: `size` is the *plaintext* length and `size64` the encoded length.
  - Final length formula: `size += sig.lastChunkSize - BlockSizeBytes` evaluated with `size` = encoded body length (i.e. multiple of 64) — 126.
  - Decode order per block is Result→XOR→Calculate; encode order is Result→Calculate→XOR (104–110 vs 152–156). Getting this wrong breaks compatibility with existing saves.
  - `error > 0` (not `!= 0`) is the failure test (115).
  - Encode always writes a full 64-byte block per iteration, including padding the final partial block with zeros (150–157).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Fully deterministic, no globals, no RNG, no time. Not thread-safe only in the sense of in-place mutation of the caller's buffer. `SHA1Context` carries mutable chaining state across blocks — the keystream is stateful and order-dependent, so blocks must be processed strictly front-to-back. `app_fatal` on a bad parameter set is a hard exit (not an error return) — the Go port must decide between `panic` and an error return (behavioral difference for corrupt-save handling).
- Test coverage: `test/codec_test.cpp` — only `TEST(Codec, codec_get_encoded_len)` expects `codec_get_encoded_len(50) == 72` and `TEST(Codec, codec_get_encoded_len_eq)` expects `codec_get_encoded_len(128) == 136`. There is **no** encode/decode round-trip test anywhere in `test/`; the Go port should add one (encode→decode identity, wrong-password → 0, truncated-block → 0, checksum-flip → 0) since the C++ suite does not protect the cipher core.
- Go mapping: `internal/codec` (pure, no SDL, no engine deps) plus `internal/sha1x` for the Diablo-flawed SHA1 primitive (must expose a stateful `Result([5]uint32)` / `Calculate([16]uint32)` pair, not Go's `crypto/sha1`). Strategy: `func EncodedLen(n int) int`, `func Decode(dst []byte, password string) (int, error)`, `func Encode(buf []byte, size int, size64 int, password string)`; use `binary.LittleEndian` for the trailer and `encoding/binary`-equivalent word loading for the password; keep byte-swap explicit so big-endian hosts behave identically. Golden-file test with a C++-produced encoded hero file is the real acceptance gate.
- Risks/open questions:
  - Go's `uint32` shifts are logical; the C++ "SHA1" deliberately uses *arithmetic* (sign-extending) right shifts — the port must special-case sign extension in the circular shift (see `Source/sha.cpp` note at lines 8–10 and `SHA1CircularShift`), otherwise digests differ and every existing save fails to decode.
  - The password is `const char*` with no length; trailing-NUL reset semantics (28–30) must be reproduced exactly for the exact password strings from `pfile_get_password()` (`PASSWORD_SPAWN_*` etc.) — need those literals ported too.
  - `codec_decode` returns `size_t` and callers treat 0 as failure; the "checksum mismatch" path logs but the C++ `LogError` is a no-op for behavior — confirm no save-migration path depends on the log.
  - `*reinterpret_cast<uint32_t *>(tmp)` (164) aliases a `uint32[5]` — reads `tmp[0]`; in Go just `tmp[0]`, no aliasing needed, but verify that's the intent (it is, per `GetCodecSignature` symmetry).

- 1:1 constraints: N/A — trivial (parameter naming differs slightly between decl `size_64` here (14) and def `size64` in codec.cpp (137); irrelevant to behavior).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: none.
- Test coverage: `test/codec.cpp` exercises the implementations via this header (`test/codec_test.cpp` includes `"codec.h"`).
- Go mapping: collapses into `internal/codec`'s exported API; no separate file.

Definitions of these symbols are spread across `control_panel.cpp` (globals at 34–49, button rects at 74/84, `CalculatePanelAreas`, `GetMainPanel`, `DrawPanelBox`, `FocusOnCharInfo`, `OpenCharPanel`, `DrawMainPanelButtons`, `ResetMainPanelButtons`, `DrawDeathText`, `DrawDurIcon`, `RedBack`, `ReleaseChrBtns`, `CheckChrBtns`, `PanelPaddingHeight` at 105 = 16), `control_infobox.cpp` (`InfoString`/`FloatingInfoString` at 23–24, `AddInfoBoxString`, `CheckPanelInfo`), `control_chat.cpp`, `control_flasks.cpp`, `control_gold.cpp` (`DropGoldFlag` at 15), `panels/spell_book.cpp` (`DrawSpellBook`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - This file is a *contract of shared mutable UI state*, not logic. The Go port must provide one package (or a small set) exporting the panel flags (`MainPanelFlag`, `ChatFlag`, `SpellbookFlag`, `CharFlag`, `SpellSelectFlag`, `DropGoldFlag`, `MainPanelButtonDown`, `LevelButtonDown`, `CharPanelButtonActive`, `CharPanelButton[4]`), the info-box text pair (`InfoString` with `StringOrView` semantics: a borrowed view or an owned string — in Go, `string` is already cheap so an owned string suffices, but keep the two separate fields), `InfoColor` (a `UiFlags` value chosen by callers), and `SpellbookTab`.
  - Panel geometry: `SidePanelSize = (320, 352)` and `InfoBoxRect = {{177,46},{288,64}}` must be exported constants; `GetMainPanel/GetLeftPanel/GetRightPanel` return *references* to rectangles recomputed by `CalculatePanelAreas()` — in Go, either return a value copy plus an explicit "layout generation" counter, or document that the returned rect must not be cached across a resize.
  - `CanPanelsCoverView()` is a view-coverage predicate combining screen size with the main panel size and `SidePanelSize.height`; must be re-implemented exactly (see constraint below) because gameplay uses it to decide whether to dim/redraw the world behind panels.
  - Function groups that must all exist as panel API entry points: (a) panel lifecycle `InitMainPanel` (returns an error string on art-load failure), `DrawMainPanel`, `FreeControlPan`; (b) mouse-hover vs mouse-up dispatch pairs for each clickable region (`CheckMainPanelButton`/`CheckMainPanelButtonUp`/`CheckMainPanelButtonDead`, `CheckLevelButton`/`CheckLevelButtonUp`, `CheckMuteButton`/`CheckMuteButtonUp`, `CheckChrBtns`/`ReleaseChrBtns`); (c) info-box producer/consumer (`AddInfoBoxString(str, floatingBox)` writes `InfoString` or `FloatingInfoString`; `DrawInfoBox`/`DrawFloatingInfoBox` render them and `CheckPanelInfo` recomputes them from mouse position); (d) automap toggles `DoAutoMap` and `CycleAutomapType` (bridging to `internal/automap`); (e) chat (forward-declared here, implemented in control_chat.cpp); (f) flasks (control_flasks.cpp); (g) gold split dialog (`OpenGoldDrop(invIndex, max)`, `CloseGoldDrop`, `control_drop_gold(vkey)`, `HandleGoldDropTextInputEvent`, `DrawGoldSplit`).
  - Two overloads of `AddInfoBoxString` (view / rvalue) collapse into one Go function taking `string`.
  - `DVL_API_FOR_TEST` marks the symbols tests poke directly (`CharPanelButton`, `CharPanelButtonActive`, `CharPanelButtonRect`, `SpellbookFlag`, `CharFlag`, `SpellSelectFlag`) → these must be exported in Go (capitalized) rather than package-private.
  - `InitMainPanel` returning `std::expected<void, std::string>` maps to Go `error` with the message string preserved (the caller shows it to the user).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `SidePanelSize { 320, 352 }` (38) and `InfoBoxRect { {177,46},{288,64} }` (40) are exact pixel layout constants.
  - `CanPanelsCoverView()` (87–88): `GetScreenWidth() <= mainPanel.size.width && GetScreenHeight() <= SidePanelSize.height + mainPanel.size.height` — note the asymmetric combination (panel height *plus* side-panel height on the vertical axis only) and `<=` (not `<`).
  - Array sizes are load-bearing: `CharPanelButton[4]`, `CharPanelButtonRect[4]`, `MainPanelButtonRect[8]` (42, 52–53) — the 8 and 4 indices are used as button IDs elsewhere.
  - `ReleaseChrBtns(bool addAllStatPoints)` (141) and `DrawLifeFlaskLower/DrawManaFlaskLower(..., bool drawFilledPortion)` (172, 184) carry behavior in their boolean args; `OpenGoldDrop(int8_t invIndex, int max)` (204) takes an `int8_t` inventory index (signed, small).
  - `PanelPaddingHeight` is *not* declared here but is `16` (`control_panel.cpp:105`) and is implicitly part of every panel-rect computation, including `InfoBoxRect` usage in `control_infobox.cpp:394` and `sgbPlrTalkTbl` in control_chat.cpp:226.
  - `CharPanelButtonRect[4]` is declared twice in this one file (53 and 147) — a real duplication; there is still exactly one definition (`control_panel.cpp:74`).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Order-of-init matters: `BottomBuffer` and `GoldBoxBuffer` are `std::optional`-owned surfaces that are empty until `InitMainPanel()` runs (defined at control_panel.cpp:48–49) and are reset in `FreeControlPan()`; the flask code dereferences `BottomBuffer` unconditionally (`control_flasks.cpp:49, 92`), so drawing before init is UB in C++ and a nil panic in Go. Panel rectangles are recomputed by `CalculatePanelAreas()` on resize — every consumer reads the globals, so a stale copy is a layout bug. `MainPanelFlag`/`ChatFlag`/`CharFlag`/`SpellbookFlag`/`SpellSelectFlag`/`DropGoldFlag` form a mutually-visible modal state machine driven from the input loop; all of it is single-threaded game-loop state. No RNG and no time dependence in this header.
- Test coverage: indirectly — `test/char_panel_test.cpp` and `test/panel_state_test.cpp` exist (and `grep` shows no `TEST(` macro hits inside them, i.e. they are fixture/support files rather than standalone cases; `test/automap_test.cpp` covers `CycleAutomapType`'s target state). No direct test of `CanPanelsCoverView`, `CalculatePanelAreas`, `GetPanelPosition`, `DrawPanelBox`, `CheckPanelInfo`, or the chat/flask/gold entry points was found in `test/`.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/panel` (geometry + flags + lifecycle) as the owner of the shared state, with sub-packages `internal/ui/infobox`, `internal/ui/chat`, `internal/ui/flasks`, `internal/ui/golddrop`, `internal/ui/charpanel`, `internal/ui/spellbook` for the implementations. Strategy: this header becomes mostly a *doc manifest*; make the flags explicit fields of a `Panel` struct rather than package globals if a single owner is acceptable, otherwise keep globals to preserve 1:1 call sites. The `SDL_Rect` parameter of `DrawPanelBox` should become a Go `Rectangle` to drop the SDL dependency.
- Risks/open questions:
  - `GetLeftPanel`/`GetRightPanel`/`IsLeftPanelOpen`/`IsRightPanelOpen` are declared here but the left/right panel rendering may not exist in this codebase's Hellfire path — verify which are actually referenced before porting (they are absent from the batch-003 file list).
  - Should `CharPanelButtonRect`'s duplicate declaration (53, 147) be treated as two symbols? No — collapse to one.
  - `StringOrView` vs plain `string`: the C++ code deliberately avoids allocation for hover text that points into static tables (e.g. item names). In Go this is a non-issue, but any test that compares identity (not equality) of `InfoString` would change behavior.
  - `DrawPanelBox` takes `SDL_Rect`; a Go port that changes the signature to the engine's rect type must update every caller (control_chat.cpp:98–108, control_infobox.cpp:394) consistently.
