  - `DrawChatBox`: bail immediately when `!ChatFlag` (92–93). Then blit the chat-region of the panel cel in 6 groups in this exact order and with these exact src/target rects, each offset vertically by `sgbPlrTalkTbl` on the source side (98–108): (1) `{175, sgb+20, 294, 5}` → `mainPanelPos+{175,4}`; (2) a 10-iteration loop building a left-slanted feather edge: `off` 0..9 with src width `i` from 293 down to 284, src x `175+off/2`, src y `sgb+off+25`, height 1 → target `{175+off/2, off+9}`; (3) `{185, sgb+35, 274, 30}` → `{185,19}`; (4) `{180, sgb+65, 284, 5}` → `{180,49}`; (5) a 10-iteration loop widening the bottom edge: src `{180, sgb+i+70, i+284, 1}` → target `{180, i+54}`; (6) `{170, sgb+80, 310, 55}` → `{170,64}`.
  - Then draw `TalkMessage` into rect `{ {mainPanelPos.x+200, mainPanelPos.y+10}, {250, 39} }` with flags `ColorWhite|PentaCursor`, `lineHeight 13`, and cursor/selection positions taken from `ChatCursor` (110–118), and **truncate the live input to what actually fit**: `ChatInputState->truncate(len)` where `len` is the width-clamped drawn length returned by `DrawString` (120). This is a write-back-on-render side effect the Go port must reproduce (typing beyond the box silently drops the tail).
  - Then, for each player slot except `MyPlayer` (122–155): compute `talkPanPosition = mainPanelPos + {172, 84 + 18*talkBtn}`; pick the whisper-button sprite with the two-branch table described below; overlay the translated label sprite from `TalkButton`; and if `player.plractive` draw the name at `{x+46 …}` i.e. `mainPanelPos.x+200+46` … precisely `x` was advanced by 46 at 121 → name rect `{ {x, y+60+18*talkBtn}, {204, 0} }` with color `ColorWhitegold` when `player.friendlyMode` else `ColorRed` (128–152). `talkBtn` increments only for non-self players (155) and is bounded by `TalkButtonsDown[3]` — i.e. at most 3 whisper buttons are drawn/handled.
  - `ResetChatMessage` (36–49): first give `CheckChatCommand(TalkMessage)` a chance to swallow the input (return if handled); otherwise build a bitmask `pmask` over `WhisperList[i]` (bit i set for each whispered-to player) across `Players.size()` slots and `NetSendCmdString(pmask, TalkMessage)`. An all-zero mask means broadcast (vanilla semantics: 0 = everyone) — this is the whisper mechanism.
  - `ControlPressEnter` (51–76): if the message is non-empty, send it, then insert into history with de-dup: scan `TalkSave[0..7]` for an exact `strcmp` match; if not found, `strcpy` into `TalkSave[NextTalkSave]` and advance `NextTalkSave = (NextTalkSave+1) & 7`; if found at index `i` and `i != (NextTalkSave-1)&7`, then move the most-recent entry into slot `i` and write the *current input value* into the most-recent slot (both via `strcpy`/`BufCopy` with explicit `'\0'`). Then clear `TalkMessage[0]` and set `TalkSaveIndex = NextTalkSave`. Finally `ResetChat()` (75) regardless of emptiness.
  - `ControlUpDown(v)` (78–88): history cycling. Repeatedly `TalkSaveIndex = (v + TalkSaveIndex) & 7` up to 8 times and stop at the first non-empty `TalkSave[...]`, assigning it into `ChatInputState`. With `v=1` (down) and `v=-1` (up) the `&7` masking on a `uint8_t` makes it wrap — negative `v` relies on unsigned wraparound.
  - `TypeChatMessage` (212–233): gate on `IsChatAvailable()`; set `ChatFlag=true`; clear `TalkMessage[0]`; construct `ChatInputState` with options `{value: TalkMessage (borrowed buffer), cursor: &ChatCursor, maxLength: sizeof(TalkMessage)-1}` (i.e. max 79 chars); clear all 3 `TalkButtonsDown`; set `sgbPlrTalkTbl = GetMainPanel().size.height + PanelPaddingHeight` (226); `RedrawEverything()`; `TalkSaveIndex = NextTalkSave` (228); set the SDL text-input area to `mainPanelPos + {200, 22}` with size `{0, 27}` and cursor 0 (230–231); start SDL text input (232).
  - `ResetChat` (235–243): `ChatFlag=false`; stop SDL text input; reset `ChatCursor = {}`; drop `ChatInputState` to nullopt; `sgbPlrTalkTbl = 0`; `RedrawEverything()`.
  - `IsChatActive` (245–254) = `IsChatAvailable() && ChatFlag`. `IsChatAvailable` (309–312) = `gbIsMultiplayer` — chat is single-player-disabled.
  - `CheckKeypress(vkey)` (256–280): bail if chat unavailable or inactive; ESC → `ResetChat()` and consume; RETURN or KP_ENTER → `ControlPressEnter()` and consume; DOWN → `ControlUpDown(1)`; UP → `ControlUpDown(-1)`; default → consume only when `vkey >= SDLK_SPACE && vkey <= SDLK_Z` (this is what lets printable keys through to SDL text input rather than triggering gameplay hotkeys).
  - `DiabloHotkeyMsg(dwMsg)` (282–307): `assert(dwMsg < QuickMessages.size())` (284, 10 quick messages). In `_DEBUG` builds only: for each configured message beginning with `"/lua "`, open the console and run the remainder as a Lua chunk (287–292) — a debug console hook. Then if chat is unavailable, return (294–296). Otherwise for each configured message (skipping `/lua ` ones in debug) copy it into a `char[MAX_SEND_STR_LEN]` via `CopyUtf8` and broadcast with mask `0xFFFFFF` (305).
  - `CheckMuteButton` (159–182): gate `ChatFlag`; take `MuteButtonRect`, reposition it via `SetPanelObjectPosition(UiPanels::Main, buttons)`, then grow its height to `MuteButtons*h + (MuteButtons-1)*padding` = `3*16 + 2*2 = 52`; if `MousePosition` is outside, return false; else clear all `TalkButtonsDown` and set `TalkButtonsDown[(MousePosition.y - (69 + mainPanelPos.y)) / 18] = true`; return true. (The `69` is the rect's y and the `18` is the hardcoded row pitch — they must match the rect constants.)
  - `CheckMuteButtonUp` (184–210): gate `ChatFlag`; clear all `TalkButtonsDown`; recompute the same grown rect; if mouse outside, return; `off = (MousePosition.y - rect.y) / (MuteButtonRect.height + padding)` = `/18`; walk `playerId` from 0 over `Players.size()` decrementing `off` for every slot that is not `MyPlayerId`; when `off` hits -1 stop; if `playerId > 0 && playerId <= Players.size()` toggle `WhisperList[playerId-1]`. This maps a visible button row to the correct player slot skipping self.
  - `HandleTalkTextInputEvent` (314–317) delegates to the templated `HandleInputEvent` which dispatches to `HandleTextInputEvent` for `TextInputState`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Buffer sizes: `MAX_SEND_STR_LEN == 80` (msg.h:22) → `TalkMessage[80]`, `TalkSave[8][80]`, `maxLength = sizeof(TalkMessage)-1 == 79` (219). `MAX_PLRS == 4` (multi.h:26) for `WhisperList`.
  - History ring is exactly 8 entries with `& 7` masking on `uint8_t` indices, used in three places: insertion (60–61), the "most recent" computation `NextTalkSave - 1` then `& 7` (65–66), and cycling `(v + TalkSaveIndex) & 7` (80).
  - Chat box blit table (98–108) — all coordinates quoted above, including the two asymmetric 10-iteration loops (`for i=293; i>283; off++, i--` and `for i=0; i<10`) whose widths are `i` (293..284) and `i+284` (284..293) respectively.
  - Vertical source offset `sgbPlrTalkTbl` is added to the *source* y of every blit while the target y is fixed (98–108) — that is the "panel grows downward into the chat region" trick; `sgbPlrTalkTbl` is either 0 (closed) or `GetMainPanel().size.height + 16` (open) (226, 241).
  - Sprite-index table for whisper buttons (134–149): when `WhisperList[i]` is true and pressed → `talkButtons[talkBtn==0 ? 2 : 3]` plus `TalkButton[2]` overlay at `{+4,-15}`; when not whispered → base `talkButtons[talkBtn==0 ? 0 : 1]`, `+4` if pressed (held sprites are indices 4 and 5), plus overlay `TalkButton[TalkButtonsDown[talkBtn] ? 1 : 0]` at `{+4,-15}`. Comment at 134/142 explains index 0 vs 1 differ because of the devil-wing tip.
  - `MuteButtonRect {{172,69},{61,16}}`, `MuteButtons=3`, `MuteButtonPadding=2` (32–34); row pitch `18` appears both in draw (130, 152) and hit-testing (180, 200); name rect width `204`, message rect `{250,39}`, `lineHeight 13` (113–116).
  - Broadcast masks: whisper mask is the per-player bit accumulation `pmask |= 1 << i` (44–47); quick-message mask is the literal `0xFFFFFF` (305).
  - Key range predicate `vkey >= SDLK_SPACE && vkey <= SDLK_Z` (278) — includes `!"#$%&'()*+,-./` and digits and `:;<=>?@` and brackets, and excludes anything above `Z` (lowercase letters arrive via text-input events, not keysyms).
  - SDL text input area `{GetMainPanel().position.x+200, +y+22, w=0, h=27}` with cursor 0 (230–231); width 0 is intentional (height-only clip).
  - Lua prefix literal is `"/lua "` (5 chars) and the payload is `substr(prefix.size())` (287–291).
  - `QuickMessages` has exactly 10 entries (quick_messages.hpp:14) — the assert bounds `dwMsg`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Entirely single-threaded UI state, but it mutates on both input and render paths: `DrawChatBox` truncates the live text buffer (120) and `CheckMuteButton` mutates `TalkButtonsDown` (176–180). Globals that persist across level/character changes and are NOT reset here: `WhisperList` (reset only implicitly by `ResetChat`? — it is not cleared by `ResetChat`; only `TalkButtonsDown` and cursor/input state are), `TalkSave`/`NextTalkSave` (survive chat open/close by design — that's history). `sgbPlrTalkTbl` must be 0 whenever `ChatFlag` is false or the blits read the wrong part of the panel cel. `talkButtons` and `TalkButton` are art owned/loaded elsewhere (mainpanel) and must be non-null while `ChatFlag` is set — dereferenced unconditionally at 136/139/145/149. No RNG, no clock; `DiabloHotkeyMsg` is `_DEBUG`-conditional (compile-time).
- Test coverage: none found (no `test/*chat*`; `grep -rln "DrawChatBox|CheckChatCommand|WhisperList|TalkSave" test/` → only unrelated memory_map fixtures).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/chat`, depending on `internal/ui/panel` (flags + main-panel rect), `internal/net` (`NetSendCmdString`), `internal/ui/clx` (blit/draw), `internal/input/textinput` (the `TextInputState` port from batch 003's `text_input.hpp`), `internal/config` (hotkey messages), and `internal/commands` (`CheckChatCommand`). Strategy: model the history ring as a fixed `[8]string` with explicit `next`/`index` uint8-style masking (port `&7` literally), and inject a `TruncatingDrawer` so the render-time truncation is testable; make the SDL text-input-area call an interface method (`StartTextInput(rect)`) so it can be faked.
- Risks/open questions:
  - `TalkButtonsDown[(MousePosition.y - (69 + mainPanelPosition.y)) / 18] = true` (180) indexes a 3-element array with a value derived from mouse Y; the rect containment check bounds it to 0..2 *only because* the grown height is 52 < 3*18=54 — a Go port must preserve both the rect growth formula and the 18 pitch or it will index out of range (Go panics where C++ overread).
  - `WhisperList` is never cleared by `ResetChat`/`TypeChatMessage`; on level or game change stale whispers could persist. Confirm whether it is cleared elsewhere (`multi.cpp`?) before porting, else replicate exactly.
  - The de-dup branch at 63–70 mutates history in a non-obvious way (moves the newest entry to the duplicate slot and writes `ChatInputState->value()` into the newest slot) — port carefully as its own function with a table-driven test, since no C++ test covers it.
  - `ControlUpDown` dereferences `ChatInputState` without a null check (82) — reachable only when chat is active, but Go needs an explicit guard or a non-nil invariant.
  - The `/lua` console hook is `_DEBUG`-only; decide whether the Go build has an equivalent debug mode or drops it (dropping changes debug behavior, not release behavior).
  - `SetPanelObjectPosition(UiPanels::Main, buttons)` is used but not declared in the batch's file list — locate its definition (`panels/ui_panels.*` or `control_panel.*`) so the Go port maps the same relative-to-panel repositioning.

### Source/control/control_chat.hpp
- Purpose: Interface for the chat box: exports the chat globals that other panels read, declares the chat functions, and provides the generic `HandleInputEvent` template that dispatches an SDL text event to either a text or a numeric input state.
- Public API: Globals `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList talkButtons` (40), `std::optional<TextInputState> ChatInputState` (41), `char TalkMessage[MAX_SEND_STR_LEN]` (42), `bool TalkButtonsDown[3]` (43), `int sgbPlrTalkTbl` (44), `bool WhisperList[MAX_PLRS]` (45). Function `bool CheckChatCommand(std::string_view text)` (47). Template `template <typename InputStateType> bool HandleInputEvent(const SDL_Event&, std::optional<InputStateType> &inputState)` (49–64).
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/text_input.hpp` (`TextInputState`, `NumberInputState`, `HandleTextInputEvent`, `HandleNumberInputEvent` — text_input.hpp:434–435), `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` (`OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList`), `msg.h` (`MAX_SEND_STR_LEN`=80), `multi.h` (`MAX_PLRS`=4), SDL headers (with SDL1 backport). Included by `control_chat.cpp` and `control_gold.cpp` (which uses `HandleInputEvent` with a `NumberInputState`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Re-export the six chat globals from one place so both the chat implementation and the gold-drop implementation see the same state (the header is the coupling point).
  - `CheckChatCommand(string_view) bool` as the single hook the chat send path calls to intercept `/`-prefixed commands.
  - `HandleInputEvent` is a compile-time dispatch on the input-state type: return false if the optional is empty; else `HandleTextInputEvent` for `TextInputState` or `HandleNumberInputEvent` for `NumberInputState`; else false. In Go this becomes either two named functions (`HandleTextInput`, `HandleNumberInput`) or one generic function over an interface with a type switch — the *behavioral* requirement is "empty state ⇒ not handled, event ignored".
- 1:1 constraints: array sizes `TalkButtonsDown[3]` (43) and `WhisperList[MAX_PLRS]` where `MAX_PLRS=4` (45); `TalkMessage[MAX_SEND_STR_LEN]` where `MAX_SEND_STR_LEN=80` (42); `HandleInputEvent` returns `false` for unknown state types (62) and short-circuits on a null optional (50–52). Note the declaration order requirement: `CheckChatCommand` (47) must be visible to control_chat.cpp before `HandleInputEvent`'s `if constexpr` branches (58–60) require both `TextInputState` and `NumberInputState` to be complete types.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Declarations only; the mutable state lives in control_chat.cpp. `talkButtons` is art owned by mainpanel load/free — must be non-null while chat is drawn.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: no dedicated file — the globals belong to `internal/ui/chat`; `HandleInputEvent` belongs to `internal/input/textinput` as the generic/interface-based event dispatcher used by both chat and gold-drop.
- Risks/open questions: The template's `if constexpr` chain returns `false` for any other type silently (56–62); a Go generic port must decide whether an unsupported state type is a compile error (better) or a runtime false (1:1).

### Source/control/control_chat_commands.cpp
- Purpose: Slash-command handler for the multiplayer chat box: a static table of text commands (`/help`, `/arena`, `/arenapot`, `/inspect`, `/seedinfo`, `/ping`) with parameter parsing, localized result strings shown as a Diablo message, and side effects (arena teleport, belt/inventory item grant, player inspection, network latency report).
- Public API: `bool CheckChatCommand(std::string_view text)` (260–280) is the only exported symbol. Anonymous namespace (22–258): `struct TextCmdItem { const std::string text; const std::string description; const std::string requiredParameter; std::string (*actionProc)(const std::string_view); }` (24–29), forward decl `extern std::vector<TextCmdItem> TextCmdList` (31), `TextCmdHelp` (33), `AppendArenaOverview` (52), `TextCmdArena` (59), `TextCmdArenaPot` (91), `TextCmdInspect` (116), `IsQuestEnabled(const Quest&)` (155), `TextCmdLevelSeed` (177), `TextCmdPing` (214), and the definition `std::vector<TextCmdItem> TextCmdList = {...}` (249–256).
- Depends on: `control.hpp` (`OpenCharPanel`, `SpellbookFlag`, `invflag`, `RedrawEverything`, `InspectPlayer` via player.h:920), `diablo_msg.hpp` (`InitDiabloMsg(std::string_view, uint32_t duration=3500)` — diablo_msg.hpp:74), `inv.h` (`AutoPlaceItemInBelt`, `AutoPlaceItemInInventory`), `levels/setmaps.h` (`QuestLevelNames[]` — setmaps.h:36, setmaps.cpp:27) and `levels/setmaps.cpp`-adjacent `StartNewLvl`, `levels/gendung.h`/`gendung_defs.hpp` (`_setlevels` enum with `SL_ARENA_CHURCH`/`SL_ARENA_HELL`/`SL_ARENA_CIRCLE_OF_LIFE`, `SL_FIRST_ARENA`, `SL_LAST` — gendung_defs.hpp:55–59; `IsArenaLevel` — gendung_defs.hpp:63; `GetArenaLevelType` — setmaps.h:17–28), `storm/storm_net.hpp` (`DvlNet_GetLatencies(uint8_t) -> DvlNetLatencies {uint32_t echoLatency; std::optional<int> providerLatency; std::optional<bool> isRelayed;}` — storm_net.hpp:49–53), `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (`c_find_if`), `utils/format.hpp` (`FormatRuntime`), `utils/log.hpp`, `utils/parse_int.hpp` (`ParseInt<int>(sv, min)` → `ParseIntResult<int>` with `has_value()/value()`), `utils/str_case.hpp` (`AsciiStrToLower`), `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat`, `StrAppend`), global game state (`gbIsMultiplayer`, `sgGameInitInfo` (`.programid`, `.bCowQuest`, `.bTheoQuest`), `setlevel`, `setlvltype`, `currlevel`, `DungeonSeeds[NUMLEVELS]` (dun_tile_data.hpp:140), `Quests`, `QUEST_NOTAVAIL`, `UseMultiplayerQuests()`, `IDI_ARENAPOT`, `InitializeItem`, `GenerateNewSeed`, `item.updateRequiredStatsCacheForPlayer`, `MyPlayer`, `Players`, `Player::_pName`, `Player::name()`, `Player::getId()`, `isOnLevel`, `isOnArenaLevel`, `WM_DIABSETLVL`), `debug.h` under `_DEBUG` (`glMid1Seed`, `glMid2Seed`, `glMid3Seed`, `glEndSeed` — debug.h:31–34), and `_()`/`N_()` translation macros.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A command registry with (text, description, requiredParameter, handler) tuples, in this fixed order (249–256): `/help`, `/arena`, `/arenapot`, `/inspect`, `/seedinfo`, `/ping`. The registry order is user-visible because `/help` lists commands in registry order (36–41).
  - Dispatch (`CheckChatCommand`, 260–280): return false unless the text starts with `'/'` and has length ≥1 (262); find the first registry entry that is a *prefix* of the text AND is either the whole text or followed by a space (264). If nothing matched, show `Command "<full text>" is unknown.` via `InitDiabloMsg` and return true (265–268) — i.e. any `/`-prefixed unknown input is consumed, never sent to chat. Extract the parameter as `text.substr(cmd.length()+1)` when `text.length() > cmd.length()+1` (271–273); run the handler; if the returned string is non-empty, show it with `InitDiabloMsg` (274–277); return true.
  - `/help [command]` (33–50): empty parameter ⇒ `"Available Commands:"` followed by `" <cmd>"` for every registry entry; non-empty ⇒ exact-match lookup in the registry, `"Command <param> is unknown."` if absent, otherwise `"Description: <desc>"` + (`"\nParameters: No additional parameter needed."` when the entry's requiredParameter is empty, else `"\nParameters: <requiredParameter>"`). All strings translated.
  - `/arena [n]` (59–89): refuse outside multiplayer (`"Arenas are only supported in multiplayer."`). No parameter ⇒ prompt `"What arena do you want to visit?"` + arena overview. With a parameter: `ParseInt<int>(param, min=0)`; on success map `n-1+SL_FIRST_ARENA` to a `_setlevels`, else `SL_NONE`; validate with `IsArenaLevel`; if invalid ⇒ `"Invalid arena-number. Valid numbers are:"` + overview. Then require the player to be in town (`isOnLevel(0)`) or already on an arena level, else `"To enter a arena, you need to be in town or another arena."` On success: set global `setlvltype = GetArenaLevelType(level)` and `StartNewLvl(*MyPlayer, WM_DIABSETLVL, level)` and return an empty string (no message).
  - `AppendArenaOverview` (52–57): append for each arena id from `SL_FIRST_ARENA` to `SL_LAST`: `"\n" + (arena - SL_FIRST_ARENA + 1) + " (" + QuestLevelNames[arena] + ")"` — 1-based display numbers, names indexed by the raw enum value.
  - `/arenapot [count]` (91–113): multiplayer-only; `count = ParseInt<int>(param, min=1).value_or(1)`; loop `count` times creating a default `Item`, `InitializeItem(item, IDI_ARENAPOT)`, `GenerateNewSeed(item)`, `item.updateRequiredStatsCacheForPlayer(myPlayer)`, then try belt (`AutoPlaceItemInBelt(myPlayer,item,true,true)`) else inventory (`AutoPlaceItemInInventory(myPlayer,item,true)`); `break` on the first failure (inventory full). Returns empty string (no message).
  - `/inspect [name]` (116–152): multiplayer-only, else `"Inspecting only supported in multiplayer."`. Empty parameter ⇒ stop inspecting: `InspectPlayer = MyPlayer` and message `"Stopped inspecting players."`. Otherwise lower-case the parameter and search `Players` for an exact lowercase-name match, then fall back to a lowercase substring match; on no match `"No players found with such a name"`; on match set `InspectPlayer = &player`, message `"Inspecting player: " + name`, open the char panel, and if `!SpellbookFlag` set `invflag = true`, then `RedrawEverything()`.
  - `/seedinfo` (177–212): builds a seed report string, not a chat message: `"Seedinfo for <set level|dungeon level> <currlevel>\nseed: <DungeonSeeds[currlevel]>\n"`; in `_DEBUG` additionally `Mid1/Mid2/Mid3/End` from `glMid1Seed..glEndSeed[currlevel]`; then `"\n<gameId> <MP|SP>\n<MP|Full> quests: <questFlags>\nStorybook: <DungeonSeeds[16]>"`. `gameId` is `sgGameInitInfo.programid` rendered as 4 chars MSB→LSB (181–186). `questFlags` is built by iterating `Quests` in order and doing `questFlags <<= 1; if (IsQuestEnabled(quest)) questFlags |= 1;` (192–196) — a shift-in bitmask whose bit order is quest-array order, printed as a decimal number.
  - `IsQuestEnabled(const Quest&)` (155–174): per-quest special cases overriding the generic test — `Q_FARMER`: `gbIsHellfire && !sgGameInitInfo.bCowQuest`; `Q_JERSEY`: `gbIsHellfire && sgGameInitInfo.bCowQuest`; `Q_GIRL`: `gbIsHellfire && sgGameInitInfo.bTheoQuest`; `Q_CORNSTN`: `gbIsHellfire && !gbIsMultiplayer`; `Q_GRAVE`/`Q_DEFILER`/`Q_NAKRUL`: `gbIsHellfire`; `Q_TRADER`: always false; default: `quest._qactive != QUEST_NOTAVAIL`.
  - `/ping <name>` (214–247): same two-pass lowercase name search as `/inspect` (no multiplayer gate); on no match `"No players found with such a name"`; else fetch `DvlNet_GetLatencies(player.getId())` and append: header `"Latency statistics for <name>:"`, `"\nEcho latency: <n> ms"`, and if `providerLatency` has a value, `"\nProvider latency: <n> ms"` with `" (Relayed)"` inserted before the `" ms"` when `isRelayed` is present and true. Uses `FormatRuntime` (printf-style `{:s}`/`{:d}`) for all localized lines.
  - Every user-visible string must go through the translation layer (`_()` / `N_()`), including the two `"Description: "`/`"Parameters: "` fragments which are translated separately from the entry's own description — i.e. the Go port keeps them as separate translatable units, not one format string.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Registry literal table (251–255), verbatim command strings: `"/help"` with param `"[command]"`, `"/arena"` with `"<arena-number>"`, `"/arenapot"` with `"<number>"`, `/inspect` with `"<player name>"`, `/seedinfo` with `""` (no parameter), `/ping` with `"<player name>"`; descriptions as in the file (localized).
  - Prefix match rule (264): `text.find(elem.text) == 0 && (text.length() == elem.text.length() || text[elem.text.length()] == ' ')` — requires position-0 match and a space-or-end boundary; note `std::string` vs `string_view` comparison of `elem.text == parameter` in `/help` (37) is case-sensitive.
  - Parameter extraction offset is `cmd.length() + 1` and only when `text.length() > cmd.length() + 1` (271–273), so `"/arena "` (trailing space) yields an empty parameter.
  - Arena mapping (72–74): `SL_FIRST_ARENA = SL_ARENA_CHURCH`, `SL_LAST = SL_ARENA_CIRCLE_OF_LIFE` (gendung_defs.hpp:55–58) with 3 arenas; `GetArenaLevelType` maps them to `DTYPE_CATHEDRAL, DTYPE_HELL, DTYPE_HELL` (setmaps.h:20–22) and out-of-range → `DTYPE_NONE`; user number is `enum - SL_FIRST_ARENA + 1`.
  - Arena entry precondition is `MyPlayer->isOnLevel(0) || MyPlayer->isOnArenaLevel()` (81) — level 0 = town.
  - `/seedinfo` format specifics: `"Seedinfo for "`, level type strings exactly `"set level"` / `"dungeon level"` chosen by the `setlevel` global (179), separator `"\n"` after every field, `Storybook: ` reads `DungeonSeeds[16]` (hard-coded index 16 — the Tristram/storybook seed slot) (209), `gameId` char extraction order `>>24, >>16, >>8, >>0` (182–185) then `'\0'`, `mode` = `"MP"`/`"SP"`, `questPool` = `"MP"`/`"Full"` from `UseMultiplayerQuests()` (190).
  - `questFlags` accumulation is `<<=1` then `|=1` per quest over the whole `Quests` array, starting from 0 (192–196) — the *last* quest in the array is bit 0; overflow past 32 bits is silent in C++ (the shift of a `uint32_t`), so the Go port must mask to uint32 to stay 1:1.
  - `/arenapot` item placement order is belt-then-inventory with args `(item, true, true)` / `(item, true)` and `break` on the first total failure (108–110); `numPots` defaults to 1 with `min=1` (98).
  - `/inspect` sets `invflag = true` only when `!SpellbookFlag` (149–150) and always calls `OpenCharPanel()` + `RedrawEverything()`.
  - `InitDiabloMsg` default duration is 3500 ms (diablo_msg.hpp:74) and is not overridden here — command output uses the default.
  - `CheckChatCommand` returns `false` only for non-`/` input (262–263) and `true` for every `/`-prefixed input including unknown commands (267).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `TextCmdList` is a non-const global `std::vector` whose *definition* (249) appears after the functions that iterate it (33–50) — a static-init-order dependency: `TextCmdHelp` dereferences the vector, and `CheckChatCommand` must never run before `TextCmdList` is constructed (safe in practice since it's file-local and initialized at load, but the Go port should use a package-level `var` slice to preserve eager, ordered init). Handlers mutate global game state (`setlvltype`, `InspectPlayer`, `invflag`, player inventory/belt) and trigger level transitions, so they must run on the game thread only — `StartNewLvl` mid-frame from the chat path is intentional. `/ping` reads live network state (`DvlNet_GetLatencies`) so its output is nondeterministic by design and must not be golden-tested. `/seedinfo` is the reproducibility report: it depends on `sgGameInitInfo`, `DungeonSeeds`, and debug seeds, so port it verbatim — it is the tool used to verify level-generation parity in the Go rewrite. `_DEBUG` gating changes the *output string* (extra Mid1..End lines), not just behavior, so build-tag parity matters for anyone diffing seedinfo between the two implementations.
- Test coverage: none found (`test/parse_int_test.cpp` covers `ParseInt` which is used here; no test references `CheckChatCommand`).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/chatcommands` (registry + dispatch) depending on `internal/ui/chat` (caller), `internal/ui/charpanel` (`OpenCharPanel`), `internal/item` (`AutoPlaceItemIn*`, `IDI_ARENAPOT`, `GenerateNewSeed`), `internal/dungeon` (`_setlevels`, `QuestLevelNames`, `StartNewLvl`, `setlvltype`), `internal/quest` (`Quests`, `IsQuestEnabled`), `internal/net` (`DvlNet_GetLatencies`), `internal/msg` (`InitDiabloMsg`), `internal/i18n` (`Gettext`). Strategy: represent the registry as `[]TextCmd{Text, Description, RequiredParameter string; Handler func(string) string}` with the descriptions held as *message ids* resolved at call time (C++ `N_()` marks strings for extraction without translating at definition time — a naive Go `string` field would break `xgettext` parity and translate too early). Expose `IsQuestEnabled` publicly so seed-comparison tests can reuse it.
- Risks/open questions:
  - `N_()` fields in `TextCmdList` are stored *untranslated* and wrapped by `_()` at use (43, 47–48); the Go equivalent must not snapshot the translation at init or language switching at runtime breaks.
  - `/arena` and `/arenapot` return "" (silent success) — verify no test/UX expectation requires feedback after a successful arena warp.
  - `questFlags` is printed as a decimal of a 32-bit accumulator; with Hellfire's quest count the shift-overflow behavior matters for cross-impl parity (mask explicitly with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` in Go).
  - `IsArenaLevel`/`GetArenaLevelType` are inline in headers not in this batch — confirm the arena list (3 levels) matches this build's `gendung_defs.hpp` before porting the number mapping.
  - `/help`'s "no additional parameter needed" branch keys off `requiredParameter.empty()`, and only `/seedinfo` has an empty one — so `/seedinfo` is the only command whose help omits a parameter line.
  - Does the Go port need `/ping` at all before networking exists? If `internal/net` lands later, the command should be registered but return an "unavailable" message rather than being omitted (omission changes `/help` output ordering).

### Source/control/control_flasks.cpp
- Purpose: Draws the life and mana flasks of the bottom panel — the dome that pokes above the panel top edge, the body inside the panel, and the numeric current/max readout — using per-flask pre-rendered "empty" surfaces composited against the panel's `BottomBuffer`.
- Public API: Globals `std::optional<OwnedSurface> pLifeBuff` and `std::optional<OwnedSurface> pManaBuff` (9–10, also declared in control_flasks.hpp). Functions `void DrawLifeFlaskUpper(const Surface&)` (102), `void DrawManaFlaskUpper(const Surface&)` (108), `void DrawLifeFlaskLower(const Surface&, bool drawFilledPortion)` (114), `void DrawManaFlaskLower(const Surface&, bool drawFilledPortion)` (120), `void DrawFlaskValues(const Surface&, Point pos, int currValue, int maxValue)` (126), `void UpdateLifeManaPercent()` (143). Anonymous namespace (12–100): `Rectangle FlaskTopRect {{11,3},{62,13}}` (14), `Rectangle FlaskBottomRect {{0,16},{88,69}}` (15), `DrawFlaskAbovePanel(out, celBuf, target)` (25), `DrawFlaskUpper(out, sourceBuffer, offset, fillPer)` (38), `DrawFlaskOnPanel(out, celBuf, target)` (65), `DrawFlaskLower(out, sourceBuffer, offset, fillPer, drawFilledPortion)` (79).
- Depends on: `control.hpp` (`GetMainPanel()` for the panel origin, `BottomBuffer`, and the declared flask entry points), `control_flasks.hpp` (the two buff surface globals), `engine/surface.hpp` (`Surface`, `OwnedSurface`, `BlitFromSkipColorIndexZero`, `BlitFrom`, `subregion`), `engine/render/clx_render.hpp` implicitly via the draw API, `engine/render/text_render.hpp` (`DrawString`, `GetLineWidth`, `GameFont12`, `UiFlags::ColorBlack/ColorGold/ColorWhite/ColorRed/KerningFitSpacing` — the flags/`UiFlags` come in transitively via `control.hpp`), `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat`), `utils/sdl_geometry.h` (`MakeSdlRect`), `multi.h`/`player.h` (`MyPlayer`, `Player::_pHPPer` (player.h:239), `_pManaPer`, `UpdateHitPointPercentage()` (player.h:682–694), `UpdateManaPercentage()` (player.h:696–703)). The buff surfaces themselves are created/filled elsewhere: `control_panel.cpp:360–361` (`pManaBuff.emplace(88,88); pLifeBuff.emplace(88,88);`), drawn at `control_panel.cpp:373–374`, and freed at `control_panel.cpp:632–633`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two offscreen "empty flask" buffers, 88×88 px each, one per flask, pre-composited with the flask cel art; plus a shared `BottomBuffer` (the panel's rendered content) used as the source for the *filled* portion.
  - `DrawFlaskUpper` behavior (38–55): given the flask's empty-cel surface, an x offset, and a fill percentage, compute `emptyRows = clamp(81 - fillPer, 0, FlaskTopRect.height=13)` and `filledRows = 13 - emptyRows`; first blit the empty-flask cel subregion `{11,3,62,13}` at `mainPanelPos + {offset, -13}` using **skip-color-index-0** transparency; then, if `filledRows > 0`, blit the `BottomBuffer` subregion `{x=offset, y=3+emptyRows, w=62, h=filledRows}` at `mainPanelPos + {offset, -13 + emptyRows}` — i.e. the filled part is taken from the already-rendered panel so it shows whatever the panel painted there (the colored liquid), layered over the empty dome.
  - `DrawFlaskLower` behavior (79–99): `filledRows = clamp(fillPer, 0, FlaskBottomRect.height=69)`, `emptyRows = 69 - filledRows`; if `emptyRows > 0`, blit the empty-cel subregion `{0,16,88,emptyRows}` at `mainPanelPos + {offset, 0}` using **opaque** `BlitFrom`; then if `drawFilledPortion && filledRows > 0`, blit `BottomBuffer` subregion `{x=offset, y=16+emptyRows, w=88, h=filledRows}` at `mainPanelPos + {offset, emptyRows}`. The `drawFilledPortion` flag lets callers draw only the empty overlay (used when the panel is drawn in pieces).
  - Four entry points with hardcoded x offsets (see constraints): life upper, mana upper, life lower, mana lower — each reads `MyPlayer->_pHPPer` or `_pManaPer` as its fill value.
  - `DrawFlaskValues(out, pos, curr, max)` (126–141): pick the color from the comparison `curr > 0 ? (curr == max ? Gold : White) : Red`; then draw three shadowed text pieces via a lambda that first draws the text 1px up-left in `ColorBlack` with `KerningFitSpacing` and `spacing = 0`, then the same text at `pos` in the chosen color. The layout is right-aligned around the slash: draw `curr` shifted left by `GetLineWidth(curr, GameFont12) + 1`, draw `"/"` at `pos`, draw `max` shifted right by `GetLineWidth("/", GameFont12) + 1`.
  - `UpdateLifeManaPercent()` (143–147) must call `MyPlayer->UpdateManaPercentage()` **then** `MyPlayer->UpdateHitPointPercentage()` — mana first (opposite of the declaration order in control.hpp's doc, and the order is observable if both read shared state).
  - Percent source semantics: `_pHPPer`/`_pManaPer` are computed as `clamp(hp * 81 / maxHP, 0, 81)` (player.h:690) and `clamp(mana * 81 / maxMana, 0, 81)` (player.h:701), 0 when max ≤ 0 — the `81` scale is why `DrawFlaskUpper` uses `81 - fillPer`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `FlaskTopRect {{11, 3}, {62, 13}}` (14) and `FlaskBottomRect {{0, 16}, {88, 69}}` (15) — exact source rectangles; note the doc comment at 20–21 says "fixed width 59" while the actual width used is `62` (the comment is stale).
  - Fill math: `emptyRows = clamp(81 - fillPer, 0, 13)` and `filledRows = 13 - emptyRows` (41–42); `filledRows = clamp(fillPer, 0, 69)` and `emptyRows = 69 - filledRows` (82–83). The `81` (not 80) constant is load-bearing, and the doc at 36 says "0 to 81" while 77 says "0 to 80" — trust the code.
  - X offsets: `LifeFlaskUpperOffset = 107` (103), `ManaFlaskUpperOffset = 475` (109), `LifeFlaskLowerOffset = 96` (115), `ManaFlaskLowerOffset = 464` (121). The 11-px difference between upper and lower offsets equals `FlaskTopRect.x = 11` (the cel's own left inset) — 107 = 96+11, 475 = 464+11.
  - Upper dome target y is `mainPanelPos.y - 13` (47) and the filled slice at `mainPanelPos.y - 13 + emptyRows` (53); lower target y is `mainPanelPos.y + 0` (89) and filled slice at `mainPanelPos.y + emptyRows` (96).
  - `BottomBuffer` slice x is the *same offset* as the target x (49, 94) — the filled portion is sampled from the panel buffer at screen-relative x, not from the cel.
  - Buff surfaces are 88×88 (control_panel.cpp:360–361) — `FlaskBottomRect` height 69 + y 16 = 85 ≤ 88 must hold for the slices to stay in bounds.
  - Two different blit modes: upper uses `BlitFromSkipColorIndexZero` (27) and lower uses `BlitFrom` (67).
  - `DrawFlaskValues`: black shadow drawn at `pos + {-1,-1}` (130–131), main text at `pos` (132–133), both with `UiFlags::KerningFitSpacing` and `spacing = 0`; color rule `curr > 0 ? (curr == max ? Gold : White) : Red` (127); the three-piece x layout uses `GetLineWidth(currText, GameFont12) + 1` (137) and `GetLineWidth("/", GameFont12) + 1` (138).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure render-time reads of `MyPlayer->_pHPPer`/`_pManaPer` — values only change when `UpdateLifeManaPercent()` runs, so a flask drawn after a health change but before the percent update shows stale fill (the update call ordering in the frame loop is a behavioral coupling the Go port must preserve). `pLifeBuff`/`pManaBuff`/`BottomBuffer` are `std::optional` and dereferenced unconditionally here (`*pLifeBuff`, `*pManaBuff`, `BottomBuffer->`) — they are non-null only between `InitMainPanel`/panel-art load and `FreeControlPan` (control_panel.cpp:632–633), so draw calls must be lifecycle-gated. No RNG, no clock, no mutation of game state (except via `UpdateLifeManaPercent`).
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln "DrawFlaskValues|UpdateLifeManaPercent|DrawManaFlaskUpper" test/` → none; `test/char_panel_test.cpp` and `test/panel_state_test.cpp` contain no `TEST(` cases for flasks).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/flasks` (pure rendering, no game-logic deps) taking a `*Panel`-provided `BottomBuffer *Surface`, its own `LifeBuff, ManaBuff *Surface` (allocated 88×88 by the panel init), and an interface `FillSource { HPPer(), ManaPer() int }` instead of `MyPlayer` directly. Strategy: keep the two `FlaskTopRect`/`FlaskBottomRect` constants and the four offsets as named unexported consts with the C++ numbers verbatim, and add a unit test that asserts the row-split math for `fillPer ∈ {0, 1, 68, 69, 81, 82}` — that math is the only non-obvious logic and has zero C++ test coverage today.
- Risks/open questions:
  - The stale doc comment ("width 59", "0 to 80") conflicts with the code (62, 81) — port the code, and flag the comments so nobody "fixes" the Go version back.
  - `DrawFlaskUpper` samples `BottomBuffer` at `y = FlaskTopRect.position.y + emptyRows` (i.e. 3 + emptyRows) while the dome is drawn above the panel — this only works because `BottomBuffer` was rendered with the panel content at those rows. Confirm `BottomBuffer`'s coordinate space before porting, otherwise the filled slice samples the wrong pixels.
  - `UpdateLifeManaPercent`'s mana-before-hp order: check whether any caller depends on hp-percentage freshness within the same frame.
  - `DrawFlaskValues` uses `GameFont12` measurement but no size flag in the draw call — the default draw size must match `GameFont12` or the shadow/text will misalign.

### Source/control/control_flasks.hpp
- Purpose: Interface header exposing the two offscreen flask "empty state" buffers so the panel code can allocate/fill them while the flask code reads them.
- Public API: `extern std::optional<OwnedSurface> pLifeBuff;` (9), `extern std::optional<OwnedSurface> pManaBuff;` (10). `#include <optional>` and `engine/surface.hpp` (3–5).
- Depends on: `engine/surface.hpp` (`OwnedSurface`); consumed by `Source/control/control_flasks.cpp` (definitions at 9–10, reads at 105, 111, 117, 123) and by `Source/control/control_panel.cpp` which allocates them at 88×88 (360–361), fills them by `ClxDraw`ing the status-panel art (373–374), and releases them (632–633).
- Requirements for Go port: only the two buffer globals plus the shared size invariant (88×88) need to exist; the draw functions are declared in control.hpp, not here.
- 1:1 constraints: the surfaces must be `88x88` to match `FlaskBottomRect {{0,16},{88,69}}` and `FlaskTopRect {{11,3},{62,13}}` slices (control_flasks.cpp:14–15 with allocation size at control_panel.cpp:360–361); the `std::optional` (nullable) wrapper encodes "not yet loaded / freed" and is dereferenced unchecked in control_flasks.cpp.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Init-order coupling — these are populated during panel-art load and nulled during `FreeControlPan`; any draw before load or after free is a null dereference (C++) / panic (Go). Render-thread only.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: fields of the panel/flask owner, e.g. `internal/ui/flasks.LifeBuff, ManaBuff *Surface` (or an unexported pair with an explicit `Init`/`Free`), sized 88×88 by `internal/ui/panel`'s art loader.
- Risks/open questions: whether to model nullability with a nil `*Surface` plus guards (Go-idiomatic) or keep pan-on-nil to mirror C++ behavior; the guards are strictly better here.

### Source/control/control_gold.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the "split gold" modal dialog: draws the gold-drop box over the inventory panel, runs a numeric text input, and on Enter removes the chosen amount from an inventory gold stack and puts it into the player's held (cursor) item as a new gold stack.
- Public API: globals `bool DropGoldFlag` (15), `TextInputCursorState GoldDropCursor` (16), `char GoldDropText[21]` (17); functions `void DrawGoldSplit(const Surface &out)` (48), `void control_drop_gold(SDL_Keycode vkey)` (85), `void OpenGoldDrop(int8_t invIndex, int max)` (110), `void CloseGoldDrop()` (127), `bool HandleGoldDropTextInputEvent(const SDL_Event &event)` (137). File-internal (`namespace {}` 19-46): `int8_t GoldDropInvIndex` (21), `std::optional<NumberInputState> GoldDropInputState` (22), `RemoveGold(Player&, int goldIndex, int amount)` (24), `GetGoldDropMax()` (41). Declared in `Source/control/control.hpp:200-206`.
- Depends on: `control.hpp` (`DropGoldFlag`, `GoldBoxBuffer`, `GetPanelPosition`, `UiPanels`), `control_chat.hpp` (via `control.hpp` include chain; chat/gold input are mutually exclusive in `diablo.cpp`), `DiabloUI/text_input.hpp` (`TextInputCursorState`, `NumberInputState`, `HandleInputEvent` — `text_input.hpp:380-430`), `engine/render/clx_render.hpp` (`ClxDraw`), `inv.h` (`SetPlrHandGoldCurs`, `CalculateGold` at `inv.h:245`, `INVITEM_INV_FIRST`), `utils/display.h` (`ghMainWnd`), `utils/sdl_compat.h` (`SDLC_StartTextInput`/`SDLC_StopTextInput`), `utils/format.hpp` (`FormatRuntime`), `utils/format_int.hpp` (`FormatInteger`), `Player::InvList/RemoveInvItem/HoldItem/_pGold` (`player.h`), `items.h:566` (`MakeGoldStack`), `cursor.h:38` (`NewCursor`), `msg`/net via `NetSyncInvItem`. Callers: `inv.cpp:1105` (`OpenGoldDrop`), `inv.cpp:756,1672,1743,2185` + `qol/stash.cpp:592` (`CloseGoldDrop`), `engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1427-1428` (`DrawGoldSplit` when `DropGoldFlag`), `diablo.cpp:554-555,3024-3025` (`control_drop_gold` on key, ESC on panel close), `diablo.cpp:772` (text-input event), `control_panel.cpp:424,605,609` (init + panel toggles), `controls/keymapper.cpp:72` (keys swallowed while `DropGoldFlag`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Modal state: a `DropGoldFlag` bool plus the held input state; opening allocates a `NumberInputState` bound to the shared `GoldDropText` buffer with `maxLength = len(GoldDropText)-1 = 20`, `min = 0`, `max = <caller-supplied>` (110-122).
  - `OpenGoldDrop`: set flag, store inv index (int8), clear text to `""`, construct input state, call SDL `StartTextInput(ghMainWnd)`.
  - `CloseGoldDrop`: no-op when flag already false (129-130); otherwise stop text input, clear flag, destroy input state (`nullopt`), reset `GoldDropInvIndex = 0`.
  - `control_drop_gold(vkey)`: dead player (`hasNoLife()`) closes immediately (91-94); `RETURN`/`KP_ENTER` → if `value() != 0` do `RemoveGold`, then always close (95-103); `ESCAPE` → close only (104-106); any other key ignored (107).
  - `RemoveGold`: index math `gi = goldIndex - INVITEM_INV_FIRST`; decrement `_ivalue`; if remaining > 0 → `SetPlrHandGoldCurs(item)` + `NetSyncInvItem(player, gi)`; else → `player.RemoveInvItem(gi)`. Then `MakeGoldStack(HoldItem, amount)` + `NewCursor(HoldItem)` and recompute `player._pGold = CalculateGold(player)` (24-39). Order matters: hold-item/cursor update happens after the inventory mutation and sync.
  - `DrawGoldSplit`: blit `GoldBoxBuffer[0]` at `GetPanelPosition(Inventory, {30, 178})`; build pluralized description from `max`; word-wrap at 200 px; draw wrapped description in a clipped 200×50 box at `{61, 75}` with lineHeight 17, white-gold + centered; draw the raw input text at `{67, 128}` white with `PentaCursor`, cursor position and selection-highlight range forwarded.
  - `HandleGoldDropTextInputEvent`: thin forwarder to the generic `HandleInputEvent(event, GoldDropInputState)`; returns whether the event was consumed (137-139).
  - `GetGoldDropMax` dereferences the optional input state without a null check (41-43) — in Go, guard or panic deliberately; only reachable while the flag is true.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `char GoldDropText[21]` → effective max input length 20 chars (`sizeof(GoldDropText) - 1`, 17, 119).
  - Dialog geometry: `dialogX = 30` (50); gold box sprite at offset `{30, 178}` (52); description rect at `{dialogX + 31, 75}` = `{61,75}` with size `{200, 50}` and `lineHeight = 17` (72-73); amount text at `{dialogX + 37, 128}` = `{67,128}` (77).
  - `WordWrapString(description, 200)` — wrap width exactly 200 (67).

  - `NumberInputState` bounds: `min = 0`, `max = max` param (121-122); value read with default 0 (`value()` → `NumberInputState::value(int defaultValue = 0)`, text_input.hpp:402).

- Determinism/thread-safety notes: single-threaded UI code. Mutable file-statics `GoldDropInvIndex` and `GoldDropInputState` (21-22) are the only hidden state; `GoldDropText`/`GoldDropCursor` are externally visible globals shared with the text-input layer, so the buffer must stay alive as long as the input state. `SDL_GetTicks`-free. Reentrancy: `CloseGoldDrop` is idempotent via the early return; `OpenGoldDrop` does not check whether a drop is already open (it silently re-inits state).
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -l "GoldDrop\|DrawGoldSplit\|control_drop_gold" test/` → no hits). `test/panel_state_test.cpp` covers panel flags only.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/golddrop` (state + input + draw), depending on `internal/ui/panel` (`GetPanelPosition`, `GoldBoxBuffer`), `internal/input/textinput` (`NumberInputState` port), `internal/item` (`SetPlrHandGoldCurs`, `MakeGoldStack`, `CalculateGold`), `internal/player`, `internal/net` (`NetSyncInvItem`), `internal/cursor`, `internal/render/clx`. Strategy: make the dialog a struct (`GoldDrop{Active bool; InvIndex int8; Text [21]byte; Cursor TextInputCursorState; Input *NumberInputState}`) with an injected `TextInputController` interface for Start/Stop so headless tests can drive `Open/Close/Key` without SDL; port the plural + wrap math as pure functions for table tests.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `GetGoldDropMax()` (41-43) dereferences the optional with no check — in Go that is a nil-pointer panic, so the port must decide between an explicit guard (behaviour change: C++ would UB) and a documented invariant "only called while Active"; (2) the whole file is untested, and the numeric clamp (`min=0`, `max=<stack size>`, 20-digit cap) is exactly where a port bug silently drops gold; (3) `ngettext` plural rules are English-specific here — confirm the i18n port exposes a plural form before hardcoding the two strings.

Returns a zero rect when nothing matches (203) — caller must tolerate `{0,0,0,0}`.

  - No RNG, no serialization, no byte order in this file.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure render/hover pass reading `MousePosition`; no statics of its own beyond the two global strings, but it *writes* `pcursinvitem` as a side effect of `CheckPanelInfo` (387) — that is a hover-state mutation the game logic reads later, so call ordering vs. `CheckMainPanelButton` matters. `InspectPlayer` may be a different player than `MyPlayer` (255/262 etc.), so port must keep that pointer explicit. `SpeakText` is a fire-and-forget external side effect called on every frame the string is non-empty (48, 267) — real port must dedupe or it will spam TTS; C++ does not dedupe.
- Test coverage: none found for infobox specifically (`grep -l "CheckPanelInfo\|DrawInfoBox\|AddInfoBoxString" test/` → no hits); indirectly exercised by `test/scrollrt_test.cpp` and the UI fixture `test/ui_test.hpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/infobox` (string buffers + main info box) and `internal/ui/tooltip` (floating box), both depending on `internal/ui/panel` for rects/flags, `internal/item` for sizes/hover, `internal/stash`, `internal/store` (visual store), `internal/accessibility` (`SpeakText`), `internal/render/primitive` (half-transparent rect/lines), `internal/i18n`. Strategy: split the layout math into pure functions taking a small `HoverContext{CursorInvItem, CursorStashItem, CursorStoreItem, CursorStoreBtn, Player *}` so `GetFloatingInfoRect` / `GetHoverSpriteHeight` / `ClampAboveOrBelow` become table-testable (this file has the most untested arithmetic in the batch); add a per-frame TTS dedupe keyed on string identity.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `StringOrView` semantics (borrowed view vs owned string) must not dangle in Go — the C++ code assigns views into `Towners[..].name`, `monster.name()`, `HoldItem.getName()` while also `StrCat`-ing owned strings (288-306); the port should just use `string` and accept the allocations, or keep an owned buffer. (2) `GetFloatingInfoRect` reads `*InspectPlayer` (75) unconditionally, i.e. it assumes a non-null inspect target whenever a tooltip is drawn — verify the invariant holds before dereferencing in Go. (3) `DrawHalfTransparent*` and `PAL16_GRAY + 10` are palette-index based; an RGBA/Ebiten renderer needs an equivalent 50 %-alpha gray pen, so exact pixel parity is not achievable — decide whether visual parity or code parity wins. (4) `SpeakText` fires every frame the string is non-empty (48, 269): real TTS spam; port must dedupe (behaviour change, call it out).

Char-panel lifecycle (301-330): `OpenCharPanel` closes quest-log-conflicting panels (gold withdraw, stash, visual store) and sets `CharFlag`; `CloseCharPanel` clears the flag and, if inspecting, resets `InspectPlayer = MyPlayer`, `RedrawEverything()`, and either clears `InspectingFromPartyPanel` or shows the "Stopped inspecting players." message; `ToggleCharPanel` dispatches.

Panel coordinate mapping (332-349): `GetPanelPosition` maps `UiPanels::{Main,Quest,Character,Stash}` → LeftPanel, `{Spell,Inventory}` → RightPanel, default → MainPanel, by adding the offset. `DrawPanelBox` blits from `BottomBuffer`. `SetPanelObjectPosition` converts a panel-local rect to absolute in place.

Every art load is skipped when `HeadlessMode`.
  7. `FreeControlPan` (629-647): release every owned surface/cel and call the sub-panel free functions in the listed order.
  8. Draw pass (433-463, 675-683, 751-772, 774-785, 787-831): `DrawMainPanel` blits the strip selected by `sgbPlrTalkTbl` then calls `DrawInfoBox`; `DrawMainPanelButtons` renders the 6 normal buttons (idle = blit from bottom buffer, pressed = `pMainPanelButtons[i]` + `PanelButtonDown[i]` at +4 px), plus chat/friendly buttons from `multiButtons` with the frame-selection table; `DrawLevelButton` renders "Level Up" text + `pChrButtons[nCel]`; `DrawDurIcon` renders 4 durability icons right-to-left with collision-aware placement; `RedBack` applies the pause TRN over the viewport; `DrawDeathText` renders the two-line death overlay.
  9. Hover/press logic (472-543, 545-627, 649-673): `CheckMainPanelButton` marks all hovered buttons down; the speed-book button on shift clears `_pRSpell`/`_pRSplType` to Invalid + `RedrawEverything`, else `DoSpeedBook()` + `gamemenu_off()`. `CheckMainPanelButtonDead` only allows menu + chat buttons when dead. `CheckMainPanelButtonUp` iterates *all* 9 ids, clears the down flag, and fires the action only if the mouse is still inside the button (per-action semantics listed in 1:1). `CheckLevelButton`/`CheckLevelButtonUp` handle the level-up button (up → `OpenCharPanel`).
  10. Stat buttons (685-749): `CheckChrBtns` sets per-attribute down flags when active and stat points exist; `ReleaseChrBtns(addAllStatPoints)` sends `CMD_ADD{STR,MAG,DEX,VIT}` with 1 or capped amount and immediately decrements local `_pStatPts` (see 1:1).
  11. Automap buttons (523-543): `DoAutoMap` toggles; `CycleAutomapType` starts automap if inactive, else advances type modulo `enum_size<AutomapType>` and closes when wrapping to FIRST.
  12. Durability icons (166-219): skip empty/healthy items, map item type → icon index when `c == 0`, compute the gold/red partition from durability, draw gold portion (frame `c+8`) and red portion (frame `c`) through y-subregions of the target surface, and return the next x.

  - No RNG, no serialization, no byte order here.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: this file *is* the order-of-init hub — `InitMainPanel` both loads art and resets flags, so any Go port must preserve its sequence (e.g. `CloseCharPanel()` runs before spell state reset; `CalculatePanelAreas()` runs after buffers exist; `InitModifierHints()` last). `ResetMainPanelButtons()` is called before `pDurIcons` load (400-406). Mutable globals read by nearly every other UI file (`MainPanel/LeftPanel/RightPanel`, `ChatFlag`, `CharFlag`, `invflag` neighbors). `SetPanelObjectPosition` mutates the caller's rect in place, and callers pass copies of the global rects (`Rectangle button = MainPanelButtonRect[i];`) — port must not accidentally mutate the table. `MainPanelButtons[9]` is a static, single-threaded; no atomics needed if all input+render stays on the game thread. `PanelPaddingHeight` is a *mutable* global int (105) even though it is only ever 16.
- Test coverage: `test/char_panel_test.cpp` (CheckChrBtns / ReleaseChrBtns / Open/Close/ToggleCharPanel / CharPanelButton — asserts local `_pStatPts` side effects, explicitly not final stat values because the net loopback is not pumped); `test/panel_state_test.cpp` (Open/Close/ToggleCharPanel and mutual-exclusion flag rules); `test/scrollrt_test.cpp` (`CalculatePanelAreas` + `gnViewportHeight` expectations at lines 17, 30, 43, 56, 69, 84, 97, 110, 123, 136, 151, 159, 167). Untested: `InitMainPanel`, `FreeControlPan`, `DrawDurIcon`, `RedBack`, `DrawDeathText`, `CheckMainPanelButton*`, `FocusOnCharInfo`, `CycleAutomapType`.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/panel` as the owner of flags + rects + `GetPanelPosition`/`SetPanelObjectPosition`/`CalculatePanelAreas`/`DrawPanelBox`, with `internal/ui/panel/init` (or an `Init` method) for the art-loading sequence and `internal/ui/panel/input` for hover/press. Art loading maps to `pkg/mpq` + `internal/render/clx` (`LoadCel` with explicit frame widths → `clx.LoadCEL(path, frameWidths []int)`). Strategy: replace the ~15 package-level bools with a single exported `State` struct owned by `internal/ui/panel` (callers like infobox/golddrop/chat take `*panel.State`) to keep the "one writer" property testable, but keep the rect tables as package-level `var` constants; inject `Headless bool` and an `AssetLoader` interface so `InitMainPanel` is testable without data files; port `char_panel_test`/`panel_state_test`/`scrollrt_test` as Go table tests, and add explicit tests for the durability partition math and `CalculatePanelAreas` viewport rule (the latter already has C++ coverage to mirror).
- Risks/open questions: (1) `InitMainPanel` returns `std::expected<void, std::string>` and 12 steps can propagate failure (`RETURN_IF_ERROR` at 363, 364, 365, 398, 420; `ASSIGN_OR_RETURN` at 367, 372, 382, 399, 402, 421, 422) — the Go port needs an error-propagating equivalent plus a partial-init rollback story matching `FreeControlPan` (629-647); note the plain `LoadCel` calls at 385, 386, 406 are *not* error-checked, so the port must decide whether `p8but2`/`talkbutt`/`duricons` load failure is fatal. (2) `RedBack` (774-785) rewrites *palette indices* in the backbuffer under the rule `leveltype != DTYPE_HELL || *dst >= 32`; if the Ebiten port renders RGBA, this function has no 1:1 counterpart and needs a design decision (per-pixel TRN over indices vs shader/overlay). (3) `DrawDurIcon` (751-772) places icons *between* panels based on screen layout; whether the port keeps that fallback depends on the target minimum resolution. (4) `MainPanelButtons[9]` vs 8 rects (144 vs 84) is a latent asymmetry: `ResetMainPanelButtons` clears 9 entries and `CheckMainPanelButtonUp` iterates 0..8 while only 0..7 have rects — confirm nothing indexes 8 before shrinking. (5) `CheckMainPanelButtonUp` (545-627) fires net commands (`CMD_FRIENDLYMODE`, `CMD_RETOWN`, `CMD_ADD*` via `ReleaseChrBtns`) from input code, so the port must keep the net layer callable from the panel package without an import cycle. (6) `FreeControlPan` releases sprite globals *owned by other files* (`pChrButtons`, `pQLogCel`, `talkButtons`, `PanelButtonDown` family) — the Go ownership split must decide who frees what or it leaks/double-frees.

### Source/control/control_panel.hpp
- Purpose: Cross-file declaration surface for the handful of panel layout constants that other files (mainly `control_infobox.cpp`, `control_chat.cpp`, `panels/*`) need without including the whole panel implementation.
- Public API: `extern int TotalSpMainPanelButtons; extern int TotalMpMainPanelButtons; extern int PanelPaddingHeight; extern const char *const PanBtnStr[8]; extern const char *const PanBtnHotKey[8]; extern Rectangle SpellButtonRect; extern Rectangle BeltRect;` and `void SetPanelObjectPosition(UiPanels panel, Rectangle &button);` (7-17).
- Depends on: `engine/rectangle.hpp`, `panels/ui_panels.hpp`; definitions all live in `control_panel.cpp` (105, 108, 120, 101, 103, 122-123, 833). Note `MainPanelButtonRect`, `CharPanelButtonRect`, `InfoBoxRect`, `GetPanelPosition`, etc. are declared in `control.hpp` instead — the split is inconsistent and worth mirroring only in docs, not in structure.
- Requirements for Go port: nothing of its own — it becomes exported identifiers of the panel package: the two button-count values, the padding height, the two button-caption/hotkey tables (message ids, resolved at use), the two rects, and `SetPanelObjectPosition`.
- 1:1 constraints: the exported *names/arity* matter less than the values, which are in `control_panel.cpp` (see its entry); arrays are fixed length 8 and `PanBtnHotKey[7]` must be a nil marker, not an empty string.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: none (declarations only).
- Test coverage: n/a (header); consumers covered via `test/char_panel_test.cpp` and `test/panel_state_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: collapses into `internal/ui/panel`'s exported API; no separate file. Keep `PanBtnStr`/`PanBtnHotKey` as `[]string` of message ids with `PanBtnHotKey[7] = ""` plus a documented "nil sentinel" convention, or as `[]*string` if strict parity is wanted.
- Risks/open questions: `PanelPaddingHeight` is declared `extern int` (mutable at runtime in C++ though never reassigned here) — port as a package `int` var only if something actually changes it; otherwise make it a const.

### Source/controls/axis_direction.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the D-pad/stick repeat throttle that turns a raw axis direction into at most one direction change per configured time interval (input-rate limiting for menu navigation and held-stick movement).
- Public API: `AxisDirection AxisDirectionRepeater::Get(AxisDirection axisDirection)` (12-57) — the only function; class/enum live in `axis_direction.h`.
- Depends on: `axis_direction.h` (own types); SDL timing (`SDL_GetTicks` from `SDL3/SDL_timer.h` or `SDL.h`, lines 3-7). Used by `Source/controls/menu_controls.cpp:24`, `Source/gmenu.cpp:156`, and 8 sites in `Source/controls/plrctrls.cpp` (569, 974, 1474, 1506, 1652, 1709, 1786, 1796) as function-local `static` instances (`grep -c 'static AxisDirectionRepeater' plrctrls.cpp` = 8), three of which pass `min_interval_ms = 150`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A value type `AxisDirection{X AxisDirectionX; Y AxisDirectionY}` and a stateful `AxisDirectionRepeater` with four per-direction timestamps plus the interval; `Get(d)` returns a *possibly zeroed* copy: the direction is suppressed (set to NONE) if it fired less than `minInterval` ago, otherwise the corresponding timestamp is updated.
  - Opposite-direction reset: entering LEFT zeroes `last_right_` and vice versa (and up/down likewise), so pressing the opposite direction is never throttled; entering NONE on an axis zeroes *both* timestamps for that axis (32, 53).
  - Each axis is handled independently (two separate switch statements), so a diagonal input can suppress one axis while passing the other.
  - Callers keep one static instance per usage site, so the port must provide independently-instantiable repeaters (a struct with a constructor taking the interval), not a global.
- 1:1 constraints: `now = SDL_GetTicks()` read once per call (13); test is `now - last < min_interval_ms` (17, 25, 38, 46) — strictly-less-than, so exactly `min_interval` elapsed passes; timestamps initialized to 0 (header ctor 31-38); default interval `200` ms (header line 31), overridden to `150` at plrctrls.cpp:974/1474/1506; all timestamps are `int` (32-bit) — SDL ticks wrap after ~49.7 days and the subtraction is signed 32-bit wrap-around arithmetic; a Go port must reproduce that wrap behaviour (use `uint32` subtraction cast to int32, or int32 arithmetic) to stay 1:1 at the wrap edge.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: wall-clock dependent, not tick-driven → output is frame-rate/timing dependent by design (it is an input debounce). Instances are function-local `static` in C++ (first-call init, single-threaded). Go equivalent must not be a package-level singleton shared across call sites — that would couple unrelated repeat rates.
- Test coverage: none found (no `AxisDirection`/`Repeater` hits in `test/`).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/controls` (or `internal/input/repeat`) with an injectable clock: `type Repeater struct { lastLeft, lastRight, lastUp, lastDown, min int32; now func() int32 }` and a default `now` reading the SDL/Ebiten tick source. Strategy: keep the two-switch structure verbatim; unit-test with a fake clock covering exactly-`min` interval, opposite-direction reset, and NONE reset.
- Risks/open questions: whether the port wants ms-based debouncing at all under Ebiten's fixed 60 TPS game loop (a tick-based variant would be deterministic but is *not* 1:1 — flag for the rewrite owner).

### Source/controls/axis_direction.h
- Purpose: Declares the 8-way axis-direction enums/struct and the `AxisDirectionRepeater` rate-limiter used by menu and player controls.
- Public API: `enum AxisDirectionX : uint8_t {NONE, LEFT, RIGHT}` (7-10), `enum AxisDirectionY : uint8_t {NONE, UP, DOWN}` (11-14), `struct AxisDirection { AxisDirectionX x; AxisDirectionY y; }` (16-24), `class AxisDirectionRepeater` with `explicit-ish ctor(int min_interval_ms = 200)` (31-38) and `AxisDirection Get(AxisDirection)` (40), private members `last_left_/last_right_/last_up_/last_down_/min_interval_ms_` (43-47).
- Depends on: `<cstdint>` only; consumed by `controls/menu_controls.cpp`, `controls/plrctrls.cpp`, `gmenu.cpp`, `controls/controller.cpp` indirectly through those; included by nothing else in this batch.
- Requirements for Go port: exported `AxisDirectionX`/`AxisDirectionY` int-typed enums with the same zero = NONE convention (so a zero-value struct means "no direction"), `AxisDirection` comparable value struct, and the repeater class as above.
- 1:1 constraints: underlying type `uint8_t` and value order NONE=0, LEFT/UP=1, RIGHT/DOWN=2 (7-14); default interval exactly `200` (31); four separate `int` timestamps initialized to 0 in the ctor (32-38).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: header has no state of its own; `Get` is non-const (mutates timestamps).
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: same package as the implementation (`internal/input/controls`); the enums become `type AxisDirectionX uint8` with `const` blocks, the class becomes a struct constructed with `NewReater` — precisely `NewRepeater(minIntervalMS int32) *Repeater`; the C++ default argument of 200 must be an explicit constructor parameter (a Go zero-value `Repeater{}` would mean interval 0 = no throttling, which is *not* equivalent), so require explicit construction.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/controls/control_mode.cpp
- Purpose: Defines the three mutable globals that record the currently active control scheme and gamepad brand, plus the compile-time default for the gamepad layout.
- Public API: `ControlTypes ControlMode = ControlTypes::None;`, `ControlTypes ControlDevice = ControlTypes::None;`, `GamepadLayout GamepadType = …` (5-16).
- Depends on: `controls/control_mode.hpp` (the enums) and, transitively, `controls/controller_buttons.h` (`GamepadLayout`). Written by input-dispatch code (`Source/diablo.cpp`, `Source/controls/*`, `Source/utils/display.cpp`, touch handlers) and read everywhere UI decisions branch on device: e.g. `control_panel.cpp:249/267` (VirtualGamepad layout), `control_panel.cpp:807-815` (death-text button label), `control_infobox.cpp:345` (pad vs key hotkey name).
- Requirements for Go port: three package-level variables of the control/gamepad enum types with `None`/`Generic` initial values; a build-time way to force the gamepad layout (C++ uses `DEVILUTIONX_GAMEPAD_TYPE` → `GamepadLayout::NAME`, else `Generic`), e.g. Go build tags or a linker-set variable / config field resolved at startup.
- 1:1 constraints: initial values `ControlMode = None`, `ControlDevice = None` (5-6); `GamepadType` default `GamepadLayout::Generic` unless `DEVILUTIONX_GAMEPAD_TYPE` is defined, in which case it is the token-pasted enumerator (7-16) — legal enumerator names are `Generic|Nintendo|PlayStation|Xbox` (controller_buttons.h:77-82).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: plain non-atomic globals mutated on the input thread and read during rendering; the distinction between `ControlMode` (input-simulation mode) and `ControlDevice` (actual device) must be preserved — code branches on both. `ControlMode` is marked `DVL_API_FOR_TEST` in the header (export for Windows test DLL); in Go just export it.
- Test coverage: `ControlMode` is referenced in `test/ui_test.hpp` (fixture setup) and `ControlDevice` in `test/spell_ui_test.cpp`; no dedicated test file.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/controlmode` (tiny package: two enums + three vars + `Init` from build/config). Strategy: one package so `panel`, `plrctrls`, and `menu` can all import it without cycles; make the gamepad default configurable via a `SetGamepadLayout` called from config/options load rather than a preprocessor tag.
- Risks/open questions: does the Go port need `DEVILUTIONX_GAMEPAD_TYPE` parity (a build-time default), or is runtime option-driven layout sufficient? Affects only the initial value.

### Source/controls/control_mode.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the control-scheme and gamepad-layout enums and the extern globals, documenting the `ControlMode` vs `ControlDevice` distinction.
- Public API: `enum class ControlTypes : uint8_t { None, KeyboardAndMouse, Gamepad, VirtualGamepad }` (10-15); `extern DVL_API_FOR_TEST ControlTypes ControlMode;` (17); `extern ControlTypes ControlDevice;` (26); `extern GamepadLayout GamepadType;` (28).
- Depends on: `<cstdint>`, `controls/controller_buttons.h` (for `GamepadLayout`), `utils/attributes.h` (`DVL_API_FOR_TEST`, empty on non-MSVC — attributes.h:58/63). Widely included (`control_panel.cpp`, `control_infobox.cpp`, `options`, `plrctrls`, `touch/*`, `DiabloUI/*`).
- Requirements for Go port: exported `ControlTypes` enum (4 values, ordered) plus the three globals; `GamepadLayout` re-exported so callers of this header get both enums (port should re-declare or alias it).
- 1:1 constraints: `None=0, KeyboardAndMouse=1, Gamepad=2, VirtualGamepad=3`, underlying `uint8_t` (10-15). Comparisons in dependent code use `==` against `VirtualGamepad`/`Gamepad`/`KeyboardAndMouse` — no numeric assumptions elsewhere, so the ordering is for storage/serialization safety only.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: doc comment (19-25) is normative: `ControlMode` becomes `KeyboardAndMouse` while a gamepad simulates the mouse, while `ControlDevice` always reflects the real device — port must keep both and not merge them.
- Test coverage: none direct; see `control_mode.cpp`.
