### Source/controls/controller.cpp
- Purpose: Device-agnostic controller event layer: converts raw SDL events (keyboard-as-controller, gamepad, joystick) into a fixed-capacity list of `ControllerButtonEvent`s, queries pressed state across all devices, unlocks one-shot trigger/hat state, and maintains the connected-device registries on add/remove events.
- Public API: `void UnlockControllerState(const SDL_Event &event)` (20), `StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent, 4> ToControllerButtonEvents(const SDL_Event &event)` (33), `bool IsControllerButtonPressed(ControllerButton button)` (76), `bool IsControllerButtonComboPressed(ControllerButtonCombo combo)` (88), `bool HandleControllerAddedOrRemovedEvent(const SDL_Event &event)` (94).
- Depends on: `controls/controller.h` (own decls), SDL event types; `controls/devices/game_controller.h` (`GameController::Get(event)`, `UnlockTriggerState`, `ToControllerButton`, `IsPressed`, `IsPressedOnAnyController`, `Add`/`Remove` — game_controller.h:23-38), `controls/devices/joystick.h` (`Joystick::Get`, `UnlockHatState`, `ToControllerButtonEvents`, `IsPressedOnAnyJoystick`, `Add`/`Remove` — joystick.h:28-41), `controls/devices/kbcontroller.h` (`KbCtrlToControllerButton`, `IsKbCtrlButtonPressed`, compiled only when `HAS_KBCTRL == 1`; kbcontroller.h:4-8 defaults it to 0), `engine/demomode.h` (`demo::IsRunning()`), `utils/sdl_compat.h` (`SDLC_EventGamepadDevice` → `event.gdevice` on SDL3 / `event.cdevice` on SDL2 — sdl_compat.h:58/292). Called from `Source/diablo.cpp:741`, `Source/DiabloUI/settingsmenu.cpp:518`, `Source/movie.cpp:62`, `Source/controls/menu_controls.cpp:39`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Per-event unlock step that must run exactly once before any pressed-state query: unlock the gamepad trigger latch for the event's controller and the joystick hat latch (20-31). Header comment states the contract "Must be called exactly once at the start of each SDL input event" (controller.h:14).
  - Event→button translation with strict device precedence: keyboard-controller mapping first (when enabled and not in demo playback), then gamepad, then joystick (and the joystick path returns *multiple* events, e.g. hat → up to 4); fallback returns a single `{NONE, up?}` (33-74).
  - `up` flag derived from event type only (`JOYSTICK_BUTTON_UP`, `KEY_UP`, `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_UP`), otherwise false (35-45).
  - Analog-trigger correction: when the mapped button is `AXIS_TRIGGERLEFT`/`AXIS_TRIGGERRIGHT`, the `up` flag is recomputed from the controller's live pressed state (`!controller->IsPressed(button)`) rather than the event type (57-62).
  - Pressed query aggregating all device kinds: gamepads first, then keyboard-controller (skipped during demo playback), then joysticks (76-86).
  - Combo query: `button` pressed AND (`modifier == NONE` OR modifier pressed) (88-91).
  - Hotplug handling for the four device add/remove event types, mapping each to the right registry call with the correct id field (`which` from the gamepad or joystick device event), returning false for every other event type (94-118).
- 1:1 constraints: static-vector capacity is exactly `4` (`StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent, 4>`) — a joystick hat can emit up to 4 events, and overflow behaviour is the container's; ordering within `ToControllerButtonEvents` (kb → gamepad → joystick) is observable because the first non-`NONE` mapping short-circuits with an early `return` (49-72); demo-mode gate `!demo::IsRunning()` appears in both the translation path (50) and the pressed query (80) — both must exist; trigger special-case compares against the two `AXIS_*` enumerators only (59); `SDL_EVENT_*` constants used are exactly those at 36-41 and 100-111; the early-exit `default: return false;` for non-device events (112-113) and `return false` under `USE_SDL1` (116).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless itself; all state lives in the device registries (`GameController`/`Joystick` statics) and in the per-device latch (`UnlockTriggerState`/`UnlockHatState`) which is a *frame-coupled* one-shot: forgetting the unlock, or calling it twice per event, changes whether a held trigger reports pressed. Demo playback must not consume keyboard-as-controller input (the `IsRunning()` guards) or demo desync occurs.
- Test coverage: none found for this file; `StaticVector` itself is covered by `test/static_vector_test.cpp` (relevant since `ToControllerButtonEvents` returns one).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/controller` (facade) over `internal/input/gamepad`, `internal/input/joystick`, `internal/input/kbctrl`; `ControllerButtonEvent` list becomes a Go slice or a fixed `[4]ControllerButtonEvent` + count to keep the static-vector bound honest. Strategy: define an `EventSource` interface (`ToControllerButtonEvents`, `IsPressed`, `Unlock`) so the precedence chain is a loop over registered sources with the trigger-correction hook; inject `DemoRunning bool`/`func() bool` so demo gating is testable; add tests for precedence, trigger up-recompute, and combo logic.
- Risks/open questions: Ebiten's input model (no raw SDL events, no `SDL_Event` type ids) means the event-type switch must be re-derived from Ebiten's Gamepad API — a real design gap, not a mechanical port. Also whether `HAS_KBCTRL` (keyboard-as-controller) is a port requirement at all.

### Source/controls/controller.h
- Purpose: Public interface header for the controller abstraction layer; documents the once-per-event unlock contract.
- Public API: the five free functions listed in `controller.cpp` (14-22), returning `StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent, 4>`.
- Depends on: SDL headers (`SDL3/SDL_events.h` or `SDL.h`, 3-7), `controller_buttons.h` (`ControllerButton`, `ControllerButtonCombo`, `ControllerButtonEvent`), `utils/static_vector.hpp` (`StaticVector`, static_vector.hpp:21). Includes `SDL.h` unconditionally (no `#ifndef USE_SDL1`), so porting note: the header itself assumes SDL2/3 event types exist.
- Requirements for Go port: the exported function set with the same signatures/return arity, plus an event abstraction replacing `const SDL_Event &`.
- 1:1 constraints: the `4` capacity in the return type (18) and the `bool` returns for the pressed/hotplug predicates; the "exactly once at the start of each SDL input event" ordering contract on `UnlockControllerState` (13-14).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: none of its own; the contract is a call-order requirement.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: collapses into `internal/input/controller`'s exported API; `SDL_Event` should become a port-defined `InputEvent` struct or interface so the package stays SDL-free (Ebiten adapter lives in a sibling package).
- Risks/open questions: whether to keep returning a capped 4-element structure (joystick hats) or a plain slice — see risks in the .cpp entry.

### Source/controls/controller_buttons.cpp
- Purpose: Maps a logical `ControllerButton` to a human-readable label or a vendor-specific glyph: a private table of 107 private-use-area icon code points (PlayStation / Nintendo / Xbox) and four per-layout mapping functions, dispatched by `ToString(GamepadLayout, ControllerButton)`.
- Public API: exactly one function, `std::string_view ToString(GamepadLayout gamepadType, ControllerButton button)` (281-294); everything else is in an anonymous namespace (4, 279): `ToGenericButtonText` (115), `ToPlayStationIcon` (159), `ToNintendoIcon` (199), `ToXboxIcon` (239), and the `controller_button_icon` string_view constants (5-113).
- Depends on: `controller_buttons.h` (the enum values it switches over). Consumed wherever button labels are rendered: `control_panel.cpp:812` (death text), `Source/options.cpp:1460/1466` (remapping UI), and by extension `DiabloUI/settingsmenu.cpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A function returning a display string (or glyph string) for a (layout, button) pair, with per-layout switch tables covering the 16 real buttons plus `NONE`/`IGNORE`.
  - Generic labels: `A B X Y Start Select LT RT LB RB LS RS Up Down Left Right`, plus `None` for `ControllerButton_NONE`, `Ignored` for `ControllerButton_IGNORE`, and `Unknown` for anything else (115-157).
  - Vendor mappings must encode the physical-position convention documented in the header (A/B and X/Y swapped on Nintendo): PlayStation A→Cross, B→Circle, X→Square, Y→Triangle; Nintendo A→B-glyph, B→A-glyph, X→Y-glyph, Y→X-glyph; Xbox identity (159-277).
  - Shoulder/trigger/stick mapping per layout: PS L2/R2/L1/R1/L3/R3, Nintendo ZL/ZR/L/R/LStick_Click/RStick_Click, Xbox LT/RT/LB/RB/LStick_Click/RStick_Click; start/back → Options/Share, Plus/Minus, Menu/View; dpad → the matching dpad glyph (159-277).
  - Any button not covered by a vendor table (including NONE/IGNORE and any glyph-only stick directions) falls back to the generic text (193-196, 233-236, 273-276) — so the generic function is part of the public behaviour, not just data.
  - The icon table (5-112) is needed only if the port renders these glyphs; unused entries (all the stick-direction icons and the extra Nintendo/Xbox buttons) exist for completeness/localization of the mapping UI.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Glyphs are UTF-8-encoded code points U+E000–U+E06A, 3 bytes each, assigned contiguously in the order listed (6-112): PS Triangle E000, Square E001, X E002, Circle E003, Options E004, Share E005, L2 E006, R2 E007, L1 E008, R1 E009, DPad Up/Right/Down/Left E00A-E00D, LStick NW/W/SW/N/center/S/NE/E/SE E00E-E016, L3 E017, RStick NW/W/SW/N/center/S/NE/E/SE E018-E020, R3 E021, Touchpad E022; Nintendo X E023, Y E024, B E025, A E026, Plus E027, Minus E028, ZL E029, ZR E02A, L E02B, R E02C, DPad Up/Right/Down/Left E02D-E030, LStick NW..SE E031-E039, LStick_Click E03A, RStick NW..SE E03B-E043, RStick_Click E044, Home E045, Screenshot E046, SL E047, SR E048; Xbox Y E049, X E04A, A E04B, B E04C, Menu E04D, View E04E, LT E04F, RT E050, LB E051, RB E052, DPad Up/Right/Down/Left E053-E056, LStick NW/W/SW/N/center/NE/E/SE E057-E05E, LStick_Click E05F, RStick NW/W/SW/N/center/S/NE/E/SE E060-E068, RStick_Click E069, Xbox logo E06A. (Note the two documented gaps: no `Playstation` home/touchpad alias beyond E022, and the Xbox LStick set omits an `S` entry — Xbox_LStick has NW,W,SW,N,center,NE,E,SE at E057-E05E.)
  - Only 16 glyphs per layout are actually reachable through the three mapping functions; the rest are `[[maybe_unused]]` data (6-112).
  - Dispatch: `PlayStation → PS table`, `Nintendo → Nintendo table`, `Xbox → Xbox table`, `default (Generic)` → generic text (283-293) — `Generic` is the explicit default, not a fallthrough error.
  - No localization of the generic English labels here (they are plain ASCII), but the returned value is a `string_view` into static storage → in Go, plain constants; no allocation.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure function over compile-time constant data; no state, no ordering effects, safe from any thread.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -l "GamepadLayout\|ToString" test/` → no hits).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/gamepadlayout` (or a file inside `internal/input/controller`) exposing `func ButtonLabel(layout GamepadLayout, button ControllerButton) string` with `map[ControllerButton]string` per layout plus a shared generic fallback map; the private-use glyph constants belong in one `icons.go` as `const` strings. Strategy: keep the *fallback-to-generic* rule explicit in code (one func with a switch on layout calling per-layout maps that return `("", false)` on miss) so behaviour parity is testable; add a table test asserting every `ControllerButton` in `[NONE..DPAD_RIGHT]` maps to a non-empty label for all four layouts.
- Risks/open questions: rendering U+E000–U+E06A requires a font with those glyphs (the game ships a custom icon font) — the Go/Ebiten port needs that font asset or a bitmap-button renderer; otherwise fall back to generic text unconditionally. Decide early, since it changes whether the icon table is ported at all.

### Source/controls/controller_buttons.h
- Purpose: The common logical button vocabulary for joystick/gamepad/keyboard-as-controller input, plus the button-event, button-combo, and gamepad-layout types, and the label function declaration.
- Public API: `enum ControllerButton : uint8_t` with `FIRST`/`LAST` sentinels (12-33); `struct ControllerButtonCombo { ControllerButton modifier; ControllerButton button; }` with three constexpr ctors (35-58); `struct ControllerButtonEvent { ControllerButton button; bool up; }` (60-70); `inline bool IsDPadButton(ControllerButton)` (69-75); `enum class GamepadLayout : uint8_t { Generic, Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox }` (77-82); `[[nodiscard]] std::string_view ToString(GamepadLayout, ControllerButton)` (84).
- Depends on: `<cstdint>`, `<functional>`, `<string_view>`. Included by `controller.h`, `control_mode.hpp`, `devices/game_controller.h`, `devices/joystick.h`, `devices/kbcontroller.h`, `options.*`, `DiabloUI/*`, `control_panel.cpp` (via `ToString`).
- Requirements for Go port: an exported int-typed `ControllerButton` enum with all 18 enumerators and `FIRST`/`LAST` bounds (used for iteration/sizing of per-button arrays), `ControllerButtonCombo{Modifier, Button}` with the "modifier defaults to NONE" semantic (including the single-arg construction form), `ControllerButtonEvent{Button, Up}`, `IsDPadButton`, `GamepadLayout`, and `ToString`/`ButtonLabel`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Enumerator order/values (12-32): `NONE=0, IGNORE=1, AXIS_TRIGGERLEFT=2, AXIS_TRIGGERRIGHT=3, BUTTON_A=4, BUTTON_B=5, BUTTON_X=6, BUTTON_Y=7, BUTTON_LEFTSTICK=8, BUTTON_RIGHTSTICK=9, BUTTON_LEFTSHOULDER=10, BUTTON_RIGHTSHOULDER=11, BUTTON_START=12, BUTTON_BACK=13, BUTTON_DPAD_UP=14, BUTTON_DPAD_DOWN=15, BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT=16, BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT=17`; `FIRST = NONE`, `LAST = BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT` (31-32). Underlying type `uint8_t`.
  - Comments at 10-11 are normative: A/B/X/Y are *physical Xbox-360 positions*; Nintendo swaps A↔B and X↔Y — this is why the vendor tables in controller_buttons.cpp cross them.
  - `IsDPadButton` is exactly the four `BUTTON_DPAD_*` values (69-75).
  - `GamepadLayout` order `Generic=0, Nintendo=1, PlayStation=2, Xbox=3`, `uint8_t` (77-82) — `Generic` is the zero value, which `ToString` treats as the default branch.
  - `ControllerButtonCombo` default and single-button forms both set `modifier = NONE` (37-52) — combo-with-no-modifier must be representable as the zero enum, not a sentinel bool.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: types only; no state. `bool up` in the event struct is "this event releases the button", the inverse of a naive `pressed` naming — keep the meaning when porting.
- Test coverage: none found (no test references these types directly).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/button` (leaf package, no deps beyond stdlib) exposing the enums/structs; `ToString` lives in `internal/input/gamepadlayout`/`controller` to avoid a cycle with the .cpp's dependency direction (Go: `button` must not import the label package). Strategy: define `type ControllerButton uint8` with `const` block preserving the numeric values verbatim (input remapping files / pad-mapper serialization may persist them), plus `func (b ControllerButton) IsDPad() bool`.
- Risks/open questions: `<functional>` is included but unused — no port obligation. If any saved config (options/ini, pad mapper) stores these numeric ids, the values must not be reordered; verify against the options serialization before touching the enum.

# vol3-006.md

# Volume III — batch 006

Scope: `Source/controls/**` motion + device layer (12 files, 2153 lines total). All files read completely.
Repo-wide convention: this layer is SDL-event-driven, not tick-driven — see per-file determinism notes.

### Source/controls/controller_motion.cpp
- Purpose: Owns the analog-stick state and turns raw SDL axis events into scaled stick values plus D-pad/padmapper/mouse-simulation movement directions. Also holds the deadzone math and the 8-way stick→direction sectoring.
- Public API: `bool SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper;` (L31), globals `float leftStickX, leftStickY, rightStickX, rightStickY` (L123), `float leftStickXUnscaled, leftStickYUnscaled, rightStickXUnscaled, rightStickYUnscaled` (L124), `bool leftStickNeedsScaling, rightStickNeedsScaling` (L125); `bool IsControllerMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (L152), `void ProcessControllerMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (L193), `StickPush GetAnalogStickPush(float,float)` (L210), `AxisDirection GetAnalogStickDirection(float,float)` (L220), `AxisDirection GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection(bool usePadmapper)` (L248), `void SimulateRightStickWithPadmapper(ControllerButtonEvent)` (L295). File-local (`namespace {}`): `ScaleJoystickAxes` (L35), `IsMovementOverriddenByPadmapper` (L81), `TriggersQuickSpellAction` (L89), `IsPressedForMovement` (L101), `SetSimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` (L109), `ScaleJoysticks` (L129).
- Depends on: `GetOptions().Controller.fDeadzone` (L130-132; default 0.07F set in Source/options.cpp:248); `PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent` / `PadmapperIsActionActive` (Source/controls/padmapper.hpp:13-14); `GetOptions().Padmapper.ButtonComboForAction` (Source/options.h:833); `IsControllerButtonPressed` (Source/controls/controller.h:19); `PadMenuNavigatorActive`, `PadHotspellMenuActive`, `SuppressedButton` (Source/controls/game_controls.h, defined in game_controls.cpp:32-34); `SpellSelectFlag` (Source/control/control.hpp:65); `GameController::Get/ProcessAxisMotion` (devices/game_controller.h), `Joystick::Get/ProcessAxisMotion` (devices/joystick.h); `VirtualGamepadState` + `ControlMode` (Source/controls/touch/gamepad.h:111, Source/controls/control_mode.hpp:17,29); `AxisDirection` (controls/axis_direction.h); `LogVerbose` (utils/log.hpp); SDL event/gamepad headers.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Ported stick state as a package-level struct (or explicit struct passed by pointer) with the same 10 fields and the same write ordering; `ProcessControllerMotion` must write unscaled + set `NeedsScaling`, and scaling must be a *separate* step invoked from the same function (L198/205), not lazily at read time.
  - `ScaleJoystickAxes` must be radial-and-scaled (not per-axis): early return when deadzone==0, zero both axes when deadzone>=1, else magnitude-gated rescale with the L58 scaling factor and the L64-72 max-axis clamp.
  - Direction derivation must be split exactly like upstream: `GetAnalogStickPush` (None/Weak/Firm from squared magnitude, no sqrt — L214-217) and `GetAnalogStickDirection` (8-way sectoring via ratio against tan(22.5°) — L220-246). The Weak/None/Firm distinction is what makes the character turn-in-place vs walk; it must be preserved as a 3-valued enum.
  - `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection`: analog sectoring only when Firm (L251-252); then OR-in D-pad sources in this precedence — padmapper actions when `usePadmapper`, otherwise real D-pad buttons unless `SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper`, then VirtualGamepad direction pad when `ControlMode==VirtualGamepad && isActive` (L260-278); finally the *override order* up-beats-down and left-beats-right (L280-289).
  - `IsPressedForMovement`: a button counts for movement only if `!PadMenuNavigatorActive && IsControllerButtonPressed(button) && !IsMovementOverriddenByPadmapper(button) && !(SpellSelectFlag && TriggersQuickSpellAction(button))` (L101-107).
  - `SimulateRightStickWithPadmapper`: ignore `ControllerButton_NONE`; ignore a non-release event whose button equals `SuppressedButton`; resolve the action name; if it is not one of the four `Mouse{Up,Down,Left,Right}` actions, only clear the sim flag when the right stick is already at rest, and return (L295-311); otherwise compute each direction as (this event pressed it) OR (the other action is still active via padmapper), zero the right stick, then accumulate ±1.0 per active direction and set the sim flag (L313-328).
  - `SetSimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` is edge-triggered and logs a verbose line on both edges (L109-118) — keep the log, it is the only observable trace of mouse-mode transitions.
  - `IsControllerMotion` must accept only the four thumb axes (gamepad axis events) or the four `JOY_AXIS_*` joystick axes — never triggers, never hat/ball (L152-190).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `maximum = 32767.0` (L50); `deadZone = deadzone * maximum` (L53).
  - `magnitude = sqrt(x*x + y*y)`; gate `magnitude >= deadZone` (L55-56).
  - `scalingFactor = 1.F / magnitude * (magnitude - deadZone) / (maximum - deadZone)` — note the association: reciprocal-of-magnitude multiply happens *before* the ratio (L58); port the expression in the same order.
  - Clamp factor: `1.F / absAnalogX` if `absAnalogX > absAnalogY` else `1.F / absAnalogY`, applied only when either abs > 1.0 (L65-71).
  - Deadzone short-circuits: `deadzone == 0` → unchanged axes (L41-43); `deadzone >= 1.0` → both axes zeroed (L44-48). Both are exact float comparisons against literals.
  - `StickDirectionThreshold = 0.6F`, `StickDirectionThresholdSquared = 0.36` (controller_motion.h:29-30); Firm test `magnitudeSquared >= StickDirectionThresholdSquared` (L217); None test `magnitudeSquared == 0.0F` (L215).
  - `DiagonalCutoff = 0.41421356F` (L227); diagonal band is `ratio > DiagonalCutoff && ratio < 1.0F/DiagonalCutoff` (≈2.4142…); special case `absX == 0.0F` → pure vertical (L228-231).
  - Sign convention: `stickY > 0` means UP for both analog (L229/239/244) and D-pad (L281-289); `stickX > 0` means RIGHT.
  - QuickSpell prefix test is a literal 10-char prefix `"QuickSpell"` compared on `actionName.data(), prefix.size()` with a `size() < prefix.size()` guard (L94-98).
  - Padmapper mouse action names are exactly `"MouseUp"`, `"MouseDown"`, `"MouseLeft"`, `"MouseRight"` (L303-306); movement action names exactly `"MoveUp"/"MoveDown"/"MoveLeft"/"MoveRight"` (L260-263).
  - Simulated right-stick magnitude is exactly ±1.0F per axis, and both up+down (or left+right) simultaneously cancel to 0 by accumulation order up, down, left, right (L320-327).
  - Left and right deadzones are read from the *same* option (L131-132) — there is no per-stick deadzone today; do not "fix" it.
  - No RNG, no serialization in this file.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: All stick state is mutable package globals written from the SDL event pump (single-threaded main loop); scaling is deferred by the `NeedsScaling` flags, so a reader can observe a scaled value derived from the *last* event, not the last axis write — same-frame ordering must be preserved. `leftStickNeedsScaling` is cleared inside `ScaleJoysticks` (L139/146). `SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` is an exported global read by `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection` and by callers elsewhere (e.g. mouse/keyboard mode detection). Order-of-init: globals are zero-initialised except `SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` (L31, BSS false) — no constructor dependency. Not reentrant: `ProcessControllerMotion` calls into device classes which write the same globals.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rln 'controller_motion' test/` matches only test/panel_state_test.cpp which includes `control/control.hpp`, not this file). No upstream unit tests for deadzone or sectoring.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/motion` (new) — `type Motion struct { LeftStickX, LeftStickY, RightStickX, RightStickY float32; ...Unscaled [4]float32; LeftNeedsScaling, RightNeedsScaling bool }` owned by the input hub and passed to the player-action layer; `ScaleJoystickAxes(x, y *float32, deadzone float32)` and `AnalogStickPush/Direction` as pure free functions so they are table-testable. Padmapper/option/flag reads become interface parameters (`PadmapperView`, `FlagsView`) rather than globals so `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection` is testable without SDL. Strategy: keep float32 (`1.F` literals ⇒ float32 in Go) — do not widen to float64, that changes results at the 0.36 threshold boundary.
- Risks/open questions: (1) The C++ "None" test is `magnitudeSquared == 0.0F`, which relies on `ScaleJoystickAxes` writing exact zeros inside the deadzone; a Go implementation that rounds or rescales will shift Weak↔None. (2) `SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` is consumed outside this file (mouse-vs-gamepad input method detection) — the port must keep it exported. (3) `tan(22.5°)` is truncated to 8 digits in the source; whether to keep the truncation (1:1) or use the exact value is a deliberate decision — keep the literal.

### Source/controls/controller_motion.h
- Purpose: Header declaring the analog-stick globals, the walk/turn threshold constants, the `StickPush` enum, and the motion entry points; the contract other subsystems read for "where is the stick".
- Public API: `extern bool SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` (L17); `extern float leftStickXUnscaled, leftStickYUnscaled, rightStickXUnscaled, rightStickYUnscaled` (L20); `extern float leftStickX, leftStickY, rightStickX, rightStickY` (L23); `extern bool leftStickNeedsScaling, rightStickNeedsScaling` (L26); `constexpr float StickDirectionThreshold = 0.6F` (L29), `constexpr float StickDirectionThresholdSquared = StickDirectionThreshold * StickDirectionThreshold` (L30); `enum class StickPush : uint8_t { None, Weak, Firm }` (L33-37); `GetAnalogStickPush` (L39), `GetAnalogStickDirection` (L40), `ProcessControllerMotion` (L43), `IsControllerMotion` (L46), `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection` (L49), `SimulateRightStickWithPadmapper` (L52).
- Depends on: `SDL_Event` (SDL3 vs SDL2 include switch, L6-10); `AxisDirection`/`AxisDirectionX/Y` (controls/axis_direction.h, L12); `ControllerButtonEvent` (controls/controller.h → controller_buttons.h, L13).
- Requirements for Go port: same exported names/signatures as listed for the .cpp; the threshold constants must be visible to whatever computes "walk vs turn" (player movement, targeting) since the value is a gameplay-facing tunable. `StickPush` needs 3 explicit values with identical underlying ordinals (None=0, Weak=1, Firm=2) because padmapper/movement code compares against them.
- 1:1 constraints: `0.6F` and its square `0.36F` (L29-30) — must be float32 and computed the same way, i.e. `const StickDirectionThresholdSquared = StickDirectionThreshold * StickDirectionThreshold`; enum underlying type `uint8_t` (L33). Comments at L16/22/25/28/32-36 carry the semantics ("inside the deadzone", "deflected, but below the walk threshold", "Minimum scaled stick magnitude to walk; below it, the character only turns in place") — port them, they are the only documentation of the turn-vs-walk rule.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Header-only constants; the `extern` block is the reason this subsystem has hidden global state. No order-of-init issues.
- Test coverage: none found (declarations only).
- Go mapping: collapses into `internal/input/motion` (`stick.go`) as exported consts `StickDirectionThreshold float32 = 0.6`, `StickDirectionThresholdSquared = StickDirectionThreshold * StickDirectionThreshold`, and `type StickPush uint8` with `StickPushNone/Weak/Firm`. Strategy: no separate Go header file; instead the globals become fields on the `Motion` struct so ownership is explicit — this header then exists only as the doc-comment source.
- Risks/open questions: If `Motion` becomes a struct rather than globals, every consumer (plrctrls, touch, mouse sim) must be threaded with it in the same call order; that is a wide-scope refactor and the main non-trivial decision in this batch.

### Source/controls/devices/game_controller.cpp
- Purpose: SDL "game controller/gamepad" device wrapper: maintains the open-gamepad list, maps gamepad events to `ControllerButton`, applies trigger hysteresis, feeds stick axes into the shared motion globals, and reports the physical gamepad layout.
- Public API (all members of `GameController`): `static std::vector<GameController> controllers_` (L25); `UnlockTriggerState()` (L27); `ControllerButton ToControllerButton(const SDL_Event&)` (L33); `static SDL_GamepadButton ToSdlGameControllerButton(ControllerButton)` (L101); `bool IsPressed(ControllerButton) const` (L139); `static bool ProcessAxisMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (L150); `static void Add(SDL_JoystickID)` / `Add(int)` (L178/180); `static void Remove(SDL_JoystickID)` (L213); `static GameController *Get(SDL_JoystickID)` (L226) and `Get(const SDL_Event&)` (L235); `static const std::vector<GameController> &All()` (L248); `static bool IsPressedOnAnyController(ControllerButton, SDL_JoystickID *which)` (L253); `static GamepadLayout getLayout(const SDL_Event&)` (L265).
- Depends on: `ControllerButton*` enum + `GamepadLayout` enum (controls/controller_buttons.h:12,77); motion globals `leftStick*Unscaled/rightStick*Unscaled` and `*NeedsScaling` (controller_motion.h:20-26); `SDLC_EventGamepadAxis/SDLC_EventGamepadButton` compat accessors (utils/sdl_compat.h); `SDL_OpenGamepad`/`SDL_GamepadHasButton`/`SDL_GetGamepadButton`/`SDL_GetGamepadTypeForID`/`SDL_GameControllerMappingForGUID` etc.; `UNIMPLEMENTED()` (utils/stubs.h); `Log`/SDL error+clear (utils/log.hpp, SDL_GetError/SDL_ClearError); `SDLUniquePtr<char>` (utils/sdl_ptrs.h). Callers: Source/controls/controller.cpp (event→button, `IsControllerButtonPressed`), controller_motion.cpp (`ProcessControllerMotion`), `UnlockControllerState` in controller.cpp:21-33.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A device registry equivalent to `controllers_` (ordered list, add by id/index, remove by instance id, lookup by instance id, lookup by event, iterate-all) and a `IsPressedOnAnyController(button) (bool, joystickID)` that returns the first matching instance id (L253-262).
  - Trigger hysteresis state machine per device: `trigger_left_is_down_/trigger_right_is_down_` booleans plus latched `trigger_left_state_/trigger_right_state_` buttons; on axis event, release when value falls below 8192, press when it rises above 16384, and return the latched state otherwise (L39-58). The latched state is what `ToControllerButton` returns even when nothing changed.
  - `UnlockTriggerState` must be called exactly once per SDL event (header comment L33-34; enforced by `UnlockControllerState` in controller.cpp) to re-arm the hysteresis latch.
  - `ToControllerButton`: axis events only for the two triggers (all other axes → `ControllerButton_NONE`); button down/up events mapped 1:1 to the 14 logical buttons (SOUTH→A, EAST→B, WEST→X, NORTH→Y, sticks, shoulders, START, BACK, DPAD x4); anything else → NONE (L61-99).
  - `ToSdlGameControllerButton`: reverse map; must raise/panic for the two trigger pseudo-buttons since SDL has no trigger button index (L102-104 `UNIMPLEMENTED()`); default → `SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_INVALID`.
  - `IsPressed`: trigger buttons read the latched booleans (L140-143); otherwise require `SDL_GamepadHasButton` *before* `SDL_GetGamepadButton` (L146-147) — capability-gated polling, not event state.
  - `ProcessAxisMotion`: only `GAMEPAD_AXIS_MOTION`; write LEFTX/LEFTY/RIGHTX/RIGHTY into the unscaled globals with Y negated and set the matching `NeedsScaling` (L150-175); returns true only for those four axes.
  - `Add`: open the gamepad, log, on failure log SDL error + clear error + return without registering; capture instance id and the mapping string (SDL3: `SDL_GetGamepadMappingForID`, SDL2: from joystick GUID) and log the mapping *after* push_back (L178-211). Note `controllers_.push_back(result)` happens at L206 before the mapping log at L208-210.
  - `Remove`: first-match erase by `instance_id_`, log "not found" if absent (L213-224).
  - `getLayout`: compile-time override `DEVILUTIONX_GAMEPAD_TYPE` wins; else SDL3 type→layout table (Xbox360/XboxOne→Xbox, PS3/4/5→PlayStation, Switch Pro/both Joy-Cons/pair→Nintendo, default Generic); SDL2 path uses version-gated cases and returns Generic for anything unmapped, including a null controller (L265-329).
- 1:1 constraints: trigger thresholds `axis.value < 8192` (25%) and `axis.value > 16384` (50%) with those exact comparison operators — strict inequality on both sides (L40,44,50,54). Comments label them "25% pressed"/"50% pressed". Y-axis inversion `static_cast<float>(-axis.value)` for LEFTY and RIGHTY only (L160,168). Default `instance_id_ = -1` (header L56). Trigger button mapping: `JOY/AXIS_TRIGGERLEFT/RIGHT` pseudo-buttons are *not* in `ToSdlGameControllerButton` (UNIMPLEMENTED at L104). Layout buckets (SDL3 branch, the live one): Xbox360+XboxOne → Xbox (L272-274); PS3+PS4+PS5 → PlayStation (L275-278); Switch Pro + JoyConLeft + JoyConRight + JoyConPair → Nintendo (L279-283); default → Generic (L284-285). Compile-time `DEVILUTIONX_GAMEPAD_TYPE` short-circuits everything (L266-269). `getLayout` reads `event.gdevice.which` (L271) so it is only valid for device events. The SDL2-only table (L290-326, gated on `SDL_VERSION_ATLEAST(2,0,12)`) buckets Xbox360/XboxOne/GoogleStadia/AmazonLuna/NVIDIAShield → Xbox (L306-315) and PS3/PS4/PS5 → PlayStation (L300-305), with VIRTUAL/UNKNOWN/MAX falling through to Generic (L316-326) — dead code for an SDL3/Ebiten target.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `controllers_` is a static mutable vector — hotplug add/remove invalidates the raw pointers returned by `Get`, so callers must not cache them across events (Go: return indices or hold `*GameController` only within one event). Trigger latch + `NeedsScaling` globals are per-event mutable state; `UnlockTriggerState` is order-critical (must run before reading buttons for the event, per header L33-34). `getLayout` reads `event.gdevice.which` in the SDL3 branch, which is only valid for device events. Logging has a side effect on the SDL error queue (`SDL_ClearError`) — a Go port must not need it since Go surfaces errors as values.
- Test coverage: none found (no test file references GameController; `grep -rn 'GameController' test/` is empty).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/gamepad` — `type Registry struct { list []*Gamepad }` with `Add/Remove/Get/All/IsPressedOnAny`, and `type Gamepad struct { handle SDLGamepadHandle (or *sdl.Gamepad); instanceID int32; triggerLeftDown, triggerRightDown bool; triggerLeftState, triggerRightState ControllerButton }`. Strategy: keep polling (`HasButton`/`GetButton`) via a small `PadPoller` interface so tests can fake button state and trigger hysteresis with synthetic axis sequences; make the UNIMPLEMENTED trigger case a panic/assert. `getLayout` becomes a pure `layoutForType(t GamepadType) GamepadLayout` function table, dropping the SDL-version `#if` maze (target SDL3/Ebiten-backed only).
- Risks/open questions: (1) Porting SDL2-only branches is dead weight — decide whether the Go port supports only the SDL3 semantics (likely) and delete the rest, which breaks strict 1:1. (2) Whether the Go build keeps a "raw joystick" path at all (joystick.cpp) or relies on Ebiten/SDL gamepad abstraction only; both files are in this batch, so the answer changes 2 files. (3) `Add` push_back-before-log ordering means a partially-constructed entry is visible; harmless in C++, but in Go with a `[]Gamepad` value slice copying matters (see joystick `Add` too).

### Source/controls/devices/game_controller.h
- Purpose: Declares the `GameController` class and its per-device trigger-latch state; the only surface other files use for gamepad buttons/axes.
- Public API: class `GameController` with statics `Add(SDL_JoystickID)`/`Add(int joystickIndex)` (L23/25), `Remove(SDL_JoystickID)` (L27), `Get(SDL_JoystickID)` (L28), `Get(const SDL_Event&)` (L29), `All()` (L30), `IsPressedOnAnyController(ControllerButton, SDL_JoystickID *which = nullptr)` (L31), `ProcessAxisMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (L39), `ToSdlGameControllerButton(ControllerButton)` (L41/43), `getLayout(const SDL_Event&)` (L47); instance `UnlockTriggerState()` (L34), `ToControllerButton(const SDL_Event&)` (L36), `IsPressed(ControllerButton) const` (L38). Private: `sdl_game_controller_` (L51/53), `instance_id_ = -1` (L56), `trigger_left_state_`/`trigger_right_state_ = ControllerButton_NONE` (L58-59), `trigger_left_is_down_`/`trigger_right_is_down_ = false` (L60-61).
- Depends on: `<vector>`; SDL gamepad/event/joystick headers; `ControllerButton`, `GamepadLayout` (controls/controller_buttons.h); `GameAction`-bearing include of controls/game_controls.h (L15-16 — this header pulls game_controls.h, so it is a hub include).
- Requirements for Go port: expose the same static-vs-instance split: registry operations on the package (or a `*GamepadRegistry`), button/trigger queries on the device. The default argument `which = nullptr` becomes a second return value or a separate lookup method. `UnlockTriggerState` must remain a public, documented "call exactly once per event" hook.
- 1:1 constraints: initial values — `instance_id_ = -1` (L56), `trigger_left_state_/trigger_right_state_ = ControllerButton_NONE` (L58-59), `trigger_*_is_down_ = false` (L60-61), SDL handle null/nil (L51/53). Comment at L35-37 ("Must be called exactly once at the start of each SDL input event") is a behavioural requirement, keep it.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `controllers_` is a static, so the class is a singleton registry with value-typed elements; copying a `GameController` into the vector is what `Add` does (L206 in .cpp) — pointer identity of `Get()` is tied to vector storage stability. No thread safety at all.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: same package as the .cpp (`internal/input/gamepad`), file `gamepad.go`; the private fields become unexported struct fields. Strategy: to remove pointer-invalidation risk, store `[]*Gamepad` and have `Get` return `*Gamepad` — behaviourally identical for callers since C++ also returns pointers.
- Risks/open questions: This header includes `game_controls.h` only for `GamepadLayout`? No — `GamepadLayout` is in controller_buttons.h; the game_controls.h include (L16) looks unnecessary and creates an include cycle risk. Worth verifying before mirroring the include graph in Go (Go will reject a real cycle).

### Source/controls/devices/joystick.cpp
- Purpose: Raw-SDL joystick wrapper for platforms without gamepad mapping: maps unnamed buttons and POV hats to logical `ControllerButton`s, feeds axes into the shared motion globals, and maintains the joystick registry.
- Public API (members of `Joystick`): `static std::vector<Joystick> joysticks_` (L24); `static StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent,4> ToControllerButtonEvents(const SDL_Event&)` (L26); `static StaticVector<ControllerButtonEvent,4> GetHatEvents()` (L139, private); `void UpdateHatState(const SDL_JoyHatEvent&)` (L155, private); `void UnlockHatState()` (L194); `static int ToSdlJoyButton(ControllerButton)` (L201, private); `bool IsHatButtonPressed(ControllerButton) const` (L281, private); `bool IsPressed(ControllerButton) const` (L309); `static bool ProcessAxisMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (L327); `static void Add(SDL_JoystickID)`/`Add(int deviceIndex)` (L366/386); `static void Remove(SDL_JoystickID)` (L406); `static const std::vector<Joystick> &All()` (L421); `static Joystick *Get(SDL_JoystickID)` (L426), `Get(const SDL_Event&)` (L435); `static bool IsPressedOnAnyJoystick(ControllerButton)` (L463).
- Depends on: `ControllerButtonEvent`/`ControllerButton` incl. `ControllerButton_IGNORE` (controls/controller_buttons.h); `StaticVector<T,4>` (utils/static_vector.hpp); motion globals `leftStick*Unscaled`/`rightStick*Unscaled`/`*NeedsScaling` (controller_motion.h:20-26); `SDL_JoystickGetHat`, `SDL_GetNumJoystickButtons`, `SDL_GetJoystickButton`, `SDL_JoystickGetButton`, `SDL_OpenJoystick`/`SDL_JoystickOpen`, `SDL_GetJoystickNameForID`/`SDL_JoystickNameForIndex`, `SDL_JoystickInstanceID`; build-time macro tables `JOY_BUTTON_*`, `JOY_AXIS_*`, `JOY_HAT_DPAD_*_HAT` + `JOY_HAT_DPAD_*` (from SDL1 backport header utils/sdl2_to_1_2_backports.h / platform config); `Log`/`LogWarn`/`LogError` + `SDL_ClearError`. Callers: controller.cpp (`ToControllerButtonEvents`, `IsPressedOnAnyJoystick`, `UnlockControllerState`→`UnlockHatState`), controller_motion.cpp (`Joystick::Get/ProcessAxisMotion`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A joystick registry mirroring add/remove/get-by-id/get-by-event/all and `IsPressedOnAnyJoystick` (first-match OR).
  - Event→button-event translation returning a *small vector* of events: exactly one entry for plain button events (or `ControllerButton_IGNORE` for unmapped buttons), possibly 0–4 entries for hat events, exactly one `ControllerButton_NONE,up=false` entry for axis/ball events, and an empty result for any other event type (L26-137).
  - Hat state machine: `hatState_[4]` = {pressed, didStateChange} for UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT in that fixed slot order (L142-149, L161-188); `didStateChange` is set only when the bit differs from the stored value; `UpdateHatState` is *re-entrant-suppressed* by `lockHatState_` (set at L191, cleared by `UnlockHatState` L194-199 along with all `didStateChange` flags).
  - Hat→events emits `up = !pressed` per changed slot in order UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT; if nothing changed, emits a single `ControllerButton_IGNORE, up=false` (L142-153).
  - `IsPressed`: bail false on null handle; hat check first; then mapped button index; then bounds-check against the device's button count before polling (L309-324).
  - `ProcessAxisMotion`: only axis events; four `JOY_AXIS_*` cases write unscaled globals (Y negated) and return true, everything else false (L327-361).
  - `Add`: SDL3 path logs name (warn + clear error if name lookup fails), opens the joystick, on failure logs error + clears + returns without registering; SDL2 path guards `SDL_NumJoysticks() <= deviceIndex` and captures the instance id from the opened joystick (L366-404).
  - `Get(event)` dispatch by `which` for axis/ball/hat/button events; SDL1 path returns `joysticks_[0]` when the list is non-empty (L435-459).
- 1:1 constraints: Hat slot indices are hard-coded: `hatState_[0]`=UP, `[1]`=DOWN, `[2]`=LEFT, `[3]`=RIGHT (L142-149, L161-188) — this ordering is also the emission order. Button-event emission order for hats is UP→DOWN→LEFT→RIGHT (L142-149) and must not change (downstream modifier/suppression logic keys off first events). `up = !event.jbutton.down` (SDL3) vs `event.jbutton.state == SDL_RELEASED` (SDL2) (L32/34); `up = !hatState_[i].pressed` (L143-149). Axis inversion: `leftStickYUnscaled = -event.jaxis.value`, `rightStickYUnscaled = -event.jaxis.value`; X not inverted (L337-355). Y-negation is applied *before* the float conversion in this file, unlike game_controller.cpp where it is inside the cast. Button bounds rule: `joyButton < numButtons && GetButton(...)` — no lower-bound check needed because -1 is filtered earlier (L315-323). `ToSdlJoyButton` returns `-1` for unmapped buttons (L273, L276). `instance_id_ = -1` default, `sdl_joystick_ = NULL` default (header L62-63). Hat bit test is `SDL_JoystickGetHat(hat, JOY_HAT_DPAD_UP_HAT) & JOY_HAT_DPAD_UP` — bitwise AND against a platform-supplied mask, four independent `if`s (not `else if`), so one hat event can update several slots (L159-190). Unmapped physical button → `ControllerButton_IGNORE` with the *real* `up` value (L106/109), while a hat with no change → IGNORE with `up=false` (L151).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `joysticks_` static vector → same pointer-stability caveat as GameController, plus `UpdateHatState`/`GetHatEvents` mutate the object found through that vector within one event. `lockHatState_`/`UnlockHatState` implement a per-event edge-detection window: hat events after the unlock in the same tick will not re-fire — order of `UnlockControllerState` before `ProcessControllerMotion` (input.h:22-23) is therefore load-bearing. Hat `didStateChange` is cleared in `UnlockHatState`, so `GetHatEvents` must be called after `UpdateHatState` in the same event (L121-122). Single-threaded only.
- Test coverage: none found (`grep -rn 'Joystick' test/` empty).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/joystick` — `type Registry struct{ list []*Joystick }`, `type Joystick struct { handle *sdl.Joystick; instanceID int32; hat [4]HatState; hatLocked bool }`, `HatState{Pressed, DidStateChange bool}`; `ToControllerButtonEvents` returns `[]ControllerButtonEvent` capped at 4 (allocate a fixed `[4]ControllerButtonEvent` + length, or return a slice backed by a stack array) — preserve "0..4 events" semantics rather than the `StaticVector` type. `JOY_BUTTON_*`/`JOY_HAT_DPAD_*` macro tables become a per-platform data table (`map[ControllerButton]int` + `hatSlotMasks [4]struct{ hat int8; mask uint8; ok bool }`) so the `#ifdef` maze becomes runtime data, which is also the only way to make this testable.
- Risks/open questions: (1) The whole file's button/hat mapping is compile-time `#ifdef` data supplied by platform toolchains; the Go port needs an actual source of truth for those tables — currently they exist only for SDL1/retro-build targets, so on a modern SDL3/Ebiten build most of these branches are dead. Confirm which platforms the rewrite must support before inventing tables. (2) `ControllerButton_IGNORE` semantics (suppress handling, L371 in game_controls.cpp) must survive the port or retro joysticks will fire gameplay actions. (3) SDL1 branch returning `joysticks_[0]` conflicts with the Go "no SDL1" story.

### Source/controls/devices/kbcontroller.cpp
- Purpose: Maps keyboard keys to gamepad buttons for builds without a gamepad (retro handhelds), so the whole controller stack can be driven by the keyboard; includes a held-key query via the SDL keyboard state array.
- Public API: `ControllerButton KbCtrlToControllerButton(const SDL_Event &event)` (L21), `SDL_Keycode ControllerButtonToKbCtrlKeyCode(ControllerButton button)` (L110), `bool IsKbCtrlButtonPressed(ControllerButton button)` (L182). Entire file is compiled only when `HAS_KBCTRL == 1` (L3 … L197 `#endif`).
- Depends on: build-time macros `HAS_KBCTRL`, `KBCTRL_IGNORE_1`, `KBCTRL_BUTTON_{A,B,X,Y,LEFTSTICK,RIGHTSTICK,LEFTSHOULDER,RIGHTSHOULDER,TRIGGERLEFT,TRIGGERRIGHT,START,BACK,DPAD_UP,DPAD_DOWN,DPAD_LEFT,DPAD_RIGHT}` supplied via `-D` flags (documented in Source/controls/README.md:25-40, e.g. `-DKBCTRL_BUTTON_A=SDLK_b`); `ControllerButton` enum (controls/controller_buttons.h); `SDL_GetKeyboardState`, `SDL_GetScancodeFromKey`, (SDL1) `SDL_GetKeyState`; `controls/controller_motion.h` + `utils/sdl_compat.h`/`utils/stubs.h` includes (present but not actually used by any function body here). Callers: Source/controls/controller.cpp:49-54 (event→button) and :83-85 (pressed query), plus menu_controls.cpp:105 and plrctrls.cpp:2082.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Bidirectional key↔button tables, each entry optional (a platform may define only a subset) — in Go these become a configured map built from the same option set, with "not mapped" falling through to NONE/`SDLK_UNKNOWN`.
  - `KbCtrlToControllerButton`: only key down/up events; returns `ControllerButton_IGNORE` for the ignore key, mapped buttons otherwise, `ControllerButton_NONE` for anything unmapped or non-key event (L21-107).
  - `ControllerButtonToKbCtrlKeyCode`: reverse mapping for 16 buttons; triggers map to `KBCTRL_BUTTON_TRIGGERLEFT/RIGHT`; default → `SDLK_UNKNOWN` (L110-180).
  - `IsKbCtrlButtonPressed`: resolve keycode, false on UNKNOWN, otherwise read the global keyboard-state array at the *scancode* derived from the keycode (L182-194). Must remain a polling call (no event state) so `IsControllerButtonPressed` can consult it at arbitrary times.
  - Demo-mode gating lives in the caller (controller.cpp:50, 83: `if (!demo::IsRunning())`) — not in this file; the Go port must keep the gate where it is.
- 1:1 constraints: Return `ControllerButton_NONE` (not IGNORE) for unmapped keys (L103) but `ControllerButton_IGNORE` for the explicit ignore key (L36); unmapped buttons → `SDLK_UNKNOWN` (L178). Keyboard-state read order: keycode→scancode→`state[scancode]`; SDL1 fallback indexes by keycode directly (L188/190/192). `KBCTRL_BUTTON_B` is commented "// Right button" and `KBCTRL_BUTTON_X` "// Left button" (L43,47) — i.e. the physical layout is Nintendo-ish; preserve the comments as they explain the pairing with the README example (`-DKBCTRL_BUTTON_B=SDLK_a`). Note the upstream SDL3 branch has a duplicate `case SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN:` twice instead of KEY_UP (L25-26) — a real bug; a faithful port must decide: replicate or fix (fixing changes behaviour for key-release events).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: No mutable state in this file at all — pure lookups plus SDL global keyboard-state polling. Its behaviour depends on `SDL_GetKeyboardState` snapshot semantics: within one event pump the array can change between calls, so button queries made at different points in a tick can disagree; the C++ stack tolerates this. Compiled away entirely when `HAS_KBCTRL != 1`, so most builds have none of this.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/kbctrl` with `type KeyMap map[Key]ControllerButton` + inverse `map[ControllerButton]Key`, constructed from config/build options; `func (m *Mapper) ButtonFromEvent(ev KeyEvent) ControllerButton`, `func (m *Mapper) KeyCodeForButton(b ControllerButton) Key`, `func (m *Mapper) IsPressed(b ControllerButton) bool` over an injected `keyboardState func() []bool` (Ebiten's `Inpututil`/`input.Key` map works). Strategy: represent "unmapped" as absence from the map with explicit sentinels `KeyUnknown` and `ControllerButtonNone`/`Ignore`.
- Risks/open questions: (1) Does the Go rewrite need keyboard-as-gamepad at all? It only matters for targets with no gamepad; if not, this file can be dropped — but then `controller.cpp`'s two call sites change. (2) The duplicate `SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN` bug means upstream SDL3 kbctrl builds never see key-release events; porting "fixed" behaviour would alter release handling (button stuck down). Needs an explicit decision, recorded, not silently changed.

### Source/controls/devices/kbcontroller.h
- Purpose: Declares the keyboard-as-gamepad surface and, more importantly, defines the `HAS_KBCTRL` compile-time switch that gates the whole feature in and out of the build.
- Public API: `#ifndef HAS_KBCTRL / #define HAS_KBCTRL 0 / #endif` (L4-6) — the feature macro itself lives here; then, only under `#if HAS_KBCTRL == 1` (L8 … L30): `ControllerButton KbCtrlToControllerButton(const SDL_Event&)` (L23), `SDL_Keycode ControllerButtonToKbCtrlKeyCode(ControllerButton)` (L25), `bool IsKbCtrlButtonPressed(ControllerButton)` (L27).
- Depends on: `ControllerButton` (controls/controller_buttons.h, L19); SDL event/keyboard headers with an SDL1 backport include (L9-17). Included by Source/controls/controller.cpp:15 and Source/utils/display.cpp:44 — the two places that consult kbctrl state (button translation / pressed polling, plus display code that presumably suppresses the on-screen keyboard).
- Requirements for Go port: a build/configuration-level feature flag rather than a preprocessor one — the port needs an explicit "kbctrl enabled?" option plus the key↔button table wired only when enabled, so the callers in controller.cpp behave identically (skip the kbctrl lookup entirely when off). The three functions keep their split: event→button, button→key, and polled `IsPressed`.
- 1:1 constraints: `HAS_KBCTRL` defaults to `0` when undefined (L4-6), and every consumer tests `== 1` (controller.cpp:49,83; menu_controls.cpp:105 uses `== 0`), that is, any non-1 value means off — the port must treat "enabled" as a boolean, not "non-zero int", to stay faithful where `== 0` branches exist. All declarations vanish when the flag is off (L8/L30), so a Go build without the feature must not leave dead symbols reachable.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Nothing stateful; this is an all-or-nothing compile-time boundary, so it is an order-of-build (not order-of-init) concern: `IsKbCtrlButtonPressed` reads SDL's global keyboard state and is polled from arbitrary call sites.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: same package/file as kbcontroller.cpp (`internal/input/kbctrl`), gated by a `Enabled bool` on the Mapper constructed from config/build tags instead of `#if`. Strategy: make the mapper a nil-safe optional collaborator (`*kbctrl.Mapper` may be nil) so controller.cpp's two call sites translate to `if h.kbctrl != nil { ... }`, preserving the compile-time absence as a runtime absence.
- Risks/open questions: Upstream also relies on `HAS_KBCTRL == 0` branches in menu_controls.cpp:105 — the Go port needs one flag readable from *those* call sites too, not just the two in controller.cpp, or keyboard-menu behaviour diverges.

- Public API: globals `bool PadMenuNavigatorActive = false` (L32), `bool PadHotspellMenuActive = false` (L33), `ControllerButton SuppressedButton = ControllerButton_NONE` (L34); `ControllerButton TranslateTo(GamepadLayout, ControllerButton)` (L331), `bool SkipsMovie(ControllerButtonEvent)` (L350), `bool IsSimulatedMouseClickBinding(ControllerButtonEvent)` (L359), `bool HandleControllerButtonEvent(const SDL_Event&, const ControllerButtonEvent, GameAction&)` (L369). File-local: `TranslateControllerButtonToGameMenuKey` (L38), `...ToMenuKey` (L55), `...ToQuestLogKey` (L81), `GetGameAction` (L96), `CanDeferToMovementHandler` (L217), `PressControllerButton` (L239).
- Depends on: `ControlMode`, `GamepadType` (controls/control_mode.hpp:17,29); `VirtualGamepadState` (controls/touch/gamepad.h:111) incl. `menuPanel.{char,quests,inventory,map}Button`, `primary/secondary/spell/cancel/health/manaButton`, each with `.isHeld/.didStateChange`; motion globals `leftStickX/Y`, `rightStickX/Y` + `IsControllerMotion`/`SimulateRightStickWithPadmapper` (controller_motion); padmapper API `PadmapperRelease/PadmapperPress/PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent` + `GetOptions().Padmapper.findAction` (padmapper.hpp:10-14, options.h:835); `IsControllerButtonPressed` (controller.h:19); player-control state `ControllerActionHeld` (plrctrls.h:24), `IsMovementHandlerActive` (:48), `PerformPrimaryActionRelease` (:59), `DetectInputMethod` (:50), `LastPlayerAction`/`PlayerActionType` (diablo.h:64,90; defined diablo.cpp:156); UI/menu state `InGameMenu()`, `sgpCurrentMenu` (gmenu.h:81), `gmenu_is_active()` (gmenu.h:86), `gamemenu_on()` (gamemenu.h), `QuestLogIsOpen` (panels/quest_log.hpp), `PressEscKey`, panel flags `CharFlag`, `SpellbookFlag`, `SpellSelectFlag`, `invflag` (control/control.hpp:62-65, inv.h:86), `DoomFlag` (doom.h:12), store state `IsPlayerInStore()` + `StartGoldWithdraw()` (stores.h), `Stash`/`IsStashOpen` + `PreviousPage/NextPage` (qol/stash.h:72-73), `SetSpeedSpell/ToggleSpell/QuickCast` (panels/spell_list.hpp), `GetOptions().Gameplay.quickCast`, `GetOptions().Graphics.zoom` + `CalcViewportGeometry()` (3DS only), `CycleAutomapType()`, `IsAnyOf` (utils/is_of.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `HandleControllerButtonEvent` must keep its exact statement order and early-return chain (see 1:1 below), including the RAII "release without invoking action" that runs on *every* exit path when the event is a button release — the C++ destructor semantics are a behavioural requirement and Go needs an explicit `defer`.
  - Button-release protocol: if the released button has a non-empty padmapper action name, optionally run `PerformPrimaryActionRelease()` for `"PrimaryAction"`, then `PadmapperRelease(button, invokeAction=true)` and return handled.
  - Modifier suppression: consume and clear `SuppressedButton` (returns handled-without-action for a press, clears and continues on release).
  - Right-stick simulation is skipped for thumbstick motion events; `DetectInputMethod` is called for every non-IGNORE event.
  - `GetGameAction`: virtual-gamepad branch handles finger-down (per-widget `isHeld && didStateChange`, in strict priority order) and finger-up (release held action) — and it must run *before* the `PadMenuNavigatorActive || PadHotspellMenuActive` early-out, which in turn runs before the key-translation table.
  - Key-translation tables for three UI contexts (store/in-game menu, in-game menu, quest log) selected by the same priority order; when a translation hits, the action becomes `GameActionSendKey{vk, up}`.
  - `PressControllerButton`: stash override, then hotspell override, then menu-navigator override, then finally padmapper lookup with movement-handler deferral.
  - `CanDeferToMovementHandler`: modifier-free DPAD actions defer to the movement handler, except `QuickSpell*` while spell-select is open.
  - `TranslateTo` and `SkipsMovie`/`IsSimulatedMouseClickBinding` as pure helpers.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `TranslateTo`: only Nintendo swaps; A↔B and X↔Y; everything else unchanged (L333-347).
  - `SkipsMovie`: exactly {A, B, START, BACK}, regardless of press/release (L352-356).
  - `IsSimulatedMouseClickBinding`: NONE→false; non-release matching `SuppressedButton`→false; action name ∈ {"LeftMouseClick1","LeftMouseClick2","RightMouseClick1","RightMouseClick2"} (L361-366).
  - Game-menu key table: {A,Y}→`SDLK_RETURN`, {B,BACK,START}→`SDLK_ESCAPE`, LEFTSTICK→`SDLK_TAB` (Map), else UNKNOWN (L40-53). Menu key table: A→`SDLK_SPACE`, {B,BACK,START}→`SDLK_ESCAPE`, Y→`SDLK_RETURN`, LEFTSTICK→`SDLK_TAB`, DPAD L/R/U/D→`SDLK_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN` (L57-79). Quest-log table: {A,Y}→`SDLK_RETURN`, B→`SDLK_SPACE`, LEFTSTICK→`SDLK_TAB` (L83-94). All three apply `TranslateTo(GamepadType, button)` first.
  - `GetGameAction` context priority: `gmenu_is_active() || IsPlayerInStore()` → game-menu table; else `inGameMenu` → menu table; else `QuestLogIsOpen` → quest-log table (L202-207).
  - Virtual-gamepad finger-down order: char, quests, inventory, map, primary, secondary, spell, cancel, health, mana (L108-175). Map button sends `GameActionSendKey{SDLK_TAB,false}` (L121).
  - Primary-action triple: if `!inGameMenu && !QuestLogIsOpen && !SpellbookFlag` → `GameActionType_PRIMARY_ACTION` and adopt as held only if `ControllerActionHeld == GameActionType_NONE`; else if `sgpCurrentMenu != nullptr || IsPlayerInStore() || QuestLogIsOpen` → `SDLK_RETURN`; else → `SDLK_SPACE` (L124-135). Secondary (L137-143) and spell (L145-151) have only the first arm and still return true.
  - Cancel chain order: `inGameMenu||DoomFlag||SpellSelectFlag`→`SDLK_ESCAPE`; else `invflag`→TOGGLE_INVENTORY; else `SpellbookFlag`→TOGGLE_SPELL_BOOK; else `QuestLogIsOpen`→TOGGLE_QUEST_LOG; else `CharFlag`→TOGGLE_CHARACTER_INFO — and it returns true even when nothing matched (L153-165).
  - Health/mana buttons: gated by `!QuestLogIsOpen && !SpellbookFlag && !IsPlayerInStore()`; return true regardless (L166-175).
  - Finger-up: clears `ControllerActionHeld` to NONE and `LastPlayerAction` to `PlayerActionType::None` when the widget for the currently-held action is no longer held (three-way OR test), calling `PerformPrimaryActionRelease()` first for PRIMARY (L182-191).
  - `PressControllerButton` stash: BACK→`StartGoldWithdraw()`, LEFTSHOULDER→`Stash.PreviousPage()`, RIGHTSHOULDER→`Stash.NextPage()` (L241-255).
  - Hotspell slot mapping is the load-bearing oddity: A→slot 2, B→slot 3, X→slot 0, Y→slot 1 (L269-280); slot action is `SetSpeedSpell(slot)` when `SpellSelectFlag`, else `ToggleSpell(slot)` when `!*quickCast` else `QuickCast(slot)` (L258-267).
  - Menu-navigator map: DPAD_UP→`PressEscKey(); LastPlayerAction=None; PadHotspellMenuActive=false; PadMenuNavigatorActive=false; gamemenu_on()` in that order (L288-294); DPAD_DOWN→`CycleAutomapType()`; DPAD_LEFT→TOGGLE_CHARACTER_INFO; DPAD_RIGHT→TOGGLE_INVENTORY; A→TOGGLE_SPELL_BOOK; B→consume-and-do-nothing; X→TOGGLE_QUEST_LOG; Y→zoom toggle + `CalcViewportGeometry()` under `__3DS__` only, else nothing (L295-317).
  - Padmapper fallback: `findAction(button, IsControllerButtonPressed)`; nil→return; `IsMovementHandlerActive() && CanDeferToMovementHandler(*action)`→return; else `PadmapperPress(button, *action)` (L323-326).
  - `HandleControllerButtonEvent` sequence: IGNORE→false; construct release-guard (deferred `PadmapperRelease(button, invokeAction=false)` on release); `isGamepadMotion = IsControllerMotion(event)`; `if !isGamepadMotion → SimulateRightStickWithPadmapper`; `DetectInputMethod(event, ctrlEvent)`; `if isGamepadMotion → true`; suppression block (L393-397); release-with-action-name block (L399-410); `GetGameAction`→`ProcessGameAction`→true (L411-413); `button != NONE` → `PressControllerButton` only when `!up` → true (L414-417); else false (L369-421).
  - `CanDeferToMovementHandler`: modifier must be `ControllerButton_NONE`; `QuickSpell` prefix rejection only when `SpellSelectFlag` and `len(key) >= 10`; final test is membership in the four DPAD buttons (L217-237).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Three mutable globals (`PadMenuNavigatorActive`, `PadHotspellMenuActive`, `SuppressedButton`) written by other subsystems (plrctrls, menu code) and read here — they are the coupling that makes ordering matter. `ControllerActionHeld` and `LastPlayerAction` are cross-file globals mutated here and read every gameplay tick. All of this is main-thread/event-driven, *not* per-tick: one call per `ControllerButtonEvent`. The `ButtonReleaser` destructor ordering (runs after the function body, so `PadmapperRelease(..., invokeAction=false)` happens last) is subtle: for release events that were handled with `invokeAction=true`, the guard still runs and is presumably idempotent — the port must confirm idempotency rather than reorder the two calls.
- Test coverage: none found for this file. Nearest: test/game_menu_test.cpp (touches gmenu state only), test/panel_state_test.cpp (control flags only). No test exercises `HandleControllerButtonEvent`, `GetGameAction`, or the hotspell slot mapping.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/gamecontrols` (the controller→action adapter), with `func (h *Handler) HandleControllerButtonEvent(ev Event, ctrl ControllerButtonEvent, out *GameAction) bool`. Strategy: inject narrow interfaces — `TouchState` (virtual gamepad widgets), `UIFlags` (inGameMenu/store/questlog/panel flags), `Padmapper` (findAction/press/release), `GameActions` (ProcessGameAction/DetectInputMethod/PerformPrimaryActionRelease) — because the file's real dependency count is ~20 globals and that is what blocks testing. Model `GameAction` as `{Type GameActionType; SendKey Key, Up}` (drop the C union; the union has exactly one active variant). The RAII releaser becomes `defer`. `PressControllerButton`/`GetGameAction`/the three key tables become table-driven maps so the slot mapping (A→2,B→3,X→0,Y→1) is asserted in a test.
- Risks/open questions: (1) The double-release for release events (explicit `PadmapperRelease(invokeAction=true)` then deferred `PadmapperRelease(invokeAction=false)`) must be understood in padmapper.cpp before porting or the port may fire actions twice — this is the single highest-risk item in the batch. (2) `GetGameAction` returns true in several arms without setting `*action` (e.g. L137-151 when the guard fails, L153-165 unmatched, L166-175 blocked) — the caller still `ProcessGameAction(action)`s a *default/uninitialised* `GameAction` in those cases (the out-param is uninitialised at game_controls.cpp:411 unless the callee set it; `GameAction`'s default ctor sets NONE, so the aggregate at the call site is default-constructed — verify). Port must always assign NONE. (3) 3DS-only zoom behaviour: keep as a build tag or drop. (4) `InGameMenu()` vs `sgpCurrentMenu != nullptr` are two different menu notions used in the same function — do not unify them.

### Source/controls/game_controls.h
- Purpose: Declares the game-action vocabulary shared by the input layer, gameplay, and touch UI, plus the controller→gamepad-layout translation helper and the three cross-file pad-menu globals.
- Public API: `enum GameActionType : uint8_t { GameActionType_NONE, USE_HEALTH_POTION, USE_MANA_POTION, PRIMARY_ACTION, SECONDARY_ACTION, CAST_SPELL, TOGGLE_INVENTORY, TOGGLE_CHARACTER_INFO, TOGGLE_QUICK_SPELL_MENU, TOGGLE_SPELL_BOOK, TOGGLE_QUEST_LOG, SEND_KEY }` (L16-29); `struct GameActionSendKey { uint32_t vk_code; bool up; }` (L31-34); `struct GameAction { GameActionType type; union { GameActionSendKey send_key; }; }` with default ctor → NONE, `explicit GameAction(GameActionType)`, and implicit `GameAction(GameActionSendKey)` → type SEND_KEY (L36-58); `TranslateTo(GamepadLayout, ControllerButton)` (L60); `SkipsMovie(ControllerButtonEvent)` (L62); `IsSimulatedMouseClickBinding(ControllerButtonEvent)` (L64); `HandleControllerButtonEvent(const SDL_Event&, const ControllerButtonEvent, GameAction&)` (L66); `extern bool PadMenuNavigatorActive; extern bool PadHotspellMenuActive;` (L68-69); `extern ControllerButton SuppressedButton;` (L76) with the explanatory comment about simultaneous-button SDL events (L70-75).
- Depends on: `<cstdint>`, SDL event header, `AxisDirection` (axis_direction.h), `ControllerButton`/`ControllerButtonEvent`/`GamepadLayout` (controls/controller.h → controller_buttons.h). Included by: devices/game_controller.h:16, controller_motion.cpp, plrctrls, padmapper, menu_controls, modifier_hints, diablo.cpp.
- Requirements for Go port: a `GameAction` type that is (a) default-constructible to NONE, (b) constructible from a bare type, (c) constructible from a send-key payload that auto-sets the SEND_KEY tag — in Go: `type GameAction struct { Type GameActionType; Key uint32; Up bool }` plus constructors `NewAction(t)`, `NewSendKey(key, up)`. `TranslateTo` must stay a free function usable by both the UI key tables and remap UI. The three `extern` globals need Go equivalents with the same *shared-mutable* semantics (they are read/written from diablo, plrctrls, and padmapper) — either package-level vars or a single `PadState` struct threaded everywhere.
- 1:1 constraints: Enum is `uint8_t` with implicit values NONE=0 … SEND_KEY=11 in exactly the listed order (L16-29) — these numbers appear in saved settings/remap UI and in the padmapper action registry keyed by string names, so ordering must not be renumbered. Comments L20-21 define PRIMARY ("Talk to towners, click on inv items, attack, etc.") and SECONDARY ("Open chests, doors, pickup items.") semantics — the only doc for those two actions. `GameActionSendKey::vk_code` is `uint32_t` (not `SDL_Keycode`) — the union is deliberately sized so a key code can be stored without the SDL type (L31-33, L55-57). `SuppressedButton` documented purpose at L70-76.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Header adds no state of its own; its globals are defined in game_controls.cpp with explicit initialisers (false/false/NONE). The anonymous-union-in-struct idiom means reading `send_key` when `type != SEND_KEY` is what upstream does on some paths — the Go port cannot express that ambiguity and must normalise.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/actions` (or a `gameaction.go` inside `internal/input`) holding `GameActionType` (with `String()` for logs), `GameAction`, `TranslateTo`, and the three shared globals in one owner package that `gamecontrols` imports. Strategy: keep the enum values identical and add a golden test asserting the 12 numeric values, since the whole rest of the port keys off them.
- Risks/open questions: The `union` has no discriminant guarantee; if any upstream path reads `send_key` for a non-SEND_KEY action, the Go struct's zero `Key` differs from C++'s uninitialised value — check whether anything relies on that. Also: game_controller.h includes this header without needing it, so package boundaries in Go will need the include graph cleaned (cyclic-import risk between `input/gamepad` and `input/actions`).

### Source/controls/input.h
- Purpose: The single event-pump helper every UI/game loop calls: poll one SDL event, then run the two per-event controller housekeeping steps in a fixed order.
- Public API: `inline bool PollEvent(SDL_Event *event)` (L14-28) — returns true iff an event was dequeued.
- Depends on: `SDL_PollEvent` (SDL3 returns bool, SDL2 returns int → `!= 0`) (L16-20); `UnlockControllerState(const SDL_Event&)` (controls/controller.h:15, defined controls/controller.cpp:21 — calls `GameController::UnlockTriggerState` and `Joystick::UnlockHatState`); `ProcessControllerMotion(const SDL_Event&)` (controller_motion.h:43). Consumers are the busy-wait loops in Source/interfac.cpp:302, Source/DiabloUI/{credits,diabloui,dialogs,progress,title}.cpp, and the main loop; note Source/engine/demomode.cpp:733 deliberately uses raw `SDL_PollEvent` instead.
- Requirements for Go port: one function that (1) dequeues the next event, (2) on success unlocks per-event controller state (trigger latch + hat-change window), (3) then processes motion for that event, (4) returns the event + ok. The two side effects must be *inside* the poll success branch, and must run before any caller inspects the event — callers rely on hat `didStateChange`/trigger latches being freshly armed for the event they just got.
- 1:1 constraints: Order is `UnlockControllerState(event)` then `ProcessControllerMotion(event)` (L22-23) — reversing them makes a joystick hat/button event never produce edge events and mis-scales sticks once per device. Side effects run only when an event was actually polled. Demo mode bypasses this function entirely (demomode.cpp:733) — a port must keep demo-mode event injection free of the unlock/motion coupling or demo playback diverges.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: This is the coupling point between the SDL queue and the mutable globals in controller_motion; every caller loop that uses `PollEvent` gets deterministic per-event ordering, but any loop that reads stick state outside `PollEvent` sees stale-but-consistent scaled values. Not thread-safe. Called from UI busy loops that can run for many frames (credits, dialogs), so per-event unlock happens at input rate, not tick rate.
- Test coverage: none found (these loops are exercised only manually/visually).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/pump.go` — `func (h *Hub) PollEvent() (Event, bool)` where the hub owns the gamepad/joystick registries and the motion state, so the unlock→motion order is enforced in one place instead of by convention. Strategy: replace the `SDL_Event*` out-param with a returned value; provide `PollEventRaw()` for the demo-mode path to mirror the SDL_PollEvent bypass.
- Risks/open questions: Several C++ loops use raw `SDL_PollEvent` (bypassing this wrapper) while others use `PollEvent`; the port must find every such site or per-event state unlocking becomes inconsistent. Worth an audit beyond this batch.

### Source/controls/keymapper.cpp
- Purpose: Keyboard-action dispatch: maps a key code (including synthetic mouse-button/scroll codes) to a registered `KeymapperOptions::Action` and invokes its press/release handler, with chat/gold-entry keys carved out.
- Public API: `void KeymapperPress(SDL_Keycode key)` (L53), `void KeymapperRelease(SDL_Keycode key)` (L65). File-local: `bool IsTextEntryKey(SDL_Keycode)` (L22), `bool IsNumberEntryKey(SDL_Keycode)` (L32), `SDL_Keycode ToAsciiUpper(SDL_Keycode)` (L37).
- Depends on: `KeymapperOptions::Action { actionPressed, actionReleased, isEnabled(), key }` and `GetOptions().Keymapper.findAction(uint32_t)` (options.h:760); `ChatFlag` (control/control.hpp:62), `DropGoldFlag` (control/control.hpp:200); `IsAnyOf` (utils/is_of.hpp); SDL keycode constants; callers in Source/diablo.cpp:487,532,567,701,716,818,836,839,841 — including mouse buttons smuggled through `key | KeymapperMouseButtonMask` and the four scroll pseudo-codes.
- Requirements for Go port: `KeymapperPress`/`KeymapperRelease(key)` doing uppercase-normalise → registry lookup → three guards (action exists, the relevant handler is non-nil, `isEnabled()`) → chat guard → invoke. `KeymapperRelease`'s carve-out is different: skip when chat is open and the key is a *text-entry* key, or when gold-drop is open and the key is a *number-entry* key. Needs the synthetic keycode namespace (mouse buttons + scroll) to remain plain integers so mouse events can flow through the same dispatcher.
- 1:1 constraints: `ToAsciiUpper` shifts only the SDL3 `SDLK_A..SDLK_Z` range / SDL2 `SDLK_a..SDLK_z` range by `-('a' - 'A')` = `-32` and returns anything else unchanged (L37-49) — note it upper-cases *lowercase* keys, so an uppercase-registered binding would never match a lowercase press; registry lookup is by `uint32_t` cast (L56/68). `IsTextEntryKey` set = {ESCAPE, RETURN, KP_ENTER, BACKSPACE, DOWN, UP} ∪ [SPACE..Z] where the Z bound is `SDLK_Z` on SDL3 and `SDLK_z` on SDL2 (L24-29). `IsNumberEntryKey` = [SDLK_0..SDLK_9] ∪ {BACKSPACE} (L32-34). Press guard is unconditional on `ChatFlag` (L60) while the release guard is per-key-class (L72). Lookup happens *before* the ChatFlag test on press, and the `isEnabled()` test precedes the ChatFlag test.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: No state owned here; behaviour is whatever the options registry holds plus the two global flags. Called from the keyboard-event path in diablo.cpp (per event, not per tick). Order of guards matters: `actionPressed == nil` / `!isEnabled()` short-circuit before the chat check, so a disabled action never logs nor fires.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/input/keymapper` — `type Action struct { Key uint32; OnPress, OnRelease func(); Enabled func() bool }` and `type Keymapper struct { byKey map[uint32]*Action }` with `Press(key Key)`/`Release(key Key)`; the two key-class predicates become `func isTextEntry(k Key) bool` / `isNumberEntry(k Key)` over the port's own Key enum. Strategy: keep a `KeymapperMouseButtonMask`/`MouseScroll*Button` constant block verbatim (defined in diablo.cpp/diablo.h, not this file) so the same synthetic-code trick works, and make `ChatFlag`/`DropGoldFlag` an injected `EntryState` interface — this file is 77 lines and has zero coverage; the Go port should be the first place it gets table tests.
- Risks/open questions: (1) The mouse/scroll codes and `KeymapperMouseButtonMask` live outside this file — the port's keymapper namespace must be defined once, consistently. (2) `ToAsciiUpper` only normalises ASCII letters, so non-latin or shifted keys (SDL3 gives different codes for Shift+letter) silently miss bindings — real behaviour to preserve, and worth a test. (3) The `// TODO: This should be handled outside of the keymapper.` comments at L59 and L71 mean the chat/gold carve-out is known-bad design; port it as-is or restructure (restructuring changes which keys reach actions while chat is open).
