# vol3-007.md

# Volume III — batch 007

### Source/controls/keymapper.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the two free functions that route a raw SDL keysym into the user-configured keyboard action map (press and release halves).
- Public API: `void KeymapperPress(SDL_Keycode key);` (line 17), `void KeymapperRelease(SDL_Keycode key);` (line 18), both in namespace `devilution`. Header includes only `<cstdint>` plus SDL keycode headers (SDL3 `<SDL3/SDL_keycode.h>` vs SDL1/2 `<SDL.h>` + `utils/sdl2_to_1_2_backports.h` backport, lines 5-13).
- Depends on: `SDL_Keycode` (SDL). Implementation (`keymapper.cpp`) consumes: `KeymapperOptions::Action` + `GetOptions().Keymapper.findAction(uint32_t)` (Source/options.h:733-760), `ChatFlag` / `DropGoldFlag` (Source/diablo.h / Source/controls/game_controls.h), `IsAnyOf` (Source/utils/is_of.hpp), and `ToAsciiUpper` local helper. The header itself depends on nothing else.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A single keyboard-action dispatch entry point: `KeymapperPress(key)` / `KeymapperRelease(key)` that (a) normalise the key to an ASCII upper form, (b) look up a bound action in the options keymap, (c) check `actionPressed`/`actionReleased` non-nil and the action's `isEnabled()` predicate, (d) honour text/number-entry suppression, then invoke the callback.
  - Key normalisation: lowercase a-z -> uppercase by subtracting `('a' - 'A')` (see 1:1 below).
  - Action table must be an external, user-editable mapping from keycode -> named action with press/release callbacks and an enable predicate (Go: `type KeyAction struct { Press, Release func(); Enabled func() bool }`).
  - Text-entry guard for release: while a chat input is active, ESC/RETURN/KP_ENTER/BACKSPACE/DOWN/UP and printable-range keys must not fire their bound action; while gold-drop is active, digits 0-9 and BACKSPACE must not fire.
  - Whole keymapper must be a no-op (return without invoking) when the key is unmapped.
- 1:1 constraints: From the header: no constants. The behaviour contract implemented elsewhere (Source/controls/keymapper.cpp) fixes the values the Go port must match: `ToAsciiUpper` = `key - ('a' - 'A')` i.e. `-32` for `a..z` only; text-entry key set = {ESCAPE, RETURN, KP_ENTER, BACKSPACE, DOWN, UP} plus range `[SDLK_SPACE, SDLK_Z]` (SDL3) / `[SDLK_SPACE, SDLK_z]` (SDL2) — keymapper.cpp lines 22-32; number-entry set = `[SDLK_0..SDLK_9]` or `SDLK_BACKSPACE` (line 36). Lookups cast the keycode to `uint32_t` before `findAction` (lines 55, 66).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Header is stateless. No tick coupling. The press/release dispatch is driven from the SDL event pump, i.e. once per polled event, not once per game tick — the Go port must keep it on the event goroutine/main thread since it invokes game-mutating callbacks.
- Test coverage: none found (no `test/keymapper*_test.cpp`; `grep -rln "controls/" test/` matches only `test/ui_test.hpp`, which includes `controls/control_mode.hpp`).
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` (package `controls`) — file `keymapper.go`. Strategy: thin dispatch over the options keymap; represent SDL keysyms as the Ebiten input-key enum plus a synthetic "keysym" int so the 32-bit lookup key stays stable; callbacks as Go func values.
- Risks/open questions: Header is a *declaration only* — the actual behaviour lives in `keymapper.cpp`, which is NOT in this batch's file list. Porting only this header would produce an empty shell; the batch must treat the .cpp behaviour (cited above) as the requirement. SDL3 vs SDL2 keysym spelling for `SDLK_Z` vs `SDLK_z` changes the text-entry range boundary.

### Source/controls/menu_controls.cpp
- Purpose: Translates one SDL event into the list of menu actions for the DiabloUI menus: gamepad button events first, then mouse-button back-navigation, then raw keyboard fallback.
- Public API: `MenuAction GetMenuHeldUpDownAction()`; `std::vector<MenuAction> GetMenuActions(const SDL_Event &event)`.
- Depends on: `MenuAction` (menu_controls.h); `AxisDirectionRepeater`, `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection(bool)` (controls/axis_direction.h, controls/controller_motion.h); `ToControllerButtonEvents`, `IsControllerMotion`, `DetectInputMethod` (controls/controller.h, controls/plrctrls.cpp); `TranslateTo(GamepadType, button)` + `ControllerButton_*` enum (controls/controller_buttons.h, game_controls.h); `GamepadType`, `ControlMode` (controls/control_mode.hpp); `IsTextInputActive()` (DiabloUI/diabloui.h:27); `remap_keyboard_key` (controls/remap_keyboard.h); `SDLC_EventKey` (utils/sdl_compat.h); SDL `SDL_GetModState`, `SDL_BUTTON_X1`, key codes.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Held-axis menu action: sample the left-stick/dpad direction (non-relative=false) through a *stateful* direction repeater and map `dir.y` UP->`MenuAction_UP`, DOWN->`MenuAction_DOWN`, else `MenuAction_NONE`.
  - Per-event action extraction returning an ordered slice of actions (possibly empty), with this exact precedence: (1) iterate controller button events derived from the raw event, skipping `ControllerButton_IGNORE`; (2) detect input method per controller event; (3) if the raw event is controller *motion*, push the held up/down action and continue; (4) otherwise, only for press events (`!ctrlEvent.up`), map layout-translated buttons to actions; (5) if any action was produced, return immediately; (6) else test mouse-button-down for X1 -> `{MenuAction_BACK}`; (7) else (only when keyboard/gamepad is not a separate control mode) test key-down events for the keyboard table; (8) else return empty.
  - Gamepad press mapping: A|START->SELECT, BACK|B->BACK, X->DELETE, DPAD_UP|DPAD_DOWN->held up/down action, DPAD_LEFT->LEFT, DPAD_RIGHT->RIGHT, LEFTSHOULDER->PAGE_UP, RIGHTSHOULDER->PAGE_DOWN, everything else ignored.
  - Keyboard mapping: UP->UP, DOWN->DOWN, TAB->UP if SHIFT held else DOWN, PAGEUP->PAGE_UP, PAGEDOWN->PAGE_DOWN, RETURN->SELECT if ALT not held (otherwise fall through), KP_ENTER->SELECT, SPACE->SELECT when no text input is active, DELETE->DELETE, LEFT->LEFT, RIGHT->RIGHT (all three suppressed while text input is active), ESCAPE->BACK.
  - Every keyboard symbol must pass through the compile-time key remap before the switch.
- 1:1 constraints: `static AxisDirectionRepeater repeater;` inside `GetMenuHeldUpDownAction` (line 23) — one shared default-interval (200 ms) repeater for all callers. `GetLeftStickOrDpadDirection(false)` (line 24) — the `false` is load-bearing. Button switch is on `TranslateTo(GamepadType, ctrlEvent.button)` (line 52), i.e. layout normalisation before mapping. Only `!ctrlEvent.up` presses generate actions (line 51). X1 back also accepts literal `8` on SDL1 (lines 97-100). Whole keyboard block is `#if HAS_KBCTRL == 0` (line 105). Modifier checks are `(SDL_GetModState() & SDL_KMOD_SHIFT) != 0` for TAB (line 115) and `(SDL_GetModState() & SDL_KMOD_ALT) == 0` for RETURN (line 124). Mouse check is `event.type == SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN` (SDL3) / `SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN` (lines 90-96).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: The function-local `static` repeater makes `GetMenuHeldUpDownAction` order-dependent across events (its repeat gating depends on wall-clock ms, not game ticks) and not reentrant/thread-safe. `GetMenuActions` allocates a fresh vector per event (no hidden state). Called from the UI event pump, so it runs at event rate, decoupled from the logic tick.
- Test coverage: none found (no test includes menu_controls.h).
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` — `menu_controls.go`. Strategy: one method on a `MenuController` struct owning the repeater instead of a file-scope static; actions as an `int8` enum with the same values/order so existing numeric comparisons survive.
- Risks/open questions: Repeated calls to `GetMenuHeldUpDownAction()` for DPAD_UP *and* the motion branch in the same event consume the repeater once each — if a Go port caches the result instead of re-calling, the repeat cadence changes. `HAS_KBCTRL` semantics must be pinned for Ebiten (no SDL).

### Source/controls/modifier_hints.cpp
- Purpose: Renders the on-screen "circle menu" modifier hints for gamepad play — two DPad/button hint clusters plus the hotspell ring — into the main panel area, and owns the CLX sprites they draw from.
- Public API (all defined here; the .h exposes only 3): `void InitModifierHints()`, `void FreeModifierHints()`, `void DrawControllerModifierHints(const Surface &out)`. File-internal: `DrawCircleMenuHint(const Surface&, const CircleMenuHint&, const Point&)`, `DrawSpellsCircleMenuHint(const Surface&, const Point&)`, `DrawGamepadMenuNavigator(const Surface&)`, `DrawGamepadHotspellMenu(const Surface&)`, `struct CircleMenuHint`, `enum HintIcon : uint8_t`.
- Depends on: `hintBox/hintBoxBackground/hintIcons` loaded from `data\hintbox.clx`, `data\hintboxbackground.clx`, `data\hinticons.clx` (lines 168-172) via `LoadClx` (engine/load_clx.hpp) and `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList`; `RenderClxSprite` + `Surface::subregion` (engine/render/clx_render.hpp); `GetMainPanel()` (panels/ui_panels.hpp) for panel geometry; `MyPlayer` + `_pSplHotKey[]`, `_pSplTHotKey[]`, `_pAblSpells/_pMemSpells/_pScrlSpells/_pISpells` (player.h); `IsValidSpell`, `GetSpellBitmask`, `GetSpellData`, `SpellType` (spells); `leveltype == DTYPE_TOWN`; `SetSpellTrans`, `DrawSmallSpellIcon` (panels/spell_icons.hpp); `PadMenuNavigatorActive`, `PadHotspellMenuActive` (controls/game_controls.h); `SimulatingMouseWithPadmapper` (controls/controller_motion.cpp:31); `GetOptions()` (options.h) and `utils/language.h` included but the visible code does not use them.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Asset lifecycle: load three CLX sprite lists at init, free them in reverse order at shutdown, all as package-level (mutable) holders that the draw functions read.
  - Draw entry `DrawControllerModifierHints(out)` = draw menu-navigator hints, then draw hotspell-menu hints (fixed order, lines 179-182).
  - Menu-navigator hints are suppressed when `!PadMenuNavigatorActive` or when the pad is simulating a mouse; hotspell hints likewise on `!PadHotspellMenuActive` / mouse simulation.
  - Two hint clusters are placed relative to the main panel rectangle: left cluster at `(panel.x + 16, panel.y - 101)`; right cluster at `(panel.x + panel.width - 3*39 - 16 - 2*5, panel.y - 101)`.
  - Left cluster = DPad hint (top=Menu, right=Inv, bottom=Map, left=Char); right cluster = button hint (bottom=Spells, left=Quests, top/right = null). Both hint structs are function-local `static const` (lines 146-147).
  - Generic 4-slot hint box drawing: for each of 4 slots in a fixed order, skip `IconNull`, else draw background sprite at an inset position, then the icon cropped into a 37x38 subregion, then the box frame sprite on top.
  - Spell-ring drawing: for each of 4 hotkey slots, take `_pSplHotKey[slot]`, validate it, and require the spell to be present in the union of the four known-spell bitmasks; mark it invalid if in town and the spell is not town-allowed; then draw the small spell icon (with the spell-type transparency set) at the slot's inset position and overlay the hint box frame.
- 1:1 constraints: `LineHeight = 25`, `CircleMarginX = 16`, `CircleTop = 101`, `IconSize = 37`, `HintBoxSize = 39`, `HintBoxMargin = 5` (lines 25-37). `backgroundDisplacement = { ((39-37)/2)+1, ((39-37)/2)-1 }` = `{2, 0}` (line 76) — note integer division: `(39-37)/2 == 1`, so y offset is `1-1 == 0`. `spellIconDisplacement = {2, 39 - 2 - 1}` = `{2, 36}` (line 109). Four hint-box offsets from origin, identical in both draw helpers (lines 78-82 and 111-115): `{0, 25-39}={0,-14}`, `{39+5, 25-78-5}={44,-58}`, `{44, 25+5}={44,30}`, `{(39*2)+(5*2), -14}={88,-14}`. Slot order for icons is `{left, top, bottom, right}` (line 89) while the position array order is `{top-slot-pos, left?, ...}` — the mismatch is deliberate and must be copied verbatim. Subregion size is hard-coded `37, 38` (line 96) — 38, not `IconSize`. Spell bitmask union order: `_pAblSpells | _pMemSpells | _pScrlSpells | _pISpells` (line 121). Right-cluster x formula (line 150) and hotspell-cluster x formula (line 158) must match exactly. `HintIcon` enum order: `IconChar, IconInv, IconQuests, IconSpells, IconMap, IconMenu, IconNull` (lines 43-51) — these become sprite indices into `hintIcons`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Three package-level `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList` globals are mutated by Init/Free and read during draw: calling draw before `InitModifierHints` (or after `FreeModifierHints`) dereferences empty optionals (`(*hintBox)[0]`) — a nil/panic condition, not a silent no-op. The two `static const CircleMenuHint` values inside `DrawGamepadMenuNavigator` are initialised once (thread-safe in C++11; in Go use package-level vars). Rendering is per-frame and purely a function of current flags — no RNG, no game-state mutation.
- Test coverage: none found (`test/` has no modifier-hint test; `test/spell_ui_test.cpp` covers spell UI, not these hints).
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` for the API surface plus `internal/render` (or `internal/panels`) for the CLX draw calls. Strategy: expose `Init/Free/Draw` as methods on a `ModifierHints` struct holding the three sprite lists, so the load-before-use hazard becomes a constructor requirement rather than a global ordering trap.
- Risks/open questions: `data\hintbox*.clx` assets must exist in the Go asset set. `SetSpellTrans` mutates a global palette-transparency state (panels/spell_icons) — the Go port needs an equivalent explicit pen. Whether the 37x38 subregion vs 37 IconSize asymmetry is a bug or intentional is unresolved; copy as-is.

### Source/controls/padmapper.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the gamepad button-mapping dispatch: remembers which mapped action is currently "held down" per button so release fires the same action, and answers queries about active pad actions.
- Public API: `void PadmapperPress(ControllerButton button, const PadmapperOptions::Action &action);`, `void PadmapperRelease(ControllerButton button, bool invokeAction);`, `void PadmapperReleaseAllActiveButtons();`, `bool PadmapperIsActionActive(std::string_view actionName);`, `std::string_view PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent(ControllerButtonEvent ctrlEvent);` (all also declared in padmapper.hpp).
- Depends on: `PadmapperOptions::Action` (`key`, `actionPressed`, `actionReleased`, `isEnabled()`, `boundInput` of type `ControllerButtonCombo{button,modifier}`) and `GetOptions().Padmapper.actions` / `.findAction(button, isModifierPressed)` (Source/options.h:780-835); `ControllerButton`/`ControllerButtonEvent` (controls/controller_buttons.h); `SuppressedButton` global (controls/game_controls.h:76); `IsControllerButtonPressed` (controls/controller.h); `enum_size<ControllerButton>::value` (utils/is_of.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A fixed-size table mapping each `ControllerButton` enum value to the action whose release it should fire, with nil meaning "unmapped / nothing held".
  - Press: invoke `action.actionPressed` if non-nil, then record the action as the pending release action for that button.
  - Release: if `invokeAction` is true, look up the pending action; if nil, return (ignore unmapped buttons); else invoke `actionReleased` only when non-nil *and* `isEnabled()`; in all cases clear the slot for that button.
  - Query "is action X active": scan the configured action list for the first action whose key == X, then check that the pending-release entry for *that action's own bound button* is the same action.
  - Query "action name triggered by this button event": for press events resolve via the options padmapper (modifier-aware lookup) and return the action key (empty if none); for release events return the key of the pending release action for that button (empty if none).
  - Release-all: iterate the table and release every non-nil entry through the normal release path with `invokeAction = true`.
- 1:1 constraints: Table size is exactly `enum_size<ControllerButton>::value` and is indexed by `static_cast<size_t>(button)` — Go must use the same enum ordinals (padmapper.cpp lines 11, 20, 26, 29, 33). Press sets `SuppressedButton = action.boundInput.modifier` (line 18) *after* invoking the press callback — the order matters because the callback may itself read `SuppressedButton`. Release clears the slot even when the action was not invoked (line 33). `PadmapperIsActionActive` returns on the *first* key match, i.e. it reports only one action's state and never continues searching (lines 38-45). `PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent` branches on `!ctrlEvent.up` (line 55).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `ButtonToReleaseAction` is a file-scope mutable array — global state shared across the whole input pipeline, so press/release must be serialised on the event thread. No tick coupling and no time dependence. `GetOptions().Padmapper.actions` order determines `PadmapperIsActionActive` results.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` — `padmapper.go`, with the table as `[numControllerButtons]*PadAction` inside a `Padmapper` struct owned by the input dispatcher (not a package global). Strategy: the "active action" query needs the options' action slice, so pass it in (interface) rather than reaching for a global `GetOptions()`.
- Risks/open questions: The release path can be called with `invokeAction=false` — used to clear state without firing effects; the Go port must keep that distinction. `PadmapperIsActionActive` semantics are subtly "is the action bound to button B currently held" rather than "is any action with this name active" — easy to "fix" wrongly.

### Source/controls/padmapper.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the padmapper dispatch API, including the held-action bookkeeping and introspection helpers used by the game-controls layer.
- Public API: exactly the five functions listed for padmapper.cpp, with `[[nodiscard]]` on `PadmapperIsActionActive` and `PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent` (padmapper.hpp lines 13-14). Includes `<string_view>`, `controls/controller_buttons.h`, `options.h`.
- Depends on: `ControllerButton`, `ControllerButtonEvent` (controller_buttons.h); `PadmapperOptions::Action` (options.h) — this header leaks the options type into its signature, so the padmapper API is not separable from the config layer.

  - `PadmapperRelease(button, invokeAction bool)`, `PadmapperReleaseAllActiveButtons()`, `PadmapperIsActionActive(name string) bool`, `PadmapperActionNameTriggeredByButtonEvent(evt) (string, bool)` (Go should return the name; empty string = none, mirroring `std::string_view{}`).

Return type of the name query is a borrowed view of the action's key — in Go this means never copying/re-allocating the action table while a returned name is in use.

- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` — declarations live beside implementations; the `Action` type should be defined once in `internal/options` and referenced here to avoid a duplicate mirror struct.
- Risks/open questions: Whether `Action` should be a pointer or value in Go (C++ passes a const ref and stores a pointer in the table) — storing a pointer into a slice-managed table risks invalidation when the options slice is re-sorted/reallocated by the settings UI.

  - **Game action dispatch**: `ProcessGameAction` handles all 11 non-NONE/non-SEND_KEY `GameActionType`s, each with the exact panel mutual-exclusion side effects (closing char panel, quest log, spell book, gold withdraw, stash, etc.).
  - **Item/spell use**: `UseBeltItem` (first matching healing/mana candidate in belt order), `PerformPrimaryAction`, `PerformPrimaryActionRelease`, `PerformSecondaryAction`, `PerformSpellAction`, `CtrlUseInvItem`, `CtrlUseStashItem`, `UpdateSpellTarget`, `SpellHasActorTarget`, `TryDropItem`, `QuickCast(slot)`.
  - **Menu-mode detection**: `InGameMenu()` returns true when the native game menu owns input (store, help, chat log, chat, quest text, gmenu, `PauseMode == 2`, or the dying/invincible player).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `FaceDir[3][3]` (lines 100-104) indexed `[dir.x][dir.y]` with the row/col order NONE/UP/DOWN vs NONE/LEFT/RIGHT: rows `{South,North,South}`, `{West,NorthWest,SouthWest}`, `{East,NorthEast,SouthEast}` — used at lines 1755 and 1869.
  - `GetRotaryDistance`: returns `-1` when target == `position.future`; `d = abs(_pdir - GetDirection(...))`; `if (d > 4) return 4 - (d % 4); return d;` (lines 118-127).

Both forms must be kept as-is.

  - `UpdateSpellTarget`: `range = (spell == Teleport ? 4 : 1)`; `cursPosition = position.future + Displacement(_pdir) * range` (lines 2397-2409); `SpellHasActorTarget` writes `cursPosition` as a side effect for wall spells (lines 2384-2395).
  - `QuickCast(slot)`: saves and restores `LastPlayerAction` around `CheckPlrSpell(false, spell, spellType)`; only re-aims the spell target when not in keyboard mode (lines 2599-2612).
  - `InGameMenu` disjunct list (lines 73-83) including the `PauseMode == 2` literal and `MyPlayer->_pInvincible && MyPlayer->hasNoLife()`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Runs on the game thread. `plrctrls_every_frame` = `ProcessLeftStickOrDPadGameUI(); HandleRightStickMotion(); ProcessAutomapMovementGamepad();` (lines 2305-2310) — this is **frame-rate coupled** and reads SDL tick time and analog stick values. `plrctrls_after_game_logic` = `Movement(*MyPlayer)` — **logic-tick coupled**. `plrctrls_after_check_curs_move` is invoked from `CheckCursMove` (cursor.cpp) — must remain after cursor resolution. Hidden state: 7 anonymous-namespace navigation globals (lines 90-95: `Slot`, `ActiveStashSlot`, `VisualStoreSlot`, `PreviousInventoryColumn`, `BeltReturnsToStash`, `BeltReturnsToVisualStore`) + ~20 `static AxisDirectionRepeater` locals + `static RightStickAccumulator acc` (line 2200) + `static int lastMouseSetTick` (line 2219) + link-visible globals at lines 62-68 and 1976 (`ControllerActionHeld`, `StandToggle`, `pcurstrig`, `pcursmissile`, `pcursquest`, `rightStickLastMove`) + `PointAndClickState` (line 2247). All of these are single-writer, event/frame-thread-only, and NOT safe for concurrent access. Wall-clock (`SDL_GetTicks`) makes the repeaters and right-stick accumulator non-deterministic across replays.
- Test coverage: none found directly (`test/` has no plrctrls test). Adjacent coverage of the state it manipulates exists in `test/inventory_ui_test.cpp`, `test/stash_test.cpp`, `test/spell_ui_test.cpp`, `test/char_panel_test.cpp`, `test/cursor_test.cpp`, `test/path_test.cpp`, `test/missiles_test.cpp`, `test/towners`-adjacent tests.
- Go mapping: split into `internal/controls` (dispatch, input detection, right-stick emulation, `ProcessGameAction`, frame/logic hooks), `internal/ui/nav` (inventory/stash/visual-store/spell-list grid navigation + slot geometry helpers), and `internal/targeting` (FindActor/FindTarget/FindTrigger/Interact). Strategy: keep one `PlayerControls` struct that owns all the repeaters and navigation state as fields, constructed once; the per-file anonymous namespace becomes an unexported `navState` struct. Frame-tick vs logic-tick entry points must stay separate functions.
- Risks/open questions: (1) `speedspellcount` is declared extern in plrctrls.h but never defined here — the Go port must locate the real definition or the linker contract breaks. (2) The two cursor-centring formulas (`(size-1)*28/2` vs `size*14`) are inconsistent between inventory and stash/visual-store; changing either alters reachable-slot orderings. (3) `VisualStoreMove` writes `VisualStoreSlot = {-1,-1}` as an "invalid" sentinel while `InvalidateInventorySlot` only resets `Slot`/`ActiveStashSlot` — asymmetric state invalidation is easy to lose. (4) The `default:` case of `GetInputTypeFromEvent` for SDL1 builds is different code; decide which SDL generation Ebiten maps to. (5) `pcursquest` iteration order over `Quests` means the *last* in-range quest wins (no distance comparison). (6) `CheckTownersNearby` and `FindTrigger`'s trig loop have no "best" comparison — ordering-dependent.

### Source/controls/plrctrls.h
- Purpose: Public surface of the gamepad player-control layer: the two frame/logic hooks, the cursor-targeting hook, the action primitives, and the two shared control-state globals.
- Public API: `enum class BeltItemType : uint8_t { Healing, Mana };`; `extern GameActionType ControllerActionHeld;`; `extern bool StandToggle;`; `void plrctrls_every_frame();`; `void plrctrls_after_game_logic();`; `void plrctrls_after_check_curs_move();`; `void HandleRightStickMotion();`; `bool InGameMenu();`; `void SetPointAndClick(bool);`; `bool IsPointAndClick();`; `bool IsMovementHandlerActive();`; `void DetectInputMethod(const SDL_Event&, const ControllerButtonEvent&);`; `void ProcessGameAction(const GameAction&);`; `void UseBeltItem(BeltItemType);`; `void PerformPrimaryAction();`; `void PerformPrimaryActionRelease();`; `void PerformSecondaryAction();`; `bool UpdateSpellTarget(SpellID)` — actually `void UpdateSpellTarget(SpellID)`; `bool TryDropItem();`; `void InvalidateInventorySlot();`; `void FocusOnInventory();`; `void FocusOnVisualStore();`; `void PerformSpellAction();`; `void QuickCast(size_t slot);`; `extern int speedspellcount;` (all in namespace `devilution`, lines 20-71).
- Depends on: `SDL_Event` (SDL), `ControllerButtonEvent`/`ControllerButton` (controls/controller.h + controller_buttons.h), `GameActionType`/`GameAction` (controls/game_controls.h), `SpellID`/`Player` (player.h). Header users: cursor.cpp (calls `plrctrls_after_check_curs_move`), panels/ui_panels + draw code (`HandleRightStickMotion`), game loop (`plrctrls_every_frame`/`after_game_logic`), controls/game_controls.cpp (`ProcessGameAction`, `ControllerActionHeld`, `StandToggle`), DiabloUI/menu paths (`DetectInputMethod`), save/load or stats code for `speedspellcount`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Expose the three lifecycle hooks as distinct entry points with the documented call sites: every frame, after every game-logic iteration, at the end of `CheckCursMove`.
  - Expose the primary/secondary/spell action primitives and belt use with the `BeltItemType` two-value enum.
  - Expose point-and-click state as a set/get pair (it is written by the touch handlers and read by targeting).
  - Expose `InvalidateInventorySlot`, `FocusOnInventory`, `FocusOnVisualStore` because the touch event handlers and menu code drive them.
  - Export the two mutable globals (`ControllerActionHeld`, `StandToggle`) — they are read by game_controls.cpp and written by the padmapper path, so in Go they need accessor functions or a shared state struct, not per-call parameters.
- 1:1 constraints: `BeltItemType` values Healing=0, Mana=1 with `uint8_t` backing (lines 20-23). `ControllerActionHeld` is a `GameActionType` (uint8_t) defaulting to `GameActionType_NONE`. `QuickCast` takes `size_t slot` (index into `_pSplHotKey`, 0..3). `speedspellcount` is `int` — and, per this repo's state, is *only* declared here.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: The two `extern` globals are mutable process state; the header itself has no init-order concerns beyond transitively including SDL and player.h. Naming convention (lowercase `plrctrls_every_frame`) differs from the rest of the codebase and is worth normalising in Go — but then the 1:1 name mapping to the C++ call sites is lost.
- Test coverage: none found (the header is included by no test file directly; `test/ui_test.hpp` includes only `controls/control_mode.hpp`).
- Go mapping: `internal/controls` — `PlayerControls` type with methods `EveryFrame`, `AfterGameLogic`, `AfterCheckCursMove`, `PerformPrimaryAction`, etc. Strategy: replace `extern` globals with methods/fields on a singleton-ish `*PlayerControls` handed to callers, so the Go port keeps a single writer instead of process-wide mutable state.
- Risks/open questions: `FocusOnVisualStore` and the visual-store navigation it implies live in the .cpp but are only conditionally compiled in practice (visual store is a QoL feature) — decide whether the Go port gates it. `PerformPrimaryActionRelease` exists solely for visual-store button visuals.

### Source/controls/remap_keyboard.h
- Purpose: Header-only, compile-time remap of one keyboard keysym to another, driven by a user-supplied `REMAP_KEYBOARD_KEYS` macro list.
- Public API: `inline void remap_keyboard_key(SDL_Keycode *sym)` — mutates the keysym in place (lines 17-32).
- Depends on: `SDL_Keycode` (SDL keycode headers, with the SDL1 backport include at lines 9-11), `<cstddef>` for `std::size_t`. Consumed by every keyboard-handling site: `controls/menu_controls.cpp:108`, and (elsewhere in the tree) DiabloUI/input and gamepad keybinding code.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A key-remap step applied to every incoming keysym *before* any switch/dispatch on the key.
  - Configuration is a list of (from, to) pairs, resolved at build/startup rather than per call; first match wins and stops the search.
  - When no remap table is configured, the function must be a no-op (the C++ compiles the body away entirely when `REMAP_KEYBOARD_KEYS` is undefined).
  - Interface may change from in-pointer mutation to `remap(k Keycode) Keycode` provided all callers assign the result.
- 1:1 constraints: `constexpr Mapping kMappings[] = { REMAP_KEYBOARD_KEYS };` (line 23) — the macro expands to a brace list, i.e. the config format is a compile-time literal; loop is `i < sizeof(kMappings)/sizeof(kMappings[0])` with `if (*sym == kMappings[i].from) { *sym = kMappings[i].to; return; }` (lines 24-29) — first-match-wins, no chaining (a -> b then b -> c does NOT apply).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Statelessness aside from the compile-time table: no globals, no init order, safe for concurrent calls.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/input` (or `internal/controls`) — a `[]KeyRemap` slice loaded from config plus `func (m KeyRemapper) Apply(k ebiten.Key) ebiten.Key`. Strategy: since Ebiten keys are a Go enum, a `map[Key]Key` or small slice lookup is equivalent; keep first-match semantics if a slice is used.
- Risks/open questions: Whether the Go port supports build-time remaps at all (the C++ macro is set by platform presets) or must move remapping to runtime config; runtime config changes would alter "first match wins" if the table is edited mid-session.

### Source/controls/touch/event_handlers.cpp
- Purpose: Routes raw SDL touch (finger) events into the on-screen virtual gamepad and, when the touch is not consumed by the pad, into mouse-simulated UI interaction with panels, menus, stores, spell book, speed book, character panel, and stash buttons.
- Public API: `void HandleTouchEvent(const SDL_Event &event);`, `void DeactivateTouchEventHandlers();`, and the member definitions `VirtualGamepadEventHandler::Handle`, `VirtualDirectionPadEventHandler::Handle/HandleFingerDown/HandleFingerUp/HandleFingerMotion`, `VirtualButtonEventHandler::Handle/HandleFingerDown/HandleFingerUp/HandleFingerMotion`.
- Depends on: `VirtualGamepadState` and the `VirtualGamepad`/`VirtualButton`/`VirtualDirectionPad`/`VirtualMenuButton`/`VirtualPadButton` structs (controls/touch/gamepad.h) incl. `isActive`, `isHeld`, `didStateChange`, `isUsable()`, `contains(Point)`, `area`; `SetPointAndClick`, `InvalidateInventorySlot`, `IsMovementHandlerActive`-adjacent state (controls/plrctrls.h); panel geometry `GetMainPanel/GetLeftPanel/GetRightPanel` (panels/ui_panels.hpp) and `GetSpellBook`-adjacent `SpellbookFlag`; `gmenu_is_active/gmenu_left_mouse/gmenu_on_mouse_move` (gmenu.h); `IsPlayerInStore/CheckStoreBtn` (stores.h); `CheckSBook` (panels/spell_book.hpp); `SetSpell` (panels/spell_list.hpp); `CheckMainPanelButton/CheckMainPanelButtonUp/ResetMainPanelButtons/MainPanelButtonDown` (inv.h / panels); `CheckChrBtns/ReleaseChrBtns/CharPanelButtonActive` (char panel); `IsStashOpen/CheckStashButtonPress/CheckStashButtonRelease` (qol/stash.h); `MousePosition`, `gnScreenWidth/gnScreenHeight` (utils/ui_fwd.h, diablo.h); `leveltype`, `DoomFlag`-adjacent flags; `SDL_RegisterEvents`, `SDL_EVENT_FINGER_*`, `SDLC_*` compat, `IsAnyOf`/`IsNoneOf`; `Circle::contains` indirectly through the VDP.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - One global-ordered touch handler: clear point-and-click, give the virtual gamepad first refusal, and only for FINGER_DOWN/UP/MOTION events continue with the mouse-simulation path.
  - Normalised touch coords (0..1 floats from the platform) must be scaled to screen pixels with rounding before any hit test.
  - Mouse-simulation guard: when the stash is open, ignore touches outside main+left+right panels unless the speed book is open; when only the inventory is open, ignore touches outside main+right unless the speed book is open. Then write `MousePosition`, set point-and-click, and invalidate the inventory slot.
  - Panel interaction handlers, each conditional on its own flag and each consuming only the relevant finger phase: game menu (down->`gmenu_left_mouse(true)`, motion->`gmenu_on_mouse_move()`, up->`gmenu_left_mouse(false)`), store (down->`CheckStoreBtn`, any phase counts as consumed when in a store), speed book (up->`SetSpell`, consumed when active), spell book (up->`CheckSBook`), bottom panel (skipped while holding an item; press phase toggles `SpellSelectFlag` around `CheckMainPanelButton`; release phase calls `CheckMainPanelButton` then `CheckMainPanelButtonUp` if a button was down; `ResetMainPanelButtons()` on entry), character panel (down->`CheckChrBtns`, up->`ReleaseChrBtns(false)` when buttons active), stash panel (skipped while holding an item; non-up->`CheckStashButtonPress`, up->`CheckStashButtonRelease`).
  - Virtual gamepad dispatch must try, in this exact order, stopping at the first handler that claims the event: char menu, quests menu, inventory menu, map menu, direction pad, stand button (only when `leveltype != DTYPE_TOWN`), primary action, secondary action, spell action, cancel, health, mana.
  - The pad as a whole is inert when `VirtualGamepadState.isActive` is false — except for the synthetic "deactivate" event — and in that case it must clear `didStateChange` on exactly the four buttons primary/secondary/spell/cancel and return false.
  - Direction pad handler: first finger down inside the pad area claims the finger id and updates the pad position; motion moves the pad only for the claiming finger; up re-centres the pad (position = area.position) and releases the claim.
  - Button handler: if the button is not usable, force `isHeld=false` and set `didStateChange = isHeld` (before the clear) and return; otherwise clear `didStateChange`; down inside -> set or toggle `isHeld`, mark changed, claim finger; up from the claiming finger -> for non-toggle buttons drop `isHeld` and mark changed if it was held; motion for the claiming finger -> `isHeld = contains(pos)` with `didStateChange` set only on transitions; toggling buttons ignore motion entirely.
  - A synthetic custom SDL event type must exist to deactivate all handlers at once, and `DeactivateTouchEventHandlers` must fire it through the same `HandleTouchEvent` entry point.
- 1:1 constraints: `ScaleToScreenCoordinates` uses C-style `(int)round(x * gnScreenWidth)` / `(int)round(y * gnScreenHeight)` — half-away-from-zero rounding (lines 37-42). `Handler` is a file-scope object constructed with `&VirtualGamepadState` (line 35) — static init order matters. `SdlEventType` is `uint16_t` on SDL2+ and `uint8_t` on SDL1 (lines 30-34). The deactivate event is obtained once via `static const SdlEventType customEventType = SDL_RegisterEvents(1);` (lines 172-175) — exactly one custom event id, lazily registered, and `IsDeactivateEvent` compares `event.type`. Finger id accessor differs by SDL major: `event.fingerID` vs `event.fingerId` (lines 59-65). Stand button is gated by `leveltype != DTYPE_TOWN` (line 231) and is the only `toggles = true` handler (event_handlers.h line 68 — `standButtonEventHandler(&virtualGamepad->standButton, true)`). `HandleBottomPanelInteraction` returns early on `!gbRunGame || !MyPlayer->HoldItem.isEmpty()` and uses `!IsFingerUp(event)` (not "IsFingerDown") for the press phase, so MOTION also presses (lines 126-141). Same asymmetry in `HandleStashPanelInteraction` (lines 158-166).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `Handler` is a single process-wide object: one active finger per sub-handler (each keeps `activeFinger` + `isActive`) and it is strictly event-thread-only. It writes game-visible state (`MousePosition`, `SpellSelectFlag`, `CharPanelButtonActive`, cursors, commands via `Check*`), so it must run on the same thread as the logic layer. The `SDL_RegisterEvents` static is a lazy one-time init; the touch handler must therefore be called after SDL video init. `didStateChange` flags are per-frame-consumed latches read by the virtual-gamepad -> controller-event bridge, so a missed read leaves stale state.
- Test coverage: none found (no test for touch handlers).
- Go mapping: `internal/controls/touch` — package `touch`. Strategy: replace the `Handle(const SDL_Event&)` chain with a `Dispatcher` struct holding the twelve sub-handlers; sub-handler "claimed the event" becomes a `bool` return. The synthetic deactivate event becomes a `Dispatcher.Deactivate()` method that walks handlers directly rather than fabricating an event. `VirtualButton` interface -> Go interface `type VirtualButton interface { Contains(Point) bool; IsUsable() bool; Held() bool; SetHeld(bool); SetChanged(bool) }` or, better, a struct with a `Toggles bool` and `Usable func() bool`.
- Risks/open questions: Ebiten exposes `input.Touches()` as a snapshot rather than a per-finger event queue — the port needs an adapter that diffs touch states into down/up/motion events, or the "one active finger" semantics and `didStateChange` latching break. The exact handler priority order is a behaviour contract (e.g. game menu before store before speed book) and reordering would change which UI eats a tap.

### Source/controls/touch/event_handlers.h
- Purpose: Declares the three virtual-gamepad event-handler classes (direction pad, generic button, aggregate gamepad) and the two free touch-entry points.
- Public API: `class VirtualDirectionPadEventHandler { explicit(VirtualDirectionPad*); bool Handle(const SDL_Event&); }`; `class VirtualButtonEventHandler { explicit(VirtualButton*, bool toggles = false); bool Handle(const SDL_Event&); }`; `class VirtualGamepadEventHandler { explicit(VirtualGamepad*); bool Handle(const SDL_Event&); }`; `void HandleTouchEvent(const SDL_Event &event);`; `void DeactivateTouchEventHandlers();`. Private members: `VirtualDirectionPad*/VirtualButton* virtualButton`, `SDL_FingerID activeFinger`, `bool isActive`, `bool toggles`; the aggregate owns 12 sub-handlers as members. Aggregate ctor initialiser order (lines 58-70) is: char, quests, inventory, map (from `menuPanel.charButton/questsButton/inventoryButton/mapButton`), directionPad, standButton (with `true`), primaryActionButton, secondaryActionButton, spellActionButton, cancelButton, healthButton, manaButton.
- Depends on: `controls/touch/gamepad.h` for `VirtualGamepad`, `VirtualGamepadState`, `VirtualDirectionPad`, `VirtualButton`, and the `menuPanel`/`standButton`/`*ActionButton`/`healthButton`/`manaButton` field names; SDL event/finger types; `<cstdint>` implicitly. Consumers: the main event pump (`HandleTouchEvent` on touch events), anything needing to drop touch state (`DeactivateTouchEventHandlers`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Each handler object binds non-owning to a widget (pad area or button) and holds exactly one claimed finger id plus an `isActive` flag — single-finger-per-widget, multi-widget concurrency is what makes multitouch work.
  - `Handle` returns a bool meaning "this event was consumed by this widget", and the aggregate depends on that to implement short-circuit priority.
  - `toggles` must be constructor-configurable with default `false` so the stand button can be the only latching control.
  - The aggregate's sub-handler set must be constructible from the `VirtualGamepad` state object alone (no per-widget registration step).
  - Two free functions remain the only touch entry surface: `HandleTouchEvent(event)` and `DeactivateTouchEventHandlers()`.
- 1:1 constraints: The twelve handler fields and their construction order in the initialiser list (lines 58-70 / 74-90) fix the dispatch order used by `Handle`. `standButtonEventHandler(&virtualGamepad->standButton, true)` (line 68) — `true` is the only non-default flag. `activeFinger` is `SDL_FingerID` (a `int64_t` in SDL2/3), initialised to `0` in every ctor (lines 15-17, 39-42) — 0 is "no finger", and since real SDL finger ids can be 0 this is a latent aliasing quirk that must be preserved or consciously changed.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Header defines no globals but declares handlers holding mutable per-widget state; the aggregate is instantiated once at file scope in the .cpp, so the Go port must likewise create it once (after `VirtualGamepadState` exists) — a static-init-order dependency on `gamepad.cpp`.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/controls/touch` — `type DPHandler struct { pad *touch.VirtualDP; activeFinger int64; isActive bool }`, `type ButtonHandler struct { button *touch.Button; activeFinger int64; isActive, toggles bool }`, `type GamepadHandler struct { charBtn, questsBtn, invBtn, mapBtn ButtonHandler; dpad DPHandler; stand, primary, secondary, spell, cancel, health, mana ButtonHandler }` with a `Handle(e InputEvent) bool` doing the ordered chain. Strategy: model SDL's finger events as a small Go event struct (`{Kind FingerEventKind; Finger int64; X, Y float32}`) so the handler classes stop depending on SDL.
- Risks/open questions: The pointer-to-widget indirection means widget geometry must be mutable at runtime (it is set by `InitializeVirtualGamepad`); a Go port that copies rectangles instead of referencing them will not track screen resizes.

### Source/controls/touch/gamepad.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the virtual (touchscreen) gamepad: geometry/layout computation for all pad buttons based on screen size and DPI, direction-pad vector math, and activate/deactivate logic.
- Public API: `VirtualGamepad VirtualGamepadState` (global); `InitializeVirtualGamepad()`; `ActivateVirtualGamepad()`; `DeactivateVirtualGamepad()`; `VirtualGamepad::Deactivate()`; `VirtualMenuPanel::Deactivate()`; `VirtualDirectionPad::UpdatePosition(Point)`; `VirtualDirectionPad::Deactivate()`; `VirtualButton::Deactivate()`.
- Depends on: `gnScreenWidth`/`gnScreenHeight` (utils/display.h); `ghMainWnd`, `renderer` (SDL globals, display.h/sdl_ptrs); `CharFlag` (control/control.hpp); `QuestLogIsOpen` (panels/quest_log.hpp); `DeactivateTouchEventHandlers` (controls/touch/event_handlers.h); geometry types from engine/circle.hpp, engine/point.hpp, engine/rectangle.hpp; SDL DPI APIs.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A global `VirtualGamepadState` struct instance in the touch-controls package.
  - `InitializeVirtualGamepad` must recompute layout from current screen dimensions; called on resolution change (matches C++ call sites in init/reinit paths).
  - DPI path: SDL3 uses `SDL_GetWindowDisplayScale`; SDL2 uses `SDL_GetDisplayDPI` on the window's display index then scales hdpi/vdpi by `gnScreenWidth/clientWidth` and `gnScreenHeight/clientHeight` and takes the min. If DPI != 0, overrides the screen-pixel-derived margins (Go/Ebiten will likely hardcode or use device DPI — needs decision).
  - health/mana buttons get `isUsable = func() bool { return !CharFlag && !QuestLogIsOpen }` closures.
  - `UpdatePosition` clamps the knob to the pad circle and computes 4-direction press state via atan2 angle sector tests; float math with `roundToInt` (round half away from zero, C `round`).
  - Deactivate cascades to every sub-button and calls `DeactivateTouchEventHandlers()`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `Pi = 3.141592653589793` (L26). Direction sector tests use ±3π/8 around each axis (L31–L59): Up = π/2 ± 3π/8 inclusive; Down = −π/2 ± 3π/8; Left = angle ≥ π−3π/8 OR angle ≤ −π+3π/8; Right = −3π/8 ≤ angle ≤ 3π/8.
  - Default layout from `screenPixels = min(gnScreenWidth, gnScreenHeight)`: inputMargin=screenPixels/10, menuButtonWidth=screenPixels/10, directionPadSize=screenPixels/4, padButtonSize=roundToInt(1.1F*screenPixels/10), padButtonSpacing=inputMargin/3 (L76–L80).
  - DPI overrides (L101–106): inputMargin=roundToInt(0.25*dpi), menuButtonWidth=roundToInt(0.2*dpi), directionPadSize=roundToInt(dpi), padButtonSize=roundToInt(0.3*dpi), padButtonSpacing=roundToInt(0.1*dpi).
  - Menu panel constants (L109–L116): menuPanelTopMargin=30, menuPanelButtonSpacing=4, menuPanelButtonSize={64,62}; menu panel area: x = screenW − 399*menuButtonWidth/64, y=0, w=399*menuButtonWidth/64, h=162*menuButtonWidth/62 (L146–L150; note width divisor uses `.width`=64, height uses `.height`=62).
  - Menu buttons x = screenW − rightMarginMenuButtonN * menuButtonWidth / 64, y = 30*menuButtonWidth/62, size {menuButtonWidth, 62*menuButtonWidth/64}.
  - `padButtonAreaWidth = roundToInt(sqrt2 * (padButtonSize + padButtonSpacing))`; padButtonRight = screenW − inputMargin − padButtonSize/2; padButtonBottom = screenH − inputMargin − padButtonSize/2 (L119–L123).
  - Stand button offset: `standButtonOffset = roundToInt((radius + padButtonSpacing/2 + padButtonSize/2) / sqrt2)`, positioned at directionPad center −offset x, +offset y (L154–L158).
  - DirectionPad center: {inputMargin + directionPadSize/2, screenH − inputMargin − directionPadSize/2}, radius=directionPadSize/2 (L133–L138).
  - Health/mana button positions (L182–L196): health at {dirPad.x − (padButtonSize+padButtonSpacing)/2, dirPad.y − (directionPadSize+padButtonSize+padButtonSpacing)/2}; mana mirrored +x.
  - UpdatePosition (L231–L260): if diff=={0,0} clear all directions; if outside circle, clamp position onto radius via `roundToInt(diff * radius / dist)`; angle = `atan2f(-diff.deltaY, diff.deltaX)` (note y negation); directions from sector tests.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutates global `VirtualGamepadState`; layout depends on window/DPI state at call time. Float rounding (`roundToInt`) can differ in Go `math.Round` — both are round-half-away-from-zero, so identical. No RNG.
- Test coverage: none found (no test/*touch* or gamepad tests).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/touch` (or `internal/ui/touchpad`): struct-based VirtualGamepad with layout function; closures become func fields; angle math in pure Go (`math.Atan2`, `math.Round`).
- Risks/open questions: DPI discovery under Ebiten differs (no SDL); the SDL2 client-size fallback (`SDL_GetRendererOutputSize` vs window size) affects logical scaling. Decide whether to keep the hardcoded 30/4/64/62/399/162 panel constants (they encode original art aspect) — yes, keep for pixel-identical layout.

### Source/crawl.cpp
- Purpose: Implements `DoCrawl` — deterministic ring-by-ring (Chebyshev radius) traversal of tile displacements around a point, visiting cells in a fixed spiral order, with early-abort when the callback returns false.
- Public API: `bool DoCrawl(unsigned radius, tl::function_ref<bool(Displacement)>)`; `bool DoCrawl(unsigned minRadius, unsigned maxRadius, tl::function_ref<bool(Displacement)>)`.
- Depends on: `engine/displacement.hpp` (Displacement); `<function_ref.hpp>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Exact iteration order per radius ring r (see 1:1). Callback returns bool: `true` = keep going, `false` = stop and `DoCrawl` returns false; full traversal returns true.
  - `DoCrawl(radius, fn)` = `DoCrawl(radius, radius, fn)`.
  - Go signature: `func DoCrawl(radius uint, fn func(Displacement) bool) bool` plus min/max variant; Displacement = {dX, dY int}.
- 1:1 constraints (order within each ring r, from L13–L43):
  1. `{0, r}`; 2. if r==0 skip rest; `{0, -r}`; for x in 1..r-1: `{-x, r}`, `{x, r}`, `{-x, -r}`, `{x, -r}`; if r>1: d=r−1: `{-d, d}`, `{d, d}`, `{-d, -d}`, `{d, -d}`; then `{-r, 0}`, `{r, 0}`; for y in 1..r-1: `{-r, y}`, `{r, y}`, `{-r, -y}`, `{r, -y}`. Rings iterate r = minRadius..maxRadius inclusive (int loop over unsigned casts).
  - Ring n=4 and n=16 diagrams in crawl.hpp document the visitation order; note the ring omits the 4 pure-diagonal corners at distance (r,r) — corners come from the d=r−1 diagonal step instead (diamond-within-square pattern).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure function; no state, no RNG. Order is the contract (used for missile target search, item drop, teleport landing).
- Test coverage: `test/crawl_test.cpp` (BasicTest, VisitationOrderTest), `test/crawl_benchmark.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/dungeon/crawl` (or `pkg/geom`): tiny pure package; port visitation order exactly; table-drive the order test from crawl_test.cpp.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/crawl.hpp
- Purpose: Declares DoCrawl and the `Crawl<>()` templates that return the callback's result value (for callbacks returning non-bool, e.g. optional/pointer), stopping at first truthy result.
- Public API: `bool DoCrawl(unsigned, function_ref<bool(Displacement)>)`; `bool DoCrawl(unsigned, unsigned, function_ref<bool(Displacement)>)`; `template<F> auto Crawl(radius, F) -> invoke_result_t<F, Displacement>`; same with (minRadius, maxRadius).
- Depends on: `engine/displacement.hpp`; `<function_ref.hpp>`; `<type_traits>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go generics: `func Crawl[T any](radius int, fn func(Displacement) T) T` where stop condition = boolean-ish truthiness. In Go there is no implicit truthiness; define two helpers: `CrawlBool` (returns bool, stops on true) or require `fn` to return `(T, bool keepGoing)`; simplest faithful mapping: `Crawl[T comparable]`-style is wrong — recommend `func Crawl[T any](radius int, fn func(Displacement) (T, bool)) T` mirroring "result stored, !result stops". Actually C++ stops when `result` (the value) is truthy — e.g. returns first non-null pointer / non-zero. Document that semantics and provide `CrawlPtr`, `CrawlInt`-style wrappers or accept a `truthy func(T) bool`.
  - ASCII diagrams in the doc comment document n=4/n=16 order — port the comment.
- 1:1 constraints: Crawl wraps DoCrawl with `result = function(d); return !result;` (L24–L26, L34–L36) — i.e., DoCrawl's bool means "continue"; Crawl returns last computed result. Header contains no other logic.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure; header-only templates.
- Test coverage: via test/crawl_test.cpp.
- Go mapping: same package as crawl.go; Go 1.18+ generics with an explicit truthiness adapter.
- Risks/open questions: Truthiness mapping for Go generics needs a deliberate API choice (see above); callers in C++ use it with pointer/optional returns.

### Source/cursor.cpp
- Purpose: Cursor tracking and entity-under-cursor selection: loads cursor CELs, computes half-size item sprites, converts mouse position to tile coordinates (panel/scroll/zoom/walking adjustments, diamond-grid alignment), and picks monsters/towners/players/objects/items under the cursor (tile-based and pixel-perfect sprite hit tests).
- Public API: globals `pcursmonst:int=-1`, `pcursinvitem:int8_t`, `pcursstashitem:uint16_t`, `pcursitem:int8_t`, `ObjectUnderCursor:Object*`, `PlayerUnderCursor:const Player*`, `cursPosition:Point`, `pcurstemp:int`, `pcurs:int`; functions `InitCursor`, `FreeCursor`, `ResetCursor`, `NewCursor(const Item&)`, `NewCursor(int)`, `InitLevelCursor`, `CheckRportal`, `CheckTown`, `CheckCursMove`, `DrawSoftwareCursor`, `DrawItem`, `GetInvItemSprite`, `GetHalfSizeItemSprite`, `GetHalfSizeItemSpriteRed`, `CreateHalfSizeItemSprites`, `FreeHalfSizeItemSprites`, `GetInvItemSize`.
- Depends on: `dMonster/dPlayer/dItem` dungeon grids, `InDungeonBounds`, `IsTileLit`, `Monsters`, `M_Talker`, `Towners`, `Players/MyPlayer/MyPlayerId/InspectPlayer`, `Items`, `TileContainsDeadPlayer`, `FindObjectAtPosition`, `Missiles`, `EntranceBoundaryContains`, `CheckTrigForce`, `trigflag/InfoString/AddInfoBoxString`, `CheckPanelInfo/CheckInvHLight/CheckStashHLight/CheckVisualStoreHLight`, `GetMainPanel/GetRightPanel/GetLeftPanel/CanPanelsCoverView/IsLeftPanelOpen/IsRightPanelOpen/RedrawComponent`, `MousePosition/sgbMouseDown/track_isscrolling/InvalidateTargets/ControllerActionHeld/LastPlayerAction`, `ViewPosition/CalcTileOffset/TilesInView/RowsCoveredByPanel/ShiftGrid/GetScreenPosition`, `GetOffsetForWalking`, `GetOptions().Graphics.zoom`, `IsHardwareCursorEnabled/SetHardwareCursor/GetCurrentCursorInfo/CursorInfo/ArtCursor/ControlDevice`, `TryDropItem`, `IsItemLabelHighlighted/ShowUniqueItemInfoBox`, `pcursstoreitem/pcursstorebtn/MainPanelFlag`, `logical_palette/paletteTransparencyLookup/GetInfravisionTRN`, `LoadCel/LoadClx/FindAsset/OpenAsset/ParseInt`, `BilinearDownscaleByHalf8/SurfaceToClx`, `demo::IsRunning/IsRecording`, `HeadlessMode`, `GetOutlineColor`, `_()`, `IsInspectingPlayer`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `CheckCursMove()` is the per-frame mouse-move entry point; full pipeline: skip if item-label highlighted → screenPosition=MousePosition → AlterMousePositionViaPanels (±screenW/4 when panels cover view) → ViaScrolling (y=mainPanel.y−1 while scroll-tracking inside panel) → ViaZoom (÷2) → ViaPlayer (tile offsets + walking offset + one-frame velocity prediction) → ConvertToTileGrid → ShiftToDiamondGridAlignment → CheckMouseHold early-return → ResetCursorInfo → CheckPlayerState → CheckPanelsAndFlags → CheckCursorActions → default cursPosition=currentTile + DisplayTriggerInfo (CheckTrigForce+CheckTown+CheckRportal).
  - Tile-based selection priority in CheckCursorActions: IDENTIFY cursor short-circuits; TrySelectPixelBased; in dungeon: re-select previous monster (pcurstemp match) then any valid monster (never when CURSOR_HEALOTHER/RESURRECT); in town: TrySelectTowner; then Player → Object → Item.
  - TrySelectMonster checks positions in exact order with flipflag variants (see 1:1); validity = !hasNoLife, !MFLAG_HIDDEN, !isPlayerMinion, tile lit, selectionRegion intersects.
  - TrySelectObject: try tile+South with Middle region, then tile with Bottom, then tile+SouthWest/SouthEast (flipflag) with Middle; sets ObjectUnderCursor+cursPosition.
  - TrySelectItem: 4 positions with region checks Middle (right/down neighbor), Bottom (current), Middle (diagonal).
  - TrySelectPlayer: neighbor/current/diagonal + dead players (whole Players scan on exact tile match) + resurrect-cursor 3×3 scan; sets PlayerUnderCursor.
  - TrySelectPixelBased: disabled for demos (running/recording) and headless; scans PointsInRectangle({−1,−1},{3,8}) in REVERSE order; monster first (town→Towners sprite; dungeon→lit+valid monster), then dPlayer, dead players, interactable objects, dItem; hit test via CLX pixel bounds incl. zoom ×2 scaling and `IsPointWithinClx`.
  - Rendering-coordinate→world-tile conversion: x→East displacement; y: nearest even ≤ y, /2 South, +1 y if odd.
  - NewCursor(int): item-held drop semantics — if switching from an item cursor to another item/spell cursor, TryDropItem first (abort if can't drop); clears HoldItem when cursId < CURSOR_HOURGLASS and player exists; sets pcurs; hardware-cursor sync when enabled and KeyboardAndMouse (ArtCursor→UserInterfaceCursor, else GameCursor(cursId), only when changed; skip when ArtCursor && cursId==CURSOR_NONE).
  - NewCursor(Item): empty→CURSOR_HAND else `_iCurs + CURSOR_FIRSTITEM`.
  - DrawSoftwareCursor: item cursors draw outline (GetOutlineColor(heldItem,true)) + DrawItem (TRN red-tinted via GetInfravisionTRN when not usable by InspectPlayer, plain otherwise); else plain ClxDraw.
  - CheckTown/CheckRportal: scan Missiles for TownPortal/RedPortal whose EntranceBoundaryContains(missile.tile, cursPosition); set trigflag, InfoString ("Town Portal"/"Portal to"), AddInfoBoxString (caster name / "The Unholy Altar" when !setlevel else "level 15"), snap cursPosition to missile tile.
  - ResetCursorInfo side effects: RedrawComponent(Belt) when pcursinvitem was set; resets all cursor globals incl. pcursstoreitem/pcursstorebtn=-1, ShowUniqueItemInfoBox=false, MainPanelFlag=false, trigflag=false; pcurstemp=old pcursmonst.
  - InitCursor loads `data\inv\objcurs` CEL (with widths file parse, UNPACKED_MPQS→CLX variant) + optional objcurs2; InitLevelCursor resets selection state and sets cursPosition=ViewPosition.
  - CreateHalfSizeItemSprites: builds half-resolution (bilinear) copies of all item sprites ≥ CURSOR_FIRSTITEM plus red-TRN variants; skips sprites ≤28×28 (1×1 items); MaxWidth/Height=28*3 buffers; SurfaceToClx with transparency index 1.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - TrySelectMonster position order (L74–L87): !flip: Top {2,1}; flip: Top {1,2}; Top {2,2}; !flip: Middle {1,0}; flip: Middle {0,1}; Bottom {0,0}; Middle {1,1}. Monster id = |dMonster[x][y]| − 1.
  - TrySelectTowner (L105–L118): !flip {1,0}; flip {0,1}; {0,0}; {1,1} — no validity checks, overwrites on each hit.
  - TrySelectPlayer (L120–L181): !flip check (x+1,y); flip (x,y+1); (x,y); dead-player scan; resurrect 3×3 (xx,yy ∈ −1..1); diagonal (x+1,y+1) last. `PlayerUnderCursor != nullptr` return.
  - TrySelectObject (L188–L219): South→Middle; tile→Bottom; SouthWest(flip)/SouthEast(!flip)→Middle.
  - TrySelectItem (L221–L248): (!flip,(x+1,y),Middle); (flip,(x,y+1),Middle); ((x,y),Bottom); ((x+1,y+1),Middle).
  - ConvertToTileGrid (L526–L550): currentTile = ViewPosition shifted by (−columns/2, −lrow/2) where lrow=rows−RowsCoveredByPanel(); alignment: both even → screenY += TILE_HEIGHT/2; both odd → screenX −= TILE_WIDTH/2; columns odd & lrow even → currentTile.y++; zoom → screenY −= TILE_HEIGHT/4; tx=X/TILE_WIDTH, ty=Y/TILE_HEIGHT; ShiftGrid(currentTile, tx, ty).
  - ShiftToDiamondGridAlignment (L557–L576): px=X%TILE_WIDTH, py=Y%TILE_HEIGHT; flipy = py < px/2 → tile.y−−; flipx = py ≥ TILE_HEIGHT − px/2 → tile.x++; clamp 0..MAXDUNX−1/MAXDUNY−1; flipflag = (flipy&&flipx) || ((flipy||flipx) && px < TILE_WIDTH/2).
  - AlterMousePositionViaPanels (L479–L487): left panel open → x −= screenW/4; right → x += screenW/4 (only when CanPanelsCoverView).
  - AlterMousePositionViaZoom: x/=2, y/=2.
  - Pixel search rect {{−1,−1},{3,8}} reverse iteration (L288); monster skip when pcurs∈{CURSOR_HEALOTHER, CURSOR_RESURRECT} (L294).
  - Walking prediction (L508–L519): fx = offset2.x/256 − (offset2.x+velocity.x)/256 (integer trunc division), same for y; screen −= fx/fy.
  - Half-size constants: MaxWidth=MaxHeight=28*3 (L369–L370); skip if sprite ≤28×28 (L375); skip red variant not — both created; fill color 1; upscale buffers halved.
  - GetInvItemSprite: cursId≤numSprites(objcurs) → objcurs[cursId−1]; else objcurs2[cursId−numSprites−1] (L341–L349).
  - CheckPanelsAndFlags order (L623–L645): mainPanel→CheckPanelInfo; DoomFlag; invflag&&rightPanel→CheckInvHLight; stash-open&&leftPanel→CheckStashHLight; visual-store&&leftPanel→CheckVisualStoreHLight; spellbook&&rightPanel→return true; leftPanelOpen&&leftPanel→true.
  - CheckMouseHold condition (L585): `(sgbMouseDown != CLICK_NONE || ControllerActionHeld != GameActionType_NONE) && IsNoneOf(LastPlayerAction, None, Attack, Spell)`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Runs on the game loop (mouse-move event coalesced per frame in C++; in Go call once per frame before input handling). Heavy global mutation (pcurs*, cursPosition, trigflag, InfoString, RedrawComponent flag). Demo compatibility: pixel-based selection MUST stay disabled for demos/headless or demo determinism breaks. No RNG.
- Test coverage: `test/cursor_test.cpp` (TEST(Cursor, NewCursor) — item drop path).
- Go mapping: `internal/game/cursor` (selection + state) + sprite halves in `internal/render/itemsprites`. Point/Displacement from `pkg/geom`. CLX pixel hit test via Go CLX decoder. Zoom/panel adjustors as pure funcs for testability.

Ebiten has no hardware cursor equivalent; `IsHardwareCursorEnabled` path becomes no-op/software-only.

### Source/data/file.cpp
- Purpose: Implements `DataFile`: loading TSV-like tab-delimited data files (from the asset system), UTF-8 BOM stripping, header parsing into ColumnDefinitions, header skipping, record counting, and fatal error reporting.
- Public API: `DataFile::load(path) -> expected<DataFile, Error>`; `DataFile::loadOrDie(path)`; `reportFatalError(Error, fileName)`; `reportFatalFieldError(DataFileField::Error, fileName, fieldName, field, details="")`; `parseHeader(ColumnDefinition* begin, end, mapper)`; templated `parseHeader<T>` (in header); `skipHeader()`; `skipHeaderOrDie(path)`; `numRecords()`; inline `resetHeader/begin/end/data/size` (header).
- Depends on: `engine/assets.hpp` (FindAsset/OpenIntegralAsset/AssetRef/AssetHandle), `DataFileField/RecordIterator` (data/iterators.hpp), `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (c_count), `utils/format.hpp` (FormatRuntime/StrCat), `utils/language.h` (_), `app_fatal`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `Load(path) ([]byte, error)` reading via the Go asset/MPQ layer; whole-file into memory (streaming TODO noted upstream).
  - Strip UTF-8 BOM `\xef\xbb\xbf` from content start; keep an owned buffer.
  - Error taxonomy: NotFound, OpenFailed, BadRead, NoContent, NotEnoughColumns (map to Go error values or sentinel errors).
  - parseHeader semantics: iterate first record's fields; for each field the mapper returns a column id or error; duplicates ignored (first wins); compute skipLength = field.column() − lastColumn − 1 (gap fields since previous key column); stop early when destination range full but still advance the record iterator to end-of-record; then `body_ = firstRecord.data()`; errors: NoContent if file ends after header, NotEnoughColumns if fewer columns mapped than destination slots.
  - skipHeader: advance one record; NoContent if at end; body_ = record start.
  - numRecords: 0 if empty; newline count `c_count(content,'\n')` + (0 if ends with '\n' else 1); if <2 → 0; else count−1 (header excluded).
  - Fatal reporters: localized messages matching the C++ TRANSLATORS strings, including row/column detail for field errors (details appended after '\n').
- 1:1 constraints:
  - BOM constant `"\xef\xbb\xbf"` (file.hpp L48).
  - numRecords formula (file.cpp L156–L162): `newlines + (back=='\n' ? 0 : 1); if <2 → 0; return n−1`.
  - parseHeader skip computation L128–L131: `skipColumns = field.column() - lastColumn - 1` when column > lastColumn, else 0.
  - Error enum order (file.hpp L64–L70): NotFound, OpenFailed, BadRead, NoContent, NotEnoughColumns.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Immutable after load (const char* body marker changes only via header ops). No RNG. Single-threaded asset-load phase.
- Test coverage: `test/data_file_test.cpp` (10+ cases: missing file, CR files, Windows line endings, no trailing newline, empty, BOM variants, ParseInt, record iteration); also used by pack_test, player_test, vendor_test, timedemo_test via data file loading.
- Go mapping: `pkg/txtdata` (DataFile + iterators) or `internal/data/file`. Strategy: `DataFile struct { data []byte; body int }` with `Records()` iterator; Go 1.23 `iter.Seq` over records/fields replaces the C++ iterator pair pattern.
- Risks/open questions: The early-break-then-increment subtlety in parseHeader (iterator must consume to record end so `data()` points at the next record) must be preserved by whatever iterator API Go exposes.

### Source/data/iterators.hpp
- Purpose: Defines the field/record cursor machinery for DataFile: `DataFileField` (lazy value access + typed parsers: int, bool, int arrays, enum arrays/lists, fixed-point 6-bit), `FieldIterator` (input iterator over fields of a record with skip support), `DataFileRecord` (range of fields), `RecordIterator` (forward iterator over records with skip support and shared-state protocol).
- Public API: `class DataFileField` — ctors private-ish (made by iterators); `value()/operator*()`; `parseInt<T>(T&)`; `parseBool(bool&)`; `parseIntArray<T>(T*, n)` + array refs; `parseEnumArray<T,ParseFn>(T*, n, optional<T> fillMissing, ParseFn)` (+array refs, +parseIntArray alias); `parseEnumList<T,ParseFn>(T&, ParseFn)` (bitwise-OR accumulation); `asInt<T>()`; `parseFixed6<T>(T&)`; `asFixed6<T>()`; `row()/column()/currentValue()`; static `mapError(std::errc)` and `mapError(ParseIntError)`; `operator<<` for test output. `class FieldIterator` — `operator++/+=(unsigned)`, `operator*` → DataFileField, `row()/column()`, end-sentinel semantics (state_==nullptr). `class DataFileRecord` — `begin()/end()/row()`. `class RecordIterator` — `operator++/+=(unsigned)`, `operator*` → DataFileRecord, `data()` (internal), `row()`; end-sentinel via next==nullptr.
- Depends on: `parser.hpp` (GetFieldResult, GetNextField, DiscardField, DiscardMultipleFields, DiscardRemainingFields, ParseFixed6 — the low-level scanner in Source/data or utils), `utils/parse_int.hpp` (ParseInt/ParseIntError/ParseIntResult), `utils/str_cat.hpp` (StrCat), `utils/str_split.hpp` (SplitByChar), `<charconv>` (from_chars).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lazy single-scan protocol: a field is scanned on first access (value or parse); result cached in state; parse may consume only the numeric prefix and then completes the field scan, prepending the parsed prefix to the stored value. Go equivalent: a `Field` struct with `scanned bool`, `value string`, `next int` into the record buffer, plus `Value()`, `ParseInt`, etc.
  - `ParseInt` must reproduce `std::from_chars` semantics: no leading whitespace skip, no sign-only, `result_out_of_range` → OutOfRange, `invalid_argument` → NotANumber; Go `strconv.ParseInt` differs (accepts underscores? no — but allows leading +, and base prefixes) — implement a from_chars-equivalent scanner or carefully validate.
  - `parseBool`: exact strings "true"/"false" only, else InvalidValue.
  - `parseIntArray`: comma-split (SplitByChar on ','), exactly n values or InvalidValue (too many → InvalidValue immediately; too few → InvalidValue at end).
  - `parseEnumArray`: comma-split; empty string → all fillMissing (error if none); too many → error "Too many values, max: N"; parseFn failure → its error string; short lists filled with fillMissing or error "Too few values, expected N got M".
  - `parseEnumList`: destination zeroed; empty → done; each part parsed and OR-ed into destination (bit flags).
  - `parseFixed6`: 6-bit fraction fixed point via ParseFixed6; error mapping like ParseIntError (OutOfRange/ParseError→NotANumber/else InvalidValue).
  - Field skipping: `FieldIterator += n` discards fields without materializing values; column counter += fieldsSkipped+1; record end → invalidated (nil state).
  - Record skipping: `RecordIterator += n` discards remainder of current record first (if the field iterator left it unconsumed), then discards n−1 more records; row_ += recordsSkipped+1; end-of-file → next=nil (end sentinel).
  - Row numbering: header row is 0; after parseHeader/skipHeader the first body record is row 1.
  - Column numbering: 0-based within record; DataFileField carries row_/column_ for error messages.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Error enums: `DataFileField::Error { NotANumber, OutOfRange, InvalidValue }` (L26–L30); mapping from errc L34–L46; from ParseIntError L48–L57.
  - parseInt first-access fast path (L108–L125): from_chars from `state_->next`; if not invalid_argument, `GetNextField(result.ptr, end_)` then value = {begin, (value.data−begin)+value.size} — prepends parsed digits. Exactly replicate so error messages show full field text.
  - parseBool string compares (L130–L140): "true"/"false".
  - parseIntArray error cases (L155–L166): i==n → InvalidValue (before storing); any from_chars error → mapError; final i != n → InvalidValue.
  - parseEnumArray messages (L181–L201): "Too many values, max: {n}"; "Too few values, expected {n} got {i}".
  - parseEnumList (L215–L228): `destination = {}` first; `destination |= result.value()`.
  - Fixed6: 6 fractional bits (doc L264); value = ParseFixed6 result.
  - FieldIterator `+=` (L303–L331): ReadyToRead → DiscardField; endOfRecord → state_=nullptr; else DiscardMultipleFields(increment−1), column_ += fieldsSkipped+1, status=ReadyToRead.
  - RecordIterator `+=` (L429–L457): !endOfRecord → DiscardRemainingFields; endOfFile → next=nullptr; else DiscardMultipleRecords(increment−1), row_ += recordsSkipped+1, status=ReadyToRead.
  - Row semantics comment L522–L528: header always row 0; after parseHeader begin() yields row 1.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Iterators share mutable `GetFieldResult` state via pointer (DataFileRecord hands &state_ of its parent RecordIterator) — single-consumer design; not safe for concurrent use. All pure parsing; no RNG.
- Test coverage: test/data_file_test.cpp (ParseInt L195, IterateOverRecords L293 and more).
- Go mapping: `pkg/txtdata` — `Record`/`Field` structs with explicit `Next`/`Skip` methods, or Go 1.23 iterators (`func (f *DataFile) Records() iter.Seq[*Record]`). Field parsers return `(err FieldError)` with Row/Column for messages.
- Risks/open questions: `std::from_chars` vs Go `strconv` behavioral deltas (leading '+', base detection, trailing garbage tolerance — from_chars stops at first non-digit and reports consumed length; ParseInt in DVL checks the tail). Reuse the ported `utils/parse_int` logic for exactness. The shared-state iterator protocol can be simplified in Go but callers relying on `Skip(n)` (e.g. ColumnDefinition skipLength) must be preserved.
