# Volume III — batch 009

### Source/data/parser.cpp
- Purpose: Tab-delimited (TSV) text-stream cursor: consumes field/record separators and reports *why* a read stopped. Three out-of-line functions; the header carries the rest inline.
- Public API: `GetFieldResult HandleRecordTerminator(const char *begin, const char *end)` (L4-28); `GetFieldResult DiscardMultipleFields(const char *begin, const char *end, unsigned skipLength, unsigned *fieldsSkipped)` (L30-46); `GetFieldResult DiscardMultipleRecords(const char *begin, const char *end, unsigned skipLength, unsigned *recordsSkipped)` (L48-64).
- Depends on: `GetFieldResult` + `GetFieldResult::Status` (parser.hpp L10-24); `IsAnyOf` via `utils/is_of.hpp` (parser.hpp L6); the inline siblings `HandleFieldSeparator` (parser.hpp L123-130), `DiscardField` (L138-144), `DiscardRemainingFields` (L176-182), `GetNextField` (L198-205); `std::find_if`/`<algorithm>` (parser.hpp L3). Consumers: `data/file.hpp`/`data/iterators.hpp` field iteration and, through them, all `Source/tables/*.cpp` TSV loaders.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A `Result` value type carrying `Value string`, `Next int` (byte offset, replaces `const char *`), `Status Status`; functions take `(buf []byte, at, end int)` or `(buf []byte, at int)` with `end == len(buf)`.
  - `HandleRecordTerminator`: `at == end` (empty tail) → `Next=end, Status=NoFinalTerminator` (L6-8). A leading `\r` is consumed (`++begin`, L11) and then **falls through** to the `\n` test (L17) — a `\r` not followed by `\n` yields `BadRecordTerminator` with `Next` pointing *after* the `\r` (L27). `\r` immediately before EOF → `FileTruncated`, `Next=end` (L12-14). `\n` as the last byte → `EndOfFile`, `Next=end` (L18-20). Otherwise `\n` with more input → `EndOfRecord`, `Next` = byte after the `\n` (L22-23).
  - `DiscardMultipleFields` (L30-46): starts from `Result{Next: begin}` (status `ReadyToRead`, L32), loops `while skipCount < skipLength` with **pre-increment** (L34-35), calls `DiscardField(result.next, end)` (L36), breaks when `result.endOfRecord()` (L37-40), and writes the *actual* count into `fieldsSkipped` if non-null (L42-44). `skipLength == 0` → no advance, status stays `ReadyToRead`.
  - `DiscardMultipleRecords` (L48-64): same shape but calls `DiscardRemainingFields(result.next, end)` (L53) and breaks on `result.endOfFile()` (L54-57), reporting `recordsSkipped` (L59-61).
  - Go should return `(Result, skipped int)` instead of the `unsigned *` out-params.
  - Semantics that must survive translation: `endOfRecord()` is true for `EndOfRecord | BadRecordTerminator | EndOfFile | FileTruncated | NoFinalTerminator` (parser.hpp L55-58); `endOfFile()` for `EndOfFile | FileTruncated | NoFinalTerminator` (L63-66) — i.e. a mangled terminator is treated as end-of-record but not end-of-file.
- 1:1 constraints: terminator/separator bytes `'\r'`/`'\n'` (parser.hpp L74-77) and `'\t'` (L86-88); Status declaration order `ReadyToRead, EndOfField, EndOfRecord, BadRecordTerminator, EndOfFile, FileTruncated, NoFinalTerminator` (parser.hpp L15-23) with default `= Status::ReadyToRead` (L24); `HandleFieldSeparator` returns `EndOfField` with `begin+1` only when `begin != end && *begin == '\t'`, otherwise delegates (parser.hpp L123-130, this file relies on it at L36); `DiscardField` scans with `IsFieldSeparator` (parser.hpp L140) while `DiscardRemainingFields` scans with `IsRecordTerminator` (parser.hpp L178) — different predicates, so a bare tab must not end a "discard remaining fields" run; loop bounds L34/L52; pre-increment L35/L53; out-param assignment L43/L60.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure functions over an immutable byte range; no globals, no allocation of consequence, no RNG, no tick coupling. Trivially portable as concurrent-safe functions. No order-of-init effects.
- Test coverage: `test/data_file_test.cpp` includes `data/parser.hpp` (L4) and drives `GetNextField` at L33, L379, L440. No standalone parser test, so `HandleRecordTerminator`'s error branches (`FileTruncated`, `BadRecordTerminator`, `NoFinalTerminator`) and both `DiscardMultiple*` skip-count paths are not directly asserted anywhere.
- Go mapping: `internal/data/parser` (sibling of `internal/data/file` + `internal/data/iterators`). Strategy: literal translation with `[]byte`+offsets; add table-driven tests for the 6 terminator cases since the C++ suite only covers the happy path. Must land before `DataFile`/`RecordReader`/`ValueReader`.
- Risks/open questions: `{ begin, len }` string_view construction (parser.hpp L204) has no Go analogue — decide `Value string` (copy per field, safe, but a copy on *every* TSV cell of every table load) vs `Value []byte` aliasing the buffer (zero-copy, unsafe if the buffer is mutated). The buffer in C++ outlives the reader (`DataFile` owns it), so aliasing is viable.

### Source/data/parser.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the TSV cursor result type plus the inline primitives (separator classification, field/separator consumption) that parser.cpp builds on. Whole TSV scanning surface lives here.
- Public API: `struct GetFieldResult` (L10-67): members `std::string_view value` (L11), `const char *next = nullptr` (L13), `Status status` (L15-24); ctors `GetFieldResult()` (L26), `GetFieldResult(const char *next)` → `ReadyToRead` (L28-33), `GetFieldResult(const char *next, const Status&)` (L35-40), `GetFieldResult(std::string_view value, const GetFieldResult &result)` → clone-with-new-value (L45-50); `[[nodiscard]] bool endOfRecord()` (L55), `[[nodiscard]] bool endOfFile()` (L63). Free functions: `constexpr bool IsRecordTerminator(char)` (L74), `constexpr bool IsFieldSeparator(char)` (L86), `HandleRecordTerminator` decl (L108), `inline GetFieldResult HandleFieldSeparator(const char*, const char*)` (L123), `inline GetFieldResult DiscardField(const char*, const char*)` (L138), `DiscardMultipleFields` decl with default `fieldsSkipped = nullptr` (L156), `DiscardMultipleRecords` decl with default `recordsSkipped = nullptr` (L168), `inline GetFieldResult DiscardRemainingFields(const char*, const char*)` (L176), `GetFieldResult DiscardField`-based `inline GetFieldResult GetNextField(const char*, const char*)` (L198).
- Depends on: `<algorithm>` (L3), `<string_view>` (L4), `utils/is_of.hpp` (L6). No game state at all.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `type Status uint8` with the seven names in declared order; `type Result struct { Value string; Next int; Status Status }` with `EndOfRecord() bool` / `EndOfFile() bool` methods reproducing the two `IsAnyOf` sets exactly (L55-66).
  - The "clone with a new value" ctor (L45-50) is what `GetNextField` uses to attach the field text while inheriting `next`/`status` from `HandleFieldSeparator` — in Go: build the separator result first, then set `Value`.
  - `IsRecordTerminator` = `c=='\r' || c=='\n'` (L74-78); `IsFieldSeparator` = `c=='\t' || IsRecordTerminator(c)` (L86-90) — record terminators *also* separate fields (doc L80-84).
  - `GetNextField` must always return a value, including the empty string for a zero-length field (doc L193-196), and must consume the separator so `Next` is the start of the following field/record or `end` (L198-205).
  - `Result{Next: begin}` single-arg construction must default `Status` to `ReadyToRead` so the Discard-multiple loops don't exit on iteration zero (L28-33 + parser.cpp L32/L49).
  - Default arguments (`nullptr` out-params, L156/L168) become two call forms or a forced extra return in Go.
- 1:1 constraints: Status list L15-23 and default L24; `endOfRecord()` includes `BadRecordTerminator` (L57); `endOfFile()` set L65; `'\t'` comparison and `begin + 1` for `EndOfField` (L125-126); `std::find_if` scan predicates L140 (field) vs L178 (record) vs L200 (field); `HandleFieldSeparator` delegates to `HandleRecordTerminator` for anything that is not a tab (L129); `DiscardField`/`GetNextField` return `HandleFieldSeparator(nextSeparator, end)` (L143/L204) while `DiscardRemainingFields` returns `HandleRecordTerminator(nextSeparator, end)` (L181).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: header-only `inline`/`constexpr`, zero mutable state and zero statics — in Go, keep it stateless (no package-level vars) so table loading can run in parallel per file if desired.
- Test coverage: same as parser.cpp (`test/data_file_test.cpp` L4/L33/L379/L440); `IsRecordTerminator`/`IsFieldSeparator` are not individually asserted.
- Go mapping: same package `internal/data/parser`; inline helpers become exported package funcs (`GetNextField`, `DiscardField`, `DiscardRemainingFields`, `HandleFieldSeparator`, `HandleRecordTerminator`) with `isRecordTerminator`/`isFieldSeparator` unexported unless iterators need them. Strategy: one file, 1:1, no abstraction — it is a leaf.
- Risks/open questions: `next` may legally equal `end` (all EOF statuses); the Go port must not model "no next field" as `Next == -1`, keep the `end` sentinel so callers' `buf[Next]` guards behave identically.

### Source/data/record_reader.cpp
- Purpose: The single out-of-line member of `RecordReader`: the cursor advance rule plus a fatal error when the reader walks off the end of a record.
- Public API: `void RecordReader::advance()` (L5-16).
- Depends on: `RecordReader` private state `it_`, `end_`, `filename_`, `needsIncrement_` (record_reader.hpp L134-137); `DataFile::reportFatalError(DataFile::Error::NotEnoughColumns, filename_)` (L13) from `data/file.hpp`; `FieldIterator` from `data/iterators.hpp`; the file includes only `data/record_reader.hpp` (L1).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Preserve the **lazy first read**: the reader is constructed positioned *before* column 0 with `needsIncrement_ = false` (record_reader.hpp L137), and the first `advance()` sets the flag without moving (L7-10); every later call increments (L7-8). Net effect: the k-th `nextField()` returns column k.
  - After the increment decision, if the cursor equals `end_` → fatal `NotEnoughColumns` carrying the filename (L12-15). This is a hard abort of asset loading (process-fatal in C++), not a recoverable per-record error.
  - `advance()` does **not** consult record-terminator status; end-of-record vs end-of-file distinction stays with the parser layer.
  - `value()` in the header resets `needsIncrement_` to false (record_reader.hpp L104-107), which makes the *next* `advance()` a no-op — this file must not re-set the flag.
- 1:1 constraints: the `if (needsIncrement_) ++it_; else needsIncrement_ = true;` branch shape (L6-11) is the entire contract; fatal error enum member `DataFile::Error::NotEnoughColumns` (L13) must map to the same code the Go `data` package reports for the same condition (message parity with `data/file`).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutates only its own instance (cursor + flag) — no globals, no statics, no RNG, no tick coupling. A reader is single-use/single-threaded; concurrent use of one reader would corrupt the cursor.
- Test coverage: none found — `RecordReader` has no dedicated test; `test/data_file_test.cpp` exercises the `DataFile` layer beneath it, and table loaders (indirectly `test/items_test.cpp`, `test/quests_test.cpp`, `test/player_test.cpp`) exercise the happy path.
- Go mapping: fold into `internal/data` as `type RecordReader` with unexported `advance()` (or exported `Advance()` if the ported table code lives in another package). Strategy: `itIdx/endIdx int` + `needsIncrement bool`; the fatal call goes through whatever port-wide asset-error policy is chosen (see Risks).
- Risks/open questions: The port must decide once, globally, whether TSV column-count problems abort (`app_fatal`) or bubble an error to the loader — this file cannot be ported without that answer, and `reportFatalError` is shared with `value_reader`.

### Source/data/record_reader.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only per-field TSV record reader used by every `Source/tables/*.cpp` static-data loader; treats any read/parse failure as fatal.
- Public API: `class RecordReader` (L18) — ctor `RecordReader(DataFileRecord &record, std::string_view filename)` (L20-25, initialises `it_(record.begin()), end_(record.end()), filename_`); `readInt<T>(std::string_view name, T &out)` (L28-34), `readOptionalInt<T>(name, T&)` (L36-42), `readIntArray<T,N>(name, T (&out)[N])` (L44-49), `readEnumArray<T,N,F>(name, std::optional<T> fillMissing, T (&out)[N], F &&parseFn)` (L51-57), `readIntArray<T,N>(name, std::array<T,N>&)` (L59-64), `readFixed6<T>(name, T&)` (L66-71), `readBool(name, bool&)` (L73-77), `readString(name, std::string&)` (L79-83), generic `read<T,F>(name, T&, F&& parseFn)` (L85-94), `readEnumList<T,F>(name, T&, F&& parseFn)` (L96-103), `std::string_view value()` (L102-108), `void advance()` (L109), `DataFileField nextField()` (L111-115); private `failOnError` overloads (L117-124, L126-134).
- Depends on: `data/file.hpp` + `data/iterators.hpp` (L11-12) for `DataFile`, `DataFileRecord`, `DataFileField`, `DataFileField::Error`, `FieldIterator`, `DataFile::reportFatalError`, `DataFile::reportFatalFieldError`; `<function_ref>` (L8, present for the `F&&` surface); `std::expected` (L5). Callers: `Source/effects.cpp` (L16), `Source/tables/{itemdat,misdat,monstdat,objdat,playerdat,questdat,spelldat,textdat,townerdat}.cpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Uniform shape for every accessor: `field = nextField()` → parse → fatal on error, with the caller-supplied field `name` threaded into the error report (L29-34 etc.).
  - `readOptionalInt` returns leaving `out` at the caller's pre-set default when the field text is empty (L40) — the "column may be absent, keep the default" behaviour all table loaders rely on.
  - `readString` bypasses parsing: `advance()` then copies `(*it_).value()` verbatim (L79-83) — no error path.
  - `value()` (L102-108) calls `advance()` and then sets `needsIncrement_ = false`, so a subsequent read re-reads the *same* column. This quirk is the only place the flag is cleared and must be reproduced exactly.
  - Generic `read` takes a `func(string) (T, error)`; on failure it reports `DataFileField::Error::InvalidValue` **plus** the parse function's message (L88-92 with L126-134).
  - `readEnumArray` passes `std::optional<T> fillMissing` so short rows fill remaining slots (L51-57).
  - `readEnumList` delegates to `DataFileField::parseEnumList` and escalates to `InvalidValue` (L96-103).
  - Error split must stay: `expected<T, DataFileField::Error>` → `reportFatalFieldError(result.error(), filename, name, field)` (L117-124); `expected<T, std::string>` → `reportFatalFieldError(error, filename, name, field, result.error())` (L126-134).
  - `readIntArray`/`readEnumArray` must accept both C-array and `std::array` destinations (L44-49 vs L59-64) — in Go a `*[N]T` generic covers both.
- 1:1 constraints: ctor binds `end_` from `record.end()` once (L22-24) and `end_` is `const` (L135); the first accessor reads column 0 because `needsIncrement_` starts `false` (L137 + record_reader.cpp L6-11); emptiness test is `field.value().empty()` (L40) — whitespace is *not* trimmed; `readEnumArray`/`read`/`readEnumList` force `DataFileField::Error::InvalidValue` regardless of the underlying parse error (L55, L91, L100); `advance()` fatal is `DataFile::Error::NotEnoughColumns` (record_reader.cpp L13).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Strictly positional — the source TSV's column ORDER is load-bearing, so a ported table must read columns in the same sequence. Per-instance mutable cursor (L134-137); no globals, no RNG, no statics. Not concurrent-safe per reader, but readers are constructed per record inside single-threaded startup loading.
- Test coverage: none found for `RecordReader` itself; only `test/data_file_test.cpp` beneath it, plus indirect coverage of loaded tables in `test/items_test.cpp`, `test/quests_test.cpp`, `test/player_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/data` (same package as parser/file, to avoid an import cycle). Strategy: generic methods `ReadInt[T constraints.Integer](name string, out *T)`, `ReadOptionalInt`, `ReadFixed6`, `ReadBool`, `ReadString`, `ReadArray[T, N]`, `Read[T](name string, out *T, parse func(string) (T, error))`, `ReadEnumList`, `Value() string`, `NextField() Field`. Keep the `name` string literals identical to the C++ call sites so error text (and thus `test` fixtures/log diffs) match.
- Risks/open questions: `std::optional<T> fillMissing` → `*T` or `(T, bool)`; whether `tl::function_ref` usage anywhere in the parse-fn surface implies non-owning callables that Go closures capture safely (they do). The `value()` re-read quirk is easy to drop and would silently shift every subsequent column read in the ported tables.

### Source/data/value_reader.cpp
- Purpose: Out-of-line half of `ValueReader`: locate the value column of a `key<TAB>value` record and abort if the key is missing or unexpected.
- Public API: `ValueReader::ValueReader(DataFile &dataFile, std::string_view filename)` (L9-13); `DataFileField ValueReader::getValueField(std::string_view expectedKey)` (L16-35).
- Depends on: `app_fatal` from `appfat.h` (L6, invoked L19 and L27); `std::format` (L4) for both messages; `DataFile`/`DataFileRecord`/`FieldIterator`/`DataFileField` (via `data/value_reader.hpp` L11-12); `DataFile::reportFatalError(DataFile::Error::NotEnoughColumns, filename_)` (L32). Consumer: `Source/tables/playerdat.cpp` (L21, alongside RecordReader).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Iterates **records**, not fields: `it_(dataFile.begin()), end_(dataFile.end())` (L10-11).
  - `getValueField(expectedKey)` sequence: (1) if the record cursor is exhausted → fatal `Missing field {expectedKey} in {filename}` (L17-20); (2) materialise the record (`DataFileRecord record = *it_`, L21) and take field 0 (L22-25); (3) compare it byte-exactly to `expectedKey`, fatal `Unexpected field in {filename}: got {key}, expected {expectedKey}` on mismatch (L26-29); (4) move to field 1 and if absent → fatal `NotEnoughColumns` (L30-33); (5) return that field (L34).
  - Key match is plain `std::string_view` equality: no case folding, no trimming (L26).
  - It must NOT advance the record cursor — that is the header's job (`readValue`, value_reader.hpp L32).
  - One record == exactly two columns here (key, value); extra columns are ignored, missing value is fatal.
- 1:1 constraints: fatal message formats L19 and L27 (`"Missing field {} in {}"`, `"Unexpected field in {}: got {}, expected {}"`) — argument order matters for log parity; the `NotEnoughColumns` code at L32 is shared with `RecordReader::advance` so both readers report the same failure identically; record/field indexing is 0-based (L22 field 0, L30 field 1).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Per-instance cursor; the TSV's record ORDER dictates which key is expected next, so ported callers must issue reads in the same sequence as the C++ loader. No globals, no RNG, no statics. All failures are process-fatal (single-threaded startup path).
- Test coverage: none found — `test/data_file_test.cpp` does not reference `ValueReader`.
- Go mapping: `internal/data` next to `RecordReader`: `func NewValueReader(f *DataFile, filename string) *ValueReader` and `func (v *ValueReader) valueField(expectedKey string) Field`. Strategy: keep the two fatal messages verbatim via `fmt.Sprintf`, and reuse the single `reportFatalError`/`reportFatalFieldError` pair created for `data/file`.
- Risks/open questions: Does the Go port need order-sensitivity, or may it build a key→value map (which would change behaviour for duplicate keys and drop the "unexpected field" guard)? Also, `app_fatal(std::format(...))` is a *different* fatal channel than `DataFile::reportFatalError` — unify or keep both?

### Source/data/value_reader.hpp
- Purpose: Header half of `ValueReader`: typed accessors that assert a record's key column, parse its value column, then step to the next record.
- Public API: `getValueField(std::string_view expectedKey)` (L22); `readValue<T,F>(std::string_view expectedKey, T &outValue, F &&readFn)` (L24-34); `read<T,F>(expectedKey, T&, F&& parseFn)` (L36-48); `readEnumList<T,F>(expectedKey, T&, F&& parseFn)` (L50-62); `readInt<T>(expectedKey, T&)` (L63-69); `readDecimal<T>(expectedKey, T&)` (L71-78); `readString(expectedKey, std::string&)` (L80-86); `readChar(expectedKey, char&)` (L87-98); private `RecordIterator it_; const RecordIterator end_; std::string_view filename_;` (L101-103).
- Depends on: `data/file.hpp` + `data/iterators.hpp` (L11-12) — `DataFileField`, `DataFileField::Error::InvalidValue`, `RecordIterator`, `DataFile::reportFatalFieldError`; `std::expected` (L5); `<function_ref>` (L8). Same consumer as the .cpp: `Source/tables/playerdat.cpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - The common engine: `readValue` = `getValueField(key)` → invoke the reader callback → on failure `reportFatalFieldError(err, filename, "Value", field)` → then `++it_` (L25-34). Record advance happens **after** the parse attempt and is *not* reached on a fatal path.
  - `read` wraps a `func(string) (T, error)`-style parse function and converts any error into `DataFileField::Error::InvalidValue` (L36-48), discarding the parse message.
  - `readDecimal` is the 6-bit fixed-point accessor (`parseFixed6`), not a float parse (L71-78) — naming trap.
  - `readString` copies the raw value with no validation (L80-86).
  - `readChar` requires value length exactly 1, else `InvalidValue`; otherwise takes byte 0 (L87-98, checks L91, extracts L95).
  - `readEnumList` delegates to `DataFileField::parseEnumList` and maps failure to `InvalidValue` (L50-62).
  - `readInt<T>` is integral-only (`std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral_v<T>>`, L63-65) → Go generic over `constraints.Integer`.
  - The literal field label `"Value"` is what appears in every fatal message from this class (L30) — port it verbatim.
- 1:1 constraints: `++it_` placement after the error check (L32); one record consumed per read; `valueField.value().size() != 1` for `readChar` (L91); `parseFixed6` for `readDecimal` (L76); `parseInt` for `readInt` (L67); `readEnumList` failure ⇒ `InvalidValue` (L55-57); the exact message label `"Value"` (L30).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutable per-instance record cursor; order-of-calls equals order-of-records in the file. No RNG, no process globals, no statics. Runs on the single-threaded startup load path.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/data` — `func (v *ValueReader) ReadInt[T constraints.Integer](key string, out *T)`, `ReadFixed6`, `ReadString`, `ReadChar`, plus `Read[T](key string, out *T, parse func(string)(T,error))` and `ReadEnumList`. Strategy: mirror the one-record-per-call contract so the ported `playerdat` loader reads the identical key sequence.
- Risks/open questions: `readValue` collapses all parse failures to `InvalidValue` and names the field `"Value"` rather than the key, so ported error strings will be less specific than the key — intentional? Preserve it (a log-parity test could otherwise fail). Also confirm nothing outside `playerdat` starts depending on `ValueReader` ordering.

### Source/dead.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the corpse (dead-monster) sprite table at level init, writes corpse+direction markers into the dungeon grid, and re-anchors unique-monster lights to their corpses.
- Public API: globals `Corpse Corpses[MaxCorpses]` (L19), `int8_t stonendx` (L20); `void InitCorpses()` (L48-93); `void AddCorpse(Point tilePosition, int8_t dv, Direction ddir)` (L95-98); `void MoveLightsToCorpses()` (L100-108). Anonymous-namespace helpers `InitDeadAnimationFromMonster(Corpse&, const CMonster&)` (L24-34) and `MoveLightToCorpse(Monster&)` (L36-45).
- Depends on: `diablo.h` (L10); `headless_mode.hpp` → `HeadlessMode` (L70); `levels/gendung.h` → `dCorpse`, `MAXDUNX`, `MAXDUNY` (L38-39, L97); `lighting.h` → `ChangeLightXY` (L41), `AddUnLight` (L44); `monster.h` → `Monsters`, `ActiveMonsters`, `ActiveMonsterCount`, `Monster::isUnique()/corpseId/lightId/type()`, `LevelMonsterTypes`, `LevelMonsterTypeCount`, `CMonster::getAnimData()/type/corpseId`, `MonsterGraphic::Death` (L26, L38-50, L79-90); `tables/misdat.h` → `GetMissileSpriteData`, `MissileGraphicID::StoneCurseShatter` (L73); `AnimStruct`/`OptionalClxSpriteListOrSheet::emplace` (L25-33). Callers: `InitCorpses` from `diablo.cpp` L3160/L3290; `AddCorpse` from monster/effects code; `MoveLightsToCorpses` from level-load paths.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `InitCorpses()` slot allocation, in this exact order: (a) walk `LevelMonsterTypes[0..LevelMonsterTypeCount)`, skip any type whose `type` field already has an assigned corpse slot via a local `int8_t mtypes[MaxMonsters]` zero-initialised lookup table (L49-51, L58-60); (b) fill the next `Corpses[nd]` from that type's death animation, set `translationPaletteIndex = 0` (L63-65); (c) `++nd` (L66); (d) write back `monsterType.corpseId = nd` and `mtypes[monsterType.type] = nd` (L68-69) — so `corpseId` is the slot index *after* the increment, i.e. the next free slot.
  - (e) consume one slot for the "unused blood spatter" entry with a bare `nd++` and no data (L71); (f) the stone-curse shatter entry: sprites from `GetMissileSpriteData(MissileGraphicID::StoneCurseShatter).sprites` only when not headless (L73), then `frame = 11`, `width = 128`, `translationPaletteIndex = 0` (L74-76), `nd++` (L77); (g) `stonendx = nd` (L79).
  - (h) for each active monster in `ActiveMonsters` order, if `isUnique()`, build a corpse from its own type's death animation, `translationPaletteIndex = ActiveMonsters[i] + 1` (L86), `nd++` (L88), `monster.corpseId = nd` (L90).
  - (i) terminal `assert(unsigned(nd) <= MaxCorpses)` (L92).
  - Death-animation copy must keep the optional-sprite behaviour: if `animData.sprites` is null, `corpse.sprites = nullopt` (L27-31); `frame = animData.frames - 1` (L32); `width = animData.width` (L33).
  - `AddCorpse` writes the packed byte into `dCorpse` with no bounds check (L97).
  - `MoveLightsToCorpses`→`MoveLightToCorpse`: full linear scan `dx` outer / `dy` inner over the whole dungeon grid for the first cell whose low 5 bits equal `monster.corpseId`, `ChangeLightXY(monster.lightId, {dx,dy})` and return (L37-44); if no cell matches, `AddUnLight(monster.lightId)` (L46). Only unique monsters are considered (L103-105).
- 1:1 constraints: pack formula `dCorpse[x][y] = (dv & 0x1F) + (int(ddir) << 5)` (L97) — 5-bit corpse index, direction in bits 5-8, and the `& 0x1F` is what makes an out-of-range `dv` wrap to 0; match test `(dCorpse[dx][dy] & 0x1F) == monster.corpseId` (L38); scan order dx-then-dy with first-match-wins (L37-39); `MaxCorpses = 31` (dead.h L17); stone corpse `frame = 11`, `width = 128` (L74-75); unique `translationPaletteIndex = ActiveMonsters[i] + 1` (L86); `mtypes` sized `MaxMonsters` and zero-initialised (L49); the extra `nd++` for blood spatter (L71); `stonendx` assigned *between* the stone entry and the uniques (L79).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `Corpses` and `stonendx` are process globals written only by `InitCorpses()` and read by render + `MoveLightsToCorpses`; `InitCorpses` must run after `ActiveMonsters`/`ActiveMonsterCount` are settled (it is called right after `InitMonsters()`/`InitMissiles()` in `diablo.cpp` L3158-3160). The corpse *slot numbering* depends on monster-type order and the unique set, which upstream is RNG-derived → save/level compat hinges on reproducing the algorithm exactly. No RNG consumed here. `mtypes` is a stack array — no cross-call state. Single-threaded; render must not read `Corpses` during `InitCorpses`.
- Test coverage: `test/dead_test.cpp` (19 lines) — `Corpses.AddCorpse` asserts `dCorpse[21][48] == 8 + (int(Direction::West) << 5)` (L10-14) and `Corpses.AddCorpse_OOB` asserts `AddCorpse(..., MaxCorpses + 1, West)` masks the index to `0 + (West << 5)` (L16-19). `InitCorpses` and `MoveLightsToCorpses` are untested.
- Go mapping: `internal/dungeon` for `dCorpse` + `AddCorpse` (keeps the packing next to the grid) and `internal/monster` for the `Corpses`/`stonendx` sprite table + `InitCorpses`; `MoveLightsToCorpses` belongs with `internal/lighting` consumers. Strategy: `[MAXDUNX][MAXDUNY]uint8` grid, formula verbatim; `Corpse.Sprites` as a nil-able pointer type to model `OptionalClxSpriteListOrSheet`.
- Risks/open questions: `mtypes[monsterType.type]` uses `0` as "not yet assigned", so a monster type whose `type == 0` would be silently skipped — preserve, don't "fix", unless the port's type IDs start at 1. Does anything serialise `translationPaletteIndex` (it is only written here)? `MoveLightToCorpse`'s early `return` from inside nested loops must still skip `AddUnLight`.

### Source/dead.h
- Purpose: Declares the corpse record type, the global corpse table, and the three corpse entry points.
- Public API: `static constexpr unsigned MaxCorpses = 31` (L17); `struct Corpse { OptionalClxSpriteListOrSheet sprites; int frame; uint16_t width; uint8_t translationPaletteIndex; [[nodiscard]] ClxSpriteList spritesForDirection(Direction) const }` (L19-35, inline body L33); `extern Corpse Corpses[MaxCorpses]` (L37); `extern int8_t stonendx` (L38); `void InitCorpses()` (L40); `void AddCorpse(Point tilePosition, int8_t dv, Direction ddir)` (L41); `void MoveLightsToCorpses()` (L42).
- Depends on: `<cstddef>`/`<cstdint>` (L8-9), `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` (L11) for `ClxSpriteList`/`OptionalClxSpriteListOrSheet`, `engine/direction.hpp` (L12), `engine/point.hpp` (L13). Included by `dead.cpp`, `diablo.cpp` (L27), `effects.cpp`, `monster.cpp`, `panels/*`/`engine/render/*` that draw corpses, and `test/dead_test.cpp` (L3).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `const MaxCorpses = 31`, `var Corpses [MaxCorpses]Corpse`, `var StoneNDX int8`.
  - `type Corpse struct { Sprites *ClxSpriteListOrSheet; Frame int32; Width uint16; TranslationPaletteIndex uint8 }` — keep the field widths, since a port that later memcpy/serialises this array must match sizes.
  - `func (c *Corpse) SpritesForDirection(d Direction) ClxSpriteList` reproducing the variant dispatch: sheet ⇒ `sheet()[int(d)]`, else `list()` (L33). Documented valid range is `[0, 15]` (L28-30).
  - `AddCorpse` signature keeps `dv` as a signed 8-bit index (L41) so the `& 0x1F` masking semantics stay identical.
  - No new validation should be introduced: the C++ dereferences `sprites` unconditionally (L33) even though `dead.cpp` can leave it `nullopt`; a Go nil check that silently returns an empty sprite list would hide bugs.
- 1:1 constraints: `MaxCorpses = 31` (L17); `spritesForDirection` `static_cast<size_t>(direction)` indexing and the `isSheet() ? sheet()[i] : list()` ternary (L33); `int8_t` for `stonendx` and `dv` (L38, L41); `int frame` vs `uint16_t width` vs `uint8_t translationPaletteIndex` (L21-23).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `static constexpr` at namespace scope (no ODR/static-init hazard). The `extern` array is mutable process state written during level init and read from the render path — same single-threaded ordering assumption as dead.cpp.
- Test coverage: `test/dead_test.cpp` includes this header (L3) and uses `MaxCorpses` (its L17) for the masking case.
- Go mapping: place `Corpse`/`Corpses`/`AddCorpse` in `internal/dungeon`; `SpritesForDirection` needs the clx types, so the port must keep `ClxSpriteListOrSheet` in a leaf package (`internal/render/clx` or `internal/assets`) to avoid an import cycle with dungeon. Strategy: one small file, 1:1, no interface abstraction.
- Risks/open questions: Is `Direction` 0..15 in all levels, or does the sheet-vs-list distinction need the `isSheet()` runtime check the C++ performs? If the Go asset layer always loads sheets, the ternary can collapse — but only after verifying the corpse CLX format.

- Determinism/thread-safety notes: All state is debug-only mutable globals (`SelectedDebugGridTextItem`, `DebugMonsterId`, three search vectors, four `uint32_t[NUMLEVELS]` seed arrays indexed by `currlevel` — so reading them is only meaningful right after the corresponding level load). No RNG consumed, no tick coupling, but `GetDebugGridText`/`ShouldHighlightDebugAutomapTile` read live d-arrays and are called from the render path → must stay on the game thread. `PrintDebugMonster` writes to the player-message queue (`EventPlrMsg`), a shared side effect. Statics are zero-initialised at load; `glMid*Seed` are only filled via `SetDebugLevelSeedInfos`.
- Test coverage: none found — debug-only code, no test references `GetDebugGridText`/`ShouldHighlightDebugAutomapTile`.
- Go mapping: `internal/debug` with two files (`debug_on.go` `//go:build debug`, `debug_off.go` stubs returning false/no-op). Strategy: `DebugGridTextItem` as `uint16` with `iota` in the declared order; `GetDebugGridText` as a `switch` (not a map) to preserve fall-through-free ordering and the `blankValue` default; search lists as `[]string` with `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(name), needle)`.
- Risks/open questions: Should the Go port ship the debug overlay at all? If yes, the enum ordering becomes a UI contract (whatever menu enumerates `DebugGridTextItem` must match). `TestMapPath`, `DebugCoordsMap`, `debugTRN`, `DebugGodMode`, `DebugVision`, `DebugPath`, `DebugGrid`, `DebugScrollViewEnabled` are defined here but *not consumed* in this file — consumers live in `panels/`, `render/`, `init`; the port must keep them exported or those files break. `LoadCel("data\\square", 64)` assumes an MPQ-resident asset path with backslashes.

25 : 17` (L2712), `WM_DIABNEWGAME`/`WM_DIABLOADGAME` (L2713-2715); cursor range test `pcurs > CURSOR_HAND && pcurs < CURSOR_FIRSTITEM` (L418, L477, L3092); belt default keys `'1' + i` (L1848), quick-spell `SDLK_F5 + i` for `i < 4` (L1864), quick-message `SDLK_F9 + i` for `i < 4` (L2027), `INVITEM_BELT_FIRST + i` (L1852, L2172); `ToggleGameMenu1` = BACK+START (L2504) vs `ToggleGameMenu2` = START+BACK (L2513) — the two orderings are distinct registrations; stand-ground → `SDL_KMOD_SHIFT : SDL_KMOD_NONE` (L2432, L2439) and `RightMouseDown(standGround)` (L2458); full-grid `DungeonFlag::Lit` loops over `MAXDUNX`/`MAXDUNY` (L3240-3244); `memcpy(dLight, dPreLight, sizeof(dLight))` (L3204); `Q_BETRAYER._qvar2 = 2` (L3215); `currlevel == 24` Nakrul condition (L3387); `NaKrulTomeSequence = 0` (L3410); `SetDungeonMicros(pDungeonCels, MicroTileLen)` (L3421); `wait = sgGameInitInfo.nTickRate * 3 : 3` (L3492); `SfxID::DiabloDeath` (L3536).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: **Explicit tick coupling** — logic advances only when `nthread_has_500ms_passed(&drawGame)` (or demo mode) permits (L925), `game_loop` runs a burst of `nTickRate*3` on startup and `3` otherwise (L3492), and its inner break condition re-checks `nthread_has_500ms_passed()` (L3503); `gGameLogicStep` is mutated for the duration of each subsystem (L1529-1553) and read elsewhere for diagnostics. RNG is load-bearing and re-seeded **four** times in the level pipeline (`SetRndSeedForDungeonLevel` at L3325, L3365, L3409, L3430, defined L3097) and its LCG state is sampled at four points purely for debug bookkeeping (L3146, L3149, L3159, L3163) — reordering or removing any of these changes dungeon layout and monster HP, i.e. breaks vanilla parity and MP. Mutable process globals (`PauseMode`, `cineflag`, `gbProcessPlayers`, `gbLoadGame`, `gbRunGameResult`, `LastPlayerAction`, `sgbMouseDown`, `sgnTimeoutCurs`, `MousePosition`, `gbGameLoopStartup`, `GameWasAlreadyPaused`, `MinimizePaused`, `was_*_init`) are written from both the event handler and the tick path, so event pump and `GameLogic` must share one thread/goroutine. **Order-of-init**: `const auto OptionChangeHandlerLanguage = (…, true)` (L1813) registers an option callback during dynamic initialisation — the Go port must run this during bootstrap *before* `LoadOptions()` (called at L2770) or language changes silently do nothing. `DebugCmdsFromCommandLine` (L151) is consumed once and cleared (L897-902). `SdlLogFile` is a process-lifetime `FILE*` closed only in `diablo_quit` (L2739). MP guard: `IsAssetIntegrityViolated` aborts multiplayer with overridden `.lua/.tsv/.sol` (L905-907).
- Test coverage: `test/diablo_test.cpp` (14 lines) covers only `diablo_pause_game` unpausing `PauseMode 1 → 0` (L8-13); `DVL_API_FOR_TEST` symbols (`MousePosition`, `gbLoadGame`, `PauseMode`) exist for that link. Of ~90 functions in this file, 1 is unit-tested. Indirect coverage only: `test/drlg_l1..l4_test.cpp` exercise the level-generation functions `CreateLevel` wraps, and `test/pack_test.cpp`/`test/items_test.cpp`/`test/quests_test.cpp` exercise tables/quests this file initialises.
- Go mapping: split, do not mirror — `cmd/devilutiongo` (`DiabloMain`, `DiabloParseFlags`, help output, `diablo_quit`), `internal/game/state` (globals block), `internal/game/loop` (`RunGameLoop`, `game_loop`, `GameLogic`, `ProcessInput`, `TimeoutCursor`, `PrepareForFadeIn`), `internal/game/input` (mouse/key handlers + `GameEventHandler` + `DisableInputEventHandler`), `internal/input/keymap` + `internal/input/padmap` (`InitKeymapActions`/`InitPadmapActions` as data-driven action registries), `internal/game/session` (`StartGame`×2, `FreeGame`, `FreeGameMem`, `StartGame/RunGameLoop` glue, focus/pause/ESC), `internal/level/loader` (all `LoadGameLevel*` + `LoadLvlGFX`/`LoadAllGFX`/`CreateLevel`), `internal/game/actions` (`LeftMouseCmd`, `TryIconCurs`, `TryOpenDungeonWithMouse`, panel hotkeys, `CycleSpellHotkeys`), `internal/gamedata/branding` (`GetGameId`), `internal/monster/upkeep` (`UnstuckChargers`, `UpdateMonsterLights`). Strategy: inject a single `*Game` context instead of process globals so the loader and input layers are testable; keep the `LoadGameLevel` helper decomposition verbatim (it is already one-function-per-step, which is the port's best asset here); treat the key/pad registration lists as tables so the 250-line lambdas become named closures.
- Risks/open questions: (a) The whole input surface is SDL-typed (`SDL_Event`, `SDL_Keycode`, `SDL_KMOD_*`, `SDL_BUTTON_X1`, `SDL_LOG_PRIORITY_*`) and must be re-expressed over Ebiten — including the `KeymapperMouseButtonMask` synthetic-button encoding and `MouseScroll*Button` pseudo-keys, which have no Ebiten equivalent. (b) `DiabloMain`'s load order (L2760-2810: flags → keymap → padmap → `LoadCoreArchives` → `LoadOptions` → `LoadLanguageArchive` → `ApplicationInit` → `CheckArchivesUpToDate` → `LuaInitialize` → `LoadGameArchives` → `LoadTextData` → player/spell/missile/monster/item/object/quest data → `DiabloInit` → `SaveOptions` → `DiabloSplash` → `mainmenu_loop` → `DiabloDeinit`) is a hard contract; decide which optional subsystems (Lua/mods, Discord, demo/timedemo, screen reader, virtual gamepad, UWP/Vita hooks, gperftools hook) the Go port commits to, since each appears in this ordering. (c) `UnstuckChargers`' early `return` inside the player loop (L1489) means the Charge reset only runs when *no* other active player is on the level — looks like an upstream bug; preserve or fix? (d) `LoadGameLevelSetVisited` (L3229-3236) computes `visited` and discards it. (e) `extern void plrctrls_*()` (L160-162) is a cross-module cycle the port must break with callbacks. (f) Tick pacing (`nthread_has_500ms_passed`) must stay wall-clock based or MP compatibility and demo playback both drift. (g) `giNumberOfLevels`/`sgGameInitInfo.nTickRate` come from the network-init struct — needs the `multi`/`nthread` layer to exist before this file can be closed.

### Source/diablo.h
- Purpose: Public interface of the game shell: branding/game-id constants, the shared input/pause globals, and the two game-logic enums used across the codebase.
- Public API: `constexpr uint32_t GameIdDiabloFull = LoadBE32("DRTL")` (L31), `GameIdDiabloSpawn = LoadBE32("DSHR")` (L32), `GameIdGenericMod = LoadBE32("DXMD")` (L34); `[[nodiscard]] uint32_t GetGameId()` (L41); `enum clicktype : int8_t { CLICK_NONE, CLICK_LEFT, CLICK_RIGHT }` (L43-47); `enum class GameLogicStep : uint8_t { None, ProcessPlayers, ProcessMonsters, ProcessObjects, ProcessMissiles, ProcessItems, ProcessTowners, ProcessItemsTown, ProcessMissilesTown }` (L52-63); `enum class PlayerActionType : uint8_t { None, Walk, Spell, SpellMonsterTarget, SpellPlayerTarget, Attack, AttackMonsterTarget, AttackPlayerTarget, OperateObject }` (L64-75); externs `MousePosition` (L76), `gbRunGameResult` (L78), `ReturnToMainMenu` (L79), `gbProcessPlayers` (L80), `gbLoadGame` (L81), `cineflag` (L82), `extern void FontsCleanup()` (L84), `PauseMode` (L85), `sgbMouseDown` (L86), `gnTickDelay` (L87), `gszProductName[64]` (L88), `LastPlayerAction` (L90), `DebugDisableNetworkTimeout` (L118, `_DEBUG` only), `gGameLogicStep` (L124); function declarations `InitKeymapActions` (L92), `SetCursorPos` (L93), `FreeGameMem` (L94), `StartGame(bool,bool)` (L95), `diablo_quit` `[[noreturn]]` (L96), `DiabloMain(int,char**)` (L97), `TryIconCurs` (L98), `diablo_pause_game` (L99), `diablo_is_focused` (L100), `diablo_focus_pause` (L101), `diablo_focus_unpause` (L102), `PressEscKey` (L103), `DisableInputEventHandler` (L104), `LoadGameLevel` (L105), `IsDiabloAlive` (L106), `PrintScreen` (L107), `game_loop` (L112), `diablo_color_cyc_logic` (L113).
- Depends on: `SDL3/SDL_events.h` + `SDL3/SDL_keycode.h` or `SDL.h` (+ `utils/sdl2_to_1_2_backports.h` under `USE_SDL1`) — the declarations at L104/L107 take `SDL_Event`/`SDL_Keycode` (L10-19); `tables/monstdat.h` under `_DEBUG` (L21-23); `levels/gendung.h` (L24) for `Point`, `interface_mode`, `lvl_entry`; `utils/attributes.h` (L25) for `DVL_API_FOR_TEST`; `utils/endian_read.hpp` (L26) for `LoadBE32`; `std::expected` is used by the `LoadGameLevel` signature (L105) but pulled in transitively. Included across the tree (`dead.cpp` L10, `debug.h` L14, `debug.cpp`, `panels/*`, `engine/*`, `diablo.cpp` L37).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Branding ids as big-endian four-char codes and `GetGameId()` as the mod-aware accessor — documented as cosmetic (shown in the game browser / chat), *not* a compatibility check (L36-40), so a wrong value degrades MP listings rather than breaking joins.
  - `GameLogicStep` and `PlayerActionType` as `uint8` enums with the declared order — `PlayerActionType` drives click-and-hold repeat (`LastPlayerAction`) and `GameLogicStep` is read by error reporting, so the values are semantic.
  - `clicktype` as a signed 8-bit type with `CLICK_NONE = 0` (the mouse latch compares against it constantly).
  - The extern block becomes one shared mutable game-state surface (struct or package vars) exported to the rest of the port, including `FontsCleanup()` which is declared here but defined in the fonts module (comment L83) — do not redefine it.
  - `LoadGameLevel` keeps `expected<void, std::string>` → `error`; `diablo_quit` is `[[noreturn]]` → an `os.Exit`/panic path that still runs the teardown order in diablo.cpp L2733-2743.
  - SDL-typed signatures (`DisableInputEventHandler(const SDL_Event&, uint16_t modState)`, `PrintScreen(SDL_Keycode)`) must be re-declared over port-local event/key types.
  - `DVL_API_FOR_TEST` marks `MousePosition`, `gbLoadGame`, `PauseMode` (L76, L81, L85) as symbols the test binary links against — in Go this just means they must be exported.
- 1:1 constraints: `GameIdDiabloFull = LoadBE32("DRTL")` (L31), `GameIdDiabloSpawn = LoadBE32("DSHR")` (L32), `GameIdGenericMod = LoadBE32("DXMD")` (L34) — `LoadBE32` reads big-endian, so `"DRTL"` → `0x4452544C`, `"DSHR"` → `0x44534852`, `"DXMD"` → `0x44584D44`; `enum clicktype : int8_t` (L43); `GameLogicStep : uint8_t` order (L52-63, `ProcessMissilesTown` last at L61); `PlayerActionType : uint8_t` order (L64-75, `OperateObject` last at L73); `char gszProductName[64]` fixed size (L88); `[[noreturn]]` on `diablo_quit` (L96); `gnTickDelay` is `uint16_t` (L87); the `_DEBUG`-conditional `tables/monstdat.h` include (L21-23) and `DebugDisableNetworkTimeout` (L117-119); `USE_SDL3`/`USE_SDL1` conditional include block (L10-19).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `constexpr` branding ids carry no init order risk. The externs are the same mutable, single-threaded globals described for diablo.cpp. The conditional SDL include block means this header's *type surface* changes per build configuration — an include-order/ODR hazard the Go port removes by not exposing SDL types at all. `debug.h` includes `diablo.h` (for `NUMLEVELS`) while `diablo.cpp` includes `debug.h`, i.e. a header-level dependency the port must break at a leaf constants package.
- Test coverage: `test/diablo_test.cpp` includes this header (L3) and asserts `diablo_pause_game` → `PauseMode == 0` (L8-13). `GetGameId()` is not covered here; mod identity is exercised in `test/mod_identity_test.cpp`, which should be checked when porting the branding logic.
- Go mapping: three targets — `internal/gamedata/branding` (`GameId*` + `GetGameId`), `internal/game/state` (the enums + globals as a `Game` struct or package vars), `internal/game` + `cmd/devilutiongo` (entry points). Strategy: define port-local `Event`/`Keycode`/`ModState`/`Button` types in `internal/input` so no SDL type crosses a package boundary; keep `const` + typed enums to preserve numeric order.
- Risks/open questions: Confirm the Go port reads the four-char codes big-endian exactly (a swapped read silently mis-brands MP sessions and would let a mod impersonate `DRTL`). Does anything persist `GameLogicStep`/`PlayerActionType` numerically (save/demo format) or are they in-memory only? `interface_mode` and `lvl_entry` values (used by `StartGame`/`LoadGameLevel`) live in `levels/gendung.h` and must be ported there with identical numbering, including `WM_DIAB*` and `ENTRY_*`.

# vol3-010.md

# Volume III — batch 010

### Source/diablo_msg.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the queued in-game popup message system ("shrine texts", save/load notices, etc.) — a deque of {text, durationMs} entries rendered inside a bordered translucent box, auto-advancing when the duration expires.
- Public API: `void InitDiabloMsg(diablo_message e, uint32_t duration=3500)`; `void InitDiabloMsg(std::string_view msg, uint32_t duration=3500)`; `bool IsDiabloMsgAvailable()`; `void CancelCurrentDiabloMsg()`; `void ClrDiabloMsg()`; `void DrawDiabloMsg(const Surface &out)`; global `const char *const MsgStrings[]` (index-aligned with `diablo_message` enum).
- Depends on: `WordWrapString`, `GetLineWidth`, `GetLineHeight`, `GameFont12` (engine/render/text_render.hpp); `SplitByChar` (utils/str_split.hpp); `c_find_if` (utils/algorithm/container.hpp); `LanguageTranslate`/`N_`/`_` (utils/language.h); `pSTextSlidCels` sprite (extern — declared in control.h, data from items\text.slidcels via gendung/ctrl); `RenderClxSprite` (engine/render/clx_render.hpp); `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo` (engine/render/primitive_render.hpp); `DrawString`, `UiFlags::AlignCenter` (DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp, text_render); `SDL_GetTicks` (SDL_timer).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Message queue is a FIFO; duplicate texts are rejected (push only if no equal entry already queued).
  - When a message becomes the front (push into empty queue, cancel, or expiry-pop), layout is recomputed lazily: wrap at width, measure line height, compute outer height, stamp start time with a tick counter.
  - Duration default 3500ms; expiry checked inside Draw (draw first, then pop+advance if elapsed >= front.duration).
  - Box drawing: 12x12 CLX border pieces from pSTextSlidCels indices 0..7 in fixed roles (TL corner=0, BL=1, BR=2, TR=3, top=4, left=5, bottom=6, right=7), tiled every 12px via subregion-clipped loops; inner area filled with half-transparent black rect; text centered horizontally and vertically within inner rect.
  - All MsgStrings entries (56, incl. index 0 = "") must be ported verbatim for translation lookup by `diablo_message` enum.
- 1:1 constraints: LineWidth starts 418 and is grown to max(418, GetLineWidth(text)) per wrapped line (L51-54); OuterHeight = TextLines.size()*LineHeight + 42 (L61); borderPartWidth=borderPartHeight=12, textPaddingX=5, borderThickness=3 (L83-88); outerHeight=min(out.h(),OuterHeight), outerWidth=min(out.w(), LineWidth+2*3+5) (L90-91); textY starts at innerYBegin+((innerHeight-LineHeight*nLines)/2) (L145); default duration 3500 (header L74/76); enum→string order in MsgStrings must exactly match `diablo_message` (hpp L16-71, cpp L64-119).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: File-scope mutable statics (DiabloMessages deque, msgStartTime, TextLines, OuterHeight, LineWidth, LineHeight). No locking — single-threaded UI/game loop only. Timing via SDL_GetTicks (wall clock); Go port should use a game tick or monotonic clock source consistent with the rest of the port.
- Test coverage: none found (no test file references InitDiabloMsg/DrawDiabloMsg).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/gamemessage` (or internal/msgq): a `Queue` struct with `Init(e MsgID, dur)`, `InitText(s, dur)`, `Available()`, `CancelCurrent()`, `Clear()`, `Draw(target)`; MsgStrings table as `[56]string` keyed by enum.
- Risks/open questions: pSTextSlidCels asset loading belongs to control.cpp — Go port needs an equivalent border sprite set or a drawn 3px-border fallback replicating metrics; note the wrap-width quirk: text wraps at 418 but LineWidth can exceed it if a single word is wider (keeps box from clipping).

### Source/discord/discord.cpp
- Purpose: Discord Rich Presence integration — builds activity strings from player/dungeon state, pushes updates when tracked PlayerData changes, and runs Discord callbacks; compiled only with DISCORD defined (else header stubs).
- Public API: (via header) `discord_manager::UpdateGame()`, `StartGame()`, `UpdateMenu(bool forced=false)`; file-local: GetLocationString/GetCharacterString/GetDetailString/GetStateString/GetTooltipString/GetPlayerAssetString/ResetStartTime/GetIconAsset; globals: discord_core (lazy IIFE-init), want_menu_update, tracked_data, start_time.
- Depends on: discord-game-sdk (discordsrc-src/cpp/discord.h); config.h (PROJECT_NAME, gszProductName); levels/gendung.h (leveltype, dungeon_type, DTYPE_*); levels/setmaps.h (setlevel, setlvlnum, QuestLevelNames, _setlevels); multi.h (sgGameInitInfo.nDifficulty); player.h (MyPlayer, _pName, _pgfxnum, Players); tables/playerdat.hpp (GetPlayerSpriteDataForClass().classChar, ArmourChar, WepChar); utils/language.h (_); utils/format.hpp (FormatRuntime); utils/str_cat.hpp (StrCat); lua/lua_global.hpp (AddModsChangedHandler → UpdateMenu(true)); panels/charpanel.hpp (getClassName/getCharacterLevel).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Activity update fires only when (dungeonArea, dungeonLevel, playerLevel, playerGfx) tuple changes — note operator!= omits questMap despite it being stored.
  - Game activity: name=PROJECT_NAME, state="{difficulty} difficulty", details="Lv {lvl} {class} - {dungeon} {floor}", instance=true, start timestamp = game/menu start, largeImage=player asset string, largeText=tooltip, smallImage=icon, smallText=gszProductName; callbacks must be pumped (RunCallbacks) on every update call.
  - Menu activity: state "In Menu", icon large image; only re-sent when want_menu_update or forced; ResetStartTime only when not forced (game start vs menu re-entry).
  - Location string: quest map name if setlevel; dungeon name from DTYPE table {None/Town/Cathedral/Catacombs/Caves/Hell/Nest/Crypt}; level number adjusted: Nest −16, Crypt −20; empty dungeonLevel → name only.
  - Player asset: 5-char string {classChar, ArmourChar[playerGfx>>4], WepChar[playerGfx&0xF], 'a', 's'}.
  - Nil-safe: all functions no-op when core creation failed (discord_core==nullptr).
  - Mods-changed Lua hook forces menu update (registered once at static init via comma-override trick).
- 1:1 constraints: App ID 795760213524742205 (L41); DungeonStrs table order {Town,Cathedral,Catacombs,Caves,Hell,Nest,Crypt} indexed by dungeon_type (L80); DifficultyStrs {Normal,Nightmare,Hell} (L99); level adjustments: DTYPE_NEST→-16, DTYPE_CRYPT→-20 (L91-93); asset chars at shift 4 / mask 0xF (L115-116); icon "hellfire" vs "icon" by gbIsHellfire (L131).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: static-init IIFE creates the Discord core before main (order-of-init coupling with SDK); start_time from system_clock (wall clock, not game ticks); mutable globals want_menu_update/tracked_data — called from game loop, assume single thread.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/discord` package; in Go the build-tag/stub split becomes either an interface with a noop impl or a separate `//go:build discord` file. Use a Go Discord RPC library or the game-sdk via cgo — flag as integration risk.
- Risks/open questions: game-sdk is C++ w/ static lib; Go will need an IPC implementation of Discord's RPC (pipe-based) or cgo binding. The `operator!=` ignoring questMap looks intentional-ish but should be replicated or consciously fixed (replicate for 1:1).

### Source/dvlnet/base.cpp
- Purpose: Core turn-based multiplayer logic shared by all real transports: message queue, turn queues per player with sequence-number synchronization, join-accept handling, disconnect propagation, echo-based latency measurement, and the SNet* entry points.
- Public API: class `base` (see base.h): SNetReceiveMessage/SNetSendMessage/SNetReceiveTurns/SNetSendTurn/SNetGetProviderCaps/SNetRegister(Unregister)EventHandler/SNetLeaveGame/SNetDropPlayer/SNetGetOwnerTurnsWaiting/SNetGetTurnsInTransit/process_network_packets/setup_gameinfo/setup_password/clear_password/get_latencies; protected: Connect, RecvLocal, RunEventHandler, SendEchoRequest, DisconnectNet (no-op here), IsConnected; private: GetOwner, AllTurnsArrived, MakeReady, SendTurnIfReady, SendFirstTurnIfReady, ClearMsg, Handle{Accept,Connect,Turn,Disconnect,EchoRequest,EchoReply}.
- Depends on: dvlnet/packet.h (packet_factory, packet, PT_* types, turn_t{SequenceNumber,Value}, cookie_t, seq_t, PLR_BROADCAST/PLR_MASTER, packet_out::GenerateCookie); multi.h (Players, MAX_PLRS, GameData, GameInfo); storm/storm_net.hpp (_SNETCAPS, _SNETEVENT, EVENT_TYPE_PLAYER_CREATE_GAME/PLAYER_LEAVE_GAME, SNPLAYER_OTHERS, PS_CONNECTED/PS_ACTIVE/PS_TURN_ARRIVED); player.h (Players.size); SDL_GetTicks; utils/log (LogVerbose/LogError/LogDebug implied).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - RecvLocal dispatch: PT_MESSAGE→queue {sender,payload}; PT_TURN→HandleTurn (push to that player's deque + MakeReady(seq)); PT_JOIN_ACCEPT→HandleAccept (adopt plr_self if cookie matches; if info != game_init_info and size==sizeof(GameData), adopt info and fire EVENT_TYPE_PLAYER_CREATE_GAME); PT_CONNECT→Connect(newPlayer); PT_DISCONNECT→HandleDisconnect (self→error "We were dropped by the owner?"; connected player→fire EVENT_TYPE_PLAYER_LEAVE_GAME with leaveinfo, DisconnectNet, ClearMsg, mark disconnected, clear turnQueue); PT_ECHO_REQUEST→reply with same timestamp; PT_ECHO_REPLY→roundTripLatency = now − sent time (guard src < MAX_PLRS).
  - SNetReceiveMessage: every ≥5s (or first call) send echo requests to all players, then poll, then pop one queued message (false if empty). Returns pointer into message_last — Go must return a copy/slice.
  - SNetSendMessage: dest SNPLAYER_OTHERS→broadcast; abort() if dest>=MAX_PLRS and not OTHERS; self-send enqueues locally and does NOT also network-send to self; network path builds PT_MESSAGE and sends, logging+false on error.
  - Turn sync (the heart): each player has deque of {seq,value}; SNetReceiveTurns polls, then per connected player discards turns with `seq - current_turn > 0x7F` (8-bit wrap window); if every connected player has ≥1 queued turn, pop front turn for each connected player where front.seq == current_turn, expose value as int32 in data[i] with status PS_CONNECTED|PS_ACTIVE|PS_TURN_ARRIVED and size=4, then current_turn++ and return true; else set PS_ACTIVE for players with any queued turn and return false.
  - SNetSendTurn: size must be 4 (ABORT otherwise); turn {seq=next_turn++, value=memcpy int32}; push to own queue and SendTurnIfReady.
  - SendTurnIfReady: while awaiting sequence number and not game host, stay silent (joiner waits for host seq via MakeReady); else send PT_TURN broadcast.
  - MakeReady(seq) (triggered by first received turn / join-accept flow): sets current_turn=next_turn=seq, clears awaiting flag, renumbers all queued own turns from seq upward and sends them.
  - SNetGetProviderCaps: fixed values (see constraints).
  - SNetLeaveGame: send PT_DISCONNECT(self,broadcast,self,type) then plr_self=PLR_BROADCAST.
  - SNetDropPlayer: build PT_DISCONNECT(self,broadcast,target,flags), DisconnectNet(target) FIRST (so they don't receive their own drop), send, then RecvLocal the packet locally to run local disconnect path.
  - GetOwner: lowest connected plr index (PLR_BROADCAST if none).
  - get_latencies: echoLatency = tracked roundTripLatency of playerid.
  - setup_password/clear_password recreate packet_factory with/without password (crypto context).
- 1:1 constraints: echo interval `now - lastEchoTime > 5000` with `if (now==0) now++` guard (L242-248); turn discard window `diff <= 0x7F` breaks, i.e. drop when diff > 0x7F (L318-322); caps: size=0, flags=0, maxmessagesize=512, maxqueuesize=0, maxplayers=MAX_PLRS, bytessec=1000000, latencyms=0, defaultturnssec=10, defaultturnsintransit=2 (L449-459); turn value size sizeof(int32_t)=4 (L349); current_turn increment only on full-arrival success path (L334); join-accept requires `info.size() == sizeof(GameData)` else ABORT (L98-100).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: timing via SDL_GetTicks for echo/latency only — not game logic. seq_t is a wrapping counter (uint8 per packet.h) — arithmetic wraps; Go must use uint8 math to preserve the 0x7F window. Single-threaded assumption: SNet* called from game loop; poll() from transports must be synchronized in Go if transport goroutines exist — recommend one goroutine owning all state (actor pattern) or a mutex in base.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `pkg/dvlnet/base.go` — `type baseNet struct` embedding a `Net` interface with unimplemented hooks (poll/send/IsGameHost as abstract methods). turn_t → struct{Seq uint8; Value int32}. Keep exact constants.
- Risks/open questions: `status[i]`/`data[i]` indexed by Players.size() (may exceed MAX_PLRS arrays? Players is vector sized MAX_PLRS — verify in multi.cpp port). message_t default ctor sets sender=-1 (uint8 wraps to 255) — irrelevant in Go but note. awaitingSequenceNumber_ initial true means even hosts start silent until first Connect — actually SendTurnIfReady flips it for hosts (`awaitingSequenceNumber_ = !IsGameHost()`), preserving that host sends immediately.

### Source/dvlnet/base_protocol.h
- Purpose: Header-only template `base_protocol<P>` — generic UDP-ish (ZeroTier-style) mesh transport over any P providing endpoint/send/recv/oob: game discovery (info request/reply), join handshake with cookie, peer introduction (PT_CONNECT addrinfo exchange), send-queue drain after echo handshake, master election, disconnect handling.
- Public API: overrides create/join/poll/send/DisconnectNet/SNetLeaveGame/make_default_gamename/send_info_request/clear_gamelist/get_gamelist/get_latencies; internals: get_master, wait_network, wait_firstpeer, wait_join, InitiateHandshake, SendTo, recv, handle_join_request, recv_decrypted, recv_ingame, DrainSendQueue, is_recognized; state: proto P, firstpeer, gamename, game_list map<string,{GameData, playerNames, endpoint}>, peers[MAX_PLRS] {endpoint, sendQueue deque<packet>}, isGameHost_.
- Depends on: dvlnet/base.h, dvlnet/packet.h (PT_INFO_REQUEST/REPLY, PT_JOIN_REQUEST/ACCEPT, PT_CONNECT, PT_ECHO_*, PLR_MASTER/PLR_BROADCAST, packet_out::GenerateCookie, Cookie(), NewPlayer(), Info(), LeaveInfo()); player.h (Players, _pName, plractive, PlayerNameLength); multi.h (GameData, SwapGameDataLE, MAX_PLRS); utils/algorithm/container.hpp (c_sort); utils/is_of.hpp (IsAnyOf); utils/log.hpp; SDL_Delay/SDL_GetTicks; P protocol concept: endpoint (bool-convertible, serialize/unserialize, operator==), send/send_oob/send_oob_mc/recv/get_disconnected/network_online/peers_ready/is_peer_connected/disconnect/get_latency_to/is_peer_relayed/make_default_gamename.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - create: gamename=addr, isGameHost=true, wait_network (5s), plr_self=0, Connect(0). join: gamename=addr, host=false, wait_network, wait_firstpeer (poll game_list via info requests, 5s), wait_join (send PT_JOIN_REQUEST{cookie, game_init_info} to firstpeer, poll 5s until plr_self assigned).
  - get_master: min(plr_self, lowest i with peers[i].endpoint set).
  - send: broadcast → SendTo all players; dest>=MAX_PLRS error; dest==self no-op; else SendTo. SendTo: queue packet on peer.sendQueue unless it's ECHO_REQUEST/ECHO_REPLY (handshake packets pass through); send via proto.
  - recv loop: drain proto.recv until empty; malformed/undecryptable packet → disconnect sender + log; then process proto.get_disconnected → map endpoint back to player and DisconnectNet.
  - recv_decrypted: INFO_REPLY (broadcast→master): parse GameData (size check `gameData.size == sizeof(GameData)` after SwapGameDataLE), then MAX_PLRS fixed PlayerNameLength name slots (NUL-trimmed, skip empty), then trailing game name; store in game_list. Else recv_ingame.
  - recv_ingame: (broadcast,master,JOIN_REQUEST) → host-side handle_join_request; (broadcast,master,INFO_REQUEST) → only master replies with buf = game_init_info + name slots (active players' _pName, zeroed for inactive) + gamename, sent OOB. (master, PT_CONNECT) must come from recognized endpoint; unserialize endpoint into peers[newPlayer], create sendQueue, Connect, and (if we're in-game, plr_self != BROADCAST) InitiateHandshake. Normal packets: source>=MAX_PLRS → drop; JOIN_ACCEPT only accepted from firstpeer (adopts peers[src].endpoint=sender, clears firstpeer); any other source must match peers[src].endpoint or drop; destination must be self or broadcast; then RecvLocal; after join (wasBroadcast→assigned), handshake-initiate to all players; finally DrainSendQueue(pkt.Source()).
  - handle_join_request (host): assign first free peer slot != plr_self (full → ignore); Connect; then for each other connected peer j: send PT_CONNECT(i, senderinfo) to j AND PT_CONNECT(j, peer_j.serialize()) to the new sender (pairwise introduction); then PT_JOIN_ACCEPT{cookie, i, game_init_info} to sender (must be LAST so new player knows all peers first); then DrainSendQueue(i).
  - InitiateHandshake: only if (plr_self < player || proto.is_peer_connected) → SendEchoRequest — avoids simultaneous TCP-style connect collisions.
  - DrainSendQueue: flush and free the queue (post-handshake).
  - is_recognized: firstpeer or any peers[].endpoint (note loop `player <= MAX_PLRS` — off-by-one harmless since array is MAX_PLRS but bounds-checked UB-free in practice; replicate as < MAX_PLRS in Go).
  - SNetLeaveGame: base leave + one recv().
  - get_gamelist: recv, map over game_list, attach proto latency + relayed flag, sort by name (c_sort with a.name < b.name).
- 1:1 constraints: wait loops 500 iterations × SDL_Delay(10ms) = 5s for network/firstpeer/join (L97-104,121-131,169-176); INFO buffer layout: game_init_info bytes ‖ MAX_PLRS × PlayerNameLength name slots ‖ gamename bytes; neededSize = sizeof(GameData) + PlayerNameLength*MAX_PLRS (L373); GameData validation `gameData.size != sizeof(GameData)` after SwapGameDataLE (L383-384); handshake gating `plr_self < player || proto.is_peer_connected(...)` (L231-233); echo-packet types bypass sendQueue (L252-254); PT_JOIN_ACCEPT strictly after all PT_CONNECTs (comment L296-297); master info reply gated on `plr_self != PLR_BROADCAST && get_master() == plr_self` (L410-411).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: blocking waits with SDL_Delay run on the game thread (UI will freeze up to 15s worst case in join) — Go port should keep this synchronous-on-goroutine behavior or consciously move to async with identical timeouts. game_list mutated by recv() from same thread only. cookie via packet_out::GenerateCookie (RNG-dependent — must match packet.cpp port for interop).
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `pkg/dvlnet/baseproto.go` as a generic `[P Protocol] struct` (Go generics) embedding baseNet; Protocol interface with the endpoint concept (comparable, Serialize/Unmarshal). Same packet layout expectations; keep 5s/10ms loops.
- Risks/open questions: `is_recognized` loop bound `<= MAX_PLRS` reads one past logical peers (array bounds MAX_PLRS so last iteration compares against default endpoint) — replicate semantics carefully (in Go just iterate 0..MAX_PLRS-1 plus note). Interop with C++ clients requires byte-exact packet.cpp + protocol_zt serialization — cross-verified in those files' entries.

### Source/dvlnet/cdwrap.cpp
- Purpose: cdwrap ("connection-drop wrapper") implementation — owns an inner abstract_net created by a factory function, rebuilds it on create/join (reconnect support), and forwards every SNet* call through while persisting registered event handlers, game_init_info, and password across resets.
- Public API: class cdwrap (see cdwrap.h): create/join/process_network_packets/setup_gameinfo/SNetReceiveMessage/SNetSendMessage/SNetReceiveTurns/SNetSendTurn/SNetGetProviderCaps/SNetUnregisterEventHandler/SNetRegisterEventHandler/SNetLeaveGame/SNetDropPlayer/SNetGetOwnerTurnsWaiting/SNetGetTurnsInTransit/make_default_gamename/send_info_request/clear_gamelist/get_gamelist/setup_password/clear_password/get_latencies; private reset().
- Depends on: dvlnet/cdwrap.h (make_net_fn_ tl::function_ref factory, game_pw optional<string>, registered_handlers map, game_init_info buffer); abstract_net interface.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - reset(): drop old inner net; construct new via factory; replay setup_gameinfo; replay password (setup_password if set else clear_password); re-register all stored event handlers.
  - create(addr): reset() then inner.create. join(addr): clear game_init_info to empty buffer, reset(), inner.join (info will be relearned from join-accept).
  - setup_gameinfo stores buffer AND forwards if inner exists (always exists post-ctor since ctor calls reset).
  - register/unregister handler: update local map and forward (unregister returns true when no inner — inner is never null in practice).
  - setup_password/clear_password: store pw (or clear) and forward.
  - All other methods are pure forwarders.
- 1:1 constraints: join clears game_init_info before reset (L41-42) — required so the wrapper doesn't push stale info into the new connection; handler replay order is map iteration order (unordered) — Go map iteration is random; use a slice or sorted registration to be deterministic if order matters (it doesn't functionally — handlers are keyed by distinct event types).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: wrapper state (game_init_info, game_pw, handlers) mutated on game thread only; forwarding is shallow — inner net's own thread rules apply.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `pkg/dvlnet/cdwrap.go` — struct with `factory func() Net`, embeds nothing, implements Net by delegation; store handlers as map[eventType]Handler plus deterministic replay (order irrelevant, but document).
- Risks/open questions: tl::function_ref means the factory must outlive wrapper — Go closures make this a non-issue.

### Source/dvlnet/cdwrap.h
- Purpose: Header-only wrapper (CD-style "connection drop" wrapper) around an inner `abstract_net` implementation; holds per-connection state (registered event handlers, game init info, password) and transparently rebuilds the inner network object, restoring that state, via a `make_net_fn_` factory callback.
- Public API: `class cdwrap : public abstract_net` — ctor `explicit cdwrap(tl::function_ref<std::unique_ptr<abstract_net>()> makeNetFn)`; overrides: `int create(std::string_view)`, `int join(std::string_view)`, `bool SNetReceiveMessage(uint8_t *sender, void **data, size_t *size)`, `bool SNetSendMessage(uint8_t dest, void *data, size_t size)`, `bool SNetReceiveTurns(char **data, size_t *size, uint32_t *status)`, `bool SNetSendTurn(char *data, size_t size)`, `void SNetGetProviderCaps(struct _SNETCAPS *)`, `bool SNetRegisterEventHandler(event_type, SEVTHANDLER)`, `bool SNetUnregisterEventHandler(event_type)`, `bool SNetLeaveGame(net::leaveinfo_t)`, `bool SNetDropPlayer(int, net::leaveinfo_t)`, `bool SNetGetOwnerTurnsWaiting(uint32_t *)`, `bool SNetGetTurnsInTransit(uint32_t *)`, `void process_network_packets()`, `void setup_gameinfo(buffer_t)`, `std::string make_default_gamename()`, `bool send_info_request()`, `void clear_gamelist()`, `std::vector<GameInfo> get_gamelist()`, `void setup_password(std::string)`, `void clear_password()`, `DvlNetLatencies get_latencies(uint8_t)`; private `void reset()`. Implementation lives in cdwrap-inline via header (cdwrap impl is in this header's .inc? — no .cpp in batch; all method bodies are declared here, defined elsewhere, e.g. `Source/dvlnet/cdwrap.cpp` exists but is not part of this batch — only this header was read).
- Depends on: `abstract_net` (base class, `dvlnet/abstract_net.h`); `SEVTHANDLER`, `event_type` (storm_net.hpp); `buffer_t`, `GameInfo`, `DvlNetLatencies`, `leaveinfo_t` (dvlnet namespace via abstract_net.h/packet.h chain); `ankerl::unordered_dense::map`, `tl::function_ref` (3rd-party headers).

### Source/dvlnet/frame_queue.cpp
- Purpose: Implementation of the length-prefixed frame codec used by every transport: byte-stream ↔ packet reassembly with an internal `std::deque<buffer_t>` of incoming chunks; `MakeFrame` produces wire frames `[u32 LE size|flags][payload]`.
- Public API: (all methods of `frame_queue` from frame_queue.h) `framesize_t Size() const` (private), `std::expected<buffer_t, PacketError> Read(framesize_t s)` (private), `PacketReady()`, `ReadPacketFlags()`, `ReadPacket()`, `Write(buffer_t)`, static `MakeFrame(buffer_t packetbuf, uint16_t flags = 0)`.
- Depends on: `frame_queue.h` (class def, `frame_size_mask`, `max_frame_size`); `PacketError` (`dvlnet/packet.h`); `LoadLE32`/`WriteLE32` (`utils/endian_read.hpp` / `utils/endian_write.hpp`); `buffer_t` = `std::vector<unsigned char>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Byte-buffer queue type: chunks appended by `Write`, consumed by `Read(s)` which drains whole front chunks while they fit, then splits a partially-consumed front chunk.
  - `current_size` tracks total buffered bytes; `nextsize` holds the current expected frame header value.
  - `PacketReady()`: if `nextsize == 0`, require ≥4 bytes, read u32 LE → nextsize; `nextsize == 0` → error "Incorrect frame size"; then return `Size() >= nextsize & 0xFFFF`.
  - `ReadPacketFlags()`: `uint16(nextsize >> 16)`.
  - `ReadPacket()`: `packetSize = nextsize & frame_size_mask`; error if `nextsize==0` or `Size() < packetSize`; read, set `nextsize = 0`.
  - `MakeFrame(buf, flags)`: error if `len > 0xFFFF`; emits 4-byte LE `size | (u32(flags) << 16)` then payload verbatim.
  - Error strings: "Incorrect frame size", "Buffer exceeds maximum frame size" — keep or map to typed errors.
- 1:1 constraints: `frame_size_mask = 0xFFFF`, `max_frame_size = 0xFFFF`, `framesize_t = uint32` (frame_queue.h lines 18-21); header layout `size | (flags<<16)` written LE32 (MakeFrame, lines 74-85 of .cpp); `PacketReady` zero-size rejection (line 50-52); `Read` must consume in deque-chunk order, splitting only the front chunk (lines 20-41).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: not thread-safe (single-threaded per-socket use in tcp_client/protocol_zt). No RNG, no statics besides anonymous-namespace error helper. No tick coupling — driven by socket receive callbacks.
- Test coverage: none found in test/ (no frame_queue test file).
- Go mapping: `internal/net` package — `type FrameQueue struct` with `chunks [][]byte`, `currentSize, nextSize uint32`; methods `Write`, `PacketReady`, `ReadPacketFlags`, `ReadPacket`, `MakeFrame`. Use `encoding/binary.LittleEndian`. Return `error`/typed `NetError` instead of std::expected.
- Risks/open questions: none — self-contained pure logic, easiest file to port first and unit-test.

### Source/dvlnet/leaveinfo.hpp
- Purpose: Defines the `leaveinfo_t` enum passed on game-leave/drop events, mirroring original Storm/Devilution codes.
