### Source/dvlnet/packet.cpp
- Purpose: Packet-layer runtime: cookie generation (libsodium random when PACKET_ENCRYPTION, else seeded std::mt19937-style engine), packet-type error formatting, `packet` field accessors with type validation, `packet_in::Create` (plaintext parse path), and (conditional) `packet_in::Decrypt` / `packet_out::Encrypt` using NaCl secretbox; `packet_factory` ctors derive the Argon2id key from the game password.
- Public API: `const char *packet_type_to_string(uint8_t)`; `PacketError PacketTypeError(uint8_t)`; `PacketError PacketTypeError(std::initializer_list<packet_type>, uint8_t)`; `packet::{Data,Type,Source,Destination,Message,Turn,Cookie,NewPlayer,Time,Info,LeaveInfo}`; `packet_in::{Create,Decrypt}`; `packet_out::{GenerateCookie,Encrypt}`; `packet_factory::{packet_factory(), packet_factory(std::string pw)}`.
- Depends on: `dvlnet/packet.h` (all templates/types); `<sodium.h>` (crypto_secretbox_*, crypto_pwhash_argon2id_*, randombytes_buf, sodium_init) when PACKET_ENCRYPTION; `<chrono>`, `<random>` otherwise; `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (`c_none_of`); `utils/str_cat.hpp` (StrCat/StrAppend); `appfat.h` (ABORT).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `GenerateCookie()`: with encryption → 4 crypto-random bytes; without → uniform uint32 from time-seeded engine (non-portable, need only "random cookie" semantics in Go: crypto/rand regardless is acceptable, but note compat constraint below).
  - `packet_type_to_string`: map 0x01→"PT_MESSAGE", 0x02→"PT_TURN", 0x11→"PT_JOIN_REQUEST", 0x12→"PT_JOIN_ACCEPT", 0x13→"PT_CONNECT", 0x14→"PT_DISCONNECT", 0x21→"PT_INFO_REQUEST", 0x22→"PT_INFO_REPLY", 0x31→"PT_ECHO_REQUEST", 0x32→"PT_ECHO_REPLY", else nil.
  - `PacketTypeError(expected[], actual)`: exact message format "Expected packet of type A or B or C, gotD" (note: no space after "got").
  - Field accessors assert decrypted and validate type via allowed-type sets: Message∈{PT_MESSAGE}, Turn∈{PT_TURN}, Cookie∈{JOIN_REQUEST,JOIN_ACCEPT}, NewPlayer∈{JOIN_ACCEPT,CONNECT,DISCONNECT}, Time∈{ECHO_REQUEST,ECHO_REPLY}, Info∈{JOIN_REQUEST,JOIN_ACCEPT,CONNECT,INFO_REPLY}, LeaveInfo∈{DISCONNECT}.
  - `packet_in::Create(buf)`: reject if `len < 1 + 2` (sizeof(packet_type)+2*sizeof(plr_t) = 3); sets decrypted AND encrypted buffer to same bytes (server forwarding).
  - Encrypt path: nonce = crypto_secretbox_NONCEBYTES (24) random bytes prepended; ciphertext = secretbox_easy(mac 16 + ciphertext) appended; Decrypt path mirrors with crypto_secretbox_open_easy; min length check `24 + 16 + 3`.
  - `packet_factory(pw)`: clamp pw to [crypto_pwhash_argon2id_PASSWD_MIN(16), PASSWD_MAX(0xFFFFFFFF..)] by resize with NULs; fixed salt string "W9bE9dQgVaeybwr2" zero-extended to 16 bytes (crypto_pwhash_argon2id_SALTBYTES); derive key with Argon2id13, opslimit = 3*OPSLIMIT_MIN(=1 → 3), memlimit = 2*MEMLIMIT_MIN(=8192 KiB? actual constant from libsodium) — cite values; `sodium_init()<0` → abort; `secure = true`.
  - `PacketError` default message "Incorrect packet size".
- 1:1 constraints: salt `"W9bE9dQgVaeybwr2"` (line ~205 of packet.cpp, packet_factory(std::string)); opslimit factor 3×, memlimit factor 2× of the argon2id _MIN constants (lines ~206-209); cookie = uniform over full uint32 range; min plaintext packet = 3 bytes (line ~149); type-to-string table (lines ~44-65); error message formats: `"Unknown packet type N"`, `"Expected packet of type X or ..., gotY"` (lines ~67-85); unencrypted cookie generator seeds `std::default_random_engine` with `system_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count()` (lines ~28-45) — Go may use crypto/rand; cross-build packet compat with the C++ unencrypted path does not depend on cookie values (cookies only need uniqueness per session).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `CookieGenerator` is a file-scope mutable global with lazy time seed (unencrypted builds) — in Go use a package-level sync-safe rng or crypto/rand. Packet objects are single-threaded per connection. `packet_factory` key derivation is deterministic given pw (needed so server/clients agree).
- Test coverage: none found in test/ for packet.cpp.
- Go mapping: `internal/net/packet.go` — `type Packet struct{...}` with fields Type, Src, Dst uint8, Message []byte, Turn Turn, Cookie uint32, NewPlr uint8, Time uint32, Info []byte, LeaveInfo LeaveInfo; `type PacketFactory struct{ key [32]byte; secure bool }`; use `golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/secretbox` + `golang.org/x/crypto/argon2` (Argon2id, t=3, m=2*8192 KiB? verify exact MEMLIMIT_MIN — libsodium argon2id MEMLIMIT_MIN = 8192 (KiB) → 8 MiB; id params must be tested against C++ build for interop, or dropped if Go-only network).
- Risks/open questions: exact argon2id parameter equivalence (x/crypto/argon2.IDKey key length 32, salt 16, time=3*OPSLIMIT_MIN, memory=2*MEMLIMIT_MIN) must be validated against libsodium constants for C++↔Go interop; if the Go port only interoperates with itself, keep values identical anyway for spec fidelity.

### Source/dvlnet/packet.h
- Purpose: Core packet definitions: `packet_type` enum, scalar typedefs (plr_t, seq_t, cookie_t, timestamp_t, key_t), `turn_t`, PLR_MASTER/PLR_BROADCAST, `PacketError` (message + ErrorCode), templated serialize/deserialize engine (`packet_proc<P>::process_data`, `packet_in/packet_out::process_element`), typed `packet_out::create<T>` constructors for each packet type, and `packet_factory` with `max_packet_size`.
- Public API: `enum packet_type : uint8_t {PT_MESSAGE=0x01, PT_TURN=0x02, PT_JOIN_REQUEST=0x11, PT_JOIN_ACCEPT=0x12, PT_CONNECT=0x13, PT_DISCONNECT=0x14, PT_INFO_REQUEST=0x21, PT_INFO_REPLY=0x22, PT_ECHO_REQUEST=0x31, PT_ECHO_REPLY=0x32}`; typedefs `plr_t=u8, seq_t=u8, cookie_t=u32, timestamp_t=u32`; `key_t` = `[crypto_secretbox_KEYBYTES]` array or `uint8_t` stub; `struct turn_t { seq_t SequenceNumber; int32_t Value; }`; `PLR_MASTER=0xFE`, `PLR_BROADCAST=0xFF`; `class PacketError` (ctors from char*/string/string_view + ErrorCode{None,EncryptionFailed,DecryptionFailed}); `IoHandlerError(std::string)`; `class packet` (+accessors); `template<class P> class packet_proc`; `class packet_in`, `class packet_out` (with `create<PT_...>` specializations per type); `class packet_factory { static constexpr unsigned short max_packet_size = 0xFFFF; ... }` with `make_packet(buffer_t)` and `make_packet<t>(Args...)`.
- Depends on: `dvlnet/abstract_net.h` (buffer_t indirectly), `dvlnet/leaveinfo.hpp` (leaveinfo_t), `appfat.h` (ABORT), `utils/endian_read.hpp` (LoadLE16/32), `utils/endian_write.hpp` (WriteLE16/32), `utils/str_cat.hpp`, `utils/stubs.h`, `utils/attributes.h` (StringOrView).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Wire format (from process_data + process_element, lines ~245-300, ~310-345, ~440-480): every packet = `type u8 LE`, `src u8`, `dest u8`, then per type:
    - PT_MESSAGE: message bytes (all remaining).
    - PT_TURN: `SequenceNumber u8` + `Value i32 LE`.
    - PT_JOIN_REQUEST: `cookie u32 LE` + info bytes (remaining).
    - PT_JOIN_ACCEPT: `cookie u32 LE` + `newplr u8` + info bytes (remaining).
    - PT_CONNECT: `newplr u8` + info bytes (remaining) — note two create<> overloads, with and without info.
    - PT_DISCONNECT: `newplr u8` + `leaveinfo u32 LE` (enum serialized as 4-byte LE).
    - PT_INFO_REQUEST: nothing after header.
    - PT_INFO_REPLY: info bytes (remaining).
    - PT_ECHO_REQUEST/REPLY: `time u32 LE`.
  - Reading scalars: 4-byte LE, 2-byte LE, 1-byte raw; bounds-checked (`decrypted_buffer.size() < sizeof(T)` → PacketError "Incorrect packet size"); buffer_t field consumes ALL remaining bytes and empties the source.
  - `packet_in::Create` min length 3 bytes (type+2 plr).
  - All `create<T>` overloads ABORT if already encrypted/decrypted; set have_decrypted, fill fields.
  - `make_packet` parse path: construct in-packet → Create/Decrypt → process_data; build path: create<T> → process_data → Encrypt if secure.
  - Go should replace CRTP templates with either codegen or hand-written per-type encode/decode functions in the exact order above.
- 1:1 constraints: type byte values (lines ~16-27: 0x01,0x02,0x11,0x12,0x13,0x14,0x21,0x22,0x31,0x32); `PLR_MASTER=0xFE`, `PLR_BROADCAST=0xFF` (lines ~52-53); `max_packet_size = 0xFFFF` (packet_factory, line ~495); all multi-byte scalars LE; `turn_t.Value` is signed int32; field order exactly as listed in process_data switch (lines ~248-296); buffer fields (m_message/m_info) always LAST and consume remainder.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: no globals in header (CookieGenerator is in packet.cpp); PacketError uses StringOrView (view may dangle in C++; Go strings immutable — fine). Packet build/parse is pure given inputs except GenerateCookie.
- Test coverage: none found in test/.
- Go mapping: `internal/net/packet.go` (+ `packet_io.go`): `type PacketType uint8` constants; `func (p *PacketFactory) MakePacket(t PacketType, fields...) ([]byte, error)` and `ParsePacket(buf []byte) (*Packet, error)`; keep a `Data()` method returning encrypted-or-decrypted bytes for sending.
- Risks/open questions: PT_CONNECT create<> exists with and without info buffer — Go port should support both construction variants; ensure signed int32 turn Value survives Go serialization (cast to uint32 on wire).

### Source/dvlnet/protocol_zt.cpp
- Purpose: ZeroTier-lwIP transport: binds IPv6 UDP+TCP sockets on port 6112 inside the ZeroTier virtual network (via lwIP sockets API), maintains per-peer TCP connections with send queues and receive frame_queues, OOB UDP send/receive, accept loop, disconnect detection, peer latency/relay queries via MAC lookup, and a random 5-char default game name.
- Public API: implementations of `protocol_zt` methods (see protocol_zt.h entry): ctor (starts zerotier network), `disconnect`, `send`, `send_oob`, `send_oob_mc`, `recv`, `get_disconnected`, `network_online`, `peers_ready`, `is_peer_connected`, `is_peer_relayed`, `get_latency_to`, static `make_default_gamename`, `endpoint::from_string`.
- Depends on: `dvlnet/zerotier_native.h` (`zerotier_network_start`, `zerotier_network_ready`, `zerotier_peers_ready`, `zerotier_is_relayed`, `zerotier_latency`); lwIP (`lwip/sockets.h` fcntl/socket/bind/listen/send/recv/recvfrom/accept/close/setsockopt; `lwip/nd6.h` `nd6_get_next_hop_addr_or_queue`; `lwip/tcpip.h` netif_default; `ipaddr_aton`); `frame_queue::MakeFrame`; `PacketError`/`ProtocolError`; SDL error functions; `utils/log.hpp` (Log/LogError).
- Requirements for Go port (if ZeroTier support is kept; else document as omitted):
  - Nonblocking lwIP-style socket helpers: set_nonblock (F_GETFL|O_NONBLOCK), set_nodelay (TCP_NODELAY), set_reuseaddr (SO_REUSEADDR).
  - `network_online()`: wait until zerotier_network_ready; create/bind UDP socket [::]:6112 with reuseaddr, nonblock; create/bind/listen(10) TCP socket [::]:6112, nonblock+nodelay; errors formatted "Error binding to ZeroTier UDP socket: {}" / "...TCP..." / "Error listening on ZeroTier TCP socket: {}".
  - `send(peer, data)`: wrap data in `MakeFrame` (default flags 0), append to peer's send_queue (creates peer_list entry implicitly).
  - `send_oob(peer, data)`: raw UDP sendto [peer]:6112 (unframed), always returns true.
  - `send_oob_mc(data)`: send_oob to the hardcoded 16-byte `dvl_multicast_addr`.
  - `send_queued_peer`: lazy lwip_connect per peer (nonblock+nodelay); drain send_queue handling partial sends (erase sent prefix, return true) and impossible-send accounting error.
  - `recv_peer`: loop recv into 64 KiB buf; append to peer recv_queue; on error return errno∈{EAGAIN,EWOULDBLOCK}.
  - `send_queued_all`, `recv_from_peers` (failing recv → disconnect_queue), `recv_from_udp` (one recvfrom → oob_recv_queue entry keyed by sender addr), `accept_all` (loop accept; overwrite-existing-connection warning path).
  - `recv(peer, data)`: call accept_all → send_queued_all → recv_from_peers → recv_from_udp; then prioritize oob_recv_queue; else scan peer_list (iteration order of hash map!) for a ready frame, ReadPacket, return it.
  - `get_disconnected`, `disconnect` (close+erase), `close_all` (close listeners, all peer fds, clear), dtor = close_all.
  - `endpoint::from_string`: ipaddr_aton; keep only IPv6; copy 16 bytes.
  - `current_ms()` returns 0 (stub).
  - `is_peer_connected` = present in peer_list with fd != -1.
  - `is_peer_relayed`/`get_latency_to`: resolve peer MAC from IPv6 via neighbor discovery (GetMAC builds ip6_addr from the 16 bytes, calls nd6_get_next_hop_addr_or_queue on netif_default, packs 6 hwaddr bytes into u64 big-endian), then zerotier_is_relayed / zerotier_latency; nullopt when MAC lookup fails.
  - `make_default_gamename`: 5 chars from alphabet `"abcdefghkopqrstuvwxyz"` using std::random_device + uniform_int_distribution.
- 1:1 constraints: `PKTBUF_LEN = 65536` (protocol_zt.h line ~86), `default_port = 6112` (line ~87); listen backlog 10; multicast address bytes `dvl_multicast_addr[16]` (defined elsewhere — zerotier_native); gamename alphabet exactly "abcdefghkopqrstuvwxyz" (note: missing i, j, l — intentional), length 5 (lines ~405-415); MAC packing: `mac = hw[0]; mac=(mac<<8)|hw[1]; ... |hw[5]` (lines ~40-53); OOB UDP datagrams carry the raw packet without frame header, while TCP carries MakeFrame framing.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `recv()` drives all I/O synchronously — single-threaded polling model, no locks. Iteration over `ankerl::unordered_dense::map` peer_list in recv/send_queued_all has unspecified order — which peer's packet is returned first when several are ready is map-order dependent; Go map iteration is randomized — if a deterministic choice is needed, maintain insertion order (affects only fairness, not correctness). `make_default_gamename` uses random_device (non-deterministic by design). SDL_SetError is a global side channel.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/net/protocol_zt.go` — requires a ZeroTier SDK/lwIP equivalent; realistically this is the file to defer/stub in the Go port (plain net.UDP/TCP on [::]:6112 reproduces the wire behavior except ZeroTier relay info; `is_peer_relayed`/`get_latency_to` return "unknown"). Strategy: implement `ProtocolZt` struct with same method set backed by Go `net` package; keep endpoints as `[16]byte`.
- Risks/open questions: depends on native ZeroTier + lwIP — Go port must decide whether to embed zerotier-core or approximate over OS sockets; `send_oob_mc` target `dvl_multicast_addr` value lives outside this file (zerotier_native), must be copied from there when porting.

### Source/dvlnet/tcp_client.cpp
- Purpose: TCP multiplayer client: `create()` spins up an in-process tcp_server then joins it as a client (host mode); `join()` parses host[:port] (with [v6]:port support), connects, sends PT_JOIN_REQUEST with a fresh cookie + game_init_info, and synchronously polls until the server assigns a player id; async receive path reassembles frames and dispatches packets; supports a 1-byte server error frame (TcpErrorCodeFlags) for password-decrypt failures.
- Public API: implementations of `tcp_client` overrides (see tcp_client.h): `int create(std::string_view)`, `int join(std::string_view)`, `std::expected<void,PacketError> poll()`, `std::expected<void,PacketError> send(packet&)`, `void DisconnectNet(plr_t)`, `bool SNetLeaveGame(net::leaveinfo_t)`, `std::string make_default_gamename()`, `bool IsGameHost()`; private `HandleReceive`, `StartReceive`, `HandleSend`, `HandleTcpErrorCode`, `RaiseIoHandlerError`.
- Depends on: `dvlnet/base.h` (`base` class: plr_self, RecvLocal, cookie_self, game_init_info, SNetLeaveGame impl), `dvlnet/tcp_server.h` (tcp_server: ctor(io_context, addr, port, pktfty), LocalhostSelf(), CheckIoHandlerError(), DisconnectNet(plr), Close()), `dvlnet/frame_queue.h` (MakeFrame, max_frame_size), `dvlnet/packet.h` (packet, PT_JOIN_REQUEST, PLR_BROADCAST/PLR_MASTER, PacketError, packet_out::GenerateCookie), `options.h` (`GetOptions().Network.port`, `.Network.szBindAddress`), `utils/language.h` (_()), `utils/str_split.hpp` (SplitByChar), asio (io_context, resolver, socket, async_receive/async_write, no_delay), SDL (SDL_SetError, SDL_Delay, SDL3/SDL1 conditionals).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `create(addrstr)`: port = options Network.port; start local tcp_server bound to addrstr:port sharing the same packet factory; then `join(LocalhostSelf())`.
  - `join(addrstr)` address parsing: if starts with '[' → "[v6]" or "[v6]:port" (colon required after ']' if anything follows, else error "Invalid hostname: expected colon after square brackets"); else split on ':' — first token host, second port; if MORE than one colon total → whole string is host (bare IPv6), port = default "6112". Default port string "6112".
  - Resolve + connect (error → SDL_SetError + return -1); set TCP_NODELAY (failure only logged: "Client error setting socket option: {}").
  - Start async receive loop; generate `cookie_self`; build PT_JOIN_REQUEST(PLR_BROADCAST→PLR_MASTER, cookie, game_init_info); send; then poll loop: max 250 iterations (`NoSleep = 250`), 10 ms sleep between polls (`MsSleep = 10`), break when `plr_self != PLR_BROADCAST`; still PLR_BROADCAST after loop → error "Unable to connect"; return plr_self.
  - `poll()`: drain ready asio handlers; if host, propagate local_server CheckIoHandlerError; first stored ioHandlerResult is returned once then cleared.
  - `HandleReceive(error, n)`: error → IoHandlerError; `n == 0` → "error: read 0 bytes from server" (translated); append n bytes to recv_queue; restore recv_buffer to max_frame_size; loop PacketReady → if `ReadPacketFlags() == TcpErrorCodeFlags` → HandleTcpErrorCode and stop; else ReadPacket → pktfty->make_packet → RecvLocal; error anywhere → RaiseIoHandlerError; finally re-arm receive.
  - `HandleTcpErrorCode`: read 1-byte packet; size != 1 → "Incorrect packet size"; code == DecryptionFailed → translated "Server failed to decrypt your packet. Check if you typed the password correctly."; else "Unknown error code received from server: 0xNN" (std::format `{:#04x}`).
  - `send(pkt)`: MakeFrame(pkt.Data()) → async_write whole frame; write error → HandleSend → RaiseIoHandlerError.
  - `DisconnectNet(plr)`: forward to local_server if hosting.
  - `SNetLeaveGame`: base leave, process_network_packets(), local_server->Close() if hosting, sock.close(); return base result.
  - `make_default_gamename`: returns options Network.szBindAddress.

Order: HandleReceive processes ALL complete frames in the queue before re-arming.

# Volume III — batch 012

### Source/dvlnet/tcp_server.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the TCP game server — accepts client connections, frames packets, assigns player slots (plr), relays/broadcasts packets between clients, and enforces connection timeouts.
- Public API: class `tcp_server` methods: `tcp_server(asio::io_context&, const std::string &bindaddr, unsigned short port, packet_factory&)` (L12-20); `std::string LocalhostSelf()` (L22); `std::expected<void,PacketError> CheckIoHandlerError()` (L222-228); `void DisconnectNet(plr_t)` (L230-237); `void Close()` (L239-241); `~tcp_server() = default`.
- Depends on: `asio` (io_context, tcp acceptor/socket/steady_timer); `dvlnet/base.h` (buffer_t, plr_t, PLR_BROADCAST, PLR_MASTER, MAX_PLRS via multi.h); `dvlnet/frame_queue.h` (frame_queue::Write/ReadPacket/PacketReady/MakeFrame, max_frame_size); `dvlnet/packet.h` (packet_factory, packet, cookie_t, leaveinfo_t, PT_CONNECT/PT_JOIN_ACCEPT/PT_DISCONNECT, PacketError); `player.h` (Players array — size only); `utils/log.hpp` (Log/LogError); ABORT macro.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A `TCPServer` type bound to a net listener; constructor binds bindaddr:port and immediately starts accept loop (StartAccept called in ctor, L19).
  - Per-connection state: recv frame queue, recv buffer sized max_frame_size, assigned plr (starts PLR_BROADCAST/255), a decremented-1-per-second timeout counter, socket + timer.
  - Read loop: read chunk → resize to bytesRead → push to frame queue → restore buffer to max_frame_size → drain packets until PacketReady false; any error (PacketReady/ReadPacket/make_packet) logs and drops connection.
  - Unauthenticated packets (plr==PLR_BROADCAST) go to join flow; others refresh timeout to 60 and forward via HandleReceivePacket→SendPacket.
  - Join flow (HandleReceiveNewPlayer): NextFree slot else ServerError("Invalid player ID"); if server empty, capture first join packet's Info() as game_init_info; for each already-connected player send PT_CONNECT(master→broadcast, newplr) to them and PT_CONNECT(master→broadcast, player) to the newcomer; then reply PT_JOIN_ACCEPT(master→broadcast, cookie from join pkt, newplr, game_init_info); only then set con->plr and connections[newplr], timeout=60.
  - Routing (SendPacket): broadcast → all connections except source; unicast → invalid if dest≥MAX_PLRS, no-op if dest==source or no connection; else single send.
  - Error-code send: on DecryptionFailed, sends 1-byte payload of the error code with frame flags 0x8000 (TcpErrorCodeFlags) before dropping.
  - Frame wrapping on every send via frame_queue::MakeFrame; async write with heap-held frame buffer; send failure drops connection.
  - Accept handler: on acceptor error raise ioHandlerResult (surfaced once via CheckIoHandlerError); if full, drop; else set TCP_NODELAY (failure only logs), timeout=30, start receive+timeout loops; always re-arm accept.
  - Timeout loop: 1-second steady timer; error → drop; decrement while >0; ≤0 → drop (with disconnect broadcast).
  - DropConnection: cancel timer, close socket; if plr==BROADCAST just return; else clear slot and broadcast PT_DISCONNECT(master→broadcast, plr, LEAVE_DROP).
  - DisconnectNet(plr): cancel/close and null the slot without broadcasting (client-requested).
  - Close(): close acceptor only.
- 1:1 constraints: timeout_connect=30, timeout_active=60 (tcp_server.h L57-58); TcpErrorCodeFlags = 0x8000 (tcp_server.h L22); error byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(errorCode) pushed as single buffer element (L159-160); NextFree scans 0..Players.size() ascending, returns PLR_BROADCAST when full (L40-45); Empty() = no connection in any slot (L47-52); join order: existing-players notifications → JOIN_ACCEPT to newcomer → slot assignment (L89-118 — slot only bound after accept packet is sent); broadcast skips i==pkt.Source() and empty slots (L127-129); HandleReceive re-arms StartReceive only after fully draining queue (L81).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: All state mutated on the single asio io_context thread — Go port should run accept/read/timeout on one goroutine per connection with a mutex on connections[]/game_init_info, or a single event loop. ioHandlerResult is an optional latched error consumed once. connections array indexed by plr; timers are per-connection asio steady_timers (1s tick).
- Test coverage: none found (no tcp_server tests in test/).
- Go mapping: `internal/net/tcpserver` (or devilutionGo/internal/dvlnet/tcp_server). Strategy: net.Listener + goroutines; keep frame_queue and packet layer byte-identical; emulate timeouts with time.Ticker/time.AfterFunc per connection; single mutex guarding connections [MAX_PLRS] and game_init_info.
- Risks/open questions: asio single-threaded serialization vs Go concurrency — ordering of broadcast vs JOIN_ACCEPT must be preserved (same socket write order). PLR_BROADCAST/MAX_PLRS values come from base/multi headers (not in this file).

### Source/dvlnet/zerotier_native.cpp
- Purpose: Native ZeroTier lifecycle: starts the ZT node from config storage, tracks node/network/peer readiness via an event callback, and queries peer relay status and latency.
- Public API (extern "C"-style free functions in devilution::net): `bool zerotier_network_ready()` (L141-144); `bool zerotier_peers_ready()` (L146-149); `void zerotier_network_start()` (L151-161); `bool zerotier_is_relayed(uint64_t mac)` (L163-176); `int zerotier_latency(uint64_t mac)` (L178-187).
- Depends on: `<ZeroTierSockets.h>` (zts_* API, zts_event_msg_t, ZTS_EVENT_* codes); SDL ticks (`SDL_GetTicks` via SDL3/SDL1 backports); ankerl::unordered_dense map; atomics; `utils/paths.h` (paths::ConfigPath); `utils/log.hpp`; `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (c_any_of); on Windows+filesystem: shlobj (SHGetFolderPathA, CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA), sodium crypto_generichash (under PACKET_ENCRYPTION), StrCat, utf8 helpers (IsTrailUtf8CodeUnit, AsHexPad2, BufCopy); `dvlnet/zerotier_lwip.h` (zt_ip6setup, print_ip6_addr).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Fixed network ID ZtNetwork = 0xa84ac5c10a7ebb5f (L34); node joins it once on first NODE_ONLINE (zt_joined guard).
  - Global atomic state: zt_network_ready, zt_node_online, zt_joined, zt_peers_ready (tick timestamp); a map peer_id→last peer event (DIRECT/RELAY), erased on PATH_DEAD.
  - Event callback semantics: NODE_ONLINE → log node id (hex), set online, join network if not yet; NODE_OFFLINE → clear online; NETWORK_READY_IP6 → zt_ip6setup(), set network_ready, record SDL_GetTicks as peers-ready baseline; ADDR_ADDED_IP6 → print_ip6_addr; PEER_DIRECT/PEER_RELAY → record in map, refresh peers-ready timestamp if not already ready; PEER_PATH_DEAD → erase.
  - zerotier_peers_ready(): true iff now − zt_peers_ready ≥ 5000 ms.
  - zerotier_network_ready(): network_ready && node_online.
  - zerotier_network_start(): configPath = paths::ConfigPath(); (Win32 only) convert to ZT-compliant path; append "zerotier"; zts_init_from_storage, zts_init_set_event_handler(&Callback), zts_node_start.
  - zerotier_is_relayed(mac): default true; obtain core lock; query peer info for (ZtNetwork, mac); look up peer_id in event map; isRelayed = (event == PEER_RELAY); release lock.
  - zerotier_latency(mac): −1 on failure; else peerInfo.latency under core lock.
  - Windows multi-byte path workaround (DVL_ZT_SYMLINK only): if config path has multi-byte UTF-8, build %ProgramData%\diasurgical\devilution, create dirs, folder name = blake2b (crypto_generichash, crypto_generichash_BYTES) of path hex-encoded 2 chars/byte, create directory symlink config→alternate if missing, return alternate + "\\"; every failure logs verbose and falls back to original path. Without PACKET_ENCRYPTION the alternate name is "" → always fallback.
- 1:1 constraints: ZtNetwork = 0xa84ac5c10a7ebb5f (L34); peers-ready threshold 5000 ms (L148); storage subdir "zerotier" (L157); Win alternate root StrCat(commonAppDataPath, "\\diasurgical\\devilution") (L78); hash = crypto_generichash default output length, hex lowercase via AsHexPad2, 2*hashSize chars (L49-63); dvl_multicast_addr bytes (header, L10-14) as listed in zerotier_lwip.cpp entry; commented-out zt_earth network 0x8056c2e21c000001 (L32, dead).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: callback runs on ZT's own thread — atomics required for the four flags; ztPeerEvents map is written from callback and read from game thread under zts core lock only in is_relayed (map itself is not otherwise locked — latent race in C++; Go port must add a mutex). zt_peers_ready uses SDL tick base (wraps at ~49 days on SDL1/2 32-bit — match behavior or use monotonic clock).
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: internal/dvlnet/zerotier — wrap libzt via cgo (CGO wrapper exposing Start/Ready/PeersReady/IsRelayed/Latency + event callback into Go), or replace with a pure-Go ZT client if available; keep network ID and 5s threshold as consts; Windows symlink fallback via golang.org/x/sys/windows known-folder + os.Symlink.
- Risks/open questions: pure-Go ZeroTier stack is a major undertaking; cgo binding of libzt (patched for multicast MAC) is the realistic 1:1 path. ztPeerEvents unsynchronized access is a real race to fix in Go.

### Source/encrypt.cpp
- Purpose: PKWARE implode/explode wrappers used for MPQ sector and network packet (de)compression.
- Public API: `uint32_t PkwareCompress(std::byte *srcData, uint32_t size)` (L14-45); `uint32_t PkwareDecompress(std::byte *inBuff, uint32_t recvSize, size_t maxBytes)` (L47-72).
- Depends on: `<mpqfs/mpqfs.h>` — external mpqfs library providing `mpqfs_pk_implode(const uint8_t*, size_t, uint8_t*, size_t*, int dict_bits)` and `mpqfs_pk_explode(const uint8_t*, size_t, uint8_t*, size_t*)`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - PkwareCompress: in-place semantics — output capacity = size*2+64 (stack ≤ 8256 bytes, else heap); call implode with dict_bits=6; on success (rc==0) AND dstSize < size, memcpy compressed bytes back over srcData and return dstSize; otherwise return original size (data left untouched).
  - PkwareDecompress: in-place — out capacity = maxBytes (stack ≤ 8192, else heap); explode(inBuff, recvSize) into out; rc!=0 → return 0; else memcpy out→inBuff and return outSize.
  - Go needs a PKWARE implode/explode implementation (the classic PKWARE DCL format): compress returns min(compressed, original) with fallback to raw; decompress bounded by maxBytes.
- 1:1 constraints: StackBufSize compress = (4096*2)+64 = 8192+64 = 8192? — exactly (4096*2)+64 = 8256 (L18); dstCap = size*2 + 64 (L21); dict_bits = 6 (L29); success requires dstSize < size strictly (L31) — equal-size output is treated as failure → returns size with original bytes; decompress StackBufSize = 8192 (L50); explode failure returns 0 (L66-67); both operate in-place on the caller's buffer.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure functions, no globals; stack/heap choice is a perf detail, not semantics.
- Test coverage: none found in test/ for Pkware (codec_test.cpp covers codec.cpp, not this).
- Go mapping: pkg/mpq or internal/pkware — port the PKWARE DCL implode/explode (well-documented format; existing Go ports exist e.g. in stormlib-derived code, verify against mpqfs). Wrap as Compress(dst/iny []byte) (n int) with same fallback semantics.
- Risks/open questions: must be bit-exact with PKWARE DCL — verify with MPQ fixtures (network save packets and MPQ sectors both depend on it).

### Source/engine/actor_position.cpp
- Purpose: Computes walking displacement offsets and velocities for actors (players/monsters) from animation progress, direction, and walk-animation frame count.
- Public API: methods on `ActorPosition` (declared in actor_position.hpp): `DisplacementOf<int8_t> CalculateWalkingOffset(Direction, const AnimationInfo&) const` (L96-101); `DisplacementOf<int16_t> CalculateWalkingOffsetShifted4(Direction, const AnimationInfo&) const` (L103-110); `DisplacementOf<int16_t> CalculateWalkingOffsetShifted8(Direction, const AnimationInfo&) const` (L112-118); `DisplacementOf<int16_t> GetWalkingVelocityShifted4(Direction, const AnimationInfo&) const` (L120-124); `DisplacementOf<int16_t> GetWalkingVelocityShifted8(Direction, const AnimationInfo&) const` (L126-132).
- Depends on: `actor_position.hpp` (ActorPosition, Direction, DisplacementOf<T>, AnimationInfo with getAnimationProgress(), numberOfFrames, baseValueFraction).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - WalkVelocityForFrames[24] table: per frame-count 1..24 the {quarter, half, full} int16 velocity components (values = 1024/frames rounded per column — copy verbatim).
  - WalkParameters[8] indexed by Direction (0=South …7=SouthEast) mapping to (VelocityX, VelocityY) selectors: S(Half,None)→(0,+half); SW(NegHalf,Quarter); W(NegFull,None); NW(NegHalf,NegQuarter); N(None,NegHalf); NE(Half,NegQuarter); E(Full,None); SE(Half,Quarter).
  - CalculateWalkingOffsetShifted4: velocityProgress = int16(getAnimationProgress()) * numberOfFrames / baseValueFraction; offset = directionVelocity(int16 pair) * velocityProgress (per-component int16 multiply).
  - Shifted8 = Shifted4 << 4 per component. CalculateWalkingOffset = Shifted4 >> 4 (arithmetic) cast to int8 per component.
  - GetWalkingVelocityShifted4/8: table lookup only (no progress), Shifted8 = Shifted4 << 4.
- 1:1 constraints: full WalkVelocityForFrames table (L40-65) — rows 1..24: {256,512,1024},{128,256,512},{85,170,341},{64,128,256},{51,102,204},{42,85,170},{36,73,146},{32,64,128},{28,56,113},{26,51,102},{23,46,93},{21,42,85},{19,39,78},{18,36,73},{17,34,68},{16,32,64},{15,30,60},{14,28,57},{13,26,54},{12,25,51},{12,24,48},{11,23,46},{11,22,44},{10,21,42}; WalkParameters order (L77-89) as listed above; index = WalkVelocityForFrames[numberOfFrames−1] (L72); velocityProgress formula (L105); >>4 and <<4 shifts (L99, L114-116, L129-131); int16 saturation-free arithmetic (C++ wraps — Go int16 ops match).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure functions of inputs (Direction, AnimationInfo state); no globals; safe concurrently. Order dependence only via animInfo.getAnimationProgress() which the animation port must supply deterministically.
- Test coverage: none found directly; animationinfo_test.cpp tests AnimationInfo (progress), not these offsets — verify by grep before claiming coverage in the port.
- Go mapping: internal/engine (package engine) — methods on ActorPosition struct; DisplacementOf[T int16|int8] generic type; Direction enum with same 0..7 ordering.
- Risks/open questions: numberOfFrames must be 1..24 (table bounds); C++ relies on callers — Go should guard or document. int8 cast after >>4 relies on offset magnitude <128 (walk offsets only).

### Source/engine/animationinfo.cpp
- Purpose: Implements animation timing/frame selection: which sprite frame to render given game ticks and the frame-distribution ("ADL") logic for skipped frames and smooth rendering.
- Public API: methods of `AnimationInfo` (class in animationinfo.h): `int8_t getFrameToUseForRendering() const; uint8_t getAnimationProgress() const; void setNewAnimation(OptionalClxSpriteList, int8_t numberOfFrames, int8_t ticksPerFrame, AnimationDistributionFlags flags=None, int8_t numSkippedFrames=0, int8_t distributeFramesBeforeFrame=0, uint8_t previewShownGameTickFragments=0); void changeAnimationData(...); void processAnimation(bool reverseAnimation=false); uint8_t getProgressToNextGameTick() const`
- Depends on: global `ProgressToNextGameTick` (nthread.h/nthread.cpp:35, updated by render loop), `Log` (utils/log.hpp), `OptionalClxSpriteList` (engine/clx_sprite.hpp), `<algorithm>` clamp/max.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `GetFrameToUseForRendering`: if `relevantFramesForDistributing_ <= 0` return max(0, currentFrame); clamp negative ticksSinceSequenceStarted_ to 0 (log); `total = ProgressToNextGameTick + ticksSinceSequenceStarted`; `absFrame = int8(total * tickModifier_ / 128 / 128)`; if skippedFramesFromPreviousAnimation_ > 0 subtract it, wrap negative by adding numberOfFrames; else if absFrame >= relevantFrames cap to relevant-1 (log if >= relevant+1); return 0 if still negative.
  - `GetAnimationProgress`: non-distribution path computes `ticksSince = ((currentFrame*ticksPerFrame)+tickCounter)*128`, `tickModifier = 128/ticksPerFrame` (guard ticksPerFrame<=0 → return 0); `progress = total * tickModifier / numberOfFrames / 128`; assert ≤128.
  - `SetNewAnimation`: RepeatedAction carry-over (`skippedFramesFromPreviousAnimation_ = numberOfFrames - currentFrame - 1` only when flags has RepeatedAction && distributeFramesBeforeFrame != 0 && same frame count && currentFrame+1 >= distributeFramesBeforeFrame && currentFrame != numberOfFrames-1); clamp ticksPerFrame<=0→1; reset state (currentFrame=numSkippedFrames, counters 0, isPetrified=false); distribution setup only if numSkippedFrames!=0 || flags!=None: relevant frames = distributeFramesBeforeFrame-1 (if nonzero) else numberOfFrames; relevantTicks = frames*ticksPerFrame; minus numSkippedFrames*ticksPerFrame; minus 1 if ProcessAnimationPending (and set ticksSinceSequenceStarted_ = -128); minus (ticksPerFrame-1) if SkipsDelayOfLastFrame; add skippedFramesFromPreviousAnimation_*ticksPerFrame to distribution ticks; scale both by 128; add previewShownGameTickFragments to ticksSince and to withSkipping; tickModifier = 128*distributionTicks/withSkipping (0 if withSkipping==0), then /= ticksPerFrame; store relevantFrames and uint16 tickModifier.
  - `ChangeAnimationData`: only resets counters if numberOfFrames or ticksPerFrame changed (clamps currentFrame into [0, n-1] or -1 when n<1); always updates sprites ref.
  - `ProcessAnimation`: tickCounter++, ticksSince += 128; when tickCounter >= ticksPerFrame reset to 0 and advance frame forward (wrap to 0, resetting ticksSince) or reverse (wrap to n-1).
  - `GetProgressToNextGameTick`: 0 when petrified else global `ProgressToNextGameTick`.
- 1:1 constraints: `baseValueFraction = 128` (h:109); division order `totalTicks * tickModifier_ / baseValueFraction / baseValueFraction` (cpp:40); `ticksSinceSequenceStarted_ = -baseValueFraction` for ProcessAnimationPending (cpp:135); `relevantAnimationTicksWithSkipping -= (ticksPerFrame - 1)` for SkipsDelayOfLastFrame (cpp:150); `tickModifier = baseValueFraction * dist / skip; tickModifier /= ticksPerFrame` (cpp:175-179); all int8/int16/int32 fixed-point truncation toward zero (C++ semantics) must be preserved.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: reads global render-phase `ProgressToNextGameTick` (nthread.cpp:35) — animation rendering depends on real-time fraction between logic ticks; petrified freezes it. No locks; instances owned per-entity.
- Test coverage: `test/animationinfo_test.cpp` (extensive).
- Go mapping: `internal/engine/animationinfo` — struct AnimationInfo with int8/int16 fields kept narrow (or int with exact truncation tests); flags as bitflags type.
- Risks/open questions: C++ int8 overflow semantics on `currentFrame*ticksPerFrame` etc. are computed in int due to promotions — Go must use wide ints then truncate exactly where C++ assigns to int8.

### Source/engine/assets.cpp
- Purpose: Asset resolution and MPQ archive management: `FindAsset` search order (absolute path → override dirs → MPQs by priority → bundled assets), open/load helpers, archive load/unload lifecycle, mod archive loading with dependency ordering, loose-logic-asset detection.
- Public API: `AssetRef FindAsset(std::string_view)`; `AssetHandle OpenAsset(AssetRef&&, bool threadsafe=false)` + 2 filename overloads (one with `size_t &fileSize`); `OpenIntegralAsset` (same 3 overloads, sets `IsAssetIntegrityViolated` on override); `SDL_IOStream *OpenAssetAsSdlRwOps(...)`; `std::expected<AssetData,std::string> LoadAsset(path)` / `LoadIntegralAsset(path)`; `std::string FailedToOpenFileErrorMessage(path, error)`; `void LoadCoreArchives(); LoadLanguageArchive(); LoadGameArchives(); LoadHellfireArchives(); UnloadModArchives(); LoadModArchives(span<string_view>)`; `ModManifest ReadModManifestByName(name)`; `bool HasLooseLogicAssets()`; globals `OverridePaths`, `MpqArchives` (map<int,MpqArchiveT,greater>), `HasHellfireMpq`, `IsAssetIntegrityViolated`.
- Depends on: `MpqArchive` (mpq/mpq_reader.hpp) — Open/FindHash/HasFile/ReadFile/GetFileSize; `SDL_RWops_FromMpqFile` (mpq/mpq_sdl_rwops.hpp); paths::* (utils/paths.h); FileExists/ListFiles/ListDirectories/OpenFile/GetFileSize/DirectoryExists (utils/file_util.h); `paths::AssetsPath()`; `gbIsSpawn`, `forceHellfire`, `gbIsHellfire`-related globals; `HeadlessMode` (headless_mode.hpp); `InsertCDDlg`, `DisplayFatalErrorAndExit` (appfat.h); `GetLanguageCode` (utils/language.h); mod system: `ModManifest/ParseModManifest/ModDependency/OrderModsByDependencies/ModIdentifier/RegisterPackedModIdentifier/RegisterBuiltinModIdentifier/ClearModIdentifiers` (mods/mod_identity.h); strings/str utils.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Central asset resolver with this exact search order (packed mode): (1) absolute path (leading '/') as direct file; (2) each `OverridePaths` entry + relativePath (with `\`→`/` on non-Windows) as override file (marks isOverridden); (3) MPQ archives in *descending* priority (std::greater map): FindHash(filename) != UINT32_MAX wins; (4) `paths::AssetsPath() + relativePath`; (5) platform fallbacks (Android/Apple relative path via SDL).
  - `UNPACKED_MPQS` variant: pathBuf juggling probing unpacked archive dirs, then assets dir — Go port should model both modes or pick packed as canonical and keep unpacked as an alternate resolver.
  - Archive priorities (constants in header): Main=1000, DevilutionX=9000, Lang=9100, Font=9200; hellfire=8000, hfbard=8110, hfbarb=8120, hfmonk=8100, hfmusic=8200, hfvoice=8500; mods start at 10000, incrementing per mod in dependency order.
  - `LoadGameArchives`: try "DIABDAT" with ".MPQ" ext first, then "diabdat", then "spawn" (sets gbIsSpawn); fatal dialog `InsertCDDlg(_("diabdat.mpq or spawn.mpq"))` when neither and !HeadlessMode; `forceHellfire && !HasHellfireMpq` → InsertCDDlg("hellfire.mpq").
  - `LoadCoreArchives`: devilutionx.mpq (priority 9000) first for fonts, then fonts.mpq (9200), `HasHellfireMpq = FindMPQ("hellfire")`.
  - `LoadLanguageArchive`: erase 9100, if language code != "en" load `<code>` at 9100.
  - `LoadModArchives`: ClearModIdentifiers; pre-pass reads each packed mod's manifest requiredMods (without registering), `OrderModsByDependencies` orders dependencies-first (lower priority = base); for each mod: PrefPath/mods/<name>/ and BasePath/mods/<name>/ dirs appended to OverridePaths (loose override, no identifier); always append PrefPath() itself last; then load mods/<name>.mpq at priority 10000+i; packed → RegisterPackedModIdentifier + read manifest from own archive (bypasses FindAsset deliberately); loose-only → hasLooseOverride; neither → RegisterBuiltinModIdentifier (provenance-whitelisted).
  - `UnloadModArchives`: clear OverridePaths; erase archives with priority in [8000,9000) or >=10000.
  - `HasLooseLogicAssets`: scan each override root recursively (max depth 16) for `.lua`/`.tsv`/`.sol` whose canonical `\`-joined lowercase path is loadable (lua\*.lua module rule, or found in MPQ, or exists under AssetsPath).
  - `LoadAsset`/`LoadIntegralAsset`: read whole file into heap buffer, return AssetData{data,size}; error strings "Asset not found: ", "Failed to open asset: ", "Read failed: ".
  - `ReadModManifestByName`: loose `mods/<name>/manifest.ini` from each search path first, then packed archive `mods/<name>.mpq`; default-constructed manifest on failure.
  - `GetMPQSearchPaths`: BasePath, PrefPath (dedup), ConfigPath (dedup), XDG_DATA_DIRS entries + "diasurgical/devilutionx/" suffix or fallback /usr/local/share + /usr/share paths on Unix; TERMUX/NXDK/GOG-Windows variants; empty-string PWD entry last.
- 1:1 constraints: priority constants (hpp:319-322) and hardcoded values 8000/8100/8110/8120/8200/8500/10000 (cpp:641-660, 682-690, 711-713); hellfire-content probes `plrgfx/monk/mha/mhaas.clx`, `music/dlvlf.wav|.mp3`, `sfx/hellfire/cowsut1.wav|.mp3` in unpacked mode (cpp:672-676); MaxScanDepth=16 (cpp:126); XDG fallback paths "/usr/local/share/diasurgical/devilutionx/", "/usr/share/diasurgical/devilutionx/" (cpp:444-446); GOG app id "1412601690" (cpp:460); duplicate-priority MPQ load is skipped with error (cpp:415-417); asset name canonical form uses `\` separators, converted to `/` only for filesystem probes on non-Windows.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable globals (`MpqArchives`, `OverridePaths`, `HasHellfireMpq`, `IsAssetIntegrityViolated`) mutated during load/unload phases; MPQ handles opened with optional `threadsafe` flag for render-thread reads; `IsAssetIntegrityViolated` set lazily when an integral asset resolves to an override (multiplayer anti-cheat backstop).
- Test coverage: `test/assets_test.cpp` (plus drlg_test.hpp, timedemo_test.cpp use it).
- Go mapping: `pkg/assets` (resolver + AssetRef/AssetHandle) + `pkg/mpq` consumer; implement resolver as interface with packed/unpacked strategies; keep priority map ordered descending.
- Risks/open questions: platform-specific search paths (GOG, XDG, Termux, NXDK) are desktop-console concerns — Go port likely trims to Base/Pref/Config/XDG; SDL_RWops thread-safety semantics need a Go equivalent (mutex per archive) since Go has no direct analog.

### Source/engine/backbuffer_state.cpp
- Purpose: Tracks per-backbuffer (keyed by pixel buffer pointer) redraw state: full-redraw / viewport-only flags, per-panel-component dirty flags, and the saved cursor background — so render loop knows what to repaint.
- Public API: `bool IsRedrawEverything(); void RedrawViewport(); bool IsRedrawViewport(); void RedrawComplete(); void RedrawEverything(); void InitBackbufferState(); void RedrawComponent(PanelDrawComponent); bool IsRedrawComponent(PanelDrawComponent); void RedrawComponentComplete(PanelDrawComponent); DrawnCursor &GetDrawnCursor();`
- Depends on: `PalSurface` global (engine/dx.h) — its `pixels` pointer keys the state; `PanelDrawComponent`, `DrawnCursor` (engine/backbuffer_state.hpp); `enum_size` (utils/enum_traits.h).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Internal `States []BackbufferPtrAndState` keyed by backbuffer pixel-pointer (Go: key by *image/pointer identity of the render target); `GetBackbufferState` linearly searches, appends new entry initialized to RedrawAll on miss.
  - RedrawEverything/RedrawViewport/RedrawComponent set flags on ALL tracked states; IsRedraw*/RedrawComplete/IsRedrawComponent/RedrawComponentComplete operate on the current backbuffer's state only.
  - `RedrawViewport` only downgrades states that aren't already RedrawAll.
  - `GetDrawnCursor` returns mutable cursor struct (rect + 8192-byte behind buffer) for the current backbuffer.

### Source/engine/clx_sprite.hpp
- Purpose: Zero-copy views and owning wrappers over the CLX sprite format (DevilutionX's runtime CL2-pixel variant): single sprites, sprite lists, sprite sheets, list-or-sheet unions, plus optional variants.
- Public API:
  - `class ClxSprite { ClxSprite(const uint8_t*, uint32_t dataSize); uint16_t width() const; uint16_t height() const; const uint8_t *pixelData() const; uint32_t pixelDataSize() const; ==/!= (pointer identity) }`
  - `class ClxSpriteList { ClxSpriteList(const uint8_t*); uint32_t numSprites(); ClxSprite operator[](size_t); uint32_t spriteOffset(size_t); uint32_t dataSize(); const uint8_t *data(); begin()/end(); OwnedClxSpriteList clone() }`
  - `ClxSpriteListIterator` (forward iterator over list);
  - `class ClxSpriteSheet { ClxSpriteSheet(const uint8_t*, uint16_t numLists); uint16_t numLists(); ClxSpriteList operator[](size_t); uint32_t sheetOffset(size_t); data(); begin()/end(); size_t dataSize() }` + `ClxSpriteSheetIterator`;
  - `class OwnedClxSpriteList { unique_ptr<uint8_t[]> data; clone(); operator[]; numSprites(); dataSize() }`;
  - `class OwnedClxSpriteSheet { data + numLists; operator[]; begin/end; dataSize() }`;
  - `uint16_t GetNumListsFromClxListOrSheetBuffer(const uint8_t*, size_t)`;
  - `class ClxSpriteListOrSheet / OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet { list()/sheet()/isSheet()/dataSize(); FromBuffer(data, size); numLists() }`;
  - `OptionalClxSprite/-List/-Sheet/-ListOrSheet`, `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList/-Sheet/-ListOrSheet` (intrusive optionals, null-data sentinel).
- Depends on: `LoadLE16/LoadLE32` (utils/endian_read.hpp); `appfat.h` (assert); `DEFINE_*_INTRUSIVE_OPTIONAL` (utils/intrusive_optional.hpp); `<cstring>` memcpy for clone.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - CLX format constants: frame header 6 bytes = uint16 headerSize, uint16 width, uint16 height, all LE; `pixelData = data + LoadLE16(data)`; `pixelDataSize = dataSize - headerSize` computed once at construction.
  - List layout: `numSprites = LoadLE32(data)`; `spriteOffset(i) = LoadLE32(&data[4 + i*4])`; sprite i spans [offset(i), offset(i+1)); `dataSize() = LoadLE32(&data[4 + numSprites*4])` (offset of next sheet or file size).
  - Sheet layout: `sheetOffset(i) = LoadLE32(&data[4*i])`, requires numLists supplied externally; sheet dataSize = end of last list (`&data[sheetOffset(n-1)] + list(n-1).dataSize() - data`).
  - `GetNumListsFromClxListOrSheetBuffer`: `maybeNumFrames = LoadLE32(data)`; if `LoadLE32(&data[maybeNumFrames*4 + 4]) != size` → it's a sheet with `maybeNumFrames/4` lists; else 0 (plain list). This is the ambiguity-resolution heuristic for loading unknown buffers.
  - Owned vs view types: Go can use `[]byte` (owned) and `SpriteList{data []byte}` views over the same backing array; slices naturally alias — keep an explicit clone (copy of data range `dataSize()`).
  - Optional variants → nullable pointers or explicit ok-flag; must preserve "no sprite" state used by AnimationInfo.
  - Equality is data-pointer identity — Go port should compare slice-data identity or just drop equality (only used in C++ for optional checks).
- 1:1 constraints: header layout table in file comment (lines 15-27); `pixel_data_size_(dataSize - LoadLE16(data))` (line 50); offsets `4 + spriteIndex*4` (list, line 119) and `4*sheetIndex` (sheet, line 303); sheet-detection heuristic `LoadLE32(&data[maybeNumFrames*4+4]) != size → maybeNumFrames/4` (lines 444-452); numLists is uint16.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: views are immutable once constructed; multiple views alias one buffer (lifetime managed by owners — Go GC handles); all reads are little-endian regardless of host.
- Test coverage: exercised by `test/clx_render_benchmark.cpp`, `test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp` (render side); no dedicated clx_sprite unit test found.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/clx` — types Sprite, SpriteList, SpriteSheet, OwnedListOrSheet with `FromBuffer`; LE decoding via encoding/binary or manual (manual for hot paths).
- Risks/open questions: none — format is fully specified in-file; the list-vs-sheet heuristic must be ported byte-exactly or assets will misparse.

### Source/engine/demomode.cpp
- Purpose: Demo playback/recording engine: reads/writes `.dmo` files (input event stream + game-tick/render markers), overrides gameplay options from demo settings, drives the game loop timing, and compares final hero state against a reference save.
- Public API: `namespace demo`: `InitPlayBack(int demoNumber, bool timedemo); InitRecording(int recordNumber, bool createDemoReference); OverrideOptions(); IsRunning(); IsRecording(); GetRunGameLoop(bool &drawGame, bool &processInput); FetchMessage(SDL_Event*, uint16_t*); RecordGameLoopResult(bool); RecordMessage(const SDL_Event&, uint16_t); NotifyGameLoopStart(); NotifyGameLoopEnd(); SimulateMillisecondsSinceStartup()`
- Depends on: globals `ProgressToNextGameTick`, `gnTickDelay`, `last_tick`, `sgGameInitInfo.nTickRate` (nthread.h); `gSaveNumber`, `gbRunGame`, `gbRunGameResult`, `gbProcessPlayers`, `gbIsMultiplayer`, `PauseMode` (diablo.h etc.); `CurrentEventHandler`, `DisableInputEventHandler`, `CustomEventToSdlEvent`, `IsCustomEvent`, `GetCustomEvent`, `interface_mode` (controls/plrctrls.h, engine/events.hpp); `GetOptions()` + option refs (options.h); `forceResolution`, `gnScreenWidth/Height` (utils/display.h); `ControlMode` (controls/control_mode.hpp); `gmenu_is_active` (gmenu.h); `pfile_write_hero_demo`, `pfile_compare_hero_demo`, `HeroCompareResult` (pfile.h); `diablo_quit` (diablo.h); `menu.h`, paths (utils/paths.h); console print utils; endian stream ReadLE16/32/WriteLE16/32/ReadByte/WriteByte (utils/endian_stream.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Demo file format v3: header = uint8 version, int32 LE gSaveNumber, uint16 LE width, uint16 LE height, then 1 byte per gameplay bool (order: runInTown, theoQuest, cowQuest, autoGoldPickup, autoElixirPickup, autoOilPickup, autoPickupInTown, adriaRefillsMana(=0 reserved), autoEquipWeapons, autoEquipArmor, autoEquipHelms, autoEquipShields, autoEquipJewelry, randomizeQuests, showItemLabels, autoRefillBelt, disableCripplingShrines) then 6 uint8 potion-pickup counts (heal, fullHeal, mana, fullMana, reju, fullReju).
  - Message stream: uint8 typeNum; if high bit (0x80) set → Rendering event with progress = typeNum & 0x7F (no further bytes); else uint8 progressToNextGameTick then per-type payloads (v2+): mousemotion u16 x,u16 y; button u8 button,u16 x,u16 y,u16 mod; wheel i16 x,i16 y,u16 mod; key u32 sym,u16 mod; quit nothing; custom events (type >= 64) nothing. v1 files: typeNum is u32 LE, event types remapped via `MapPreV2DemoMsgEventType` (0x100 quit, 0x300/0x301 key, 0x400 motion, 0x401/0x402 button, 0x403 wheel, 0x8000+ custom), wheel x/y are i32.
  - Event type constants: GameTick=0, Rendering=1, MinEvent=8, Quit=8, MouseMotion=9, MouseButtonDown=10, MouseButtonUp=11, MouseWheel=12, KeyDown=13, KeyUp=14, MinCustomEvent=64.
  - `GetRunGameLoop`: fetch next message (fatal "Demo queue empty" when exhausted); timedemo → drawGame only on GameTick && !HeadlessMode; otherwise wall-clock pacing vs `gnTickDelay`: if tick not due, compute `fraction = ticksElapsed * 128 / gnTickDelay` clamped [0,128]; if msg is GameTick or msg.progress > fraction → inject an extra render (set global ProgressToNextGameTick=fraction only when game running, unpaused, no menu, processing players; processInput=false; drawGame=true; return false). On consume: set global ProgressToNextGameTick = msg progress; GameTick increments LogicTick.
  - `FetchMessage`: poll real SDL events first — QUIT passes through; ESC aborts demo (closes file, clears state, resets last_tick); KP+/- adjust tick rate (clamped 1..255, recompute gnTickDelay=1000/nTickRate); then replay stored events via CreateSdlEvent; input disabled when CurrentEventHandler == DisableInputEventHandler.
  - `CreateSdlEvent`: rebuild SDL events from stored data incl. custom events (type - 64 → interface_mode); SDL1 fallbacks (key remap tables, wheel-as-button) can be dropped for Go/Ebiten — keep custom-event mapping.
  - Recording: `NotifyGameLoopStart` opens PrefPath/demo_N.dmo "wb", writes Version(3), gSaveNumber LE32, settings; `WriteDemoMsgHeader` uses the 0x80 inline-rendering packing when Rendering && ProgressToNextGameTick <= 127; `RecordMessage` serializes live SDL events (motion/button/wheel/key/quit/window-close/custom) with int16 wheel range check (fatal on overflow); `NotifyGameLoopEnd` closes file, optionally `pfile_write_hero_demo`, logs fps `LogicTick / seconds`, ends game, compares hero to reference via `pfile_compare_hero_demo` and logs Same/Difference/ReferenceNotFound.
  - `OverrideOptions`: fitToScreen=false, hardwareCursor=false, timedemo→frameRateControl=None, forceResolution = demo width/height, and all 22 gameplay options from DemoSettings.
  - `SimulateMillisecondsSinceStartup` = LogicTick * 50 (20 Hz assumption).
- 1:1 constraints: `Version = 3` (line 51); event type enum values (lines 76-91); settings byte order in ReadSettings/WriteSettings (lines 155-235 — note reserved adriaRefillsMana byte); inline rendering bit `0b10000000`/mask `0b01111111` (lines 530-533, 553-557); v1 compat mapping table (lines 425-446); `LogicTick * 50` (line 985); `gnTickDelay = 1000 / nTickRate` recomputation (lines 794, 798); default graphics 640x480 (line 149-150); demo filename pattern `demo_<N>.dmo` under PrefPath (lines 506, 856).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: all state is file-scope mutable globals (DemoFile, CurrentDemoMessage, Timedemo, RecordNumber, DemoSettings, LogicTick, DemoModeLastTick...); playback drives the global game-loop pacing and mutates global `ProgressToNextGameTick`; recording is a pure side-channel of the live loop; ESC-abort mutates globals mid-loop. Single-threaded (main loop) by design.
- Test coverage: `test/timedemo_test.cpp` (playback + hero comparison end-to-end).
- Go mapping: `internal/demo` — package with Recorder/Player over a Go event abstraction (Ebiten input events instead of SDL_Event); keep the .dmo byte format identical for cross-compat with C++ demos and CI references.
- Risks/open questions: Go port must define its own event enum mapped 1:1 to the stored type numbers; SDL-specific keycodes (u32 sym values are SDL keysym constants) — Go needs a stable keycode table matching SDL values or demos recorded by C++ builds won't replay; SDL1 code paths can be omitted.

### Source/engine/direction.hpp

- Depends on: only `<cstdint>`, `<string_view>`, `<type_traits>`, `utils/attributes.h` (DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE). No devilution symbols.
- Requirements for Go port:

  - Methods `Left()`, `Right()`, `Opposite()` with same modular arithmetic.
  - `DirectionToString` (port from direction.cpp, same names) returning string.
  - All logic is pure; no state.
- 1:1 constraints: enum ordering is semantically load-bearing (monster AI, walk dirs). `Left = (v+7)%8` (L24), `Right = (v+1)%8` (L30), `Opposite = (v+4)%8` (L36). NoDirection=8 is never passed through turn helpers in practice but Go must not panic on it.

### Source/engine/displacement.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only generic `DisplacementOf<DeltaT>` 2D vector (int default) with isometric world<->screen transforms, normalization, quadrant rotation, flips, and full operator set. The single most-used math primitive in the game.
- Public API: `using Displacement = DisplacementOf<int>` (L16). Ctors: default; converting from other DeltaT (L22); `(deltaX, deltaY)` (L31); explicit single scalar for both (L36); explicit from `SizeOf<SizeT>` (L43); explicit from `Direction` via `fromDirection` (L51, L247). Methods: `operator==/!=` (cross-type), `+= -= *= *=(float) *=(Displacement) /= /=(float)`, `float magnitude()` (L132–137), `worldToScreen()` (L151), `screenToWorld()` (L164), `screenToMissile()` (L174), `screenToLight()` (L184), `worldToNormalScreen()` (L195), `normalized()` (L213, def at L363), `Rotate(int quadrants)` (L215), `flipX/flipY/flipXY` (L228/234/240). Free ops: `+ - * (int/float/Displacement) / (int/float), unary-, <<, >>, abs()` (L349–360).
- Depends on: `appfat.h` (assert), `engine/direction.hpp` (fromDirection), `engine/size.hpp` (SizeOf ctor), `utils/attributes.h`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Generic or int-based struct `Displacement{X, Y int}`; float variants handled where callers need them.
  - Every transform must exist with identical arithmetic, since gameplay math depends on exact rounding.
  - Generic instantiation matters: template members returning `DisplacementOf<DeltaT>` keep the element type through ops; Go port can use int16/int32 instances — survey callers before fixing one Go type.
  - `magnitude()` uses float sqrt (sqrtf, L137) with int-square overflow asserts (L130–134, < 2^24) — Go: int64 squares cast to float32? No — `sqrtf(float(dx*dx+dy*dy))`: compute in Go as float32(math.Sqrt(float64(...))) matching float32 precision; asserts optional (panics in debug).
  - `normalized()` (L363–368): 16.16 fixed point: `(d << 16) / magnitude`.
  - Operators map to Go methods: Add, Sub, Mul(int), MulFloat, MulComp (componentwise), Div, DivFloat, Neg, Shl, Shr, Abs.
  - Build-tagged operator<< for tests only (L283) — Go String()/fmt.Stringer equivalent.
- 1:1 constraints (cite lines):
  - worldToScreen (L155–157): `{ (dy-dx)*32, (dy+dx)*-16 }`.
  - screenToWorld (L168–170): `{ (2*dy+dx)/-64, (2*dy-dx)/-64 }` — C++ trunc-toward-zero division; Go must replicate (int division in Go also truncates).
  - screenToMissile (L178–183): numerators `2*dy+dx`, `2*dy-dx`; offsets `+32` if num>=0 else `-32`; then `/64` (round-half-away-from-zero emulation).
  - screenToLight (L186–188): `{(2*dy+dx)/8, (2*dy-dx)/8}` trunc division.
  - worldToNormalScreen (L199–208): rotate `{dy-dx, -(dy+dx)}`, normalize (16.16), then `{nx, ny/2}` — note y divided AFTER normalization.
  - Rotate (L215–226): Sines={0,1,0,-1}; `quadrants=(q%4+4)%4`; sine=Sines[q], cosine=Sines[(q+1)%4]; result `{x*cos - y*sin, x*sin + y*cos}`.
  - fromDirection (L247–272): South(1,1), SW(0,1), W(-1,1), NW(-1,0), N(-1,-1), NE(0,-1), E(1,-1), SE(1,0), NoDirection(0,0).
  - normalized (L363): `Displacement(*this) << 16` then `/ magnitude` (element-wise float divide, trunc to int).
  - `*=` float (L93–98): `static_cast<DeltaT>(deltaX * factor)` — int*float then trunc.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: value type, no globals; all constexpr. Division semantics (C++ trunc) == Go int division for positive and negative numerators (Go also truncates toward zero) — safe.
- Test coverage: `test/math_test.cpp` has worldToScreen/screenToWorld/normalized golden values (e.g. (-96,-112), (39321,52428), (-60848,24339)); also `test/vision_test.cpp`, `test/path_test.cpp` consumers.
- Go mapping: `internal/engine` (geometry core) — pure struct + methods; port math_test.cpp golden cases verbatim.
- Risks/open questions: float32 vs float64 in magnitude/normalized must be pinned (C++ uses float; use float32 in Go to match bit-exact results). Template breadth (which DeltaT instantiations exist) — survey call sites.

### Source/engine/dx.cpp
- Purpose: SDL graphics pipeline setup and frame present: 8-bit back buffer creation, dirty-rect tracking, palette/surface lifecycle, CPU frame limiting, present with optional renderer/upscale path.
- Public API (via dx.h): globals `int refreshDelay` (L45), `SDL_Renderer *renderer` (L46), `SDLPaletteUniquePtr Palette` (L52), `SDLSurfaceUniquePtr RendererTextureSurface` (L56), `SDL_Surface *PalSurface` (L59), `bool RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface` (L75); functions `dx_init()` (L116), `Surface GlobalBackBuffer()` (L127), `dx_cleanup()` (L133), `CreateBackBuffer()` (L150), `BltFast(SDL_Rect*, SDL_Rect*)` (L171), `Blit(SDL_Surface*, SDL_Rect*, SDL_Rect*)` (L187), `RenderPresent()` (L261).
- Depends on: `controls/control_mode.hpp` (ControlMode), `controls/plrctrls.h`, `engine/render/primitive_render.hpp` (Surface), `headless_mode.hpp` (HeadlessMode), `init.hpp` (ghMainWnd), `options.h` (GetOptions().Graphics.frameRateControl/upscale), `utils/display.h` (GetOutputSurface, gnScreenWidth/gnScreenHeight, OutputRequiresScaling, ScaleOutputRect), `utils/sdl_wrap.h` (SDLWrap, unique-ptr types), `utils/static_vector.hpp`, `controls/touch/renderers.h` (RenderVirtualGamepad, FreeVirtualGamepadTextures), `palette_init` via `palette_init()` (palette.cpp).
- Requirements for Go port: With Ebiten, the SDL surface/renderer machinery is replaced by an *image-based indexed framebuffer + palette* abstraction:
  - Back buffer: fixed-size 8-bit indexed buffer (gnScreenWidth×gnScreenHeight) exposed as the global render target; `GlobalBackBuffer()` returns a Surface view of it.
  - Palette global; set at init; applied at present time (convert 8-bit indices → RGBA via palette) — Ebiten present hook.
  - `RenderPresent()`: each Ebiten frame, upload/convert back buffer to a *image.NRGBA/RGBA screen texture and draw via Ebiten; keep a "paused/inactive" branch: when gbActive is false, limit framerate / sleep and skip present.
  - Frame rate control options: VerticalSync (map to Ebiten FPS/vsync) and CPUSleep (LimitFrameRate logic, see 1:1).
  - BltFast(dstRect): dirty-rect recording — in Ebiten we can always full-present; keep DirtyRects semantics only if partial update perf is needed; may drop.
  - dx_cleanup: free textures, hide window — Ebiten game exit.
  - HeadlessMode: all present/blit functions become no-ops (used by tests).
  - Virtual gamepad overlay rendering hook when ControlMode==VirtualGamepad (skip in Go port; console target).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - LimitFrameRate (L96–111): only when option FrameRateControl==CPUSleep; static `frameDeadline` in µs (`SDL_GetTicks()*1000`); if `frameDeadline > tc` then `v = tc % refreshDelay; SDL_Delay(v/1000 + 1)` (ceil); else `frameDeadline = tc + v + refreshDelay` (note v=0 in that branch → deadline=tc+refreshDelay).
  - `refreshDelay` in microseconds (used as % operand and deadline add).
  - Dirty-rect path (L171–182): when rendering directly to output, a null dstRect OR DirtyRects reaching MaxDirtyRects=16 (L66) sets ForceFullUpdate; else push rect.
  - UpdateOutputSurface (L222–258): partial update only if `!ForceFullUpdate && !DirtyRects.empty() && pixels==lastPixels`; records LastPresentedPixels pointer for equality; otherwise SDL_UpdateWindowSurface full.
  - Present renderer path (SDL3/SDL2, L279–296): SetRenderDrawColor(0,0,0,255), RenderClear, UpdateTexture(full surface, pitch), RenderCopy, present; LimitFrameRate after present unless vsync option.
  - `RenderPresent` returns early on `!gbActive` with LimitFrameRate (or emscripten_sleep(1)).
  - CanRenderDirectlyToOutputSurface (L78–99): SDL1 variant vs renderer==nullptr + size==screen + 8bpp — mostly N/A in Go; document decision to always use back buffer.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable globals (refreshDelay, renderer, PalSurface, Palette, RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface, DirtyRects/ForceFullUpdate/LastPresentedPixels statics in anon ns, LimitFrameRate static frameDeadline). Main-thread only in practice; Go port should own these in a render singleton. Not tick-coupled but frame-coupled.
- Test coverage: none found for dx.cpp itself (SDL-dependent); headless mode covered indirectly via app tests. `test/visual_store_test.cpp` touches rendering pipeline states.
- Go mapping: `internal/render` — Ebiten Game wrapper (Update/Draw), back-buffer type, palette application, FPS limiter. Keep function names dxInit/dxCleanup/globalBackBuffer/renderPresent for auditability.
- Risks/open questions: whether to keep direct-render and SDL1/3DS paths (drop — desktop Ebiten only); how `Surface` primitive (engine/render) maps to Go image region.

### Source/engine/events.cpp
- Purpose: SDL event pump and dispatch: filters/handles raw SDL events (touch, controller, keymap, audio-device, RG350 bad keys, synthetic touch-mouse), converts to render coords, records/replays demo input, and invokes the single current input handler.
- Public API (events.hpp): `EventHandler CurrentEventHandler` (L151, fn ptr `void(*)(const SDL_Event&, uint16_t)`); `EventHandler SetEventHandler(EventHandler)` (L153); `bool FetchMessage(SDL_Event*, uint16_t*)` (L163); `void HandleMessage(const SDL_Event&, uint16_t)` (L172).
- Depends on: `controls/input.h`, `controls/padmapper.hpp` (PadmapperReleaseAllActiveButtons), `engine/demomode.h` (demo::IsRunning/IsRecording/FetchMessage/RecordMessage), `engine/render/primitive_render.hpp` (Surface? included for SDL_Rect types), `interfac.h` (IsCustomEvent), `movie.h` (movie_playing), `options.h`, `panels/console.hpp`, `utils/display.h` (PollEvent, renderer, MousePosition), `utils/is_of.hpp` (IsAnyOf), `utils/log.hpp`, `utils/sdl_compat.h` (SDLC_ConvertEventToRenderCoordinates, SDLC_EventKey), `controls/touch/event_handlers.h` (HandleTouchEvent), `HandleControllerAddedOrRemovedEvent` (controls).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - An input event abstraction replacing SDL_Event (key, mouse, wheel, finger/touch, controller axis/button, window events, quit).
  - Event pump per frame: fetch one event; translate into internal event; maintain a pluggable current-handler function pointer (SetEventHandler stores previous and returns it — used by menus vs game vs movies).
  - Demo record/replay hook: FetchMessage must route through demo mode when running (record raw events + modState when recording).
  - modState (key modifiers) must accompany each event.
  - Filter semantics preserved: unknown/unhandled event types are logged verbose and consumed (return true) rather than delivered.
  - Controller hot-plug handling hook before the main switch.
  - Touch→mouse synthetic events suppressed when not playing a movie (SDL behavior quirk) — in Go port with Ebiten input, decide whether this exists at all; likely not needed but document.
  - `FetchMessage_Real` calls `HandleDocking()` on Switch — platform-specific, skip.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Event-type allowlist (SDL3 L107–128 / SDL2 L131–148): gamepad axis/button, finger down/up, text editing/input, window resized/pixel-size/shown/min/max/restored/HDR/focus gained/lost, mouse wheel/motion/button down/up, joystick axis/hat/button — these are *delivered*; key events with unknown key, audio-device added/removed, keymap-changed are consumed via FalseAvail (verbose log + true).
  - Default: unknown types → FalseAvail("unknown", type).
  - `*event = e` full-copy semantics: only ONE event is returned per call; callers loop.
  - `event->type = static_cast<SDL_EventType>(0)` zeroing first (L71).
  - SetEventHandler (L153–158): calls PadmapperReleaseAllActiveButtons() BEFORE swapping the handler (prevents stuck pad buttons across modal transitions).
  - HandleMessage asserts CurrentEventHandler != nullptr (L172–175).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `CurrentEventHandler` global mutated by SetEventHandler; demo recording writes events (order = pump order); `HandleTouchEvent(e)` mutates global MousePosition on vita path. Main-thread only. Statics: none beyond anon-ns FalseAvail/FetchMessage_Real.
- Test coverage: none found (input plumbing); demo replay covered by demo mode code itself.
- Go mapping: `internal/input` — event types, pump adapter over Ebiten input (and demo recorder/replayer hooks), handler registry mirroring SetEventHandler/CurrentEventHandler.
- Risks/open questions: how many event categories the Ebiten port actually needs (keyboard/mouse/gamepad); whether demo-mode event capture format must stay byte-identical (only matters if sharing demo files with C++ builds — likely no).

### Source/engine/light_tables.cpp
- Purpose: Generates all runtime lighting data: 16 palette-index translation tables (per shade level), radius-based light falloff tables, and light-cone interpolation tables; with level-type-specific variants (Hell blood walls, Nest/Crypt lava brightening).
- Public API (light_tables.hpp): `std::array<std::array<uint8_t,256>,16> LightTables` (L20); `uint8_t *FullyLitLightTable` (L21), `*FullyDarkLightTable` (L22); `uint8_t LightFalloffs[16][128]` (L24); `uint8_t LightConeInterpolations[8][8][16][16]` (L25); `void MakeLightTable()` (L27).
- Depends on: `levels/dun_tile_data.hpp` (leveltype, DTYPE_*), `utils/is_of.hpp` (IsAnyOf), `engine/lighting_defs.hpp` constants.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Pure table generator, deterministic; call once per level load (leveltype-dependent output!).
  - Globals: LightTables [16][256]uint8, FullyLitLightTable/FullyDarkLightTable as optional (nil-able) references, LightFalloffs [16][128]uint8, LightConeInterpolations [8][8][16][16]uint8.
  - Preserve nil-vs-non-nil semantics of FullyLit/FullyDark — renderers branch on them (perf shortcut); Hell sets FullyLit=nil, Nest/Crypt set FullyDark=nil.
  - All arithmetic integer except falloff floats (see 1:1).
- 1:1 constraints (exact):
  - Shade-table generation (L23–44): for shade 0..15; step-groups `{16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,8,8,8,8,16,16,16,16,16,16}` (L28, 18 groups); `shading = shade*steps/16` (uint8 math); shadeStart=colorIndex; shadeEnd=shadeStart+steps-1; per step: colorIndex==0 → output Black(0); else `color = shadeStart + step + shading`; if `color > shadeEnd || color == 255(White)` → color=Black; store at colorIndex++.
  - `LightTables[15] = {}` — entire level-15 table zeroed (pitch black) (L46).
  - FullyLit = &LightTables[0][0], FullyDark = &LightTables[LightsMax=15][0] (L47–48).
  - Hell (leveltype==DTYPE_HELL, L50–64): shades=15; for i in 0..14, j in 0..15: `color = ((15<<4)/15 * (15-i) / 16 * (j+1)); color = 1 + (color>>4)`; write to indices `j+1` and `31-j`. FullyLitLightTable=nil (L62).
  - Nest/Crypt (L66–74): `std::iota` over first 16 entries = 0..15 for every table; then LightTables[15][0]=0 and entries 1..15 = 1; FullyDarkLightTable=nil (L72).
  - Asserts (L76–78): FullyLit non-nil ⇔ table0 is identity 0..255 (checked via adjacent_find); FullyDark non-nil ⇔ table15 all zeros. Port as debug assertions or test.
  - Falloffs (L80–102): maxDarkness=15.0f; for radius 0..15: maxDistance=(radius+1)*8; for distance 0..127: distance>maxDistance → 15; else factor=float(distance)/float(maxDistance); Nest/Crypt: `brightness = radius*1.25f; scaled = f*f*brightness + (15-brightness); scaled=max(0, scaled)` (quadratic w/ over-exposure, L90–94); else `scaled = factor*15` (linear, L97); then `scaled += 0.5f` (round, L99); store uint8.
  - Cone interpolations (L104–116): `a = 8*x - offsetX; b = 8*y - offsetY; value = uint8(sqrt(a*a+b*b))` (double sqrt) — indexed [offsetX][offsetY][x][y] each 0..7/0..7/0..15/0..15.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: depends on global `leveltype` at call time → must be called after level type known; tables are globals reused across levels (regenerated per level). Fully deterministic given leveltype. No RNG. Float math in falloffs — use Go float32 to match `1.25f` constants exactly.
- Test coverage: none found (no test file references MakeLightTable; only `test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp` touches light-table-adjacent rendering).
- Go mapping: `internal/render` (or `internal/engine/light`) — `MakeLightTable(levelType)` filling package-level arrays; golden-value unit test strongly recommended (generate expected bytes via C++ once).
- Risks/open questions: float32 rounding of `factor*factor*brightness + 14ish + 0.5` could differ from C++ in last ULP — verify with golden dump.

# Volume III — batch 015

### Source/engine/load_cl2.hpp
- Purpose: CL2 sprite/list/sheet loading layer. Under `UNPACKED_MPQS` it loads `.clx` directly via the CLX path; otherwise converts CL2→CLX with a fixed frame width. Also builds multi-file CL2 sheets (levels) by concatenating files behind a 4-bytes-per-entry offset header.
- Public API: `LoadCl2ListOrSheetWithStatus(name, PointerOrValue<uint16_t>) -> expected<OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet,string>`; `LoadCl2ListOrSheet(...)` (fatal on error); template `<size_t MaxCount> LoadMultipleCl2Sheet(tl::function_ref<const char*(size_t)> filenames, size_t count, uint16_t width) -> expected<OwnedClxSpriteSheet,string>`; inline `LoadCl2WithStatus(name, uint16_t)`; `LoadCl2(name, uint16_t)`; `LoadCl2(name, const uint16_t*)`; `LoadCl2Sheet(name, uint16_t)`; macro `DEVILUTIONX_CL2_EXT` = `".clx"` (L23, UNPACKED) or `".cl2"` (L27).
- Depends on: `OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet`/`.list()`/`.sheet()` and `OwnedClxSpriteSheet/List` (engine/clx_sprite.hpp); `FindAsset`/`OpenAsset`/`AssetRef`/`AssetHandle` (engine/load_file.hpp → assets.hpp); `FailedToOpenFileError` (appfat.h); `WriteLE32` (utils/endian_write.hpp); `Cl2ToClx(...).sheet()` (utils/cl2_to_clx.hpp, non-UNPACKED only); `PointerOrValue<uint16_t>` (utils/pointer_value_union.hpp); `StaticVector` (utils/static_vector.hpp); `MaxMpqPathSize` (mpq/mpq_common.hpp); `ASSIGN_OR_RETURN` (utils/status_macros.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package `internal/assets` (or sprite loader pkg) with `LoadCl2(name string, width uint16) ClxList`, `LoadCl2Widths(name string, widths []uint16) ClxList`, `LoadCl2Sheet(name string, width uint16) ClxSheet`, status variants returning `(T, error)`.
  - `LoadMultipleCl2Sheet(count, pathFn func(int) string, width)` generic with a compile-time max count: two passes — first pass opens each asset, records sizes, sums total; second pass re-opens and reads each file into the concatenated buffer at its offset, writing a 4-byte LE offset header first.
  - UNPACKED_MPQS branch must exist as a build mode: extension `.clx`, direct `OwnedClxSpriteSheet{data, uint16(count)}` from the concatenated buffer; MPQ mode: extension `.cl2`, run Cl2ToClx with the single width and take `.sheet()`.
  - Fatal-on-error wrappers: call the same `app_fatal` equivalent as the rest of the asset layer (read-only status variant returns error).
  - Missing file in first pass → immediate fatal `FailedToOpenFileError(path, err)`; open/read failure in second pass → same fatal.
  - The `LoadCl2ListOrSheet` non-status overloads terminate the process on error (app_fatal), the WithStatus ones propagate errors.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `sheetHeaderSize = 4 * count` (L41); offsets written as `WriteLE32(&data[i*4], uint32(accumulatedSize))` — little-endian 32-bit sheet offsets (L69).
  - `accumulatedSize` starts at `sheetHeaderSize` (L62), grows by each file size.
  - UNPACKED sheet cast: `OwnedClxSpriteSheet{ data, uint16(count) }` (L76).
  - Non-UNPACKED uses `Cl2ToClx(std::move(data), accumulatedSize, frameWidth).sheet()` (L78) — note it passes `accumulatedSize` (header+data), and `frameWidth` = the single `width` value.
  - `frameWidth` PointerOrValue only exists in the non-UNPACKED branch (L37, `#ifndef`).
  - `LoadCl2WithStatus` moves `.list()` out of the result (L84-87).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless; all state lives in returned sprites. No globals mutated. Buffer allocation size depends only on file sizes.
- Test coverage: none found for LoadCl2 itself (test/clx_render_benchmark.cpp uses CLX render, not this loader).
- Go mapping: `internal/assets/cl2.go`; mirror UNPACKED vs MPQ with two files or a build tag; sheet concatenation logic is pure byte manipulation — port exactly, incl. LE32 header.
- Risks/open questions: `LoadCl2ListOrSheetWithStatus` is only declared here (implemented in load_clx.cpp); in Go they merge naturally. `tl::function_ref<const char*(size_t)>` maps to `func(i int) string`.
