### Source/engine/load_file.hpp
- Purpose: Generic typed file-loading helpers: load a whole asset into a caller buffer (with sizeof(T) alignment check), load into arrays, allocate-and-load returning the buffer, and `MultiFileLoader` which concatenates several filtered files into one buffer while emitting per-file offsets (used for e.g. town/level composites).
- Public API: templates — `LoadFileInMemWithStatus<T>(path, T*)`, `LoadIntegralFileInMemWithStatus<T>(path, T*)` (OpenIntegralAsset), `LoadFileInMem<T>(path, T*)` fatal; `LoadFileInMemWithStatus<T>(path, T*, count)`, `LoadFileInMem<T>(path, T*, count)`; `LoadOptionalFileInMem<T>(path, T*, count) -> bool`; array overloads `<T,N>` for `std::array`; allocating `LoadFileInMemWithStatus<T=std::byte>(path, size_t *numRead=nullptr) -> expected<unique_ptr<T[]>,string>` and fatal `LoadFileInMem<T>`; `template<size_t MaxFiles> struct MultiFileLoader` with `operator()(numFiles, pathFn, uint32_t *outOffsets, filterFn=always-true) -> unique_ptr<std::byte[]>`.
- Depends on: `OpenAsset`/`OpenIntegralAsset`/`FindAsset`/`AssetRef`/`AssetHandle`/`ValidatAssetRef` (engine/assets.hpp); `FailedToOpenFileErrorMessage`/`FailedToOpenFileError` (appfat.h); `app_fatal` (appfat.h); `StrCat`/`BufCopy` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `StaticVector` (utils/static_vector.hpp); `MaxMpqPathSize` (mpq/mpq_common.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Typed loaders keyed by element size: `LoadFileInto[T any](path string, buf []T) error` with `size % unsafe.Sizeof/T-size == 0` check producing the exact error strings; fatal variant calling app_fatal.
  - Count-based variant reads `count*sizeof(T)` bytes without alignment check (mirrors C++ L48-56: only checks open + read).
  - `LoadOptionalFileInMem`: open ok AND read ok → true; any failure → false, no error surfaced.
  - Allocating variant: `LoadFileBytes(path) ([]byte, error)` returning buffer and optional numRead.
  - `MultiFileLoader`: offsets are `uint32` absolute within the concatenated buffer; after the loop `outOffsets[numLoadedFiles] = totalSize` (L148) — a sentinel end entry. Skipped (filtered-out) indices get no offset. First pass resolves all assets and sizes; second pass opens again and reads each into `buf[outOffsets[j]]`.
  - `ValidatAssetRef(path, ref)` failure in first pass → return nullptr buffer (not fatal); second-pass open/read failure → fatal `FailedToOpenFileError`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Alignment error strings: `"File size does not align with type\n<path>"` (L21-23, L40-42, L96-98); read failure error `"handle.read failed"` (L26, L54, L103).
  - `outOffsets[j] = uint32(totalSize)` before adding size (L146); final `outOffsets[files.size()] = uint32(totalSize)` (L148) — note `files.size()` counts only loaded files.
  - Path copies are `MaxMpqPathSize` char arrays, `memcpy` including NUL (L135-138).
  - Offsets are host-order uint32 values in memory (no endian conversion — consumers interpret them; CL2 sheet path converts separately).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless apart from asset system; MultiFileLoader offsets depend on filter predicate and file order — deterministic given same inputs.
- Test coverage: none found for these templates directly (assets_test.cpp tests the asset layer beneath).
- Go mapping: `internal/assets/loadfile.go`; generics `[T any]`; `MultiFileLoader` as a function `LoadMultipleFiles(numFiles int, pathFn, outOffsets []uint32, filterFn) []byte`.
- Risks/open questions: `LoadIntegralFileInMemWithStatus` uses `OpenIntegralAsset` (integral = integer-divisible asset reads; MPQ nuance) — confirm its Go counterpart semantics when porting the asset layer.

### Source/engine/load_pcx.cpp
- Purpose: Loads a PCX sprite as a CLX sprite list. UNPACKED mode loads the pre-converted `.clx` plus a sibling `.pal` for palette output; MPQ mode decodes PCX straight from the asset handle via `PcxToClx` (frame splitting by count or frame height, transparent color, palette extraction).
- Public API: `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList LoadPcxSpriteList(const char *filename, int numFramesOrFrameHeight, std::optional<uint8_t> transparentColor, SDL_Color *outPalette, bool logError)`.
- Depends on: `MaxMpqPathSize`, `DEVILUTIONX_PCX_EXT` (mpq_common.hpp / load_pcx.hpp); `BufCopy` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `LoadOptionalClx`, `LoadFileInMem` (UNPACKED: load_clx.hpp, load_file.hpp); `OpenAsset`/`AssetHandle` (engine/assets.hpp); `PcxToClx` (utils/pcx_to_clx.hpp); `LogError` (utils/log.hpp); SDL_Color/SDL_ALPHA_OPAQUE (SDL headers).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `LoadPcxSpriteList(filename string, numFramesOrFrameHeight int, transparentColor optional[uint8], outPalette []SDLColor-equivalent, logError bool) OptionalClxList`.
  - Builds path = filename + ext (`.pcx` MPQ mode / `.clx` unpacked mode); NUL-terminated in C++, plain string concat in Go.
  - UNPACKED branch: `LoadOptionalClx(path)`; absent + logError → log `"Missing file: {path}"` and return absent. If outPalette != nil: replace last 3 chars of path before ext with `"pal"` (i.e. `pathEnd-3`), load 768-byte pal file (fatal via LoadFileInMem on failure), fill outPalette 256 entries r,g,b from triplets, alpha = opaque (non-SDL1).
  - MPQ branch: `OpenAsset(path, &fileSize)`; not ok → optional log + absent; else `PcxToClx(handle, fileSize, numFramesOrFrameHeight, transparentColor, outPalette)`; failure → absent.
  - `numFramesOrFrameHeight` semantics: positive = frame count, negative = frame height (documented in header L14-20).
  - DEBUG_PCX_TO_CL2_SIZE prints filename to stdout before decode — debug-only, can be dropped or kept behind a flag.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Palette overwrite: `std::memcpy(pathEnd - 3, "pal", 3)` (L51) — assumes 3-char extension ("clx"→"pal" in-place), palette laid out as 256×3 bytes r,g,b (L53-61), alpha `SDL_ALPHA_OPAQUE` (255) on non-SDL1 (L59-60).
  - Path buffer is `char path[MaxMpqPathSize]` (L39).
  - MPQ mode passes `fileSize` from `OpenAsset` directly to PcxToClx (L66-75).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless; palette side effect only through outPalette pointer; logging side effect.
- Test coverage: none found for LoadPcxSpriteList specifically.
- Go mapping: `internal/assets/pcx.go`; UNPACKED branch as build tag or runtime mode flag; palette extraction trivially portable.
- Risks/open questions: The `pathEnd - 3` trick assumes the extension is exactly 3 chars — keep `.clx`→`.pal` mapping explicit in Go instead of pointer arithmetic.

### Source/engine/palette.cpp
- Purpose: Engine palette management: logical (level) vs system (rendered) 256-color palettes, global-brightness tone mapping, fade in/out, per-leveltype palette loads with random variant selection, palette color-cycling animations (caves/crypt/hive), and palette-driven transparency/blending table maintenance.
- Public API (globals): `std::array<SDL_Color,256> logical_palette; std::array<SDL_Color,256> system_palette;` (L26-27). Functions: `ApplyGlobalBrightness(dst, src)`; `ApplyFadeLevel(fadeval, dst, src)`; `UpdateSystemPalette(src)`; `SystemPaletteUpdated(first=0, ncolor=256)`; `palette_init()`; `LoadPalette(path)`; `LoadPaletteAndInitBlending(path)`; `LoadRndLvlPal(dungeon_type)`; `IncreaseBrightness()`; `DecreaseBrightness()`; `UpdateBrightness(int)->int`; `BlackPalette()`; `PaletteFadeIn(fr, srcPalette)`; `PaletteFadeOut(fr, srcPalette)`; `palette_update_caves()`; `palette_update_crypt()`; `palette_update_hive()`; `SetLogicalPaletteColor(i, color)`.
- Depends on: `GetOptions().Graphics.brightness`, `.alternateNestArt` (options.h); `LoadFileInMem` (engine/load_file.hpp); `RandomIntBetween` (engine/random.hpp); `leveltype`/`dungeon_type`/`DTYPE_*` (levels/gendung_defs.hpp via palette.h); `HeadlessMode` (headless_mode.hpp); `demo::IsRunning()` (engine/demomode.h); `Palette`/`PalSurface`/`SDLC_SetSurfaceAndPaletteColors`/`ErrSdl()` (engine/dx.h, utils/sdl_compat.h); `BltFast`/`RenderPresent`/`RedrawEverything` (engine/dx.h, engine/backbuffer_state.hpp); `IsHardwareCursor`/`ReinitializeHardwareCursor` (hwcursor.hpp); `GenerateBlendedLookupTable`/`UpdateBlendedLookupTableSingleColor` (utils/palette_blending.hpp); `paletteTransparencyLookup` + `DEVILUTIONX_PALETTE_TRANSPARENCY_BLACK_16_LUT`/`UpdateTransparencyLookupBlack16` (render/ transparency lookup globals); `BufCopy`/`StrCat` (utils/str_cat.hpp); SDL_GetTicks/SDL_Delay/SDL_ALPHA_OPAQUE.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two exported 256-entry palettes: logical (pre-effects, but receives color cycling) and system (post brightness/fade, used for rendering).
  - Brightness option: clamp to [0,100] then round down to multiple of 5 at init (`LoadBrightness`, L33-38); Increase/Decrease step by 5 with min/max 0/100 then `UpdateSystemPalette(logical_palette)`; `UpdateBrightness(v)`: if v>=0 set + update; always returns current option value.
  - Tone mapping: per-channel LUT `toneMap[256]` built from slider value; `ApplyGlobalBrightness` writes dst from src via LUT; single-color variant recomputes `a` each call.
  - Fade: `ApplyFadeLevel(fadeval,...)` = `(fadeval * c) / 256` per channel (integer math), fadeval 0=black 256=identity. `PaletteFadeIn/Out(fr,...)`: if demo running → fr=0; fr>0 → animated loop `fr *= 3`, per-frame i = `fr * (now - tc) / 50` stepping 0..255, `SDL_Delay(1)` when i unchanged, apply fade level, `SystemPaletteUpdated()`, hardware cursor reinit when i!=0 (fadeIn) / always (after), `BltFast(nullptr,nullptr)` + `RenderPresent()` each step; skip-hardware-cursor-update-when-black optimization at i==0 in FadeIn; FadeOut applies `256 - i` and ends with `BlackPalette()`; sets/clears `sgbFadedIn`; final `RedrawEverything()` in FadeIn; non-animated path (fr<=0) still blits+renders once after setting palette.
  - Palette loads: `LoadPalette(path)` reads 256×3-byte file into Color array, converts to logical_palette with alpha opaque; headless → return early. `LoadPaletteAndInitBlending`: load then `GenerateBlendedLookupTable(logical, skipFrom=1, skipTo=31)` for CAVES/CRYPT, `(1,15)` for NEST, no skips otherwise. `LoadRndLvlPal(l)`: TOWN → `levels\towndata\town.pal`; CRYPT → `nlevels\l5data\l5base.pal`; else `rv = RandomIntBetween(1,4)`; NEST: rv++ unless alternateNestArt option, path `nlevels\l6data\l6base{rv}.pal`; others: `levels\l{n}data\l{n}_{rv}.pal` where n = int(l); then LoadPaletteAndInitBlending.
  - Color cycling: `CycleColors(from,to)` / `CycleColorsReverse` rotate ranges in logical_palette, system_palette, every row of paletteTransparencyLookup (columns), and the paletteTransparencyLookup row range, plus optional Black16 LUT update; `palette_update_caves` = forward cycle 1..31; `palette_update_crypt` = reverse cycles with lava every other call; `palette_update_hive` = every 3rd call, reverse cycles 1..8 and 9..15.
  - `SetLogicalPaletteColor(i,color)`: set logical, apply brightness to system[i], `SystemPaletteUpdated(i,1)`, `UpdateBlendedLookupTableSingleColor(logical, i)`.
  - `SystemPaletteUpdated(first,ncolor)`: headless no-op; asserts Palette; sets SDL surface palette colors from system_palette+first for ncolor entries; failure → ErrSdl (fatal).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `CalculateToneMappingParameter`: `a = -(brightness/100.0F) * 2.0F` (MaxAdjustment 2.0F, L96-99); brightness 0 → a=0 identity, 100 → a=-2.
  - `MapTone(a,color)`: `x = color/255.0F`; `y = clamp(a*x*x + (1-a)*x, 0, 1)`; return `uint8(y*255.0F + 0.5F)` (L101-109). Quadratic tone curve; float32 semantics matter for bit-exact output (use float32 in Go).
  - `ApplyFadeLevel`: `(fadeval * src) / 256` integer per channel (L134-141).
  - Fade loop step: `fr *= 3` then `i = fr * (SDL_GetTicks()-tc) / 50` (L190-191, L246-248) — i.e. 50ms per `fr` steps scaled ×3; uint32 arithmetic.
  - FadeIn skips `ReinitializeHardwareCursor` only when `i == 0` (L199-201); after loop always reinitializes if hardware cursor (L207); `sgbFadedIn = true` (L212).
  - FadeOut uses `256 - i` fade level (L252) and `BlackPalette()` at end (L263); `sgbFadedIn = false` (L272); guarded by `if (!sgbFadedIn || HeadlessMode) return;` (L217-218).
  - Cycle ranges: caves forward (1,31); crypt reverse (1,15) lava only when `!delayLava` toggle — note code sets `delayLava = false` inside (L296-299, effectively always cycles lava on its active turns; toggle is `delayLava = !delayLava` at L305) and reverse (16,31) glow every call, `SystemPaletteUpdated(1,31)`; hive: static `delay` counter, return unless `delay == 2`, then reverse (1,8), reverse (9,15), `SystemPaletteUpdated(1,15)`, delay=0.
  - Rotation formulas: forward `std::rotate(begin+from, begin+from+1, begin+to+1)`; reverse `std::rotate(begin+from, begin+to, begin+to+1)` (L58, L79 for logical; same for system and each transparency row; row-rotate uses `paletteTransparencyLookup[from][0]`, `[from+1][0]`/`[to][0]`, `[to+1][0]` — L65, L86).
  - `LoadRndLvlPal` buffer `char szFileName[27]` (L167); nest path `nlevels\l6data\l6base` + rv + `.pal`; normal `levels\l` + n + `data\l` + n + `_` + rv + `.pal` (L173-179); backslash separators literal (Windows-style asset paths).
  - `LoadBrightness`: clamp(0,100) then `SetValue(brightnessValue - (brightnessValue % 5))` (L33-38).
  - Brightness increase/decrease: ±5 clamped (L185-204).
  - `LoadPaletteAndInitBlending` skip pairs: CAVES/CRYPT (1,31), NEST (1,15), default none (L154-163).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable globals `logical_palette`, `system_palette`, `sgbFadedIn` (init true), static locals `delayLava` (crypt) and `delay` (hive) — per-process animation state tied to game tick callers. `LoadRndLvlPal` consumes `RandomIntBetween(1,4)` — couples palette choice to the global RNG stream (affects determinism/replays; demo mode relies on recorded RNG). Fade timing uses SDL_GetTicks — real-time coupled, but demo forces fr=0. HeadlessMode short-circuits most paths.
- Test coverage: none for palette.cpp itself; test/palette_blending_test.cpp + palette_blending_benchmark.cpp cover utils/palette_blending.hpp used here; test/text_render_integration_test.cpp touches palette usage.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/palette` (or internal/engine/palette): palette.go with the two [256]Color arrays as package state (guarded by the game-loop goroutine), tone/fade as pure functions (unit-testable), cycling as pure rotate helpers, SDL surface push replaced by Ebiten palette application + RedrawEverything event. RNG call must go through the same seeded engine RNG for demo parity.
- Risks/open questions: float32 rounding in MapTone must match C++ (`(y*255.0F)+0.5F` truncation via cast) — verify with golden vectors. `paletteTransparencyLookup` lives in render code (Volume for engine/render?) — cross-file dependency to resolve. Crypt `delayLava` logic looks odd (sets false then toggles) but must be replicated as-is for animation parity; fade timing loop is wall-clock based — for demo/timedemo parity keep fr=0 shortcut.

### Source/engine/path.cpp
- Purpose: A* pathfinding over the 8-direction tile grid with tie-breaking heuristics, plus closest-valid-position search via ring crawl. Custom fixed-capacity hash map for explored nodes and a bounded binary heap for the frontier.
- Public API: `const int PathAxisAlignedStepCost = 100; const int PathDiagonalStepCost = 101;` (L32-33); `int8_t GetPathDirection(Point start, Point dest)` (L180-183); `int FindPath(tl::function_ref<bool(Point,Point)> canStep, tl::function_ref<bool(Point)> posOk, Point startPosition, Point destinationPosition, int8_t *path, size_t maxPathLength)` (L185-289); `std::optional<Point> FindClosestValidPosition(tl::function_ref<bool(Point)> posOk, Point startingPosition, unsigned minimumRadius, unsigned maximumRadius)` (L291-296); test-only `int TestPathGetHeuristicCost(Point, Point)` under BUILD_TESTING (L293-299).
- Depends on: `Point`/`PointOf`/`DisplacementOf` (engine/point.hpp, engine/displacement.hpp); `PathDirs` (engine/path.h); `Crawl(minimumRadius, maximumRadius, fn)` (crawl.hpp); `app_fatal` (appfat.h); `c_find_if` (utils/algorithm/container.hpp); `StaticVector` (utils/static_vector.hpp); std heap algorithms.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A* with: frontier as min-heap of (position, f); explored map position→(prev, g); early exit when `initialHeuristicCost > PathDiagonalStepCost * maxPathLength` → return 0.
  - Pop loop: if popped position == destination → ReconstructPath; pop_heap; skip if `curG >= PathDiagonalStepCost * maxPathLength` (max steps approx); skip stale entries when `curG + h(cur,dest) > cur.f`.
  - Neighbor loop over the 8 `PathDirs` in PathDirs order; uint8 underflow guard: skip when `(cur.x==0 && d.deltaX<0) || (cur.y==0 && d.deltaY<0)`; neighbor ok→require canStep(cur,neighbor); not ok→allowed only if neighbor==dest; relax if unexplored (insert if bucket capacity allows) or better g; push to frontier if `frontier.size() < MaxPathNodes`.
  - Heap comparator (exact order matters for tie-breaking): min by f; tie → lower heuristic h; tie → prefer diagonal step (from prev); tie → smaller x; tie → smaller y. (C++ uses reversed `>` comparisons to invert the max-heap.)
  - ReconstructPath: walk prev chain from dest until g==0 (start); direction = GetPathDirection(prev,cur) per step; if length hits maxPathLength → return 0-length (path too long); reverse step order; fill remaining `maxPathLength - len` entries with -1; return len. Missing node during walk → app_fatal.
  - FindClosestValidPosition delegates to `Crawl` ring iterator testing `posOk(start + displacement)`, returns first hit or none.
  - Internal types: coordinates uint8 (dungeon fits), node index/cost uint16, MaxPathNodes=1024, hash map 64 buckets × capacity `3*1024/64 = 48`, bucket index `((x & 7) << 3) | (y & 7)`, key repr `(x << 8) | y`.
  - GetPathDirection: table {5,1,6,2,0,3,8,4,7} indexed by `3*(dy) + 4 + dx`.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Costs: axis-aligned 100, diagonal 101 (L32-33).
  - Heuristic (admissible): `diagSteps*101 + |dx-dy|*100` where diagSteps = min(dx,dy), dx/dy = abs coordinate deltas (L136-154).
  - `GetPathDirection` table and index formula (L180-183).
  - MaxPathNodes 1024 (L37); NumBuckets 64, BucketCapacity 3*1024/64=48 (L62-63); bucketIndex `((x & 0b111) << 3) | (y & 0b111)` (L105-108); repr `(x << 8) | y` (L110-113).
  - Comparator tie-break chain exactly: f asc, then h asc, then diagonal-preferred, then x asc, then y asc (L203-226).
  - Stale-node discard `curG + GetHeuristicCost(cur.position, dest) > cur.f` (L244).
  - Neighbor validity rules incl. destination-exception (L250-260); the inner re-check `if (curG >= PathDiagonalStepCost * maxPathLength) continue;` at L263 is redundant-but-present (curG didn't change) — harmless, replicate or drop.
  - ReconstructPath: path too long → len=0 break; fill tail with -1 (`std::fill(path+len, path+maxPathLength, -1)`) (L157-174).
  - Early bail: `initialHeuristicCost > PathDiagonalStepCost * maxPathLength` → return 0 (L189-192).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: fully deterministic given canStep/posOk predicates (no RNG, no clock); function-local state only (`frontier`, `explored`) — thread-safe as long as predicates are. Heap tie-breaking defines exact path choice; must match for replay/visual parity.
- Test coverage: test/path_test.cpp (heuristic via TestPathGetHeuristicCost, FindPath directions incl. "diagonals first" cases, FindClosestValidPosition) and test/path_benchmark.cpp.
- Go mapping: `internal/dungeon/path` (or internal/engine/path): `FindPath(canStep func(a,b Point) bool, posOk func(Point) bool, start, dest Point, path []int8, maxPathLength int) int`; Go container/heap with the same comparator; map can be a plain `map[uint16]node` (perf note: bucketed array was an optimization — keep semantics, may keep fixed arrays for cache behavior).
- Risks/open questions: `ExploredNodes.find` returning nullptr as `end()` means the heap comparator dereferences `explored.find(...)->second` for nodes guaranteed explored — safe in C++, in Go use zero-value semantics or assert. StaticVector overflow silently drops frontier pushes (bounded search) — intended behavior, document it.

### Source/engine/point.hpp
- Purpose: The core 2D point template `PointOf<CoordT>` (with `Point = PointOf<int>`) providing arithmetic, distance metrics (approx/exact/manhattan/walking), megatile↔world tile conversion, and `GetDirection` (best-fit compass direction between tiles).
- Public API: `template<typename CoordT> struct PointOf { CoordT x, y; }` with: converting ctor from other coord types and from `DisplacementOf` (explicit); `operator==/!=` (cross-type); `operator+=/-=` (Displacement and Direction); `operator*=` (float — truncates via static_cast<int> — and int); `operator/=` (int); unary `-` (signed only, static_assert); `ApproxDistance(other) -> int`; `ExactDistance(other) -> int`; `ManhattanDistance`, `WalkingDistance` (constexpr); `megaToWorld()`, `worldToMega()`; free operators `+`, `-` (point-point → Displacement, point-displacement → point), `*`, `abs(PointOf)`; `GetDirection(Point start, Point destination) -> Direction`; test-only `operator<<`.
- Depends on: `DisplacementOf`/`Displacement` and Direction→Displacement conversion (engine/displacement.hpp, engine/direction.hpp); `DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE` (utils/attributes.h); std::minmax/abs/sqrt.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Generic point type — in practice two instantiations matter: `Point` (int) and small-coordinate points (uint8 used by path.cpp). Go: either `type Point struct{ X, Y int }` plus `type PointU8 struct{...}` used by pathfinder, or generics `[T int | uint8 | ...]`.
  - Point − Point → Displacement (requires same signedness — static_assert; Go: separate signed/unsigned types or convert).
  - Direction addition: `Point + Direction` uses signed displacement of Direction.
  - `*=` with float factor truncates toward zero after multiply (C++ static_cast<int>) — Go int(float64) conversion truncates similarly; use float32? C++ float here is usually float32 — for exactness use float32 then truncate.
  - All distance functions: ApproxDistance (integer approximation), ExactDistance (int64 multiply before sqrt), ManhattanDistance, WalkingDistance (Chebyshev).
  - megaToWorld/worldToMega: world offset 16, scale 2; integer division in worldToMega (negative coordinates: C++ division truncates toward zero — dungeon coords are non-negative, but document).
  - GetDirection octant selection with 5×/2× comparisons (tan 22.5° approximation).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - ApproxDistance (L110-122): `offset = abs(p1-p2)`; `(min,max)=minmax(dx,dy)`; `approx = max*1007 + min*441`; if `max < min*16` then `approx -= max*40`; return `(approx + 512) / 1024` — ~5% error integer approximation; must match exactly (used for gameplay distances).
  - ExactDistance (L133-139): `int(sqrt(int64(dx)*dx + int64(dy)*dy))`.
  - Manhattan: `|dx| + |dy|`; Walking: `max(|dx|, |dy|)` (L146-155).
  - megaToWorld (L166-169): `{16 + 2*x, 16 + 2*y}`; worldToMega (L176-179): `{(x-16)/2, (y-16)/2}`.
  - GetDirection (L238-277): quadrant logic — mx>=0&&my>=0: `5*mx <= my*2` → SouthWest else South, then `5*my <= mx*2` → SouthEast; mx>=0&&my<0: `5*mx <= -my*2`... precisely: my negated first, `5*mx <= (my*2)` → NorthEast else East, then `5*my <= mx*2` → SouthEast; mirrored for mx<0 (West/North/NorthWest). The comparisons implement `slope <= 0.4 ≈ tan(22.5°)`.
  - `operator*=` float: `x = int(x * factor)` per coordinate (L81-86).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure value types, fully deterministic; ExactDistance uses sqrt (float) — deterministic within a platform; integer paths (Approx/Manhattan/Walking) bit-exact.
- Test coverage: no dedicated point_test.cpp; Point used broadly (test/math_test.cpp has none of Point per grep; rectangle_test.cpp, missiles_test.cpp exercise points indirectly).
- Go mapping: `internal/engine/geom` or `internal/dungeon` types package: `Point`, `Displacement`, `Direction` in one geometry package to mirror the interdependent operators; keep `ApproxDistance` constants exactly.
- Risks/open questions: exact float behavior of `ExactDistance` (sqrt on int64→int) — Go math.Sqrt on float64 matches; ApproxDistance must be ported with the same integer ops (no float) to stay bit-exact. Cross-type operator templates → Go generics or explicit conversions; choose based on how often uint8 points appear (path.cpp only).

### Source/engine/points_in_rectangle_range.hpp
- Purpose: Lazy iterable ranges over all points in a `RectangleOf<CoordT>` — row-major (`PointsInRectangle`) and column-major (`PointsInRectangleColMajor`) — implemented as C++ random-access iterators over a flattened index (used for level/room tile iteration).
- Public API: `template<typename CoordT> class PointsInRectangleIteratorBase` (protected: origin, majorDimension, majorIndex, minorIndex; Increment/Decrement/Offset); `class PointsInRectangle` with nested `PointsInRectangleIterator` (random access: `*`, `==/!=`, `>=/</<=>/>`, `-` (iterator difference), `++/--` pre+post, `+`, `+=`, `-=``, `-`, `[]`), `begin/cbegin` (index 0), `end/cend` (index width*height), reverse iterators `rbegin/rend`; `class PointsInRectangleColMajor` with nested `PointsInRectangleIteratorColMajor` (identical interface, transposed deref).
- Depends on: `PointOf`, `Displacement` (point.hpp); `RectangleOf` (rectangle.hpp); std::reverse_iterator, iterator tags.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Iterable over rectangle points in row-major order `{0,0},{1,0},{2,0},{0,1}...` and col-major `{0,0},{0,1},{0,2},{1,0}...` — Go: provide `func (r Rectangle) Points() iter.Seq[Point]` (Go 1.23+) plus reverse variants, or an index-based iterator type with `Next()/Value()`.
  - Flat index = `majorIndex * majorDimension + minorIndex`; majorDimension = width (row-major) or height (col-major).
  - Increment: `minorIndex++; if minorIndex >= majorDimension { majorIndex++; minorIndex -= majorDimension }`.
  - Decrement (L48-54): `if (minorIndex <= 0) { --majorIndex; minorIndex += majorDimension; } --minorIndex;` — note `majorDimension` is the constant stride, so the borrow adds the full stride after decrementing the major index.
  - Offset (L57-65): `majorIndex += (minorIndex + delta) / majorDimension; minorIndex = (minorIndex + delta) % majorDimension; if (minorIndex < 0) { minorIndex += majorDimension; --majorIndex; }` — C++ `/` and `%` truncate toward zero, hence the explicit negative fix-up.
  - Dereference: row-major `origin + Displacement{minorIndex, majorIndex}`; col-major `origin + Displacement{majorIndex, minorIndex}`.
  - End sentinel index `region.size.width * region.size.height`.
  - Reverse iteration supported (rbegin/rend over the same sequence reversed).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Iteration orders as above (comments L214-215, L315-316 confirm row-major vs col-major examples).
  - end index = `region.size.width * region.size.height` (L235-238, L435-438 — `cend` passes that index).
  - Increment/Decrement/Offset formulas verbatim (L43-66); `Offset` fixes negative modulo explicitly (L57-65).
  - Iterator difference: `(majorIndex - rhs.majorIndex) * majorDimension + (minorIndex - rhs.minorIndex)` (L171-174, L372-375).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure value semantics; no shared state; fully deterministic iteration order.
- Test coverage: none found dedicated (PointsInRectangle referenced in test/drlg_common_test.cpp and path_benchmark.cpp usage contexts).
- Go mapping: `internal/engine/geom` (with rectangle.go): implement as `iter.Seq[Point]` generators `PointsInRectangle(rect)` / `PointsInRectangleColMajor(rect)` + reversed variants; keep flat-index math identical. Random-access iterator semantics rarely needed by callers — check call sites; if `it + n` is used, expose an index-carrying iterator instead.
- Risks/open questions: confirm call sites don't rely on full random-access iterator algebra (only forward iteration + reverse is typical); Decrement/Offset edge cases for negative deltas are subtle — port with unit tests derived from the C++ formulas.

# vol3-016.md

# Volume III — batch 016

### Source/engine/random.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the global vanilla-compatible Borland LCG RNG, the non-deterministic xoshiro128plusplus seed generator, and the seed-saving/derivation free functions used across game logic.
- Public API: `sglGameSeed` (uint32_t global), `diabloGenerator` (global LCG), `seedGenerator` (global xoshiro), `xoshiro128plusplus::next/timeSeed/copy`, `ReserveSeedSequence()`, `GenerateSeed()`, `SetRndSeed(uint32_t)`, `GetLCGEngineState()`, `DiscardRandomValues(unsigned)`, `GenerateRandomNumber()`, `AdvanceRndSeed()`, `GenerateRnd(int32_t)`, `FlipCoin(unsigned)`.
- Depends on: `<random>` `std::linear_congruential_engine`, `<chrono>` system_clock, `<bit>` `std::rotl` (std lib only; no devilution deps). Header sibling random.hpp.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go package exposes global vanilla RNG state: `SglGameSeed uint32` and the LCG state; `SetRndSeed(seed)` sets both; `GenerateRandomNumber()` advances `x := 0x015A4E35*x + 1` (mod 2^32), stores to seed, returns it.
  - `AdvanceRndSeed` = int32(GenerateRandomNumber()), abs of it, with INT32_MIN returned as INT32_MIN (no panic; use explicit branch, Go math.Abs on float would be wrong).
  - `GenerateRnd(v)`: v<=0 → 0 (no RNG call); v<=0x7FFF → (AdvanceRndSeed()>>16)%v; else AdvanceRndSeed()%v — signed Go % must mirror C semantics (result may be negative in rare INT_MIN case; keep int32 arithmetic).
  - `FlipCoin(freq)` = GenerateRnd(int32(freq))==0.
  - `DiscardRandomValues(n)` loops GenerateRandomNumber n times.
  - `xoshiro128plusplus`: `next()` per algorithm below; `jump()` (2^64 advance); `timeSeed()` = nanoseconds since Unix epoch; copy by value ([4]uint32).
  - `ReserveSeedSequence()` returns copy of global seedGenerator then jump()s the global; `GenerateSeed()` = seedGenerator.next().
  - Static (default) construction of `seedGenerator` seeds from time then XORs std::random_device per word; Go: at init, seed from time + crypto/rand or OS entropy; skipped on AmigaOS/old-Win32 in C++ but Go always has an entropy source.
- 1:1 constraints: LCG: `std::linear_congruential_engine<uint32_t, 0x015A4E35, 1, 0>` (random.cpp:17) — recurrence seed = 0x015A4E35*seed + 1 mod 2^32; note libstdc++ initial seed() transform: passing seed s sets state to (s==0 ? 1 : s)... actually implementation detail: cppreference states min=1; **critical**: must verify against expected values in test/random_test.cpp (AdvanceRndSeed expected values 0,1,1,22695477 for seeds -1,0,1,2 in test lines 42–52) — those pin exact behavior including any seed() adjustment for 0. xoshiro next (random.cpp:24-44): `result = rotl(s0+s3,7)+s0; t = s1<<9; s2^=s0; s3^=s1; s1^=s2; s0^=s3; s2^=t; s3 = rotl(s3,11)`. jump constants (random.hpp:222): `{0x8764000b,0xf542d2d3,0x6fa035c3,0x77f2db5b}`, LSB-first over 32 bits each. AdvanceRndSeed INT_MIN special case at random.cpp:92-93. GenerateRnd 0x7FFF threshold at random.cpp:100.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `sglGameSeed`, `diabloGenerator`, `seedGenerator` are mutable globals with no locking; vanilla RNG order is gameplay-deterministic — all call sites must occur in identical order in Go. `seedGenerator` construction is a static-init order effect (time+random_device). Not thread-safe; single-threaded game loop assumed.
- Test coverage: test/random_test.cpp (9 TESTs incl. exact AdvanceRndSeed sequences and xoshiro jump/distribution tests).
- Go mapping: `internal/rng` (or pkg/rng): types `LCG`, `Xoshiro128PlusPlus`, `SplitMix32/64`; global vanilla funcs as package-level with explicit `SetRndSeed`. Copy exact constants; table-test against C++ test vectors.
- Risks/open questions: libstdc++ `lcg.seed(0)` behavior (maps 0→1? min()==1) must be confirmed from test/random_test.cpp expected values before finalizing Go seed handling; C++ `std::abs(INT32_MIN)` UB avoided — Go must mirror branch, not panic.

### Source/engine/random.hpp
- Purpose: Declares vanilla-compat RNG free functions plus self-contained generator classes: `DiabloGenerator` (instance-based vanilla RNG), `SplitMix32/64`, `xoshiro128plusplus`; also templated helpers `PickRandomlyAmong`, `RandomIntLessThan`, `RandomIntBetween`.
- Public API: classes listed above with all methods (`DiabloGenerator(uint32_t seed)`, `discardRandomValues`, `advanceRndSeed`, `generateRnd`, `flipCoin`, `pickRandomlyAmong<T>`, `randomIntLessThan`, `randomIntBetween(min,max,halfOpen)`); `SplitMix32(uint32_t).next()/generate(u32*,u32*)`; `SplitMix64(uint64_t).next()/generate`; `xoshiro128plusplus` ctors (default, `const state&`, uint64, uint32), `next()`, `jump()`, `save(state&)`; free functions declared for random.cpp.
- Depends on: `<random>`, `<algorithm>` (std::max), `<initializer_list>`; no devilution includes.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - All four generator types with exact state layouts: DiabloGenerator{lcg uint32}, SplitMix32{state uint32}, SplitMix64{state uint64}, Xoshiro{[4]uint32}.
  - `RandomIntLessThan(v)` = max(GenerateRnd(v), 0); `RandomIntBetween(min,max,halfOpen)` = RandomIntLessThan(max-min+(halfOpen?0:1))+min (random.hpp:376-396 region); both preserve rare-negative clamping only in LessThan (Between can still push negative if LessThan returned negative? no—LessThan clamps).
  - `pickRandomlyAmong(values)`: index = max(generateRnd(len(values)), 0); pick values[index] — Go generic `PickRandomlyAmong[T any](g, values []T) T`.
  - `DiabloGenerator` mirrors free-function semantics but on private state (used by logic needing isolated reproducible streams, e.g. item generation).
  - xoshiro `seed(uint64)` via SplitMix64 producing 2×u64 → s[0]=seeds[0]>>32, s[1]=seeds[0] low, s[2]=seeds[1]>>32, s[3]=seeds[1] low; `seed(uint32)` via SplitMix32 filling s[0..3] in order.
- 1:1 constraints: SplitMix32 (random.hpp:158-161): `z=(state+=0x9e3779b9); z=(z^(z>>16))*0x85ebca6b; z=(z^(z>>13))*0xc2b2ae35; return z^(z>>16)` (all uint32 wrap). SplitMix64 (random.hpp:190-193): `z=(state+=0x9e3779b97f4a7c15); z=(z^(z>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9; z=(z^(z>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb; return z^(z>>31)`. GenerateRnd bias-correction threshold `v <= 0x7FFF` (random.hpp:80). advanceRndSeed INT_MIN branch (random.hpp:58).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure types are value-safe; free functions share the globals from random.cpp. Header-only inline helpers consume global state.
- Test coverage: test/random_test.cpp covers AdvanceRndSeed/GenerateRnd vectors and (per its content) SplitMix/xoshiro/jump sequences.
- Go mapping: `internal/rng` package; generators as structs with methods, free functions as package funcs; generics for PickRandomlyAmong.
- Risks/open questions: none beyond the libstdc++ seed(0) nuance tracked in random.cpp entry.

### Source/engine/rectangle.hpp
- Purpose: Generic `RectangleOf<CoordT, SizeT>` value type (position+size) with contains/center/inset helpers and the square-around-center constructor; `Rectangle` alias = int/int.
- Public API: `template<typename CoordT, typename SizeT=CoordT> struct RectangleOf` — default ctor; `(PointOf<CoordT>, SizeOf<SizeT>)` constexpr; `explicit constexpr RectangleOf(PointOf<CoordT> center, SizeT radius)` (square 2r+1); `template<PointCoordT> bool contains(PointOf<PointCoordT>)`; `template<T> constexpr bool contains(T x, T y)`; `constexpr PointOf<CoordT> Center()`; `constexpr RectangleOf inset(DisplacementOf<SizeT> factor)`; `using Rectangle = RectangleOf<int,int>`.
- Depends on: `engine/point.hpp` (PointOf, DisplacementOf), `engine/size.hpp` (SizeOf), `utils/attributes.h` (DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Generic-free Go: `type Rectangle struct { X, Y, Width, Height int }` (or with Point/Size fields if those types exist); methods `Contains(x, y int) bool`, `ContainsPoint(Point) bool`, `Center() Point`, `Inset(dx, dy int) Rectangle`, constructor `RectAroundCenter(center Point, radius int) Rectangle`.
  - Half-open semantics: contains is x in [pos.x, pos.x+width), y likewise (rectangle.hpp:44-50 region).
  - Center: position + Displacement(size/2) — integer division truncation toward zero (C++ `/` on ints) must match Go integer division for positive values; negative sizes unusual.
  - Radius ctor: position = center − {radius,radius}; size = 2*radius+1 in each dimension (rectangle.hpp:30-37 region).
  - Inset: new position = position+factor; new size = size − 2*factor per axis (rectangle.hpp:62-69 region).
- 1:1 constraints: contains uses strict `<` on right/bottom edges (rectangle.hpp:47-49); Center uses `size / 2` via DisplacementOf (rectangle.hpp:57); radius ctor `2 * radius + 1` (rectangle.hpp:36); inset formula `size.width - factor.deltaX * 2` (rectangle.hpp:66).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure value type; no state.
- Test coverage: test/rectangle_test.cpp (3 TESTs).
- Go mapping: `internal/geometry` (with Point/Size/Displacement); plain struct + methods, no generics needed.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/engine/render/automap_render.cpp
- Purpose: Draws automap line primitives (diagonal atan(1/2) and steep atan(2) lines with 1px black shadow, N/S/E/W lines, and arbitrary Bresenham free lines) and the mode-aware `SetMapPixel`.
- Public API: `DrawMapLineNS(out, from, height, colorIndex)`, `DrawMapLineWE(out, from, width, colorIndex)`, `DrawMapLineNE/SE/NW/SW(out, from, height, colorIndex)`, `DrawMapLineSteepNE/SE/NW/SW(out, from, width, colorIndex)`, `DrawMapFreeLine(out, from, to, colorIndex)`, `SetMapPixel(out, position, color)`.
- Depends on: `automap.h` — `AutomapType` enum, `GetAutomapType()`, `MinimapRect` (Rectangle global), `AutomapType::Minimap`, `AutomapType::Transparent`; `engine/render/primitive_render.hpp` — `SetHalfTransparentPixel`; `engine/surface.hpp` — `Surface::SetPixel/w()/h()`; `engine/point.hpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Pixel-write order of diagonal templates is fixed: per outer iteration write shadow (y+1, color 0) then color at current x, advance x by DirX, write shadow+color again, advance x again, then advance y by DirY; final trailing pair after loop (automap_render.cpp:26-38, 41-53). Must preserve exact double-wide pixel pattern.
  - NS/WE lines clip manually: reject if fully outside, trim negative start, clamp to surface bounds, then loop SetMapPixel (automap_render.cpp:56-85).
  - `DrawMapFreeLine`: classic Bresenham err = dx−dy, e2 = 2*err, step x if e2 > −dy, step y if e2 < dx, no shadow (automap_render.cpp:126-150).
  - `SetMapPixel` semantics: Minimap mode → drop pixel if outside MinimapRect; Transparent mode → SetHalfTransparentPixel; otherwise direct SetPixel (automap_render.cpp:153-163).
  - All draws are bounds-checked/clipped or rely on Surface::SetPixel being safe.
- 1:1 constraints: shadow always written one row below color (offset +1 y) with colorIndex 0 (lines 27-31); template directions EAST=1/WEST=−1, SOUTH=1/NORTH=−1 (lines 17-24); free line `err = dx - dy`, `e2 = 2*err` comparisons `e2 > -dy` / `e2 < dx` (lines 130-145); NS clip conditions at lines 57-58.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: reads globals `CurrentAutomapType` and `MinimapRect` each pixel — behavior couples to automap mode set elsewhere; no writes to globals; pure rendering given surface.
- Test coverage: none found (no automap_render-specific tests; automap_test.cpp covers logic, not these primitives).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/automap` (or internal/render package); functions over a `Surface` type with `SetPixel(Point, uint8)`; keep per-pixel mode dispatch identical.
- Risks/open questions: `MinimapRect` containment check per pixel could differ if Go port changes MinimapRect semantics; verify contains() half-open behavior matches.

These formulas are the acceptance criteria for Go implementations.

### Source/engine/render/blit_impl.hpp
- Purpose: Core blitting primitives and blit-policy functor structs (direct copy/fill, color-map TRN, per-pixel lightmap, 50% palette blend, and blend+map / blend+lightmap combinations) shared by CLX and DUN renderers.
- Public API: `BlitFillDirect(dst,length,color)`, `BlitPixelsDirect(dst,src,length)`; functors `BlitDirect`, `BlitWithMap{colorMap}`, `BlitWithLightmap{lightmap}`, `BlitBlended`, `BlitBlendedWithMap{colorMap}`, `BlitBlendedWithLightmap{lightmap}` — each with two `operator()` overloads: `(length, dst, src)` pixel-copy form and `(length, color, dst)` fill form; plus named free funcs `BlitFillWithMap`, `BlitPixelsWithMap`, `BlitFillWithLightmap`, `BlitPixelsWithLightmap`, `BlitFillBlended`, `BlitPixelsBlended`, `BlitPixelsBlendedWithMap`, `BlitFillBlendedWithLightmap`, `BlitPixelsBlendedWithLightmap`.
- Depends on: `engine/render/light_render.hpp` — `Lightmap::getLightingAt(dst)`, `Lightmap::adjustColor(color, lightLevel)`; `utils/palette_blending.hpp` — global `uint8_t paletteTransparencyLookup[256][256]`; `<cstring>` memset/memcpy; `<execution>` (optional unseq policy).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two-verb interface per policy: `BlitPixels(dst, src []byte)` and `BlitFill(dst []byte, color byte)`.
  - Direct: fill = memset(dst, color); copy = copy(dst, src).
  - WithMap: fill dst[i]=colorMap[color]; copy dst[i]=colorMap[src[i]].
  - WithLightmap: light level sampled per destination byte via lightmap.getLightingAt(dstPtr) — lighting array parallel to dst; fill: dst[i]=adjustColor(color, light[i]); copy: dst[i]=adjustColor(src[i], light[i]).
  - Blended (50%): fill: dst[i]=pal[color][dst[i]]; copy: dst[i]=pal[src[i]][dst[i]].
  - BlendedWithMap: fill: dst[i]=pal[colorMap[color]][dst[i]] (fill goes through colorMap first, line 137-140); copy: dst[i]=pal[dst[i]][colorMap[src[i]]] — NOTE asymmetric index order pal[dstColor][colorMap[srcColor]] (line 125-128) vs BlitBlended copy pal[srcColor][dstColor]: blended-with-map indexes [dst][src-mapped]; blended indexes [src][dst]. Both tables are the same 256×256 pal; verify order per line cited.
  - BlendedWithLightmap: fill: srcColor=adjustColor(color, light[i]); dst[i]=pal[srcColor][dst[i]] (lines 143-148). copy (lines 150-173): if length<1024 use stack buffer: litSrc[i]=adjustColor(src[i],light[i]) then dst[i]=pal[dst[i]][litSrc[i]]; else per-pixel loop dst[i]=pal[dst[i]][litColor]. Again [dst][litSrc] order.
- 1:1 constraints: exact index orders: `paletteTransparencyLookup[color][dstColor]` for BlitFillBlended (line 104-106); `pal[srcColor][dstColor]` BlitPixelsBlended (line 113-115); `pal[dstColor][colorMap[srcColor]]` BlitPixelsBlendedWithMap (line 125-128); `pal[dstColor][srcColor]` where srcColor is the lit source in BlendedWithMap paths (lines 156-158, 170-171). Fill-with-map blend = `BlitFillBlended(dst, len, colorMap[color])` (line 137-140). 1024-byte threshold for stack-buffer path (line 151). Light sampled from `lightmap.getLightingAt(dst)` BEFORE transform (lines 75-77, 96-98).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: reads mutable global `paletteTransparencyLookup` (set when palette loads); functors are stateless views over external buffers; no writes to globals. Pure function of inputs given loaded palette.
- Test coverage: test/palette_blending_test.cpp (for the lookup table itself); blit paths exercised indirectly via test/scrollrt_test.cpp and benchmarks (clx_render_benchmark, dun_render_benchmark).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/blit` package: `type Blitter interface { BlitPixels(dst, src []byte); BlitFill(dst []byte, color byte) }` with six implementations; keep the asymmetric pal index orders as separate documented methods.
- Risks/open questions: the [dst][src] vs [src][dst] pal index asymmetry between Blended and BlendedWithMap/WithLightmap variants is easy to get wrong in Go — pin with unit tests against C++ output bytes.

### Source/engine/render/clx_render.cpp
- Purpose: CL2/CLX sprite rendering: backwards RLE blitting with clipping (Y-only and XY), outline generation with a single-entry cache, in-place TRN application, point-in-sprite hit testing, solid-bounds measurement, and the 8 public draw entry points.
- Public API: `ClxApplyTrans(ClxSpriteList, const uint8_t *trn)`, `ClxApplyTrans(ClxSpriteSheet, trn)`, `IsPointWithinClx(Point, ClxSprite)`, `ClxMeasureSolidHorizontalBounds(ClxSprite) -> std::pair<int,int>`, `ClxDraw(out, position, clx)`, `ClxDrawTRN(out, position, clx, trn)`, `ClxDrawWithLightmap(out, position, clx, lightmap)`, `ClxDrawBlended`, `ClxDrawBlendedTRN`, `ClxDrawBlendedWithLightmap`, `ClxDrawOutline(out, col, position, clx)`, `ClxDrawOutlineSkipColorZero(...)`, `ClearClxDrawCache()`, (DEBUG_CLX only) `ClxDescribe`.
- Depends on: `utils/clx_decode.hpp` — `IsClxOpaque`, `IsClxOpaqueFill`, `GetClxOpaqueFillWidth`, `GetClxOpaquePixelsWidth`, `SkipSize`, `GetSkipSize(remainingWidth, srcWidth)`; `engine/render/blit_impl.hpp` — all six blit functors; `engine/clx_sprite.hpp` — ClxSprite width()/height()/pixelData()/pixelDataSize(), list/sheet iteration; `engine/surface.hpp` — `out[position]`, `out.at(x,y)`, `out.SetPixel`, `pitch()`, `begin()`, `w()/h()`; `utils/static_vector.hpp`; `engine/point.hpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - CLX RLE decode rules: control byte c: if !IsClxOpaque(c) → transparent run of c px (src+1); if IsClxOpaqueFill(c) → fill width=GetClxOpaqueFillWidth(c), color=src[1] (src+2); else pixels width=GetClxOpaquePixelsWidth(c), data at src+1 (src+1+width). `ClxBlitInfo` returns {srcEnd, length} (clx_render.cpp:37-49).
  - Backwards rendering: sprites stored bottom-line-first; `DoRenderBackwards` skips bottom-clipped lines via overrun-aware skipping (`SkipRestOfLineWithOverrun` + `GetSkipSize`), writes upward while dst >= out.begin(), decrementing dst by pitch per line and adjusting by src.width − remainingWidth for line overrun (lines 106-229).
  - ClipX computed by `CalculateClipX(x, w, out)` {left,right,width} (lines 56-66); full-width fast path uses ClipY-only variant.
  - Left-clip overshoot handling in DoRenderBackwardsClipXY: when a run crosses into visible area, blit partial run `length = min(remainingWidth, length - remainingLeftClip)` (lines 178-205); right clipping by consuming `unclippedLength` against remainingWidth then possibly skipping rest-of-line via overrun (lines 206-229).
  - Outline: `GetOutline<SkipColorIndexZero>` computes, per row, solid runs and emits outline pixels: left/right edge columns (x=begin−1 and x=end) and rows above/below solid spans; uses three bool rows and two run lists with rotation (0,1,2)→(2,0,1) (lines 236-375). Transparent overrun handling skips whole lines (lines 352-365). Cache keyed on spriteData pointer + skipColorIndexZero (lines 378-390); `ClearClxDrawCache()` nulls the key.
  - `RenderClxOutline`: position.x −= 1, position.y −= height; if sprite fits with 2px margin use direct `out.at` writes else SetPixel (clipped) (lines 392-413).
  - `ClxApplyTrans` mutates sprite pixel data in place (const_cast hack): every opaque pixel replaced by trn[pixel]; fill runs replace the single color byte (lines 415-437, 440-448).
  - `IsPointWithinClx`: walk from bottom row; skip lines via overrun until matching y; within row, transparent run past position.x → false; fill covering x → return color != 0; pixel runs → color != 0 at exact x (lines 453-500).
  - `ClxMeasureSolidHorizontalBounds`: scan all rows tracking min xBegin / max xEnd over opaque runs; early exit when xBegin==0 && xEnd==width (lines 502-530).
- 1:1 constraints: draw dispatch mapping: ClxDraw→BlitDirect, TRN→BlitWithMap, WithLightmap→BlitWithLightmap, Blended→BlitBlended, BlendedTRN→BlitBlendedWithMap, BlendedWithLightmap→BlitBlendedWithLightmap (lines 568-601). Cache limits: MaxOutlinePixels=4096, MaxOutlineSpriteWidth=253 (lines 237-238) — sprites wider than 253 asserted. RenderClxOutline bounds test `position.x + sprite.width() + 2 < out.w()` etc. (lines 396-397). Backwards cull: `position.y < 0 || position.y + 1 >= out.h() + srcHeight` returns (lines 213-214).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `OutlinePixelsCache` is a mutable file-scope static (single entry) — not thread-safe, stale-pointer risk if sprite memory freed without ClearClxDrawCache (hence the public clear). ClxApplyTrans mutates shared sprite data — permanent transformation, order-dependent. No RNG.
- Test coverage: test/clx_render_benchmark.cpp (benchmark only); outline/decode logic otherwise covered indirectly via scrollrt_test.cpp; no dedicated unit test file found.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/clx`: `Draw`, `DrawTRN`, `DrawWithLightmap`, `DrawBlended`, `DrawBlendedTRN`, `DrawBlendedWithLightmap`, `DrawOutline`, `DrawOutlineSkipColorZero`, `ApplyTRN`, `IsPointWithin`, `MeasureSolidHorizontalBounds`, `ClearDrawCache`; RLE walker + backwards renderer over byte slices with explicit index arithmetic replacing pointers.
- Risks/open questions: pointer-keyed cache must become (slice identity/hash or generation counter) in Go; StaticVector 4096 cap could overflow for pathological sprites — Go can use append but keep assert semantics via panic or error.

  - RenderLine* families per LightType: FullyDark opaque=fill 0 (ignore src); FullyLit=copy src; PartiallyLit=blit with tbl map; PerPixel=blit with lightmap. Transparent variants: FullyDark=blend-fill 0; FullyLit=blend src; PartiallyLit=blend with map; PerPixel=blend with lightmap (lines 120-214).
  - Square tiles: 32 full-width lines bottom-up (RenderSquareFull lines 317-325); clipped variant advances src by clip.bottom*Height + clip.left, draws clip.height lines of clip.width (lines 327-336).
  - TransparentSquare: RLE with signed int8 control bytes — positive v = v opaque pixels (then src+=v), negative = −v transparent; overrun across line boundaries handled via drawWidth loop and prefix bookkeeping (RenderTransparentSquareFull lines 343-363; Clipped lines 365-436 incl. left-clip overshoot partial-run render, right-clip rest-of-line skip via skipRestOfTheLine lambda).
  - Triangle shapes: lower triangle 16 rows of widths 2,4,…,32 (src offsets 0,2,6,12,…,240, total 272 bytes consumed, dst advanced 16 lines); upper triangle 15 rows of widths 30,28,…,2 (src offsets 0,30,58,…,238) — fully unrolled in C++ (RenderTriangleLower/Upper lines 457-507); Go may use loops with identical offset sequences: lower offsets k(k+1) for k=0..15, upper offsets 480−(2*32−w)(…) computed as cumulative: 0,30,58,84,108,130,150,168,184,198,210,220,228,234,238.

Left triangle lower part is offset by XStep*(LowerHeight−1) horizontally and dstLineOffset = pitch+XStep; right triangle uses plain pitch (RenderLeftTriangleLower lines 509-515 vs RenderRightTriangleLower lines 613-616). Left/right horizontal clip variants clamp per-row via startX/skip formulas (lines 517-543, 545-563, 624-652, 654-673).
  - Trapezoids: lower half = corresponding triangle lower; upper half 16 rows with prefix mask growing by PrefixIncrement (Left:+2 → transparent wedge on left; Right:−2 → on right). RenderTrapezoidUpperHalf handles first row fully opaque specially, then rows with prefixWidth from (Mask==Right?30:2)+increment stepping ±2 (lines 778-802). Clipped variants pass prefix − clip.left adjustments (lines 804-833).

### Source/engine/render/light_render.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the per-pixel lightmap buffer for the per-pixel lighting option (marching-squares interpolation of the 2×2 tile-light grid into isometric diamonds with 28.4 fixed-point triangle rasterization) and implements Lightmap construction/bleed-up for wall tiles.
- Public API: `Lightmap::Lightmap(...)` (full ctor), `static Lightmap::build(perPixelLighting, tilePosition, targetBufferPosition, viewportWidth, viewportHeight, rows, columns, outBuffer, outPitch, lightTables, fullyLitLightTable, fullyDarkLightTable, tileLights, microTileLen)`, `static Lightmap::bleedUp(perPixelLighting, source, targetBufferPosition, lightmapBuffer)`.
- Depends on: `engine/lighting_defs.hpp` — LightsMax(=15), LightTableSize(=256), NumLightingLevels(=16); `levels/gendung_defs.hpp` — MAXDUNX/MAXDUNY; `levels/dun_tile.hpp` — TILE_WIDTH(64), TILE_HEIGHT(32); `engine/render/overlapped_memset.hpp` — FillBytesUpTo64; `engine/displacement.hpp` (incl. Direction::NorthWest/East/West vector math); `engine/point.hpp`; file-scope `std::vector<uint8_t> LightmapBuffer` (persistent buffer reused across frames).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `RenderFullTile`: fills an isometric diamond centered at (position.x, position.y+1)-anchored top/bottom row pointers; top starts at lightmap + (y+1)*pitch + x − 32; rows grow w=4,8,…; final full 64-wide row (lines 25-37).
  - `RenderTriangle`: half-space rasterizer on 28.4 fixed-point CCW triangles; bounding box clamped to [0,pitch]×[0,scanLines]; half-edge constants with top-left-ish fill convention correction `(dy<0 || (dy==0 && dx>0) ? 1 : 0)`; per-scanline start/end via CalcStartX/CalcEndX using `DecrementTowardZero` (num − ((num>>31)|1)); fills rows with FillBytesUpTo64 (lines 48-139).
  - `InterpTable[n][d] = (n*16+8)/d` for n<15, d in 1..15 (constexpr, lines 141-152); Interpolate(q1,q2,lightLevel) = table[lightLevel−q1][q2−q1] — linear interpolation position along edge where lightLevel crosses.
  - `RenderCell`: marching squares over quad {q0=tile(pos), q1=E, q2=SE, q3=SW-reused}; shape bits 8/4/2/1 for quad[0..3] <= lightLevel; 16 cases emitting 0–6 triangles each with edge-interpolated vertices (fpCenter + (center_j − center_i) * factor); cases 5 and 10 use cell average (q0+q1+q2+q3+2)/4 to decide center fill and emit two different 4/6-triangle decompositions (lines 158-430). Full-cell case 15 uses fast diamond path when on-screen (lines 415-428).
  - `BuildLightmap`: buffer height = viewportHeight + TILE_HEIGHT*(microTileLen/2 + 1); rows += microTileLen + 2; buffer resized to viewportWidth*bufferHeight; memset entire buffer to LightsMax (15); expand start tilePosition by 2 tiles NW, targetBufferPosition − {64,32}, rows += 3, columns++; iterate rows: seed q3 = tileLights[pos+{0,1}]; per column compute quad, and if minLight < LightsMax, loop lightLevel from min(maxLight, LightsMax−1) down to minLight rendering cells; after each row return x, advance y by TILE_HEIGHT/2, alternate columns++/−− and x by TILE_WIDTH/2 zig-zag (lines 432-505).
  - `Lightmap::build`: if perPixelLighting, run BuildLightmap (filling the shared static buffer); construct Lightmap wrapping LightmapBuffer with pitch=viewportWidth (lines 507-521).
  - `Lightmap::bleedUp`: for wall tiles above lightmap top — computes clip rect vs source; copies bottom-up rows from source lightmap into a 64×32 caller buffer, duplicating (memcpy from row below) when clipped, with `bleed = max(0, (rowCount − TILE_HEIGHT/2)*2)` diamond narrowing; returns new Lightmap with outBuffer anchored at last visible row (lines 523-573).
- 1:1 constants: LightsMax=15 (lighting_defs.hpp:11); TILE_WIDTH=64, TILE_HEIGHT=32 (dun_tile.hpp:7-8); InterpTable formula (light_render.cpp:141-146); fill-convention bias (line 78); DecrementTowardZero (line 39-41); buffer growth rows/columns arithmetic (lines 436-447); shape bit assignment 8,4,2,1 for quad[0..3] (lines 186-190); cell average rounding `(sum + 2) / 4` (cases 5/10).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `LightmapBuffer` is a function-static std::vector reused across frames — Lightmap::build's returned spans alias it until the next build; single-threaded frame usage assumed. Not thread-safe. No RNG. Order of triangle emission affects nothing (additive fills of constant), but keep identical for byte-identical output only if overlapping — triangles do not overlap within a cell.
- Test coverage: test/light_render_benchmark.cpp (benchmark only); vision_test.cpp / scrollrt_test.cpp exercise lighting pipeline indirectly. No unit test for marching-squares cases found.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/light`: `type Lightmap struct` with OutBuffer/OutPitch/LightmapBuffer/LightmapPitch/LightTables/FullyLit/FullyDark; `BuildLightmap(...)` filling a package-level reusable `[]byte`; `BleedUp(...)`; marching-squares `renderCell` as a switch over 16 shapes. Fixed-point 28.4 helpers must be explicit (int arithmetic, shifts by 4).
- Risks/open questions: exact rasterization fill-convention must match C++ or per-pixel light edges will differ by a pixel — port CalcStartX/CalcEndX/DecrementTowardZero verbatim and golden-test against C++ renders. BleedUp pointer arithmetic with negative offsets (outLoc before buffer start) needs careful Go slice-index translation; keep as raw offsets into a flat []byte with explicit index math.

# vol3-017.md

# Volume III — batch 017

### Source/engine/render/overlapped_memset.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only micro-optimization primitives: copy/fill of 0–32 (or 0–64) byte blocks via fixed-size overlapping stores so the compiler emits inline mov instructions instead of calls to memcpy/memset.
- Public API: (all `DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE`, in `devilution` namespace)
  - `void CopyBytesUpTo32(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, int n)`
  - `void FillBytesUpTo32(uint8_t *dst, int n, uint8_t value)`
  - `void FillBytesUpTo64(uint8_t *dst, int n, uint8_t value)`
- Depends on: `<cassert>` (assert), `<cstdint>`, `<cstring>` (memcpy), `utils/attributes.h` for `DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE` / `DVL_RESTRICT`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Provide equivalents in a render-utility package; consumers are the CEL/CLX/dun renderers' fast inner loops.
  - Behavior must be byte-exact: result identical to plain copy/fill for 0 < n ≤ limit.
  - n > limit leaves middle gap uninitialized — in Go slices must be pre-initialized or documented; safest is to assert/panic on n > limit (callers never exceed).
  - 64-bit path only is needed in Go (no 32-bit pointer branch).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Tier thresholds in order: n≥16 (4×uint64 / 8×uint32 stores), n≥8, then common n≥4 (2×uint32), then byte0 + (n≥2: last 2 bytes as uint16). CopyBytesUpTo32 lines 22–66; FillBytesUpTo32 lines 106–155; FillBytesUpTo64 adds an n≥32 tier (8×uint64) lines 191–201.
  - Fill constants: `fill64 = value * 0x0101010101010101ULL` (line 113), `fill32 = value * 0x01010101U` (line 121/149), `fill16 = value * 0x0101U` (line 152).
  - Reads-before-writes ordering in CopyBytesUpTo32 is only needed for exact dst==src-overlap aliasing; in Go, `copy(dst, src)` on non-overlapping slices suffices for semantics.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure functions, no state. Pure performance construct — in Go a simple loop or `copy`/`bytes.Repeat`-style fill yields the same observable bytes.
- Test coverage: none found (no test references to FillBytesUpTo32/overlapped_memset).
- Go mapping: internal/render — small funcs `copyBytesUpTo32`, `fillBytesUpTo32/64`; or just use built-in `copy`/loop and keep the assert bounds.
- Risks/open questions: none (semantics trivial; only perf differs).

### Source/engine/render/primitive_render.cpp
- Purpose: Implements primitive blitters: clipped/safe and unsafe H/V lines, rect fill (loop of H lines), half-transparent (blended) rect via palette transparency LUT (with optional 32-bit aligned fast path), half-transparent pixel, and a 2px inset border.

- Depends on: `utils/palette_blending.hpp` → `paletteTransparencyLookup[color]` (256×256 byte LUT), `paletteTransparencyLookupBlack16` (uint16 LUT, only when `DEVILUTIONX_PALETTE_TRANSPARENCY_BLACK_16_LUT`); `Surface` (`.at()`, `operator[]`, `pitch()`, `w()`, `h()`, `InBounds()`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `FillRect(out,x,y,w,h,color)`: height iterations of DrawHorizontalLine (line 41–46).
  - Safe H-line clip: reject if `y<0||y>=h||x>=w||width<=0||x+width<=0`; clip left (`width+=x; x=0`) and right (`width=w-x`) (lines 48–60); Unsafe = memset row segment.
  - Safe V-line clip analogous on y (lines 68–77); Unsafe walks `dst += pitch` per row.
  - Half-transparent H/V lines: compute `x0=max(0,x)`, `x1=min(w,x+width)` and SetHalfTransparentPixel per pixel (lines 79–107).
  - `SetHalfTransparentPixel`: bounds-check then `*pix = LUT[color][*pix]` (lines 193–200).
  - `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo`: full reject (sx+w<0, sy+h<0, sx>=w, sy>=h), then clamp left/right and top/bottom (`else if` so only one side clamps each axis) then blend via `DrawHalfTransparentBlendedRectTo` (lines 109–127); colored overload identical but always uses unaligned per-pixel path with `paletteTransparencyLookup[color]` (lines 129–149).
  - Unaligned blend loop: `pix = out.at(sx,sy)`, per pixel `*pix = lookupTable[*pix]`, row advance `pix += pitch - width` (lines 19–29).
  - Aligned32 path (conditional compile): if `sx%4!=0` handle leading 1–3 cols, extend width to pitch when rect reaches right edge, handle trailing, then process 4 bytes at a time through `paletteTransparencyLookupBlack16` on two 16-bit halves (lines 32–83). In Go: the unaligned loop alone is byte-identical; keep aligned path optional.
  - `UnsafeDrawBorder2px`: memset top two rows full width, then rows 4..h-1 set only cols 0,1 and w-2,w-1 (note: rows 2 and 3 — indexes 2,3 — only get the side pixels because loop starts at i=4... actually side pixels for rows 2..h-3), then memset last two rows (lines 202–217).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Blend formula: `*pix = paletteTransparencyLookup[color][*pix]` (line 22) — dest-color-indexed lookup, not alpha math.
  - Aligned variant per-uint32: `*pix = lut16[v & 0xFFFF] | (lut16[(v >> 16) & 0xFFFF] << 16)` (line 44).
  - Border loop `for (size_t i = 4; i < height; ++i)` (line 210) — first side-only row is index 4? No: indexes 2..h-3 get sides via this loop starting at 4 only for i≥4; rows 2,3 get nothing except from the two top memsets. Port loop bounds exactly.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless; depends on global palette LUTs being set (palette load order matters — LUT must be built before any half-transparent draw).
- Test coverage: none found (no primitive_render test file).
- Go mapping: internal/render — same function set over a byte-slice Surface with pitch; keep an internal `unsafe` set (no clip) and safe wrappers.
- Risks/open questions: `paletteTransparencyLookupBlack16` alignment fast path can be omitted in Go if LUT semantics preserved; verify border loop off-by-two against a visual test.

### Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp
- Purpose: The core scene renderer: computes viewport tile geometry, draws floor/cell/wall tiles, corpses, items, objects, players, monsters, missiles with lighting and TRN tinting; OOB dirt/black tiles; zoom; then orchestrates every UI overlay (automap, panels, flasks, XP bar, messages) and presents the frame; also FPS meter and dirty-rect blit.
- Public API (extern-visible): globals `AutoMapShowItems`, `frameflag`; `GetOffsetForWalking`, `ClearCursor`, `ShiftGrid`, `RowsCoveredByPanel`, `CalcTileOffset`, `TilesInView`, `CalcViewportGeometry`, `GetScreenPosition`, `ClearScreenBuffer`, `ScrollView` (_DEBUG), `EnableFrameCount`, `scrollrt_draw_game_screen`, `DrawAndBlit` (header scrollrt.h).
- Depends on: nearly the whole game: `dPiece/dMonster/dPlayer/dItem/dCorpse/dTransVal/dSpecial/dFlags/dLight` (levels/gendung.h), `DPieceMicros`, `pDungeonCels`, `pSpecialCels`, `MicroTileLen`, `TransList` (levels/*), `LightTables/LightsMax` + `Lightmap` (lighting.h, light_render), CLX blitters `ClxDraw/ClxDrawTRN/ClxDrawBlended/ClxDrawBlendedTRN/ClxDrawOutlineSkipColorZero/ClxDrawWithLightmap/ClxDrawBlendedWithLightmap` and `RenderTile/RenderTileFoliage/RenderTileFrame/world_draw_black_tile` (render/clx_render, dun_render), `Missiles/Missile/GetMissileData/GetMissileSpriteData/IsMissileBlockedByTile` (missiles.h), `Players/MyPlayer/PlayerUnderCursor/InspectPlayer` (player.h), `Monsters/Towners/Corpses` (monstr, towners, dead), `Items/pcursitem` (items, cursor), `pcurs/pcursmonst` (cursor.h), `ProgressToNextGameTick/nthread_UpdateProgressToNextGameTick` (nthread), options (`GetOptions().Graphics.*`, `Gameplay.*`), screen globals `gnScreenWidth/gnScreenHeight/gnViewportHeight` (utils/display.h), backbuffer `GlobalBackBuffer/GetDrawnCursor/IsRedrawEverything etc.` (engine/backbuffer_state, control.h Redraw*), `AnimInfo::baseValueFraction`, `TILE_WIDTH/TILE_HEIGHT/DunFrameWidth/DunFrameTriangleHeight/SidePanelSize`, dozens of UI draw calls (inv, gmenu, stext, help, chatlog, xpbar, panels/*, qol/*), `PalSurface`, `BltFast/RenderPresent` (dx), SDL timers.
- Requirements for Go port (grouped by function):
  - **Missile render interpolation** (`UpdateMissilePositionForRendering`, lines 129–137; `UpdateMissileRendererData`, 139–162; `UpdateMissilesRendererData`, 164–172): compute per-frame interpolated missile position from velocity*progress/baseValueFraction, `>>16` to pixels, `screenToMissile()` for tile offset; if interpolated tile != current tile and `CouldMissileCollide` at new tile, walk `progress` down by 1 until back in old tile or progress≤0 (reset to tile+offset). Bucket missiles per tile in `MissilesAtRenderingTile` map, rebuilt every DrawGame.
  - **Cursor save/restore** (`BlitCursor`/`UndrawCursor`/`DrawCursor`/`ShouldShowCursor`, 185–281): software cursor draws behind-buffer save/restore; hide conditions (control mode, CURSOR_TELEPORT, invflag, charpanel with statpts); item cursor offset `cursSize/2`, outline +1px, Clip lambda for screen edges; `PrevCursorRect` tracked for dirty blit. Hardware cursor path toggles visibility only.
  - **Entity draws**: `DrawMissilePrivate/DrawMissile` (283–318): skip if `_miPreFlag != pre || !_miDrawFlag`; render pos = target + offsetForRendering − `{_miAnimWidth2,0}`; TRN if `_miUniqTrans`, else light if `_miLightFlag`, else plain. `DrawMonster` (320–352): NULL sprite log; infravision TRN when tile unlit; unique TRN; stone TRN when Petrified; infravision if `_pInfraFlag && lightTableIndex > 8`; else ClxDrawLight. `DrawPlayerIconHelper/DrawPlayerIcons` (354–394): ManaShield/Reflect missile graphics at −animWidth2, Reflect shifted +{0,16}; only lit for non-MyPlayer; walking offset applied. `GetPlayerOutlineColor` (448–460): 4-entry table from PAL16_*+7, fallback to Player1 color. `DrawPlayer` (462–500): skip-if-dark conditions incl. arena/town exceptions; outline if under cursor; MyPlayer non-Nest/Crypt drawn unlit + icons; infravision TRN when unlit or (infra/arena && light>8); otherwise `lightTableIndex = max(lightTableIndex − 5, 0)` then ClxDrawLight. `DrawDeadPlayer` (502–519): clears then re-sets `DungeonFlag::DeadPlayer`, draws matching dead players at tile. `DrawObject` (521–535): outline if under cursor; ClxDrawLight if `applyLighting` else plain. `DrawItem` (713–725): outline when `itemIndex==pcursitem || AutoMapShowItems` (and not in store); label queued when last frame or magic rock.
  - **Tile rendering** (`DrawCell` 537–646, `DrawFloorTile` 648–712, `DrawDungeon` 799–969): exact micro-tile iteration — first two blocks mt[0]/mt[1] with mask selection from TileType + TransparentLeft/Right properties when transparency (`TransList[dTransVal]`); foliage path for floor+TransparentSquare via `RenderTileFoliage`; then loop `i=2; i<MicroTileLen; i+=2` with `targetBufferPosition.y -= TILE_HEIGHT` per row and right frame at `+{DunFrameWidth,0}`; per-tile `Lightmap::bleedUp` into a 64×32 stack buffer. DrawDungeon order: DrawCell → pre-missiles (if MissilePreFlag) → corpse (`dCorpse&0x1F` index, direction `(bDead>>5)&7`, unique TRN by translationPaletteIndex, only when `lightTableIndex < LightsMax`) → pre-object → pre-item → dead player → player (with negative-id movement offset logic) → monster (same) → post-missile → post-object → post-item → arch/special (`dSpecial−1` via pSpecialCels blended/lit, or town tree-leaf delayed draw from tile x−1,y−1 at −TILE_HEIGHT). Player/monster walking offset table: SW +{32,−16}, S +{0,−32}, SE +{−32,−16}, East-sideways +{−64,0}, tile += Opposite(dir) (lines 855–905).
  - **Row loops** (`DrawFloor` 971–997, `DrawTileContent` 999–1066, `DrawOOB` 1109–1146): isometric diamond walk — per row `tilePosition += East`, x += TILE_WIDTH; row end rewind `+= West*columns`, x −= columns*TILE_WIDTH; y += TILE_HEIGHT/2; odd rows: x++, columns−−, x += TILE_WIDTH/2; even rows: y++, columns++, x −= TILE_WIDTH/2. DrawTileContent adds `rows += MicroTileLen` and the wall-behind-lookahead (draw tile+East first, skipNext) when wall aligned on x-axis and walkable behind (lines 1030–1045). DrawOOB does rows+5; town → `world_draw_black_tile`, dungeon → `DrawDirtTile` (samples 2×2 dirt pattern at world (0,0)+parity, clamped, fallback black; lines 1068–1107).
  - **Zoom** (1148–1193): 2× nearest-neighbor upscale of the top-left quadrant into the viewport, bottom-up right-to-left, with odd-width/height extra copy, panel-aware viewport width.
  - **Viewport math** (`CalcFirstTilePosition` 1195–1246, `DrawGame` 1248–1330, `CalcTileOffset`/`TilesInView`/`CalcViewportGeometry` 1648–1720): panel-cover adjustments (±TILE_WIDTH multipliers, SidePanelSize.width offset), walking-direction extra rows/columns per direction table (N/S +2 rows; NE +1 col +2 rows; E/W +1 col; SE/SW/NW +1 col +1 row), `Lightmap::build(...)` params, then DrawFloor/DrawTileContent/DrawOOB in that order, optional Zoom, optional DUN_RENDER_STATS overlay.
  - **DrawView** (1333–1436): automap over viewport, _DEBUG grid overlay, item labels, monster health bar, floating numbers, store text, inventory/spellbook, durability icons, level button, char/quest/stash/visualstore panels, unique info, qtext, spell list, gold split/withdraw, help, chatlog, death red-back + text, pause menu, diablo msg, controller hints, player messages, gmenu, doom, infobox, life/mana percent update + upper flasks — exact order as listed (lines 1401–1435).
  - **DrawFPS** (1438–1470): static counters; 1s update window; `fps = 1000*10*frames/ms`; formatting `BufCopy(buf, fps/10, ".", fps%10, " FPS")` variants; drawn at {8,8} in red.
  - **DoBlitScreen/DrawMain** (1472–1545): SDL rect blit of dirty regions — main viewport {0,0,w,hgt}; belt {204,5,232,28}; desc box (chat variant {171,6,298,116} vs InfoBoxRect); mana {460,0,88,72}+{564,64,56,56}; hp {96,0,88,72}; buttons {8,7,74,114}+{559,7,74,48} and MP {86,91,34,32}+{526,91,34,32}; previous+current cursor rects.
  - **Public geometry helpers** (1573–1720): `GetOffsetForWalking` MovingOffset table; `ShiftGrid`; `RowsCoveredByPanel` (panelHeight/TILE_HEIGHT, halved when zoom); `CalcTileOffset` (`x=(w%TW)`, `y=(h%TH)`, then `(TW-x)/2` style complements); `TilesInView` (ceil div, zoom halves rounded up after even-rounding); `CalcViewportGeometry` (zoomFactor 2/1; playerPosition at {screenWidth/2,(screenHeight−panelHeight)/2} +TILE_HEIGHT/4 if zoom; tilesToTop/Left ceil-div; startPosition; tileShift via North*tilesToTop + West*tilesToLeft; extra NorthEast shift when tilesToLeft*TW ≥ playerPosition.x; extra North row when tilesToTop*TH < playerPosition.y; tileOffset = {startX − TW/2, startY + TH/2 − 1}; tileRows/tileColumns ceil formulas lines 1717–1719); `GetScreenPosition` (firstTile − tile, worldToScreen + offset).
  - **Frame presenters** (`ClearScreenBuffer` SDL fill 0 unless headless; `scrollrt_draw_game_screen` undraw/draw cursor + DrawMain(hgt or full on RedrawEverything) + RenderPresent; `DrawAndBlit` full pipeline with redraw-component flags, nthread progress update, thread yields, flask values {134,28} HP and {w−138,28} mana with `_pHitPoints>>6` shifts and NoMana zeroing, floating info box, party panel, FPS, lua GameDrawComplete, DrawMain, _DEBUG console, RedrawComplete/RedrawComponentComplete loop, RenderPresent; lines 1737–1928).
  - **Static-init side effect**: `OptionChangeHandlerShowFPS` registers showFPS option callback at namespace-scope init (line 1548).
- 1:1 constraints (copy values):
  - Outline colors (lines 94–100): Player1–4 = PAL16_ORANGE+7, PAL16_YELLOW+7, PAL16_RED+7, PAL16_BLUE+7; Object = PAL16_YELLOW+2; Towner = PAL16_BEIGE+6; Monster = PAL16_RED+9.
  - `RightFrameDisplacement = {DunFrameWidth, 0}` (line 83).
  - MovingOffset table (line 1579): S{0,32} SW{−32,16} W{−64,0} NW{−32,−16} N{0,−32} NE{32,−16} E{64,0} SE{32,16}, scaled by animationProgress/baseValueFraction, negated in cameraMode.
  - Player light reduction `max(lightTableIndex−5, 0)` (line 492); infravision threshold `lightTableIndex > 8` (lines 346, 487).
  - DrawMain blit rects listed above with exact offsets (lines 1519–1539).
  - CalcViewportGeometry formulas incl. `tileOffset.y = startPosition.y + TILE_HEIGHT/2 − 1` (line 1710) and tileRows/Columns ceil divisions (1718–1719).
  - FPS: `1000 * 10 * framesSinceLastUpdate / msSinceLastUpdate`, threshold `>= 1000` ms, `buf[15]`, pos {8,8} (lines 1448–1468).
  - Zoom source corner `out.at(srcWidth−1, srcHeight−1)`, dst bottom-right, per-line `memcpy(dst−pitch+1, dst+1, viewportWidth)` doubling (lines 1158–1193).
  - DrawOOB extra rows = +5 (line 1114); DrawTileContent rows += MicroTileLen (line 1002).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Rendering is driven per-frame; `MissilesAtRenderingTile`, `tileOffset/tileShift/tileColumns/tileRows`, `lastFpsUpdateInMs`, `PrevCursorRect`, static FPS buffers are mutable file/module state — in Go make them fields on a Renderer struct. `nthread_UpdateProgressToNextGameTick()` must be called before DrawView (tick-coupled interpolation). `this_sdl_thread::yield()` twice per frame (lines 1896, 1911). Option callbacks registered at static init must become explicit init in Go. dFlags DeadPlayer bit is mutated during rendering (DrawDeadPlayer) — rendering has gameplay-visible side effect.
- Test coverage: test/scrollrt_test.cpp (13 TESTs: TilesInView/CalcTileOffset variants at 640×480 and zoom, RowsCoveredByPanel, ShiftGrid equivalents).
- Go mapping: internal/render/scrollrt (geometry + tile walkers), internal/render/scene (DrawView/DrawAndBlit orchestration) — geometry funcs are pure and unit-testable first; port DrawDungeon/DrawCell against golden pixel dumps later.
- Risks/open questions: DrawView couples to ~30 UI subsystems — needs a staged port order; DUN_RENDER_STATS/_DEBUG blocks can be dropped; SDL3 vs SDL2 keyboard/timer branches collapse in Go.
