### Source/engine/render/text_render.cpp
- Purpose: Font loading (per size + Unicode row, language override fonts, .clx with .pcx fallback), color TRN translation tables, glyph metrics (line width/height), word wrap, and the full UTF-8 DrawString engine with alignment, kerning-fit, highlight, cursors, per-argument colors, and the pentagram spinner cursor.
- Public API: `pSPentSpn2Cels` global; `LoadSmallSelectionSpinner()`, `UnloadFonts()`, two `GetLineWidth` overloads (plain text; fmt+args), `GetLineHeight(text, fontIndex)`, `WordWrapString(text, width, size, spacing)`, `DrawString(Surface, text, Rectangle, TextRenderOptions)`, `DrawStringWithColors(...)`, `PentSpn2Spin()`, `IsBreakableWhitespace(char32_t)`.
- Depends on: ui_flags.hpp (UiFlags color/size/align enums), clx_render.hpp (`ClxDraw`, `RenderClxSprite`, `RenderClxSpriteWithTRN`, `ClxDrawOutlineSkipColorZero`), load_cel/load_clx/load_pcx/load_file (asset loading incl. `LoadFileInMem` for .trn), utils/utf8.hpp (`Utf8CodePoints`, `DecodeFirstUtf8CodePoint`, `ConsumeFirstUtf8CodePoint`), utils/language.h (`GetLanguageCode`, `IsSmallFontTall`), utils/str_cat/format (`BufCopy`, `AsHexPad2`, `FormatRuntime`), engine/ticks.hpp (`GetAnimationFrame(2,500)` cursor blink, `GetAnimationFrame(8,50)` spinner), game_mode.hpp (`gbRunGame`), primitive_render.hpp (`FillRect` for highlight), app_fatal on missing fonts.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Font registry keyed by `(size<<16)|row` (line 164: `GetFontId`), each entry = base font + optional language override font (override glyph used when its width != 0, lines 68–72). Load order: try `fonts\<lang>\<size>-<row hex2>.clx` for zh/ja/ko (and tr row 0), then base `fonts\<size>-<row hex2>.clx`, then PCX fallback (256 frames, transparent color 1) when MPQ-packed, log error if missing.
  - Color translation tables: 19 entries (lines 87–107) loaded lazily from `fonts\*.trn` into 256-byte arrays; `ColorTranslationsData[color]` optional — DrawFont uses TRN render when present else plain (lines 321–330).
  - `GetColorFromFlags`: exact flag→color precedence chain (lines 109–133), ending default ColorWhitegold; ColorDialogWhite maps to in-game variant when `gbRunGame` (line 120).
  - Unicode row logic: `row = cp >> 8`; CJK rows 0x30–0x9F; Hangul 0xAC–0xD7; SmallFontTall when either (lines 135–154).
  - `GetLineWidth` (plain, 618–643): sum glyph.width()+spacing per codepoint (skip ZWSP, stop at '\n' or decode error), subtract trailing spacing; counts codepoints into charactersInLine; loads fonts with ColorDialogWhite.
  - `GetLineWidth` (fmt+args, 645–703): walks fmt and formatted arg values alternately, handles `{{`/`}}` escapes, `{}`/`{0}`-style args via FmtArgParser (positional single-digit or sequential `next_`), resets currentFont on arg boundary, firstArgOffset support.
  - `WordWrapString` (705–780): break at `IsBreakableWhitespace` (space, U+3000, ZWSP) or after full-width punct (，、。？！) when next isn't also punct; ZWSP zero width; single-word-overflow force break at current codepoint; rebuilds with '\n' inserts; preserves existing newlines.
  - `DrawString` (782–887): font size/color from flags; initial line width when centered/right/kerningFit; `GetLineStartX` (center uses `max(rect.x, rect.x + (w−lineWidth)/2)`, right = x+w−lineWidth, else x); rightMargin = rect right; bottomMargin = min(rect bottom + BaseLineOffset[size], out.h()) or out.h() when height 0; lineHeight default from GetLineHeight; VerticalCenter adds `max(0,(rect.h − (newlines+1)*lineHeight)/2)`; y += BaseLineOffset[size]; surface clipped via ClipSurface; PentaCursor suppressed at end-of-text; delegates to DoDrawString; PentaCursor drawn at `{x, y + lineHeight − BaseLineOffset[size]}` with wrap via MaybeWrap.
  - `DoDrawString` (452–613) + `DrawLine` (407–450): per-codepoint iteration; font per row with '?' fallback then app_fatal("Missing fonts"); frame = `c & 0xFF`; wrap when `x + width > rightMargin` or '\n'; per-line `drawLine` re-walks the line substring and draws each glyph with highlight (FillRect under glyph+spacing, last-in-range excludes spacing), cursor '|' blink `GetAnimationFrame(2,500)` or cursorStatic, renderedCursorPositionOut capture; returns bytes consumed = `remaining.data() − text.data()`.
  - `DrawStringWithColors` (889–985): same loop but arg color from each DrawStringFormatArg's flags; KerningFitSpacing recomputes spacing per line incl. mid-argument continuation offsets; line-start recompute on center/right.
  - `AdjustSpacingToFitHorizontally` (398–406): `spacingRedux = (overhang + chars − 2)/(chars − 1)` when lineWidth>available && chars≥2.
  - `PentSpn2Spin` = `GetAnimationFrame(8, 50)` (line 989); spinner sprite loaded from `data\pentspn2` frame height 12 (line 616).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `FontSizes = {12,24,30,42,46,22}` (line 82); `LineHeights = {12,26,38,42,50,22}` (lines 83 and 379); `SmallFontTallLineHeight = 16` (line 84); `BaseLineOffset = {−3,−2,−3,−6,−7,3}` (line 85).
  - ZWSP = U+200B (line 36). Font path format `fonts\<size>-<row:02x>.clx` (lines 175–181).
  - ColorTranslations array exactly as lines 87–107 (order matches text_color enum in the header; nullptr for dialog white/red, and index 7).
  - Cursor blink `GetAnimationFrame(2, 500)`; spinner `GetAnimationFrame(8, 50)`.
  - Highlight default color `PAL8_RED + 6` (header). DrawFont outline position `{position.x, position.y + glyph.height() − 1}` with color 0 (lines 322–324).
  - GetLineWidth returns `lineWidth != 0 ? lineWidth − spacing : 0`.
  - CJK/Hangul row ranges above; full-width punct set U+FF0C U+3001 U+3002 U+FF1F U+FF01 (lines 332–335).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `Fonts` map and `ColorTranslationsData` are mutable global caches (lazy load, never evicted except UnloadFonts); CurrentFont caches last row. In Go use a FontRegistry struct with sync.Once or explicit init; app_fatal on missing base font is a hard stop. Blink/spinner depend on tick time — deterministic under fixed clock injection.
- Test coverage: test/text_render_integration_test.cpp (3 TESTs covering GetLineWidth/WordWrapString/DrawString integration).
- Go mapping: internal/render/text — FontRegistry, ColorTRN, TextOptions struct mirroring TextRenderOptions; use Go's unicode/utf8 instead of utils/utf8; fmt-arg variant can be simplified to pre-formatted strings if callers pre-format, but per-arg colors need the arg list kept.
- Risks/open questions: FmtArgParser subset of std::format (single-digit positional only) — Go port should match the subset or pre-format; PCX font fallback only matters for MPQ-packed old assets.

### Source/engine/size.hpp
- Purpose: Generic 2D size template `SizeOf<SizeT>` with width/height, scalar arithmetic (add/sub/mul/div, float mul), equality, and a test-only stream operator; `Size = SizeOf<int>`.
- Public API: `template<typename SizeT> struct SizeOf { SizeT width, height; ... }` with constexpr ctors `(w,h)` and `explicit (size)`, operators `== != += -= *= (SizeT) *= (float) /=`, binary `+ − * /`, `operator<<` under BUILD_TESTING; `using Size = SizeOf<int>;`.
- Depends on: utils/attributes.h (DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE), `<ostream>` under BUILD_TESTING.
- Requirements for Go port: a `Size` struct {W, H int} with the same arithmetic helpers used across rendering (e.g. `cursSize/2` scalar division, `tileSize *= 2` in scrollrt debug). Float multiply truncates via static_cast (line 63) — Go int(float64) conversion equivalent.

From the paired .cpp (verified, lines 8–23): `pan = (delta.deltaX - delta.deltaY) * 256`, clamp to PAN_MIN..PAN_MAX; `volume = playerPosition.ApproxDistance(soundPosition) * -64`; early-return false when `volume <= ATTENUATION_MIN`. ### Source/engine/surface.cpp
- Purpose: Implements `Surface::BlitFrom` and `BlitFromSkipColorIndexZero` — manual 8-bit indexed blits between surfaces that may have different palettes (deliberately avoiding SDL_BlitSurface palette mapping).
- Public API: `void Surface::BlitFrom(const Surface &src, SDL_Rect srcRect, Point targetPosition) const` and `void Surface::BlitFromSkipColorIndexZero(const Surface &src, SDL_Rect srcRect, Point targetPosition) const`, via private template `SurfaceBlit<SkipColorIndexZero>`.
- Depends on: engine/surface.hpp; `Surface::Clip`, `Surface::at`, `Surface::pitch`, `operator[]`; `<cstring>` memcpy; SDL_Rect/Point types.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Blit routine over 8-bit index buffers: first clip srcRect + target position against the destination region; if resulting w<=0 or h<=0 return.
  - Row loop with per-surface pitch (Go byte slices with stride); row offset advance = pitch − copiedWidth when skipping zero (src and dst advance identically since same width copied), else advance by full pitch after memcpy.
  - SkipColorIndexZero variant: copy each byte only if source index != 0 (index 0 = transparent).
  - Plain variant: bulk copy of srcRect.w bytes per row.
  - Must respect independent src/dst pitches and the region offsets baked into each Surface.
- 1:1 constraints: Exact clipping = Surface::Clip (see surface.hpp lines ~117–137). Loop counts down `h != 0`. Skip test is `*srcBuf != 0` (surface.cpp lines 24–27). Advance: `srcBuf += srcPitch - srcRect.w; dstBuf += dstPitch - srcRect.w` (skip path, lines 29–30) vs `srcBuf += srcPitch; dstBuf += dstPitch` (plain path, lines 37–38).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: No globals; reads only src, writes only dst. Safe if caller guarantees no aliasing overlap (C++ shares the same assumptions).
- Test coverage: no surface_test.cpp; benchmarks test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp, test/clx_render_benchmark.cpp, test/light_render_benchmark.cpp exercise Surface indirectly.
- Go mapping: `internal/render` — type `Surface` (or `Index8Buffer`) with `BlitFrom`, `BlitFromSkipIndexZero`, `Clip` ported exactly; stride-based []byte access.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/engine/surface.hpp
- Purpose: Defines `Surface`, a non-owning view (SDL_Surface* + SDL_Rect region) over an 8-bit indexed pixel buffer with bounds-checked helpers, subregion views, clipping, and blitting; plus `OwnedSurface` which pins the SDL_Surface allocation.
- Public API: struct `Surface { SDL_Surface *surface; SDL_Rect region; }`; ctors: default, `explicit Surface(SDL_Surface*)` (region = whole surface), `Surface(SDL_Surface*, SDL_Rect)`; copy-assign defaulted; `int w() const; int h() const;` (region dims); `uint8_t &operator[](Point) const`; `uint8_t *at(int x, int y) const`; `uint8_t *begin() const; uint8_t *end() const` (end = at(0, region.h)); `void SetPixel(Point, uint8_t) const` (bounds-checked); `uint16_t pitch() const`; `bool InBounds(Point) const`; `Surface subregion(int x,int y,int w,int h) const`; `Surface subregionX(int x,int w) const`; `Surface subregionY(int y,int h) const`; `void Clip(SDL_Rect *srcRect, Point *targetPosition) const`; `void BlitFrom(...) const; void BlitFromSkipColorIndexZero(...) const;`. class `OwnedSurface : Surface` — `explicit OwnedSurface(SDLSurfaceUniquePtr)`, `OwnedSurface(int width,int height)` (8bpp INDEX8), `explicit OwnedSurface(Size)`.
- Depends on: engine/point.hpp (Point), engine/size.hpp via utils; utils/sdl_wrap.h (SDLSurfaceUniquePtr, SDLWrap::CreateRGBSurfaceWithFormat), utils/sdl_geometry.h (MakeSdlRect); SDL2/SDL3/SDL1.2 header shims; cstdint/cstddef.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go Surface type: a byte-buffer view with {buf []byte or *SDL-like, pitch int, region rect}; must support nested subregions that accumulate x/y offsets (subregion adds to current region, keeps pitch).
  - `at(x,y)`: address = base + region.x + x + pitch * (region.y + y) — Go: index = r.x + x + pitch*(r.y+y).
  - InBounds strictly on region dims; SetPixel writes only when in bounds (no error).
  - Clip algorithm: shift srcRect and clamp target exactly as in header (left/top overflow moves into srcRect, right/bottom truncates srcRect w/h).
  - OwnedSurface: allocates an 8-bit indexed buffer (Go: make([]byte, w*h) with pitch=w, or Ebiten *image.Paletted) and keeps it alive; Go GC removes the "pinning" need but keep the type for API parity.
  - Pitch is uint16_t in C++ (SDL field); in Go use int, but preserve semantics "may be wider than logical width".
- 1:1 constraints: `at` address formula (header, `at()` body); Clip order: x-negative, y-negative, x-overflow, y-overflow (lines ~117–137); end() = at(0, region.h); subregionX only mutates x/w, subregionY only y/h (keeps other region fields). OwnedSurface ctor uses bpp 8, format SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8, flags 0.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Surface views alias shared memory (backbuffer); not thread-safe by design — document single-goroutine render use. OwnedSurface adds ownership only.
- Test coverage: no direct surface_test; render benchmarks (test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp etc.) exercise it.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/surface.go` — `type Surface struct { buf []byte; pitch int; X, Y, W, H int }` with the same method set; `OwnedSurface` wraps allocation. Consider image.Paletted adapter for Ebiten.
- Risks/open questions: none.

Save msg timing currentTime+1000 (line ~355). Load uses fade 8 both directions.

### Source/hwcursor.cpp
- Purpose: Hardware (OS) mouse cursor management: builds SDL_Cursor objects from game sprites, handles scaling to display size, hotpoints, and fallback when unsupported. Only compiled for SDL2+ (guarded by SDL_VERSION_ATLEAST(2,0,0)).
- Public API: `CursorInfo &GetCurrentCursorInfo();` (file-static CurrentCursorInfo accessor), `void SetHardwareCursor(CursorInfo)`.
- Depends on: `DiabloUI/diabloui.h` (ArtCursor), `cursor.h` (DrawSoftwareCursor, GetInvItemSize), `engine/render/clx_render.hpp` (RenderClxSprite), `engine/surface.hpp` (OwnedSurface, Palette), `utils/display.h` (renderer, ghMainWnd, GetUIRectangle not used), `utils/sdl_bilinear_scale.hpp` (BilinearScale32), `utils/sdl_wrap.h` (SDLCursorUniquePtr/SDLSurfaceUniquePtr), `options.h` (Graphics.hardwareCursorMaxSize, hardwareCursorForItems, scaleQuality), MyPlayer->HoldItem.
- Requirements for Go port:

If not Enabled() → SetHardwareCursorVisible(false).
  - Game sprite build: size = GetInvItemSize(pcurs) + 2*outlineWidth (outline 1px if holding item); fill surface with palette index 1 as color key; DrawSoftwareCursor at {outline, size.h-outline-1}; hotpoint Center for items, TopLeft otherwise.
  - Scaling: ScaledSize computes renderer logical→output scale (SDL3: logical presentation rect / logical size / window display scale; SDL2: SDL_GetRenderScale); if scaled != original, convert to ARGB8888 then bilinear (unless scaleQuality == NearestPixel → SDL_BlitScaled/PIXELART).
  - Size gate IsCursorSizeAllowed: hardwareCursorMaxSize<=0 → always allowed, else scaled dims must fit.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Line 210: `TransparentColor = 1` (palette index; comment: colors 1-127 outside UI palette are safe).

### Source/interfac.cpp
- Purpose: Load/progress screens ("cutscenes"): picks a background by game transition message, draws it with a progress bar while a worker thread (or main thread on Emscripten) performs the actual level/game load via DoLoad, then restores state, fades, and sends network join-level command.
- Public API: `RegisterCustomEvents(); IsCustomEvent(SdlEventType); interface_mode GetCustomEvent(const SDL_Event&); CustomEventToSdlEvent(SDL_Event&, interface_mode); interface_msg_pump(); IncProgress(uint32_t steps=1); CompleteProgress(); ShowProgress(interface_mode uMsg);`
- Depends on: `engine/events.hpp` (EventHandler, SetEventHandler, FetchMessage, PollEvent, HandleMessage, DisableInputEventHandler, SdlEventType, SDL_EVENT_USER registration), `engine/load_cel.hpp`/`load_clx.hpp` (LoadCel/LoadOptionalClx), `engine/palette.h` (LoadPalette, logical_palette, BlackPalette, PaletteFadeIn/Out, UpdateSystemPalette), `engine/dx.h` (GlobalBackBuffer, PalSurface, BltFast, RenderPresent, RenderDirectlyToOutputSurface, ClearScreenBuffer), `loadsave.h` (LoadGame, LoadGameLevel, FreeGameMem, ENTRY_*), `multi.h` (NetSendCmdLocParam2, DeltaSaveLevel, GetPortalLevel), `plrmsg.h` (DelayPlrMessages), `pfile.h` (pfile_remove_temp_files, pfile_save_level), `game_mode.hpp` (gbIsMultiplayer, gbRunGame, gbIsHellfire, gbSomebodyWonGameKludge), `cursor.h` (NewCursor, CURSOR_HAND), `hwcursor.hpp`, `headless_mode.hpp`, `controls/touch/renderers.h` (virtual gamepad textures), `utils/sdl_thread.h` (SdlThread), setlvlnum/setlvltype/IsArenaLevel (levels), ReturnLevel/ReturnLevelType/ReturnLvlPosition, GetMapReturnLevel/Position, GetLevelType, myPlayer fields.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Cutscene selection: PickCutscene maps interface_mode (WM_DIAB*) to Cutscenes enum; town gate special cases (lvl 1 + NEXTLVL → CutTown; lvl 16 + NEXTLVL → CutGate); set-level special cases (SL_BONECHAMB → Level2, SL_VILEBETRAYER → PortalRed, arena → level type or town); default LevelType-based; unknown → app_fatal.
  - LoadCutsceneBackground: per-cutscene CLX/cel/pal paths + progress_id 0/1/2 (drives BarColor/BarPos selection); LoadCel(cel, 640) frame width; LoadPalette + UpdateSystemPalette(logical_palette); reset sgdwProgress=0; assert sgpBackCel empty.
  - DrawCutsceneBackground: fill 0, optional widescreen sprite centered on UI rect, main cel at y=479+uiY (480-1).
  - DrawCutsceneForeground: progress rect w=sgdwProgress, h=22, at BarPos[progress_id] + UI offset, color BarColor[progress_id]; BltFast+RenderPresent when DiabloUiSurface==PalSurface.
  - Progress flow: ShowProgress sets IsProgress, resets kludge flag, installs ProgressEventHandler, sets skipRendering=true with loadStartedAt; skips rendering while `loadStartedAt + skipLoadingScreenThresholdMs > ticks` (fast loads show nothing); otherwise InitRendering blits background into all backbuffers then PaletteFadeIn(8, saved palette).
  - DoLoad: per-mode choreography (save level or DeltaSaveLevel, FreeGameMem, set currlevel/leveltype/setlevel, LoadGameLevel with entry type), IncProgress sprinkled with exact step counts (1,1,2,load,2 etc. per case); on error pushes WM_ERROR with heap-allocated string; on success WM_DONE.
  - WM_DONE handler: NewCursor(CURSOR_HAND), restore palette snapshot, fill all backbuffers with full bar, PaletteFadeOut(8), UpdateSystemPalette(logical_palette), restore prev handler, IsProgress=false, NetSendCmdLocParam2(CMD_PLAYER_JOINLEVEL, tile, plrlevel, plrIsOnSetLevel?1:0), DelayPlrMessages(ticks-loadStartedAt), if gbSomebodyWonGameKludge && on level 16 → PrepDoEnding, clear kludge, done=true, reinit virtual gamepad textures.
  - IncProgress(steps): only if IsProgress; `sgdwProgress += 23*steps` clamped to 534; pushes WM_PROGRESS when changed and not headless; DOS yields 15ms; LOAD_ON_MAIN_THREAD variant pumps events inline.
  - CompleteProgress: headless/no-progress no-op; else IncProgress((534-progress)/23).
  - Threading: background SdlThread runs DoLoad (except Emscripten); main thread HandleProgressBarUpdate loops PollEvent; event handler chain DisableInputEventHandler + custom events.
  - Custom event plumbing: RegisterCustomEvents registers 1 SDL user event; GetCustomEvent reads event.user.code; CustomEventToSdlEvent writes it.

  - Lines 59-60: `MaxProgress = 534`, `ProgressStepSize = 23`.
  - Line 69: `BarColor[3] = { 138, 43, 254 }` (palette indices); line 71: `BarPos[3][2] = { {53,37},{53,421},{53,37} }`; line 241: `ProgressHeight = 22`.

Cel frame width 640.
  - Fade rates: PaletteFadeIn(8,...)/PaletteFadeOut(8,...).

Go port should use explicit channels/mutex instead; preserve behavior (progress events, error propagation, palette isolation).

SdlThread → goroutine with WaitGroup; WM_ERROR string ownership (new/delete) must become a value copy.

# Volume III — batch 020

### Source/interfac.h
- Purpose: Declares the load-screen/progress interface: custom SDL event registration/mapping and the progress-bar pump functions (`interface_msg_pump`, `IncProgress`, `CompleteProgress`, `ShowProgress`).
- Public API: `enum interface_mode : uint8_t` (WM_DIABNEXTLVL=0 … WM_DIABLOADGAME=9, async WM_PROGRESS/WM_ERROR/WM_DONE, WM_FIRST/WM_LAST bounds, lines 30–46); `enum Cutscenes : uint8_t` (CutStart…CutGate, lines 62–73); `RegisterCustomEvents()`; `using SdlEventType = uint16_t` (SDL2+, else uint8_t, lines 51–55); `IsCustomEvent(SdlEventType)`, `GetCustomEvent(const SDL_Event&)`, `CustomEventToSdlEvent(SDL_Event&, interface_mode)`; `interface_msg_pump()`, `IncProgress(uint32_t steps = 1)`, `CompleteProgress()`, `ShowProgress(interface_mode uMsg)`.
- Depends on: SDL events/version headers; `utils/ui_fwd.h`. Implementation lives in interfac.cpp (not in this batch).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go event enum mirroring `interface_mode` with identical numeric values (0–13) and WM_FIRST/WM_LAST sentinels.
  - A custom-event channel/queue abstraction replacing SDL custom events (Go/Ebiten has no SDL); `RegisterCustomEvents` becomes allocation of a base event ID range.
  - Progress-bar driver: `IncProgress(steps)` increments a counter, pumps messages, redraws progress; `CompleteProgress()` runs to 100%; `ShowProgress(mode)` performs the mode-specific level transition screen.
  - Cutscenes enum for selecting load-screen art per dungeon theme.
- 1:1 constraints: enum orderings exactly as lines 30–46 (NEXTLVL=0, PREVLVL, RTNLVL, SETLVL, WARPLVL, TOWNWARP, TWARPUP, RETOWN, NEWGAME, LOADGAME, PROGRESS, ERROR, DONE); Cutscenes order CutStart, CutTown, CutLevel1..6, CutPortal, CutPortalRed, CutGate (lines 62–73). SDL-version-dependent SdlEventType width (uint16 for SDL≥2).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: purely declarative; async events (WM_PROGRESS/WM_ERROR/WM_DONE) imply a background-loading thread in the .cpp — Go port must keep loading thread sending progress ticks to main loop.
- Test coverage: none found for interfac specifically in test/ (no interfac_test.cpp).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/loadscreen` (or `internal/game` events): interface_mode as typed enum; custom events via a Go event bus.
- Risks/open questions: none (header only).

- Test coverage: test/inv_test.cpp, test/inventory_ui_test.cpp (AutoEquip/AutoPlace/CanFit/CanBePlacedOnBelt/ReorganizeInventory/TransferToStash cases).
- Go mapping: `internal/inventory` (logic: place/fit/equip/gold/quests) + `internal/render/inventory` (panel drawing). InvGrid as [40]int8. Keep functions free of globals by passing a GameContext (MyPlayer, net sink, options).
- Risks/open questions: CheckInvCut's two-hand juggling is the most intricate stateful code — port with a dedicated table-driven test (existing gtest cases are good specs). Visual-store ctrl-click sell path depends on qol/visual_store (not in batch).

### Source/inv_iterators.hpp
- Purpose: STL-compatible forward-iterator ranges over non-empty items in containers and over a player's Equipped/Inventory/Belt/combined item sets — the backbone for item search/remove helpers.
- Public API: `template<ItemT> class ItemsContainerRange` (skips isEmpty() entries; Iterator exposes `index()` and `atEnd()`); `ItemsContainerListRange<ItemT>` (chains multiple range iterators); `EquippedPlayerItemsRange<PlayerT>` (InvBody[0..7)); `InventoryPlayerItemsRange<PlayerT>` (InvList[0.._pNumInv)); `BeltPlayerItemsRange<PlayerT>` (SpdList[0..8)); `InventoryAndBeltPlayerItemsRange` (Inventory then Belt); `PlayerItemsRange` (Equipped, Inventory, Belt in that order).
- Depends on: `items.h` (Item::isEmpty), `player.h` (Player fields InvBody/InvList/SpdList/_pNumInv).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go iterator funcs/channels yielding (index, *Item) skipping empty items, with the same container bounds: equipped = full InvBody array; inventory = first _pNumInv entries of InvList; belt = full SpdList.
  - Order guarantees: PlayerItems iteration order Equipped→Inventory→Belt must be preserved (affects "first matching item" semantics of Remove/Has helpers).
  - `Iterator::index()` semantics: raw container index (used by RemoveInventoryItem to call RemoveInvItem(index) and RemoveBeltItem → RemoveSpdBarItem(index)).
- 1:1 constraints: iteration orders and bounds as above; skip rule = `item.isEmpty()` (_itype == None); InventoryPlayerItemsRange end = _pNumInv (not array size) — trailing garbage entries are not visited; Equipped/Belt ranges span the full arrays.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: iterators hold raw pointers into player arrays; not thread-safe against concurrent inventory mutation (single-threaded game loop in Go port).
- Test coverage: indirectly via inv_test.cpp / items_test.cpp consumers; no dedicated iterator test found.
- Go mapping: `internal/inventory/iterate.go`: `EachEquipped(p)`, `EachInventory(p)`, `EachBelt(p)`, `EachPlayerItem(p)` as callback-based iterators returning indexes; Go 1.23 iter.Seq optional.
- Risks/open questions: none.

Item recreation (RecreateItem/GetTranslatedItemNameMagical) replays these DiscardRandomValues counts — line-for-line parity required.

  - Staff generation GetStaffSpell (Hellfire vs Diablo FlipCoin(4) path), charges minc..maxc, value += charges*staffCost/5, GetStaffPower 10% prefix (FlipCoin(10) unless onlygood).
  - Unique items: GetValidUniques (UIItemId match + lvl ≥ UIMinLvl), CheckUnique (rnd>uper abort; DiscardRandomValues(1); uidOffset selects validUniques[size−1−offset]), GetUniqueItem applies powers in order until IPL_INVALID, sets name/cursor/value, IMISC_UNIQUE stores uid in _iSeed, CF_UNIQUE flag.

Bard test items; InitItems DiscardRandomValues(1) when !setlevel; spawn eggs: rock {11,11} mega offset, cow suits {25,25} randarea 3, fungal/elix randarea 5 MP-only; SetItemRecord MAXITEMS cap.

- Risks/open questions: TryRandomUniqueItem and GetTranslatedItemNameMagical DevilutionX extensions intentionally diverge from vanilla RNG streams (they use private DiabloGenerator / discard annotations) — port decision needed: replicate DX behavior 1:1 (recommended, since saves/tests assume it). CalcPlrGraphics couples stat recalc to animation loading; in Go separate pure calc from asset loading behind an interface.

### Source/items.h

### Source/items/validation.cpp
- Purpose: Multiplayer anti-cheat validation of item data: creation-flag combos, town/shop item plausibility, price limits, unique-monster and dungeon item level legitimacy, Hellfire spell-book level checks, and delta-message item validation.
- Public API: `IsCreationFlagComboValid(uint16_t iCreateInfo)`, `IsTownItemValid(uint16_t, const Player&)`, `IsShopPriceValid(const Item&)`, `IsUniqueMonsterItemValid(uint16_t, uint32_t dwBuff)`, `IsDungeonItemValid(uint16_t, uint32_t)`, `IsHellfireSpellBookValid(const Item&)`, `IsItemValid(const Player&, const Item&)`, `IsItemDeltaValid(const TCmdPItem&)`.
- Depends on: items.h (CF_* constants, MaxBoyValue/MaxVendorValue*), msg.h (TCmdPItem layout, RecreateItem via items.h), player.h (getMaxCharacterLevel), spells.h (GetSpellBookLevel), tables/monstdat.h (MonstersData, UniqueMonstersData, MT_* enums), utils/endian_swap (Swap16LE), gendung (InDungeonBounds), diablo.h (gbIsMultiplayer, gbIsHellfire), MyPlayer global.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Same predicates, all no-ops in singleplayer (`!gbIsMultiplayer → true`) and for ears.
  - Creation-flag rules: pregen impossible in inventory; CF_USEFUL must be exclusive; town items have exactly one towner flag (hasMultipleFlags via `flags & (flags-1)`).
  - Town levels: ≤30 except Boy items bounded by player max character level.
  - Price limits: Diablo-only Boy ≤ MaxBoyValue(90000), premium ≤ MaxVendorValue(140000); smith|witch ≤ MaxVendorValueHf(200000) in Hellfire else 140000.
  - Unique-monster item level must equal some unique monster's MonstersData level, skipping MT_DEFILER/MT_NAKRUL/MT_HORKDMN.
  - Dungeon item level must equal some spawnable monster level (skip availability==Never except MT_DIABLO; Hellfire Diablo +15), else bounded by doubled max dungeon level: Hellfire (24−7)*2=34, Diablo (16−1)*2=30.
  - Hellfire books: (GetSpellBookLevel(spell)+1)*2 == CF_LEVEL, fallback dungeon check.
  - Delta validation: cmd ∈ {FloorItem, PickedUpItem, DroppedItem} (not CMD_INVALID), InDungeonBounds, idx available (IsItemAvailable), then RecreateItem and full IsItemValid; wIndx read via Swap16LE.

- Requirements for Go port:
  - Generator state: `nRoomCnt`, `RoomList[81]` (topLeft/bottomRight), `HallList` (FIFO of {beginning,end,direction}), `predungeon[DMAXX][DMAY] char` grid.
  - Room creation: `CreateRoom(topLeft, bottomRight, nRDest, nHDir, optional size)` — recursive BSP-ish subdivision with `AreaMin=2`, `RoomMax=10`, `RoomMin=4`, clamps to [1,38]; when `size` given it's a quest room and sets `SetPieceRoom = topLeft+{2,2}, size-1`.
  - `DefineRoom` marks corners 'C','E','B','A', walls '#', floor '.', optional forceHW writes Protected (with original BUGFIX-commented bug preserved).
  - `ConnectHall` walks from hall start to end with random turns; door placement `CreateDoorType` (avoids adjacent 'D', corners); `PlaceHallExt` sets ','; termination `while(beginning != end)`; boundary-flip rules at 38/1; corner-char redirect rules; random-turn probabilities `min(2*nDx,30)` and `min(5*nDy,80)`; final alignment rules for nDy<10/nDx<10/nDy==1/nDx==1/nDx==0/nDy==0 cases.

  - `DoPatternCheck(i,j)` matches `Patterns[k][0..8]` 3x3 neighborhood (top-left at i-1,j-1; x resets when l==3||6) against predungeon char classes 0(any)/1('#')/2('.')/4(' ')/3('D')/5(D|.) /6(D|#)/7(' '|'.')/8(D|#|'.'); sentinel row `{0,...,255,...,0}`; on match `dungeon[i][j]=Patterns[k][9]`.
  - `FixTilesPatterns` 6 inline tile fixes; `Substitution()` swaps same-BTYPESL2-class tiles randomly (FlipCoin(4), GenerateRnd(16) scan from -1, dedup check in 4x4 window excluding SetPieceRoom); `ApplyShadowsPatterns` uses BSTYPESL2 + SPATSL2 (see constraints).
  - `FixTransparency` (dTransVal copies for mega tiles at xx=16+2i, yy=16+2j for tiles 14/15/10/11/16), `FixDirtTiles` (13→146, 11→144, 15→148, 10→143, 14→147 conditional), `FixLockout` (converts orphan doors 4→1,5→2; inserts door 5/4 at end of wall runs, Protected respected; NOTE third loop iterates j over DMAXX-1 and i over DMAXY-1 — transposed, preserve), `FixDoors` (4→7 when above 3; 5→9 when left 3).
  - `PlaceStairs`: USTAIRS then DSTAIRS (both required), WARPSTAIRS only currlevel==5; ViewPosition = pos.megaToWorld()+{5,4}(ENTRY_MAIN)/{4,6}(ENTRY_PREV)/{5,4}(ENTRY_TWARPDN).

- Depends on: `dungeon`, `pdungeon`, `Protected`, `DungeonMask`, `SetPiece`, `currlevel`, `leveltype`, `ViewPosition`, `LevelSeeds`, `dPiece` (dun_tile_data.hpp); `PlaceMiniSet`, `PlaceDunTiles`, `GetDunSize`, `DRLG_LPass3`, `DRLG_PlaceThemeRooms`, `IsNearThemeRoom`, `LoadDungeonBase`, `Make_SetPC` (gendung.cpp/h); `GenerateRnd`, `RandomIntBetween`, `FlipCoin`, `PickRandomlyAmong`, `DiscardRandomValues`, `SetRndSeed`, `GetLCGEngineState` (random.hpp); `DoLighting` (lighting.h); `Quests[Q_ANVIL]` (questdat.hpp); `AddL3Objs` (objects.h).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Init: `InitDungeonFlags` memsets dungeon=0, Protected.reset.
  - `FillRoom(x1,y1,x2,y2)`: rejects if x1<=1||x2>=34||y1<=1||y2>=38 or any nonzero inside; interior=1; border cells set to 1 with probability 1/2 each via `FlipCoin()` (4 edges loops).
  - `CreateBlock(point, obs, dir)`: blksizex/blksizey = RandomIntBetween(3,4); dir 0..3 offsets per original code; recurses on FillRoom success with 25% stop chance (FlipCoin(4) returns→continue) and 4 directional recursive calls excluding incoming dir.
  - `FloorArea` fills rectangle with 1. `FillDiagonals`: v = d[i+1][j+1] + 2*d[i][j+1] + 4*d[i+1][j] + 8*d[i][j]; v==6 → set d[i][j] or d[i+1][j+1] to 1 by FlipCoin; v==9 → d[i+1][j] or d[i][j+1].
  - `FillSingles`: fills 0-cell surrounded by exactly the 8-neighborhood pattern (sums 3/2/3). `FillStraights`: 4 scan passes over i<37/j<37, runs xs>3 with !FlipCoin() fill GenerateRnd(2) values. `Edges`: zero last row/col. `GetFloorArea`: sum of dungeon.
  - `MakeMegas` (line 994): same 2x2 v formula; v==6→PickRandomlyAmong({12,5}); v==9→PickRandomlyAmong({13,14}); then `dungeon[i][j]=L3ConvTbl[v]`; right col and bottom row = 8.
  - `River` (line 1014): up to 200 tries, up to 4 rivers; finds lava edge tile 25–28, walks dir via GenerateRnd(4) with nodir/nodir2 exclusions, records river[3][100] (x,y,tile), corner fixes 19–24, endcap tiles 42/43/23/24, then bridge search (30 tries, GenerateRnd(riveramt), tiles 44/45) and commits river path to dungeon.
  - `Spawn`/`SpawnEdge` (1267/1316): recursive flood with visit bit 0x80, spawntable nibbles (low 4 bits = SpawnEdge moves, high bits = Spawn moves), bail if totarea>40 or out of bounds or tile>15. Two different 15-entry tables.
  - `CanReplaceTile`: for replace 84..100, uses ComparisonWithBoundsCheck p2-workaround bug (always NorthWest as p2) over 4 diagonal checks.
  - `PlaceMiniSetRandom` (bool-returning variant): scan, match, CanReplaceTile check, `GenerateRnd(100) >= rndper` skip, place; returns whether any placed.
  - `PlaceSlimePool` (Hive): HivePattern41@30, 42@40, 39@50, 40@60; success if ≥3 placed. `PlaceLavaPool`: scan all tiles==8, mark 0x80, Spawn in 4 directions (note the if/else chain quirk: `if (dunx-1>0 && !found) ... else found=true`), placePool = GenerateRnd(100)<25, clears 0x80 in totarea window, converts via Poolsub[15] = {0,35,26,36,25,29,34,7,33,28,27,37,32,31,30} when totarea>4 && placePool && !found && k!=0 && k<=37.
  - `PoolFix`: tile 8 adjacent (3x3) to 25..41 → 33. `Warp`: first 2x2 of 125s → 156/155/153/154 then return; also 5 followed by SE 7 → 7. `HallOfHeroes`: 5 with SE 12 patterns → 7s.
  - Fence family: `FenceVerticalUp/Down`, `FenceHorizontalLeft/Right` predicates on tiles 7/2/4/10/9 and 126–137 ranges; `AddFenceDoors` (7 between two 130–152 horizontally →146, vertically →147); `FenceDoorFix` (revert 146/147 to 7 based on neighbor ranges {130,132,133,134,136,138,140} / {131,132,133,135,137,138,139}); `Fence` (line 1631): horizontal/vertical fence runs from 10/9/11 seeds with PickRandomlyAmong({129,126})/({124,121}), corner 125, then second pass on 7 tiles with `DiscardRandomValues(1)` comma-operator RNG advancement (must consume one RNG value even when tile not near theme room), vertical/horizontal wall-to-fence conversion with skip-gap rp=GenerateRnd(span-1)+min+1 and per-tile substitution map.

FillRoom; CreateBlock×4 with obs=2 dirs 0..3; if Q_ANVIL available: x1=GenerateRnd(10)+10,y1 same,x2=x1+12,y2=y1+12, FloorArea; FillDiagonals, FillSingles, FillStraights, FillDiagonals, Edges; require GetFloorArea()>=600 && Lockout(); MakeMegas; PlaceStairs; if Q_ANVIL && !PlaceAnvil() continue; if PlacePool() break }.

Then memcpy pdungeon.

DMAXX/2-1-w]; level16 stores L4Hold; SetPieceRoom={pos+{1,1}, size+1} for quest rooms else zeroed; MapRoom + GenerateRoom(room, !FlipCoin()).

  - `PrepareInnerBorders`: hallok[20] row/col scans; carve guaranteed halls at random ry/rx (GenerateRnd((DMAX/2)-1)+1) with wrap; sets DungeonMask pairs.
  - Walls: `HorizontalWallOk/VerticalWallOk` (walk while 6, Protected/neighbor checks; accept when end tile ∈ {10,12,13,15,16,21,22}/{8,9,11,14,15,16,21,23} and len>3); `HorizontalWall/VerticalWall` lay tiles 2/1 with end conversions and random door group (57/56/60 + 58/59 or 53/52/6 + 54/55) at GenerateRnd(dx-3)+1; `AddWall` scans all tiles, per matching tile calls DiscardRandomValues(1) then tries both directions (two Discard calls possible per tile).

  - `GenerateLevel` order: seed restore; loop { DRLG_InitTrans; inner do{LevelSeeds=GetLCG; InitDungeonFlags; FirstRoom; CloseOuterBorders} while FindArea<692; PrepareInnerBorders; MirrorDungeonLayout; MakeDmt; FixTilesPatterns; ProtectQuads if 16; quest-room Protected fill; AddWall; FloodTransparencyValues(6); FixTransparency; InitSetPiece (warlord.dun or vile1.dun at lvl15 MP); LoadDiabQuads(true) if 16; break if PlaceStairs } ; then GeneralFix; theme rooms (7,10,6,8,true) unless 16; ApplyShadowsPatterns; FixCornerTiles; Substitution; pdungeon copy; DRLG_CheckQuests; level15 gate logic (closed → L4PENTA.place at Q_DIABLO position; scan 98/107 → Make_SetPC 5x5 at (i-1,j-1), Q_BETRAYER position = pentagram NW world pos); level16 → LoadDiabQuads(false).

- Determinism/thread-safety notes: globals DiabloQuad1..4 (public), hallok[20], L4Hold; RNG ordering strict (GenerateRoom tries, AddWall double Discard, Substitution, PlaceMiniSet internals); regeneration depends on FindArea≥692 and PlaceStairs success.

### Source/levels/dun_tile.hpp
- Purpose: Core tile-type definitions: TileType enum (cel encodings), LevelCelBlock (16-bit packed micro descriptor), TileProperties flags, MICROS struct, and frame dimension constants.
- Public API: types/constants only: `TileType`, `LevelCelBlock{uint16_t data; hasValue(); type(); frame()}`, `TileProperties` flags, `MICROS{LevelCelBlock mt[16]}`, `TILE_WIDTH=64`, `TILE_HEIGHT=32`, `DunFrameWidth=32`, `DunFrameHeight=32`, `DunFrameTriangleHeight=31`, `ReencodedTriangleFrameSize=544-32=512`, `ReencodedTrapezoidFrameSize=800-16=784`, `CalculateSpriteTileCenterX(width)=(width-64)/2`.
- Depends on: utils/enum_traits.h (use_enum_as_flags); <cstdint>.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - TileType values in exact order: Square=0, TransparentSquare=1, LeftTriangle=2, RightTriangle=3, LeftTrapezoid=4, RightTrapezoid=5 (uint8).
  - LevelCelBlock decode: type = (data & 0x7000)>>12; frame = data & 0xFFF (1-based).
  - TileProperties bits: Solid=1, BlockLight=2, BlockMissile=4, Transparent=8, TransparentLeft=0x10, TransparentRight=0x20, Trap=0x80.
  - RLE semantics for TransparentSquare (int8 run lengths, positive=opaque, negative=-count transparent, no cross-row runs); triangle/trapezoid row encodings with 2-byte padding on even rows (padding stripped by ReencodeDungeonCels) — document for renderer.
- 1:1 constraints: all bit masks and constants above (lines 20–131); triangle geometry: 31 rows, 2px at extremes, 32px middle; trapezoid = triangle bottom-16 + 32x16 rect.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure definitions, no state.
- Test coverage: test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp uses these types; test/tile_properties_test.cpp exercises TileProperties logic.
- Go mapping: internal/render or internal/dungeon `dun_tile.go` — plain Go types + constants; LevelCelBlock as uint16 with methods.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/levels/dun_tile_data.cpp
- Purpose: Definitions of all dungeon tile/map globals plus SOL (solidity) data loading and MIN-file micro-tile expansion (SetDungeonMicros) with cel re-encoding.
- Public API: defines globals declared in dun_tile_data.hpp (`currlevel`, `setlevel`, `DungeonMask`, `dungeon`, `pdungeon`, `Protected`, `SetPieceRoom`, `SetPiece`, `pSpecialCels`, `pMegaTiles`, `pDungeonCels`, `SOLData[MAXTILES=1379]`, `dminPosition`, `dmaxPosition`, `leveltype`, `setlvlnum`, `setlvltype`, `ViewPosition`, `MicroTileLen`, `TransVal`, `TransList[256]`, `dPiece[MAXDUNX][MAXDUNY]`, `DPieceMicros[MAXTILES]`, `dTransVal`, `dLight`, `dPreLight`, `dFlags`, `dPlayer`, `dMonster`, `dCorpse`, `dObject`, `dSpecial`, `themeCount`, `themeLoc[50]`, `DungeonSeeds[NUMLEVELS]`, `LevelSeeds[NUMLEVELS]`); functions `std::expected<void,std::string> LoadLevelSOLData()` (99), `void SetDungeonMicros(std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]>&, uint_fast8_t&)` (166).
- Depends on: `leveltype` switch on dungeon_type; `LoadFileInMem[WithStatus]<uint16_t>`, `LoadIntegralFileInMemWithStatus` (engine/load_file.hpp); `ReencodeDungeonCels`, `ComputeCelBlockAdjustments`, `DunFrameInfo` (levels/reencode_dun_cels.hpp); `Swap16LE`; ankerl::unordered_dense map; `app_fatal`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - All globals as a shared level-state struct or package-level vars in internal/dungeon (these are THE central map arrays every drlg file mutates).
  - `LoadMinData(leveltype)` — .min file per type: town (nlevels fallback to levels), l1, l2, l3, l4, l6 (nest), l5 (crypt); returns uint16 array + tileCount.
  - `LoadLevelSOLData` — loads .sol per type into SOLData, then applies hardcoded corrections: Cathedral adds BlockLight|BlockMissile to tiles 9,15,16,20,21,51,56,58,61,63,65,72,208,247,253,257,323,450; BlockMissile to 27,28; BlockLight to 24,403. Caves: BlockMissile to 170; Solid to 481,487. Hell: SOLData[210]=None. Crypt: SOLData[142]=None. Returns error for unknown type.
  - `SetDungeonMicros(dungeonCels, microTileLen)`: microTileLen=10/blocks=10 default; town: 16/16; hell: 12 blocks=16. Iterates levelPieceId over tileCount/blocks; per block builds LevelCelBlock from `Swap16LE(pieces[blocks-2+(block&1)-(block&0xE)])` — index formula must be exact; fills DPieceMicros[id].mt[block]; builds frame→DunFrameInfo{block, type, SOLData[id]} map (first occurrence wins); extracts, sorts by frame; calls ReencodeDungeonCels; then ComputeCelBlockAdjustments and applies frame-index decrements via upper_bound on (frame,frame) pairs — subtract adjustment from levelCelBlock.data.
- 1:1 constraints: block index formula `blocks - 2 + (block & 1) - (block & 0xE)`; microTileLen/blocks triples (10/10, 16/16, 12/16); all SOL tile correction indices listed above; MAXTILES=1379; MAXTHEMES=50.

### Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp
- Purpose: Post-load optimization pass over dungeon CEL data: (1) strips the 2-zero-byte "bloat" padding from left/right triangle and trapezoid frames, (2) converts eligible TransparentSquare *floor* tiles into a triangle (floor) + separate 16-px-tall transparent-square (foliage) pair, reducing memory and simplifying rendering. Also computes frame-index adjustments for the cel-block lookup tables after unreferenced frames are dropped.
- Public API:
  - `void ReencodeDungeonCels(std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]> &dungeonCels, std::span<std::pair<uint16_t,DunFrameInfo>> frames)` (line 175)
  - `std::vector<std::pair<uint16_t,uint16_t>> ComputeCelBlockAdjustments(std::span<std::pair<uint16_t,DunFrameInfo>> frames)` (line 228)
- Depends on: `DunFrameWidth`(=32), `DunFrameHeight`(=64), `TileType`, `TileProperties`, `ReencodedTriangleFrameSize`(=544-32=512), `ReencodedTrapezoidFrameSize`(=800-16=784) from levels/dun_tile.hpp; `Swap32LE/WriteLE32` (utils/endian_*); `LogVerbose`+`FormatInteger` (utils/log.hpp, format_int.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Byte-exact re-encoding: input is a CEL file image (uint32 LE frame-count, frame offsets[], file size); output rewrites header with new frame count = len(frames), new offsets, new total size; frames emitted in `frames` order, each transformed by its TileType:
    - TransparentSquare non-floor → verbatim copy (size = next offset delta).
    - TransparentSquare floor → `ReencodeFloorWithFoliage` (see below), counted in `numFoliage`.
    - Square → copy `DunFrameWidth*DunFrameHeight` = 32*64 = 2048 bytes.
    - Left/RightTriangle → copy without the 2-byte zero padding per row-pair (output size 512 each).
    - Left/RightTrapezoid → triangle-lower reencode + 16 full lines (32*16=512 bytes) copy (output 784).
  - `ReencodeFloorWithFoliage` (line 133): renders the source TransparentSquare frame into a 32×64 stack buffer via `RenderTransparentSquare` (RLE decode, bottom-up, `dst -= 2*DunFrameWidth` per line), then depending on Left/Right extracts the triangle pixels (`ExtractFoliageLeftTriangle`/`RightTriangle`: rows y=31..16 widths 2,4..32; rows y=15..1 widths 30,28..2; copies from `surface + (32-w)` for left, `surface` for right, zeroing the source region) and finally `ExtractFoliageTransparentSquare` re-RLE-encodes the remaining upper 16 lines (runs: positive byte = solid pixel count followed by pixels; negative byte = transparent run; bottom 16 lines always skipped).
  - `ComputeCelBlockAdjustments`: for each (frame,info) in order, `diff = frame - lastFrameIndex - 1`; if diff>0 record (frame, cumulativeAdjustment); cumulativeAdjustment += diff; lastFrameIndex = frame; final sentinel entry (0xFFFF, adjustment) if adjustment>0.
  - Floor eligibility (`DunFrameInfo::isFloor`, header lines 25–32): NOT(Solid|BlockMissile flags) AND microTileIndex∈{0,1}; `isFloorLeft()` = microTileIndex==0.
  - Verbose logging of frame/byte counts before and after (LogVerbose — optional in Go but keep counts computable).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Triangle row pattern (lines 22–52): each of 16 row-pairs drops exactly 2 leading zero bytes; widths grow 2,4,6,...,32 (lower) then shrink 32,30,...,2 (upper), with final upper segment after loop handled explicitly (lines 40–44 right variant mirrors without src skip at end).
  - `RenderTransparentSquare` (line 78): iterates DunFrameHeight=64 lines bottom-up (`dst -= 2*DunFrameWidth`), RLE: `v = int8(*src++)`; v>0 → memcpy v pixels; dst += |v|; drawWidth -= v, until drawWidth==0.
  - Foliage extraction widths (lines 96–115): left triangle `src + (DunFrameWidth - w)`; loops `y=31..16, w+=2` then `y=15..1 (>0), w-=2`.
  - `ExtractFoliageTransparentSquare` (line 154): starts `src -= DunFrameHeight * 16` (bottom 16 lines always transparent — comment lines 155–157), then per line `src -= 2*DunFrameWidth` for 16 lines; run encoder emits `-transparentRun` as `uint8(-int8(run))` and `solidRun` byte + pixels.
  - `GetReencodedSize` (line 139): `result = (2 + frames.size()) * 4` header bytes + per-frame sizes per the switch above.
  - Header write (lines 186–189): `WriteLE32(resultPtr, frames.size())`; offsets start at `(2+frames.size())*4`; final `WriteLE32(lookup, outSize)` after last frame.
  - All multi-byte reads/writes little-endian (Swap32LE on read, WriteLE32 on write).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure function of input bytes; allocates fresh output buffer and swaps ownership into `dungeonCels`. No globals; no RNG. Must run single-threaded per level load in Go too (or be made pure — it is pure already).
- Test coverage: none found for ReencodeDungeonCels directly; related render tests exist (test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp is a benchmark, not assertions).
- Go mapping: `internal/render` (or `internal/dungeon/cel`): `ReencodeDungeonCels(data []byte, frames []FrameRef) []byte` and `ComputeCelBlockAdjustments(frames []FrameRef) [][2]uint16`. Keep DunFrameInfo in the same package as tile type defs.
- Risks/open questions: byte-exactness is testable via golden .CEL fixtures — recommend capturing before/after buffers from devilutionX for tests. The `surface[1024]` stack buffer in ReencodeFloorWithFoliage equals 32*32 (only upper half used after render offsets); preserve exact indexing.

### Source/levels/town.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the town level (level 0): loads the four fixed .dun sectors into dPiece via mega-tile expansion, patches closed/open Hive and Grave layouts, sets special tiles, and positions the player on entry. Also hosts the rune-bomb/grave-map open actions that update quests and send net commands.
- Public API: `bool OpensHive(Point)`, `bool OpensGrave(Point)`, `void OpenHive()`, `void OpenGrave()`, `void TownOpenHive()`, `void TownOpenGrave()`, `void CleanTownFountain()`, `void CreateTown(lvl_entry entry)` (all declared in levels/town.h). Internal (anon ns): `FillSector(path,xi,yy)`, `FillTile(xx,yy,t)`, `TownCloseHive()`, `TownCloseGrave()`, `InitTownPieces()`, `DrlgTPass3()`.
- Depends on: `dPiece`, `dSpecial`, `dungeon`, `dminPosition`/`dmaxPosition`, `ViewPosition`, `pMegaTiles` (levels/gendung.h + levels/dun_tile_data.hpp `MegaTile` micro1..4), `GetDunSize`/`PlaceDunTiles` (levels/gendung.h), `LoadFileInMem<uint16_t>` (engine/load_file.hpp), `Swap16LE` (utils/endian_swap.hpp), `PickRandomlyAmong` (engine/random.hpp), `IsWarpOpen`/`TWarpFrom` (levels/trigs.cpp), `NetSendCmd`/`NetSendCmdQuest` (multi.h), `Quests[Q_FARMER|Q_GRAVE|Q_PWATER]` (quests.h), `gbIsHellfire`/`gbIsMultiplayer` (game_mode.hpp), `MAXDUNX/MAXDUNY` (levels/gendung.h).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `FillSector`: load MPQ `.dun` file as []uint16 LE; size = (w,h) from first two words; tile layer starts at word index 2; per dun-cell expand mega-tile: dun id `t-1` indexes pMegaTiles; write its 4 micros into dPiece as 2x2 block; tileId<0 → all four = 218; destination steps xx+=2 per column, yy+=2 per row. Paths use backslashes: `levels\towndata\sector1s.dun` etc. (Go: normalize to MPQ path).
  - `FillTile(xx,yy,t)`: write 4 micros of pMegaTiles[t-1] as 2x2 block at (xx,yy).
  - `TownCloseHive`/`TownOpenHive`/`TownCloseGrave`/`TownOpenGrave`: exact dPiece patch tables (hex constants) + `dungeon` cell patches (see 1:1).
  - `InitTownPieces`: full MAXDUNY×MAXDUNX scan mapping specific dPiece ids to dSpecial values (table below).
  - `DrlgTPass3`: fill entire dPiece grid with 426 (2x2 pattern), load 4 sectors at fixed offsets (sector1s→(46,46), sector2s→(46,0), sector3s→(0,46), sector4s→(0,0)); load `levels\towndata\automap.dun` and PlaceDunTiles at (0,0); closed-warp patches for catacombs/caves/hell using IsWarpOpen; Hive/Grave open/close when gbIsHellfire; poisoned-water fountain tile choice by Q_PWATER state; then InitTownPieces.
  - Hell warp-closed stairs: `FillTile(x, 78, PickRandomlyAmong({1,2,3,4}))` for x in 36..45 — consumes game RNG; must preserve call order/sing-count for determinism of RNG-dependent tests.

  - `CleanTownFountain`: no-op if pMegaTiles==nil; else FillTile(60,70,71).

### Source/lighting.cpp
- Purpose: Core light/vision engine: per-tile light map updates (dLight/dPreLight) using precomputed LightConeInterpolations/LightFalloffs tables, light-list add/remove/change processing, and per-player vision rays (via vision.hpp DoVision) marking automap/visibility flags and transparency list.
- Public API: globals `VisionActive[MAXVISION]`, `VisionList[MAXVISION]`, `Lights[MAXLIGHTS]`, `ActiveLights[MAXLIGHTS]`, `ActiveLightCount`, `InfravisionTable[256]`, `StoneTable[256]`, `PauseTable[256]`, `UpdateLighting` (+debug `DisableLighting`); functions `DoUnLight`, `DoLighting`, `DoUnVision`, `DoVision`, `LoadTrns`, `ToggleLighting`(debug), `InitLighting`, `AddLight`, `AddUnLight`, `ChangeLightRadius`, `ChangeLightXY`, `ChangeLightOffset`, `ChangeLight`, `ProcessLightList`, `SavePreLighting`, `ActivateVision`, `ChangeVisionRadius`, `ChangeVisionXY`, `ProcessVisionList`, `lighting_color_cycling`.
- Depends on: `dLight`, `dPreLight`, `dFlags`, `dTransVal`, `InDungeonBounds`, `TileHasAny`/TileProperties (levels/gendung.h, levels/tile_properties.hpp); `TransList`, `LoadingMapObjects` (levels/dun_tile_data.hpp, objects.h); `LightConeInterpolations`, `LightFalloffs`, `NumLightRadiuses` (engine/lighting_defs.hpp); `LightTables` (engine/light_tables.hpp); `DoVision(...)` templated ray caster (vision.hpp); `SetAutomapView`, `MapExplorationType` (automap.h); `Players`, `MyPlayer`, Player fields (plractive, isOnActiveLevel, _pLvlChanging, friendlyMode, getId) (player.h); `LevelSeeds`-no; LoadFileInMemWithStatus (engine/load_file.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Light/Vision record: position tile+offset(int8 pair)+old, radius/oldRadius uint8, isInvalid/hasChanged bools (lighting.h structs).
  - `DoUnLight(pos, radius)`: radius+=2; copy dPreLight→dLight over square (PointsInRectangle WorldTileRectangle) clipped to bounds.
  - `DoLighting(pos, radius, offset)` exact algorithm (L117-179): normalize negative offsets (offset+=8 and shift position -1 on that axis); bounds minX/maxX/minY/maxY clamped to 15 vs grid edges (MAXDUNX/MAXDUNY); NEST/CRYPT dim-light special: clamp center to LightFalloffs[radius][0] only if current > it, else set 0; loop i=0..3 quadrants: yBound=(i>0&&i<3)?maxY:minY, xBound=(i<2)?maxX:minX; inner x from 1 (not 0); linearDistance = LightConeInterpolations[offset.dx][offset.dy][x+block.dx][y+block.dy]; skip >=128; temp = position + (x,y).Rotate(-i); v=LightFalloffs[radius][linearDistance]; only decrease (v < GetLight(temp)); then RotateRadius(offset,dist,light,block). SetLight/GetLight write dPreLight when LoadingMapObjects else dLight.
  - `RotateRadius` (L49-62): dist={7-dist.dy, dist.dx}; light={7-light.dy, light.dx}; offset={dist.dx-light.dx, dist.dy-light.dy}; block.dx=1 if offset.dx<0 (then +=8), similarly dy.
  - `DoUnVision`: radius+=2, clear Visible|Lit flags over square.
  - `DoVision(pos,radius,doAutomap,visible)`: wraps templated vision ray-caster with callbacks: markVisible (DoVisionFlags), markTransparent (dTransVal→TransList), passesLight (TileAllowsLight: in bounds && !BlockLight), inBounds. DoVisionFlags: if automap≠NONE: SetAutomapView when tile flags ≠ None, set Explored; visible→Lit; always Visible.
  - `LoadTrns`: read `plrgfx\infra.trn`→InfravisionTable, `plrgfx\stone.trn`→StoneTable, `gendata\pause.trn`→PauseTable (256 bytes each), errors propagate.
  - `InitLighting`: ActiveLightCount=0; UpdateLighting/UpdateVision=false; iota ActiveLights 0..31; clear VisionActive, TransList.
  - AddLight: NO_LIGHT (-1?) when full or debug-disabled; pops id from ActiveLights; init record; UpdateLighting=true. AddUnLight marks isInvalid. Change* set hasChanged + stash old pos/radius then apply change. ChangeLightOffset early-outs when offset unchanged.
  - `ProcessLightList` (L366-398): if !UpdateLighting return; pass1: for invalid lights DoUnLight(tile,radius); for changed DoUnLight(old,oldRadius) and clear flag; pass2: remove invalid (swap-with-last trick decrementing count), skip lights on Solid tiles (monster in wall), else DoLighting(tile,radius,offset); finally UpdateLighting=false.
  - `SavePreLighting`: memcpy dPreLight←dLight.
  - Vision: ActivateVision(id)/ChangeVisionRadius/ChangeVisionXY mirror light ops on VisionList[playerId]; `ProcessVisionList` (L437-475): if !UpdateVision return; TransList reset; pass1 deactivate visions of inactive/off-level/level-changing(non-my) players with DoUnVision; pass2 DoVision per active player with doautomap MAP_EXP_SELF for MyPlayer, else friendlyMode?MAP_EXP_OTHERS:MAP_EXP_NONE; visible only for MyPlayer.
  - `lighting_color_cycling`: for each of LightTables rotate indexes 1..31 left by one (std::rotate begin+1, begin+2, begin+32) — light-source palette animation each ~2 game ticks (caller in dvl life).
- 1:1 constraints: radius+2 increments in DoUnLight/DoUnVision (L106-107, 183-184); quadrant loop constants (i<2→x max, etc. L169-171); linearDistance cutoff 128 (L172); falloff dim clamp only for DTYPE_NEST/DTYPE_CRYPT (L161-166); RotateRadius formulas above; MAXLIGHTS=32, MAXVISION=4 (lighting_defs.hpp); rotation of light table indices 1..31 (L477-482); ActiveLights removal via swap (L384-388).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: all state is global mutable arrays; UpdateLighting/UpdateVision dirty flags gate per-tick work; LoadingMapObjects (set while placing objects at level load) redirects writes to dPreLight — order-of-init matters between object loading and lighting. No threads.
- Test coverage: none found for this file's functions; adjacent: test/light_render_benchmark.cpp (dLight consumption only).
- Go mapping: `internal/dungeon/lighting` (or internal/render/light): port DoLighting with precomputed tables generated in Go (LightConeInterpolations/LightFalloffs from engine/lighting_defs data); keep byte-level dLight arrays for renderer parity.
- Risks/open questions: engine/lighting_defs.hpp + engine/vision.hpp are separate files (other batches) — the interpolation/falloff table generation and ray caster live there; DoLighting's exact index math is the parity-critical piece.

Stash ("spstashitems"/"mpstashitems"): version uint8(0), gold uint32, page count, per page: page uint32 + 10×10 uint16 grid, item count, items, current page uint32; validation via IsStashSizeValid (exact byte-size formula); errors → EventPlrMsg red + Stash reset. Hotkeys ("hotkeys"): optional header byte count (detect old 4-slot format via size check HotkeysSize), spell ids int32 × n, spell types uint8 × n, then selected _pRSpell int32 + _pRSplType uint8; Save writes NumHotkeys.
  - **Conversion**: ConvertLevels: save/restore setlevel/setlvlnum/currlevel/leveltype; gbSkipSync=true; iterate regular levels (0..giNumberOfLevels) then quest levels (non-NOTAVAIL, leveltype≠NONE, _qslvl), LoadLevel+SaveLevel with MonsterConversionData; restore state; gbSkipSync=false. Item idx remaps: From/ToDiablo (SORCERER swap; ≥156 +5; ≥88 +1; ≥83 +4 / inverse with -1 for Hellfire-exclusives), From/ToSpawn (≥62 +9; ≥96/98/99/101/102/104 +1 each / inverse ≥71 -9). RemoveInvalidItem rules: !IsItemAvailable || uid≥UniqueItems.size(); Diablo-only: staff w/o staff level, book w/o book level, _iDamAcFlags≠None, pre/suf power > IPL_LASTDIABLO.

### Source/lua/autocomplete.cpp
- Purpose: Debug-only (entire file `#ifdef _DEBUG`) Lua console autocomplete: given typed text and cursor, enumerate matching keys from the Lua environment (tables, metatables, userdata members) producing display text + completion text.
- Public API: `GetLuaAutocompleteSuggestions(std::string_view text, size_t cursorPos, const sol::environment &lua, size_t maxSuggestions, std::vector<LuaAutocompleteSuggestion> &out)` (via autocomplete.hpp).
- Depends on: sol2 (sol::state/table/userdata/protected_function, metatable_key, meta_function::call), `GetLuaState`, `SafeCallResult` (lua/lua_global.hpp/cpp), `GetSignature`/`GetDocstring`/`GetLuaUserdataSignature`/`GetLuaUserdataDocstring`/`GetLuaUserdataMemberType`+`LuaUserdataMemberType` (lua/metadoc.hpp), `LoadAsset` (engine/assets.hpp), app_fatal, StrCat/StrAppend (utils/str_cat.hpp), SplitByChar (utils/str_split.hpp), c_sort/c_any_of (utils/algorithm/container.hpp), embedded asset `lua_internal\get_lua_function_signature.lua`.
- Requirements for Go port (only if a debug Lua console with sol-equivalent is ported — Go uses gopher-lua or similar):
  - GetLastToken: scan back while chars not ' ', '(', ','.
  - ValueInfo{callable, signature, docstring}; signatures from metadoc first, else for functions: C functions → "(...)", Lua functions → run embedded signature-getter script cached in registry key `__DEVILUTIONX_GET_LUA_SIGNATURE`; __call metamethods get first argument stripped (RemoveFirstArgumentFromFunctionSignature: find first ',' or ')', cut, handle space and empty-args).
  - Suggest loop per table key: string keys only; must start with prefix and be longer than prefix; skip `__*` unless prefix starts with `__`; skip keys containing ♻/☢/🔩 (sol internals); userdata queries filter by colon-vs-dot access (MemberFunction requires colon); completionText = key minus prefix, append "()" and cursorAdjust=-1 when callable; displayText appends ": " (non-function userdata members) + signature + " - " + first line of docstring; insert into set (dedupe by displayText), stop at maxSuggestions; recurse into metatable fallback (`__index` as table) — metatable chain walk.
  - Main entry: bail when prefix empty; suffix first char is identifier/expr char ('-','+','*','/','=') or (' ' followed by more text); bail "id space" pattern; bail prevChar '(' or ','; token split at last '.' or ':'; walk lua env table by '.'-then-':' segments (obj must remain table or userdata); empty token → suggest from env and `_G`; userdata → SuggestionsFromUserdata with colonAccess flag; final out = sorted (c_sort) by displayText.
  - Colon access only completes member functions; dot access completes properties/functions.
- 1:1 constraints: skip-char set ' ', '(', ',' (L25); expr chars '-','+','*','/' plus alnum/_ (L269-277); registry key name `__DEVILUTIONX_GET_LUA_SIGNATURE` (L55); asset path `lua_internal\get_lua_function_signature.lua` (L50); emoji exclusion set ♻ ☢ 🔩 (L196-199); cursorAdjust=-1 for callables; maxSuggestions break at ==.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: lazily caches signature-getter function in the Lua registry — first call does script load; suggestion set is unordered (hash set) then sorted → deterministic final order by displayText only (ties by insertion not guaranteed, but operator< is strict on displayText).
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/autocomplete` (debug build tag): needs gopher-lua equivalent of environment walk, metatable walk, userdata member typing (metadoc port). If the Go port ships no debug console, document as intentionally omitted.
- Risks/open questions: depends on sol2-specific behaviors (metatable_key traversal, protected functions) and on lua/metadoc.hpp (another file); Go Lua runtime choice changes this file's shape substantially.

### Source/lua/lua_event.cpp
- Purpose: Fire game lifecycle/combat events into mod Lua (`events.<name>:trigger(...)` handlers), with a defaulting variant for return values. All no-ops when no Lua event table exists; handler errors are logged, not fatal.
- Public API (namespace devilution::lua): `MonsterDataLoaded()`, `UniqueMonsterDataLoaded()`, `ItemDataLoaded()`, `UniqueItemDataLoaded()`, `StoreOpened(std::string_view name)`, `OnMonsterTakeDamage(const Monster*, int damage, int damageType)`, `OnPlayerGainExperience(const Player*, uint32_t exp)`, `OnPlayerTakeDamage(const Player*, int damage, int damageType)`, `LoadModsComplete()`, `GameDrawComplete()`, `GameStart()`.
- Depends on: `GetLuaEvents()` (lua/lua_global.hpp — returns sol::table* or nullptr), `SafeCallResult(fn, optional=true)` (lua_global), Monster/Player types (passed as sol usertypes registered elsewhere), LogError.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two templates: CallLuaEvent(name, args...) — fetch events table; traverse_get<name,"trigger">; if missing or not a protected function → LogError("events.{}.trigger is not a function") and return; call with SafeCallResult(optional=true). CallLuaEventReturn(default, name, args...) — same but if result converts to T return it else default (currently unused by the listed wrappers but exported behavior).
  - Event names must match exactly: "MonsterDataLoaded", "UniqueMonsterDataLoaded", "ItemDataLoaded", "UniqueItemDataLoaded", "StoreOpened" (arg: store name string), "OnMonsterTakeDamage" (monster ptr, damage int, damageType int), "OnPlayerGainExperience" (player ptr, exp uint32), "OnPlayerTakeDamage", "LoadModsComplete", "GameDrawComplete", "GameStart".
  - Callers across the codebase (monster damage, player exp, stores, game loop) hook these — the Go event bus must be callable from those sites with identical argument tuples.
- 1:1 constraints: error path requires presence check `events == nullptr` return silently (no log) vs trigger-not-function → LogError; optional=true safe call swallows handler errors; event name strings as above (L55-103).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: GameDrawComplete fires per frame from render loop; others from game logic; Lua state access assumes single-threaded; if no Lua mod system loaded everything is a cheap null-check.
- Test coverage: test/stores_test.cpp asserts StoreOpened fires only for top-level store open (sub-pages must not fire).
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/events.go`: an EventBus with Fire(name, args...) and typed wrappers; nil bus → no-op. If the Go port keeps gopher-lua mods, mirror trigger lookup `events.<name>.trigger`.
- Risks/open questions: Monster/Player userdata registration (lua metadoc/luaproxy files, other batches) needed for args to be meaningful in Lua.

# vol3-024.md

# Volume III — batch 024

### Source/lua/lua_global.cpp
- Purpose: Core Lua runtime bootstrap for mods: owns the global sol::state, sandboxed environments, an asset-backed `require` with bytecode caching, mod (re)loading pipeline, and error/panic handling.
- Public API (all in `devilution` ns, decls in lua_global.hpp): `void LuaInitialize()`, `void LuaReloadActiveMods()`, `void LuaShutdown()`, `sol::state &GetLuaState()`, `sol::environment CreateLuaSandbox()`, `sol::object SafeCallResult(sol::protected_function_result, bool optional)`, `sol::table *GetLuaEvents()`, `void AddModsChangedHandler(tl::function_ref<void()>)`, `void Sol2DebugPrintStack(lua_State*)`, `void Sol2DebugPrintSection(const std::string&, lua_State*)`.
- Depends on: all `Lua*Module` factories (audio.hpp, floatingnumbers.hpp, hellfire.hpp, i18n.hpp, items.hpp, log.hpp, monsters.hpp, player.hpp, render.hpp, system.hpp, towners.hpp; dev.hpp + repl.hpp under `_DEBUG`); `engine/assets.hpp` `LoadIntegralAsset`; `appfat.h` `app_fatal`; `options.h` `GetOptions().Mods.GetActiveModList/GetEntries`; `stores.h` `ClearTownerDialogOptions`; `plrmsg.h` `EventPlrMsg` + `UiFlags::ColorRed`; `effects.h` `effects_cleanup_sfx/sound_init/ui_sound_init`; text/spell/missile/monster/item/object/quest data loaders (LoadTextData…LoadQuestData); `lua_event.hpp` `lua::LoadModsComplete`; `utils/console.h` `printInConsole/printNewlineInConsole`; `utils/log.hpp` Log*; `utils/str_cat.hpp`; config.h `PROJECT_VERSION`; sol2 (state, environment, protected_function, bytecode, debug dump).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A Lua host equivalent (gopher-lua or similar) with: panic handler that logs and aborts; a warn hook (`lua_setwarnf` semantics: buffer message pieces until `continued == 0`, then log warn and clear — static `warnBuffer`, lines ~152–159).
  - Global singleton `CurrentLuaState` (optional<LuaState>) holding: lua state, `commonPackages` table, `compiledScripts` segmented_map path→bytecode, `sandbox` env, `events` table.
  - `requireGen` Lua source compiled at init and stored under global `requireGen`; custom `require` built per-sandbox by calling `requireGen(env, commonPackages, loadFn)`; loader semantics: check `loaded[packageName]`, else `loadFn(packageName)`; string result → `error(loader)`; else `setEnvironment(env, loader)`, call `loader(packageName)`, cache result.
  - `LuaLoadScriptFromAssets`: path = `lua\` + packageName with `.`→`\` + `.lua`; bytecode cache hit → `load(binary)`; else `LoadIntegralAsset(path)` (error → push error string), `load(text)`, on success cache `fn.dump()`.
  - `RunScript(env, packageName, optional)`: load, string error → `app_fatal` if !optional else LogInfo + nil; set env on function if given; `SafeCallResult(fn(), optional)`.
  - `LuaPrint`: iterate stack args 1..n, `luaL_tolstring` each, tab-separate, `printInConsole`, newline at end, return 0.
  - `CreateLuaSandbox`: fresh env with `print=LuaPrint`, `_DEBUG` (true only in debug builds), `_VERSION`; copy safe builtins list: assert, warn, error, ipairs, next, pairs, pcall, select, tonumber, tostring, type, xpcall, rawequal, rawget, rawset, setmetatable (+ `debug` in _DEBUG; base, coroutine, table, string, math, utf8) — missing global → `app_fatal`; `os` restricted to date/difftime/time; `require` = requireGen(sandbox, commonPackages, LuaLoadScriptFromAssets); `SfxID` global exposed.
  - `LuaInitialize`: emplace state; set warn fn; open libs base, coroutine, debug, math, os, package, string, table, utf8; run RequireGenSrc (non-optional); build commonPackages table with keys: (debug: `devilutionx.dev`), `devilutionx.version`=PROJECT_VERSION, `devilutionx.i18n`, `.items`, `.log`, `.audio`, `.monsters`, `.player`, `.render`, `.towners`, `.hellfire`, `.system`, `.floatingnumbers`, `devilutionx.message` = fn(text)→EventPlrMsg(text, ColorRed), and `inspect` loaded WITHOUT sandbox (non-optional RunScript of "inspect"); register `setEnvironment` global; hook every Mods option entry's value-changed callback to LuaReloadActiveMods; call LuaReloadActiveMods.
  - `LuaReloadActiveMods` exact order: (1) events = RunScript(no env, "devilutionx.events", optional=false) and store into commonPackages; (2) ClearTownerDialogOptions(); (3) gbIsHellfire=false; (4) UnloadModArchives(); (5) read active mod list from options; LoadModArchives(names); (6) for each mod: RunScript(CreateLuaSandbox(), "mods.<name>.init", optional=true); (7) run all IsModChangeHandlers; (8) effects_cleanup_sfx() then sound_init() if gbRunGame else ui_sound_init(); (9) LoadTextData, LoadPlayerDataFiles, LoadSpellData, LoadMissileData, LoadMonsterData, LoadItemData, LoadObjectData, LoadQuestData; (10) lua::LoadModsComplete().
  - `LuaShutdown`: (debug: LuaReplShutdown); ClearTownerDialogOptions() BEFORE destroying state (callbacks hold sol::function handles); reset CurrentLuaState.
  - `SafeCallResult`: invalid → string-typed error → "Lua error: <msg>" else "Unknown Lua error"; !optional → app_fatal else LogError; return result.
- 1:1 constraints: sandbox builtin list order/values at lines ~196–207 (exact set listed above); `os` allowlist exactly {date, difftime, time} (~209–213); requireGen Lua source verbatim at lines ~73–90 (semantics matter: loaded-cache, string→error, setEnvironment before call, cache after call); mod package name format `"mods." + modname + ".init"` (line ~247); LuaReloadActiveMods step ordering lines 238–283 (exact sequence above); path building `lua\` prefix, `.lua` suffix, `.`→`\` replacement only between prefix/suffix (lines ~103–109); events package name "devilutionx.events"; commonPackages key strings lines 297–316; `_DEBUG` true iff compiled with _DEBUG.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `CurrentLuaState` is a global optional — single-threaded assumption; `warnBuffer` is a function-static mutable string; `IsModChangeHandlers` global vector of function_refs (refs are non-owning — callers must keep targets alive); reload path mutates many globals (gbIsHellfire, DungeonSeeds via data reloads) and re-inits audio — order-sensitive; compiledScripts cache grows monotonically (no invalidation except full shutdown).
- Test coverage: none found for lua_global itself (grep for SafeCallResult/LuaAudioModule in test/ returns nothing; test/assets_test.cpp and test/inv_test.cpp reference lua headers only incidentally).
- Go mapping: `internal/lua` (or `pkg/lua`) — a `Runtime` struct owning `*lua.LState`, packages map, bytecode cache, sandbox constructor; mod loader in `internal/mods`. Use gopher-lua; replicate requireGen as a Go-registered closure set rather than Lua source where possible, but keep observable semantics identical.
- Risks/open questions: gopher-lua lacks `sol::` usertypes — the module factories need a Go binding layer; `inspect` script must exist as a game asset (loaded non-optional, non-sandboxed — its absence is fatal); segmented_map iteration order is never relied on, so a Go map suffices.

### Source/lua/metadoc.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only helpers to attach machine-readable signature/docstring/member-type metadata to sol2 usertypes and tables (used by the REPL/docs tooling), plus getters to read them back.
- Public API: enum `LuaUserdataMemberType : uint8_t { ReadonlyProperty, Property, MemberFunction, Constructor }`; key builders `LuaSignatureKey/LuaDocstringKey/LuaUserdataMemberTypeKey` (prefix `__sig_`/`__doc_`/`__udt_`); templates `LuaSetDocFn` (usertype and table overloads; one 4-arg table overload without doc), `LuaSetDocReadonlyProperty`, `LuaSetDocProperty` (getter/setter and member-pointer overloads), `LuaSetDoc`; getters `GetSignature(table,key)`, `GetDocstring(table,key)`, `GetLuaUserdataSignature(userdata,key)`, `GetLuaUserdataDocstring(userdata,key)`, `GetLuaUserdataMemberType(userdata,key,value)`.
- Depends on: sol/sol.hpp; utils/str_cat.hpp (StrCat for key building).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Metadata must be stored as hidden table fields with keys `__sig_<key>`, `__doc_<key>`, `__udt_<key>` on the metatable/usertype table so any Lua-side doc tooling still works.
  - Member-type inference fallback in `GetLuaUserdataMemberType` (lines ~117–126): no `__udt_` entry → if value is userdata → Property; if function AND key=="new" → Constructor; else nil.
  - Registering a documented member must set both the callable/property and the three metadata fields atomically per member.
- 1:1 constraints: key prefixes `__sig_`, `__doc_`, `__udt_` (lines 22–32); enum ordinals 0..3 in declaration order (lines 15–20); inference rules above; the 3-arg `LuaSetDocFn` table overload sets only signature, no doc (lines ~101–106).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: none (pure helpers).
- Test coverage: none found.

- Requirements for Go port:
  - `get`: selection precedence — HoldItem if non-empty; else pcursinvitem != -1: < INVITEM_INV_FIRST → InvBody[pcursinvitem]; <= INVITEM_INV_LAST → InvList[pcursinvitem - INVITEM_INV_FIRST]; else SpdList[pcursinvitem - INVITEM_BELT_FIRST]; else pcursitem != -1 → Items[pcursitem]; else nil.
  - `info`: if item found, multi-line dump of _iIName, IDidx (+AllItemsList[iName]), _iSeed, _iCreateInfo, `_iCreateInfo & CF_LEVEL` as "Level", then boolean flags Only Good/Unique Monster/Dungeon Item/Unique Item/Smith/Smith Premium/Boy/Witch/Healer/Pregen from CF_ONLYGOOD/CF_UPER15/CF_UPER1/CF_UNIQUE/CF_SMITH/CF_SMITHPREMIUM/CF_BOY/CF_WITCH/CF_HEALER/CF_PREGEN (True when bit set); in multiplayer also round-trip PackNetItem→UnPackNetItem and report "Success"/"Failure"; no item → "Num items: <ActiveItemCount>".
  - `spawn(name)`: refuse if ActiveItemCount >= MAXITEMS ("No space to generate the item!"); lowercase the name; loop: seed global RNG with `uniform_int_distribution<int32_t>(0, INT_MAX)(BetterRng)` (BetterRng is a dedicated non-seeded mt19937 global, line 85); time limit 3000 ms ("Item not found in 3 seconds!") and iteration limit 1,000,000 ("Item not found in 1000000 tries!"); per iteration: monsterLevel = dist(BetterRng) % CF_LEVEL + 1; idx = RndItemForMonsterLevel(monsterLevel); skip IDI_NONE/IDI_GOLD; reset testItem{}; SetupAllItems(*MyPlayer, testItem, idx, AdvanceRndSeed(), monsterLevel, 1, false, false); TryRandomUniqueItem(testItem, idx, monsterLevel, 1, false, false); SetupItem(testItem); break when lowercased _iIName contains name; then AllocateItem, item = testItem.pop(), _iIdentified=true, GetSuperItemSpace(MyPlayer tile, ii), NetSendCmdPItem(false, CMD_SPAWNITEM, pos, item); return "Item generated successfully - iterations: <i>".
  - `spawnUnique(name)`: same capacity guard; find first UniqueItems entry whose lowercased UIName contains name (remember index); not found → "No unique item found!"; find first available base item j with AllItemsList[j].iItemId == uniqueItem.UIItemId (IsItemAvailable), starting sentinel IDI_GOLD → "Base item not available!" if unchanged; loop with same 3000 ms/1M iter limits: testItem={}, copy _iMiscId from base, seed RNG via BetterRng, set ALL UniqueItemFlags true then [uniqueIndex]=false, SetupAllItems with seed = (iMiscId==IMISC_UNIQUE ? uniqueIndex : AdvanceRndSeed()) and UIMinLvl as level, TryRandomUniqueItem, SetupItem, clear ALL UniqueItemFlags to false; accept when _iMagical == ITEM_QUALITY_UNIQUE and name matches; place identical to spawn (note: sets _iIdentified AFTER GetSuperItemSpace here, and returns same success string).
- 1:1 constraints: seeding scheme — global RNG reseeded each iteration from BetterRng `dist(0, INT_MAX)`; monsterLevel formula `(dist % CF_LEVEL) + 1`; limits max_time=3000, max_iter=1000000; UniqueItemFlags manipulation (all true, target false, restore all false) is the forcing mechanism and must be preserved; unique spawn seed special-case IMISC_UNIQUE → uniqueIndex; name matching is substring-on-lowercased; net commands CMD_SPAWNITEM with `false` (not pawdent? — first arg false); spawn sets _iIdentified before placement, spawnUnique after placement (lines 156 vs 190) — preserve.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `std::mt19937 BetterRng` at namespace scope, default-seeded (line 85) — deterministic across a session but NOT across runs unless seeded; the shared UniqueItemFlags array is temporarily corrupted during search — a concurrent reader would misbehave; global RNG (SetRndSeed) is mutated per iteration.

### Source/lua/modules/dev/level.cpp
- Purpose: Debug-only level commands: export current level as a .DUN file, reset a level (optionally reseeding), query level seeds; aggregates `map` and `warp` submodules.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaDevLevelModule(sol::state_view &lua)`; module-local: `std::string ExportDun()`, `std::string DebugCmdResetLevel(uint8_t, std::optional<int>)`, `std::string DebugCmdLevelSeed(std::optional<uint8_t>)`.
- Depends on: `levels/gendung.h` DMAXX/DMAXY/dungeon/dTransVal/dMonster/DungeonSeeds/LevelSeeds/MAXDUNX/MAXDUNY; `monster.h` Monsters/MonstConvTbl (tables/monstdat.h, 157 entries); `objects.h` FindObjectAtPosition/ObjTypeConv (tables/objdat.h, 147 entries); `player.h` MyPlayer; `diablo.h` gbIsHellfire/gbRunGame? (currlevel via diablo.h); DeltaClearLevel (levels/drlg common via gendung chain — declared in levels headers); utils/endian_stream WriteLE16; utils/file_util OpenFile; dev/level/{map,warp}.hpp submodules; metadoc.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `exportDun`: filename `<currlevel>-<DungeonSeeds[currlevel]>.dun` opened in append-binary ("ab"); write LE16 DMAXX, LE16 DMAXY; tiles: for y in [0,DMAXY) x in [0,DMAXX) LE16 dungeon[x][y]; padding: for y,x in [16, MAXDUN{Y,X}-16) LE16 0; monsters: same 16..MAX-16 range, monsterId=0 default, if dMonster[x][y] > 0 scan MonstConvTbl[0..156] for match with Monsters[|dMonster|-1].type().type → monsterId = i+1; objects: same range, FindObjectAtPosition({x,y}, false), scan ObjTypeConv[0..146] for _otype match → objectId = i (NOTE: not i+1); transparency: same range LE16 dTransVal[x][y]; close; return "Successfully exported <name>."
  - `reset(n, seed)`: level > (gbIsHellfire ? 24 : 16) → "Level <n> does not exist!"; if MyPlayer is on that level → "Unable to reset dungeon levels occupied by players!"; set _pLvlVisited[level]=false; DeltaClearLevel(level); with seed: DungeonSeeds[level]=seed, LevelSeeds[level]=nil, "Successfully reset level <n> with seed <seed>."; without: "Successfully reset level <n>."
  - `seed(level)`: NumLevels = len(DungeonSeeds); explicit level >= NumLevels → "level out of range, max: <NumLevels-1>"; return string of DungeonSeeds[level or currlevel].
  - Module table: exportDun "()" "Save the current level as a dun-file."; map (submodule) "Automap-related commands."; reset "(n: number, seed: number = nil)" "Resets specified level."; seed "(level: number = nil)" "Get the seed of the current or given level."; warp (submodule) "Warp to a level or a custom map."
- 1:1 constraints: .DUN byte order little-endian, section order tiles→padding→monsters→objects→transparency; tile area is DMAXX×DMAXY (full), other sections clipped to [16, MAXDUN-16); monster id = tableIndex+1 (1-based), object id = tableIndex (0-based) — asymmetry is original-game-format; table sizes 157 (MonstConvTbl) and 147 (ObjTypeConv) hardcoded (lines 63, 80); append mode "ab" (repeated exports append); Hellfire level cap 24 vs 16; filename format `StrCat(currlevel, "-", DungeonSeeds[currlevel], ".dun")`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: file side effect in CWD (append) — repeated calls grow file; reads global dungeon state; reset mutates DungeonSeeds/LevelSeeds/_pLvlVisited and delta state.
- Test coverage: none found for the binding; DRLG tests (test/drlg_*_test.cpp) exercise dungeon generation, not export.
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/modules/dev/level` + reuse `pkg/dun` (or internal/levels/dunfile) writer with encoding/binary LittleEndian; conversion tables mirrored from Source/tables/{monstdat,objdat}.h.
- Risks/open questions: MonstConvTbl/ObjTypeConv live outside this batch — their exact 157/147 values must be ported from those headers; "ab" append semantics mean a Go port should decide whether to truncate instead (1:1 says append).

- Purpose: Implements `dev.monsters`: `spawn(name, count)` spawns regular monsters near the player; `spawnUnique(name, count)` spawns uniques — both use crawl-based free-tile search and dynamic monster-type slot registration.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaDevMonstersModule(sol::state_view &lua)` (line 172); internal `DebugCmdSpawnUniqueMonster(std::string, std::optional<unsigned>)` (24), `DebugCmdSpawnMonster(std::string, std::optional<unsigned>)` (99).
