- Requirements for Go port:
  - Shared prelude (both commands): town check "Can't spawn monsters in town"; empty name "name is required"; `count = countOpt ?? 1`; `count < 1` → "count must be positive"; lowercase name via `AsciiStrToLower`.
  - Unique name resolution: scan `UniqueMonstersData` in index order; substring match on lowercased `mName`; exact match breaks early; keep `mtype` and `uniqueIndex = UniqueMonsterType(i)`. Not found → "Monster not found".
  - Regular name resolution: same scan over `MonstersData`; `mtype = index`; exact match breaks early. Additionally requires `MyPlayer->isLevelOwnedByLocalClient()` else "You are not the level owner." (line 121).
  - Type-slot resolution (both): search `LevelMonsterTypes[0..LevelMonsterTypeCount)` for `.type == mtype` → reuse id; else if `LevelMonsterTypeCount == MaxLvlMTypes` decrement it first (overwrite last slot, lines 60–61 / 135–136), then `AddMonsterType(...)` (unique variant takes `UniqueMonsterType`, regular takes `_monster_id`, both with `PLACE_SCATTER`); on error return the error string; then `InitMonsterGFX(slot)`; `slot.corpseId = 1` (67 / 142).
  - Unique spawn loop: `Crawl(0, MaxCrawlRadius, cb)` (74); cb: `pos = playerTile + displacement`; skip if `dPlayer != 0 || dMonster != 0` or `!IsTileWalkable(pos)`; else `AddMonster(pos, myPlayer._pdir, id, true)`; nullptr → terminate with "Spawned N monsters. (Unable to spawn more)"; else `PrepareUniqueMonst(*monster, uniqueIndex, 0, 0, UniqueMonstersData[uniqueIndex])` (84), `monster->corpseId = 1` (85), increment; at `spawnedMonster >= count` return "Spawned N monsters."; crawl exhausted → "Spawned N monsters. (Unable to spawn more)".

(Unable to spawn more)" else "Spawned N monsters."
- 1:1 constraints: MaxCrawlRadius = 18 (lighting.h:74; used at 74 and 152), crawl starts at radius 0 (player tile first); `PrepareUniqueMonst` args exactly `(monster, uniqueIndex, 0, 0, UniqueMonstersData[uniqueIndex])` (84); `corpseId = 1` on both the type slot (67/142) and each spawned unique (85); slot-overflow decrements `LevelMonsterTypeCount` before `AddMonsterType` (60–61, 135–136); unique path has NO level-owner gate, regular path does (121); regular caps by `MaxMonsters - ActiveMonsterCount`, unique relies on `AddMonster` returning null.

- Depends on: `MyPlayer`; `Player::InvGrid` (int8_t[40]), `InvList` (Item[40]), `_pNumInv`, `_pGold`, `RemoveInvItem(int)` (player.h; `InventoryGridCells` = 40 at player.h:38); `Item::isGold`, `isEmpty`, `_ivalue`, `MakeGoldStack` (items.h; `GOLD_MAX_LIMIT` = 5000 at items.h:30); `CalcPlrInv(player, true)`; `StrCat`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `give(amount?)`: `goldToAdd = amount ?? GOLD_MAX_LIMIT * InventoryGridCells` (19); `<= 0` → "amount must be positive". Loop over `InvGrid` in order; skip cells `itemIndex < 0` (24). Item select: `InvList[itemIndex != 0 ? itemIndex - 1 : _pNumInv]` (27). For nonzero cell: skip if (!isGold && !isEmpty) or (isGold && _ivalue == GOLD_MAX_LIMIT) (30). For zero cell: item = InvList[_pNumInv]; if empty → `MakeGoldStack(item, 0)`, `_pNumInv++`, write `itemIndex = _pNumInv` (33–36). Then `addable = GOLD_MAX_LIMIT - _ivalue` (40); if addable >= goldToAdd → `_ivalue += goldToAdd; _pGold += goldToAdd; break` (41–44); else `_ivalue += addable; goldToAdd -= addable; _pGold += addable` (47–49). Finally `CalcPlrInv(myPlayer, true)` (52); return "Set your gold to {X}, added {X-before}."
  - `take(amount?)`: `goldToRemove = amount ?? GOLD_MAX_LIMIT * InventoryGridCells` (60); `<= 0` → "amount must be positive". Loop over InvGrid; `itemIndex -= 1` (65); skip `< 0` (67); item = InvList[itemIndex] (70); skip `!isGold` (71); if `_ivalue >= goldToRemove` → `_pGold -= goldToRemove; _ivalue -= goldToRemove; if _ivalue == 0 RemoveInvItem(itemIndex); break` (74–79); else `_pGold -= _ivalue; goldToRemove -= _ivalue; RemoveInvItem(itemIndex)` (82–84). Return "Set your gold to {X}, removed {before-X}."
- 1:1 constraints: default amount = 5000 × 40 = 200000 (19, 60); give's asymmetric index arithmetic — `- 1` for nonzero cells, bare `_pNumInv` for zero cells (27); zero-value stack removed only in the `>=` full-consume branch (77–78), partial branch always removes (84); `CalcPlrInv(…, true)` called in give only (52), never in take.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutates inventory and `_pGold` directly, bypassing normal gold-pickup messages; game-tick context; CalcPlrInv recalculates derived stats; no RNG.

- Go mapping: `internal/player` inventory port (InvGrid/InvList/RemoveInvItem/CalcPlrInv) + binding; gold constants from `internal/items`.
- Risks/open questions: if goldToAdd exceeds what all stacks absorb, the leftover is silently dropped — message still reports true delta via before/after; replicate.

### Source/lua/modules/dev/player/stats.cpp
- Purpose: Debug player stat commands exposed to Lua: adjust HP/mana, level up via cheat network command, set attributes to max/min, refill life/mana.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaDevPlayerStatsModule(sol::state_view &lua)` registering: `adjustHealth(amount:number)`, `adjustMana(amount:number)`, `levelUp(amount:number=1)`, `rejuvenate()`, `setAttrToMax()`, `setAttrToMin()`.
- Depends on: `MyPlayer` (player.h), `Player::{getCharacterLevel,RestoreFullLife,RestoreFullMana,_pHitPoints,_pMana,_pManaBase,_pMaxManaBase,_pMaxMana,_pBaseStr/_pBaseMag/_pBaseDex/_pBaseVit,GetMaximumAttributeValue}`; `NetSendCmd(true, CMD_CHEAT_EXPERIENCE)`; `ModifyPlrStr/Mag/Dex/Vit`; `SetPlayerHitPoints`; `SyncPlrKill(p, DeathReason::MonsterOrTrap)`; `RedrawComponent(PanelDrawComponent::Health/Mana)` (engine/backbuffer_state.hpp); `StrCat/StrAppend` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `LuaSetDocFn` (lua/metadoc.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - All six functions return a human-readable result string (exact wording matters for parity; see 1:1).
  - `levelUp`: loops `levelsToAdd` times sending `CMD_CHEAT_EXPERIENCE` as a command (param1=true); reports the *predicted* new level (`current + levelsToAdd`) — it does NOT re-read actual level.
  - `setAttrToMax`/`setAttrToMin`: compute deltas vs base attributes and call Modify* helpers (which clamp and apply derived-stat recalc on the C++ side); Go must route through equivalent attribute-modification functions, not raw field writes.
  - `rejuvenate`: RestoreFullLife + RestoreFullMana + redraw health and mana panel components.
  - `adjustHealth`: `newHealth = _pHitPoints + change*64` (64 = internal HP per point), via `SetPlayerHitPoints`; if result <= 0 → `SyncPlrKill(MonsterOrTrap)`.
  - `adjustMana`: raw write `_pMana = _pMana + change*64`, then `_pManaBase = _pMana + _pMaxManaBase - _pMaxMana` (preserves the base/current offset), then redraw Mana only. Note: no clamping and no kill check.
  - Zero-amount guards for health/mana return the exact error strings.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - L15: `levelsToAdd = levels.value_or(1)`; L17 error string `"amount must be positive"` when `<= 0`; L20 returns `StrCat("New character level: ", level + levelsToAdd)`.
  - L24-30: max-stats deltas = `GetMaximumAttributeValue(attr) - _pBase<attr>` for Str/Mag/Dex/Vit in that order.
  - L33-39: min-stats deltas = `-_pBase<attr>` (i.e. subtract all base).
  - L50/L60: HP/mana scale factor `change * 64` (both).
  - L52: `"Enter a value not equal to 0 to change life!"`; L61: `"Enter a value not equal to 0 to change mana!"`.
  - L55: kill only when `newHealth <= 0`, reason `DeathReason::MonsterOrTrap`.
  - L63: `_pManaBase = _pMana + _pMaxManaBase - _pMaxMana`.
  - L65: `"Changed life by <n>"` / L68 `"Changed mana by <n>"`.
  - Registration table keys are alphabetical: adjustHealth, adjustMana, levelUp, rejuvenate, setAttrToMax, setAttrToMin (L76-81).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutates live `*MyPlayer` (global) and sends network commands; only safe on game/logic thread. Debug builds only (`#ifdef _DEBUG` L1). No RNG.
- Test coverage: none found (no tests reference these debug commands or the module function).
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/modules/dev/player` — stats.go with debug build tag; thin wrappers over `internal/player` attribute/hitpoint APIs and `internal/net` command send.
- Risks/open questions: `CMD_CHEAT_EXPERIENCE` is singleplayer-cheat only in some contexts; Go port must keep the "predicted level" behavior (string uses pre-apply level + N) for message parity.

  - Single binding `devilutionx.floatingnumbers.add(...)`; the velocity argument is hard-coded to `{0, 0}` (zero vector) — the Lua API does not expose velocity.
  - Optional params default: `id=0`, `reverseDirection=false`.
  - Go needs a Point type bound to Lua (x,y) and a UiFlags enum binding acceptable from Lua (style flags such as color/alignment used by floating numbers).
  - Registered in the global module table as `devilutionx.floatingnumbers` (lua_global.cpp:317).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - L14: doc string `"(text: string, pos: Point, style: UiFlags, id: integer = 0, reverseDirection: boolean = false)"`, description `"Add a floating number"`.
  - L17: call is `AddFloatingNumber(pos, { 0, 0 }, text, style, id.value_or(0), reverseDirection.value_or(false))` — second arg literal zero-vector.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Release build (no `_DEBUG` guard — available in normal games/scripts). Floating numbers are render-side transient state managed in qol/floatingnumbers; call from game thread. No RNG here.
- Test coverage: none found (no test references to LuaFloatingNumbersModule or Lua-driven AddFloatingNumber; floating-numbers core itself is also untested per grep).
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/modules` — floatingnumbers.go binding `internal/qol/floatingnumbers.Add`.
- Risks/open questions: UiFlags binding surface — Go port must decide how Lua passes style flags (integer bitmask vs named constants); C++ relies on sol's automatic enum conversion.

### Source/lua/modules/hellfire.cpp
- Purpose: Lua exposure of Hellfire control: load Hellfire MPQ archives on demand and flip the global `gbIsHellfire` flag to enable Hellfire mode at runtime.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaHellfireModule(sol::state_view &lua)` registering `loadData()` (bound directly to `LoadHellfireArchives`) and `enable()` (lambda setting `gbIsHellfire = true`).
- Depends on: `LoadHellfireArchives` (engine/assets.hpp); global `bool gbIsHellfire` (declared in a core header, e.g. options/defs — set here); `LuaSetDocFn`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two bindings under `devilutionx.hellfire` (registered at lua_global.cpp:315): `loadData` calls the archive-loading routine (loads hellfire MPQs); `enable` sets the global Hellfire-mode boolean to true.
  - `loadData` returns whatever `LoadHellfireArchives` returns (void or status — bind 1:1 to the Go loader signature); doc string is empty (`""`), description defaults to the function name — i.e. no user-facing doc text.
  - `enable` has no return value.
  - Release build — not debug-gated.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - L13: `LuaSetDocFn(table, "loadData", "()", LoadHellfireArchives)` — empty doc string, direct function binding.
  - L14: `LuaSetDocFn(table, "enable", "()", []() { gbIsHellfire = true; })` — sets global, returns nothing.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutates the process-global `gbIsHellfire` — affects data-table selection, monster/item sets, and many downstream branches; flipping it after content is loaded will leave mixed state (C++ has the same hazard). Archive loading touches global asset handles. No RNG. Call order relative to game init matters (intended for early/scripted init).
- Test coverage: none found (no test references to LuaHellfireModule or scripted gbIsHellfire toggling).
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/modules` — hellfire.go binding `internal/assets.LoadHellfireArchives` and a setter for the global mode flag (e.g. `internal/game.SetHellfire(true)`).
- Risks/open questions: Real hazard: enabling after Diablo data is cached produces inconsistent state in C++; Go port should either replicate the hazard faithfully or (better) document/restrict when `enable` may be called — decide explicitly.

### Source/lua/modules/i18n.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the Lua `i18n` module table exposing translation functions from the C++ i18n layer to scripts.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaI18nModule(sol::state_view &lua)` (line 9). Module table functions:
  - `language_code()` → string (GetLanguageCode)
  - `translate(text: string)` → string (LanguageTranslate)
  - `plural_translate(singular: string, plural: string, count: integer)` → string
  - `particular_translate(context: string, text: string)` → string (LanguageParticularTranslate)
  - `is_small_font_tall()` → bool (IsSmallFontTall)
- Depends on: `GetLanguageCode`, `LanguageTranslate`, `LanguagePluralTranslate`, `LanguageParticularTranslate`, `IsSmallFontTall` from Source/utils/language.h; `FormatRuntime` from Source/utils/format.hpp; `LuaSetDocFn` from Source/lua/metadoc.hpp.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lua module `i18n` with the five functions above, identical names/arity/signatures.
  - `translate` takes a Lua string (C `const char*`) and returns translated string via the Go translation table.
  - `plural_translate` must select singular/plural by count via plural rule then **substitute the count into the resulting format string**: `FormatRuntime(LanguagePluralTranslate(singular, plural, count), count)` (lines 21–24). So the translated plural template contains `{}`-style (fmt::runtime) placeholders and count is the substitution argument.
  - `particular_translate` passes (context, text) straight through to the particular-translation lookup (msgid with context prefix).
  - `is_small_font_tall` exposes the small-font-tall (16px) language property (used to pick small text font variant).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Exact binding names/signatures at lines 13–29; `plural_translate` order: translate first, then FormatRuntime with count (lines 21–24).
  - Return of translate family is a plain Lua string; language_code returns the current code string.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Reads global language state set at startup; no mutation. Safe if language isn't hot-swapped at runtime.
- Test coverage: none found (no test/ file references LuaI18nModule).
- Go mapping: internal/lua/modules/i18n.go wrapping internal/i18n (or pkg/translate) — thin adapter; keep function names verbatim.
- Risks/open questions: FormatRuntime semantics (fmt-style `{}` vs `%`) must match Go translation-file templates; confirm placeholder convention of devilutionX .mo/translation pipeline during the i18n core port.

### Source/lua/modules/log.cpp
- Purpose: Implements the Lua `log` module: `log.info/verbose/debug/warn/error(fmt, ...)` with a runtime-parsed `std::format`-style formatter for Lua arguments, routed to SDL logging.
- Public API:
  - `sol::table LuaLogModule(sol::state_view &lua)` (line 161) → table with `info`, `verbose`, `debug`, `warn`, `error` (lines 164–169).
  - Internal: `FormatLuaMessage(fmt, args) -> expected<string,string>` (line 36); `LuaLogMessage(priority, fmt, variadic_args)` (line 111); thin wrappers LuaLogInfo/Verbose/Debug/Warn/Error (lines 149–159).
- Depends on: `SDL_LogMessage`/`SDL_LogCritical` + `SDL_LOG_CATEGORY_APPLICATION` (SDL2/SDL3 headers, lines 3–6); `LogPriority` from Source/utils/log.hpp (mapped to SDL_LogPriority); `StrCat` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `sol::utility::to_string` for fallback conversion; `DVL_EXCEPTIONS` macro (utils/attributes.h).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lua module `log` with the five level functions accepting (fmt, ...) variadic Lua args.
  - Argument coercion order (lines 115–129): boolean → bool; number → lua_Integer if `lua_isinteger` else lua_Number; string → string; anything else → `tostring`-style conversion (sol utility to_string) as string.
  - Format parser supporting `std::format` replacement-field grammar subset: literal `{{`/`}}` escapes; `{}` auto-indexing; `{N}` manual indexing; `{...:spec}` format spec passed through; mixed auto/manual indexing is an ERROR ("cannot switch from manual to automatic argument indexing" / reverse); unmatched `{` or `}` errors; out-of-range argument index error (lines 36–108).
  - On format error: log via SDL_LogCritical with message `"Format error, fmt: <fmt> error: <err>"` and do NOT log the original message (lines 132–136).
  - Success: `SDL_LogMessage(SDL_LOG_CATEGORY_APPLICATION, priority, "%s", formatted)` (lines 138–140).
  - Format spec applied per-argument by rebuilding `"{:" + spec + "}"` and calling std::vformat (lines 95–99) — Go equivalent: fmt.Sprintf with translated spec (see risks).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Error strings verbatim (lines 46, 63, 72, 75, 78, 85): `"unmatched '}' in format string"`, `"unmatched '{' in format string"`, `"cannot switch from manual to automatic argument indexing"`, `"cannot switch from automatic to manual argument indexing"`, `"invalid argument id \"<argId>\""`, `"argument index <N> out of range"`.
  - `}}`→`}` and `{{`→`{` escape handling at lines 42–45 and 60–63.
  - Field scan: `fmt.find_first_of("{}", i+1)` — a nested `{` inside a field is an error (line 66).
  - Levels map to LogPriority::Info/Verbose/Debug/Warn/Error → SDL priorities (lines 149–159).
  - Priority passed through as `static_cast<SDL_LogPriority>(priority)` — LogPriority enum values must line up with SDL_LogPriority (SDL_LOG_PRIORITY_VERBOSE..SDL_LOG_PRIORITY_CRITICAL).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: no game state touched; pure logging. SDL log call is thread-safe per SDL. Format parse is deterministic given (fmt, args).
- Test coverage: none found (FormatLuaMessage not referenced in test/).
- Go mapping: internal/lua/modules/log.go + a small formatter util (internal/lua/format). Strategy: implement a `{}`/`{N}`/`{:.spec}` parser producing fmt.Sprintf calls; for spec translation, map common std::format specs (d, s, f precisions) — or pre-translate at the Lua boundary since Go fmt verbs differ from std::format.
- Risks/open questions: std::format spec grammar (e.g. `{:.2f}`, `{:>10}`) is not identical to Go fmt verbs; a 1:1 port needs a spec-translator or an embedded format implementation. Also `sol::utility::to_string` for non-scalar args (tables) produces Lua `tostring` semantics — replicate with Lua's tostring.

  - `addMonsterDataFromTsv(path: string)` (line 51)
  - `addUniqueMonsterDataFromTsv(path: string)` (line 56)
  - Monster usertype: readonly `position` → Point (lines 38–41), readonly `id` → integer (lines 42–45).
- Depends on: `Monster` (Source/monster.h); `LoadMonstDatFromFile(dataFile, path, true)` and `LoadUniqueMonstDatFromFile(dataFile, path)` (Source/tables/monstdat.h); `DataFile::loadOrDie` (Source/data/file.hpp); `Point` (Source/engine/point.hpp); `LuaSetDocFn`/`LuaSetDocReadonlyProperty` (Source/lua/metadoc.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lua userdata type for Go `Monster`, no constructor.
  - `position` getter returns Point {tile x,y} — readonly, no setter.
  - `id` getter returns pointer-based identity: `static_cast<int>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(&monster))` (line 44) — Go equivalent: unique per-object id; use a monotonically assigned id or map-based object identity (Go can't cast a pointer to int portably at 32-bit truncation parity — see risks).
  - `addMonsterDataFromTsv`: DataFile::loadOrDie(path) then `LoadMonstDatFromFile(dataFile, path, /*translate=*/true)` — note the hardcoded `true` third arg (line 35).

- 1:1 constraints:
  - Monster data loader passes `true` for translate flag (line 35) — unique loader has no such flag (line 40).
  - `id` is the C++ object address truncated to int (line 44).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: loaders mutate global monster data tables (MonstDat/UniqueMonstDat arrays). Position read is a snapshot; no locking. Pointer-based id is stable only while object address is stable.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: internal/lua/modules/monsters.go wrapping internal/game (Monster type) + tables/monstdat TSV parser. For id, prefer an explicit per-monster numeric ID if the engine has one; otherwise registry-assigned handle.

Confirm `translate=true` semantics in LoadMonstDatFromFile port (string translation of monster names).

### Source/lua/modules/player.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the Lua `player` module: Player usertype (readonly name/id/position, writable characterLevel, methods for experience, item add/has/remove, HP/MP restore, mana getters) plus module-level `self()` and `walk_to(x,y)`.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaPlayerModule(sol::state_view &lua)` (line 121). Module functions: `self()` → Player (line 126), `walk_to(x: integer, y: integer)` (line 131). Player usertype:
  - readonly: `name` (string), `id` (integer, pointer-derived), `position` (Point), `mana` (`_pMana >> 6`), `maxMana` (`_pMaxMana >> 6`)
  - read/write: `characterLevel` via getCharacterLevel/setCharacterLevel (line 33)
  - methods: `addExperience(experience, monsterLevel = nil)`, `addItem(itemId, count = 1) → bool`, `hasItem(itemId) → bool`, `removeItem(itemId, count = 1) → int`, `restoreFullLife()`, `restoreFullMana()`
- Depends on: `Player`, `MyPlayer`, `MyPlayerId` (Source/player.h); `SetupAllItems`, `_item_indexes`, `CalcPlrInv` (Source/items.h); `AutoPlaceItemInInventory`, `HasInventoryOrBeltItemWithId` (Source/inv.h); `AdvanceRndSeed` (Source/engine/random.hpp); `NetSendCmdLoc`, `CMD_WALKXY` (Source/effects.h); `Point` (engine/point.hpp); `MaxBeltItems` (inv.h).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `self()` returns the local player object (MyPlayer).
  - `walk_to(x, y)` sends network command `NetSendCmdLoc(MyPlayerId, true, CMD_WALKXY, Point{x,y})` — this queues a network-replicated walk command, not an instant teleport.
  - `addExperience` dispatches: with monsterLevel → `player.addExperience(exp, level)`, without → `player.addExperience(exp)` (two overloads; monsterLevel is optional Lua arg).
  - `addItem(itemId, count=1)` loop: for each of count items — create zero Item, `SetupAllItems(player, tempItem, itemIndex, AdvanceRndSeed(), 1, 1, true, false)` then `AutoPlaceItemInInventory(player, tempItem, true)`; on any placement failure return false immediately; after loop `CalcPlrInv(player, true)` and return true. NOTE: consumes one RNG advance per item via AdvanceRndSeed.
  - `hasItem` delegates to HasInventoryOrBeltItemWithId with the cast index.
  - `removeItem(itemId, count=1)`: scan inventory BACKWARD (`for i = _pNumInv-1; i >= 0 && removed < itemCount; i--`) calling `player.RemoveInvItem(i)` on IDidx match; then belt backward (`MaxBeltItems-1 .. 0`) skipping empty slots, calling `player.RemoveSpdBarItem(i)`; if removed>0 `CalcPlrInv(player, true)`; return removed count.
  - `restoreFullLife`: `_pHitPoints = _pMaxHP; _pHPBase = _pMaxHPBase`. `restoreFullMana`: `_pMana = _pMaxMana; _pManaBase = _pMaxManaBase`.
  - `mana`/`maxMana` getters shift right by 6 (fixed→whole points conversion).
  - `id` = pointer truncated to int (line 22).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - SetupAllItems arg tuple exact: `(player, tempItem, itemIndex, AdvanceRndSeed(), 1, 1, true, false)` (line 48).
  - Removal iteration order and bounds: inventory index descending from `_pNumInv-1`; belt descending from `MaxBeltItems-1`; stop as soon as `removed == itemCount` (lines 66–77).
  - `mana >> 6` and `maxMana >> 6` (lines 105, 109).
  - walk_to sends `CMD_WALKXY` with `true` auto-routing flag (line 134).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `addItem` advances the global RNG (AdvanceRndSeed) — call order affects determinism of subsequent game RNG draws; must match in Go. Methods mutate live player state and trigger inventory recalculation. NetSendCmdLoc enqueues a command — timing-sensitive in multiplayer replication.
- Test coverage: none found for the Lua module; underlying inv functions covered by test/inv_test.cpp (inventory placement logic).
- Go mapping: internal/lua/modules/player.go wrapping internal/game Player; RNG from the shared deterministic engine RNG package (must be the same stream as C++ AdvanceRndSeed-equivalent, not math/rand).
- Risks/open questions: pointer-derived `id` (same divergence question as monsters.cpp). `addItem` failure mid-loop leaves earlier items placed but returns false (no rollback) — preserve that behavior. addExperience overload semantics (default monsterLevel path) defined in player.h — verify during core port.

### Source/lua/modules/render.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the Lua `render` module: draw a string to the global back buffer, query screen dimensions, and expose a `UiFlags` bit-flag table for text rendering options.
- Public API: `sol::table LuaRenderModule(sol::state_view &lua)` (line 14). Module functions:
  - `string(text: string, x: integer, y: integer)` — `DrawString(GlobalBackBuffer(), text, {x, y})` (lines 17–19)
  - `screen_width()` → gnScreenWidth (line 21)
  - `screen_height()` → gnScreenHeight (line 23)
  - `UiFlags` sub-table (lines 25–69) with entries below.
- Depends on: `GlobalBackBuffer()` (Source/engine/backbuffer_state.hpp — note: included but the function comes via dx.h/backbuffer state); `DrawString` (Source/engine/render/text_render.hpp); `gnScreenWidth`/`gnScreenHeight` (Source/utils/display.h); `UiFlags` enum (Source/DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp); `LuaSetDocFn` (Source/lua/metadoc.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lua `render.string(text, x, y)`: immediate text draw into the frame's back buffer at pixel coords, using default flags/rectangle `{x, y}` (rectangle with only position → unbounded width/height, default font). Must be callable during render callbacks.
  - `screen_width`/`screen_height` return current logical screen dims (globals updated on resolution change).
  - `UiFlags` table mapping Lua names to flag bit values, combinable with Lua bitwise ops; exact member list:
    - None
    - FontSize12, FontSize24, FontSize30, FontSize42, FontSize46, FontSizeDialog
    - ColorUiGold, ColorUiSilver, ColorUiGoldDark, ColorUiSilverDark, ColorDialogWhite, ColorDialogYellow, ColorDialogRed, ColorYellow, ColorGold, ColorBlack, ColorWhite, ColorWhitegold, ColorRed, ColorBlue, ColorOrange, ColorButtonface, ColorButtonpushed
    - AlignCenter, AlignRight, VerticalCenter
    - KerningFitSpacing
    - ElementDisabled, ElementHidden
    - PentaCursor, Outlined
    - NeedsNextElement
  - Go render text API must accept flags OR-combination and apply font-size/color/alignment/kerning/outline semantics identical to C++ DrawString.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `string` uses `DrawString(GlobalBackBuffer(), text, { x, y })` — Rectangle constructed from two ints only (lines 17–19): no size limits, no UiFlags argument (defaults). Lua cannot pass flags to `render.string` in this version; flags exist only as data (for other consumers/mods composing values).
  - UiFlags member list above is the exact exposure set (lines 27–69); any UiFlags enum members NOT in this list are invisible to Lua.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `string` writes into the global back buffer — only valid on render thread / during draw phase; calling outside frame rendering is UB in C++ (buffer may be locked/unavailable). gnScreenWidth/Height are mutable globals changed on resize.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: internal/lua/modules/render.go wrapping internal/render text drawing + internal/ui UiFlags constants; screen dims from the display/resolution manager. Keep the exact Lua-visible flag names.
- Risks/open questions: back-buffer lifetime (Ebiten: draw only inside Draw callback — the Lua API needs a guard or a command buffer for calls made outside the frame); UiFlags numeric values must match C++ enum bit positions if mods serialize them.

### Source/lua/repl.cpp
- Purpose: Debug-only (`#ifdef _DEBUG`) Lua REPL line evaluator: sandboxed environment, print/warn redirection to in-game console, try-expression-then-statement semantics.
- Public API: (via repl.hpp) `RunLuaReplLine(std::string_view) -> std::expected<std::string, std::string>`; `GetLuaReplEnvironment() -> sol::environment &`; `LuaReplShutdown()`.

- Requirements for Go port:
  - Entire file compiled only in debug builds (build tag or runtime guard).
  - Lazily-created singleton REPL environment from the sandbox; `print` overridden to concatenate args with tabs via luaL_tolstring semantics (each arg's `__tostring`-converted value, tab separator, index from 1).
  - Warning handler accumulates continuation chunks (`continued != 0` appends without flush) then flushes one warning line.
  - Eval order: compile `"return " + code + ";"` first; on failure compile raw code; on both failures return load error as unexpected.
  - Successful expression result converted to string via sol::utility::to_string; statement with no result → empty string; invalid result → error string if result is string else "Unknown Lua error".
- 1:1 constraints: expression prefix is exactly `"return "` with trailing `";"` (line 61); load mode "text"; chunk names via sol default chunk-name scheme (debug info only); print joins with `'\t'` between args (not before first); warn buffer is a function-local `static std::string` (line 25) reset after flush. `LuaReplShutdown` clears the optional env (idempotent).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `static std::string warnBuffer` and `std::optional<sol::environment> replEnv` are mutable globals — assume main-thread-only use; lazy init via GetLuaReplEnvironment has order-of-init coupling with Lua state creation.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/lua/repl` (debug build tag), using gopher-lua: compile with `L.LoadString("return "+code+";")` fallback to `L.LoadString(code)`; errors returned as strings.
- Risks/open questions: sol chunk-name generation has no Go equivalent — error message prefixes will differ slightly (acceptable; note it).

### Source/minitext.cpp
- Purpose: Scrolling quest-narration text window: loads/wraps speech text, computes audio-synced scroll speed, draws bordered background and gold 30pt text lines.
- Public API: (via minitext.h) `qtextflag` global; `FreeQuestText()`; `InitQuestText()`; `InitQTextMsg(_speech_id m)`; `DrawQTextBack(const Surface &out)`; `DrawQText(const Surface &out)`.
- Depends on: `Speeches[]` + `_speech_id` (tables/textdat.h); `WordWrapString(text, 543, GameFont30)` (utils/language / engine text); `GetSFXLength(SfxID)` + `PlaySFX` + `SfxID::Warrior1/10/11/12/54/55/56` (audio); `GetHeroSound(cls, HeroSpeech::...)` (tables/playerdat.hpp); `MyPlayer->_pClass`; `LoadCel("data\\textbox", 591)` (engine/load_cel); `ClxDraw`, `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo`, `DrawString` with `UiFlags::FontSize30|ColorGold` (render); `GetUIRectangle()` (engine); `QuestLogIsOpen` (panels/quest_log); `GetMillisecondsSinceStartup()` (utils/timer); `_()` translation.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Globals: qtextflag (bool, test-visible), qtextSpd (ms/px int), ScrollStart (uint32 ms), pTextBoxCels (CLX list), TextLines vector.
  - InitQuestText: load CEL `data\textbox` width 591; FreeQuestText: release.
  - InitQTextMsg(m): remap Warrior lore SFX to current hero class speech (7 cases); if Speeches[m].scrlltxt: close quest log, wrap translated text at 543 px in GameFont30, split on '\n' into TextLines, set qtextflag=true, qtextSpd=CalculateTextSpeed, ScrollStart=now; always PlaySFX(sfxnr) — even when not scrolling.
  - CalculateTextSpeed: ms/px = sfxFrames / textHeight where textHeight = LineHeight*(numLines+5); with NOSOUND sfxFrames = numLines*3000. Guard: assert non-zero.
  - CalculateTextPosition: y = ((now-ScrollStart)/qtextSpd) − 260; when y >= LineHeight*numLines → qtextflag=false (scroll finished).
  - DrawQTextBack: draw CEL frame 0 at UI-origin + (24,327); half-transparent black rect at +(27,28) size 585x297.
  - DrawQText: back + content clipped to subregion starting at UI y+49, height 260; content: sx = UI x+48, sy = −(y mod LineHeight), skipLines = y / LineHeight, render 8 line slots (i=0..7), skipping empty and out-of-range lines, each in rect 543x38 at sy + i*38, FontSize30|ColorGold.
- 1:1 constraints: LineHeight = 38 (line 40); wrap width 543; NOSOUND estimate 3000 ms per line (line 63); "+5 lines" adjustment so two lines remain when speaker finishes (line 78); y offset −260 (line 77); 8 visible slots (line 109); textbox CEL frame at displacement (24,327); dark rect (27,28,585,297); content subregion y+49 h=260; text origin x+48; SFX remap table: Warrior1→ChamberOfBoneLore, Warrior10→ValorLore, Warrior11→HallsOfTheBlindLore, Warrior12→WarlordOfBloodLore, Warrior54→InSpirituSanctum, Warrior55→PraedictumOtium, Warrior56→EfficioObitusUtInimicus (lines 141–159). Integer division semantics (C truncation) matter for y and skipLines — Go int division matches.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: ScrollStart/clock coupling — scrolling is driven by wall-clock ms since startup, so rendering depends on frame timing; qtextflag mutated inside draw (CalculateTextPosition). All state is mutable file-globals; single-threaded UI assumptions.

### Source/missiles.cpp
- Purpose: Full missile subsystem implementation: the global missile list/tick, collision/damage resolution vs monsters and players, ~50 per-missile-type Add* constructors, ~40 Process* per-tick update functions, and spell damage tables.
- Public API: `std::list<Missile> Missiles` (L73), `bool MissilePreFlag` (L74); `Missile::setAnimation(MissileGraphicID)` (L66); `IsMissileBlockedByTile(Point)` (L857); `DamageRange GetDamageAmt(SpellID,int)` (L872); `Direction16 GetDirection16(Point,Point)` (L986); `MonsterTrapHit(...)` (L1022); `PlayerMHit(...)` (L1060); `InitMissiles()` (L1202); all `Add*(Missile&,AddMissileParameter&)` (L1248–2789); `Missile *AddMissile(src,dst,mdir,mitype,micaster,id,midam,spllvl,parent,lSFX)` (L2793); all `Process*(Missile&)` (L2848–4181); `ProcessManaShield()` (L4189); `ProcessMissiles()` (L4198); `SetUpMissileAnimationData()` (L4236); `RedoMissileFlags()` (L4261); test hook `TestRotateBlockedMissile` (L849-855, BUILD_TESTING).

- Requirements for Go port:
  - Central `Missiles` container preserving insertion order with pointer/ID stability (parent-missile links, iteration during mutation via `AddMissile` inside process loops — Go must use a slice with stable indices or ID indirection, never raw pointers into a reallocating slice).
  - Global flag `MissilePreFlag` recomputed each tick from live missiles.
  - `AddMissile` factory: emplace, fill defaults from `MissileData` (graphic, draw flag, cast sound, addFn), unique-monster tint (`_miUniqTrans = uniqTrans+1` only when `TARGET_PLAYERS` non-trap, L2816), anim frame-group setup (`animFAmt < 8` → group 0, else direction), optional sfx override, dispatch to `addFn`, return nil if `spellFizzled`.
  - Every Add* constructor as its own function/table entry keyed by MissileID, with exact damage/duration/velocity/light init (values below).
  - Every Process* update as table entry; per-tick order: processFn → animation advance (unless `NotAnimated`) → `ProcessManaShield` → delete pass.
  - Collision core `CheckMissileCol` handling monsters (faction rules: trap / opposing minion / berserk attacker or target), players (`TARGET_MONSTERS` friendly-fire via Plr2PlrMHit, monster→player via PlayerMHit, trap/both via PlayerMHit with deathReason by source), Hellfire blocked-missile rotation, tile blocking + breakable objects, hit sound on expiry.
  - `MoveMissile` sub-tile stepping so fast missiles cannot skip tiles (exact algorithm below) with optional "don't move to hit tile" rollback.
  - `lastCollisionTargetHash` dedup so slow missiles hit an entity at most once per tile-occupancy change.
  - Damage/hit-resolution trio `MonsterMHit`, `MonsterTrapHit`, `PlayerMHit`, `Plr2PlrMHit` with to-hit clamps, petrified/gargoyle rules, arrow damage bonuses, resist quartering, knockback, net send only from `MyPlayer`.
  - Spell bookkeeping: `GetDamageAmt` per SpellID for the character screen; `InitMissiles` level-reset semantics (clear Etherealize, Infravision recalc, Rage penalty, clear list + dFlags sweep).
  - Light lifecycle: every missile owning `_mlid` must AddLight/ChangeLight/AddUnLight exactly where the C++ does (visual + gameplay radius).
  - Net commands emitted: CMD_SETREFLECT, CMD_SETSHIELD, CMD_REMSHIELD, CMD_ACTIVATEPORTAL, CMD_REQUESTSPAWNGOLEM, CMD_WARP, CMD_DISARMXY, NetSendCmdDamage.

  - Go `Missile` struct with every field: type, position (offset/velocity/traveled/tile/start/tileForRendering/offsetForRendering), spllvl, delFlag, animType/Flags/Data/Width/Width2/Cnt/Add/Frame, drawFlag, lightFlag, preFlag, uniqTrans(uint32), duration, source, caster, dam, hitFlag, dist, lid, rnd, var1..var7(int), limitReached, lastCollisionTargetHash(int16).

GuardianFrame Start=0/Idle=1/Attack=2; AcidPuddleFrame Idle=0/End=1; FireWallFrame Start=0/Idle=1; PortalFrame/RedPortalFrame Start=0/Idle=1 (L57-83).

- Requirements for Go port:
  - Global ordered slice of active mod identifiers reset on every mod reload.
  - Streaming SHA-256 over 32768-byte chunks with read-error detection (crypto/sha256 + bufio).
  - Hex decode/encode of exactly 64 chars ↔ 32 bytes, case-insensitive on input, lowercase output.
  - INI manifest parser: section `mod`, keys name/description/version/author/homepage/license/saveExtension/programId, repeated `requires` and `compatible` values; invalid `compatible` hex logged and skipped; malformed INI → empty manifest.
  - Whitelist check against a hardcoded (currently empty) approved-hash array.
  - Save-extension rule: default `msv` when any non-whitelisted mod active; explicit extensions (leading dot stripped, `sv` ignored) — last declarer in load order wins.
  - Stable topological sort: repeat passes emitting mods whose present required-mods are all emitted; leftovers (cycles) appended in original order with error log; missing requirements logged.
- 1:1 constraints: buffer size 32768 (L45); `ApprovedModHashes` is empty `std::array<...,0>` (L29) — every hash currently fails whitelist; hex nibble decode accepts `0-9 a-f A-F` (L96-102); `SatisfiesRequiredIdentifier` = own hash equal OR any `compatibleWith` entry equal (L130-135); builtin identifiers get all-zero hash + `whitelisted=true` (L141); `GetActiveModSaveExtension`: first loop sets `"msv"` on first non-whitelisted mod and breaks; second loop picks last non-empty, non-`.sv`-stripped-to-`sv` extension (L164-180); topological emission checks `emittedNames` and `presentNames` sets (L201-215), cycle leftovers appended in index order (L220-224), missing-mod errors logged after (L227-231).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `ActiveModIdentifiers` is a global mutated at mod-load time; returned `string_view` into it is invalidated by reload — Go should return a copied string or guard reload.
- Test coverage: test/mod_identity_test.cpp — 15 TESTs covering hashing vectors, chunked vs one-shot, missing file, whitelist, hex round-trip/reject, manifest fields, SatisfiesRequiredIdentifier, register/clear, save extension last-wins, and 5 ordering cases.
- Go mapping: `internal/mods` package: `Identity.go` (hash/whitelist/manifest), `Order.go` (topo sort); manifest via a small INI lib shared with options parsing.
- Risks/open questions: none — self-contained; only external dependency is a SHA-256 (stdlib in Go).

# vol3-030.md

# Volume III — batch 030

### Source/mpq/mpq_reader.cpp
- Purpose: RAII wrapper over the C `mpqfs` archive API — open/close/clone an MPQ, query file presence/size, hash-based fast lookup, and whole-file decompressing reads. All errors are returned as `std::expected<T, std::string>` where the string folds `errno` into `MPQFS_ERR_IO` messages.
- Public API: class `MpqArchive` (defined in hpp; impl here): `Open(const char*) -> expected<MpqArchive,string>`; `Clone() -> expected<MpqArchive,string>`; move ctor/assign (close previous handle on assign); dtor (`mpqfs_close`); `HasFile(string_view) const`; `GetFileSize(string_view) const`; `FindHash(string_view) const -> uint32_t`; `HasFileHash(uint32_t) const`; `GetFileSizeFromHash(uint32_t) const`; `ReadFile(string_view, size_t &fileSize, int32_t &error) -> unique_ptr<std::byte[]>`; `handle() const`.
- Depends on: external `mpqfs/mpqfs.h` (`mpqfs_open`, `mpqfs_clone`, `mpqfs_close`, `mpqfs_has_file`, `mpqfs_file_size`, `mpqfs_find_hash`, `mpqfs_has_file_hash`, `mpqfs_file_size_from_hash`, `mpqfs_read_file_into`, `mpqfs_error_message`, `mpqfs_error_code`); `utils/str_cat.hpp` (StrCat); `<cerrno>/<cstring>` for errno/strerror.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go `pkg/mpq.Archive` type wrapping the same mpqfs-equivalent core (or a pure-Go MPQ reader): Open, Clone, Close (io.Closer semantics), HasFile, GetFileSize, FindHash, HasFileHash, GetFileSizeFromHash, ReadFile (returns []byte + error).
  - Copy-to-256-byte-NUL-buffer semantics are a C artifact; in Go pass names as strings, but keep the "name longer than 255 fails" rule if the underlying mpqfs port needs it (return not-found/0 instead of error).
  - Move semantics → Go GC + explicit Close; Clone must be independent (own FILE handle) so concurrent readers don't race.
  - `FindHash` returns `0xFFFFFFFF` on overflow/too-long-name (matches `numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max()`), not an error.
  - `ReadFile` two-phase: query size, allocate, read; error int is 0 on success, negative (-1) for bad name, or mpqfs error code otherwise; map to Go error values preserving the codes.
- 1:1 constraints: stack buffer size 256 (`char buf[256]` at lines 88, 96, 104 in HasFile/GetFileSize/FindHash and 119 in ReadFile); `sv.size() >= bufSize` → fail; `FormatMpqfsError`: for `MPQFS_ERR_IO` return `message + ": " + strerror(errno)` (lines 42-45); `FindHash` overflow sentinel = `0xFFFFFFFF` (line 103); `ReadFile` error = −1 for long name, else the mpqfs code cast to int32 (lines 119-121, 131, 141).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: immutable after open except for Clone (const methods thread-safe given mpqfs guarantees); errno read immediately after failing call — in Go capture OS error at the point of failure, not later.
- Test coverage: none found (test/ has no mpq_reader test; writehero_test.cpp touches save writing only).
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/pkg/mpq` — Archive struct with `Open(path) (*Archive, error)`, `Clone()`, embedded `io/fs`-style helpers. Pure-Go MPQ v1/v2/v3 reader replaces mpqfs; keep hash-cache API (`FindHash`) because hot paths (multi.cpp asset lookup) call it per-tick.
- Risks/open questions: mpqfs supports encrypted+PKWARE-compressed sectors; Go port must replicate DecryptBytes/Splode exactly or saves/levels won't match. Whether the Go project vendors mpqfs or writes a Go MPQ decoder decides how much of this becomes real work.

### Source/mpq/mpq_sdl_rwops.cpp
- Purpose: Bridges MPQ files into SDL's stream abstraction (`SDL_RWops`/`SDL_IOStream`) so SDL_image and other SDL consumers can read directly from archives; supports sector-streaming with on-demand decompression and an optional thread-safe mode that clones the archive.
- Public API: `SdlRwopsType *SDL_RWops_FromMpqFile(MpqArchive &archive, uint32_t hashIndex, std::string_view filename, bool threadsafe)` (declared in hpp).
- Depends on: mpqfs stream API (`mpqfs_stream_open_from_hash`, `mpqfs_stream_open`, `mpqfs_stream_read/seek/size/close`, `mpqfs_clone`, `mpqfs_close`, `mpqfs_error_message`); SDL2/SDL3 headers; `utils/sdl_compat.h`; `mpq_reader.hpp` (MpqArchive::handle).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - In Go the SDL RWops bridge is unnecessary; instead implement `io.ReadSeeker` + `Size()` over an MPQ sub-file (sector-decompressing reader). Ebiten-side image loaders accept io.Reader.
  - Keep the two-tier open: try hash first (`hashIndex != 0xFFFFFFFF`), fall back to filename open (needed for encrypted files) — lines 68-75.
  - Thread-safe variant: each stream owns its own archive clone; mirror with per-stream state, Go maps handle concurrency via immutable structures but clone keeps OS file descriptors independent.
  - Seek must support SET/CUR/END; unknown whence = error. Read returns 0-at-EOF distinctly from error. Write is read-only error.
  - All callbacks must clean up stream + owned clone on close exactly once.
- 1:1 constraints: `MaxMpqPathSize = 256` (line 23); filename `>= sizeof(pathBuf)` → nullptr (lines 272-274); `hashIndex != UINT32_MAX` guard (line 69); SDL3 status mapping: `n==0 && size>0` → `SDL_IO_STATUS_EOF`, else READY, error → ERROR (lines 108-117); SDL2 read returns whole objects `n / size` (line 253); SDL1 uses int offsets; RWops type `SDL_RWOPS_UNKNOWN` for SDL2 (line 296).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `threadsafe=true` clones archive because main thread shares one FILE*; this is the core concurrency contract — Go port should give each background-loaded stream its own reader instance.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/pkg/mpq` — `OpenStream(archive, name) (io.ReadSeekCloser, error)` plus `Size()`; feed to Go image decoders and any Ebiten asset loader expecting io.Reader.
- Risks/open questions: SDL_RWops consumers in Go are replaced wholesale; only the streaming semantics (seek-anywhere, incremental decompress) must survive for animated assets (e.g. ogg via SDL_mixer if reused via cgo).

### Source/mpq/mpq_writer.cpp
- Purpose: Creates/edits MPQ archives via mpqfs writer API — creates parent dirs, optionally carries forward all files from an existing archive (via rename-to-.tmp dance), then supports HasFile/Remove/Write/Rename with a fixed 2048-entry hash table.
- Public API: `MpqWriter(const char *path, bool carryForward=true)` (also std::string overload in hpp); move-only; dtor closes (finalize) archive; `HasFile(string_view)`; `RemoveHashEntry(string_view)`; `RemoveHashEntries(bool (*fnGetName)(uint8_t, char*))`; `WriteFile(string_view, const std::byte*, size_t) -> bool`; `RenameFile(string_view, string_view)`.
- Depends on: mpqfs writer API (`mpqfs_writer_create`, `mpqfs_writer_carry_forward_all`, `mpqfs_writer_close`, `mpqfs_writer_discard`, `mpqfs_writer_has_file`, `mpqfs_writer_remove_file`, `mpqfs_writer_add_file`, `mpqfs_writer_rename_file`); `utils/file_util.h` (RecursivelyCreateDir, FileExists, RemoveFile, RenameFile, Dirname); `utils/log.hpp`; `utils/str_cat.hpp`; `mpq_common.hpp` (MaxMpqPathSize).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Writer with same semantics: create dir tree, optional carry-forward of every file from a pre-existing archive at that path, hash table size 2048.
  - Carry-forward algorithm (lines 31-63): if path exists → compute tmp path by replacing extension (after last `.` that is after last `/` or `\`) with `.tmp`, remove stale tmp, rename old→tmp, open tmp as archive, create new writer at original path, carry forward all, close old, remove tmp. If open of tmp fails (corrupt) proceed without carry-forward. If writer_create fails: close old archive and remove tmp.
  - `WriteFile` must remove any existing entry with that name first (line 165) so last write wins.
  - `RemoveHashEntry`: missing name is not an error (line 149).
  - `RemoveHashEntries(fn)`: iterate `uint8_t i=0` while `fnGetName(i, buf)` returns true, remove each — used to purge e.g. all level files.
  - All names truncated/rejected at 255 bytes (NUL at 256th).
  - Errors: return false + LogError with formatted mpqfs message (with errno for IO).
- 1:1 constraints: `MpqWriterHashTableSize = 2048` (hpp line 19); tmp extension rule "replace extension, 8.3 compliant" (lines 40-45); `WriteFile` remove-then-add (line 165); name length check `name.size() >= sizeof(buf)` i.e. >=256 (lines 122-125 etc.); dtor: null writer → no-op, else close + LogVerbose/LogError (lines 82-92).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: single-threaded use only (one writer per path at a time; save-file flow). Move-assign discards previous writer without flushing (`mpqfs_writer_discard`, line 75) — intentional.
- Test coverage: indirectly via test/writehero_test.cpp (save round-trips); no direct mpq_writer test found.
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/pkg/mpq` — `Writer` struct; `NewWriter(path string, carryForward bool)`; methods HasFile/Remove/RemoveWhere(func(i int) (string, bool))/WriteFile/RenameFile; `Close()` finalizes. Pure-Go MPQ writer or cgo to mpqfs.
- Risks/open questions: byte-identical MPQ output matters only for interop with the original game (share saves between C++ and Go builds) — decide whether Go writes standard MPQ or a simpler container if interop is dropped.

### Source/msg.cpp
- Purpose: The entire network message layer: command serialization/deserialization (NetSendCmd* family), the receive dispatch (`ParseCmd`), the multiplayer level-delta system (Delta* functions — item/object/monster/quest/portal state export, PKWARE-compressed transfer, import), mega-packet buffering during resync, and per-command server-side handlers (On*) that mutate world state.

### Source/multi.cpp
- Purpose: Multiplayer session plumbing: game-data init and seed derivation, high/low priority message buffers, packet send/receive loop with TPkt framing and header validation, player join/leave handling with localized messages and timeouts, turn parsing (upper-bit delta-send handshake), and single/multiplayer NetInit/NetClose lifecycle.
- Public API: `gbSomebodyWonGameKludge`, `sgwPackPlrOffsetTbl[MAX_PLRS]`, `gbActivePlayers`, `gbGameDestroyed`, `gbSelectProvider`, `GameName`, `GamePassword`, `PublicGame`, `gbDeltaSender`, `player_state[MAX_PLRS]`, `IsLoopback`; `SwapGameDataLE(GameData&)`, `DescribeLeaveReason(leaveinfo_t)` (DVL_API_FOR_TEST), `FormatGameSeed(const uint32_t[4])`, `InitGameInfo()`, `NetSendLoPri/NetSendHiPri(playerId,data,size)`, `multi_send_msg_packet(pmask,...)`, `multi_msg_countdown()`, `multi_player_left(pnum,reason)`, `multi_net_ping()`, `multi_handle_delta()`, `ProcessGameMessagePackets()`, `multi_send_zero_packet(pnum,cmd,data,size)`, `NetClose()`, `NetInit(bool)`, `recv_plrinfo(Player&, TCmdPlrInfoHdr&, bool)`.
- Depends on: msg.h (ParseCmd, TPkt, msg_send_drop_pkt, msg_wait_resync, delta_close_portal, DeltaExportData, delta_init); nthread.h (all nthread_* fns); storm/storm_net.hpp (SNetSendMessage/ReceiveMessage/SendTurn/ReceiveTurns/GetTurnsInTransit/GetProviderCaps/RegisterEventHandler/LeaveGame/CreateGame/SetBasePlayer/InitializeProvider, SNPLAYER_OTHERS, PS_* flags, provider/ConnectionNames); tmsg.h; pfile.h (pfile_read_player_from_save, gSaveNumber); pack.h (PackNetPlayer/UnPackNetPlayer, PlayerNetPack); player.h + players/validation.hpp (IsNetPlayerValid, Players, MyPlayer/MyPlayerId/InspectPlayer); plrmsg.h (InitPlrMsg, EventPlrMsg); qol/chatlog.h; sync.h (sync_all_monsters, sync_init); diablo.h (gbRunGame, gbIsMultiplayer, sgGameInitInfo, DungeonSeeds, LevelSeeds, currlevel, setlevel, gnTickDelay, SetRndSeed); engine/random.hpp (ReserveSeedSequence, GenerateSeed, xoshiro128plusplus); monster.h (Monsters, MaxMonsters); game_mode.hpp (GetGameId, GameData); options.h (tickRate, runInTown, theoQuest, cowQuest, friendlyFire, multiplayerFullQuests); gamemenu, menu, DiabloUI (UiSelectProvider/UiSelectGame); engine/demomode.h; utils/endian (Swap16/32LE, LoadBE16/LoadLE16).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go net layer must reproduce: TBuffer{offset, 4096B} for lo/hi priority with CopyPacket (max 0x1000 with +2 slack check) and CopyBufferedPackets (length-prefixed chunks, u8 size prefix, memmove remainder).
  - TPkt framing: wCheck magic (0x6970 "ip" chosen so it differs by endianness), wLen = total packet size LE; validation chain in ProcessGameMessagePackets: size ≥ sizeof(TPktHdr), playerId < Players.size(), wCheck match, wLen == totalPacketSize, untrusted-player filter (only CMD_SEND_PLRINFO/CMD_ACK_PLRINFO allowed until IsNetPlayerValid).
  - SyncPacketHeaderData: update remote player pos/HP/mana/base stats/direction from header, with the >3-tile WalkingDistance resync (FixPlrWalkTags twice, snap tile/future, occupyTile) and future-target pathing via MakePlrPath.
  - Turn system integration: multi_handle_delta() called per game tick — export deltas for flagged players, send/receive turns, share hi-pri buffer every other received tick (shareNextHighPriorityMessage toggle), MonsterSeeds() update.
  - ParseTurn: upper bit 0x80000000 triggers delta-sender handshake (HandleTurnUpperBit); sgdwGameLoops resync = `4 * absTurns * sgbNetUpdateRate`; `sgbSentThisCycle` floor logic with 0x7FFFFFFF clamp to 0xFFFF.
  - MonsterSeeds: `seed = (loops>>8) | (loops<<24)` (rotate), `aiSeed = seed + i` for all MaxMonsters — determinism-critical.
  - Player info chunk reassembly (recv_plrinfo): offset table per player, request/ack protocol, static PlayerNetPack buffer, UnPackNetPlayer validation → drop on failure, join messaging (joined vs already-in via sgbPlayerTurnBitTbl), dead-player rendering path (PM_DEATH, frame = numberOfFrames−2, DeadPlayer flag).
  - Timeouts: CheckPlayerInfoTimeouts drops invalid-but-connected players after 15000ms; BeginTimeout: >20000ms → gbRunGame=false, ≥10000ms → CheckDropPlayer; multi_net_ping() restarts timer.
  - NetInit lifecycle exactly: SetRndSeed(0) → InitGameInfo (seed from ReserveSeedSequence().save) → tables cleared → InitSingle (loopback provider, "local"/"local" game) or InitMulti (UI select loops) → buffers/tmsg/sync/nthread start → msg_wait_resync unless turn bit → post-loop: gnTickDelay = 1000/nTickRate, DungeonSeeds[i] = gameGenerator.next() for NUMLEVELS with LevelSeeds cleared, then DungeonSeeds[0] = GenerateSeed() (explicit town/shop divorce), PublicGame from DvlNet_IsPublicGame, chat-log join messages, seed-format logging for joiners.
  - SetupLocalPositions: nine spawn tiles for MyPlayerId, PM_NEWLVL mode, _pLvlChanging=true.
  - GameData wire layout + SwapGameDataLE (size, programid, 4 seed words) with size self-check `gameData.size == sizeof(GameData)` else app_fatal.
  - HeaderCheckVal is endian-dependent (`LoadBE16("ip")` on LE hosts) — packet rejection cross-endian is intentional; Go on any host must compute equivalently to the peers it talks to.
- 1:1 constraints: HeaderCheckVal lines 106-109; TBuffer 4096/0x1000 (118-123); drop timeout 15000 (206); game-loops rotate formula (228); turn upper bit (251, 258); spawns table (446); leave reasons map to three message formats + LEAVE_ENDING sets gbSomebodyWonGameKludge (289-306); 20000/10000 thresholds (344-348); DescribeLeaveReason strings "normal exit"/"Diablo defeated"/"connection timeout"/`code 0x%08X` (587-598); FormatGameSeed `%08X`×4 concat (601-604); multi_send_zero_packet chunk size = gdwLargestMsgSize − sizeof(TPktHdr) − sizeof(TCmdPlrInfoHdr) (790); NetClose SDL_Delay(2000) only if multiplayer (846-848); gnTickDelay = 1000/nTickRate (897); dungeon seed loop + town override (899-904).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: nearly all globals; SNET event callbacks (HandleEvents) fire from network thread → they only set tables consumed later on main thread. NthreadHandler background thread calls nthread_* under MemCrit; multi send functions called both from main loop and that thread. Go: protect buffers/tables with one mutex mirroring MemCrit, or funnel sends through a channel. MonsterSeeds + DungeonSeeds derivation order is determinism-critical for MP sync.
- Test coverage: test/multi_logging_test.cpp covers DescribeLeaveReason (4 cases). No other multi tests.
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/internal/net` — `session.go` (NetInit/Close, GameData), `buffers.go`, `packet.go` (TPkt framing + validation), `playerinfo.go` (recv_plrinfo), `events.go`. Transport abstracted behind a Go `SNet`-like interface so loopback (single player) and real UDP/TCP providers plug in.
- Risks/open questions: storm_net is a large C++ abstraction (dvlnet backend) — the Go port needs its own provider interface before this file ports cleanly. static PlayerNetPack buffer in recv_plrinfo assumes MAX_PLRS=4; fine in Go as array.

### Source/nthread.cpp
- Purpose: Game-tick timing and turn transport: background thread that drives turn send/receive at the network update rate, countdown state machine for packets/syncs, provider-capacity-derived message sizing, and wall-clock helpers (`nthread_has_500ms_passed`, progress-to-next-tick for animation interpolation).
- Public API: globals `sgbNetUpdateRate`, `gdwMsgLenTbl[MAX_PLRS]`, `gdwTurnsInTransit`, `glpMsgTbl[MAX_PLRS]`, `gdwLargestMsgSize`, `gdwNormalMsgSize`, `ProgressToNextGameTick` (test-exported), `last_tick`; functions `nthread_terminate_game(const char*)`, `nthread_send_and_recv_turn(curTurn, turnDelta) -> uint32_t`, `nthread_recv_turns(bool *pfSendAsync) -> bool`, `nthread_set_turn_upper_bit()`, `nthread_start(bool)`, `nthread_cleanup()`, `nthread_ignore_mutex(bool)`, `nthread_has_500ms_passed(bool *drawGame) -> bool`, `nthread_UpdateProgressToNextGameTick()`.
- Depends on: storm/storm_net.hpp (SNetGetTurnsInTransit, SNetSendTurn, SNetReceiveTurns, SNetGetProviderCaps, _SNETCAPS); multi.h (multi_msg_countdown, player_state, MAX_PLRS, MyPlayerId, Players, gbGameDestroyed); diablo.h (app_fatal, gbRunGame, gnTickDelay, gbIsMultiplayer, gbProcessPlayers, PauseMode); engine/animationinfo.h (baseValueFraction); engine/demomode.h; gmenu.h (gmenu_is_active); utils/sdl_mutex.h / sdl_thread.h; SDL_GetTicks/SDL_Delay.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Tick clock: `last_tick` ms base; has_500ms_passed returns `ticksElapsed >= 0` after the missed-ticks (>10×gnTickDelay) reset logic that is skipped when other players are connected (needed to keep MP tick sync); drawGame hint = elapsed <= gnTickDelay.
  - ProgressToNextGameTick: fraction = (gnTickDelay − (last_tick − now)) × baseValueFraction / gnTickDelay, clamped [0, baseValueFraction]; forced to baseValueFraction when due; not updated when !gbRunGame, paused, single-player-with-menu-active, !gbProcessPlayers, or demo running.
  - Turn countdown machine: per call decrement sgbPacketCountdown; when ≤0 decrement sgbSyncCountdown, reset packet countdown = sgbNetUpdateRate; sync countdown !=0 → still on-time (advance last_tick += gnTickDelay, signal async); ==0 → SNetReceiveTurns for all players; failure resets out-of-sync state (ticsOutOfSync=false, both countdowns=1, return false); success: if was in sync set last_tick=now, sync countdown=4, multi_msg_countdown().
  - nthread_send_and_recv_turn: send `gdwTurnsInTransit` turns per call; each turn = `turn_upper_bit | (curTurn & 0x7FFFFFFF)`; turn_upper_bit cleared after first send; curTurn += turnDelta with 0x7FFFFFFF wrap → &=0xFFFF.
  - nthread_start caps math: turnsInTransit = caps.defaultturnsintransit (min 1); netUpdateRate = 20/defaultturnssec if ≤20 and ≠0 else 1; largestMsgSize = 512 or caps.maxmessagesize if <0x200; normalMsgSize = bytessec×rate/20, ×3, >>2 (i.e. ×0.75), ÷ min(caps.maxplayers, MAX_PLRS), doubled along with rate while <0x80, clamped to largestMsgSize.
  - Background thread (multiplayer only): loop { lock MemCrit; if !should_run break; send_and_recv_turn(0,0); delta = gnTickDelay; if recv_turns() delta = last_tick − now; unlock; if delta>0 Delay(delta); }.
  - cleanup: stop thread, zero sizes, join with the mutex handoff dance (if !sgbThreadIsRunning unlock first) — in Go: cancel context + WaitGroup; nthread_ignore_mutex toggles for UI thread handoff.
  - nthread_terminate_game: app_fatal then gbGameDestroyed=true (unreachable second line in practice).
- 1:1 constraints: turn_upper_bit = 0x80000000 (142); turn mask 0x7FFFFFFF and wrap &=0xFFFF (113-114, 89-90); sync countdown reset 4 (128); caps.size=36 passed to SNetGetProviderCaps (160); 512/0x200 threshold (166-168); normalMsgSize arithmetic 169-176 incl. ×3>>2 and <0x80 doubling loop; missed-ticks threshold ×10 (190) and drawGame comparison (205); ProgressToNextGameTick formula and clamp (228-238); countdown init 1/1 and ticsOutOfSync=true at start (154-156).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: this is the tick authority — every game-logic advance is gated by nthread_has_500ms_passed; the background thread shares MemCrit with main-thread send paths (see msg/multi entries). last_tick is written by both threads. Go port: single ticker goroutine + mutex, or run everything on one goroutine with a timer; keep the missed-tick multiplayer exception or clients desync.
- Test coverage: test/animationinfo_test.cpp includes nthread.h and exercises ProgressToNextGameTick-adjacent interpolation logic (not the thread functions).
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/internal/net/tick.go` (clock + progress) and `turns.go` (countdown machine + transport calls); background thread → goroutine with context cancellation; SDL_GetTicks → time.Now ms monotonic.
- Risks/open questions: SDL ticks are Uint32 (wraps ~49 days) — Go int/monotonic won't wrap; behavior differs only after 49 days uptime, acceptable. Provider caps values come from the Go transport — defaults must be chosen to reproduce single-player loopback pacing.

### Source/nthread.h
- Purpose: Declares game-tick management API and its globals.
- Public API: externs `sgbNetUpdateRate`, `gdwMsgLenTbl[MAX_PLRS]`, `gdwTurnsInTransit`, `glpMsgTbl[MAX_PLRS]`, `gdwLargestMsgSize`, `gdwNormalMsgSize`, `ProgressToNextGameTick` (DVL_API_FOR_TEST), `last_tick`; decls for the nine nthread_* functions (signatures in the .cpp entry; `nthread_recv_turns(bool *pfSendAsync = nullptr)`, `nthread_has_500ms_passed(bool *drawGame = nullptr)`).
- Depends on: player.h (for MAX_PLRS via player.h→multi.h chain), utils/attributes.h (DVL_API_FOR_TEST).
- Requirements for Go port: expose tick clock (LastTick, Has500msPassed, UpdateProgress) and turn machine API; ProgressToNextGameTick must be readable by the render layer for animation interpolation.
- 1:1 constraints: default args nullptr (lines 38, 46); comment documents ProgressToNextGameTick as AnimationInfo::baseValueFraction fraction.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: declared globals documented in .cpp entry.
- Test coverage: test/animationinfo_test.cpp includes it.
- Go mapping: `devilutionGo/internal/net/nthread.go` — package-level clock struct.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/pack.cpp
- Purpose: Serializes/deserializes players and items between runtime structs and on-disk/network packed formats, with extensive validation of remote (network) data.
- Public API: `bool RecreateHellfireSpellBook(const Player&, const TItem&, Item*)`, `void PackItem(ItemPack&, const Item&, bool isHellfire)`, `void PackPlayer(PlayerPack&, const Player&)`, `void PackNetItem(const Item&, ItemNetPack&)`, `void PackNetPlayer(PlayerNetPack&, const Player&)`, `void UnPackItem(const ItemPack&, const Player&, Item&, bool)`, `void UnPackPlayer(const PlayerPack&, Player&)`, `bool UnPackNetItem(const Player&, const ItemNetPack&, Item&)`, `bool UnPackNetPlayer(const PlayerNetPack&, Player&)`.
- Depends on: `RecreateItem/RecreateEar/ClampDurability/RemapItemIdxToDiablo/FromDiablo/ToSpawn/FromSpawn/IsItemAvailable` (items.h, items/validation.h); `GetSpellBookLevel` (spelldat); `AdvanceRndSeed` (engine/random.hpp); `InitPlayer/CalcPlrInv/CalculateGold/CalcStatDiff` (player.cpp/inv.cpp); `PlayerNameLength/NUMLEVELS/GetNumPlayerClasses/InventoryGridCells/MaxBeltItems/NUM_INVLOC/MaxSpellLevel` (player.h/inv.h); `IsCreationFlagComboValid/IsTownItemValid/IsUniqueMonsterItemValid/IsDungeonItemValid` (items/validation.h); `EventPlrMsg` (plrmsg.h); endian helpers `Swap16LE/Swap32LE/Swap64LE/LoadBE32/SwapSigned32LE`; `gbIsHellfire/gbIsSpawn/gbVanilla` (diablo.h / game_mode.hpp); `InDungeonBounds` (gendung); `GetInventorySize/GetItemLocation` (inv.h); item constants `CF_LEVEL/CF_TOWN/CF_USEFUL/CF_UPER15/CF_HELLFIRE`, `ICURS_EAR_SORCERER`, `IMISC_*`, `IDI_EAR/IDI_GOLD`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Little-endian byte-exact serialization for all packed fields (Swap*LE on big-endian hosts — in Go just binary.LittleEndian).
  - Ear items: the 16-char hero name is smeared across iCreateInfo/iSeed/bId/bDur/bMDur/bCh/bMCh/wValue/dwBuff with 7-bit chars and specific shifts; PackItem writes `iCreateInfo = iName[1] | (iName[0]<<8)`, `iSeed = LoadBE32(&iName[2])` (note big-endian load then LE store), `wValue = ivalue | (iName[11]<<8) | ((curs - ICURS_EAR_SORCERER)<<6)`, `dwBuff = LoadBE32(&iName[12])`; unpack mirrors with &0x7F.
  - Durability clamps: pack `bMDur = min(_iMaxDur,254)`, `bDur = min(_iDurability,bMDur)`; unpack `ClampDurability`.
  - Charges clamp to max; identified bit = bId&1; magical bit bId bit1.
  - PlayerPack: 37 spell levels in pSplLvl + 10 in pSplLvl2 (Hellfire spells 37-46); unpack zeroes levels for non-learnable spells and forces Apocalypse/Nova to 0 when !gbIsHellfire; experience/gold/HP/mana fields as int32 LE; pMemSpells uint64 LE; only learnable spells read.
  - UnPackPlayer stat clamping: base stats `min(packed, class max)`; `_pHPBase & 0xFFFFFFC0 < 64 → 64` (min 64 HP base); level clamp via setCharacterLevel; class clamp 0..numClasses-1; level clamp 0..NUMLEVELS; `VerifyGoldSeeds` dedupes duplicate gold seeds by AdvanceRndSeed.
  - Pack direction: InvBody NUM_INVLOC, InvList only `_pNumInv` entries, InvGrid InventoryGridCells raw, SpdList MaxBeltItems; wReflections u16; pDamAcFlags u32; bIsHellfire byte; vanilla adds targx/targy.
  - Net packing: full derived-stat block (pStrength..pILMaxDam, 22 int32 fields) packed for cross-checking playerdat consistency; unpack recomputes CalcPlrInv and validates every derived stat equals the packed value; belt items validated 1x1, non-gold, usable; equipment location validated per slot (helm/ring/amulet/hands/chest); HP/mana sanity `baseHp >= baseHpMax - hpMax && baseHp <= baseHpMax`; `pMaxHPBase <= calculateBaseLife()`, `pMaxManaBase <= calculateBaseMana()`.
  - Validation failure path: LogDebug + EventPlrMsg "Player '<name>' sent invalid player data during attempt to join the game." + return false.
  - RecreateHellfireSpellBook: recreate; check `(iCreateInfo & CF_LEVEL) == (GetSpellBookLevel(spell)+1)*2` for legitimacy, else validate as dungeon item.
  - Gold: `wValue = Swap16LE(_ivalue)` on pack; unpack passes wValue into RecreateItem.
  - `UnPackNetItem` treats negative/oversize idx as empty(true); ear recreated from ear struct; town/unique/dungeon validation branching on CF bits; `dwBuff & CF_HELLFIRE` + book → RecreateHellfireSpellBook.
- 1:1 constraints: `#define MAX_SPELLS 52` (pack.h:14); split `pSplLvl[37]` + `pSplLvl2[10]` (l.150-155); HP floor 64: `if ((int)(player._pHPBase & 0xFFFFFFC0) < 64) player._pHPBase = 64` (l.364-365); mana base clamp `min(pManaBase, pMaxManaBase)` (l.372); bMDur 254 cap (l.125-128); ear shifts as above (l.111-121, 291-320); `VerifyGoldSeeds` restart scan `j=-1` after reseed (l.70-85); PlayerPack written with `memset 0` first — all reserved fields zero on save.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `VerifyGoldSeeds` consumes global RNG (AdvanceRndSeed) during unpack — affects subsequent seed state; singleplayer save/load determinism depends on it. No threads.
- Test coverage: test/pack_test.cpp (1459 lines — pack/unpack roundtrips), test/writehero_test.cpp.
- Go mapping: pkg/save + internal/net: Go structs with fixed-order binary encoding via encoding/binary manual writes (no reflection) to guarantee byte layout; validation as separate pure functions returning error lists.
- Risks/open questions: PlayerPack is on-disk save format — byte-compat with original .sv files is a hard requirement; ItemNetPack is a union (def/item/ear overlay) — in Go model as struct with reinterpretation or three views. `packedItem.dwBuff` for net item read via `Swap16LE` on a uint32 field (l.480) — quirk to verify against network peers (likely benign since validation only checks CF_HELLFIRE bit of low 16 bits... actually reads garbage high bits; preserve behavior).

  - Labels drawn twice (black shadow at +2,+2 then white) with right-alignment offset `-labelLength - (IsSmallFontTall() ? 2 : 3)`.

- Purpose: Debug-only (_DEBUG) Lua console: toggled by backtick/grave, full-screen overlay with input line, scrollable output history, input/output history navigation, and Lua autocomplete popup.
- Public API: `void InitConsole()`, `bool IsConsoleOpen()`, `void OpenConsole()`, `bool ConsoleHandleEvent(const SDL_Event &)`, `void DrawConsole(const Surface &)`, `void RunInConsole(std::string_view)`, `void PrintToConsole(std::string_view)`, `void PrintWarningToConsole(std::string_view)`.
- Depends on: Lua REPL `RunLuaReplLine/GetLuaReplEnvironment` (lua/repl.hpp), autocomplete `GetLuaAutocompleteSuggestions/LuaAutocompleteSuggestion` (lua/autocomplete.hpp); `TextInputState/TextInputCursorState/HandleTextInputEvent` (DiabloUI/text_input.hpp); asset `lua\repl_prelude.lua` via `LoadAsset` (engine/assets.hpp); SDL events/keyboard/rect; rendering `DrawString/WordWrapString/GetLineWidth/GetFontSizeFromUiFlags/UiFlags` colors (Dialog White/Yellow/Red, FontSizeDialog); `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo/DrawHorizontalLine/FillRect`; `PAL8_YELLOW/PAL16_BLUE+14/+8` palette indices; `GetMainPanel` (panels/ui_panels.hpp); `SDLC_StopTextInput/SDLC_StartTextInput/SDL_SetTextInputArea/ghMainWnd/BltFast` (engine/dx.h, utils/sdl_compat.h); `Utf8CodePoints/DecodeFirstUtf8CodePoint/IsBreakableWhitespace` (utils/utf8.hpp); `SplitByChar/StrCat/c_count`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Whole file is behind `#ifdef _DEBUG` — port only if a debug console is wanted; depends on embedding a Lua interpreter (gopher-lua or similar) with a REPL environment and autocomplete.
  - Console state machine: input buffer 4096, cursor/selection via TextInputState; input text state (UpToDate/Edited/RestoredFromHistory) drives rewrap + autocomplete refresh; suggestions max 12.
  - Output model: vector of ConsoleLine {Help/Input/Output/Warning/Error, text, wrapped, numLines}; lazy wrap on render; total height accumulates; scroll offset clamped to `[0, totalHeight - innerHeight]`; PageUp/Down scroll by inner-height pages; wheel scroll by `ScrollStep = 3*LineHeight = 60`.
  - History: HistoryIndex from end; Up/Down over input lines (Shift = output lines); DraftInput saved on first navigation and restored at index -1; filter skips duplicates of current input.
  - Autocomplete: popup above cursor position, blue box `PAL16_BLUE+14` fill, focused row `PAL16_BLUE+8`, clamped to screen; Tab/Enter accept; `cursorAdjust == -1` moves cursor left one after insert.
  - Prompt "> " rendered as part of wrapped input; cursor-position mapping across wrapped lines handles newline-replaced whitespace (numRendered accounting incl. prompt).
  - Keys: grave opens (any layout), Esc closes (or clears suggestions), Ctrl+L clears, Shift+Enter newline, Return executes via RunLuaReplLine, empty error → "Unknown error".
  - DrawConsole sizes: OuterRect = full width, height = screen height - main panel height - 2; input rect at bottom with numLines*20+4 height; separator line PAL8_YELLOW at input top-1; final `BltFast` blit of console region.
  - InitConsole loads repl prelude once and runs it; first render sets SDL text-input area and starts text input.
- 1:1 constraints: `Prompt = "> "`; HelpText string verbatim (l.76-82); buffer 4096 (l.86); `MaxSuggestions = 12` (l.97); `LineHeight = 20`, `TextPaddingYTop = 0`, `TextPaddingYBottom = 4`, `TextPaddingX = 4`, `BorderColor = PAL8_YELLOW` (l.132-137); `ScrollStep = LineHeight * 3` (l.158); text colors per line type (Input/Output DialogWhite, Warning DialogYellow, Error DialogRed, focused suggestion DialogYellow) (l.139-146); console height `out.h() - GetMainPanel().size.height - 2` (l.613-616).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: file-scope mutable statics (ConsoleLines, scroll, history, suggestions); all called from main loop; ConsolePrelude cached optional<expected> — load failure becomes an Error console line at init. PrintToConsole callable from Lua at arbitrary points.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: internal/debug/console (build-tag gated, e.g. `//go:build debug`), backed by an internal/lua package; only port if Lua modding/debug is in scope.
- Risks/open questions: requires Lua runtime decision for the Go port; if mods (options.cpp DiscoverMods, lua/mods paths) are kept, the REPL/prelude assets must be ported too.

# vol3-032.md

# Volume III — batch 032

### Source/panels/mainpanel.cpp
- Purpose: Loads and prerenders the main control panel's button sprites (pressed states + localized button captions) into CLX lists at startup, for both the bottom panel and the (multiplayer chat) talk buttons.
- Public API: `std::expected<void,std::string> LoadMainPanel()`, `void FreeMainPanel()`; globals `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList PanelButtonDown`, `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList TalkButton` (declared in hpp).
- Depends on: `BottomBuffer` and `GetMainPanel()`/`MainPanelButtonRect` from control/control.hpp; `LoadClxWithStatus`/`LoadOptionalClx`/`LoadClx` (engine/load_clx.hpp), `LoadClxWithStatus` for CEL (not used here); `RenderClxSprite`/`ClxSpriteList` iteration (engine/render/clx_render.hpp, engine/clx_sprite.hpp); `DrawString`/`GetLineWidth`/`GameFont12`/`UiFlags::Color*` (engine/render/text_render.hpp); `IsChatAvailable()` (control); `GetMainPanel().size.height` via control.hpp; `SurfaceToClx` (utils/surface_to_clx.hpp); `_(...)` translations (utils/language.h); `Surface::subregion` (engine).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Load `data\panel8bucp.clx` (6 button backgrounds), stack all frames vertically into one surface (width = frame width, height = sum of frame heights), then overlay grime and caption text per button, producing a 6-sprite CLX-equivalent list exposed as `PanelButtonDown`.
  - Also load `data\panel8buc.clx` (unpressed button art), `data\dirtybuc.clx` (unpressed grime), `data\dirtybucp.clx` (pressed grime) as intermediates; they are freed at the end of LoadMainPanel (lines 150-153).
  - Buttons, in order (lines 87-92): 0=`char`(frame 0), 1=`quests`(frame 1), 2=`map`(frame 1), 3=`menu`(frame 0), 4=`inv`(frame 1), 5=`spells`(frame 0).
  - Each button caption is drawn twice: black shadow at +1px y then the styled color (lines 24-29), centered, with spacing computed by: try spacing 2, measure with `GetLineWidth(text, GameFont12, spacing)`, clamp to sprite width; if >38 retry with spacing 1 (lines 35-39 and 66-71).
  - For multiplayer (`IsChatAvailable()`), draw three "voice" unpressed buttons directly into `BottomBuffer` at x=176, y = mainPanel.y + 101 + 18*i, i=0..2 (lines 100-107), with grime clipped to a 9px-high subregion at y+6 and centered text.
  - Build `TalkButton`: 3-sprite surface (background frame 0 unpressed-mute, frame 1 pressed-mute, frame 1 pressed-voice; lines 117-121), then grime+text overlays: "mute" unpressed at {0,0}, "mute" pressed at {0,17}, "voice" pressed at {0,33}, grime rects at y 6/23/39 with 9px height, widths = `GetLineWidth(_("mute"), GameFont12, 2)` (lines 124-131).
  - `FreeMainPanel()` resets `TalkButton` and `PanelButtonDown` to nullopt (lines 156-160).
  - `RenderMainButton` also duplicates each caption onto the panel image in `BottomBuffer` at panelPosition + (0, mainPanelHeight+16) when chat is available (lines 62-63).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `NumButtonSprites = 6` (line 73); `NumOtherPlayers = 3` (line 97); `NumTalkButtonSprites = 3` (line 119).
  - Caption fitting threshold: `width > 38` → drop spacing from 2 to 1 (lines 35-38, 66-70).
  - Button-on-panel offsets: caption at position+(0,+1) shadow; text placement rect y+7 grime (line 41); pressed-caption y+9 grime and text at +2 y (lines 72-73).
  - Panel button position = `MainPanelButtonRect[buttonId].position + {4,17}` (line 59); second copy at +{0, mainPanelHeight+16} (line 62).
  - Voice buttons: `{176, mainPanelY + 101 + 18*i}` (line 103); grime subregion `(talkButtonWidth - width)/2` x, +6 y, height 9 (line 105).
  - Talk sprite y positions: 0, talkButtonHeight, talkButtonHeight*2 (lines 118-120); grime y 6/23/39 (lines 125-129); text y 0/17/33.
  - Colors: `UiFlags::ColorButtonface` for unpressed, `UiFlags::ColorButtonpushed` for pressed, `ColorBlack` shadow.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: No RNG. Mutates module-static `PanelButton`, `PanelButtonGrime`, `PanelButtonGrime` (down) during load only. `PanelButtonDown`/`TalkButton` are globals consumed by control panel rendering; init order matters only vs asset loader. Rendering into `BottomBuffer` is a one-time load side effect — in Go, do the same at load time, single-threaded.
- Test coverage: none found (no test file references mainpanel).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/panels` (or `internal/control`) — a `mainpanel.go` with `LoadMainPanel(ctx) error`, `FreeMainPanel()`, exported `PanelButtonDown`, `TalkButton` sprite-list handles; needs the CLX/CEL loader (`pkg/mpq` + sprite decode) and a text renderer with kerning-fit spacing.
- Risks/open questions: The double-draw into `BottomBuffer` for chat mode assumes `BottomBuffer` already sized/allocated; Go port must guarantee bottom-buffer creation before `LoadMainPanel`. `GetLineWidth(text.data())` in spell_list uses C-string truncation; not here.
