### Source/panels/partypanel.cpp
- Purpose: Builds and draws the side party panel (multiplayer): per-player portrait frame with health/mana bars, class-specific portrait sprite offsets, player tags, dead overlay, name, and right-click-to-inspect handling.
- Public API: `bool PartySidePanelOpen` (true), `bool InspectingFromPartyPanel`, `int PortraitIdUnderCursor` (-1); `std::expected<void,std::string> LoadPartyPanel()`, `void FreePartyPanel()`, `void DrawPartyMemberInfoPanel(const Surface&)`, `bool DidRightClickPartyPortrait()`.
- Depends on: `AutomapActive` (automap.h); `BottomBuffer`-independent — uses `gnViewportHeight`, `RedrawEverything`, `MainPanelButtonRect` not needed; `GetMainPanel()` (control/control.hpp); CLX/CEL loaders (`LoadCelWithStatus("data\\textslid", 12)`, `LoadClxWithStatus("data\\monstertags.clx")`); `SurfaceToClx`; `RenderClxSprite`, `FillRect`, `DrawVerticalLine`, `DrawHalfTransparentRectTo`; palette constants; `Players`, `MyPlayer`, `InspectPlayer`, `Player::getId/isOnLevel/_pHitPoints/_pMaxHP/_pMana/_pMaxMana/_pClass/pManaShield/_pName/plractive/friendlyMode`; `IsPlayerUnarmed`, `GetPlayerPortraitSprite` (player/tables); `OpenCharPanel`, `invflag`, `SpellbookFlag`, `CharFlag` (control/inv); `IsPlayerInStore` (stores.h), `IsStashOpen` (qol/stash.h); `GetOptions().Graphics.showFPS`; `MAX_PLRS`; `DrawString`/`GetLineWidth`/`UiFlags::ColorGold|Outlined|FontSize12`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Load `data\textslid` CEL with frame size 12x12 and `data\monstertags.clx`; compose a single frame surface 48x62 (frame 48x48 + 7px HP bar + 7px mana bar) and convert to CLX as `PartyMemberFrame` (lines 105-118): gray (PAL16_GRAY+10) HP/mana background bars at y=0 and y=HealthBar+48, member frame drawn at y=7.
  - `DrawMemberFrame` fills background PAL16_BLUE+14 then draws 4x4 grid of 12px border sprites with index mapping: 0=TL,1=BL,2=BR,3=TR,4=top,5=left,6=bottom,7=right; interior skipped (lines 50-79).
  - `DrawPartyMemberInfoPanel` early-outs (and clears hover id) when `CharFlag || !gbIsMultiplayer || !MyPlayer->friendlyMode || IsPlayerInStore() || IsStashOpen` (lines 124-129).
  - Panel position starts {8,8}, shifted +60 (FrameGap*4) if automap active, +15 if showFPS (lines 133-136).
  - Per player (skip inactive, non-friendly, and self unless `_DEBUG`): draw frame sprite; HP bar ticks = `((_pHitPoints * 48) + (_pMaxHP/2)) / _pMaxHP` with color PAL8_YELLOW+5 if mana shield else PAL8_RED+4, height 7 (lines 160-166); portrait = `GetPlayerPortraitSprite(player)` with class offset: in-town vs in-dungeon vs isDead (dead only if HP<=0 and unarmed) (lines 171-176); portrait pos x = `(-(w/2) + 24) + offset.x`, y = offset.y (line 178); frame subregion inset by 3px border on each side used for portrait + tag + dead overlay; tag sprite = `PlayerTags[playerId+1]` (if exists) at x = `48 - (tagWidth + tagWidth/2)`, y=0 (lines 187-194); dead overlay: half-transparent red rect (PAL8_RED+4) over full frame subregion (lines 197-204); mana ticks = `((_pMana * 48) + (_pMaxMana/2)) / _pMaxMana`, color PAL8_BLUE+3 (lines 209-212); name drawn gold/outlined/12px at pos (lines 217-221); y advances 7→48→7→(FrameGap+5 = 20) (lines 168, 205, 213, 222); column wrap when `pos.y >= mainPanel.y - 48 - 10`: reset y to panel start (with same automap/FPS offsets) and x += longest name width + 7 (FrameGap/2) (lines 238-247).
  - Hover tracking sets `PortraitIdUnderCursor`; cleared if no portrait under cursor at end (lines 229-232, 250-251).
  - `RightClickedPortraitIndex` handled after loop: `HandleRightClickPortait` sets `InspectPlayer`, opens char panel, opens inventory if spellbook closed, `RedrawEverything()`, resets index — only if player active and not self (lines 82-90).

### Source/panels/quest_log.cpp
- Purpose: Quest log side panel: collects active+finished quests, sorts by questBookOrder, lays them out in the panel with computed spacing, handles mouse selection, keyboard up/down/enter/ESC, and draws entries with spinning-pentagram markers.
- Public API: `bool QuestLogIsOpen`, `OptionalOwnedClxSpriteList pQLogCel`; `void DrawQuestLog(const Surface&)`, `void StartQuestlog()`, `void QuestlogUp()`, `void QuestlogDown()`, `void QuestlogEnter()`, `void QuestlogESC()`.
- Depends on: `Quests`/`QuestsData`/`quest_id`/`MAXQUESTS`/`QUEST_ACTIVE|QUEST_DONE|QUEST_HIVE_DONE`/`InitQTextMsg` (quests.h); `pSPentSpn2Cels` + `PentSpn2Spin()` (minitext.h — animated spinner, tick-coupled); `PlaySFX`/`SfxID::MenuMove|MenuSelect` (effects.h); `GetLeftPanel()`, `GetPanelPosition(UiPanels::Quest, ...)`, `MousePosition`, `RedrawEverything` not used here (control.hpp / panels/ui_panels.hpp); `ClxDraw`, `DrawString`, `GetLineWidth`, `UiFlags::ColorWhitegold|ColorWhite`; `_(...)` translation of quest names.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `StartQuestlog()`: gather active quests (`_qactive == QUEST_ACTIVE && _qlog`) in Quests array order into `EncounteredQuests`, then finished (`QUEST_DONE` or `QUEST_HIVE_DONE`) after them; sort each block by `QuestsData[q].questBookOrder`; compute layout (see constraints); set `SelectedQuest = FirstFinishedQuest == 0 ? -1 : 0`; set `QuestLogIsOpen = true` (lines 82-128).
  - `DrawQuestLog(out)`: hover-hit-test first (updates SelectedQuest), draw `pQLogCel[0]` at panel position {0,351}; for each entry, if `i == FirstFinishedQuest` add `FinishedQuestOffset` extra, print centered name (marked with spinner icons both sides if selected; finished entries disabled/whitegold), advance `LineSpacing` (lines 63-78).
  - `QuestLogMouseToEntry()`: only selectable (active) entries hit-test; inner panel offset by left panel position; y ranges `[ListYOffset + i*LineSpacing, +LineHeight)` (lines 48-60).
  - `PrintQLString`: x centered via `max((257 - width)/2, 0)`; markers at `x-20` and `x+width+7`, both at `y+13`, frame `PentSpn2Spin()` (lines 62-74).
  - `QuestlogUp/Down`: navigate only among active entries (0..FirstFinishedQuest-1) with wraparound and `MenuMove` SFX; when no active quests sets SelectedQuest=-1 (lines 130-148).
  - `QuestlogEnter`: play `MenuSelect`, if a valid active selection `InitQTextMsg(Quests[EncounteredQuests[SelectedQuest]]._qmsg)`, close log (lines 150-157).
  - `QuestlogESC`: if mouse currently over an entry, behave as Enter (lines 159-165).
  - Note: `pQLogCel` is loaded elsewhere (not in this file); only consumed here.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `InnerPanel = {{32,26},{280,300}}` (line 39); `LineHeight = 12`, `MaxSpacing = 24` (40-41).
  - Layout math (lines 105-124): `twoBlocks = FirstFinishedQuest != 0 && FirstFinishedQuest < EncounteredQuestCount`; initial `FinishedQuestOffset = twoBlocks ? 6 : 0` (LineHeight/2); `overallMinHeight = count*12 + FinishedQuestOffset`; `space = 300`; if count>0: `addLineSpacing = min(12, (space - overallMinHeight)/count)`; `LineSpacing = 12 + addLineSpacing`; if twoBlocks: `additionalSepSpace = min(12, additionalSpace - addLineSpacing*count)`, `FinishedQuestOffset = max(4, additionalSepSpace)`; `overallHeight = count*LineSpacing + FinishedQuestOffset`; `ListYOffset = (space - overallHeight)/2`.
  - Text centering base width 257; marker offsets -20/+7/+13; panel draw at {0,351} (lines 66, 69-74).
  - Sort comparator: strict `questBookOrder` less-than within each block (lines 84-86, 101-102).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `PentSpn2Spin()` is animation-tick dependent (marker frame advances per game tick) — in Go, drive from the same tick counter as other spinners. Statics `EncounteredQuests/Count/FirstFinishedQuest/SelectedQuest/ListYOffset/LineSpacing/FinishedQuestOffset` are module state rebuilt on `StartQuestlog`. No RNG.
- Test coverage: `test/panel_state_test.cpp` exercises `StartQuestlog()` and quest-log open/close behavior around lines 77, 113-138.
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/panels/questlog.go`; state struct with the six layout fields; quests data table with `questBookOrder`; SFX and text-message hooks.
- Risks/open questions: `std::sort` is not stable — ties in questBookOrder could reorder equal-order quests; Go should use the same non-stable sort semantics (sort.Slice) to match, or verify no ties exist.

### Source/panels/spell_icons.cpp
- Purpose: Loads large (56x56) and small (37x38) spell icon sprite sets, maps SpellID → icon frame, draws icons with a 256-entry palette translation table (per SpellType recolor), and draws 2px selection borders.
- Public API: `LoadLargeSpellIcons()/FreeLargeSpellIcons()/LoadSmallSpellIcons()/FreeSmallSpellIcons()` (expected<void,string> for loads), `uint8_t GetSpellIconFrame(SpellID)`, `DrawLargeSpellIcon(out, pos, spell)`, `DrawSmallSpellIcon(out, pos, spell)`, `DrawLargeSpellIconBorder(out, pos, color)`, `DrawSmallSpellIconBorder(out, pos)`, `SetSpellTrans(SpellType)`.
- Depends on: `LoadOptionalClx`/`LoadClxWithStatus`/`LoadOptionalCel`/`LoadCelWithStatus` (load_cel/load_clx); palette constants PAL8_*/PAL16_* (engine/palette.h); `ClxDrawTRN`, `UnsafeDrawBorder2px` (render); `SPLICONLENGTH` (own header); `UNPACKED_MPQS` build define switching between split fg/bg CLX and single CEL assets (`data\spelicon_fg.clx`/`data\spelicon_bg.clx` vs `data\spelicon`; `data\spelli2_fg.clx`/`data\spelli2_bg.clx` vs `data\spelli2`); fallback paths under `ctrlpan\` for the packed variant.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two sprite sets with load/free; packed (CEL) path is the default: large from `data\spelicon` frame width 56, small from `data\spelli2` frame width 37; unpacked path uses fg+bg CLX pairs with `ctrlpan\` fallback (lines 100-133).
  - `SpellITbl` — full SpellID→SpellIcon frame mapping (52 entries, lines 52-104): copy verbatim, including aliases (Guardian→DoomSerpents, Rage→BloodBoil, Mana/Magi→Mana, all runes→PentaStar, Null→Empty) and note `SpellIcon::Sentinel/BloodRitual/Invisibility/RedSkull/Pentagram/FireCloud/LongHorn` unused.
  - `GetSpellIconFrame(spell)` = `SpellITbl[int8(spell)]` (line 135-138).
  - `DrawLarge/SmallSpellIcon`: if unpacked, draw background frame 0 first, then icon frame via TRN `SplTransTbl`; packed just draws the frame with TRN (lines 153-165).
  - Borders: 2px inset border around rect `{x, y-height+1, width, height}` of sprite 0; large takes explicit color, small uses `SplTransTbl[PAL8_YELLOW+2]` (lines 167-178).
  - `SetSpellTrans(t)` builds the 256-byte TRN: identity for 0..127 only when Skill; always identity 128..255; entry 255→0; then per-type remaps (exact values in constraints) (lines 180-229).
  - `LoadLargeSpellIcons` leaves trans set to `SetSpellTrans(SpellType::Skill)` as final side effect (line 112).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `SPLICONLENGTH = 56` (header line 14).
  - TRN construction exact values: Skill: 0..127 identity, 128..255 identity, [255]=0. Spell: `SplTransTbl[PAL8_YELLOW]=PAL16_BLUE+1 (177)`, `+1=179`, `+2=181`; loop `i in [PAL16_BLUE..+16)`: `[PAL16_BEIGE-PAL16_BLUE+i]=i`, `[PAL16_YELLOW-PAL16_BLUE+i]=i`, `[PAL16_ORANGE-PAL16_BLUE+i]=i`. Scroll: yellow→`PAL16_BEIGE+{1,3,5}`; loop over BEIGE block maps YELLOW/ORANGE. Charges: yellow→`PAL16_ORANGE+{1,3,5}`; loop maps BEIGE/YELLOW. Invalid: yellow→`PAL16_GRAY+{1,3,5}`; loop `i in [PAL16_GRAY..+15)` maps BEIGE/YELLOW/ORANGE, then `[PAL16_BEIGE+15]=[PAL16_YELLOW+15]=[PAL16_ORANGE+15]=0`. Palette bases: PAL8_YELLOW=144, PAL16_BEIGE=160, PAL16_BLUE=176, PAL16_YELLOW=192, PAL16_ORANGE=208, PAL16_GRAY=240 (palette.h lines 31-40).
  - Note for Spell/Scroll/Charges/Invalid: indices 0..127 are NOT reset (only when t==Skill is the identity loop over 0..127 run) — stale values persist across calls; replicate by keeping the persistent table and only writing the specified entries.
  - Border rect anchored at `y - height + 1` (bottom-left position convention).
  - Small icon width 37 (load line 127); large 56.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `SplTransTbl` is a module-global mutable 256-byte TRN shared by all icon draws; `SetSpellTrans` must be called before each draw batch (callers do). Partial-reset semantics (0..127 only on Skill) make the table stateful across type switches — Go must keep one persistent table to be byte-identical.
- Test coverage: none found (spell_icons not referenced in test/).
- Go mapping: `internal/ui/panels/spellicons.go` (or `internal/render/spellicons`); TRN as [256]byte; keep SetSpellTrans/DRAW functions; asset loader must support both CEL and CLX forms or just packed CEL if MPQ handling guarantees it.
- Risks/open questions: The partial identity-reset is subtle: after Scroll→Skill, upper entries from Scroll remain — this is faithful vanilla behavior; port must not "fix" it. `static_cast<int8_t>(spell)` sign behavior for SpellID values >127 is irrelevant given enum size.

- Risks/open questions: SDL_FITHEIGHT/SDL_FITWIDTH are 3DS-SDL-specific (not SDL2 standard) — the Go port must define its own equivalent scale-fit semantics; exact on-screen scaling math lives in the 3DS SDL port, not here.

### Source/platform/ctr/keyboard.cpp
- Purpose: Deferred 3DS software-keyboard (swkbd) input: game code queues text-input requests via `ctr_vkbdInput`, and `ctr_vkbdFlush` (called once per UI frame from DiabloUI) opens the system keyboard sequentially for each queued event and delivers confirmed text via callback.
- Public API: `ctr_vkbdInput(std::string_view hintText, std::string_view inText, void (*textInputFn)(std::string_view))` (keyboard.h lines 12-16, defined cpp lines 18-26); `ctr_vkbdFlush()` (keyboard.h line 20, defined cpp lines 28-53). Internal: `constexpr size_t MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 255` (line 7); `struct vkbdEvent { hintText, inText, textInputFn }` (lines 9-13); static `events[16]`, static `eventCount` (lines 15-16).
- Depends on: 3DS swkbd API via `<3ds.h>` (keyboard.h line 5): `SwkbdState`, `swkbdInit`, `swkbdSetValidation`, `swkbdSetInitialText`, `swkbdSetHintText`, `swkbdInputText`, `SWKBD_TYPE_WESTERN`, `SWKBD_NOTEMPTY_NOTBLANK`, `SwkbdButton`, `SWKBD_BUTTON_CONFIRM`; `devilution::CopyUtf8` from `Source/utils/utf8.hpp:94` (cpp line 5, used line 42); callers: `Source/DiabloUI/diabloui.cpp:226` (queue) and `:868` (flush) — verified by grep.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Queue semantics: up to 16 pending events; `ctr_vkbdInput` silently drops (returns without queuing) when the queue is full (`eventCount >= sizeof(events)` — note: byte-size 16*sizeof(vkbdEvent) vs int count comparison, effectively never trips; Go port should compare against 16 properly).
  - Flush processes events FIFO in queue order, one system-keyboard session per event, then resets `eventCount = 0` even if some events were dropped or cancelled.
  - Keyboard config: WESTERN type, 2 buttons (Confirm/Cancel), max length 255, validation NOTEMPTY_NOTBLANK with 0/0 filters.
  - Initial text is passed as a null-terminated copy alive until input completes; hint text is copied immediately into a 256-byte buffer (`MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + 1`) via CopyUtf8; the same buffer is zeroed (`memset`) and reused as the output buffer for `swkbdInputText`.
  - Callback fires ONLY on SWKBD_BUTTON_CONFIRM with the NUL-terminated buffer contents; cancel/input-abort delivers nothing.
  - string_view lifetime hazard: queued hintText/inText are views into caller memory that must stay alive until flush — Go port with strings removes this hazard (copy at enqueue time).
- 1:1 constraints: `MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 255` (line 7); queue capacity 16 (line 15); `swkbdInit(&swkbd, SWKBD_TYPE_WESTERN, 2, MAX_TEXT_LENGTH)` (line 34) — button count exactly 2; `swkbdSetValidation(&swkbd, SWKBD_NOTEMPTY_NOTBLANK, 0, 0)` (line 35); buffer size `MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + 1 = 256` (lines 41, 44); `memset(mybuf, 0, sizeof(mybuf))` before input (line 44); confirm-only dispatch (lines 46-48); `eventCount = 0` at end (line 52).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable statics `events`/`eventCount` (lines 15-16) — single-threaded UI usage only; enqueue from UI code, flush from DiabloUI frame loop (diabloui.cpp:868). No locking; Go port must keep queue access on the UI goroutine or add a mutex.
- Test coverage: none found (no keyboard tests in test/).
- Go mapping: devilutionGo internal/ui (or internal/platform/keyboard) — `VkbdQueue` struct with `Input(hint, initial string, cb func(string))` and `Flush()`; on desktop Go builds this maps to an on-screen/text-entry dialog or is a no-op stub; keep the confirm-only callback contract.
- Risks/open questions: real buffer-overrun-ish quirk: `eventCount >= sizeof(events)` compares int to byte count (line 20) — intent was 16 events; Go port should use explicit capacity 16. Platform-specific behavior (blocking modal system keyboard) has no desktop equivalent; define expected Go fallback explicitly.

### Source/platform/ctr/random.cpp
- Purpose: Registers a libsodium randombytes implementation backed by the 3DS PS service (`PS_GenerateRandomBytes`), so all of the game's libsodium crypto randomness comes from the console's hardware/system RNG.
- Public API: `void randombytes_ctrrandom_init()` (random.hpp line 2, defined cpp lines 46-49) — installs `randombytes_ctrrandom_implementation` via `randombytes_set_implementation`. Internal: implementation-name fn returning `"ctrrandom"` (lines 6-9); `tryfill` (lines 11-21); `random()` u32 (lines 23-29); `buf()` (lines 31-35); exported-ish struct `randombytes_ctrrandom_implementation` (lines 37-44, positionally initialized: name, random, nullptr, nullptr, buf, nullptr).
- Depends on: `<3ds.h>` for `psGetSessionHandle()`, `psInit()`, `PS_GenerateRandomBytes()`, `Result`, `R_SUCCEEDED` (lines 14-19); `<sodium.h>` for `randombytes_implementation` struct, `randombytes_set_implementation`, `sodium_misuse` (line 3); caller: `Source/platform/ctr/system.cpp:118` calls init during 3DS startup (verified by grep).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Lazy PS-service init: on first fill, if no session handle, `psInit()`; failure to init → fill fails.
  - Fill semantics: single syscall `PS_GenerateRandomBytes(buf, size)` for the whole buffer; success/failure by Result.
  - Hard-fail semantics: `random()`/`buf()` call `sodium_misuse()` (abort) if fill fails — cryptographic RNG failure is fatal, never silently degraded.
  - Registration is process-global and must happen once at platform startup, BEFORE any libsodium use.
  - In Go: libsodium is typically replaced by Go stdlib `crypto/rand`, which on a given platform already uses the OS CSPRNG — a direct counterpart is usually unnecessary; if a Go 3DS port exists, provide a `crypto/rand` reader backed by PS_GenerateRandomBytes with the same lazy-init + hard-fail contract.
- 1:1 constraints: implementation name string `"ctrrandom"` (line 8); struct field order for positional init (lines 37-44): implementation_name, random, stub(null), stub(null), buf, stub(null) — i.e. `random` uses buf-style fill of 4 bytes (line 26: `sizeof(uint32_t)`); `sodium_misuse()` on any fill failure (lines 27, 34); lazy `psInit()` guarded by `!psGetSessionHandle()` (lines 14-18).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: NOT deterministic by design — this is the CSPRNG source (the only legitimate non-determinism in the game; gameplay RNG lives elsewhere). Registration is a one-time global side effect (order: at system.cpp startup, before network/crypto). The PS session, once initialized, is shared process-wide; `randombytes` calls may come from multiple threads post-registration — thread safety is inherited from the 3DS PS service, and the lazy-init race is handled by libsodium's init-once pattern; Go port should use `sync.Once` for init.
- Test coverage: none found (no ctr random tests).
- Go mapping: devilutionGo — no direct file needed if using Go `crypto/rand` (maps 1:1 in intent: OS CSPRNG). If platform plumbing is kept: internal/platform/n3ds `randomReader` implementing `io.Reader` with lazy PS init + panic on failure, registered in the platform bootstrap.
- Risks/open questions: verify which code paths actually consume libsodium randomness in the Go port (e.g. packet encryption via PKWare/Storm is not CSPRNG; if nothing needs libsodium, this file drops out entirely).

### Source/platform/ctr/sockets.cpp
- Purpose: Initializes/tears down the 3DS `soc:` (sockets) service: waits for Wi-Fi, allocates an aligned network buffer, calls `socInit`, and registers cleanup via `atexit`.
- Public API: `void n3ds_socInit()` (line 45), `void n3ds_socExit()` (line 36) — defined in `namespace devilution`.
- Depends on: `platform/ctr/sockets.hpp` (self decl), `<3ds.h>` (socInit/socExit/ACU_GetWifiStatus/svcSleepThread/R_SUCCEEDED/u32/Result), `<malloc.h>` (memalign/free), `utils/log.hpp` (LogError, lines 48/55/61).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - On desktop Go, sockets need no init — Go net package self-initializes. Port = no-op pair or omit.
  - If a "wait for network up" behavior is desired (handheld parity), Go equivalent: poll a cheap net op with 100 ms sleeps, ≤50 attempts (5 s budget), then log error and give up.
  - Ensure teardown registered exactly once (the `initialized` flag semantics).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `SOC_ALIGN = 0x1000` (line 12); `SOC_BUFFERSIZE = 0x100000` (1 MiB, line 13).
  - Wi-Fi poll: `sleepNano = 100 * 1000 * 1000` (100 ms, line 20); `loopCount = 5 * 1000 / 100` = 50 iterations (line 23) → total 5 s max; success = `R_SUCCEEDED(ACU_GetWifiStatus(&wifi)) && wifi != 0` (lines 28-29).
  - `socExit()` only if `socBuffer != nullptr` (lines 38-40); after exit, `free(socBuffer); socBuffer = nullptr` (lines 40-41).
  - On `socInit` failure the buffer is freed and NOT retried (lines 60-63); note `initialized` is not set on that path but `atexit` also not registered — matching C semantics means: register cleanup only after successful init.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutable file-scope statics `socBuffer` (line 14) and `initialized` (line 15) — not thread-safe; in Go model as package-level state guarded once at startup, or dropped entirely.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: devilutionGo `internal/platform/ctr` (stub) or simply drop; note in port docs that `net.Dial`/`net.Listen` need no SOC init.
- Risks/open questions: none (desktop Go ignores this file's behavior entirely).

### Source/platform/locale.cpp
- Purpose: `GetLocales()` — returns the user's preferred locale list as POSIX codes (`lang` or `lang_REGION`), per-platform (Android JNI, PS Vita, 3DS, Windows, macOS CoreFoundation, generic POSIX env).
- Public API: `std::vector<std::string> GetLocales()` (line 61), `namespace devilution`. File-local helper `std::string IetfToPosix(std::string_view)` (line 37, anonymous namespace, Windows/Apple builds only).
- Depends on: `locale.hpp` (self), `<algorithm>` (std::replace), `platform/ctr/locale.hpp` (`n3ds::GetLocale`, line 114); platform SDKs per branch (SDL/JNI, psp2, windows.h/winnls.h, CoreFoundation, clocale). Sole caller: `Source/options.cpp:979` (language selection for translations).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Port the POSIX branch (lines 183-206) — the desktop path: read env `LANGUAGE` first (colon-separated list, each entry pushed unless empty), else `LANG`, else `setlocale(LC_MESSAGES)`/`(LC_CTYPE)`; strip everything from the first `.` (codeset suffix).
  - Also port `IetfToPosix` logic if Go ever gets IETF codes from an OS API: zh-Hans→zh_CN, zh-Hant→zh_TW prefix mapping, then '-'→'_'.
  - Go equivalents: `os.Getenv("LANGUAGE")` / `os.Getenv("LANG")`; Go has no setlocale — treat absent env as empty list.
  - Return order = preference order; caller (options.cpp) tries each in sequence against available translations.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `IetfToPosix`: `langCode.substr(0, 7) == "zh-Hans"` → `"zh_CN"` (lines 43-45); `"zh-Hant"` → `"zh_TW"` (lines 46-48); otherwise replace all `-` with `_` (line 53).
  - Windows conversion: buffer `char utf8Buffer[16]` zero-init, converts up to 10 chars via `WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, wideString, 10, …)` (lines 119-122).

### Source/platform/switch/docking.cpp
- Purpose: Detects Nintendo Switch dock/handheld transitions via `appletGetOperationMode()` and resizes the SDL window to the new display resolution, clearing stale framebuffers first.
- Public API: `void HandleDocking()` (declared in docking.h).
- Depends on: `devilution::renderer`, `devilution::ghMainWnd` from `utils/display.h` (SDL renderer + window globals); libnx `<switch.h>` (`appletGetOperationMode`, `AppletOperationMode_Console/Handheld`); SDL2 (`SDL_RenderClear/Present/SetWindowSize`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A platform hook that can be polled per-frame (or on an event) to check operation mode and trigger a window resize.
  - On dock→handheld or handheld→dock transition: set window to 1920×1080 (docked) or 1280×720 (handheld).
  - Before resize, perform exactly 3× (render-clear + present) cycles to flush stale frames from the swapchain.
  - Maintain last-known-mode state so resize only happens on change; initial state is "Uninitialized" so the first call always resizes.
  - Needs access to the Go equivalent of the main window/renderer (Ebiten: `SetWindowSize`; the triple-clear maps to letting 3 frames draw).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Docked resolution = 1920×1080; handheld = 1280×720 (lines 33-37).
  - Exactly 3 clear+present iterations (line 41-44 comment explains flicker rationale).
  - `static OperationMode currentMode` starts `Uninitialized = -1`; enum values Handheld=0, Docked=1, Uninitialized=-1 (int8_t).
  - Unknown `appletGetOperationMode` return values fall through to Handheld (default case).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `static` local `currentMode` is mutable global state (function-local); intended to be called from main/render thread. No locking.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/platform/switch` (or `internal/platform` hooks package) — expose `HandleDocking(window)` called from the platform event loop; on Go/Ebiten desktop targets this becomes a no-op stub.
- Risks/open questions: Ebiten's swapchain management differs; the 3-clear trick may not translate — verify against Ebiten window-resize behavior if Switch target ever exists.

### Source/platform/switch/keyboard.cpp
- Purpose: Opens the Switch software keyboard (swkbd), then feeds the result into the app by synthesizing SDL key events: 600× backspace down/up to clear the current text field, 600× delete down/up, then one SDL_TEXTINPUT event per UTF-8 character.
- Public API: `switch_start_text_input(guide_text, initial_text, max_length)` (declared in keyboard.h).
- Depends on: libnx swkbd (`swkbdCreate`, `swkbdConfigMakePresetDefault`, `swkbdConfigSetGuideText/InitialText/StringLenMax`, `swkbdShow`, `swkbdClose`); SDL2 event queue (`SDL_PushEvent`, keycodes/scancodes); `devilution::CopyUtf8` from `utils/utf8.hpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Text-input entry point: blocking call that shows an on-screen/soft keyboard, returns user text (or falls back to `initial_text` when the dialog returns empty).
  - After obtaining text, simulate the input pipeline the game expects: erase existing field content (the Go text-field widget must support programmatic "clear" — replacing the 1200 synthetic key events), then deliver the final string as text-input events.
  - Must truncate/honor `max_length` bytes.
  - Handle multi-byte UTF-8: iterate per codepoint, not per byte.
  - Guide text and initial text passed to dialog only when non-empty; copies made before handing to C API (NUL-termination safety).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Backspace loop: 600 iterations; Delete loop: 600 iterations (lines 66-71) — both down+up pairs.
  - UTF-8 length heuristics in `get_utf8_character_bytes`: 1/2/3/4-byte branch table with masks 0x80, 0xe0/0xc0, 0xf0/0xc0, 0xf8/0xc0 and fallback return 1 on malformed sequences.
  - Empty-result fallback: `CopyUtf8(text, initial_text, sizeof(text))`.
  - TEXTINPUT event carries exactly `bytes_in_char` bytes, NUL-terminated.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `text[max_length]` is a VLA on the caller's stack; blocking call (swkbdShow blocks). No shared state; safe from any single thread that owns SDL events.
- Test coverage: none found (no tests reference switch keyboard).
- Go mapping: `internal/platform/switch` text input → bridge to a generic Go `TextInput(guide, initial string, maxLen int) (string, error)` service that pushes results into the game's input queue; on desktop Ebiten, soft keyboard is typically unnecessary (hardware keyboard).
- Risks/open questions: the 600-erase-event hack assumes the game's text field buffer; the Go text-widget design must define clearing semantics. Whether to preserve the 600 constant or replace with explicit clear is a design decision for the widget layer.

### Source/platform/switch/random.cpp
- Purpose: Implements a libsodium `randombytes_implementation` backed by the Switch console's hardware CSRNG service, and registers it as sodium's random source at startup.

### Source/platform/vita/keyboard.cpp
- Purpose: PlayStation Vita text input — opens the native IME dialog (async) and spawns a polling thread that, when the dialog finishes, converts UTF16→UTF8 and pushes one SDL_TEXTINPUT event; unlike the Switch version it does NOT synthesize erase keystrokes and does NOT block.
- Public API: `vita_start_text_input(guide_text, initial_text, max_length)` (declared in vita/keyboard.h, not in this batch).
- Depends on: psp2 `<psp2/ime_dialog.h>` (`sceImeDialogInit/GetStatus/GetResult/Term`, `SceImeDialogParam`, `SCE_IME_DIALOG_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH/TITLE_LENGTH`, `SCE_IME_TYPE_DEFAULT`, `SCE_IME_DIALOG_TEXTBOX_MODE_WITH_CLEAR`); SDL2 threads/events (`SDL_CreateThread`, `SDL_PushEvent`, `SDL_utf8strlcpy`); `std::string_view`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Async text input: open dialog, spawn poller (goroutine) that waits for FINISHED status, fetches result, converts to UTF-8, pushes text-input event(s) into the game input queue, then terminates the dialog.
  - Pure, in-file UTF16→UTF8 and UTF8→UTF16 converters must be replicated exactly (they handle surrogate pairs and clamp to source length); note the UTF8→UTF16 decoder only supports up to 3-byte sequences (no 4-byte UTF-8 input) and breaks on truncation.
  - Dialog params: supportedLanguages=0, languagesForced=false, type=DEFAULT, option=0, textBoxMode=WITH_CLEAR, maxTextLength=max_len.
  - On init failure (`res < 0`): silently no dialog (returns 0 → no thread spawned).
  - Result buffer sizes: title = MAX_TITLE_LENGTH UTF-16 units, text/buffer = MAX_TEXT_LENGTH.
  - Note: no fallback to initial_text on empty result (Switch has one; Vita does not).
  - `vita_input_thread`'s buffer `ime_buffer` is a stack array of the caller captured by the spawned thread — a latent dangling-stack bug in C++ (thread outlives `vita_start_text_input`'s frame); the Go port with goroutines must pass an owned copy/slice.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - utf16→utf8: ASCII passthrough when `(c & 0xFF80) == 0`; 2-byte when `(c & 0xF800) == 0` → `0xC0|(c>>6)`, `0x80|(c&0x3F)`; surrogate pair when `(c & 0xFC00) == 0xD800 && (next & 0xFC00) == 0xDC00` → 4 bytes `0xF0|((c+64)>>8 & 0x3)`, `0x80|((c>>2)+16 & 0x3F)`, `0x80|((c>>4)&0x30) | ((next<<2)&0xF)`, `0x80|(next&0x3F)`; else 3-byte `0xE0|(c>>12)`, `0x80|(c>>6 & 0x3F)`, `0x80|(c&0x3F)`; NUL-terminate.
  - utf8→utf16: 3-byte lead `(b & 0xE0) == 0xE0` → `(b&0x0F)<<12 | (b1&0x3F)<<6 | (b2&0x3F)`; 2-byte lead `(b & 0xC0) == 0xC0` → `(b&0x1F)<<6 | (b1&0x3F)`; else 1 unit; break when fewer bytes remain than needed (bounds: `i+2 >= src_size` / `i+1 >= src_size`).
  - Thread busy-loops with no sleep polling `sceImeDialogGetStatus()` until FINISHED.
  - SDL event text copied with `SDL_utf8strlcpy` into `event.text.text` (SDL_TEXTINPUT field, 32 bytes).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: not deterministic (user input). Background thread pushes to SDL queue (thread-safe API). The stack-buffer capture is a real UAF risk in the original; document, don't replicate.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/platform/vita` or generic `internal/input` soft-keyboard service: goroutine + channel feeding the input event queue; converters replaced by Go `unicode/utf16` + `unicode/utf8` (standard library equivalents exist and handle all cases — prefer stdlib over hand-rolled bit math).
- Risks/open questions: the dangling `ime_buffer` pointer into a returned stack frame is UB in the original; the Go port must own the buffer. Also note `(b & 0xE0) == 0xE0` misclassifies 4-byte UTF-8 leads (0xF0-0xF4) as 3-byte sequences — stdlib avoids this; decide whether to preserve original (buggy) behavior or fix (recommend fix, note deviation).

### Source/platform/vita/touch.cpp
- Purpose: Translates Vita multitouch finger events into synthetic SDL mouse events (taps = clicks, 1/2/3-finger drags = LMB drag / LMB drag / RMB drag) and maps rear-touch to controller triggers.
- Public API: `HandleTouchEvent(SDL_Event*, Point mousePosition)`, `FinishSimulatedMouseClicks(Point mousePosition)` (touch.h).
- Depends on: options.h (`GetOptions().Controller.bRearTouch`), utils/display.h (`OutputToLogical`, `GetOutputSurface`, `gnScreenWidth/gnScreenHeight`), utils/ui_fwd.h, SDL events/touch, engine Point.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Touch-gesture→mouse mapping layer if a touch target exists: finger down/up/motion preprocessor maintaining per-finger state (id, timeLastDown, last coords, down coords).
  - Tap detection: short tap (<250 ms) with motion < 10 px → click; # fingers down at lift time decides button (1=LMB, 2=RMB).
  - Simulated clicks auto-release after 50 ms (`FinishSimulatedMouseClicks` pushes SDL_MOUSEBUTTONUP).
  - Multi-finger drag start requires ≥2 fingers held >250 ms; 2-finger = LMB drag, ≥3 = RMB drag; drag ends when last finger lifts.
  - Pointer follows "oldest" finger; relative mode uses dx/dy × SpeedFactor 1.25.
  - Rear touch (port != 0) → trigger axis events (value 32767/0; x<=0.5 left else right) only if `bRearTouch` option.
  - Aspect-fit letterbox math: visible_width = h*gnScreenWidth/gnScreenHeight; borders = (full−visible)/2.
- 1:1 constraints: TOUCH_PORT_MAX_NUM=1, NO_TOUCH=-1 (lines 14–17); MaxNumFingers=3, MaxTapTime=250 ms, MaxTapMotionDistance=10 px, SimulatedClickDuration=50 ms (enum, lines 50–56); SpeedFactor=1.25F (line 296); tap-motion test is squared distance vs 10²; clip to [0, surface w/h]; finger motion event mutation in-place (`event->type` rewritten); `HandleTouchEvent` rewrites unconsumed finger events to a registered ignore-event type; drag start picks button-press position = oldest-other-finger's lastX/lastY.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: file-scope mutable statics (finger table, drag state, click timers, Mouse, IgnoreEvent); lazy init on first call (`touch_initialized`); event-loop single-thread assumed.
- Test coverage: none found (no touch tests under test/).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/touch` — only if touch input is in scope; otherwise omit with a note.
- Risks/open questions: SDL-specific event coercion (reuse of one SDL_Event) has no direct Go analog; needs an event-translation interface.

### Source/player.cpp
- Purpose: The player gameplay core: per-mode animation processing (walk/attack/ranged/spell/block/hit/death), melee & PvP hit resolution, damage/durability handling, item drops on death, leveling & experience, stat validation/modification, sprite loading (CL2 sheets + TRN), level transitions, and the per-tick `ProcessPlayers` driver.
- Public API: globals `MyPlayerId`, `MyPlayer`, `Players`, `InspectPlayer`, `MyPlayerIsDead` (lines 63–68); ~60 free functions listed in player.h (CreatePlayer, ProcessPlayers, ApplyPlrDamage, StartPlayerKill, StartNewLvl, CheckPlrSpell, PosOkPlayer, MakePlrPath, PlayDungMsgs, …) plus the full set of `Player::` method implementations.
- Depends on: control.h (RedrawComponent/RedrawEverything), controls/plrctrls (ControlMode), cursor (pcurs, NewCursor), dead, engine/random (GenerateRnd, RandomIntBetween, FlipCoin), engine/render/clx_render + load_cl2 (LoadCl2Sheet, ClxApplyTrans), engine/trn (GetClassTRN), lighting (AddLight/ChangeLightXY/ChangeLightOffset), ChangeVisionXY/ActivateVision, loadsave (LoadHotkeys), missiles (AddMissile, RemovePlrMissiles, CastSpell), monster (Monsters, M_StartHit/M_StartKill/M_GetKnockback, AddDoppelganger), nthread (gbBufferMsgs), objects (Objects, OperateObject, BreakObject), qol/stash, qol/autopickup (AutoPickup), spells (CheckSpell, CanUseScroll/Staff, GetSpellData, IsWallSpell), stores, towners (TalkToTowner), levels/trigs, tables/playerdat (ClassAttributes, PlayerAnimData, PlayerSpriteData, GetPlayerStartingLoadoutForClass), inv helpers (inv_iterators, GoldAutoPlace, AutoEquip, FindGetItem, AllocateItem), msg network sends (NetSendCmd* family), Lua hooks (OnPlayerGainExperience, OnPlayerTakeDamage).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A `Player` struct mirroring player.h fields; a per-tick `ProcessPlayers` that: decrements pLvlLoad, runs sfxdelay queued-speech state machine (Defiler1–4 → InitQTextMsg else PlaySFX), calls ValidatePlayer, then per active on-level player runs a do/while on mode handlers (DoWalk/DoAttack/DoRangeAttack/DoBlock/DoSpell/DoGotHit/DoDeath) with CheckNewPath until stable, then clears previewCelSprite and advances AnimInfo (skip advance when PM_DEATH && tickCounterOfCurrentFrame==40).
  - Walk: WalkSettings table maps each Direction → PM walk mode (South/SW→SOUTHWARDS, W/E→SIDEWAYS, NW/N/NE→NORTHWARDS, SE→SOUTHWARDS); PlrDirOK extra solid-tile check for East(SE)/West(SW); town run-in-town skips 2 frames; occupyTile sets dPlayer negative while moving.
  - Attack start frame skip table (lines 174–205): FastestAttack 4/2, FasterAttack 3/2, FastAttack 2/1, QuickAttack 1/0 (includesFirstFrame ? a : b); ranged non-Hellfire: Quick|Fast +1, Fast +1.
  - Melee hit: hit roll GenerateRnd(100) (petrified → 0), hper = GetMeleePiercingToHit − CalculateArmorPierce(monster.armorClass, true), clamp [5,95]; adjacentDamage penalty −30 if lvl>20 else −(35−lvl)*2; damage = RandomIntBetween(min,max) + dam*%bonus/100 + %mod + _pDamageMod; class CriticalStrike (Bard/Barbarian/…) doubles on rnd100<level; monster-class modifiers (Undead: sword −50%/mace +50%; Animal: mace −50%/sword +50%; Demon ×3 with TripleDemonDamage); HF pDamAcFlags: Devastation ×3 on rnd100<5, Doppelganger on rnd100<10 (non-unique non-Diablo), Jesters r=rnd(201), r>=100→100+(r−100)*5, dam=dam*r/100; adjacentDamage dam>>=2; Peril (MyPlayer): self-dam2 += _pIGetHit<<6 then dam*=2; steal-life rnd(dam/8), StealMana 3/5 %, StealLife 3/5 % capped at max; FireDamage|LightningDamage+Hellfire → SpectralArrow missile with RandomIntBetween(_pIFMinDam,_pIFMaxDam).
  - PvP: hit/blk rolls, blkper = GetBlockChance() − attackerLevel*2 clamp [0,100]; block triggers StartPlrBlock; damage skdam=dam<<6; steal-life rnd(skdam/8); MyPlayer attacker → NetSendCmdDamage.
  - DoAttack: on frame _pAFNum−2 PlaySfxLoc(Swing); on frame _pAFNum−1 resolve monster→player→object at tile+dir; talkable monster aborts; cleave (Monk w/ staff, Bard dual swords, Barbarian axe or 2h mace/sword w/o shield) hits Left(dir) and Right(dir) tiles with adjacentDamage=true and monster.position.old==position; elemental explosions unless Hellfire fire+lightning combo; DamageWeapon(player, 30) on hit.
  - DoRangeAttack: 1 arrow at _pAFNum−1, 2nd at +1 with MultipleArrows; spread offsets from angle ∓1 by target quadrant; missile type Fire/Lightning/SpectralArrow selection; DamageWeapon(player, 40).
  - Durability: WeaponDecay (HF Decay flag: −5 _iPLDam, remove at ≤−100); DamageWeapon coin-flip damageFrequency, indestructible guard, remove at 0, shield parry in DamageParryItem (1-in-10 after block), DamageArmor (3-in-4 on hit, head/chest selection FlipCoin(3) with single-slot forcing).
  - Death: drop rules dropGold = !multiplayer || !(level 16 or arena); dropItems = dropGold && MonsterOrTrap; dropEar = dropGold && Player; ear item built from name chars: _iCreateInfo = name[0]<<8|name[1], _iSeed = name[2]<<24|name[3]<<16|name[4]<<8|name[5], _ivalue = level, curs by class; equipment dropped rotating direction Left per item; MyPlayerIsDead at death-frame tick 30; ticksPerFrame forced 100 at death anim end.
  - ApplyPlrDamage: totalDamage=(dam<<6)+frac; Lua OnPlayerTakeDamage; mana shield: level>0 → totalDamage += totalDamage/−GetManaShieldDamageReduction(); absorb from mana, overflow re-adds totalDamage/(reduction−1), sets mana base delta, sends CMD_REMSHIELD; clamp HP at max, min floor minHP<<6, SyncPlrKill on no-life.
  - Experience: _addExperience clamps exp*(1+levelDelta/10.0) to u32; multiplayer cap min(exp, nextThreshold/20, 200*level) — note: min() of BOTH caps unconditionally (level 1–5 and 6–50 applied together); Lua hook; add min(clamped, maxExp−_pExperience); level-up loop calls NextPlrLevel (stat pts: CalcStatDiff<5 → set to diff else +5; +lvlLife HP, +lvlMana mana with NoMana guard).
  - CreatePlayer seeds RNG with SDL_GetTicks (line 2303) and resets seed to 0 at end; InitPlayer randomizes stand frame `GenerateRnd(_pNFrames−1)` and tick `GenerateRnd(3)`.
  - Sprite system: LoadPlrGFX builds path "plrgfx\{classPath}\{prefix}{suffix}" where prefix = classChar + ArmourChar[_pgfxnum>>4] + WepChar[weapon]; suffixes as→st(town), aw→wl, at, ht, lm/fm/qm, dt (forces Unarmed), bl (needs _pBlockFlag, not town); Attack/Hit/Block return early in town; loads CL2 sheet at class sprite width; applies graphic TRN then class TRN; SetPlrAnims copies PlayerAnimData per weapon graphic; Warrior/Barbarian bow-in-dungeon _pNFrames=8 and armor>0 → _pDFrames=15.
  - UpdatePreviewCelSprite: only when game running, unpaused, gbProcessPlayers, PM_STAND; per _cmd_id resolves graphic/dir, optional pathfind (FindPath with CanStep + PosOkPlayer), walk preview PlrDirOK gate; stores first sprite + ProgressToNextGameTick for AnimationInfo preview accounting.
  - Level flow: StartNewLvl (fom switch: NEXT/PREV/RTN/TOWNWARP→setLevel(lvl); SETLVL→setlvlnum; TWARPUP→pTownWarps |= 1<<(leveltype−2); RETOWN) pushes SDL custom event + CMD_NEWLVL in MP; RestartTownLvl sets HP 64, mana 0/base delta; StartWarpLvl via Portals[pidx]; InitLevelChange clears mana shield/reflections (re-broadcasts own), FixPlrWalkTags, pLvlLoad=10 for MyPlayer.
  - PlayDungMsgs one-shot speeches keyed to first visit of levels 1/5/9/13/16/17/19/21, set-level skeleton king; Defiler quest activation (Q_DEFILER quest + NetSendCmdQuest).
  - TryDisarm: trapdisper = 2*_pDexterity − 5*currlevel; success when rnd(100) ≤ trapdisper; arms linked traps (_oVar4=1).
- 1:1 constraints: values cited inline above; WalkSettings order S,SW,W,NW,N,NE,E,SE with modes (lines 92–102); StartWalkAnimation skippedFrames = −2 base, +2 town+runInTown, +1 pmWillBeCalled; GetManaShieldDamageReduction = 24 − min(spellLvl,7)*3; PlrHitPlr block roll precedes damage; ValidatePlayer gold cap GOLD_MAX_LIMIT (×2 Hellfire) and recompute _pGold; spell bitmask mask over GetSpellBookLevel != −1, _pSplLvl clamp MaxSpellLevel(15); ear-shift encoding (UB-sanitizer suppressed on StartPlayerKill/StartNewLvl); DoDeath dFlags |= DungeonFlag::DeadPlayer; InitPlayer first-time readied spell from staff via ReadySpellFromEquipment (staff w/ charges); GetPlayerGraphicsPath BufCopy layout "plrgfx\\%s\\%3s%s"; PosOkPlayer: InDungeonBounds, IsTileWalkable, no live other player, monster tile rules (town blocks always, else only dead monsters with positive dMonster index pass); MakePlrPath endspace=false drops last step (path−1); CheckPlrSpell town/panel/pcurs gates, Teleport queue-retarget when cursPosition within WalkingDistance 1 of temp; AddPlrMonstExper splits exp over popcount(pmask), local player must be in mask.

### Source/portal.cpp
- Purpose: Town-portal state and logic: per-player portal array, portal missiles in town/dungeon, activation/deactivation, level/position switching on portal use, and PosOk check for level-entry placement.
- Public API: `Portal Portals[MAXPORTAL]` (global array, MAXPORTAL=4); `InitPortals()`; `SetPortalStats(int i, bool o, Point position, int lvl, dungeon_type lvltype, bool isSetLevel)`; `AddPortalMissile(const Player&, Point, bool sync)`; `SyncPortals()`; `AddPortalInTown(const Player&)`; `ActivatePortal(const Player&, Point, int, dungeon_type, bool)`; `DeactivatePortal(const Player&)`; `bool PortalOnLevel(const Player&)`; `RemovePortalMissile(const Player&)`; `SetCurrentPortal(size_t p)`; `GetPortalLevel()`; `GetPortalLvlPos()`; `bool PosOkPortal(int lvl, Point position)`.
- Depends on: `AddMissile`, `MissileID::TownPortal`, `Missiles` (missiles.h); `AddLight`/`AddUnLight` (lighting.h); `NetSendCmd`/`CMD_DEACTIVATEPORTAL` (multi.h); `Players`, `MyPlayer`, `MyPlayerId` (player.h); `PortalFrame::Idle`, `SfxID::None` (tables/misdat.h); globals `leveltype`, `currlevel`, `setlevel`, `setlvlnum`, `setlvltype`, `dFlags`, `ViewPosition`, `DungeonFlag::Missile`, `Direction::South`, `DTYPE_TOWN`, `_setlevels`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `Portals [4]Portal` package-level state; `Portal{Open bool, Position Point, Level int, Ltype dungeon_type, Setlvl bool}`.
  - `InitPortals` clears only `.open` (not other fields) for all 4.
  - `SyncPortals`: for each open portal i — in town place missile at `PortalTownPosition[i]`; in dungeon, compute `lvl = setlevel ? setlvlnum : currlevel` and place only if `Portals[i].level == lvl && Portals[i].setlvl == setlevel`. Always `sync=true`.
  - `AddPortalMissile`: AddMissile from `{0,0}` to position, dir South, `TARGET_MONSTERS`, damage 0/0, no parent, no sfx; if sync → `setFrameGroup(PortalFrame::Idle)` (skip opening animation); if `leveltype != DTYPE_TOWN` attach light radius 15.
  - `ActivatePortal`: set `open=true` always; only overwrite position/level/ltype/setlvl when `lvl != 0`.
  - `PortalOnLevel`: `setlvl==setlevel && level == (setlevel ? setlvlnum : currlevel)`, OR `leveltype == DTYPE_TOWN`.
  - `RemovePortalMissile`: remove all missiles with `_mitype==TownPortal && _misource==player id`, clearing `DungeonFlag::Missile` from their tile and calling `AddUnLight(_mlid)` if `Portals[id].level != 0`.
  - `GetPortalLevel`: if not in town → return to town (`setlevel=false; currlevel=0; MyPlayer->setLevel(0); leveltype=DTYPE_TOWN`). ### Source/qol/floatingnumbers.cpp
- Purpose: QoL floating combat numbers (damage/etc.): a time-based queue of texts rising (or falling) from world positions, with recent-merge by source id, drawn during world render and expired by tick deadline.
- Public API: `AddFloatingNumber(Point pos, Displacement offset, std::string text, UiFlags style, int id = 0, bool reverseDirection = false)`; `DrawFloatingNumbers(const Surface &out, Point viewPosition, Displacement offset)`; `ClearFloatingNumbers()`.
- Depends on: `SDL_GetTicks` (SDL2/SDL3 timer); `Point`/`Displacement`/`worldToScreen()` (engine/point.hpp, displacement.hpp); `TILE_WIDTH`/`TILE_HEIGHT` (engine/point geometry headers); `DrawString`/`GetLineWidth`/`GameFontTables`/`GameFont12/24/30` (engine/render/text_render.hpp); `UiFlags::FontSize30/24/Outlined`, `HasAnyOf` (DiabloUI/ui_flags.hpp); `GetOptions().Graphics.zoom` (options.h); `StrCat` (utils/str_cat.hpp).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `FloatingNumber` record: startPos, startOffset, endOffset, text, time (uint32 tick deadline), lastMerge (uint32 tick), style UiFlags (with Outlined bit added), id int, reverseDirection bool. Stored in a FIFO deque.
  - `AddFloatingNumber`: endOffset = `{0,-140}` normal, `{0,+140}` reversed. Merge pass: if `id != 0` and an existing entry has same id and `SDL_GetTicks() − lastMerge <= 100` → overwrite text/lastMerge/style/startPos and return (keeps original animation clock). Otherwise push new entry with `time = now+2500`, `lastMerge = now`, style |= Outlined.
  - `DrawFloatingNumbers(out, viewPosition, offset)`: for each entry: `worldOffset = viewPosition − startPos`, then `.worldToScreen() + offset + {TILE_WIDTH/2, −TILE_HEIGHT/2} + startOffset`; if zoom option → `*2`. Center horizontally: `x −= lineWidth/2` where lineWidth = GetLineWidth(text, fontFromStyle). Rise: `mul = 1 − (timeLeft/2500.0)` (float), `screenPos += endOffset * mul`. DrawString with style. After the loop, `ClearExpiredNumbers()`: pop front while `front.time <= now`.
  - `ClearFloatingNumbers`: clears the queue **and calls `srand(time(nullptr))`** — a stray reseed of the global C RNG (side effect to preserve or consciously drop).
  - `GetGameFontSize`: FontSize30→GameFont30, FontSize24→GameFont24, else GameFont12.
- 1:1 constraints: rise distance 140 px (L74–L77); lifetime 2500 ms (L90); merge window 100 ms (L84); tile-center offset `{TILE_WIDTH/2, −TILE_HEIGHT/2}` (L105); zoom ×2 (L108); font-size ladder order 30→24→12 (L39–L43); expiration `time > SDL_GetTicks()` break condition — entries live until tick passes deadline (L29–L31); `timeLeft`/2500.0F float math for position (sub-pixel truncation behavior on int add — Go should mirror int truncation).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Ticks-based timing (SDL_GetTicks → Go: monotonic ms clock abstraction); NOT deterministic replay-safe (depends on wall time between Add and Draw). The `srand(time(nullptr))` in ClearFloatingNumbers perturbs the shared RNG — in Go, if game RNG is separated, note this reseeds the C global rand used elsewhere; safest 1:1 is to replicate against the same RNG abstraction or document removal. Queue is single-threaded render-path state.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: `internal/qol/floatingnumbers` — inject `now() func() uint32` clock; merge logic and font-ladder trivially unit-testable. For 1:1, keep pixel math on ints with the same truncation.
- Risks/open questions: the `srand` reseed is almost certainly unintended coupling — decide in Go whether to keep (affects future `rand()` consumers) or drop with a note; flag as deliberate deviation if dropped.

  - `IsHighlightingLabelsEnabled` = `!IsPlayerInStore() && highlightKeyPressed != showItemLabels` (XOR semantics).
  - `AddItemToLabelQueue(id, pos)`: skip if highlighting disabled; text = gold → `"{:s} gold"` with `FormatInteger(_ivalue)` (localized), else `getName()`; `nameWidth = GetLineWidth(text) + 2*MarginX`; per-cursor-anim center offset from `ClxMeasureSolidHorizontalBounds(currentFrame)` cached in `labelCenterOffsets[ItemCAnimTbl[_iCurs]]` as `(xBegin+xEnd)/2`; `pos.x += center; pos.y -= TILE_HEIGHT`; if zoom → `pos *= 2`; `pos.x -= width/2; pos.y -= LabelHeight`; append.

Repeat do/while until a full pass makes no move. Then per label: hover-test rect (pos..pos+width/labelHeight) → if also `!gmenu_is_active && PauseMode==0 && !MyPlayerIsDead && !IsPlayerInStore() && IsMouseOverGameArea() && LastPlayerAction==None` → set `isLabelHighlighted=true`, `cursPosition=item.position`, `pcursitem=label.id`. Cache array size `ITEMTYPES`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `labelCenterOffsets` is a run-lifetime cache keyed by cursor-anim index — depends on item animation data being loaded; reset concerns on asset reload. Queue is cleared every frame (single-threaded render). Mouse/cursor globals tie into input path.

- Requirements for Go port:
  - State: `VisualStoreState{vendor, activeTab, currentPage, pages}` where each page = grid `uint16[10][9]` storing index+1 plus `items []{index uint16, position Point}` (anchor bottom-left convention: `position = slot + {0, h-1}`).
  - Layout builder `RefreshVisualStoreLayout`: clear pages; first-fit row-major placement in 10×9 grid; items that don't fit start a new page (retry once there); empty item list → one zeroed empty page; clamp currentPage to last page if out of range.
  - Vendor item sources: Smith basic=SmithItems, Smith premium=PremiumItems, Witch=WitchItems, Healer=HealerItems, Boy=[BoyItem] if non-empty.
  - Tab buttons only for Smith; Witch/Boy/Healer show a single non-functional "Misc" tab button.
  - Purchase flow (`CheckVisualStoreItem`): hover-resolve item; affordability check against `MyPlayer._pGold + Stash.gold`; `StoreAutoPlace(item,false)` dry-run then `TakePlrsMoney(price)` then persist placement; per-vendor removal: Smith premium → clear slot + `SpawnPremium`; Smith basic → erase from vector (shifts indices!); Witch → erase only if index ≥ 3 (first 3 pinned); Healer → erase only if index ≥ (multiplayer?3:2); Boy → clear BoyItem. After: reset hover, rebuild layout.
  - Sell flow (`CheckVisualStorePaste` via drop, `SellItemToVisualStore` from inventory): only Smith/Witch buy; `SmithWillBuy`/`WitchWillBuy` gate; price `GetSellPrice`; add gold, SFX `ItemGold`; paste path clears HoldItem and resets cursor to hand.
  - Repair: `GetRepairCost` (0 if empty/full/indestructible; magic-identified formula `30*_iIvalue*due/(_iMaxDur*100*2)` else `max(_ivalue*due/(_iMaxDur*2), 1)`); `VisualStoreRepairAll` sums body+inventory costs, checks `PlayerCanAfford` (silently returns if not — note empty if-body), takes money, sets `_iDurability=_iMaxDur` for non-indestructible, SFX, `CalcPlrInv(true)`; `VisualStoreRepair` sets `CURSOR_REPAIR` cursor; `VisualStoreRepairItem(invIndex)` resolves body vs inventory index ranges, charges and repairs one item.
  - Draw: panel sprite at Stash panel position; tab buttons with up/down sprite frame indexed by `(activeTab != Basic)` etc.; two-pass grid draw (slot backs then sprites with hover outline); total gold string `"Gold: N"` at `{20,320}` w280 h13; repair-all/repair-single button sprites for Smith.
  - Hover info (`CheckVisualStoreHLight`): buttons first (only when not holding an item; non-tab vendors only expose Basic button); per-button InfoString/FloatingInfoString/AddInfoBoxString pairs (duplicated with `true` flag); repair-all shows total cost or "Nothing to repair"; grid items show name, color (red if can't afford, else item color), details/durability, price `"N Gold"`.
  - Button press/release: press records id, release triggers tab switch / repair actions if still over the button; skip non-Basic tabs when vendor lacks tabs.

  - `GetRepairCost` formulas exact (lines ~341–352); `30 * _iIvalue * due / (_iMaxDur * 100 * 2)`, `max(_ivalue*due/(_iMaxDur*2), 1)`.
  - Witch pinned = first 3; Healer pinned = first 3 MP / first 2 SP (lines ~764–775).
  - Buy affordability: `totalGold < uint32(price)` → silent return (commented-out messages).
  - Text: "Basic", "Premium", "Misc", "Gold: ", "Repair All", "Repair", "Nothing to repair", "Repair a single item", "Basic items", "Premium items", "Miscellaneous items" (translated).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: layout depends on vendor item vector order (Smith basic erase shifts indices — hover index invalid after purchase, hence immediate relayout); globals mirror stash pattern; `VisualStoreButtonPressed` file-static; pages rebuilt on every tab switch/open/purchase.

### Source/sha.cpp
- Purpose: Implements Diablo's broken "X-SHA-1": a single-block (16 uint32) hash with SHA-1-style rounds but a *buggy* rotate that sign-extends (arithmetic shift), message schedule of only 16→80 words from the raw 16-word buffer, and no length padding. Used by codec.cpp for save/MPQ-style auth.
- Public API: (internal anon-ns) `SHA1CircularShift`, `SHA1ProcessMessageBlock`; exported `SHA1Result`, `SHA1Calculate`.
- Depends on: `SHA1Context`, `BlockSize=16`, `SHA1HashSize=5` from sha.h; `<cstring>` memcpy.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `SHA1Result(ctx, out [5]uint32)`: copies ctx.state (sha.cpp:71-74).
  - `SHA1Calculate(ctx, data [16]uint32)`: memcpy data→ctx.buffer then process one block (sha.cpp:76-80). NOT incremental streaming — whole 64-byte block per call, state persists across calls.
  - ProcessMessageBlock: w[0..15] = buffer (raw uint32 copy, host-endian memcpy — on LE machines this byte-swaps relative to big-endian SHA-1; Go port must memcpy LE semantics, i.e. `binary.LittleEndian` on LE targets; x86 original is LE so use LittleEndian for 1:1); w[i] = w[i-16]^w[i-14]^w[i-8]^w[i-3] for i=16..79 (sha.cpp:29-32).
  - Rounds with constants 0x5A827999 / 0x6ED9EBA1 / 0x8F1BBCDC / 0xCA62C1D6 and f-functions (b&c)|(~b&d), b^c^d, majority, b^c^d; rotate amounts 5 and 30 (sha.cpp:43-66).
  - Critical bug to reproduce: SHA1CircularShift (sha.cpp:18-23): if bit31 of word set, result = (0xFFFFFFFF << bits) | (word >> (32-bits)) — sets HIGH bits to 1 (this is the sign-extending rotate of the original). Must reproduce exactly or hashes won't match codec.cpp expectations.
  - State init constants {0x67452301, 0xEFCDAB89, 0x98BADCFE, 0x10325476, 0xC3D2E1F0} are in sha.h struct default.
- 1:1 constraints: all constants above; message-schedule taps (16,14,8,3); 4×20-round structure; state added (not replaced) at end (sha.cpp:68-72... lines 67-72); buffer copy is a full 64-byte memcpy per Calculate call. `bits` for shift is 5 or 30 only.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure computation; no globals; context is caller-owned. Safe.
- Test coverage: test/codec_test.cpp exercises codec (which uses sha.h API via Source/codec.cpp); no direct sha_test found, but hash vectors are transitively covered by codec tests.
- Go mapping: pkg/mpq or internal/security — `SHA1Calculate/SHA1Result` with explicit LittleEndian word load; keep exact buggy rotate.
- Risks/open questions: verify endianness assumption — memcpy into uint32 array means host-endian; original targets LE, so encode LE in Go for byte-exact behavior.

# vol3-041.md

# Volume III — batch 041

### Source/storm/storm_net.cpp
- Purpose: Storm networking shim — every SNet* entry point delegates to a single `dvlnet::abstract_net` instance (`dvlnet_inst`), serialized under a mutex (unless NONET), plus devilutionX extensions (DvlNet_* lobby/password/latency helpers).
- Public API: `SNetReceiveMessage(uint8_t*, void**, size_t*)`, `SNetSendMessage(uint8_t, void*, size_t)`, `SNetReceiveTurns(int, char**, size_t*, uint32_t*)`, `SNetSendTurn(char*, size_t)`, `SNetGetProviderCaps(_SNETCAPS*)`, `SNetUnregisterEventHandler(event_type)`, `SNetRegisterEventHandler(event_type, SEVTHANDLER)`, `SNetDestroy()`, `SNetDropPlayer(uint8_t, leaveinfo_t)`, `SNetLeaveGame(leaveinfo_t)`, `SNetInitializeProvider(uint32_t, GameData*)`, `SNetCreateGame(const char*, const char*, char*, int, int*)`, `SNetJoinGame(char*, char*, int*)`, `SNetGetOwnerTurnsWaiting(uint32_t*)`, `SNetGetTurnsInTransit(uint32_t*)`, `SNetSetBasePlayer(int)` (always true), `DvlNet_ProcessNetworkPackets()`, `DvlNet_SendInfoRequest()`, `DvlNet_ClearGamelist()`, `DvlNet_GetGamelist() -> vector<GameInfo>`, `DvlNet_SetPassword(string)`, `DvlNet_ClearPassword()`, `DvlNet_IsPublicGame() -> bool`, `DvlNet_GetLatencies(uint8_t) -> DvlNetLatencies`.
- Depends on: `net::abstract_net::MakeNet` (dvlnet/abstract_net.h); `MAX_PLRS`, `GameName`, `GamePassword`, `GameInfo`, `FormatGameSeed`, `provider`, `IsLoopback` (multi.h); `mainmenu_select_hero_dialog` (menu.h); `HeadlessMode` (headless_mode.hpp); `demo::IsRunning` (engine/demomode.h); `LogInfo` (utils/log.hpp); `SdlMutex` (utils/sdl_mutex.h); `UNIMPLEMENTED`/`ABORT` (utils/stubs.h); `ConnectionNames[]` (declared in storm_net.hpp, defined in dvlnet).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package-level singleton `dvlnetInst` of an `AbstractNet` interface + package-level `gameIsPublic bool`.
  - Every public function takes the same lock (`stormNetMutex`) around the call — exact semantics: lock exists only when networking is compiled in (Go: always exists, singleplayer loopback provider returns no-op behavior).
  - `SNetReceiveTurns` must enforce `arraysize == MAX_PLRS` and panic/UNIMPLEMENTED otherwise (line 57).
  - `SNetDestroy`/`SNetUnregisterEventHandler`/`SNetLeaveGame` must tolerate nil instance (lines 84–85, 101–102, 118–119: return true).
  - `SNetInitializeProvider`: create net via `MakeNet(provider)`, then success = `HeadlessMode && !demo.IsRunning()` OR `mainmenu_select_hero_dialog(gameData)` (line 141).
  - `SNetCreateGame`: abort if `gameTemplateSize != sizeof(GameData)`; copy template bytes to `setup_gameinfo`; default game name from `make_default_gamename()` when null; set global GameName; set/clear password; `create(name)` returns -1 → false; write playerID; log "Created {public|private} {provider} multiplayer game '{UPPERNAME}' (player id: {id}, seed: {seed|unavailable})" — only when `!IsLoopback` (line 172).
  - `SNetJoinGame`: same password/name handling; `join(name)` → id or fail; no join log here (deferred to NetInit).
  - `SNetSetBasePlayer`: ignore arg, return true (doc: engine calls once with 1).
  - `DvlNet_SetPassword` sets `GameIsPublic=false` + stores pw + `setup_password`; `DvlNet_ClearPassword` sets `GameIsPublic=true` + clears + `clear_password`.
  - Game-name uppercasing via `::toupper` per char for the log strings (lines 122, 174).
- 1:1 constraints: none — pure delegation; only logic values: `SNetSetBasePlayer` returns true unconditionally (line 230–235); `SNetDestroy` returns true after nulling instance (line 101–102); `SNetInitializeProvider` return expression line 141 `return (HeadlessMode && !demo::IsRunning()) || mainmenu_select_hero_dialog(gameData);`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `dvlnet_inst` mutable global; every API call serialized by `storm_net_mutex` (NONET builds omit lock entirely); `GameIsPublic` written by DvlNet_* without extra locking (protected by same mutex since those don't take it — in Go, wrap DvlNet_* in same mutex for safety).
- Test coverage: test/multi_logging_test.cpp exercises related logging; no direct storm_net test found.
- Go mapping: pkg/storm (or internal/net) — thin facade over internal/dvlnet `AbstractNet` interface; keep function-for-function.
- Risks/open questions: `SNetLeaveGame` logs before checking `dvlnet_inst == nullptr` — potential nil deref if called before init (upstream behavior; replicate order exactly or guard — verify callers).

### Source/storm/storm_net.hpp

### Source/storm/storm_svid.cpp
- Purpose: Smacker (.SMK) fullscreen video player for intro/cinematics — opens asset, decodes frames to an 8-bit indexed surface, scales/blits to output, streams audio, manages frame pacing in SMK time units, restores renderer/window state on end.
- Public API: `SVidPlayBegin(const char *filename, int flags) -> bool`; `SVidPlayContinue() -> bool` (returns false when playback finished); `SVidPlayEnd()`; `SVidMute()`; `SVidUnmute()`.
- Depends on: `Smacker*` API (SmackerDecoder.h — third-party); `OpenAssetAsSdlRwOps` (engine/assets.hpp); `GetOutputSurface`, `renderer`, `texture`, `gnScreenWidth/Height`, `ghMainWnd`, `ErrSdl`, `GetNearestDisplayMode`, `SetVideoModeToPrimary`, `IsFullScreen`, `diablo_is_focused` (engine/dx.h, utils/display.h); `sound_stop` (engine/sound.h); `GetOptions().Audio.soundVolume`, `VOLUME_MIN` (options.h); Aulib stream/decoder or SDL3 audio stream; `SDLWrap::*`, `SDLC_*` helpers.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Smacker decoder in Go (pkg/smk or equivalent) exposing: Open(rw), GetCurrentFrameNum, GetNumFrames, Rewind, GetNextFrame, GetFrame(buf), GetFrameSize(w,h), GetFrameRate, GetPalette(768B), DidPaletteChange, GetAudioTrackDetails(track0), GetAudioData(track0, buf16), Close.
  - Frame buffer W*H 8-bit palette indices; palette = 256*3 bytes → RGBA; surface pitch = width.
  - Blit paths: renderer-texture path (logical presentation W×H, integer-scaling option chooses INTEGER_SCALE vs LETTERBOX), else direct surface blit with aspect-fit rect: landscape-fit → w=dstW, h=srcH*dstW/srcW else w=srcW*dstH/srcH, h=dstH; centered `x=(dstW-w)/2`, `y=(dstH-h)/2`; no scaling when output indexed or exact size; else convert format then scaled blit.
  - Audio: track 0 only; buffer of `idealBufferSize/2` int16 (line 378); push per continue-call gated by ShouldPushAudioData (SDL3: stream exists && auto-enabled(focused); SDL2: stream isPlaying); 8-bit depth pushes bytes, 16-bit pushes len/2 samples; volume = (soundVolume - VOLUME_MIN)/-VOLUME_MIN (line 155); mute when window unfocused at begin; `sound_stop()` before audio init.
  - Loop semantics: at last frame, rewind if SVidLoop else stop (SVidLoadNextFrame, rewind at lines 170–174); skip both video+audio when behind schedule before audio push, skip video-only when behind after audio push.
  - SVidPlayEnd: destroy audio stream/device, close smacker, free buffers, then RECREATE main texture at gnScreenWidth×gnScreenHeight and restore logical presentation / display mode / (SDL1) primary video mode.
  - Ebiten mapping: draw 8-bit indices through a Go palette to *image.NRGBA via Ebiten texture; scale via DrawImageOptions with filter nearest (source is pixel art; original uses LINEAR only for SDL3 scaled blit); audio via oto/beeep-agnostic player package with same push semantics.
- 1:1 constraints: `SmackerTimeUnit = 100` (SMK units per ms, line 60); `TimeMsToSmk(ms)=ms*100`, `TimeSmkToMs(t)=t/100` (lines 61–62); flags: reject `0x10000|0x20000000` (line 348), loop=`0x40000` (353), disable-audio=`0x1000000` (369); `SVidFrameLength = 100000 / Smacker_GetFrameRate()` (line 409); landscape-fit = `srcW*dstH > dstW*srcH` (line 86); frame end init `GetTicksSmk()+SVidFrameLength` (line 469); delay until frame end via `SDL_Delay(TimeSmkToMs(SVidFrameEnd-now))` (line 517); palette alpha opaque for non-SDL1; indexed-output branch keeps 1:1 size (lines 253–256).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: all state is file-static (SVidHandle, buffers, palette, frame timing); single-threaded by contract (called from main loop during cutscenes); timing is wall-clock (SDL ticks) — NOT deterministic; audio presence depends on focus; Go port should keep wall-clock pacing, no RNG.
- Test coverage: none found (no test references SVid).
- Go mapping: internal/cinematic (or internal/video/smk) — player struct with Begin/Continue/End/Mute/Unmute; needs pkg/smk decoder dependency.
- Risks/open questions: SmackerDecoder library must be ported/vendored for Go (largest effort); SDL3-specific audio stream gain/mute semantics need an oto equivalent; the exact per-frame audio push cadence (once per Continue call) affects audio buffer underruns — must match.

### Source/sync.cpp
- Purpose: Builds and applies CMD_SYNCDATA packets: per-game-tick serializes the "most important" monsters (LRU/priority heuristics), one ground item, and one own body-equipment slot into `TSyncHeader`+N×`TSyncMonster`; receives peer sync data and reconciles local monster positions/hitpoints via walk/teleport-stand logic.
- Public API: `size_t sync_all_monsters(std::byte *pbBuf, size_t dwMaxLen)`; `size_t OnSyncData(const TSyncHeader &header, size_t maxCmdSize, const Player &player)`; `void sync_init()`.
- Depends on: `ActiveMonsters/ActiveMonsterCount/Monsters/Monster/MonsterMode/M_ClearSquares/Walk/M_StartStand/DirOK/encode_enemy/decode_enemy/MaxMonsters` (monster.h, monsters/*); `MyPlayer/MyPlayerId/NUM_INVLOC/InvBody` (player.h); `Items/ActiveItems/ActiveItemCount/Item fields, IDI_EAR, IDI_GOLD, ICURS_EAR_SORCERER` (items.h); `dMonster, InDungeonBounds` (levels/gendung.h); `ChangeLightXY, NO_LIGHT` (lighting.h); `IsEnemyIdValid/IsEnemyValid` (monsters/validation.hpp); `Swap16LE/Swap32LE` (utils/endian_swap.hpp); `TSyncHeader/TSyncMonster/CMD_SYNCDATA/ValidateCmdSize/gbBufferMsgs/delta_sync_monster/GetLevelForMultiplayer/IsValidLevelForMultiplayer` (msg.h); `GetDirection, Point, ManhattanDistance, WalkingDistance` (engine/point etc. via monster.h chain).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - State: `sgnMonsterPriority [MaxMonsters]uint16`, `sgnMonsters size_t`, `sgwLRU [MaxMonsters]uint16`, `sgnSyncItem, sgnSyncPInv int`.
  - sync_all_monsters: bail (return dwMaxLen untouched) when no active monsters, buffer < header+1 monster, or `MyPlayer._pLvlChanging`; write `bCmd=CMD_SYNCDATA` (line 249), `bLevel=GetLevelForMultiplayer(MyPlayer)`, `wLen` counts monster bytes; first 2 monsters chosen by SyncMonsterActive2 (round-robin cursor `sgnMonsters` starting at `16*MyPlayerId`, gate `if (i < 2)` line 259), remaining by SyncMonsterActive (lowest priority among non-LRU-exhausted); header item/inv fields via SyncPlrInv; final `wLen = Swap16LE` (line 272).
  - SyncPlrInv: `bItemI=-1` default; round-robin one active item index (`sgnSyncItem` wrap); EAR special packing from `_iIName[0..15]` chars exactly as coded; gold packs `wItemVal=ivalue` only for IDI_GOLD; `bPInvLoc=-1` default, packs one InvBody slot per call cycling `sgnSyncPInv` 0..NUM_INVLOC-1 (assert bounds).
  - OnSyncData: validate size (`ValidateCmdSize(wLen+sizeof(header),...)` fail → return maxCmdSize); if `gbBufferMsgs==1` or sender is MyPlayer → return consumed size without applying; owner = `player.getId() > MyPlayerId`; per-monster validity (id<MaxMonsters, InDungeonBounds, IsEnemyIdValid) then local-level gate (`!_pLvlChanging && level match`) applies enemy validity + SyncMonster; always `delta_sync_monster(monsterSync, level)` when level valid for MP.
  - SyncMonster: skip dead/Death-mode; if active locally, compute clamped Manhattan delta and return early when peer's info is "better" (`delta < _mdelta` or equal-and-isOwner) or `position.future == target`; skip Charge/Petrified; WalkingDistance ≤ 2 → face target, DirOK → M_ClearSquares, occupyTile(false), Walk, activeForTicks=255; else if dMonster[target]==0 → clear squares, occupy target, set tile, move light, decode enemy, M_StartStand toward enemyPosition, activeForTicks=255; finally decode_enemy + `whoHit |= mWhoHit`.
  - sync_init: `sgnMonsters = 16*MyPlayerId`, `memset(sgwLRU, 255, ...)` (i.e., all 0xFFFF... note: memset with byte 255 fills uint16 with 0xFFFF).
- 1:1 constraints: constants: `0x1000` priority bump for inactive monsters (line 35); LRU sentinels `sgnMonsterPriority=0xFFFF`, `sgwLRU = activeForTicks==0 ? 0xFFFF : 0xFFFE` (lines 53–54); selection thresholds `sgwLRU[m] < 0xFFFE` (line 64) and `< 0xFFFE` with start lru 0xFFFE in Active2 (lines 81–85); `_mdelta` clamp to 255 (line 51); byte order: all multi-byte fields via Swap16LE/Swap32LE (lines 52, 118–133, 273); EAR packing formulas (lines 117–125): `wItemCI=(IName[0]<<8)|IName[1]`, `dwItemSeed=(IName[2]<<24)|(IName[3]<<16)|(IName[4]<<8)|IName[5]`, `wItemVal=(IName[11]<<8)|((iCurs-ICURS_EAR_SORCERER)<<6)|ivalue`, `dwItemBuff=(IName[12]<<24)|(IName[13]<<16)|(IName[14]<<8)|IName[15]`; `activeForTicks = 255` (uint8 max, lines 191, 203); `sync_init` seed `16*MyPlayerId` (line 322); header layout must match `TSyncHeader` (msg.h: bCmd,bLevel,wLen,bItemI,bItemX,bItemY,wItemIndx,wItemCI,dwItemSeed,bItemId,bItemDur,bItemMDur,bItemCh,bItemMCh,wItemVal,dwItemBuff,bPInvLoc,wPInvIndx,wPInvCI,dwPInvSeed,bPInvId — 32 bytes with padding per C++ layout) and `TSyncMonster` (mndx,mx,my,menemy,mdelta,_mhitpoints int32 → 12 bytes w/ packing).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable file-static LRU/priority state drives WHICH monsters get synced — order of ActiveMonsters iteration matters for byte-identical output; per-tick coupling: called each game tick from msg loop; not thread-safe (main thread only); `sync_init` depends on MyPlayerId at game start.
- Test coverage: none found in test/ for sync_all_monsters/OnSyncData (indirect coverage via timedemo/multi tests absent).
- Go mapping: internal/net/sync (or internal/game/syncmsg) — pure functions over byte buffers using encoding/binary LittleEndian; structs TSyncHeader/TSyncMonster with exact fixed layout (use explicit uint8/int32 fields, no compiler padding — Go structs are compact by default; C++ padding: TSyncMonster is packed to 12 via #pragma presumably — verify against msg.h packing).
- Risks/open questions: C++ struct padding of TSyncHeader (offsets depend on packing macros in msg.h) must be replicated exactly or cross-version MP breaks; `sgnSyncPInv` starts 0 and is NOT reset by sync_init (only in zero-init) — preserve.

### Source/tables/itemdat.cpp
- Purpose: Loads all item-related data tables from TSV data files (base items, unique items, prefixes, suffixes) into global vectors/maps, with string→enum parsers for every field, mapping-ID registration for save compatibility, and Lua event hooks.
- Public API: globals `std::vector<ItemData> AllItemsList`, `map<int32_t,int16_t> ItemMappingIdsToIndices`, `map<string,int8_t> AdditionalUniqueBaseItemStringsToIndices`, `std::vector<UniqueItem> UniqueItems`, `map<int32_t,int32_t> UniqueItemMappingIdsToIndices`, `std::vector<PLStruct> ItemPrefixes`, `std::vector<PLStruct> ItemSuffixes`; `ParseItemId(string_view) -> expected<_item_indexes,string>`; `LoadItemDatFromFile(DataFile&, string_view filename, int32_t baseMappingId)`; `LoadUniqueItemDatFromFile(...)`; `LoadItemData()`; `ItemTypeToString(ItemType) -> string_view`.
- Depends on: magic_enum (enum_cast for _item_indexes); `DataFile/RecordReader/DataFileRecord` (data/file.hpp, data/record_reader.hpp); `ParseSpellId` (tables/spelldat.h); `lua::ItemDataLoaded/UniqueItemDataLoaded` (lua/lua_event.hpp); `DisplayFatalErrorAndExit` (appfat.h); `ParseInt` (utils/str_cat.hpp); ItemData/PLStruct/UniqueItem + all enums from itemdat.h; TSV assets `txtdata\items\itemdat.tsv`, `unique_itemdat.tsv`, `item_prefixes.tsv`, `item_suffixes.tsv`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package-level slices/maps mirroring the globals; loaded from the same TSV files (embed or read from mpq/unpacked dir).
  - Parse functions for: item class (None/Weapon/Armor/Misc/Gold/Quest), equip type (8 names), cursor graphic (~200 names + numeric fallback: empty string→ICURS_DEFAULT; bare number parsed as uint8 frame), item type (14 names), unique base item (~70 names + extension map + auto-add `ParseOrAddUniqueBaseItem` allocating indices NUM_DEFAULT_UITYPES.. up to NUM_MAX_UITYPES=127 with error when full), special effects (26 flag names), misc id (~48 names), effect type (IPL_* ~80 names), affix item type flags (6 names), alignment (Any/Evil/Good).
  - LoadItemDatFromFile: skip header; per record skip first column (item ID string), read 21 named fields in order (dropRate, class, equipType, cursorGraphic, itemType, uniqueBaseItem, name, shortName, minMonsterLevel, durability, minDamage, maxDamage, minArmor, maxArmor, minStrength, minMagic, minDexterity, specialEffects(list), miscId, spell, usable, value); assign `iMappingId = baseMappingId + record#`; register in ItemMappingIdsToIndices; duplicate mapping ID → fatal error+exit.
  - LoadItemDat: clears AllItemsList, extension map, mapping map; loads with baseMappingId 0; fires Lua ItemDataLoaded.
  - Unique items: fields name, cursorGraphic, uniqueBaseItem, minLevel, value, then up to 6 powers (power{type,value1,value2} — stops at first empty value cell); mapping IDs sequential from base; Lua UniqueItemDataLoaded.
  - Affixes (prefix+suffix, same loader): name, power(type+optional value1/value2), minLevel, itemTypes(list), alignment, chance, useful, minVal, maxVal, multVal.
  - ItemTypeToString: exact 14-string mapping + "" fallback.
- 1:1 constraints: TSV column names exactly as in reader.read* calls (lines 578–600, 645–663, 693–707); mapping ID = base + record index, first failure message strings "An item already exists for mapping ID {}." / "A unique item already exists for mapping ID {}."; file paths `txtdata\items\itemdat.tsv` etc. (lines 616, 674, 714–715); NUM_MAX_UITYPES = int8 max = 127 (itemdat.h line 382); ParseOrAddUniqueBaseItem new index = NUM_DEFAULT_UITYPES + extension-count (line 369); cursor-graphic numeric fallback path (lines 256–258); powers loop `i < 6` with break on `reader.value().empty()` (line 653).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: globals populated at startup before gameplay; load order LoadItemDat→LoadUniqueItemDat→prefixes→suffixes; Lua hooks may mutate further (modding); no locking — read-only after load.
- Test coverage: test/items_test.cpp, test/pack_test.cpp, test/inv_test.cpp use AllItemsList/LoadItemData ( indirectly via fixtures).
- Go mapping: internal/data/items — loader + types; TSV parsing shared with other tables packages via internal/datafile; keep maps keyed exactly (int32→int16 etc.).
- Risks/open questions: `IDI_BOOK1 = 114` etc. in _item_indexes have gaps (enum values pinned: BOOK1=114, BARBARIAN=139, SHORT_BATTLE_BOW=148, RUNEOFSTONE=165) — magic_enum range custom [IDI_NONE, IDI_NUM_DEFAULT_ITEMS]; Go needs the same numeric pins for save-game enum identity via ParseItemId string match; verify actual TSV row count matches IDI_NUM_DEFAULT_ITEMS.

- Purpose: Loads missile data tables from TSV (sprite metadata with deduplicated 16-entry anim delay/length arrays, and per-missile-ID behavior data binding add/process function pointers, sounds, graphics, flags), and manages missile graphic loading/freeing.
- Public API: `MissileFileData::animDelay(uint8 dir)`, `MissileFileData::animLen(uint8 dir)`, `MissileFileData::LoadGFX() -> expected<void,string>`, `GetMissileSpriteData(MissileGraphicID) -> MissileFileData&`, `LoadMissileData()`, `GetMissileData(MissileID) -> const MissileData&`, `InitMissileGFX() -> expected<void,string>`, `FreeMissileGFX()`.
- Depends on: DataFile/RecordReader; `AddMissile*`/`ProcessMissile*` function set (~78 add fns, ~49 process fns) from missiles.h; `SfxID` names (sound_effect_enums.h); CL2/CLX loaders `LoadCl2WithStatus`, `LoadMultipleCl2Sheet<16>`, `LoadClxListOrSheetWithStatus`, `OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet` (engine/clx_sprite.hpp, engine/load_cl2.hpp, load_clx.hpp); `MaxMpqPathSize`, `DEVILUTIONX_CL2_EXT` (mpq/mpq_common.hpp); `FileNameGenerator` (utils/file_name_generator.hpp); `HeadlessMode`; `MissileID::LastDiablo/LAST` (missiles.h).

  - Tables: `MissileSpriteData []MissileFileData`, `MissileAnimDelays/MissileAnimLengths [][]byte` (16 entries each), `MissilesData []MissileData` — loaded from `txtdata\missiles\missile_sprites.tsv` and `txtdata\missiles\misdat.tsv`.
  - `ToIndex` dedup: linear search by full 16-array equality, append if missing — index stored as uint8 in MissileFileData (order-dependent dedup, must be deterministic given same TSV).
  - Parsers: MissileGraphicsFlag (empty/None, MonsterOwned, NotAnimated); MissileGraphicID (~59 names); MissileDataFlags (Physical/Fire/Lightning/Magic/Acid/Arrow/Invisible); movement distribution (empty→Disabled, Blockable, Unblockable); add-fn name→function map (~78 entries); process-fn name→function map (~49 entries); cast sound (28 names, subset); hit sound (6 names).
  - LoadGFX: skip if sprites loaded or name empty; UNPACKED_MPQS: load `missiles\{name}.clx`; else animFAmt==1 → single CL2 list `missiles\{name}`; else sheet `missiles\{name}\{i}.clx`-style via FileNameGenerator, 16 dirs, animFAmt files, width=animWidth.
  - InitMissileGFX: skip entirely in HeadlessMode; load all non-MonsterOwned sprites; FreeMissileGFX clears all.

### Source/tables/monstdat.cpp

- Test coverage: test/pack_test.cpp, player_test.cpp, timedemo_test.cpp reference MonstersData; monstConvTbl consumed by drlg code.
