# Volume III — batch 042

### Source/tables/objdat.cpp
- Purpose: Loads per-object-ID data (`AllObjects`), the dun_object_id→object_id mapping table (`ObjTypeConv`), and the deduplicated CEL-file list (`ObjMasterLoadList`) from `txtdata\objects\objdat.tsv`.
- Public API: `const _object_id ObjTypeConv[]`; `std::vector<ObjectData> AllObjects`; `std::vector<std::string> ObjMasterLoadList`; `void LoadObjectData()`.
- Depends on: `tables/objdat.h` (this pair); `data/file.hpp` (`DataFile::loadOrDie`, `skipHeaderOrDie`), `data/iterators.hpp` (`DataFileRecord`), `data/record_reader.hpp` (`RecordReader` with `readString/readInt/read/readEnumList/advance`); `levels/parse_dungeon_type.hpp` (`ParseDungeonType`); enum values `theme_id`/`quest_id`/`_object_id` from objdat.h/questdat.hpp; `ankerl::unordered_dense::map`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Hard-code `ObjTypeConv` as a 160-entry array mapping DUN object indices to `_object_id` values (many `OBJ_NULL`); order is behavioral.
  - `LoadObjectData()` must: clear both vectors, read each TSV record, dedupe the `file` column into `ObjMasterLoadList` assigning first-seen `uint8_t` ids (ofindex), then parse minlvl/maxlvl (int8), levelType via ParseDungeonType, theme/quest via string parsers, flags list, animDelay/animLen/animWidth, selectionRegion list.
  - Parse helpers: `ParseTheme` (empty→THEME_NONE, else 17 name match, else error), `ParseQuest` (empty→Q_INVALID, else 24 names), `ParseObjectDataFlags` (6 names: Animated, Solid, MissilesPassThrough, Light, Trap, Breakable), `ParseSelectionRegion` (Bottom, Middle, Top).
  - Post-load sanity: `OBJ_LAST+1 == len(AllObjects)` assert; shrink vectors.
  - All parse failures must be fatal (loadOrDie / record-reader error reporting).
- 1:1 constraints: ObjTypeConv values in exact file order, lines 16–176: [0]=OBJ_NULL, [1]=OBJ_LEVER, [2..3]=CRUX1..3, [5]=OBJ_ANGEL, [6..8]=BANNERL/M/R, [14..15]=BOOK2L/R, [16]=BCROSS, [18..20]=CANDLE1/2/O, [21]=CAULDRON, [30]=FLAMEHOLE, [36..37]=MCIRCLE1/2, [38]=SKFIRE, [39]=SKPILE, [40..44]=SKSTICK1..5, [51]=SWITCHSKL, [53..54]=TRAPL/TRAPR, [55..59]=TORTURE1..5, [65]=NUDEW2R, [70..76]=TNUDEM1..4,TNUDEW1..3, [77..85]=CHEST1×3,CHEST2×3,CHEST3×3, [91]=PEDESTAL, [103]=ALTBOY, [106..107]=WARARMOR/WARWEAP, [108..109]=TORCHR2/TORCHL2, [110]=MUSHPATCH, [111]=STAND, [112..113]=TORCHL/TORCHR, [114]=FLAMELVR, [115]=SARC, [116..117]=BARREL/BARRELEX, [118..120]=BOOKSHELF/BOOKCASEL/BOOKCASER, [121..122]=ARMORSTANDN/WEAPONRACKN, [123..125]=BLOODFTN/PURIFYINGFTN/SHRINEL, [126]=SHRINER, [127]=GOATSHRINE, [128..129]=MURKYFTN/TEARFTN, [130]=DECAP, [131..133]=TCHEST1..3, [134]=LAZSTAND, [135..136]=BOOKSTAND/BOOKSHELFR, [137..140]=POD/PODEX/URN/URNEX, [141..144]=L5BOOKS/L5CANDLE/L5LEVER/L5SARC; all unlisted indices OBJ_NULL. ParseTheme list (lines 87–105) and ParseQuest list (lines 108–136) must match name-for-name.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable global state (`AllObjects`, `ObjMasterLoadList`) mutated only by `LoadObjectData()` — call during data-load phase, not during play. No RNG, no tick coupling. `ankerl` map only affects dedupe order, not output order.
- Test coverage: none found (test/quests_test.cpp and test/tile_properties_test.cpp only include objdat.h for enum ids).
- Go mapping: `internal/tables` (or `internal/dungeon/objdata`); table `ObjTypeConv` as a Go array literal; loader using the shared Go TSV DataFile/RecordReader port; parse helpers as `func(string) (T, error)`.
- Risks/open questions: none (pure data load; TSV assets must ship with the Go port or values must be baked in).

### Source/tables/playerdat.cpp
- Purpose: Loads all per-class player data (class list, attributes, starting loadout, sprite widths, animation frame counts, hero sounds) and the experience-level threshold table from TSV files; exposes accessor functions.
- Public API: `LoadClassDatFromFile(DataFile&, std::string_view)`, `LoadPlayerDataFiles()`, `SfxID GetHeroSound(HeroClass, HeroSpeech)`, `uint32_t GetNextExperienceThresholdForLevel(unsigned)`, `uint8_t GetMaximumCharacterLevel()`, `size_t GetNumPlayerClasses()`, `const PlayerData& GetPlayerDataForClass(HeroClass)`, `const PlayerCombatData& GetPlayerCombatDataForClass(HeroClass)`, `const PlayerStartingLoadoutData& GetPlayerStartingLoadoutForClass(HeroClass)`, `const PlayerSpriteData& GetPlayerSpriteDataForClass(HeroClass)`, `const PlayerAnimData& GetPlayerAnimDataForClass(HeroClass)`, `const ClassAttributes& GetClassAttributes(HeroClass)`.
- Depends on: `tables/playerdat.hpp`; `data/file.hpp`, `data/record_reader.hpp` (RecordReader), `data/value_reader.hpp` (ValueReader: reads keyed values from single-row files); `items.h`/`tables/itemdat.h` (`_item_indexes`, ParseItemId); `tables/spelldat.h` (SpellID, `ParseSpellId`); `tables/textdat.h` (via header chain); `sound_effect_enums.h` (HeroSpeech, SfxID); `utils/format.hpp`, `utils/language.h` (`_()`, DisplayFatalErrorAndExit); `utils/str_cat.hpp`; `magic_enum` (enum_cast, enum_for_each, enum_name).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Global stores (populated by LoadPlayerDataFiles, indexed by HeroClass): `PlayersData`, `ClassAttributesPerClass`, `PlayersCombatData`, `PlayersStartingLoadoutData`, `PlayersSpriteData`, `PlayersAnimData`, `herosounds` (map[HeroSpeech]SfxID per class).
  - Experience table: `ReloadExperienceData()` parses `txtdata\Experience.tsv` with header-column mapping (Level, Experience columns, skip-length aware). Records whose Level field is the literal "MaxLevel" are skipped. Gaps fill with `math.MaxUint32` on resize (line 66) so ValidatePlayer won't reset XP.
  - `ExperienceData.getThresholdForLevel(level)`: 0 for level 0, else `levelThresholds[min(level-1, maxLevel)]`; `getMaxLevel()` = min(len, 255).
  - Per-class file set, all under `txtdata\classes\<folderName>\`: `attributes.tsv` (classFlags enum list via magic_enum-style parse, 8 stat ints, blockBonus→combat.baseToBlock, then 13 readDecimal fields into int16 attributes, 3 to-hit ints into combat), `starting_loadout.tsv` (skill, spell, spellLevel, items[0..4] each column `item0`..`item4`, gold), `sprites.tsv` (classPath, classChar, trn, 10 frame-width ints), `animations.tsv` (27 int8 frame/action-frame fields), `sounds.tsv` (one column per HeroSpeech enum name, parsed with ParseSfxId).
  - `LoadClassDat()`: clear PlayersData, load `txtdata\classes\classdat.tsv` (className, folderName, portrait, inv). `LoadClassDatFromFile` (public, used for testing/mods) appends without clearing and enforces max class count = 255 (HeroClass::NUM_MAX_CLASSES) with fatal error.
  - `LoadClassesAttributes()` clears all six per-class stores and iterates PlayersData loading the five per-class files in that fixed order.
  - `GetHeroSound` returns `SfxID::None` when the class/speech pair is absent.
  - All accessors index by `size_t(HeroClass)`; asserts bounds.
- 1:1 constraints: Experience column header names "Level"/"Experience" (lines 64–69); "MaxLevel" sentinel skip (lines 111–115); gap fill `uint32 max` (line 66); attributes.tsv field names and target fields in exact read order lines 165–198 (readDecimal → int16 division-free scaled values; ValueReader decimal semantics must be replicated — check data/value_reader.hpp in its own batch); starting_loadout items loop `item0..item4` (lines 209–212); sounds.tsv iterates `magic_enum::enum_for_each<HeroSpeech>` so every HeroSpeech name is a required column (lines 252–255); fatal-error strings use translation `_()`; file paths use backslash separators ("txtdata\\classes\\...").
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: anonymous-namespace `ExperienceData` instance is a mutable static global with `DVL_REINITIALIZES` clear(); loaders run at data-load time only. Load order matters: ReloadExperienceData → LoadClassDat → LoadClassesAttributes (LoadPlayerDataFiles, lines 361–366). No RNG.
- Test coverage: test/player_test.cpp (includes playerdat.hpp, calls LoadPlayerDataFiles at lines 92, 200); also pack_test, store_transaction_test, timedemo_test, ui_test.hpp, vendor_test, writehero_test reference player data APIs indirectly.
- Go mapping: `internal/tables/playerdat` (data + accessors) with the shared `internal/datafile` reader port; keep accessors returning slices indexed by class; experience table as []uint32 with same gap-fill semantics.
- Risks/open questions: readDecimal semantics (fixed-point? divisor 8?) live in data/value_reader.hpp — resolve in that file's batch before fixing Go field types.

# vol3-043.md

# Volume III — batch 043

### Source/tmsg.cpp
- Purpose: Timed message queue for network chat/command packets — messages are held for `gnTickDelay * 10` ms of real time before being handed back to the caller.
- Public API: `uint8_t tmsg_get(std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]> *msg)`; `void tmsg_add(const std::byte *msg, uint8_t len)`; `void tmsg_start()` (asserts queue empty); `void tmsg_cleanup()` (clears). Internal `struct TMsg { uint32_t time; unique_ptr<byte[]> body; uint8_t len; }`.
- Depends on: `gnTickDelay` (diablo.h — game logic ms per tick), `SDL_GetTicks()` (SDL2/SDL3 timer), `assert` (cassert implied).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - FIFO queue of `{deadline uint32, body []byte, len uint8}`; body copied on add (value semantics, ownership transfer on get).
  - `tmsg_get` returns 0 when queue empty OR when head's deadline not yet passed; otherwise pops head, transfers body to caller, returns length (len 0 is the "no message" sentinel — same encoding as C).
  - `tmsg_add` computes `deadline = now_ms + gnTickDelay*10`; appends at back.
  - `tmsg_start` must fail loudly (panic/error) if queue non-empty — mirrors `assert`.
  - `tmsg_cleanup` clears all entries.
- 1:1 constraints: expiry check is `(int)(head.time - SDL_GetTicks()) >= 0 → not ready` (line 46) — i.e. signed 32-bit wraparound-tolerant comparison; must be replicated with int32 arithmetic in Go, not unsigned compare. Delay = `SDL_GetTicks() + (gnTickDelay * 10)` (line 57). `len` is uint8 — max 255 bytes per message. Time base = real-time ms (SDL ticks), not game ticks.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Uses wall-clock (SDL_GetTicks) → messages expire in real time independent of game-logic determinism; no locking — caller must serialize get/add. Queue is a file-static mutable global.
- Test coverage: none found (no test/tmsg_test.cpp).
- Go mapping: `internal/net` (or `pkg/msgqueue`) — small `TimedMsgQueue` struct with `Get() ([]byte, uint8)` / `Add(b []byte)` / `Start()` / `Cleanup()`; inject clock func for testability.
- Risks/open questions: In devilutionX this is only used with dvnetsrv/loopback; confirm Go port actually needs it before porting (queue consumer is the message pump in multi.cpp).

### Source/track.cpp
- Purpose: Mouse/target tracking for gamepad/keyboard+mouse repeat actions: invalidates stale cursor targets and repeats the last player action while a button is held (attack/spell/object/walk).
- Public API: `void InvalidateTargets()`; `void RepeatPlayerAction()`; `bool track_isscrolling()` (= `LastPlayerAction == PlayerActionType::Walk`).
- Depends on: `cursPosition`, `pcurs`, `pcursmonst`, `ObjectUnderCursor`, `PlayerUnderCursor`, `sgbMouseDown` (cursor.h), `Monsters[]`, `MFLAG_HIDDEN` (monster.h via player.h), `IsTileLit` (lighting), `Players`/`MyPlayer`/`MyPlayerId`, `PM_STAND`/`PM_DEATH`/`PM_QUIT`/`AnimInfo.getFrameToUseForRendering()`/`isWalking()`/`GetTargetPosition()`/`destAction`/`ACTION_NONE`/`CanChangeAction()`/`_pInvincible`/`UsesRangedWeapon()`/`friendlyMode`/`SaySpecific` (player.h), `LastPlayerAction`/`PlayerActionType`/`UpdateSpellTarget`/`CheckPlrSpell` (controls/plrctrls.h), `ControllerActionHeld`/`GameActionType_NONE` (controls/game_controls.h), `ControlMode`/`ControlTypes` (controls/control_mode.hpp), `InDungeonBounds` (levels), `IsPlayerInStore` (stores.h), `NetSendCmdLoc`/`NetSendCmdParam1` + `CMD_WALKXY`/`CMD_RATTACKXY`/`CMD_SATTACKXY`/`CMD_RATTACKID`/`CMD_ATTACKID`/`CMD_RATTACKPID`/`CMD_ATTACKPID`/`CMD_OPOBJXY` (network commands).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `InvalidateTargets`: clear `pcursmonst` if monster invalid/no-life/`MFLAG_HIDDEN`/tile not lit; clear `ObjectUnderCursor` unless `canInteractWith()`; clear `PlayerUnderCursor` if target in DEATH/QUIT mode, inactive, not on active level, no life, or unlit tile.
  - `RepeatWalk` (private): only if cursor in dungeon bounds; skip if player mode != STAND and (not walking or render frame <= 6); skip if cursor == target position; else `NetSendCmdLoc(myPlayerId, true, CMD_WALKXY, cursPosition)`.
  - `RepeatPlayerAction`: gate on `pcurs == CURSOR_HAND`, `(sgbMouseDown != CLICK_NONE || ControllerActionHeld != NONE)`, not in store, `LastPlayerAction != None`, `destAction == ACTION_NONE`, not invincible, `CanChangeAction()`; then switch over PlayerActionType exactly as coded (Attack→SATTACKXY/RATTACKXY by cursor pos; AttackMonsterTarget→ATTACKID/RATTACKID by pcursmonst; AttackPlayerTarget→ATTACKPID/RATTACKPID if cursor player && !friendlyMode; Spell→non-KBM retarget via UpdateSpellTarget then CheckPlrSpell(KBM?); SpellMonsterTarget/SpellPlayerTarget→CheckPlrSpell(false); OperateObject→CMD_OPOBJXY only if object not a door; Walk→RepeatWalk).
- 1:1 constraints: walking-interlock constant `getFrameToUseForRendering() <= 6` (line ~21); distance/range checks via InDungeonBounds; ranged-vs-melee command chosen by `UsesRangedWeapon()`; attack-player gated on `!friendlyMode`; `track_isscrolling()` is exactly `LastPlayerAction == Walk`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Reads/writes cursor globals — must run on the UI/input thread in step with the game loop; no RNG; no serialization.
- Test coverage: none found (no test/track_test.cpp).
- Go mapping: `internal/input/track` (or internal/ui) — functions over the cursor/target globals; keep the exact gating order since it defines feel of hold-to-repeat.
- Risks/open questions: none — pure orchestration over existing subsystems; port depends on Player.AnimInfo render-frame accessor existing.

### Source/utils/aulib.hpp
- Purpose: Factory that constructs an Aulib (SDL audio) resampler for a sound stream when the source rate differs from the device rate; selects Speex or SDL resampler per audio options.

- Requirements for Go port: audio pipeline must resample decoded sound from source rate to output device rate when they differ; resampler choice (speex vs SDL-equivalent) and quality setting come from user options; when rates equal, no resampler. In Go/Ebiten, either use oto/ebiten audio with a Go resampler (e.g. beep resampler) honoring the same options, or resample at load time.

### Source/utils/cel_to_clx.cpp
- Purpose: Converts vanilla Diablo CEL sprite data to the CLX/CL2 format used by devilutionX at load time — handles single-group CELs and multi-group "CEL sheet" files, per-frame RLE transcoding.
- Public API: `OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet CelToClx(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, PointerOrValue<uint16_t> widthOrWidths)`.
- Depends on: `utils/cel_to_clx.hpp` (PointerOrValue, OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet from engine/clx_sprite.hpp), `utils/clx_encode.hpp` (`ClxFrameHeaderSize`, `AppendClxTransparentRun`, `AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun`), `utils/endian_read.hpp` (`LoadLE32`, `LoadLE16`), `utils/endian_write.hpp` (`WriteLE32`, `WriteLE16`), `appfat.h` (unused-fatal include), optional DEBUG_CEL_TO_CL2_SIZE stdout stats.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Parse CEL header: `maybeNumFrames = LE32(data[0])`; if `LE32(data[maybeNumFrames*4+4]) != size` then it's a group sheet: `numGroups = maybeNumFrames/4`, `groupsHeaderSize = maybeNumFrames`, skip that many bytes, output begins with group-offset table of same byte size.
  - Per group: read numFrames (or reuse maybeNumFrames when single group); write CL2 group header (numFrames, per-frame offsets, trailing group size); write group offset into sheet header when multi-group (`WriteLE32(cl2Data[4*group], cl2Data.size())` before appending group).
  - Per frame: frame offsets from CEL `LE32(data[4*(frame+1)])`; skip 10-byte CEL frame header if `LE16(src) == 10`; frame width = per-frame widths pointer entry [frame-1] or fixed value.
  - Write CLX frame header (LE16: header size, width; height backfilled after scan).
  - RLE transcode loop: while src != srcEnd, per "line" consume exactly frameWidth pixels: control byte val; if `val >= 0x80` it's transparent run of `-int8(val)` pixels (accumulate); else flush pending transparent run via AppendClxTransparentRun then AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun(src, val) and skip val pixels; subtract val from remaining width; increment frameHeight per line.
  - After frame: backfill height LE16 at frameHeaderPos+4; append trailing transparent run.
  - Return sheet/list: copy cl2Data to owned buffer; numGroups==1 → list (0), else sheet with numGroups.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Transparent control: `CelTransparentMin = 0x80`, transparent when `control >= 0x80`, run width = `-int8(control)` (lines 22–30).
  - CEL frame header size 10, detected via `LE16(src) == 10` (lines 81–84).
  - Reserve heuristic `size + 4445` — only file that grows is `data\hf_logo3.cel` by exactly 4445 bytes (lines 46–48) — informational; Go can use a growing buffer.
  - All multi-byte reads/writes little-endian (LE32/LE16).
  - Group detection invariant: `LE32(&data[maybeNumFrames*4 + 4]) == size` ⇒ plain CEL (single group) — the check indexes `4*(numFrames+1)` which is the last frame offset == file size.
  - CL2 group header layout: [numFrames:u32][frame offsets… numFrames+1 entries:u32] where last entry = group byte size; CLX frame header: {u16 headerSize, u16 width, u16 height}.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure function of input bytes; no RNG; no global state; deterministic output bit-for-bit — Go port should be golden-tested against C++ output.
- Test coverage: none found (no cel_to_clx test; exercised indirectly via load_cel in assets tests).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/clx` (converter) — `CelToClx(data []byte, widths WidthsOrValue) (OwnedClxListOrSheet, error)`; reuse ported clx_encode helpers; add golden tests with real .CEL assets.
- Risks/open questions: `PointerOrValue<uint16_t>` widths semantics (per-frame array vs single) must be ported faithfully; `AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun` internal RLE encoding (shared with cl2 encode) is defined in clx_encode.hpp — port together; no bounds checking exists in C++ (trusts asset), Go should validate to avoid panics on corrupt data.

### Source/utils/cl2_to_clx.cpp
- Purpose: Implements CL2→CLX conversion: parses CL2 group/frame headers, decodes CL2 run-control bytes, re-encodes runs as CLX, and builds the CLX file/group/frame header tables.
- Public API: `uint16_t Cl2ToClx(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, PointerOrValue<uint16_t> widthOrWidths, std::vector<uint8_t> &clxData)` (line 15) — returns number of lists in a sheet, 0 for a single list.
- Depends on: `utils/clx_decode.hpp` (IsClxOpaque, IsClxOpaqueFill, GetClxOpaqueFillWidth, GetClxOpaquePixelsWidth, GetSkipSize), `utils/clx_encode.hpp` (AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun, AppendClxTransparentRun, ClxFrameHeaderSize), `utils/endian_read.hpp` (LoadLE32/LoadLE16), `utils/endian_write.hpp` (WriteLE32/WriteLE16).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Detect single-list vs sheet: read first LE32 (`maybeNumFrames`, line 20); if `LoadLE32(&data[(maybeNumFrames*4) + 4]) != size` (line 23) then it's a sheet: `numGroups = maybeNumFrames / 4` (line 26) and `clxData.resize(maybeNumFrames)` (group-offset table of that byte size).
  - Per group: single-group case uses `groupBegin = data` and `numFrames = maybeNumFrames`; multi-group case reads group start `LoadLE32(&data[group*4])`, `numFrames = LoadLE32(groupBegin)`, writes group offset into CLX header at `clxData[4*group]` (lines 37-41).
  - CLX group header: resize for `4*(2+numFrames)` bytes (line 46); write frame count at `clxDataOffset` (line 47); per-frame relative offsets (`clxData.size() - clxDataOffset`, lines 51-53); last slot = group size (line 109).
  - Per frame: width from `widthOrWidths` (pointer → `widths[frame-1]`, value → fixed, line 57). Write CLX frame header (6 bytes): size=ClxFrameHeaderSize at +0 (line 61), width at +2 (line 62), height at +4 (line 106, written after decode).
  - Frame body decode: `src = frameBegin + LoadLE16(frameBegin)` (line 63) — CL2 frame begins with a uint16 skip value. Iterate control bytes while `src != frameEnd` (line 68), where `frameEnd = &groupBegin[LoadLE32(&groupBegin[4*(frame+1)])]` (line 56):
    - control < 0x80: transparent run of `control` px; flush pending pixels via AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun first; `transparentRunWidth += control; remainingWidth -= control`.
    - 0x80..0xBE: flush transparent run (AppendClxTransparentRun), then fill: `width = 0xBF - control`, one color byte follows; append width copies of color to pixels buffer; `remainingWidth -= width`.
    - else (0xBF..0xFF): flush transparent run; `width = -(int8_t)control` (1..65); copy next `width` bytes verbatim into pixels; `src += width`; `remainingWidth -= width`.
    - inner loop while `remainingWidth > 0` (line 70); after inner loop `GetSkipSize(remainingWidth, frameWidth)` (line 96) → `{wholeLines, xOffset}`, accumulate `frameHeight += wholeLines`, carry `xOffset`.
  - After loop: flush remaining pixels, then `AppendClxTransparentRun(transparentRunWidth)` (lines 101-104), then write `frameHeight` as LE16 at frameHeaderPos+4 (line 106).
  - `pixels` is a reusable scratch buffer reserved 4096 (line 32), cleared per flush — mirror for allocation behavior.
  - Return `numGroups == 1 ? 0 : numGroups` (line 111).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Sheet detection formula: `LoadLE32(&data[(maybeNumFrames*4)+4]) != size` → sheet with `numGroups = maybeNumFrames/4` (lines 23-27).
  - CLX group header size `4*(2+numFrames)` (line 46); frame offsets relative to `clxDataOffset` (lines 51-53).
  - Frame header: LE16 size=6 (line 61), LE16 width (line 62), LE16 height at +4 (line 106).
  - Transparent runs accumulate ACROSS skip lines until an opaque command or end-of-frame flush (lines 64-104); fill widths `0xBF - control`; pixel-run widths `-(int8_t)control` (via GetClx* helpers).
  - Group-size trailer: `clxData.size() - clxDataOffset` written at `clxDataOffset + 4*(1+numFrames)` (line 109).
  - All multi-byte reads/writes little-endian (LoadLE32/LoadLE16/WriteLE32/WriteLE16).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure function of inputs; scratch buffer is local. No globals.
- Test coverage: none found (no test/ file references Cl2ToClx).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/clx` — pure conversion func; reuse shared scratch via local slice; return (clxData []byte, numLists uint16).
- Risks/open questions: `remainingWidth` is int_fast16_t and can go negative (overrun semantics relied on by GetSkipSize); Go port must use int16/int with identical signed arithmetic. `frameHeight` is size_t summed from int_fast16_t wholeLines.

### Source/utils/clx_decode.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only CLX control-byte classification helpers and the line-skip arithmetic used by both decoder and renderer.
- Public API (all constexpr/inline in namespace devilution):
  - `constexpr bool IsClxOpaque(uint8_t control)` — `control >= ClxOpaqueMin` where `ClxOpaqueMin = 0x80` (lines 10-13).
  - `constexpr uint8_t GetClxOpaquePixelsWidth(uint8_t control)` — `width = -static_cast<int8_t>(control)`, DVL_ASSUME 1..65 (lines 16-21).
  - `constexpr bool IsClxOpaqueFill(uint8_t control)` — `control <= ClxFillMax` where `ClxFillMax = 0xBE` (lines 24-27); requires IsClxOpaque first.
  - `constexpr uint8_t GetClxOpaqueFillWidth(uint8_t control)` — `width = ClxFillEnd - control` where `ClxFillEnd = 0xBF`, assumed 1..63 (lines 29-34).
  - `struct SkipSize { int_fast16_t wholeLines; int_fast16_t xOffset; };` (line 37).
  - `DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE SkipSize GetSkipSize(int_fast16_t remainingWidth, int_fast16_t srcWidth)` (line 46) — requires remainingWidth <= 0; if 0 → `{1, 0}` (line 54); else `overrun = -remainingWidth` (unsigned), `overrunLines = overrun/srcWidth + 1` (line 57), `xOffset = overrun % srcWidth` (line 58).
- Depends on: `appfat.h`, `utils/attributes.h` (DVL_ASSUME, DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE) — macro-only, no runtime deps.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package-level funcs: IsClxOpaque, GetClxOpaquePixelsWidth, IsClxOpaqueFill, GetClxOpaqueFillWidth, GetSkipSize(remainingWidth, srcWidth int16) (wholeLines, xOffset int16).
  - Exact width semantics: pixel-run control 0xC0..0xFF encodes width 65..1 (two's complement of int8); fill control 0x80..0xBE encodes width 63..1 via 0xBF-control; 0xBF is the 65-wide pixel run.
  - GetSkipSize must replicate the overrun→line-advance math for commands that exceed the line width (used when a run crosses scanline boundaries).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `ClxOpaqueMin = 0x80` (line 11), `ClxFillMax = 0xBE` (line 25), `ClxFillEnd = 0xBF` (line 31).
  - GetSkipSize formulas (lines 54-58): zero-overrun fast path `{1,0}`; `overrunLines = overrun/srcWidth + 1`, `xOffset = overrun % srcWidth` with unsigned intermediate math.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure functions; stateless.
- Test coverage: none found (helpers exercised indirectly by clx_render_benchmark.cpp rendering path).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/clx` — small pure helper file; heavily inlined in hot render loops, keep unexported if only used in-package but exported for tests.
- Risks/open questions: unsigned intermediate (`uint_fast16_t`) in GetSkipSize — with valid inputs overrun ≥ 1 and srcWidth ≥ 1 so no division-by-zero; Go must guard srcWidth==0 defensively.

### Source/utils/clx_encode.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only CLX encoder primitives: transparent-run, fill-run, pixels-run emitters and the pixels-vs-fill RLE optimizer.
- Public API (inline, namespace devilution):
  - `constexpr size_t ClxFrameHeaderSize = 6;` (line 18).
  - `inline void AppendClxTransparentRun(unsigned width, std::vector<uint8_t> &out)` (lines 20-29) — emits 0x7F bytes while width ≥ 0x7F (lines 22-25) then final `width` byte (line 28).
  - `inline void AppendClxFillRun(uint8_t color, unsigned width, std::vector<uint8_t> &out)` (lines 31-42) — emits `0x80,color` while width ≥ 0x3F (lines 33-37) then `0xBF-width, color` (lines 40-41).
  - `inline void AppendClxPixelsRun(const uint8_t *src, unsigned width, std::vector<uint8_t> &out)` (lines 44-58) — while width ≥ 0x41: `0xBF` + 0x41 literal bytes (lines 46-52); remainder: `256-width` (== 0x100-width truncated to u8) + width literals (lines 55-57).
  - `inline void AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun(const uint8_t *src, size_t length, std::vector<uint8_t> &out)` (lines 60-95) — scans run, splits into fill runs when a repeated color reaches MinFillRunLength.
- Depends on: nothing beyond `<cstdint>`, `<cstddef>`, `<vector>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Byte-exact emitters appending to a `*[]byte`/bytes.Buffer: transparent runs chunked at 0x7F, fill at 0x3F, pixel runs at 0x41.
  - Optimizer logic: track prevColor run; on color change, if `prevColorRunLength >= MinFillRunLength` (=3, line 73), emit pixels-run for the non-fill prefix then fill-run, reset begin; at end use threshold 2 (line 89) — final run abuts transparency (comment lines 86-88: width-2 fill is 2 bytes vs 3 for pixels).
  - Empty-length input: `prevColorRunLength` initialized to 1 and `*src++` read unconditionally (lines 64-66) — caller (cl2_to_clx.cpp) only invokes with non-empty pixels; Go should guard len==0.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Chunk sizes: transparent 0x7F (line 22), fill 0x3F with control 0x80 (line 33), pixels 0x41 with control 0xBF (line 46); tail controls `0xBF-width` (line 40) and `256-width` (line 55).
  - `MinFillRunLength = 3` (line 73); end-of-run threshold 2 (line 89).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure functions of (src, length) → bytes; deterministic output.

RendererTextureSurface defined in dx.cpp (extern here, line 68).

### Source/utils/display.h
- Purpose: Declares display globals and window/coordinate helpers incl. templates converting between output and logical coordinates.
- Public API:

### Source/utils/endian_read.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only little/big-endian unsigned 16/32-bit readers from byte buffers (constexpr).
- Public API: `template<typename T> constexpr uint16_t LoadLE16(const T *b)` (line 8), `LoadBE16` (16), `LoadLE32` (24), `LoadBE32` (32) — T must be 1-byte elements (static_assert per function).
- Depends on: `<cstdint>` only.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go equivalents: encoding/binary LittleEndian.Uint16/32, BigEndian.Uint16/32 over []byte — no custom code needed; keep thin wrappers named LoadLE16/LoadLE32/LoadBE16/LoadBE32 only if call-site parity is desired.
  - Must work on unaligned byte slices exactly like the C++ pointer reads.
- 1:1 constraints: byte assembly order: LE16 `b[1]<<8|b[0]` (line 12), BE16 `b[0]<<8|b[1]` (line 20), LE32 `b[3]<<24|b[2]<<16|b[1]<<8|b[0]` (line 28), BE32 `b[0]<<24|b[1]<<16|b[2]<<8|b[3]` (line 36).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure; stateless.
- Test coverage: indirectly via test/pack_test.cpp and test/writehero_test.cpp (LoadLE32 usage).
- Go mapping: stdlib `encoding/binary`; no dedicated package.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/utils/endian_stream.hpp
- Purpose: Buffered stdio endian helpers: logged fread/fwrite wrappers plus single-byte and LE 16/32-bit and LE-float read/write on FILE*.
- Public API: `inline void LoggedFread(void*, size_t, FILE*)` (line 17), `LoggedFwrite(const void*, size_t, FILE*)` (line 24); `template<T=uint8_t> T ReadByte(FILE*)` (line 31); `template<T=uint16_t> T ReadLE16(FILE*)` (line 41); `template<T=uint32_t> T ReadLE32(FILE*)` (line 51); `inline float ReadLEFloat(FILE*)` (line 56); `WriteByte` (line 68), `WriteLE16` (line 74), `WriteLE32` (line 81) on FILE*; `inline void WriteLEFloat(FILE*, float)` (line 84).
- Depends on: `utils/endian_read.hpp` (LoadLE16/32), `utils/endian_write.hpp` (WriteLE16/32 to buffer), `utils/log.hpp` (LogError).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go io.Reader/Writer based: ReadByte/ReadLE16/ReadLE32/ReadLEFloat returning values+error (C++ swallows errors after logging — Go must decide error policy; for 1:1 parity with save/load code, mirror "log and continue" only where callers relied on it, else propagate).
  - LoggedFread/LoggedFwrite semantics: fread/fwrite of 1 item of `size` bytes; on short read that is not EOF → LogError("fread failed: {strerror}") (lines 19-21); on any write failure → LogError("fwrite failed: ...") (lines 26-28).
  - ReadLEFloat: bit-cast uint32↔float via memcpy (lines 58-63) — Go math.Float32frombits/bits; WriteLEFloat mirrors (lines 86-91). static_assert sizeof(float)==sizeof(uint32_t) at lines 57 and 85.
  - Write path serializes into a small stack buffer then single fwrite — Go: binary.Write or manual byte order append.
- 1:1 constraints: all stream reads/writes little-endian; float is IEEE-754 32-bit bit-pattern copy (lines 56-63, 84-91).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless functions over FILE*; not thread-safe per-stream (stdio semantics), Go: io.Reader/Writer not concurrency-safe either — same discipline.
- Test coverage: indirectly via test/pack_test.cpp, test/writehero_test.cpp (save file serialization paths).
- Go mapping: `pkg/dsave` or `internal/serial` — small binary IO helper file used by save-game code; error returns instead of logging.
- Risks/open questions: error-swallowing behavior of LoggedFread (continues with uninitialized buffer on failure) is UB-ish in C++; Go port should return errors and let callers handle — note divergence.

### Source/utils/endian_swap.hpp
- Purpose: Header-only byte-swap helpers dispatching to SDL's endian macros (conditional on host endianness) for 16/32/64-bit LE/BE values.
- Public API: `inline uint16_t Swap16LE/BE(uint16_t)` (lines 13, 21), `inline uint32_t Swap32LE/BE(uint32_t)` (lines 29, 41), `inline int32_t SwapSigned32LE(int32_t)` (line 40), `inline uint64_t Swap64LE/BE(uint64_t)` (lines 49, 57).
- Depends on: SDL_endian.h (SDL_SwapLE16/BE16/LE32/BE32/LE64/BE64 or SDL3 SDL_Swap16LE etc.).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - On big-endian targets these swap; on little-endian they are identity. Go: binary.LittleEndian/big-endian conversion or direct value use — implement as no-ops on LE (all supported Go targets in scope are LE) but keep functions so big-endian ports remain possible.
  - `SwapSigned32LE` = bit-preserving cast of Swap32LE result (lines 40-43) — in Go just int32(uint32(v)) conversion.
- 1:1 constraints: semantics defined by SDL_Swap*LE/BE (host-endian conditional); no local constants beyond the SDL macro dispatch.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure; stateless.
- Test coverage: indirectly via test/pack_test.cpp / writehero_test.cpp (dungeon file save paths use Swap32LE).
- Go mapping: stdlib `encoding/binary` — replace with binary.LittleEndian.Uint32/PutUint32 at call sites; keep a compat shim only during transition.
- Risks/open questions: none.

# vol3-045.md

# Volume III — batch 045

### Source/utils/endian_write.hpp
- Purpose: Writes little-endian uint16/uint32 values into a raw byte buffer via memcpy after conditional byte swap.
- Public API: `inline void WriteLE16(void *out, uint16_t val)` (L9); `inline void WriteLE32(void *out, uint32_t val)` (L15).
- Depends on: `Swap16LE`/`Swap32LE` from `utils/endian_swap.hpp`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Functions that take a destination slice (offset 0) and write 2 or 4 bytes little-endian.
  - On big-endian hosts must still produce LE bytes (Go: `binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16/32` handles this unconditionally — the swap is a no-op concern that disappears).
  - No error return; caller guarantees ≥2/≥4 bytes capacity.
- 1:1 constraints: LE byte order for both widths (L9-13, L15-19). 2-byte and 4-byte exact sizes.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Stateless inline functions; fully thread-safe.
- Test coverage: none found (covered indirectly by save-file / mpq tests).
- Go mapping: `pkg/endian` — `PutLE16(out []byte, v uint16)`, `PutLE32(out []byte, v uint32)` wrapping `encoding/binary.LittleEndian`.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/utils/enum_traits.h
- Purpose: Compile-time enum helpers: `enum_size` (count via `T::LAST+1`), `enum_values<T>` range-for iteration over `T::FIRST..T::LAST`, and opt-in bitwise operators for flags enums via `use_enum_as_flags`.
- Public API: `template<T> struct enum_size { value = size_t(T::LAST)+1 }` (L12); `template<T> class enum_values` with `Iterator` (L17-42) and free `begin(enum_values<T>)`/`end(enum_values<T>)` (L45-53); `is_flags_enum` default false_type (L56-58); `use_enum_as_flags(Type)` macro (L60-63); constexpr `operator|`, `operator|=`, `operator&`, `operator&=`, `operator~`, `HasAnyOf`, `HasAllOf`, `HasNoneOf` (L65-117).
- Depends on: `DVL_ALWAYS_INLINE` from `utils/attributes.h`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go enums are int-based; no template machinery needed. Provide: iteration helper `EnumValues(first, last int) []int` or codegen per enum; `EnumSize = LAST+1` convention must be documented as a repo-wide rule.
  - Flags enums: since Go allows bitwise ops on integer-typed enums natively, the `is_flags_enum` gate is only needed to guard against accidental bit ops on non-flags enums — in Go this becomes a convention, not a type-system guarantee (or use a named `type FlagsXX uint32` distinct from the sequential enum type).
  - `HasAnyOf/HasAllOf/HasNoneOf(lhs, test)` helper functions with exact semantics: `(lhs&test) != 0`, `(lhs&test) == test`, `!HasAnyOf`.
  - Iteration order: underlying value ascending from FIRST to LAST inclusive.
- 1:1 constraints: `enum_size.value = size_t(T::LAST)+1` (L13); iteration `[FIRST, LAST]` inclusive — `end()` = LAST+1 (L51); `HasAnyOf` does NOT require an `EnumType::None` member, compares against `static_cast<EnumType>(0)` (L103 comment + L104).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Header-only, stateless, constexpr; zero runtime cost, no globals.
- Test coverage: none found as direct unit tests; exercised everywhere enums iterate.
- Go mapping: `pkg/enumutil` (size/iteration/has-any/all/none helpers) + per-package Go `const` blocks following FIRST/LAST convention.
- Risks/open questions: Go cannot enforce "flags only on opted-in enums" — port must decide whether that guard matters (it is compile-time hygiene, not behavior).

### Source/utils/file_name_generator.hpp
- Purpose: Builds asset file names into a fixed 256-byte stack buffer by concatenating prefix parts, an optional index or char affix, and a suffix (e.g. `"a/b1.txt"`).
- Public API:
  - `BaseFileNameGenerator(initializer_list<string_view> prefixes, string_view suffix)` (L16); `const char *operator()() const` returns prefix+suffix (L23); protected `Append` (L34), `Suffix()`/`PrefixEnd()`/`Buffer()` (L40-49).
  - `FileNameGenerator(prefixes, suffix, unsigned min = 1)` (L69); `const char *operator()(size_t i) const` → prefix + (min+i) + suffix (L76).
  - `FileNameWithCharAffixGenerator(prefixes, suffix, const char *chars)` (L99); `const char *operator()(size_t i) const` → replaces char at PrefixEnd with `chars_[i]` (L106).
- Depends on: `BufCopy` from `utils/str_cat.hpp` (writes and returns one-past-end pointer).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Three generator types over a shared prefix/suffix base. In Go, string concatenation is cheap; keep the API shape: `func() string` returning prefix+suffix; `func(i int) string` returning prefix+itoa(min+i)+suffix; and char-affix variant returning prefix+chars[i]+suffix.
  - Buffer is reused across calls in C++ (returns pointer to same `buf_`); Go returns fresh strings — callers in Go must not rely on pointer identity; fine.
  - `min` defaults to 1, i.e. first call `f(0)` yields index `1` (doc comment L57-64).
  - Char-affix constructor pre-writes suffix at `PrefixEnd()+1` and mutates `PrefixEnd()[0]` per call (L101, L107) — equivalent Go: build `prefix + string(chars[i]) + suffix` per call.
  - 256-byte buffer cap: C++ would overflow silently if exceeded; Go has no cap — verify no asset name exceeds 255 chars (they don't; longest prefixes like "nlevels\\data\\" are short).
- 1:1 constraints: index = `min_ + i` cast to `unsigned` (L78); default `min = 1` (L69); buffer size 256 (L52); examples in doc comments: `f()`→"a/b.txt", `f(0)`→"a/b1.txt", `f(1)`→"a/b2.txt" (L57-63), char affix `f(0)`→"a/bA.txt" (L90-95).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Instances are value-objects with mutable internal buffer — NOT thread-safe if shared; each generator owned by one user.
- Test coverage: none found (used by CEL/CLX/level asset loading paths).
- Go mapping: `pkg/strutil` or `internal/assets` — small struct types `FileNameGenerator{prefix []string; suffix string; min int}` with `String()`/`At(i)`.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### Source/utils/file_util.cpp
- Purpose: Cross-platform filesystem helpers (exists/dir checks, size, mkdir, resize, rename, copy, delete, open, directory listing) with per-OS branches (Win32, POSIX, std::filesystem, SDL fallback).
- Public API: implements everything declared in `file_util.h` (see below) plus internal `ToWideChar(string_view)->unique_ptr<wchar_t[]>` (Win32 only, L82), Win32 helpers `WindowsGetFileAttributes`, `WindowsFindFile`, `WindowsFileExists` (L107-176).
- Depends on: `LogError`/`LogVerbose` from `utils/log.hpp`; `DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR_STR`/`DirectorySeparator` from `file_util.h`; `std::filesystem` via `utils/stdcompat/filesystem.hpp`; SDL3 `SDL_iostream.h` or SDL1/2 `SDL.h` + `sdl_compat.h`; on Win32 `shlwapi.h` (PathFileExistsW).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go stdlib `os`/`os.Path` covers everything: `FileExists`→`os.Stat`+`!IsNotExist` (or `access(F_OK)`); `DirectoryExists`→`Stat.IsDir()`; `FileExistsAndIsWriteable`→Unix: `access(W_OK)` — Go: check write bit or open append; `GetFileSize`→`Stat.Size()`; `CreateDir`→`os.Mkdir` treating EEXIST as success; `RecursivelyCreateDir`→`os.MkdirAll` (but note: C++ fallback builds parent chain via `Dirname` loop — Go just uses MkdirAll); `ResizeFile`→`os.Truncate`; `RenameFile`→`os.Rename` (errors ignored — C++ discards result); `CopyFileOverwrite`→`io.Copy` with `os.Create` (overwrite semantics, bFailIfExists=false); `RemoveFile`→non-Win path first fopen "r+" then `remove` — Go `os.Remove` equivalent, with `\`→`/` replacement on the path (L399-401) — that replacement is for SDL/3DS-style paths, decide if Go target needs it; `OpenFile(path, mode)`→`os.OpenFile` with mode-string translation ("rb"→RDONLY, "wb"→CREATE|TRUNC|WRONLY, "ab"→APPEND|CREATE, "r+"→RDWR).
  - `Dirname`: strip trailing separators while size>1; if single "/" return "/"; no separator → "."; else prefix up to last separator (L94-104).
  - `ListDirectories`/`ListFiles`: return names (not paths) of subdirectories / regular files, skipping "." and ".."; empty vector on failure or missing dir (opendir null → empty, iterator ec → iterate nothing).
  - Windows UTF-16 layer (`ToWideChar` with `MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS`) is not needed for a Go port targeting UTF-8-native APIs.
- 1:1 constraints: `DirectorySeparator` = `'\\'` on Win32/DJGPP else `'/'` (header L11-15); `Dirname` returns `"."` when no separator, `"/"` when path is exactly one separator (L94-104); `CreateDir` success if already exists (EEXIST/ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS → true, L274-283, L295-303); non-filesystem `mkdir(path, 0777)` mode (L311); `ListDirectories` filters `d_type == DT_DIR` (L467) / attribute bit (L437-438); `ListFiles` filters `DT_REG` (L497) / NOT directory attribute (L527-528); copy buffer 4096 bytes in manual fallback (L381).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: All functions stateless and thread-safe; directory-listing order is OS/filesystem-dependent (not sorted!) — any consumer needing order must sort.
- Test coverage: `test/file_util_test.cpp`, `test/assets_test.cpp`, `test/writehero_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `pkg/fsutil` — thin wrappers over `os`/`io`; keep function-per-function names for easy diffing; Dirname implemented by hand (do NOT use `path/filepath.Dir` blindly — it differs on trailing-slash and "." cases; verify against L94-104 semantics).
- Risks/open questions: `Dirname` vs `filepath.Dir` differ on edge cases (e.g. "a/" → C++ gives ".", filepath.Dir gives "a"); port must reimplement exactly. `RemoveFile`'s backslash→slash rewrite and fopen-before-remove dance exist for platform quirks; Go port likely simplifies to `os.Remove` — note the LogVerbose messages differ.

### Source/utils/file_util.h
- Purpose: Declares the cross-platform filesystem utility API + the platform `DirectorySeparator` constant/macro.
- Public API: `constexpr char DirectorySeparator` and `DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR_STR` macro (L11-16); `bool FileExists(const char*)` + inline `string` overload (L19, L22); `DirectoryExists` ×2 (L26, L30); `std::string_view Dirname(std::string_view)` (L34); `bool FileExistsAndIsWriteable(const char*)` (L35); `bool GetFileSize(const char*, uintmax_t *size)` (L36); `bool CreateDir(const char*)` — true if existed or created (L42); `void RecursivelyCreateDir(const char*)` (L49); `bool ResizeFile(const char*, uintmax_t)` (L50); `void RenameFile(from, to)` (L51); `void CopyFileOverwrite(from, to)` (L52); `void RemoveFile(const char*)` (L53); `FILE *OpenFile(path, mode)` (L54); Win32 `ToWideChar` (L57-58); `std::vector<std::string> ListDirectories(const char*)` (L60); `ListFiles` (L61).

### Source/utils/format.hpp
- Purpose: Single helper `FormatRuntime` — `std::format` with a runtime (non-compile-checked) format string, used for translations.
- Public API: `template<typename... Args> std::string FormatRuntime(std::string_view fmt, Args&&... args)` (L15-18).
- Depends on: `<format>` (C++20).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Direct equivalent: `fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)` — Go's Sprintf is inherently runtime-format.
  - Must be used where the format string comes from translation catalogs, since the string is data.
- 1:1 constraints: C++ `{}`-style placeholders vs Go `%v`-style — translation strings in the C++ codebase use `{}`; the Go port's translation layer must either convert `{}`→Go verbs or keep a small formatter that understands `{}`. Placeholder syntax difference is the one real 1:1 hazard.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Stateless; thread-safe.
- Test coverage: none found (used via translations across UI code).
- Go mapping: `pkg/strutil` — `FormatRuntime(format string, args ...any) string` mapping to `fmt.Sprintf`, plus a `{}`→`%v` adapter if translations are copied verbatim.
- Risks/open questions: Translation format-string syntax (`{}` vs printf) — needs a project-wide decision; this file is where it lands.

### Source/utils/format_int.cpp
- Purpose: `FormatInteger` — formats int/uint32 with a translatable thousands separator, grouping by 3 digits.
- Public API: `std::string FormatInteger(int n)` (L12-47); `std::string FormatInteger(uint32_t n)` (L49-75).
- Depends on: `BufCopy(buf, n)` from `utils/str_cat.hpp` (integer→chars); translation macro `_()` from `utils/language.h`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Two functions (signed, unsigned32) that: render the number, then insert separator every 3 digits from the right; separator string from the translation system with msgid `","` and TRANSLATORS comment "Thousands separator".
  - Short-circuit: if digit-count (excluding '-' sign) ≤ 3, return the plain digits, no separator.
  - Signed: reserve '-' then process remaining digits.
  - Buffer 40 chars — no constraint in Go.
- 1:1 constraints: `GroupSize = 3` (L14, L51); separator = `_(","`) — translatable, may be multi-byte UTF-8 (L31, L68); first group length `mlen = numLen % 3; if 0 → 3` (L33-35, L70-72); reserve formula `len + separator.size()*(numLen-1)/3` (L32, L69); signed path strips sign into `out` first (L27-30); output for n<0 always '-' + grouped digits.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: No globals; translation lookup at call time (locale-dependent output by design).

### Source/utils/ini.cpp
- Purpose: Full INI parser/serializer: parses a buffer into ordered sections/keys/values with comment attachment, provides typed getters (string/bool/int/float/utf8buf), mutation via `set` with value-history semantics, and serializes back with CRLF and preserved comments.
- Public API (all `Ini::` methods): `parse(string_view) -> expected<Ini, string>` (L113-206); `serialize() -> string` (L336-358); `getKeys(section)` (L66-78); `get(section, key) -> span<const Value>` (L208-215); `getString(section, key, default="")` (L217-221); `getInt` (L223-237); `getBool` (L239-248); `getFloat` (L250-272); `getUtf8Buf` ×2 (L274-277, header L69); `set(section, key, Values&&)` core (L279-329); `set(span<const string>)` (L331-345); `set(string&&)`, `set(string_view)`, `set(const char*)` (header/inline, L347-353); `set(int)` (L355), `set(bool)` (L359), `set(float)` (L363-374); internal helpers `AppendComment`, `AppendSection`, `AppendKeyValue` (L378-401); `Values` ctors and `get()/append()` (L48-64, L80-96).
- Depends on: `app_fatal` (extern, from `appfat.h`, decl at L33 to avoid SDL dep in tests); `c_sort` from `utils/algorithm/container.hpp`; `BufCopy`/`StrCat` from `utils/str_cat.hpp`; `StringViewHash`/`StringViewEquals` from `utils/string_view_hash.hpp`; `CopyUtf8` from `utils/utf8.hpp`; `ankerl::unordered_dense::map`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Parser rules: skip UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) at buffer start (L96-100); split on `\n`, strip single trailing `\r` (L121-124); line whitespace = only ' ' and '\t' (L45, L54); blank lines skipped; lines starting with ';' (after leading ws) begin/run a comment block — consecutive comment lines accumulate, the block attaches to the next section or key (L127-134, L138-141); `[section]` lines: name up to ']', trailing ws after ']' allowed but any other content is an error "content after section [x]: y" (L143-159); duplicate section names merge (second occurrence reuses map entry and updates `sectionEntries` pointer, L161-168); keys before any section → error "line N: key not in any section" (L171); key=value: key trimmed of trailing ws before '=', value trimmed of leading ws after '=', value may contain '=' (memchr finds first, L172-177); duplicate keys in same section append to the value list (L180-182).
  - Errors are `unexpected(string)` with messages exactly `line {N}: unclosed section name {name}`, `line {N}: content after section [{name}]: {rest}`, `line {N}: key not in any section`, `line {N}: key {key} has no value` (L150, L155, L171, L175).
  - Typed getters use the LAST value in the list (`xs.back()`); empty value string → default (L218-220, L225, L241, L254). `getBool` accepts only "0"/"1", anything else `app_fatal("ini: Failed to parse {s}.{k}={v} as bool")` (L239-248). `getInt` uses `from_chars` (no leading ws, full-string parse else fatal, L226-235). `getFloat` uses `from_chars`/`strtof` fallback (L250-272).
  - `set` semantics: empty Values deletes key (and section if it becomes empty, L305-310); setting equal values (same count, all `.value` equal) leaves file unchanged (`changed_` stays false, L312-321); comments with `nullopt` inherit the existing comment at same index (L323-327); new sections/keys get index = current map size (insertion order, L286-296).
  - `set(float)` formats via `to_chars` into 64-char buffer — shortest round-trip representation (L363-374); Go: `strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', -1, 32)` is the closest — verify precision matches for 32-bit floats.
  - Serializer: sections in insertion order (index sort), blank CRLF line between sections (except before first), section comment then `[name]\r\n`, then keys in insertion order; each value's comment (if set and non-empty) then `key=value\r\n` — one line per value for multi-valued keys (L336-358).
  - `AppendComment` converts bare `\n` to `\r\n` (tracks prev `\r` to avoid doubling, L378-388).
  - `Values` representation: single value or vector, `append` promotes single→vector (L80-96).
- 1:1 constraints: whitespace set { ' ', '\t' } only (L45/L54 comments); BOM bytes `0xEF 0xBB 0xBF` (L99); CRLF output everywhere (`AppendSection` L393, `AppendKeyValue` L397, inter-section `"\r\n"` L342); error message formats L150/155/171/175; `getBool` whitelist "0"/"1" (L242-243); last-value-wins for getters; insertion-order indices `uint32_t index = map.size()` at insert (L166, L185, L287, L297); changed-flag only set on real mutation (L291, L301, L309, L328).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Single-threaded object, no shared globals besides `app_fatal`; parse/serialize are pure functions of content + insertion order — deterministic. Hash map iteration is never used for output order (always index-sorted, L73, L340, L351).
- Test coverage: `test/ini_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `pkg/ini` — `type Ini struct`; ordered maps as `[]section{ name; comment; entries []entry }` + index maps for lookup (Go has no ankerl; keep insertion-order slices as source of truth, hash only for get). Errors via `(Ini, error)` or a small `ParseError` string.
- Risks/open questions: `getFloat`/`set(float)` textual round-trip: C++ `to_chars` shortest-form vs Go `strconv.FormatFloat(-1)` — need a test on representative option values (e.g. 0.5, 1.25, 0.001); C++ from_chars accepts forms Go ParseFloat also accepts, but edge syntax (hex floats, inf) differs — in practice option files never contain those.

### Source/utils/ini.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the `Ini` class: value/comment structures, multi-value `Values`, typed getters, `set` overloads, and private ordered section/key storage.

### Source/utils/intrusive_optional.hpp
- Purpose: Macro that injects an optional-like interface into a class, using a designated member field's sentinel value as "empty" instead of a separate bool (saves memory in hot structs).
- Public API: `DEFINE_INTRUSIVE_OPTIONAL_IMPL(CLASS, VALUE_CLASS, FIELD, NULL_VALUE, CONSTEXPR)` generating: default ctor, value move-ctor, nullopt ctor, variadic `emplace`, `operator=(U&&)` (self-assign-safe SFINAE), `operator=(nullopt_t)` (value-resets), `operator*`/`operator->` const+mutable with assert, `has_value()`, `operator bool`, private `VALUE_CLASS value_` (L13-85); convenience wrappers `DEFINE_CONSTEXPR_INTRUSIVE_OPTIONAL` (L88) and `DEFINE_INTRUSIVE_OPTIONAL` (L92).
- Depends on: `assert` via `appfat.h` include (L8) — actually pulls whole appfat; C++ `<optional>`, `<type_traits>`, `<utility>`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - In Go, this is a design pattern, not a macro: struct with sentinel-based `IsValid()`. Each user (e.g. `Cmd`-like or missile/object structs) defines its zero-value sentinel (`FIELD == NULL_VALUE` means empty).
  - Must preserve: dereference-on-empty is an assertion failure (debug abort) in C++; Go equivalents should panic in debug builds or document UB.
  - `operator=(nullopt)` resets whole VALUE_CLASS to default (`value_ = VALUE_CLASS{}`) — Go zero-value assignment.
  - `emplace(args...)` constructs in place and returns reference.
- 1:1 constraints: emptiness test is exactly `value_.FIELD != NULL_VALUE` (L66-69); assignment from nullopt resets the ENTIRE value, not just the field (L52-55); assert (not throw) on empty deref (L58-62).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: macro-generated members; instances are plain values — thread-safety inherited from containing struct; no statics.
- Test coverage: none found.
- Go mapping: no direct equivalent needed — port structs with sentinel fields (e.g. `Index == -1` / `ID == 0` means empty) plus `HasValue()` methods at each use site; optionally a tiny `internal/intrusive` doc comment capturing the convention.
- Risks/open questions: none behaviorally; just ensure each C++ use site's sentinel value is carried over (grep DEFINE_INTRUSIVE_OPTIONAL users when porting those files).

### Source/utils/language.cpp
- Purpose: gettext-style i18n: loads GNU .mo/.gmo translation catalogs, parses Plural-Forms metadata, serves `LanguageTranslate` / `LanguagePluralTranslate` / `LanguageParticularTranslate` lookups.
- Public API (all in `devilution` ns; decls in language.h):
  - `std::string forceLocale` (global, defined here)
  - `std::string_view GetLanguageCode()` — forceLocale if set else options `Language.code`
  - `bool HasTranslation(const std::string &locale)` — "en" always true; else checks FindAsset for `<locale>.mo`/`<locale>.gmo`
  - `void LanguageInitialize()` — full .mo loader
  - `std::string_view LanguageTranslate(const char *key)`; `LanguagePluralTranslate(const char *singular, std::string_view plural, int count)`; `LanguageParticularTranslate(std::string_view context, std::string_view message)`
  - Internal: `unsigned PluralForms = 2`; `tl::function_ref<int(int)> GetLocalPluralId = PluralIfNotOne` (file-scope mutable globals)
- Depends on: `engine/assets.hpp` (AssetHandle, OpenAsset, FindAsset), `options.h` (GetOptions().Language.code), `utils/algorithm/container.hpp` (c_any_of), `utils/endian_swap.hpp` (Swap32LE/Swap16LE), `utils/file_util.h` (OpenFile — used via LoggedFStream? no: `OpenFile` not used here; only via header chain), `utils/log.hpp` (LogError/LogVerbose), `utils/paths.h`, `utils/string_view_hash.hpp` (StringViewHash/StringViewEquals), ankerl::unordered_dense, function_ref, SDL_GetTicks (SDL2/SDL3 timer), UiErrorOkDialog + StrCat + IsSmallFontTall/HaveExtraFonts (via options.h/language.h chain).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package holding translation state: `map[string]ref` per plural form (slice of maps sized PluralForms), plus two backing byte buffers `translationKeys`/`translationValues` — in Go just store `[]string` values or offset+len refs into one []byte; returned strings must be null-terminated views (Go strings are fine).
  - MO file parser: magic 0x950412de, revision major/minor ≤1, LE 32/16 swaps; entry tables at srcOffset/dstOffset, 8-byte MoEntry {length, offset} each; entry 0 is the header (src[0].length must be 0; its dst value parsed as metadata).
  - Plural-Forms parsing: find "nplurals", parse single digit, then "plural=" expression matched against 8 exact known expression strings (see 1:1) selecting a Go closure; unknown → LogError.
  - Lookup semantics: missing key returns the key itself (Translate), plural missing returns plural when count!=1 else singular, context lookup builds `context '\004' message` key.
  - `LanguageInitialize` side effects: resets maps and buffers; en → default plural fn; tall-font locales (zh/ja/ko) without fonts.mpq → UiErrorOkDialog then forceLocale="en"; asset open tries .mo then .gmo; failure → forceLocale="en". LogVerbose with load time in ms (SDL_GetTicks delta).
  - Data model note: plural translation values are `\0`-separated, up to PluralForms forms stored per key in maps translation[j], j < PluralForms, stopping at empty value.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `MO_MAGIC = 0x950412de` (line 21).
  - TranslationRef packing: offsetBits=19, sizeBits=13, sizeMask=(1<<13)-1; Encode=(offset<<13)|size; GetTranslation splits via >>13 and &mask (lines 38–49).
  - Plural expression table (exact strings + behavior), lines ~99–160: `"0"`→always 0; `"(n != 1)"`→n!=1; `"(n > 1)"`→n>1; East-Slavic `(n%10==1 && n%100!=11 ? 0 : n%10>=2 && n%10<=4 && (n%100<12 || n%100>14) ? 1 : 2)`; Polish `(n==1 ? 0 : n%10>=2 && n%10<=4 && (n%100<12 || n%100>14) ? 1 : 2)`; Romanian `(n==1 ? 0 : n==0 || (n!=1 && n%100>=1 && n%100<=19) ? 1 : 2)`; Czech `(n==1) ? 0 : (n>=2 && n<=4) ? 1 : 2`. Default `PluralIfNotOne` = n!=1.
  - nplurals parse: only first char, must be ≥'0', nonzero digit (lines ~170–186).
  - Glue char for context keys: `'\004'` (line ~331).
  - Metadata parse loop: split on ':', value to '\n', match key "Plural-Forms" exactly then break.
  - Entry ordering: strings loaded from i=1..nbMappings-1 (entry 0 is header); plural forms loop `j < PluralForms && !value.empty()`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutable globals `forceLocale`, `translation`, `translationKeys/Values`, `PluralForms`, `GetLocalPluralId` — language (re)initialize mutates all; not thread-safe; must be re-init safe (translation= { {}, {} } resets only 2 maps, then resized to PluralForms after header parse).
- Test coverage: `test/language_for_testing.cpp` (test shim), `test/parse_int_test.cpp` unrelated; no dedicated language_test.cpp found.
- Go mapping: `internal/i18n` — maps keyed by string, []string per plural form; MO parser in same package; expose Translate/TranslatePlural/TranslateContext + Init(locale) returning reset semantics; forceLocale as package var with accessor.
- Risks/open questions: returned `std::string_view` lifetime is tied to translationValues buffer (never freed until next init) — in Go use string copies or immutable slices; UiErrorOkDialog dependency pulls in UI stack (inversion needed: return error and let caller show dialog).

### Source/utils/log.hpp
- Purpose: SDL-backed logging facade with fmt-style `{}` formatting via std::format, per-priority/per-category functions with lazy formatting (Verbose/Debug check level before formatting).

  - Category+priority leveled logger; format functions take fmt string + args; on bad format spec: log critical + fatal (app_fatal equivalent).
  - Lazy formatting gate: only format when level enabled — Go natural via `if !enabled(level) { return }` or fmt args passed lazily; keep the LogVerbose/LogDebug gate (lines ~131, 153) since it is an intentional perf behavior.
  - Default category Application for the no-category overloads.
- 1:1 constraints: priority ordering compare `SDL_GetLogPriority(category) <= priority` for enabled-check (line ~112); Verbose/Debug early-return before format; Info/Warn/Error/Critical always format. Format-error path: `SDL_LogCritical` then `app_fatal(fullError)` where fullError = `StrCat("Format error, fmt: ", fmt, " error: ", e.what())`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: stateless wrappers over SDL log (SDL log itself is thread-safe); no globals defined here.

### Source/utils/logged_fstream.hpp
- Purpose: `FILE*` wrapper struct that logs every operation (open/seek/tell/read/write) success-or-failure with errno text, via LogVerbose (success) / LogError (fail), category System.
- Public API: `struct LoggedFStream` — `bool Open(const char *path, const char *mode)` (uses file_util OpenFile); `void Close()`; `bool IsOpen() const`; `bool Seekp(long pos, int dir = SEEK_SET)`; `bool Tellp(long *result)`; `bool Write(const char *data, size_t size)` (fwrite size 1 item); `bool Read(char *out, size_t size)` (fread size 1 item); private `static DirToString(int)` (impl in .cpp) and template `CheckError(bool ok, const char *fmt, args...)` — on failure appends `: failed with "{}"` and strerror(errno) (empty string if null), LogError; else LogVerbose.
- Depends on: `utils/file_util.h` (OpenFile), `utils/log.hpp` (LogError/LogVerbose/LogCategory::System), `<cerrno>/<cstring>` strerror/errno, `<optional>/<string>`.

  - Go wrapper struct over `*os.File` (or an interface {io.ReadWriteSeeker}) with identical per-op logging: Open (path, mode), Seek, Tell, Read, Write; log via internal/log with System category; include syscall error string.
  - Write/Read semantics: C++ checks `fwrite/fread == 1` item of `size` bytes → Go io.ReadFull/Write return err check is equivalent.
  - Default Seekp dir = SEEK_SET.
- 1:1 constraints: error-message formats — `"fopen(\"{}\", \"{}\")"`, `"fseek({}, {})"` with DirToString, `"ftell() = {}"`, `"fwrite(data, {})"`, `"fread(out, {})"`; failure suffix `": failed with \"{}\""` + strerror(errno) (lines ~46–78).

### Source/utils/math.h
- Purpose: Small generic math helpers: Sign, Lerp, InvLerp, Remap.

- Depends on: nothing (header-only).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Generic funcs (Go generics, one numeric constraint): Sign, Lerp, InvLerp, Remap — exact formulas; integer and float instantiations both occur in C++ (invLerp used with ints in palette/light code) — Go needs separate int/float variants or a Numeric constraint.
  - InvLerp(0,0,v) guard returns 0 (avoid div-by-zero) — preserve.
- 1:1 constraints: formulas as above, lines 17 `(t > T(0)) - (t < T(0))`; 31 `a + (b - a) * t`; 46–47 b==a→T(0) else (v-a)/(b-a); 58 Remap = Lerp∘InvLerp.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure.
- Test coverage: `test/math_test.cpp` (exists — covers Sign/Lerp/InvLerp/Remap presumably; grep-able).
- Go mapping: `internal/mathutil` or `pkg/mathutil` — tiny generics file + table tests ported from test/math_test.cpp.
- Risks/open questions: C++ template mixed-type Lerp (V return, T interpolator) — Go single-constraint generic may need explicit casts at callsites.

### Source/utils/palette_blending.cpp
- Purpose: Builds the 256×256 transparency lookup (blended-color nearest-palette index, Quake2-style) plus optional black-16 LUT; regenerates single rows via k-d tree.
- Public API (decl in hpp): `uint8_t paletteTransparencyLookup[256][256]` (global array); `void GenerateBlendedLookupTable(const SDL_Color *palette, int skipFrom = -1, int skipTo = -1)`; `void UpdateBlendedLookupTableSingleColor(const SDL_Color *palette, unsigned i)`; (ifdef `DEVILUTIONX_PALETTE_TRANSPARENCY_BLACK_16_LUT`) `uint16_t paletteTransparencyLookupBlack16[65536]`; `void UpdateTransparencyLookupBlack16(unsigned from, unsigned to)`.
- Depends on: `utils/palette_kd_tree.hpp` (PaletteKdTree), SDL_Color type, internal static `PaletteKdTree CurrentPaletteKdTree` (file-scope, persists between calls).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Package-level `PaletteTransparencyLookup [256][256]uint8` (hot read path every frame — keep as flat array [65536]uint8 or [256][256], avoid bounds-check overhead via local copies).
  - `GenerateBlendedLookupTable(palette [256]SDLColor, skipFrom, skipTo int)`: rebuild kd-tree; diagonal LUT[i][i]=i; mirror upper triangle from lower; compute blended nearest for j>i via kd-tree of averaged RGB.
  - BlendColors: per-channel (a+b)/2 integer average cast to uint8 — exact.
  - `UpdateBlendedLookupTableSingleColor`: recompute row+column i only (symmetric write LUT[i][j]=LUT[j][i]=best), using existing CurrentPaletteKdTree; diagonal = j.
  - CurrentPaletteKdTree must persist as package state so single-color updates work between full regenerations.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Blend = `(int(a.r)+int(b.r))/2` per channel truncating (lines ~26–31).
  - Loop structure lines ~49–60: for i in 0..255: LUT[i][i]=i; for j<i: LUT[i][j]=LUT[j][i]; then j from i+1..255: kd-tree findNearestNeighbor(blend(palette[i],palette[j])).
  - Black16 LUT (ifdef): index `i | (j<<8)`; value `LUT[0][i] | (LUT[0][j]<<8)`; big-endian note in hpp (indices j|(i<<8), value order same) — lines ~34–37, 63–68; single-color update also refreshes Black16 for (i,i) only in UpdateBlendedLookupTableSingleColor (line ~76) while full gen refreshes all pairs.
  - `GenerateBlendedLookupTable` default args skipFrom=-1, skipTo=-1 (decl in hpp line 24).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: `paletteTransparencyLookup` global mutated at palette-change time (engine/palette.cpp calls these); read every frame by renderers; single-threaded assumption (main thread); CurrentPaletteKdTree statics — same.
- Test coverage: `test/palette_blending_test.cpp`, `test/palette_blending_benchmark.cpp` (exist).
- Go mapping: `internal/render/palette` (or internal/palette) — LUT arrays + kd-tree in same package; SDL_Color → own RGBA struct.
- Risks/open questions: Black16 LUT only for platforms defining the macro (likely 3DS/Amiga big-endian targets — grep CMake to confirm before porting; can likely be dropped for Go if those targets don't exist).

### Source/utils/palette_kd_tree.cpp
- Purpose: Implements PaletteKdTree construction: median-split pivots per depth level (R,G,B axes), bucketing palette colors into 32 leaves, plus Graphviz debug dump.
- Public API: `PaletteKdTree::PaletteKdTree(const SDL_Color palette[256], int skipFrom, int skipTo)`; `std::string PaletteKdTree::toGraphvizDot() const`; `PaletteKdTreeNode<0>::toGraphvizDot(...)` (debug only).
- Depends on: `utils/palette_kd_tree.hpp`, `utils/static_vector.hpp` (StaticVector<uint8_t,256> leafValues[NumLeaves]), `utils/str_cat.hpp` (StrAppend, AsHexPad2), SDL_Color, `<span>`, graphviz ifdef `DEVILUTIONX_PRINT_PALETTE_BLENDING_TREE_GRAPHVIZ` (0 by default, hpp line 14).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Construction: (1) PopulatePivots — for each tree depth d in 0..4, compute per-subdivision histograms of the split axis component for non-skipped palette entries and set node pivots to the median (GetMedian). Median split repeated for all 5 depths refining subdivisions. (2) Bucket each non-skipped palette index into leaf via LeafIndexForColor (bits chosen by comparing component < pivot at each level). (3) Flatten into values_ array grouped by leaf, storing leaf ranges as inclusive uint8 begin/end ([1,0] = empty).
  - GetMedian: scan counts accumulating until partialSum >= (numValues+1)/2; returns index i (may roll over to 0 when all-same value 255) — special cases documented lines ~59–63.
  - Iteration order matters for ties: leaf values appended in ascending palette index order (for i 0..255).
  - toGraphvizDot: debug-only; port as optional method or drop (guarded by constant=0).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Depth=5 (hpp line 19), NumLeaves=32 (hpp line 74); axis at depth = (PaletteKdTreeDepth - RemainingDepth) % 3 → levels cycle R,G,B,R,G (hpp line 29).
  - GetMedian: `medianTarget = (numValues + 1) / 2`; loop `for (; partialSum < medianTarget && partialSum != numValues; ++i) partialSum += counts[i];` return uint8(i) (lines ~52–64).
  - Skip condition `i >= skipFrom && i <= skipTo` in both pivot pass and bucketing (lines ~117, 137).
  - Leaf empty representation valuesBegin=1, valuesEndInclusive=0 (lines ~143–146).
  - values_ is exactly 256 pairs — with skips, trailing slots uninitialized garbage (C++ UB-ish but never read past ranges; Go must zero them).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: construction deterministic given palette; no globals; safe to build concurrently (tree is value state) except static helper templates.
- Test coverage: `test/palette_blending_test.cpp` covers kd-tree indirectly; `test/static_vector_test.cpp` covers dependency.
- Go mapping: `internal/render/palette/kdtree.go` — recursive struct or flat arrays: pivots [31]uint8 (5 levels: 1+2+4+8+16 nodes), values [256]struct{rgb [3]uint8; idx uint8} + per-leaf [begin,endInclusive]. Median logic identical.
- Risks/open questions: uninitialized trailing values_ slots — Go must define behavior (zero); verify no caller relies on garbage.

### Source/utils/palette_kd_tree.hpp
- Purpose: Declares the k-d tree over palette colors: node template by depth (left/right child + pivot), leaf node with inclusive value range, and PaletteKdTree with nearest-neighbor search.
- Public API: `constexpr size_t PaletteKdTreeDepth = 5`; `template<size_t D> struct PaletteKdTreeNode` (members left, right, uint8_t pivot; child(bool); toGraphvizDot debug); specialization `PaletteKdTreeNode<0>` (uint8_t valuesBegin, valuesEndInclusive); `class PaletteKdTree`: ctor()(default), ctor(palette[256], skipFrom, skipTo); `uint8_t findNearestNeighbor(const RGB &rgb)`; `std::string toGraphvizDot() const`; private VisitState{best,bestDiff}, getColorDistance (squared Euclid over RGB), getColorDistanceToPlane ((x1-x2)^2), recursive findNearestNeighborVisit (descend near child first; visit far child iff planeDist < bestDiff), leaf scan do-while over inclusive range.

- Requirements for Go port:
  - Same structure: nearest-neighbor query over 256 palette points; visit near subtree always, far subtree iff squared plane distance < current best squared distance (strict <).
  - getColorDistance: sum of squared per-channel diffs using int arithmetic then uint32 result.
  - Leaf scan: empty check (begin > endInclusive) early-out; then do-while over [begin, endInclusive]; ties keep first (strict < when updating best).
  - findNearestNeighbor initializes bestDiff = MaxUint32; best unset (0) if all leaves empty — impossible in practice.
  - RGB type = [3]uint8.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Depth 5 (line 19); Coord = (Depth - RemainingDepth) % 3 (line 29); NumLeaves = 1<<5 = 32 (line 74).
  - Plane-visit condition `getColorDistanceToPlane(pivot, coord) < visitState.bestDiff` (lines ~116–119) — strict less-than.
  - Best update condition `diff < visitState.bestDiff` (line ~138) — strict; first (lowest palette index in leaf order) wins ties.
  - bestDiff init `std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max()` (line ~83).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: query is const/read-only after construction; tree instances value-semantic (C++ copy assignment used in palette_blending.cpp line 46).
- Test coverage: via test/palette_blending_test.cpp.

### Source/utils/parse_int.cpp
- Purpose: Implements `ParseFixed6Fraction` — parse decimal fraction digits into a 6-bit fixed-point value with round-to-nearest, mimicking std::from_chars end-pointer behavior.
- Public API: `uint8_t ParseFixed6Fraction(std::string_view str, const char **endOfParse)` (decl in parse_int.hpp with ParseInt/ParseIntError templates).
- Depends on: `parse_int.hpp` (which uses <charconv>, <expected>); `<algorithm>` std::find_if_not.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Function ParseFixed6Fraction(s string) (val uint8, endOfParse int or string): read at most 7 leading ASCII digits, accumulate decimalFraction = d*10+digit; then if endOfParse requested, consume ALL remaining digits (beyond the 7) for the end pointer; normalize to 7 digits by *10; result = (decimalFraction + 78125) / 156250.
  - Non-digit stops the digit loop; the end pointer is the first non-digit position after consuming any extra digits.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - 7-digit cap (line 10 comment + loop line 12); round-to-nearest via +78125 (half of 156250) then /156250 (lines 26–30): 156250 = 10^7/64, 78125 = half-step.
  - endOfParse consumes all remaining digits even beyond 7 (lines 19–22).
  - Normalization loop multiplies by 10 until numDigits==7 (lines 24–27).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure function.
- Test coverage: `test/parse_int_test.cpp` (exists — covers ParseFixed6Fraction and ParseInt).
- Go mapping: `internal/parseint` or `pkg/parseint` — port with table tests from test/parse_int_test.cpp; ParseInt generic in parse_int.hpp maps to Go strconv-like wrapper with min/max and end-offset return.
- Risks/open questions: parse_int.hpp itself (ParseInt template) is a separate file outside this batch — port together for coherent API.

# vol3-047.md

# Volume III — batch 047

### Source/utils/parse_int.hpp
- Purpose: Type-generic integer and 2.6 fixed-point string parsing built on `std::from_chars`, with range checking and out-param end-of-parse pointers. Declares `ParseIntError`, `ParseInt<T>`, `ParseFixed6<T>` templates plus `ParseFixed6Fraction` (defined in parse_int.cpp).
- Public API:
  - `enum class ParseIntError { ParseError = 1, OutOfRange }`
  - `template<typename IntT> using ParseIntResult<IntT> = std::expected<IntT, ParseIntError>`
  - `template<typename IntT> ParseIntResult<IntT> ParseInt(std::string_view str, IntT min = numeric_limits<IntT>::min(), IntT max = numeric_limits<IntT>::max(), const char **endOfParse = nullptr)`
  - `uint8_t ParseFixed6Fraction(std::string_view str, const char **endOfParse = nullptr)` (impl in parse_int.cpp)
  - `template<typename IntT> ParseIntResult<IntT> ParseFixed6(std::string_view str, const char **endOfParse = nullptr)`
- Depends on: `<charconv>` (`std::from_chars`), `<expected>`, `<string_view>`, `<system_error>` — stdlib only, no devilution deps. Companion impl parse_int.cpp uses `<algorithm>` (std::find_if_not).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go package (e.g. `internal/parseint`) with generic `ParseInt[T constraints.Integer](s string, minV, maxV T) (T, endIdx int, err error)`.
  - Must replicate `std::from_chars` base-10 semantics: no leading whitespace allowed, optional `-` (for signed; `+` NOT accepted by from_chars), digits until first non-digit; empty/no-digit prefix = ParseError.
  - Out-of-range (overflow of IntT) is a distinct error from malformed input — Go port must keep this distinction (`ErrParse` vs `ErrRange`).
  - Range check against caller-supplied min/max maps to OutOfRange, not a separate error.
  - `endOfParse` semantics: always set on entry to str start in ParseFixed6 error paths (lines 68–70); set to final consumed position on success; from_chars sets ptr even on partial parse — Go must return byte index of first unconsumed char.
  - `ParseFixed6Fraction`: parse at most 7 fraction digits (line 20 of parse_int.cpp), normalize to 7 decimal places by *10 padding, round-half-up via adding 5 to /10 reduction down to 6 bits — copy algorithm exactly (see parse_int.cpp; cited because hpp declares it).
  - `ParseFixed6`: handles `-` sign, `.fraction` without integer part (".123" → 0.123), "-.1"; integer part range-shifted by >>6; fraction 64 (rounded up to 1.0) must not overflow (lines 118–124); negative numbers subtract fraction (line 128).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Line 27: `min = std::numeric_limits<IntT>::min()`, `max = ...max()` defaults.
  - Lines 57–58: `minIntegerValue = min >> 6`, `maxIntegerValue = max >> 6` (arithmetic shift for signed).
  - Line 63: `isNegative = std::is_signed_v<IntT> && str[0] == '-'` — for unsigned types a leading `-` is NOT treated as negative sign here (but from_chars rejects `-` for unsigned → ParseError path).
  - Line 66: `haveDigits = has_value() || error == OutOfRange` — out-of-range integer still counts as digits consumed.
  - parse_int.cpp line 20: 7-digit cap; lines 30–33: pad `decimalFraction *= 10` to 7 digits; rounding constant from parse_int.cpp: add half-step before truncating to /64.
  - Lines 118–131: overflow guard `fractionPart >= 64 && (integerPart >= maxIntegerValue || (signed && integerPart <= minIntegerValue))` → OutOfRange; else `fixedValue = integerPart << 6; isNegative ? -= fractionPart : += fractionPart`.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure functions, no state, fully deterministic. Templates instantiated per IntT — Go generics give same instantiation set.
- Test coverage: `test/parse_int_test.cpp` (extensive); also used by `test/data_file_test.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/parseint` — generics + two sentinel errors; port test/parse_int_test.cpp verbatim as the acceptance gate.
- Risks/open questions: Go lacks `std::expected`; use `(T, error)` tuple. from_chars rejects leading `+` and whitespace — Go `strconv` accepts both, so a hand-rolled digit scanner is required for exact parity.
