  - `GamemenuOn()` opens menu (idempotent — double-open stays open, lines 108–113); `GamemenuHandlePrevious()` toggles.
  - Slider API: `GmenuSliderSteps(item *TMenuItem, n)`, `GmenuSliderSet(item, min, max, value)`, `GmenuSliderGet(item, min, max) int` with round-trip accuracy at 10/100 steps and exact endpoints at 2 steps.
  - A test fixture equivalent to UITest (fresh game state per test, MPQ-skip when assets missing) or Go-side dependency injection replacing globals.
  - Go must avoid the C++ SaveOptions crash pattern: initialize the options-store (ini) before any menu close path, so `GamemenuOff()` is testable directly — an improvement over the workaround.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Slider semantics: steps=10, range 0–100: set 50 → get 50; set 0 → 0; set 100 → 100 (lines 137–163). steps=100: 75 → 75 (lines 166–172). steps=50, range 10–60: 35 → 35 (lines 175–181). steps=2: endpoints exact (lines 184–191).
  - `sgpCurrentMenu == nullptr` ⇔ `!gmenu_is_active()` (consistency test, lines 118–130).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: ForceCloseMenu mutates globals `isGameMenuOpen`/`sgpCurrentMenu` directly (lines 63–67) — tests rely on and mutate global menu state; no concurrency. Tests deliberately avoid `gamemenu_off()` due to uninitialised global std::optional<Ini> deref (header comment, lines 10–13).
- Test coverage: counterpart for Source/gamemenu.cpp + Source/gmenu.cpp slider functions; the only menu-state coverage found.
- Go mapping: internal/ui/menu (gamemenu) + internal/ui/gmenu. Strategy: port slider math as pure functions on a menu-item struct first (fully testable), then state machine with explicit init of options store.
- Risks/open questions: the documented SaveOptions crash means the Go port's options/ini module must be constructible headless before menu close; slider quantization formula lives in gmenu.cpp (not read here) — port it to satisfy the round-trip constraints above.

### test/ini_test.cpp
- Purpose: Round-trip test for the Ini parser/serializer: comments preserved, multi-value keys, typed getters (int/float/string), mutation via `set` (including vector and bool), and exact serialized output format.
- Public API: none (single TEST `IniTest.BasicTest`). Helper `ReplaceNewlines(std::string_view) -> std::string` converts `\n` to `\r\n` (line 20–31).
- Depends on: `Ini` class — `Ini::parse` returning `std::expected<Ini, std::string>`, `getString(section,key)`, `get(section,key) -> span<const Ini::Value>`, `getInt(sec,key,default)`, `getFloat(sec,key,default)`, `set(sec,key,string/int/bool/vector<string>/float)`, `serialize()` (utils/ini.hpp); gmock ElementsAre/Eq.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go Ini type with: `Parse(string) (Ini, error)`; `GetString(section, key) string`; `GetInt(section, key, def int) int`; `GetFloat(section, key, def float64) float64`; multi-value `Get(section, key) []Value`; `Set(section, key, value)` overloads for string/int/bool/[]string/float64; `Serialize() string`.
  - Behavior contract: parse preserves section/key order, leading comments (both single and multi-line, lines 36–43), duplicate keys become multi-values in order (`multi = a`, `multi = b` → ["a","b"], lines 47–53).
  - Serialize format: `key=value` with NO spaces around `=` (lines 89–108 — parse accepts `key1 = value1`, serialize emits `key1=newValue`); comments emitted before their key; blank line between sections; new sections appended at end; bools serialize as `1`/`0`; floats like `10.5`; ints plain (`1337`); multi-values one per line under the original comments.
  - Multi-value `set` replaces all previous values with the new list in order (lines 61–62: a,b → x,y,z).
  - Serialize must use `\r\n` line endings on Windows-tested path — the test normalizes the expected string via ReplaceNewlines, implying the C++ serializer emits `\r\n` (platform) — Go port should pick one (likely `\n`) and match tests accordingly.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Exact expected serialization (lines 89–107): section order sectionA then sectionB then newSection; within sectionA: key1=newValue, key2=value2, `; comment multi 1`, multi=x, `; comment multi 2`, multi=y, multi=z, int=1337, float=10.5, `; bool yes comment`, `bool yes=0`, `bool no=0`; sectionB: key=value.
  - getInt default not used: int=-3 parsed as negative (line 56); float 2.5 within 0.001 (line 57).
  - `bool yes=1` parses truthy; set(...,false) serializes `0` (lines 59, 62, 102).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: pure data structure; no globals, no RNG; ordering fully deterministic from parse/insert order.
- Test coverage: counterpart for Source/utils/ini.cpp; sole coverage.
- Go mapping: pkg/ini. Strategy: ordered map (slice of sections each with ordered key list + comment attachments) — Go maps are unordered so explicit ordering structures are mandatory. Round-trip test ported verbatim.
- Risks/open questions: line-ending policy of the original serializer (test only proves content, normalizing endings); whitespace tolerance on parse (accepts ` = `) vs strict emit (`=`) must be preserved.

Helpers: `set_up_scroll(Item&, SpellID)`, `clear_inventory()`.
- Depends on: `CanUseScroll`, `CalculateGold`, `GoldAutoPlace`, `ConsumeScroll`, `GetInventorySize`, `InventoryGridCells`, `MaxBeltItems`, `INVITEM_INV_FIRST`, `INVITEM_BELT_FIRST` (inv.h); `Player` fields InvList/InvGrid/_pNumInv/SpdList/HoldItem/_pRSpell/executedSpell, `Player::RemoveInvItem`, `Player::RemoveSpdBarItem` (player.h); `Item` fields _itype/_iMiscId/_iSpell/_ivalue/_iUid, `InitializeItem`, `UniqueItemFlags` (items.h); `InitCursor`, `LoadSpellData`, `LoadItemData` (cursor.h, engine/assets.hpp); `pcurs`, `CURSOR_HAND`, `leveltype`, `DTYPE_*` (cursor.h, levels/gendung.h); `SNetInitializeProvider(SELCONN_LOOPBACK, nullptr)` (storm/storm_net.hpp); `GOLD_MAX_LIMIT` (inv.h); `gbIsHellfire`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Inventory model: InvList (fixed array of Items), InvGrid (signed cell map: positive = item index+1 occupying, negative = continuation cell of item |v|−1), _pNumInv count, SpdList belt of MaxBeltItems (8), HoldItem.
  - Functions under test, byte-exact semantics: CanUseScroll (checks leveltype != TOWN, _pRSpell == _iSpell, _iMiscId == IMISC_SCROLL, item not empty, searches InvList when _pNumInv covers index and SpdList), CalculateGold (sum _ivalue over ItemType::Gold entries), GoldAutoPlace (fills existing gold piles to GOLD_MAX_LIMIT then new slots), RemoveInvItem(id) (clears grid cells via InvGrid sign decoding, compacts InvList and renumbers grid refs), RemoveSpdBarItem (clears slot), ConsumeScroll (uses executedSpell.spellFrom: exact slot or first match by spellId in inv then belt).
  - `set_up_scroll` equivalent: pcurs=CURSOR_HAND, leveltype=DTYPE_CATACOMBS, _pRSpell=spell, _itype=Misc, _iMiscId=IMISC_SCROLL, _iSpell=spell (lines 42–49).
  - Sprite-size table access: GetInventorySize(item) → Size(w,h) driven by item sprite data; requires LoadItemData + MPQ sprites for IDI_* constants.
  - MPQ-conditional skip: suite skips when spawn/diabdat missing (lines 22–38) — Go port should t.Skip similarly or use fixtures.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - CalculateGold: gold at InvList[1]=100,[5]=200,[2]=3,[3]=30 with _pNumInv=10 → 333 (lines 134–148).
  - GoldAutoPlace: existing pile 1000, held 4900 (= GOLD_MAX_LIMIT−100) → InvList[0]=GOLD_MAX_LIMIT (5000), InvList[1]=900 (lines 158–171). Encodes GOLD_MAX_LIMIT=5000.
  - RemoveInvItem middle: grid [1,-1,2,3,-3] → after removing index 1 → [1,-1,0,2,-2], InvList[0]=Misc, InvList[1]=Misc, _pNumInv=2 (lines 222–248).
  - RemoveInvItem front: same setup → after removing index 0 → [0,0,1,2,-2], InvList[0]=Ring, InvList[1]=Misc, _pNumInv=2 (lines 251–277).
  - UseScroll valid from InvList[2] with _pNumInv=5 → true (lines 89–93); from SpdList[2] → true (lines 96–100).
  - Invalid: leveltype=DTYPE_TOWN → false; _pRSpell=Healing (mismatch vs Firebolt scroll) → false; _iMiscId=IMISC_STAFF → false; cleared item → false — for both inventory and belt sources (lines 105–151).
  - ConsumeScroll: spellFrom=INVITEM_INV_FIRST consumes exact inv slot (grid[0]→0, count→0); spellFrom=0 consumes first matching; belt: spellFrom=INVITEM_BELT_FIRST+3 or 0 empties SpdList[3] (lines 280–345).
  - Item sizes (Hellfire only for first three): IDI_RUNEOFSTONE→(1,1), IDI_GREYSUIT→(2,2), IDI_AURIC→(1,1); always: IDI_SHORT_BATTLE_BOW→(2,3) (lines 350–386).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutates globals Players/MyPlayer/pcurs/leveltype per test; SNetInitializeProvider(LOOPBACK) needed before Remove*/Consume* (they send net commands). missingMpqAssets_ static shared across suite. No RNG.
- Test coverage: counterpart for Source/inv.cpp (+ Player methods in Source/player.cpp); this is the primary inv coverage alongside inventory_ui_test.cpp.
- Go mapping: internal/items (inv logic) — port CanUseScroll/CalculateGold/GoldAutoPlace/RemoveInvItem/ConsumeScroll as methods on Player or inv package funcs; grid semantics (signed cells) must be identical for savegame/net parity.
- Risks/open questions: net-command side effects of RemoveInvItem require a loopback provider in Go tests (or refactoring to command queue); GOLD_MAX_LIMIT is asserted implicitly (=5000 via 4900 = LIMIT−100 → result 5000).

### test/items_test.cpp
- Purpose: Verifies that every droppable unique item can actually be generated by the item-generation RNG pipeline, for Diablo (79 uniques) and Hellfire (99 uniques), using a time-seeded mt19937 driver over the game's deterministic seed-based item rolls.
- Public API: none (TEST_F `ItemsTest.AllDiabloUniquesCanDrop`, `ItemsTest.AllHellfireUniquesCanDrop`). Helper `GenerateAllUniques(bool hellfire, size_t expectedUniques)`.
- Depends on: `UniqueItems`, `UniqueItemFlags`, `AllItemsList`, `IsItemAvailable`, `IDI_GOLD`, `SetupAllItems`, `TryRandomUniqueItem`, `SetupItem`, `InitializeItem`, Item fields _iMiscId/_iMagical/_iUid, `ITEM_QUALITY_UNIQUE`, `_item_indexes` (items.h); `LoadItemData`, `LoadModArchives`/`UnloadModArchives` (engine/assets.hpp); `LoadSpellData` (spells.h); `SetRndSeed`, `AdvanceRndSeed` (engine/random.hpp); `gbIsSpawn/gbIsHellfire/gbIsMultiplayer` (game_mode.hpp); `StrCat` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `Players`/`MyPlayer` (player.h); std::mt19937 + uniform_int_distribution.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - The complete item-generation pipeline in Go: SetupAllItems, TryRandomUniqueItem, SetupItem with identical RNG consumption so unique outcomes match.
  - Game RNG: SetRndSeed(seed)/AdvanceRndSeed() semantics must consume the same number of draws in the same order as C++ (seeded per iteration from driver RNG, lines 79–80).
  - Item data tables loaded from MPQ (LoadItemData; Hellfire via LoadModArchives({"hf"})), availability predicate IsItemAvailable, dropRate>0 base lookup (lines 63–70).
  - Test driver: seed a mt19937-equivalent (Go: implement mt19937 or use a fixed PRNG — but to reproduce failures the driver seed is printed via testRunSeed; Go should log its seed too), roll uint32/int32 seeds, loop up to 1,000,000 iterations per unique.
  - unique loop: skip quest uniques (no droppable base → uniqueBaseIndex stays IDI_GOLD, line 73); uper=15 and targetLvl=UIMinLvl−4 when UIMinLvl>4 else uper=1/targetLvl=UIMinLvl (lines 92–96); SetupAllItems(..., forceNotIdentified? args (true,false) per call, line 100).
  - Assert each unique's _iUid obtainable and total distinct count == expected (79 Diablo / 99 Hellfire).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Expected unique counts: 79 (line 117), 99 (line 122).
  - max_iterations = 1000000 (line 54); testRunSeed = uint32(time(nullptr)) logged on failure (lines 49–50, 84).
  - uper=15 when `UIMinLvl - 4 > 0`, targetLvl = UIMinLvl−4; else uper=1, targetLvl=UIMinLvl (lines 92–96).
  - SetupAllItems signature order: (player, item, baseIndex, seed=AdvanceRndSeed(), targetLvl, uper, /*onlygood=*/true, /*forceNotIdentified=*/false) (line 100); TryRandomUniqueItem(testItem, baseIndex, targetLvl, uper, true, false) (line 101).
  - Base selection: first j in AllItemsList with IsItemAvailable(j) && iItemId==UIItemId; use it only if dropRate>0 else keep looking? — code sets uniqueBaseIndex only when dropRate>0 but breaks after first id match regardless (lines 63–70).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutates globals gbIsHellfire (via GenerateAllUniques), reloads mod archives mid-suite (UnloadModArchives/LoadModArchives — affects other suites if run in-process after; gtest suites share the process), gbIsSpawn/gbIsMultiplayer set in SetUpTestSuite (lines 35–36). Driver RNG seeded from wall time → NOT reproducible unless seed hardcoded on failure (documented in comment, line 48). Game RNG per-iteration via SetRndSeed is deterministic given seed.
- Test coverage: counterpart for Source/items.cpp item generation; the only unique-drop coverage.
- Go mapping: internal/items. Strategy: this test is the acceptance gate for the Go RNG+item pipeline; implement C++-compatible engine random (engine/random.hpp port) first, then port data tables, then this test with a --seed flag for reproducibility.
- Risks/open questions: requires real MPQ assets (hf mod zip for Hellfire); mt19937 driver must be replicated or replaced — driver seed differs from game seed so any PRNG works for the driver, but the game RNG must be exact; UniqueItemFlags reset per test (line 31) since generation sets flags.

- Determinism/thread-safety notes: fully deterministic given the fixture file; missing fixture silently proceeds with zeroed dLight (file-open null check only — no error, lines 20–26). No globals mutated; all locals. Single-threaded benchmark.
- Test coverage: benchmark counterpart for engine/render/light_render.cpp; correctness tests would live in test/light_render_tests.cpp if present (not in this batch).
- Go mapping: internal/render — lightmap_bench_test.go with checked-in testdata/dLight.dmp (already a repo fixture, portable). Strategy: port Lightmap::build math exactly; keep the fixture bytes identical for comparable output.
- Risks/open questions: the silent-zero fallback when fixture missing makes benchmark numbers meaningless without the file — Go version should fail loudly instead (minor improvement, behavior-compatible).

### test/main.cpp
- Purpose: gtest entry point for the whole test binary: enables headless mode (no error dialogs, no hardware cursor), sets macOS asset path, and installs a custom listener that summarizes skipped tests grouped by reason (MPQ-asset skips aggregated, no-reason skips attributed to setup failure).
- Public API: `int main(int argc, char **argv)` (line 76) — the test binary entry point. Class `SkippedTestListener : testing::EmptyTestEventListener` (anonymous namespace, line 17).
- Depends on: `devilution::HeadlessMode` global (headless_mode.hpp); `devilution::GetOptions().Graphics.hardwareCursor.SetValue(false)` (options.h); `devilution::paths::SetAssetsPath/BasePath` (utils/paths.h); gtest listener API (`testing::UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners()`, `TestPartResult::skipped()/message()`); SDL_VERSION_ATLEAST guard.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - TestMain(m *testing.M) equivalent in the Go test root: set HeadlessMode=true, disable hardware cursor, on darwin set assets path to BasePath()+"devilutionx.app/Contents/Resources/".
  - Skip-summary reporting: Go tests use t.Skip with reasons; a TestMain wrapper cannot intercept skips natively — replicate the summary by either (a) a custom skip-reason registry the fixtures write to, or (b) parsing `go test -v` output / json in a helper script. The C++ behavior: count skips, group by message, print "Test Skip Summary" block at end, folding any skip message containing "MPQ assets" into one line "MPQ assets (spawn.mpq or DIABDAT.MPQ) not found", and folding empty-reason skips into "(N tests automatically skipped due to test suite setup failure)" under the MPQ line (lines 44–73).
  - Exact strings matter for CI greps: header "Test Skip Summary", "Total tests skipped: N", bullet "• N test(s) skipped: <reason>", MPQ combined message.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - `devilution::HeadlessMode = true` before InitGoogleTest (line 80).
  - hardwareCursor=false only when SDL ≥ 2.0 (lines 83–86).
  - macOS assets path append `devilutionx.app/Contents/Resources/` (lines 88–92).
  - MPQ reason match: `reason.find("MPQ assets") != npos` (line 51); empty reason → "No reason provided" (lines 29–33); plural "s" when count>1 (line 61 etc.).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: listener has mutable member state (skipReasons map, totalSkipped) mutated from OnTestPartResult — gtest calls are serialized main-thread; unordered_map iteration order is nondeterministic in C++ (output line order of non-MPQ reasons may vary) — Go should sort for stable output.
- Test coverage: N/A — infrastructure (entry point for all test/*.cpp in this batch).
- Go mapping: devilutionGo test root TestMain (e.g. internal/testsupport or a top-level main_test.go). Strategy: implement a SkipSummary helper invoked via TestMain, fed by a package-level registry the fixtures (MPQ skip logic) append to; keep messages byte-identical for CI compatibility.
- Risks/open questions: Go's testing framework hides skip reasons from TestMain — needs the registry indirection or post-run output parsing; unordered_map ordering nondeterminism in C++ means exact line order was never guaranteed anyway (sorting in Go is safe).

# Volume III — batch 054

### test/math_test.cpp
- Purpose: Unit tests for `engine/displacement.hpp` world↔screen isometric transforms, 16.16 fixed-point displacement normalization, and the missile-facing `worldToNormalScreen()` projection.
- Public API: None (gtest suite). Tests: `WorldScreenTransformation` (L7), `NormalizeDisplacement` (L31), `MissileTransformation` (L47).
- Depends on: `devilution::Displacement` methods `worldToScreen()`, `screenToWorld()`, `worldToNormalScreen()`, `magnitude()`, `normalized()` from `engine/displacement.hpp` (include L3).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go test (Go test package mirroring `internal/engine` displacement tests) asserting exact int results for the transforms — these values double as spec for the transform implementation itself.
  - `worldToScreen`/`screenToWorld` reversible except for int truncation; screen→world is lossy (L25).
  - `normalized()` returns 16.16 fixed point (1.0 == 1<<16).
  - `magnitude()` is float (gtest uses EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ, tolerance ~4 ulps).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - (5,2).worldToScreen() == (-96,-112); (2,5).worldToScreen() == (96,-112) (L12, L19).
  - (342,-150).screenToWorld() == (0,10); round trip yields (320,-160) (L23-25).
  - (5,0) normalized == (1<<16, 0); (3,4) == (39321, 52428); (-5,2) == (-60848, 24339), magnitude 5.3851647f (L31-43).
  - (2,-2).worldToNormalScreen() == (-65536, 0); (8,1) == (-40235, -25865); (8,0) == (-46340, -23170) (L48-59). Tile metric: ±96/±112 per world unit ⇒ half-tile 32/32 (screen half-height 32 per unit ⇒ 96,112 are 3*32 / 3.5*32).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Pure functions, no globals, no RNG.
- Test coverage: This IS the counterpart for `engine/displacement.hpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/engine` (displacement_test.go); table-driven tests with exact expected Displacement values transcribed above.
- Risks/open questions: none

### test/mod_identity_test.cpp
- Purpose: Tests mod identity hashing/registry in `mods/mod_identity.h`: SHA-256 file hashing, hex encode/decode, manifest (`[mod]` ini) parsing, whitelist checks, active-identifier register/clear, save-extension policy, and dependency-based topological ordering.
- Public API: Test helpers `TmpPath` (L18), `WriteFile` (L23); 16 TEST(ModIdentity, …) cases L36-319.
- Depends on: `ComputeFileSha256`, `ModHashToHex`, `HexToModHash`, `IsHashWhitelisted`, `ParseModManifest`, `ModManifest`, `ModIdentifier`, `SatisfiesRequiredIdentifier`, `RegisterBuiltinModIdentifier`, `RegisterPackedModIdentifier`, `ClearModIdentifiers`, `ActiveModIdentifiers`, `GetActiveModSaveExtension`, `ModDependency`, `OrderModsByDependencies` (mods/mod_identity.h); `picosha2` reference hash.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - `ComputeFileSha256(path) ([32]byte, bool)` with chunked streaming reads (32 KiB internal buffer, verified by 100000-byte file at L52-66); missing file → false (L72-75).
  - `ModHashToHex` lowercase hex, `HexToModHash` accepts upper+lower, rejects length≠64 and non-hex chars (L86-112).
  - Manifest parser: `[mod]` section, keys name/description/version/author/homepage/license/saveExtension/programId; repeatable `requires` (string list) and `compatible` (hash list, invalid entries dropped) (L114-160); empty manifest → empty fields (L163-167).
  - `SatisfiesRequiredIdentifier(mod, hash)`: true if hash == mod.hash or in mod.manifest.compatibleWith (L171-188).
  - Registry: builtin entries are whitelisted with zero hash; packed entries hashed, whitelisted only if hash in approved list; `ClearModIdentifiers()` empties (L191-214).
  - `GetActiveModSaveExtension`: "" when none/no opt-in; strips leading dot; last active mod declaring one wins; any untrusted (non-whitelisted) active mod forces floor "msv" sandbox namespace; whitelisted declaration overrides floor (L218-262).
  - `OrderModsByDependencies`: dependencies-first, stable without deps, transitive chains, missing dep keeps mod (best-effort), cycles keep all mods (L268-319).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - SHA-256("abc") = `ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad`; SHA-256("") = `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` (L40, L47).
  - Chunk data pattern: `data[i] = (i*31+7) & 0xFF` for 100000 bytes (L56-58).
  - Sandbox save extension constant `"msv"` (L246); dot-stripping (".hsv"→"hsv").
  - Test hex round-trip hash: `hash[i] = i*7+1` (L87-88).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Mutates global `ActiveModIdentifiers`; every policy test must start/end with `ClearModIdentifiers()` (Go: reset in t.Cleanup). Temp files written to CWD named `Test_<suite>_<name><suffix>` — Go should use t.TempDir().
- Test coverage: Counterpart for `Source/mods/mod_identity.cpp`.
- Go mapping: `internal/mods` (identity_test.go); stdlib `crypto/sha256` + `encoding/hex`; manifest parse as manual ini scanner, not a generic lib (repeatable keys).
- Risks/open questions: The exact approved-whitelist contents live in production code, not here — port from `mods/mod_identity.cpp` separately.

  - Hellfire-only items in Diablo mode unpack to `_itype == None` (Scroll of Search idx 92 case, L803-815); empty item: idx 0xFFFF → None (L818); PackItem of None writes idx 0xFFFF (L829-840).
  - Gold: wValue 1000→ICURS_GOLD_SMALL, 1001→ICURS_GOLD_MEDIUM, 2500→ICURS_GOLD_LARGE; _ivalue == wValue, IDidx==IDI_GOLD, class ICLASS_GOLD, exact repack (L844-877).

(boy items fail at maxCharacterLevel+1, others at 31); unique-monster items (CF_USEFUL == CF_UPER15) level 31 fails; non-town monster items level 31 fails. Gold/ear exempt everywhere; each test asserts count>0 (fixtures contain applicable items).

- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Heavy global mutation per test: gbIsHellfire/gbIsMultiplayer/gbIsSpawn, Players vector, MyPlayer, mod archive load state — tests must be serial; gtest fixtures enforce fresh state per test. NetPackTest silently skips without MPQ assets (C++ `missingMpqAssets_` static, Go: t.Skip).
- Test coverage: Counterpart for `Source/pack.cpp`, `Source/itemdat.cpp`/item generation, `Source/player.cpp` CreatePlayer/CalcPlrItemVals.
- Go mapping: `internal/pack` (pack_test.go) — golden vectors ported as literal structs; validation tests table-driven; ear/gold/unique-bug as separate Go subtests. `PlayerPack` via encoding/binary LittleEndian reader over a fixed byte layout.
- Risks/open questions: Golden item tables are ~170 rows × 41 fields — transcription risk; recommend generating the Go tables mechanically from this file. `UnPackItem` determinism implies the Go item generator (prefix/suffix/unique tables) must be byte-exact, driven by iSeed — the largest hidden dependency of this suite.

### test/palette_blending_test.cpp
- Purpose: Functional test for `GenerateBlendedLookupTable`: blend of two palette indices must map to the palette index nearest to the 50/50 averaged RGB, symmetric in arguments.
- Public API: `PrintTo(const SDL_Color&, std::ostream*)` for gtest output (L21), matcher `ColorIs(r,g,b)` (L29), test `GenerateBlendedLookupTableTest.BasicTest` (L42).

- Requirements for Go port:
  - `GenerateBlendedLookupTable(pal [256]color.RGBA)` filling a [256][256]uint8 LUT where LUT[a][b] = nearest palette entry to ((pal[a]+pal[b])/2 per channel, truncated int math), symmetric.
  - Optional black-16 packed LUT: `Black16[(a<<0)|(b<<8)]` packs two results as `res1 | (res2<<8)` (L83-85).
  - Go test asserts the exact expected values below on the synthetic palette.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Synthetic palette identical to benchmark: r=i*max(j,1), g=i*j, b=i*2 (L32-40).
  - Expected LUT values: [100][100]=100; [17][150]=[150][17]=86; [27][130]=[130][27]=15; [0][100]=[100][0]=82; [0][200]=[200][0]=196 (L47-77).
  - Palette spot values: pal[17]=(17,0,34), pal[150]=(44,44,44), pal[86]=(22,22,44), pal[27]=(27,0,54), pal[130]=(4,4,4), pal[15]=(15,0,30), pal[100]=(36,36,72), pal[82]=(18,18,36), pal[0]=(0,0,0), pal[200]=(24,24,16), pal[196]=(12,12,8) (L49-75) — b channel wraps mod 256 (i*2 up to 126; pal[200] b=16 proves 200 = j=3,i=8 → r=8*3=24, g=24, b=16).
  - Black16: [100|100<<8] = 82|82<<8; [100|200<<8] = 82|196<<8 (L83-84).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: Writes process-global LUT; tests must not run concurrently with anything reading the LUT.
- Test coverage: Counterpart for `Source/utils/palette_blending.cpp` (+ kd-tree indirectly).
- Go mapping: `internal/render` (palette_blend_test.go); use color.RGBA or a [3]uint8; keep exact expected constants.
- Risks/open questions: Tie-breaking in "nearest palette entry" is defined by kd-tree traversal order — port `palette_kd_tree` semantics first or values like 86/15 may differ.

  - `FindClosestValidPosition(ok func(Point) bool, center Point, minRadius, maxRadius int) (Point, bool)`: rings by increasing radius; with fixed min==max==3 forms a square ring with inset corners (no pure corner tiles); with min 0 max 50 covers every tile of 101×101 exactly once except the four extreme corners (skipped by inset/rounded search space); with min 1 skips center; first candidate at min radius 21 is `{0, +21}` offset (up in coordinate space) (L246-250).

Constants' values live in path.h; the cost pairing axis↔world-diagonal is the tested invariant.

Direction indices: enum order None,Up,Left,Right,Down,UpLeft,UpRight,DownRight,DownLeft = 0..8 (L48-56) — FindPath writes these int8 values.

### test/random_test.cpp
- Purpose: Exhaustive behavioral spec of the Diablo LCG (Borland constants) and its distributions: raw engine, abs distribution, mod/shift-mod distributions, negative return values.
- Public API: Tests: `RandomEngineParams` (line 11), `AbsDistribution` (line 36), `ModDistributionInvalidRange` (line 105), `ShiftModDistributionSingleRange` (line 121), `ShiftModDistributionSignCarry` (line 143), `ShiftModDistributionLowBits` (line 160), `ShiftModDistributionHighBits` (line 204), `ModDistributionSignPreserving` (line 240), `NegativeReturnValues` (line 258).
- Depends on: `engine/random.hpp` — `SetRndSeed`, `GenerateRandomNumber`, `AdvanceRndSeed`, `GenerateRnd`, `GetLCGEngineState`, `DiscardRandomValues`.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - LCG: state' = 22695477 * state + 1 (mod 2^32), uint32 arithmetic (lines 14-15, 23).
  - `SetRndSeed(0)`: first GenerateRandomNumber() == 1, second == 22695477+1 = 22695478 (lines 20-23).
  - After discarding to the 9999th/10000th draws from state 1: states 3495122800 then 3007658545 (lines 30-33); `DiscardRandomValues(9997)` skips values (line 28).
  - `AdvanceRndSeed` = abs((int32)state) with UB-pinned behavior: INT_MIN → INT_MIN (line 41); ±x → x. Golden pairs: 3604671459→0, 0→1, 2914375622→1, 3604671460→22695477, 3604671458→22695477, 1902003768→429496729, 1012371854→429496729, 189776845→1212022642, 2724598777→1212022642, 76596137→2147483646, 2837779485→2147483646, 766891974→2147483647, 2147483648→2147483647 (lines 39-61).
  - `GenerateRnd(bound)` with bound <= 0 returns 0 WITHOUT advancing engine state (lines 107-115, incl. bound = INT_MIN).
  - bound == 1: result 0, engine still advances (lines 121-133); INT_MIN abs value still yields 0.
  - bound in [1, 32768): value = (AdvanceRndSeed result) >> 16 (arithmetic/sign-carry shift on int32), then mod bound (C++ sign-preserving %). INT_MIN >> 16 = -32768; -32768 % 32767 == -1 (line 152).
  - Low/high-bit golden values for bound 32767 (lines 165-238): 0→0, 1→0, -1→0, 64→0, -64→0, 65→0, -65→0, 128→0, -128→0, 7625→0, -7625→0, 32458→0, -32458→0, 32768→0, -32768→0, 65534→0 (bound 32766), -65534→0 (bound 32766), 65535→0, -65535→0, 65536→1, -65536→1, 131072→2, -131072→2, 262144→4, -262144→4, 22695477→346, -22695477→346, 429496729→6553, -429496729→6553, 1212022642→18493, -1212022642→18493, 2147483646→0, -2147483646→0, 2147483647→0, -2147483647→0 (note 2^31-k >>16 = 32767 → 32767%32767 = 0).
  - bound in [32768, INT_MAX]: plain sign-preserving %: INT_MIN % 32768 == 0, % 32769 == -2, % 65535 == -32768, % INT_MAX == -1 (lines 242-253).
  - Negative outputs from INT_MIN seed (line 258+): GenerateRnd(3)=-2, (5)=-3, (6)=-2, (7)=-1, (11)=-10, (17)=-9, (19)=-12, (22)=-10, (23)=-16, (25)=-18, (27)=-17, (29)=-27, (31)=-1; bounds {9,10,12,13,14,15,18,20,21,24,26,28,30} → -8; (37)=-23, (38)=-12, (40)=-8, (41)=-9, (52)=-8, (80)=-48, (100)=-68; all powers of 2 from 1..16384 → 0.
- 1:1 constraints: ALL constants above are line-cited golden values; Go must emulate 32-bit wrapping multiply (`uint32`), cast to int32, Go's `%` matches C++ sign-preserving semantics; Go `>>` on int32 is arithmetic — matches. abs(INT_MIN) must return INT_MIN (not panic/negate-to-self is fine in Go: int32 math.Abs won't work; implement `if v == math.MinInt32 { return v }; if v < 0 { return -v }`).

  - Case 1 (line 10): rect{0,0,10,20} of uint8: contains (9,9) true; (-1,-1) false; (257,257) false (i.e. point is int, larger than rect coords — mixed-width comparison works).
  - Case 2 (line 19): rect uint8 {0,0,255,255}: contains int8 (5,5) true; (-1,-1) false; (-2,-2) false.
  - Case 3 (line 28): rect int8 {-10,-10,127,127}: contains uint8 (0,0) true; (255,255) false.
- 1:1 constraints: Exact three scenarios above; the essential property is no wrap: comparing int8 -1 against uint8 bounds must not convert -1 to 255. Lines 11-15, 20-23, 29-32.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: N/A — trivial, pure.
- Test coverage: This is the test for `engine/rectangle.h`.
- Go mapping: devilutionGo `internal/engine` (geometry): implement `RectangleOf[T Integer]` with `Contains(p PointOf[T]) bool` using signed-safe comparison (promote both to int64 internally); mirror these three tests.
- Risks/open questions: Go generics can't directly mix uint8 rect with int8 point in one call — the C++ tests imply contains() does heterogeneous comparison; Go API may need `ContainsPoint(x, y int) bool` with explicit widening at call sites.

### test/str_cat_test.cpp
- Purpose: Minimal tests for string concatenation helpers `StrCat` (variadic, returns std::string) and `BufCopy` (variadic, writes into char buffer, returns end pointer), plus `LeftPad`.
- Public API: Tests: `StrCatBasicTest` (line 11), `LeftPadTest` (line 16), `BufCopyBasicTest` (line 21).
- Depends on: `utils/str_cat.hpp` (`StrCat(...)`, `LeftPad(uint8_t, width, fill)`, `BufCopy(char*, ...)`).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go equivalent: `StrCat(args ...any) string` concatenating strings and integers (e.g. "a","b","c",5 → "abc5", line 12).
  - `LeftPad(uint8(5), 2, '0')` → "05" (line 18) — zero-pad numeric to width.
  - `BufCopy(buf, ...)` writes into caller buffer and returns end pointer/length: buf "abc5" length 4 into char[5] (lines 22-25). In Go this is naturally `AppendBytes`/`strconv.AppendInt` style; port as append-to-[]byte returning the slice.
- 1:1 constraints: Exact outputs: "abc5" (lines 12, 24), "05" (line 18). BufCopy must fit NUL in char[5] for "abc5" (C string).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: N/A — trivial.
- Test coverage: This is the test for `utils/str_cat.h`.
- Go mapping: devilutionGo `internal/util/strcat` — mostly unnecessary in Go (fmt.Sprintf/strings.Repeat); keep LeftPad helper for hot paths avoiding reflection; port the three tests.
- Risks/open questions: none.

### test/text_render_integration_test.cpp
- Purpose: Golden-image integration test for the text renderer. Parameterized over 26 in-file fixtures covering plain DrawString, per-arg colored DrawStringWithColors, KerningFitSpacing, AlignCenter/Right, newlines, overflow, cursor positions, and highlight ranges; renders to an indexed SDL surface and pixel-compares against PNGs in `test/fixtures/text_render_integration_test/` (path const at line 42).
- Public API: `main(argc, argv)` custom gtest main supporting `--update_expected` (lines 442–457, unknown args → exit 64); file-static `UpdateExpected` flag (line 37); everything else in an anonymous namespace.
- Depends on: `LoadFileInMem` (engine/load_file.hpp) to load `ui_art\diablo.pal`; `DrawString`/`DrawStringWithColors`/`TextRenderOptions`/`DrawStringFormatArg`/`UiFlags` (engine/render/text_render.hpp); `DrawHorizontalLine`/`DrawVerticalLine` (engine/render/primitive_render.hpp); `OwnedSurface`/`Surface` (engine/surface.hpp); `LoadPNG` (utils/png.h); `WriteSurfaceToFilePng` (utils/surface_to_png.hpp); `SDLWrap::AllocPalette` (utils/sdl_wrap.h); `CopyFileOverwrite` (utils/paths.h); `StrCat` (utils/str_cat.hpp); `PAL8_RED`/`PAL8_BLUE` (engine/palette.h); `Rectangle`/`Point`/`Size`/`Displacement` geometry types.
- Requirements for Go port:
  - A golden-image test harness for internal/render text drawing with 26 named fixtures matching the exact names/widths/heights/fmts/args/opts of the C++ `Fixtures[]` array (lines 58–357).
  - Render into a palettized surface of `width+20 × height+20`, set diablo.pal as palette, draw a PAL8_RED 1px border around the `width×height` rect inset at (10,10), then render text into the rect inset by 1 (DrawWithBorder, ~line 397).
  - Write actual PNG, load actual+expected PNGs, compare per-byte palette indices with pitch-aware indexing (y*pitch+x); on mismatch report first differing (x,y) with both index values; support `--update_expected` to overwrite expected from actual.
  - Diagonal-blit surface from MPQ or embedded palette path must resolve `ui_art\diablo.pal` (256×3 bytes).
  - Colored-args variant: `{}` placeholders each take a string + color flag; mix with literal text and `\n` inside both fmt and arg values.
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Fixture table values (lines 58–357), e.g. `basic` 96×15 "DrawString"; `horizontal_overflow` 50×28; `kerning_fit_spacing` 120×15; center/right align variants 170×15 / 170×42; cursor fixtures "Hello World" 120×15 with cursorPosition 0/5/11, cursorStatic=true; multiline 100×50 with positions 10/11/14/22; highlight fixtures: partial {5,10} " Worl", full {0,11}, multiline {3,8} "lo\nWo", highlightColor PAL8_BLUE. Default opts flags = UiFlags::ColorUiGold.
  - Only fixture entries with non-empty `args` use DrawStringWithColors (RenderAndCompareTest, ~line 372).
  - `PrintTo` prints fixture name; test names replace '-' with '_' (line 431).
  - Pixel comparison loops y in [0,expectedSurface->h), x in [0,expectedSurface->w) — note x bound uses w, y uses h, both pitch-indexed (~lines 383–389).
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: static suite palette (SetUpTestSuite/TearDownTestSuite) shared across params; file-static `UpdateExpected` mutated only in main before tests run. No RNG. Golden files depend on exact font rasterization — any Go renderer difference will surface here (that's the point).
- Test coverage: this file IS the test; fixtures in test/fixtures/text_render_integration_test/*.png.
- Go mapping: internal/render (or internal/render/textrender_test) — Go golden tests with same 26 cases; store expected PNGs in same relative fixture dir; use image/paletted and Go PNG decode; pixel index comparison equivalent (de-code as paletted or convert RGB back to palette indices via palette LUT).
- Risks/open questions: Go PNG decode of palettized images returns color.Palette — must compare palette indices (or map RGB→index via the diablo.pal LUT) rather than RGBA bytes; expected fixtures were generated by the C++ renderer, so a 1:1 Go rasterizer is required to pass byte-identical.

### test/tile_properties_test.cpp
- Purpose: Unit tests for tile solidity/walkability queries (`IsTileSolid`, `IsTileNotSolid`, `IsTileWalkable`, `CanStep`) by manually setting dPiece/SOLData/dObject entries rather than loading a level.
- Public API: none (anonymous-namespace TESTs only).
- Depends on: `dPiece`, `dObject` (levels/gendung.h); `SOLData` (levels/dun_tile.hpp); `TileProperties` enum with at least `None`/`Solid` (levels/tile_properties.hpp); `Objects[]` with `_oSolidFlag`, `_otype` (objects.h); `_object_id::OBJ_L1LDOOR`; `IsTileSolid`/`IsTileNotSolid`/`IsTileWalkable`/`CanStep` (levels/tile_properties.hpp / gendung).
- Requirements for Go port:
  - Go unit tests replicating the three test groups: Solid (line 14), Walkable (line 30), CanStepTest (line 59).
  - Mutability of the global tile arrays and SOLData table from tests (or injected level-state accessor in Go).
  - Object table access: set `Objects[0]._oSolidFlag`, `_otype` to emulate doors.
  - Out-of-bounds query semantics: `IsTileSolid({-1,1})` returns false AND `IsTileNotSolid({-1,1})` also returns false (line 26–27 — current code reads OOB; Go must bounds-check and return false for both).
- 1:1 constraints:
  - Walkable truth table (lines 30–57): SOL Solid ⇒ not walkable, with ignoreDoors=true still not walkable (non-door object case); object solid ⇒ not walkable; door OBJ_L1LDOOR with _oSolidFlag=true ⇒ blocked normally, walkable with ignoreDoors=true; open door (_oSolidFlag=false) ⇒ walkable both; solid SOL + open door ⇒ blocked, walkable with ignoreDoors.
  - CanStep truth table (lines 59–103): all 4 open-space diagonal steps true; SOLData[1]=Solid with dPiece[1][0]=1: stepping to/from a solid destination is allowed; cardinal steps ignore solids; diagonal {0,0}↔{1,1} blocked when either adjacent corner solid; boundary between two solid corners ({0,0} and {1,1} both solid) blocks {1,0}↔{0,1}; then mirrored for the other diagonal pair.
- Determinism/thread-safety notes: mutates globals dPiece/SOLData/dObject/Objects directly — tests are order-dependent within file; no cleanup between tests (each sets its own cells). No RNG.
- Test coverage: this is the test for levels/tile_properties.
- Go mapping: internal/dungeon (tileprops_test.go) — mirror the truth tables; keep globals behind the level-state struct so tests can inject.
- Risks/open questions: C++ OOB read note (line 26 comment) — Go version must bounds-check, not reproduce the UB.

# Graphics — G1–G5

# Graphics Pipeline — 1:1 Ebitengine Port Spec

Extracted read-only from devilutionX @ `ca91d778fba92a1f680afb1fb2cdf09337ff1b42` (cwd `/home/blaze/github/bmcszk/devilutionX`).
Every `file:line` citation below was opened and read during this extraction. Byte-level examples were produced by
decoding real asset files (`assets/data/*.clx`, and fixtures extracted read-only from a local `DIABDAT.MPQ` into
`/tmp/dgx/`), never from memory.

**Terminology used throughout**
- *micro tile / frame* = one 32×32 (or 32×31) tile drawing primitive inside a dungeon CEL frame.
- *tile* = one dungeon tile = 64×32 px = 2×2 micro tiles (`TILE_WIDTH 64`, `TILE_HEIGHT 32`, `Source/levels/dun_tile.hpp:7`).
- *index* = an 8-bit palette index. devilutionX renders into an **8-bit indexed backbuffer** and only the palette
  (`logical_palette`/`system_palette`, 256 × RGB8) turns indices into colours at present time.
- *TRN* = a 256-byte palette→palette lookup (`dst = trn[src]`), including the 16 light tables.

**The single most important parity fact:** in the C++ game, the entire world is drawn as *indices*, and lighting,
unique-monster colours, class colours, petrification, infravision and 50 % transparency are all **exact 8-bit table
lookups**, not blends. Any Go renderer that reaches for `ColorScale`/alpha compositing instead of reproducing those
tables *will not* be pixel-exact. Section G4/G5/G8 define the required Go equivalents; the recommended architecture
is "index textures + one palette-lookup Kage fragment shader" (see G10).

### Formats & algorithms

**1. There is exactly one logical framebuffer: an 8-bit indexed surface of `gnScreenWidth × gnScreenHeight`
(default 640×480), `PalSurface`.** Everything — world, panels, text, cursor, automap — is blitted into that single
buffer. There is no world-vs-UI layer separation in C++; ordering is purely "later draw wins".

```
Source/engine/dx.cpp:58   SDL_Surface *PalSurface;              // 8-bit INDEX8 surface, we render to this
Source/engine/dx.cpp:122   ... SDL_CreateSurface/... /*depth=*/8, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_INDEX8)
```
Present path (`Source/engine/dx.cpp:287` `RenderPresent`):
```
if (renderer != nullptr) {              // SDL2/3 GPU path
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0,0,0,255); SDL_RenderClear(renderer);
    SDL_UpdateTexture(texture, nullptr, surface->pixels, surface->pitch);   // 8-bit + palette -> RGBA
    SDL_RenderTexture(renderer, texture, nullptr, nullptr);                 // logical presentation scales
    SDL_RenderPresent(renderer);
} else {                                 // surface path (SDL1 / direct)
    UpdateOutputSurface();               // possibly SDL_UpdateWindowSurfaceRects(dirtyRects)
}
```
`BltFast` (`Source/engine/dx.cpp:181`) is the "copy PalSurface → window" step, called *before* `RenderPresent`;
with a renderer it is a no-op full-update, with the surface path it records up to 16 dirty rects
(`Source/engine/dx.cpp:60` `MaxDirtyRects = 16`). **Dirty-rect bookkeeping is a presentation optimisation only and is
explicitly not ported** (Ebitengine redraws the whole logical screen each frame).

**2. Frame sequence.** `DrawAndBlit()` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1834`) per call:
```
hgt = 0
drawHealth/drawMana/drawControlButtons/drawBelt from backbuffer_state component flags
if (gnScreenWidth > mainPanel.width || IsRedrawEverything()) { full redraw: hgt = gnScreenHeight, drawCtrlPan=true }
else if (IsRedrawViewport()) { hgt = gnViewportHeight; drawCtrlPan = false }
out = GlobalBackBuffer()                      // Surface over PalSurface, full screen
UndrawCursor(out)                             // restore the pixels saved behind the cursor (see below)
nthread_UpdateProgressToNextGameTick()        // ProgressToNextGameTick <- 0..128  (rendering interpolation!)
DrawView(out, ViewPosition)                   // world + automap + QoL labels + panels + flasks-upper
if (drawCtrlPan) DrawMainPanel(out)
if (drawHealth)  DrawLifeFlaskLower(out, ...)
if (drawMana)    DrawManaFlaskLower(out, ...); DrawSpell(out)
if (drawControlButtons) DrawMainPanelButtons(out)
if (drawBelt)    DrawInvBelt(out)
if (drawChatInput) DrawChatBox(out)
DrawXPBar(out); [DrawFlaskValues(...)]
DrawCursor(out)                               // saves pixels behind cursor, then blits cursor sprite
DrawFPS(out)
DrawMain(hgt, drawInfoBox, drawHealth, drawMana, drawBelt, drawControlButtons)   // BltFast of regions
RedrawComplete(); clear component flags
RenderPresent()
```

**3. `DrawView` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1313`) order** — this is the definitive "draw order" the port
must reproduce:
```
offset = {}; CalcFirstTilePosition(startPosition, offset);
DrawGame(out, startPosition, offset);
if (AutomapActive) DrawAutomap(out.subregionY(0, gnViewportHeight));
[_DEBUG grid / debug text]
DrawItemNameLabels(out)        // QoL item labels
DrawMonsterHealthBar(out)
DrawFloatingNumbers(out, startPosition, offset)   // damage numbers
[store text, inventory, spellbook, durability, level button, char, quest log, stash, visual store,
 unique info box, quest text, spell list, gold split/withdraw, help, chat log, death screen, pause menu,
 diablo msg, plr msg, gamemap menu, help screen (doom_draw), info box]
UpdateLifeManaPercent()
DrawLifeFlaskUpper(out); DrawManaFlaskUpper(out)
```
`DrawGame` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1229`) does, in order:
```
out = fullOut.subregionY(0, zoom ? (gnViewportHeight+1)/2 : gnViewportHeight)   // zoom renders at half res
columns = tileColumns; rows = tileRows
if (CanPanelsCoverView() && (leftPanel||rightPanel)) columns -= zoom ? 2 : 4
UpdateMissilesRendererData()                       // interpolates missiles + buckets by rendering tile
if (MyPlayer->isWalking()) expand rows/columns by direction  (North/South: rows+=2; NE: cols+1 rows+2; E/W: cols+1;
                                                              SE/SW/NW: cols+1 rows+1)
Lightmap lightmap = Lightmap::build(perPixelLighting, position, offset, gnScreenWidth, gnViewportHeight,
                                    rows, columns, out.at(0,0), out.pitch(), LightTables,
                                    FullyLitLightTable, FullyDarkLightTable, dLight, MicroTileLen)
DrawFloor(out, lightmap, position, offset, rows, columns)
DrawTileContent(out, lightmap, position, offset, rows, columns)
DrawOOB(out, lightmap, position, offset, rows, columns)
if (zoom) Zoom(fullOut.subregionY(0, gnViewportHeight))
```

**4. Row-walk (the isometric scan order).** Identical in `DrawFloor`/`DrawTileContent`/`DrawOOB`
(`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:955`, `:992`, `:1088`):
```
for i in 0..rows-1:
  for j in 0..columns-1:
     tilePos  += Direction::East        # (+1,-1)
     bufferPos.x += TILE_WIDTH
  tilePos  += Direction::West * columns # rewind
  bufferPos.x -= columns * TILE_WIDTH
  bufferPos.y += TILE_HEIGHT/2          # 16
  if (i & 1) == 1: tilePos.x++; columns--;          bufferPos.x += TILE_WIDTH/2   #  32
  else:            tilePos.y++; columns++;          bufferPos.x -= TILE_WIDTH/2   # -32
```
`Direction::East = {+1,-1}`, `West = {-1,+1}`, `North = {0,-1}`, `South = {0,+1}`, `NorthEast = {+1,0}`,
`NorthWest = {0,-1}`… conversion table: `Source/engine/displacement.hpp:247` `fromDirection`.
`DrawTileContent` first does `rows += MicroTileLen` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:995`) so tall walls from
rows below can still overwrite. `DrawOOB` uses `rows + 5` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1089`).

**5. Viewport geometry** (`CalcViewportGeometry`, `Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1675`, at 640×480/zoom off):
```
zoomFactor = zoom ? 2 : 1
screenWidth  = gnScreenWidth  / zoomFactor      # 640
screenHeight = gnScreenHeight / zoomFactor      # 480
panelHeight  = mainPanel.height / zoomFactor    # 128
pixelsToPanel = screenHeight - panelHeight      # 352
playerPosition = { screenWidth/2 , pixelsToPanel/2 }          # {320, 176}
tilesToTop  = (playerPosition.y + TILE_HEIGHT - 1) / TILE_HEIGHT  # (176+31)/32 = 6
tilesToLeft = (playerPosition.x + TILE_WIDTH - 1) / TILE_WIDTH  # (320+63)/64 = 5
startPosition = playerPosition - { tilesToLeft*64, tilesToTop*32 }   # {-0, -16} → {0,-16}
tileShift = North*tilesToTop + West*tilesToLeft
if (tilesToLeft*64 >= playerPosition.x) { startPosition += {32,-16}; tileShift += NorthEast }
elif (tilesToTop*32 < playerPosition.y) { startPosition += {0,-32}; tileShift += North }
tileOffset = { startPosition.x - 32, startPosition.y + 16 - 1 }
renderStart = startPosition - {32, 16}
tileRows    = (viewportHeight - renderStart.y + 16 - 1) / 16
tileColumns = (screenWidth     - renderStart.x + 64 - 1) / 64
```
These exact formulas have golden values already in `test/scrollrt_test.cpp:13` (tiles-in-view) and
`:80` (tile offset) — **port the test first, the formula second.**

**6. Zoom mode.** `Graphics.zoom` renders the world into a 320×240 region and then `Zoom()`
(`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1121`) doubles it *in place, back-to-front* (byte-wise: for each of the top
`h/2` source rows, duplicate every pixel horizontally, then `memcpy` the doubled row into the row below). In
Ebitengine this is simply "draw the world buffer with `FilterNearest` at 2×", but note the C++ zoom only doubles the
*viewport*, not the panels, and the mouse coordinates are halved (`AlterMousePositionViaZoom`,
`Source/cursor.cpp:682`).

**7. Palette lifecycle.**
- `LoadPalette(path)` (`Source/engine/palette.cpp:175`): reads a 768-byte `.pal` (256 × RGB, 3 bytes each,
  verified on `/tmp/dgx/levels/l1data/l1_1.pal` → `size 768, first 6 bytes 00 00 00 68 68 7A`) into
  `logical_palette` (`std::array<SDL_Color,256>`).
- `UpdateSystemPalette` (`:152`) applies **brightness tone mapping** (`ApplyGlobalBrightness`, `:118`) producing
  `system_palette`, then `SystemPaletteUpdated(first,ncolor)` pushes it to the SDL surface palette and
  `RedrawEverything()`.
  Tone curve: `a = -(brightness/100)*2.0`; `f(x) = a*x² + (1-a)*x` over `x = c/255`, output
  `uint8((clamp(f,0,1)*255)+0.5)` (`Source/engine/palette.cpp:96-110`). Default brightness → identity.
- Fades (`:271`/`:324`): time-driven; `ApplyFadeLevel(fadeval, dst, src)` = `dst[i] = (fadeval*src[i])/256` per
  channel (`:140`). Loop: `for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 256; i = fr * (elapsed_ms) / 50)` with `fr *= 3`; each step
  re-sets the palette and presents. **Fade = whole-palette multiply, not a screen overlay.**
- Cycling (`palette_update_caves` `:363`, `_crypt` `:373`, `_hive` `:391`): `CycleColors(from,to)` rotates
  `logical_palette[from..to]`, `system_palette[from..to]`, **all rows and columns of
  `paletteTransparencyLookup`** in the same range (`Source/engine/palette.cpp:52-64`). Called from the tick loop
  (`Source/diablo.cpp:3521`), i.e. after ticks, not after frames.
- There is **no gamma** in this fork: only the brightness tone-map above.
- **No `SetPalette` function exists in this tree**; the equivalents are `LoadPalette` (`Source/engine/palette.cpp:175`),
  `UpdateSystemPalette` (`:152`), `SystemPaletteUpdated` (`:170`) and `SetLogicalPaletteColor(i,color)` (`:406`,
  which also refreshes one row of the blending LUT).

### Ebitengine mapping
- `Layout(outsideW, outsideH) (640, 480)` **fixed** (`Source/options.h:41`). Ebitengine then letterboxes/scales the
  logical screen; set `ebiten.SetScreenScalingPosition(...)`/`SetFilter(ebiten.FilterNearest)` for the vanilla
  integer-scale behaviour (`SDL_LOGICAL_PRESENTATION_INTEGER_SCALE`, `Source/utils/display.cpp:734`).
  For user-selected non-integer scaling use `ebiten.FilterPixelated` (v2.9+) which is "nearest with crisp edges";
  the C++ "bilinear scaling" quality option has no exact 8-bit equivalent and is declared *cosmetic, not ported*.
- Buffers (all allocated once at startup, never per frame):
  1. `world *ebiten.Image` 640×480 — floor + tile content + entities + automap (the `out` region passed to
     `DrawGame` is a *subregion* of the same buffer in C++; we can use one buffer and skip the panel rows).
  2. `ui *ebiten.Image` 640×480 — panels, flasks, menus, text, cursor. Separating world/UI is a **Go-only**
     optimisation: it lets us skip re-drawing the world when only a panel component is dirty (mirrors the
     `PanelDrawComponent` flags of `Source/engine/backbuffer_state.hpp:41`). It must not change pixels.
  3. `final *ebiten.Image` (or draw straight to `screen`) = `world` then `ui`, one `DrawImage` each.
- The C++ "index8 buffer + palette" becomes: keep an `indices []uint8` CPU mirror? **No.** Keep
  *index textures on the GPU* and one `palette *ebiten.Image` (256×1 RGBA) updated on every palette change
  (`UpdateSystemPalette`, cycling, fades). See G4/G10 for the shader contract.
- `Draw()` must contain **zero** allocation and zero `At()/ReadPixels()` (perf tips:
  https://ebitengine.org/en/documents/performancetips.html "Don't call (*Image).ReplacePixels too much").
- Frame pacing: Ebitengine `Update()` is the game tick driver (20 TPS logic inside, see dg-epic-01); `Draw()` runs
  at 60 FPS and computes `progress = ProgressToNextGameTick ∈ [0,128)` — exactly the C++ model where
  `nthread_UpdateProgressToNextGameTick()` is called from the draw path (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1866`).

### Parity test
`TestViewportGeometry` table-driven over the four cases in `test/scrollrt_test.cpp` (640×480, 640×480 zoom,
960×540, 640×512, 768×480 zoom) asserting `tileRows`, `tileColumns`, `tileOffset.x/y` equal to the C++ numbers.
`TestFrameOrder`: instrumented renderer recording an ordered list of (layer, kind) ops; assert the list equals the
C++ order encoded from `DrawAndBlit` + `DrawView` above.
`TestPaletteFadeLevel`: port `ApplyFadeLevel` and assert `dst[i] == uint8(fadeval*src[i]/256)` for all
`fadeval ∈ {0,1,255,256}` against a C++-dumped golden (1024-byte array per step).

### Open questions
- Does the Go port need the 1920×1080 "big UI" mode (Volume I §7 mentions it)? The 640×480 decision here assumes no.
- `PanelDrawComponent` partial redraws save CPU in C++ surface mode; in Go the world re-draw is one batch — confirm
  we still want the world/ui split (adds a 640×480 offscreen; offscreens don't batch with the atlas).

### Formats & algorithms

**1. Dungeon CEL (macro→micro frame blob, big-endian frame table).**
Verified on the real file `/tmp/dgx/levels/l1data/l1.cel`:
```
bytes 0..3    u32 LE  = 0x0000045f = 1119   -> frame count (LE!)
bytes 4..(4+4*n)  u32 LE frame offsets, ascending, last == file size (738836)  [verified: ascending? True,
                                         offs[n]==size]
frame i begins at offs[i]; NO per-frame header (raw pixel runs only)
```
Caveat: `Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:188` reads these offsets with **`Swap32LE`** (i.e. big-endian swap)
because the retail `*.cel` frame table is documented as big-endian in vanilla, while devilutionX's
`GetDunFrame` (`Source/engine/render/dun_render.hpp:123`) also uses `Swap32LE` — but after `ReencodeDungeonCels`
rewrites the table with `WriteLE32` (`Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:216`). **This is a real trap: the input
table is BE-swapped, the re-encoded output table is LE, and `GetDunFrame` still swaps.** Read
`GetReencodedSize`/`ReencodeDungeonCels` again when porting; do not "fix" it. Empirically on our GOG file the table
is already ascending-LE and `Swap32LE` yields the same values only because… it doesn't. See "Open questions".

Frame pixel formats (`Source/levels/dun_tile.hpp:19` doc comments, all **bottom row first**):

| TileType | encoding | size after re-encode |
|---|---|---|
| `Square` (0) | flat `32*32` index bytes | 1024 |
| `TransparentSquare` (1) | 32 rows of int8 RLE, runs never cross a row: `v>0` → copy v pixels; `v<0` → skip `-v` transparent | as-is (`Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:226`) |
| `LeftTriangle` (2) | 31 rows, widths 2,4,…,32,…,2; **2 unused padding bytes before every even row (bottom-counted)** | 512 (`544-32`) |
| `RightTriangle` (3) | same, padding **after** every even row | 512 |
| `LeftTrapezoid` (4) | triangle-lower part (16 rows, widths 2..32) with padding, then a flat 32×16 rect on top | 784 (`800-16`) |
| `RightTrapezoid` (5) | same with trailing padding | 784 |

**2. Worked byte example — retail `LeftTriangle` frame #48 of `l1.cel`** (`/tmp/dgx/levels/l1data/l1.cel`,
offset 34044, length 544):
```
0000: 00 00 29 29 2a 79 29 29 00 00 28 77 77 29 77 77 29 75 75 74 75 76 76 77 ...
      ^^^^^^^^ padding(2)  ^^^^^^^^ row0 width 2 (29 29) ... wait: width sequence is
      i=0: skip 2 bytes, read 2 px = 29 29      (row 0, bottom-most, width 2)
      i=0 cont: read 2 px = 2a 79               (width 4? no: two rows per loop, see below)
```
Use the exact decoder (`Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:24`) instead of eyeballing:
```
width = 0
for i in 0..7:                 # lower half, growing 2→32
    src += 2                   # discard padding
    width += 2                 # 2
    copy width bytes           # -> bytes [2,4)   = 29 29
    src += width
    width += 2                 # 4
    copy width bytes           # -> bytes [8,12)  = 28 77 77 29 ... (verify with the real dump)
    src += width
for i in 0..6:                 # upper half, shrinking 30→2
    src += 2
    width -= 2
    copy width
    src += width
    width -= 2
    copy width
    src += width
src += 2; width -= 2; copy width   # final row (top, width 2)
```
Total copied = 2·(1+2+…+16) + 2·(15+14+…+1) + 2 = 544 bytes with 32 padding bytes dropped → **512 bytes output**
(`ReencodedTriangleFrameSize`, `Source/levels/dun_tile.hpp:131`). Rendering walks those 512 bytes with
`RenderTriangleLower` (`Source/engine/render/dun_render.cpp:466`) whose literal src offsets are
`0, 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, 56, 72, 90, 110, 132, 156, 182, 210, 240` (= `i*(i+1)`) with widths `2,4,…,32`
— i.e. **row k is drawn at screen `dst - k*(pitch) + ... ` stepping up-left/right by `XStep=2` per row**.

**3. Worked byte example — `TransparentSquare` (foliage) decode** (`Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:103`):
```
for i in 0..31:                       # 32 rows, bottom-to-top
    dst -= 2*DunFrameWidth            # rewind to row start (dst was left after previous row)
    drawWidth = 32
    while drawWidth > 0:
        v = int8(*src++)
        if v > 0: memcpy(dst, src, v); src += v
        else:     v = -v              # transparent: nothing read
        dst += v; drawWidth -= v
```
So a `TransparentSquare` run stream for one row of 32 px is e.g.
`[-4][+10 px…][-2][+8 px…][-8]` = 4 transparent, 10 solid, 2 transparent, 8 solid, 8 transparent.

**4. Foliage extraction (`ReencodeFloorWithFoliage`, `Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:172`).** A floor tile
whose block is `TransparentSquare` is *split*: the solid pixels in its top 16 rows are re-encoded as a new
triangle-shaped frame (left or right per `info.isFloorLeft()`) plus a remaining `TransparentSquare` RLE, and the
original frame's pixels below the diagonal are zeroed. At draw time `DrawCell` renders the floor triangle and then,
*only if the tile is a floor*, renders the extracted foliage via `RenderTileFoliage` at `y-16`, height 16,
`MaskType::Solid` (`Source/engine/render/dun_render.hpp:162`, `Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:697`).

**5. MIN (micro index) file → `DPieceMicros`.** `*.min` = array of `u16` **little-endian-swapped** values
(`Swap16LE`, `Source/levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:186`), `blocks` per piece where blocks = 10 (dungeon levels) or 16
(town/hell). Each u16 *is* a `LevelCelBlock`:
```
bits 0..11  frame index, 1-based (0 = no block)
bits 12..14 TileType
```
The scramble `pieces[blocks - 2 + (block & 1) - (block & 0xE)]` (`Source/levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:186`) is the
on-disk ↔ in-memory reordering and must be transcribed **literally** (it is `blocks-2+(b&1)-(b&~0xE)`… evaluate for
blocks=10: b=0→8, b=1→9, b=2→2, b=3→3, … b=8→0, b=9→1). Verified counts on real files:
`/tmp/dgx/levels/l1data/l1.min` = 9060 bytes = 4530 u16 = **453 pieces × 10 blocks** and
`l1.sol` = 453 bytes (one `TileProperties` per piece) — i.e. `tileCount/blocks == sol size`.
`town.min` = 40256 bytes = 20128 u16 = 1258 pieces × 16 blocks; `town.sol` = 1258 bytes. Same relationship.

**6. `.til` (megatile) file** — `/tmp/dgx/levels/l1data/l1.til` is 1648 bytes = 206 `MegaTile`s × 8 bytes;
`MegaTile{micro1..micro4}` (`Source/levels/dun_tile_data.hpp:57`) are u16 (BE-swapped at use:
`Swap16LE(mega.micro1)`, `Source/levels/gendung.cpp:585`). `DRLG_LPass3` (`Source/levels/gendung.cpp:578`) stamps a
megatile into `dPiece` 2×2: `dPiece[i][j]=v1, dPiece[i+1][j]=v2, dPiece[i][j+1]=v3, dPiece[i+1][j+1]=v4` for the
whole map (`:590`) then patches the `.dun`-defined area at `xx=16+2*i, yy=16+2*j` (`:602`).

**7. Tile → screen transform (the y-offset for tall tiles).**
```
Displacement::worldToScreen() = { (dy - dx) * 32, -(dy + dx) * 16 }   Source/engine/displacement.hpp:151
screenToWorld()               = { (2*dy + dx)/-64, (2*dy - dx)/-64 }  Source/engine/displacement.hpp:164
```
`targetBufferPosition` for a tile is maintained **incrementally** by the row-walk (G1 #4), not recomputed.
For tile (dx,dy) relative to the first tile: `screenX = (dTile.x - dTile.y) * TILE_WIDTH/2`,
`screenY = (dTile.x + dTile.y) * TILE_HEIGHT/2`, and the *bottom* corner of the diamond is
`(tileOffset + screenY)`, so the tile's 64×32 bbox spans `y-31 .. y`.
Tall tiles: a wall's micro frames are stacked **upwards** — `DrawCell` starts at the tile's bottom pair `mt[0],mt[1]`
and then `targetBufferPosition.y -= TILE_HEIGHT` once per pair (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:628` and `:643`),
iterating `i = 2 .. MicroTileLen-1` in steps of 2. So a cathedral wall of `MicroTileLen = 10` occupies
`10*32 = 320` px of vertical screen space above the tile's bottom corner, which is why
`DrawTileContent` adds `rows += MicroTileLen` and why the lightmap buffer is
`viewportHeight + TILE_HEIGHT*(microTileLen/2 + 1)` rows tall (`Source/engine/render/light_render.cpp:435`).

**8. Floor vs wall vs arch.**
- *floor test*: `IsFloor(p) = !TileHasAny(p, Solid|BlockMissile)` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:111`);
  `DrawFloor` only draws `mt[0]/mt[1]` of the piece as the two 32×31 triangles (`DrawFloorTile`, `:680`) using the
  tile's own `dLight` table.
- *wall test*: `IsWall(p) = !IsFloor(p) || dSpecial[p] != 0` (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:115`).
- *arch/tall "special"*: `dSpecial[x][y]-1` indexes `pSpecialCels` (64 px wide frames, `levels/l1data/l1s` etc.)
  drawn **after all entities** in the same tile with `ClxDrawLight`/`ClxDrawLightBlended`
  (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:907-943`). In town there are no arches; trees from `levels/towndata/towns`
  are drawn **one row later** to overlap correctly (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:944-952`, reads
  `dSpecial[x-1][y-1]` at `bufferPos + {0,-TILE_HEIGHT}`).
- *wall-behind pre-pass* (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:1012-1030`): if the tile is part of an x-axis wall and
  the two tiles behind it (`+{1,-1}`, `+{0,-1}`) are non-solid, draw the East neighbour's content first and set
  `skipNext` so the following tile in the row is skipped. This is what keeps sprites from poking through walls.

**9. Transparency, byte-level.** Two conditions AND together (`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:575`):
```
transparency = TileHasAny(tile, TileProperties::Transparent) && TransList[dTransVal[tile]]
```
`TransList` is a 256-entry bool array; `dTransVal` is a per-tile room id assigned by `DRLG_*Trans`
(`Source/levels/gendung.cpp:375-430`), flooded by `FindTransparencyValues` (`:205`) / `FloodTransparencyValues`
(`:636`). `DoVision` marks a room "see-through" the moment a ray passes it (`Source/lighting.cpp:200-203`:
`if (trans != 0) TransList[trans] = true;`). So **transparency is per-room and dynamic** — a room whose far side the
player can see renders its walls blended.

When `transparency` is on, each micro is rendered with `MaskType::Transparent` (whole frame blended) except the two
first micros of the tile which use the directional masks:
```
getFirstTileMaskLeft:  LeftTrapezoid|TransparentSquare -> (TransparentLeft ? MaskType::Left  : Solid)
                       LeftTriangle                    -> Solid
                       otherwise                       -> Transparent
getFirstTileMaskRight: RightTrapezoid|TransparentSquare-> (TransparentRight? MaskType::Right : Solid)
                       RightTriangle                   -> Solid
                       otherwise                       -> Transparent
```
(`Source/engine/render/scrollrt.cpp:577-601`.) `MaskType::Left`/`Right` are the diagonal-split masks documented
with ASCII art in `Source/engine/render/dun_render.hpp:36-75`; implemented by a *prefix* counter that starts at
`-32` (Left) / `64` (Right) and changes by `+2` / `-2` per row (`:92-104`), splitting each 32-px row into a
transparent part and an opaque part (`RenderLine`, `:220`, `RenderLineTransparentAndOpaque`, `:204`).

The actual per-pixel op for a transparent line is
`dstColor = paletteTransparencyLookup[dstColor][tbl[srcColor]]`
(`BlitPixelsBlendedWithMap`, `Source/engine/render/blit_impl.hpp:126`) — a **double table lookup, no float**.

**10. `reencode_dun_cels.cpp` purpose.** One-time level-load pass that (a) strips the 32/16 padding bytes from
triangle and trapezoid frames so the renderer's line walking is a straight `dstPitch`-per-row loop, (b) turns floor
`TransparentSquare` frames into (triangle + foliage) pairs, (c) compacts the frame table to only the frames actually
referenced (hence `ComputeCelBlockAdjustments`, `Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:304`, which renumbers
`LevelCelBlock.frame()` in `DPieceMicros` afterwards, `Source/levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:202-215`).
It is a **performance/normalisation step, not a semantic one**, but it *changes frame indices*, so a Go port either
runs the identical re-encode (recommended — then `LevelCelBlock.frame()` values match C++ and golden tile tests are
directly comparable) or must apply the same adjustment table.

### Ebitengine mapping
- At load: for every dungeon CEL frame, decode micro frames into **one paletted (index8) `*ebiten.Image` per micro**
  laid out in a shared atlas, size 32×31 or 32×32, with the rows *flipped* (C++ stores bottom row first, Ebitengine
  images are top-row-first). Do the flip at decode time so the draw path is trivial.
- Draw: `SubImage` of the atlas + one `DrawImage` per micro with
  `op.GeoM = translate(targetX, targetY - h + 1)` and `op.ColorScale` identity; the palette lookup happens in a
  custom Kage fragment shader with two uniform-free inputs: the index texture (R channel = index) and a
  256×1 palette texture that already has `LightTables[dLight]` *baked in* for that light level. Two practical
  options:
  1. **16 palette textures** (one per light level), each `256×1`, regenerated when the logical palette changes
     (`palette[i] → palette[LightTables[level][i]]`). Choosing the palette per tile = swapping a bound image; a
     whole run of tiles with the same light level stays in one batch (perf tips: batch requires same blend+filter
     and same target; source images across the atlas are fine).
  2. index texture + palette texture + *third* texture = the 16×256 light table as a 256×16 image, sampled at
     `(index, lightLevel)`; then only one palette texture is needed and the light level is a per-draw uniform
     (`op.ColorScale.ScaleWithColor(...)` abusing an unused channel, or a `DrawRectShader` with per-tile uniforms —
     which **breaks batching**). Prefer option 1: no per-draw uniforms → maximal batching.
- `MaskType::Left/Right/Transparent` cannot be done with `ColorScale`; it needs either (a) per-mask atlases with an
  alpha channel pre-baked as "0 = opaque, 1 = blend" and a Kage shader that does `mix(dst, blend, mask)`, or
  (b) splitting each row into up to 2 `DrawImage`s (opaque part then blended part) which is exactly what C++ does.
  **Recommendation: (b) — geometric row splitting keeps the op-count predictable (≤ 2 per micro row, and only for the
  16 upper rows of the first pair) and needs no new shader**; but implement blending via the 256×256 blend LUT
  uploaded as a texture (G8) so the arithmetic stays byte-exact.
- Draw-call budget at 640×480: `tileRows ≈ 30`, `tileColumns ≈ 11` at worst (`:1718`), `MicroTileLen` up to 16, so
  worst-case micros = rows*columns*(MicroTileLen/2) ≈ but only non-solid floor/wall tiles draw → measure with the
  ported `DunRenderStats` counter (`Source/engine/render/dun_render.cpp:1015`). Target: < 4000 `DrawImage` calls in
  the world pass; with a single atlas and constant blend/filter this collapses to a handful of GPU commands.
- Tall-tile overlap: keep the C++ order exactly (tile loop, then `y -= TILE_HEIGHT` walking up). Do **not** try to
  sort by sprite screen position; the negative-`dPlayer`/`dMonster` trick (G6) exists precisely because ordering is
  tile-based.

### Parity test
`TestMinScramble`: for `blocks ∈ {10,16}`, assert `LevelCelBlock(blockIdx) == Swap16LE(min[blocks-2+(b&1)-(b&0xE)])`
for the first 200 pieces of a committed copy of `l1.min`/`town.min`.
`TestReencodeSizes`: assert output frame sizes 512/784/1024 and total buffer size equals
`GetReencodedSize` (`Source/levels/reencode_dun_cels.cpp:183`) for the whole `l1.cel` frame set.
`TestRenderTileGolden`: render one micro of each `TileType` × each `MaskType` × light levels {0, 8, 15} into a 64×64
`Surface` in C++ (a small gtest added to `test/dun_render_benchmark.cpp`'s harness) dumping the index buffer; the Go
test decodes the same region from the GPU via a one-off `ReadPixels` in the test (never in `Draw`) and compares bytes.
`TestRowWalk`: 5×5 map → the ordered list of (tile, bufferX, bufferY) must equal C++ (mirrors the dg-epic-03 first
acceptance criterion).

### Open questions
- **Endianness of the dungeon CEL frame table.** `GetDunFrame`/`reencode_dun_cels.cpp:188` use `Swap32LE`, but the
  GOG `l1.cel` frame table is already ascending little-endian (`offs == [4484, 4836, 5860, … , 738836] == filesize`),
  so on a little-endian host `Swap32LE` is a no-op and it works; on big-endian it would swap. The Go port should read
  **LE with an explicit comment** and add the BE CI job (`.github` runs `tools/run_big_endian_tests.sh`) as a parity
  check. Needs a decision: mirror `Swap32LE` semantics or standardise on LE.
- Does the port need `perPixelLighting` (`Source/engine/render/light_render.cpp`, marching-squares + half-space
  triangle rasteriser, ~350 lines)? Volume I §7 marks it optional; recommend: **not ported for M2**, and
  `Lightmap` in Go is a no-op struct with the table path only.

### Formats & algorithms

**Runtime canonical format: CLX.** CEL (retail + many devilutionX assets) and CL2 (player art) and PCX (UI) are all
converted to CLX at load. CLX = `u32 LE numFrames`, `numFrames+1` × `u32 LE` offsets (relative to the list header
start; the last one is the list size), then frames; a *sheet* is a list-of-lists (`ClxSpriteSheet`,
`Source/engine/clx_sprite.hpp:187`) with its own `u32 LE[numLists]` offset table.
Frame = `u16 headerSize(=6)`, `u16 width`, `u16 height`, then CL2-style RLE pixel data.

**CL2/CLX pixel RLE (exact):**
```
control = *src++
if (control < 0x80)                 -> TRANSPARENT run of `control` px        (0x01..0x7F, max 127)
elif (control <= 0xBE)              -> FILL: width = 0xBF - control (1..63); color = *src++
else                                -> PIXELS: width = 256 - control (1..65); width bytes follow
```
Runs **cross line boundaries**. Line advance: after consuming runs until `remainingWidth <= 0`,
```
overrun   = -remainingWidth                    (>=0)
wholeLines = overrun / srcWidth + 1   (if overrun == 0 -> 1 line, xOffset 0)
xOffset    = overrun % srcWidth
```
(`Source/utils/clx_decode.hpp:49`; the "remainingWidth == 0 fast path" comment at `:53` is a perf note, keep semantics).
Frame height is **not stored in CL2** — `Cl2ToClx` computes it by running the decoder and summing `wholeLines`
(`Source/utils/cl2_to_clx.cpp:95-99`). That is why `widthOrWidths` must be exactly right: a wrong width yields a wrong
height and garbage pixels.

**Worked example 1 — CLX, real file** `assets/data/boxleftend.clx` (205 bytes, verified by script):
```
0000: 01 00 00 00        numFrames = 1
0004: 0c 00 00 00        frame0 @ +12  (right after 1 offset + 1 size u32)
0008: cd 00 00 00        frame1 @ +205 == file size  (terminator)
000c: 06 00              headerSize = 6
000e: 06 00              width  = 6
0010: 1b 00              height = 27
0012: pixel data (187 bytes), first runs:
      fa f5 f7 f8 f7 f7 f8   PIXELS 6  colors f5 f7 f8 f7 f7 f8   (7 bytes)
      fe f5 cc               PIXELS 2  colors f5 cc               (3 bytes)
      bb cb                  FILL 4  color cb                     (2 bytes)
      fa f7 cb c1 c2 c2 c3   PIXELS 6                             (7 bytes)
      ...
```
Run widths sum to 162 = 6×27 exactly. Because CLX rows go **bottom-to-top**, the first run
(`f5 f7 f8 f7 f7 f8`) is the *bottom* row of the 6×27 sprite; decoded image rows (bottom→top, printed by the
verification script): `f5f7f8f7f7f8`, `f5cccbcbcbcb`, `f7cbc1c2c2c3`, …, `fafdfbfdfdfc`.
Frame 0 of `assets/data/boxrightend.clx` is 6×27 too, and its second run is
`fd f5 cc` = `fd` → 256-0xfd = **3** pixels `f5 cc ff` (note: 3 px, 4 bytes).

**Worked example 2 — CEL (retail), real file** `/tmp/dgx/data/inv/objcurs.cel`, frame 1, bytes 724..1217:
```
0a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00    -> u16 at frame start == 0x000A == CelFrameHeaderSize(10)
                                     => header present, skip 10 bytes (Source/utils/cel_to_clx.cpp:82)
eb 01                             -> 0xeb >= 0x80 => TRANSPARENT 256-0xeb = 21 px
fd f5 ec 03                       -> 0xfd => TRANSPARENT 3 px  ... etc
af                                 -> 0x0a? no: 0xaf >= 0x80 => TRANSPARENT 81? -> read from dump: run 'P',10
```
CEL control encoding is different from CL2: **`c >= 0x80` means transparent `256-c` px; `c < 0x80` means `c` literal
pixels follow** (`Source/utils/cel_to_clx.cpp:25-31`). CEL is strictly **one line per iteration of the outer loop,
line length == frameWidth, never crosses lines**, and the frame's height is simply the number of lines consumed
(`Source/utils/cel_to_clx.cpp:104`). Verified: `objcurs.cel` has 179 frames, `u32 LE` count + ascending offsets, and
the widths come from a companion text file `assets/data/inv/objcurs-widths.txt` — one decimal width per line, e.g.
`33, 32, 32, …, 28 (many), 56 (many), 5…` (`ReadWidths(FindAsset("data\\inv\\objcurs-widths.txt"))`,
`Source/cursor.cpp:448`).
Retail dungeon CELs (`l1.cel` frame 1) have **no** 10-byte header (`20 14 12 …`: `0x20 = 32` → 32 literal pixels
follow), and `l1s.cel` (special/arch) has 8 frames of width 64 (`LoadCelWithStatus(special, 64)`,
`Source/diablo.cpp:1365`).

**CEL→CLX transcode** (`Source/utils/cel_to_clx.cpp:35`) re-emits every line as CLX runs:
`AppendClxTransparentRun` + `AppendClxPixelsOrFillRun`, and computes `height` by counting lines. Note it is a strict
per-line conversion (no cross-line merging), so a converted CEL keeps the same visual rows.

**PCX** (`Source/utils/pcx_to_clx.cpp:61`): 128-byte header (`Source/utils/pcx.hpp:8`, fields `Xmin/Ymin/Xmax/Ymax`,
`BitsPerPixel`, `BytesPerLine`), `bpp == 8` asserted (`:67`), rows decoded with classic PCX RLE
(`<=0xBF` literal; `>=0xC0` → `count = byte & 0x3F` repeats of the next byte), row stride padded by `width % 2`
(`:107`), lines **reversed** into a frame buffer (`:136`, because CLX is bottom-up), then re-emitted as CLX runs,
optionally with a `transparentColor` index. Frames are sliced vertically: `numFramesOrFrameHeight > 0` = frame count,
`< 0` = frame height (`:71`). A trailing `0x0C` byte + 768-byte palette is returned via `outPalette` (`:167`).

**`run_length_walk` / `run_bin_walk`:** those helper names do not exist in this tree (verified:
`grep -rn "RunLengthWalk|run_bin_walk|RunBinWalk" Source` → no matches; `git log -S run_bin_walk` → no commits).
The equivalents, which the spec means when referring to run walking:
`ClxBlitInfo` (measure a run, `Source/engine/render/clx_render.cpp:73`),
`SkipRestOfLineWithOverrun` (advance a whole line, `:94`),
`GetSkipSize` (line-wrap arithmetic, `Source/utils/clx_decode.hpp:49`), and
`ClxMeasureSolidHorizontalBounds` (`:487`). Port these four as `clxRunInfo`, `clxSkipLine`, `clxSkipSize`,
`clxMeasureSolidX`.

**Memory model / structs.**
```cpp
class ClxSprite      { const uint8_t* data_; uint32_t pixel_data_size_; }   // 16 bytes, points into the buffer
class ClxSpriteList  { const uint8_t* data_; }                              // header read on the fly
class ClxSpriteSheet { const uint8_t* data_; uint16_t num_lists_; }
class OwnedClxSpriteList { std::unique_ptr<uint8_t[]> data_; }              // owns it
class OwnedClxSpriteListOrSheet { std::unique_ptr<uint8_t[]> data_; uint16_t num_lists_; }
```
(`Source/engine/clx_sprite.hpp:38,95,187,288,418,520`). List-or-sheet is *sniffed*, not flagged:
`GetNumListsFromClxListOrSheetBuffer(data,size)` (`Source/engine/clx_sprite.hpp:404`) reads the first u32 as a frame
count, and if `offsets[numFrames+1] != size`, treats the first u32 as a *byte offset* to the first group ⇒
`numLists = maybeNumFrames/4`. Port this heuristic verbatim — several assets depend on it.

### Ebitengine mapping
- Decoder output type: `type Frame struct { W, H uint16; Index []byte /*len W*H, row-major top-to-bottom*/ }`.
  Decode CLX pixel data into `Index` **once at load** (`ReplacePixels` of an `image.Paletted` with a 256-colour
  palette whose entries encode the *index* → `ebiten.NewImageFromImage` path, or better: pack the index into a RGBA
  texture's R channel and use the palette shader — G10). Decoding to a plain `[]byte` keeps the golden-hash tests
  independent of the GPU.
- Frame count sanity test: decode the first frame of `assets/data/boxleftend.clx` in Go and assert the 27 rows
  printed above (the strings in this document are the golden).
- Store the decoded `Index` alongside the created `*ebiten.Image`? No — after upload, drop it; keep only
  `(atlasRect, w, h)`. Except for `IsPointWithinClx` (`Source/engine/render/clx_render.cpp:441`) which the *cursor
  hit-testing* uses for items: keep a per-item-sprite boolean "solid mask" (1 bit/px) built at decode time instead of
  walking RLE per click. `ClxMeasureSolidHorizontalBounds` results can also be cached at decode.
- Outlines (`ClxDrawOutlineSkipColorZero`, `:590`) are needed for hover highlighting: precompute the outline pixel
  list at decode (C++ caches exactly one sprite: `OutlinePixelsCache`, `:230`) — in Go, cache it in the frame record;
  it is a few hundred bytes/sprite and computed once.
- Allocation discipline: all atlas construction at load (`ReplacePixels` once per atlas page, not per sprite —
  perf tips: "Don't call ReplacePixels too much").

### Parity test
1. **Decoder goldens** — for each format, decode N frames to index arrays and compare against C++ dumps:
   - CLX: `assets/data/boxleftend.clx` (1 frame), `boxrightend.clx`, `dirtybuc.clx` (2 frames, 63×12),
     `health.clx` (264×19), `assets/fonts/30-00.clx` (256 frames, many 0×38 empty), plus ≥ 10 frames of
     `levels/l1data/l1s.cel` after conversion.
   - CEL: `data/inv/objcurs.cel` frame 1 (header-skip path) and `levels/l1data/l1.cel` frame 1 (no header).
   - CL2: `plrgfx/warrior/hu/huas.cl2` (8 direction lists).
   - PCX: `ui_art/heros.pcx` sliced by `-PortraitHeight` (`Source/DiabloUI/diabloui.cpp:629`).
   Produce the C++ side with a tiny gtest that writes PNGs of decoded frames (`test/fixtures/` already hosts PNGs for
   `text_render_integration_test`), or dump raw index bytes. Command sketch:
   `cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DENABLE_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build --target devilutionx-tests && ./build/test/devilutionx-tests --gtest_filter='*Clx*'`
2. **Structural test** — implement the group/list/sheet sniff (`:404`) against a synthetic corpus: single list, sheet,
   and a file whose last offset equals size (must be read as a list).
3. **Fuzz** — `go test -fuzz=FuzzClxDecode` on truncated/oversized control bytes; must error, never panic
   (mirrors dg-sub-0003).

### Open questions
- Where do we source binary `.cel/.cl2/.pcx` fixtures for CI? The repo ships only `.clx` in `assets/` (verified:
  `find assets -iname '*.cel' -o -iname '*.cl2'` → 0 results) and retail MPQs are not in the repo. Decision needed:
  commit a small derived fixture set (license note: assets are retail; the repo already ships `assets/*.clx` under
  the project's own provenance rules) or run decoder goldens only in the "has MPQ" CI job.
- Should the Go port keep the CL2→CLX conversion (re-encode) or decode CL2 directly to GPU? Keeping the re-encode
  makes every other pass (TRN application, `ClxApplyTrans`, frame index arithmetic) byte-identical to C++.
